intro.heading: The syllabus is the thing being examined
paragraphs: A family in Hydra Village looking for IGCSE support is usually told about experience, patience and results. Useful information, and none of it tells you whether the person understands that Cambridge Physics 0625 is assessed across a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and that the last of those is where a confident student most often loses marks. The syllabus is what is being examined. A tutor who does not work from it is teaching the subject and hoping it overlaps.

This page is therefore written about content rather than service. It sets out the components for the subjects Hydra Village students most often need, by syllabus code. It lists the command terms that decide marks, because a candidate who writes a description when the question says explain has lost marks on work they knew. It covers the practical and alternative-to-practical papers, which are the least-taught part of the science syllabuses and the most predictable source of loss. And it explains what to do with a past paper after it has been marked, since the marking is where improvement actually comes from.

There is a local reason for taking this approach. Hydra Village sits on the eastern mainland, out towards the Zayed City corridor, and the resident pool of subject specialists here is small. The emirate's teaching staff are concentrated well to the west around Khalifa City and the Al Raha belt. That means a family choosing locally and in person is often choosing a capable generalist, and the difference between a generalist and a specialist is almost entirely the material on this page: components, command terms, practical papers and mark-scheme literacy.

The second local reason is the school run. Students here travel, which compresses the usable evening to a single block, so the content that gets taught in that hour has to be chosen well. A session spent re-explaining a topic the student already understands is not neutral; it consumes the only hour available. Choosing what to teach is a syllabus decision, which is another way of saying that the knowledge described on this page is what makes a scarce hour productive. Ask for the week's topic in advance, so the hour starts on the right component rather than finding it.

One statement of model. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The phrase families search is home tutor, so this page uses it, and delivery is one-to-one live video in Gulf Standard Time. From a community this far east it also means the choice of tutor is made on syllabus knowledge rather than on who is willing to drive out at six in the evening.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-hydra-vill.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names the components and the specific content work, because that is the level of detail a tutor should be able to discuss before being hired.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Two written papers of equal weight, one without a calculator. Content work concentrates on algebraic manipulation, functions and transformations, bearings, similar-shape scale factors, histograms with unequal class widths and vectors, which arrive late in most schemes of work.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight with a calculator permitted in both, graded 9 to 1. Higher-tier content runs into surds, algebraic proof and vectors, and the losses concentrate in the long multi-step questions at the back of each paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper, a theory paper, and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Content work targets equation rearrangement, graph interpretation, and the experimental-design language the practical component assesses.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Same component structure as Physics. The content bottlenecks are moles and stoichiometry, electrolysis products, rates of reaction, and organic naming and reactions, where reliable marks are available to anyone who learns the rules properly.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Same component structure again. Content work focuses on transport in plants and humans, enzymes, genetics and inheritance crosses, and the ecology questions that carry data-handling marks alongside recall.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: A reduced-content route taken by students carrying a broad subject load. The content is narrower than the separate sciences, which makes thorough coverage realistic, and the command terms and practical component work identically.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Directed writing, reading responses and composition. Content work is planning under time and matching the response to the exact task, since a strong writer can still write the wrong thing and lose most of the available marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Reading comprehension technique, the summary task and the writing registers. Fluent speakers lose marks on structure rather than vocabulary, so content work targets the shape of each response type.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the data-response paper, where candidates quote the extract instead of using it. Calculation questions are reliable marks for a numerate student and evaluation is where nearly everyone loses them.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Pseudocode to the syllabus conventions, trace tables, and the theory paper covering data representation, networks and security. Students who can program and cannot write conventional pseudocode lose marks for correct thinking.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography 0460 and History 0470
subjects.description: Case-study specificity and source handling respectively. Both reward a named example and a structured judgement, and both punish general answers, which makes them unusually responsive to short technique work.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies alongside the IGCSE course
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools beside the licensed curriculum, with published rules on class organisation and language of instruction. Plan the timetable space they occupy before designing any Year 11 revision schedule.

sections.heading: Which papers your child actually sits
paragraphs: Parents are rarely told this and it changes how revision should be organised. In the Cambridge sciences, a candidate sits a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and then either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, depending on what the school offers. Multiple choice rewards precise recall and punishes approximate understanding; the theory paper rewards structured extended answers; the practical component rewards experimental reasoning, which is a third distinct skill that most revision ignores entirely.

In mathematics, Cambridge 0580 is assessed by two written papers of equal weight with one sat without a calculator, while Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 has two papers of equal weight with a calculator permitted in both. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 assumes a graphics calculator and adds an investigation component. In English, First Language 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510 assess different things and reward different response shapes, and a fluent speaker entered for 0510 can still score poorly by writing without structure.

The practical consequence for a Hydra Village household with one usable evening is that revision should be allocated by component rather than by subject. A student who is strong on theory and weak on the practical paper does not need more chemistry; they need four sessions on experimental design. A student who loses marks on multiple choice needs precision drilling, which is a different activity from writing extended answers. The table sets out the components by syllabus code so a family can see what their child is actually facing.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary the mark scheme is waiting for
paragraphs: This is the cheapest improvement available in any IGCSE subject and the one most consistently neglected. Every command term carries a precise expectation, and a candidate who answers a different instruction than the one given loses marks on content they know perfectly well. State wants a bare fact with no justification. Describe wants what happens, in sequence, without reasons. Explain wants the reason, usually with a because in it. Suggest wants a plausible answer applied to an unfamiliar situation, and is marked generously if the reasoning is sound.

Calculate wants a numerical answer with working shown. Determine implies the value must be obtained rather than recalled, often from supplied data. Deduce wants a conclusion drawn from given information with the reasoning visible. Compare wants both things referenced in each point of comparison, which is where most candidates lose half the marks by describing one and then the other. Evaluate and discuss want a judgement supported by evidence on both sides, and a candidate who presents only one side cannot reach the top band however good that side is.

Teaching this takes one session per subject and it pays off across every paper. The method is simple: take a marked past paper, find each question where the answer was factually correct and the marks were not awarded, and identify which command term was misread. Students are usually surprised by how many there are. It is also the single easiest thing for a parent to check at home with a published mark scheme, because the scheme states what each mark requires and the mismatch is visible without any subject knowledge.

sections.heading: The practical paper nobody practises
paragraphs: In the Cambridge sciences, candidates sit either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and in both cases they are assessed on experimental reasoning rather than on laboratory dexterity. This is the component with the largest gap between what students know and what they score, because school practical work is often about performing an experiment while the paper is about designing, criticising and interpreting one.

The assessable skills are specific and teachable. Identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables in an unfamiliar experiment. Reading an instrument to the correct precision and recording it with units. Tabulating data with headings and units in the right place, because marks are awarded for table conventions. Plotting a graph with sensible scales, labelled axes and a line of best fit drawn properly. Describing an improvement to a method in terms of what error it reduces. Identifying a source of error and distinguishing it from a mistake.

None of that requires a laboratory, which is why this component supports well over video. Past practical papers can be worked and marked against the scheme exactly as theory papers can, and the gain is usually faster because the skills are narrow and the conventions are rigid. For a Hydra Village family with one usable evening block, four sessions on this component is often the highest-value spend available in a science subject, and almost nobody buys it because the losses are invisible in a theory-focused report. Ask which of the two components the centre enters, because the preparation is not the same.

sections.heading: What to do with a past paper after it is marked
paragraphs: Sitting a paper produces a score, which is almost useless on its own. Marking it against the published scheme and sorting the losses produces a plan, which is the whole point. The sort is simple enough for a parent to do with the student: for every lost mark, decide whether the cause was a misread command term, an arithmetic or accuracy slip, missing working, or genuine unknown content. Four categories, and each one has a completely different remedy.

Misread command terms are the cheapest to fix and usually the largest category among students who feel they knew the material. Accuracy slips respond to rounding discipline and to writing intermediate values down. Missing working is a habit problem: method marks are awarded only for method the examiner can see, so a student who computes mentally earns nothing when the final answer fails. Unknown content is the only category that needs teaching, and it is usually the smallest of the four.

The practical routine for a Hydra Village household works around the commute. The paper is sat at the weekend, to the published duration, because a full paper plus a walkthrough is a two-hour job no school night will hold. The walkthrough happens in the weekday session. Three targets carry into the following week as short tasks sized to fifteen or twenty minutes, because tasks sized for an hour do not get done after a long bus journey. And no new content is introduced in the last three weeks before a series, because material learned that late tends to displace material already secure.

sections.heading: Core against Extended: what actually changes
paragraphs: Families often treat the Core and Extended decision as a judgement about ability, when it is also a decision about content coverage and about the grade that can be awarded. On Cambridge 0580 mathematics, Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E. In the sciences, the Core and Extended routes sit different papers and the Extended route carries additional content, with the supplement clearly marked in the published syllabus. Pearson Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher tiers with Foundation capped at grade 5 and Higher running 9 to 4.

The practical reading of that is twofold. A student on the lower route cannot be awarded above the cap however well they perform, so the entry has to be checked against the family's ambitions in Year 10 while a change is still administratively possible. And a student moved up a tier late faces genuinely new content, not merely harder questions, which is a teaching job with a realistic duration rather than a matter of confidence.

The useful conversation with a school is evidence-based. Ask for the syllabus code and tier in writing. If the tier looks wrong, have the student sit a full past paper at the higher route under timed conditions at home and mark it against the published scheme. That result is a stronger argument than a parental opinion and costs a weekend. Ask also for the exam centre and its Cambridge administrative zone, because Cambridge states that using the correct version of the timetable for your zone is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong one.

sections.heading: Why syllabus knowledge is scarce locally, and what that costs
paragraphs: Hydra Village is residential and the emirate's teaching staff live mostly to the west, around Khalifa City and the Al Raha belt. A family choosing an in-home tutor from here is choosing from a small pool of people willing to drive east at the evening peak, and inside that pool the number who can discuss components, command terms and the alternative-to-practical paper for a specific syllabus code is smaller again. The likely outcome is a capable generalist, and the cost of that is precisely the content on this page going untaught.

The price comparison points the same way. Published figures put in-home one-to-one across Abu Dhabi at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. From a community this far east the in-home figure sits towards the upper end, because the journey is long and is billed.

The honest trade-offs of a screen deserve stating. A younger or easily distracted student is harder to supervise remotely, and a tutor needs to see written working, which means a tablet and stylus or a phone propped over paper; both are worth testing in a free trial. Against that, a shared screen is the easiest place to read a syllabus, a past paper and a mark scheme side by side, which is exactly the activity this page argues for. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service available only in India.

sections.heading: What we measure, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: A page built on syllabus detail should report in the same currency. Progress is measured as classified losses on timed papers: command term, accuracy, missing working or unknown content, with the same question types re-sat after the targeted work. At six sessions you receive a written statement of what has moved and the three categories still costing most marks, checkable against your child's own scripts. A report that the student seems more confident is not a measurement.

If the match is wrong the tutor changes at our cost, reviewed at six sessions. Nothing renews automatically, and a household that wants only the diagnosis can take it and stop. In a community where the usable study evening is a single block, that matters more than usual: a mismatched tutor is not just a cost, it is the loss of the only hour available.

What we will not do is publish or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure, and because the official version is the current one. We publish no satisfaction percentage, score-improvement figure, student count or star rating, because none could be shown with a sample size, a date and a method. We claim no accreditation from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and have no UAE premises. And on the Cambridge 0607 investigation or any later Internal Assessment, a tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on your child's own work and never produces it; one provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments, and that risk falls on the candidate.
bullets: Progress reported as classified losses, re-measured on the same question types

faqs.question: Which papers does my child sit in each IGCSE science subject?
faqs.answer: In the Cambridge sciences, a candidate sits a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper, and then either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, depending on what the school offers. Those three components test different skills: precise recall, structured extended writing, and experimental reasoning respectively. Most revision addresses the first two and ignores the third, which is why the practical component shows the largest gap between what a student knows and what they score. The exact components for your child's entry are in the published syllabus for the code.

faqs.question: What are command terms in the Cambridge sciences, and why do they cost my child marks?
faqs.answer: They are the instruction words at the start of each question, and each carries a precise expectation. State wants a bare fact. Describe wants what happens, in sequence, without reasons. Explain wants the reason, usually with a because in it. Suggest wants plausible reasoning applied to an unfamiliar case. Compare wants both items referenced in every point. A candidate who answers a different instruction loses marks on content they knew, and one session per subject usually fixes the habit permanently.

faqs.question: What does the alternative-to-practical paper actually assess?
faqs.answer: Experimental reasoning rather than laboratory skill. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables in an unfamiliar experiment. Reading instruments to the correct precision and recording units properly. Tabulating data with headings and units in the heading rather than beside each value. Plotting graphs with sensible scales, labelled axes and a proper line of best fit. Naming the error a suggested improvement would reduce. Distinguishing a source of error from a careless mistake. None of it needs a laboratory, so it supports well over video.

faqs.question: My child understands the science but scores badly. Where are the marks going?
faqs.answer: Usually to three places that have nothing to do with knowledge. Misread command terms, where a description is given and an explanation was asked for. Missing working in calculation questions, since method marks are awarded only for method the examiner can see. And the practical component, where school lab work teaches performing an experiment while the paper assesses designing and criticising one. Mark a full paper against the published scheme and sort the losses into four categories; the pattern is usually obvious within half an hour.

faqs.question: What should we actually do with a past paper once it is marked?
faqs.answer: Sort every lost mark into one of four causes: a misread command term, an accuracy or arithmetic slip, missing working, or genuine unknown content. Each has a different remedy and only the last needs teaching, which is usually the smallest category. Then carry three targets into the following week as short tasks of fifteen to twenty minutes. A score on its own is a thermometer; a classified paper is a plan, and the sorting needs no subject knowledge beyond the published scheme.

faqs.question: Is there any point sitting past papers without a tutor to mark them?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided somebody marks them against the published scheme, and a parent can do that. The scheme states what each mark requires, so a mismatch is visible without subject knowledge: the answer is factually right and the mark was not awarded, which usually means a command term or an accuracy convention. What a tutor adds is speed and diagnosis across subjects, and an explanation of why a particular approach was unrewardable. The sitting is the cheap part; the marking is where improvement comes from.

faqs.question: How much does the Core or Extended decision change the content?
faqs.answer: More than families expect. The Extended and Higher routes carry additional syllabus content, clearly marked as a supplement in the published syllabus, rather than simply harder versions of the same questions. That matters if a student is moved up a tier late, because it is a teaching job with a real duration rather than a confidence issue. It also matters because Cambridge 0580 Core is graded C to G and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation caps at grade 5, so the entry limits the grade administratively.

faqs.question: How do I know which syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: It is on the exam entry statement, and the school's exams officer will confirm it along with the tier in one email. Schools reachable from Hydra Village use both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, occasionally with different boards for different subjects within one school, so the school's name tells you nothing. Ask for the exam centre and its Cambridge administrative zone at the same time, because the timetable version depends on the centre rather than on your home address.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and two sciences for a Hydra Village student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the question to ask is about components rather than subjects. Someone who can discuss mole arithmetic, equation rearrangement and the alternative-to-practical paper is genuinely covering three syllabuses. Someone who knows science broadly will teach content and miss the components where the marks are being lost. Ask the component questions for each subject separately in the trial. Where we cannot cover a combination well, we say so rather than stretching one tutor across three codes.

faqs.question: Does the long commute from Hydra Village change how we should revise?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. Weeknights carry short specific work of fifteen to twenty minutes, because tasks sized for an hour do not get done after a long bus journey. And the weekend carries the long work, because a full paper plus a mark-scheme walkthrough is a two-hour job no school night will hold. One protected weekday session plus a weekend paper is the pattern that survives a term here, and two aspirational weekday sessions is the pattern that does not.

faqs.question: Which series do candidates out here sit, and when do results land?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only and must not appear in an Abu Dhabi plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. As a guide to the rhythm, Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Confirm every date on the board's live timetable.

faqs.question: Will IGCSE content be enough for A-Level or IB next year?
faqs.answer: The grade will not tell you; the marked papers will. A-Level chemistry assumes fluent mole arithmetic, A-Level mathematics assumes confident algebraic manipulation, and IB Analysis and Approaches assumes non-calculator technique. A student can reach a respectable IGCSE grade while any of those remains shaky, because reliable marks elsewhere compensate. Ask a tutor directly whether the underlying content is secure for the intended Year 12 course, which is a more useful question than what grade is likely.

faqs.question: Can you give us copies of the syllabus and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and nor should any provider. We reference board materials and link to the official source rather than redistributing them, because reproducing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Working from the official site also means you are reading the current version rather than something since revised. Cambridge and Pearson publish what is available, and your child's school can advise on access to anything else.

faqs.question: What will a progress report tell me that a school report does not?
faqs.answer: Where the marks went rather than how many there were. We report classified losses: command term, accuracy, missing working or unknown content, re-measured on the same question types after the targeted work, with the three categories still costing most marks named at six sessions. A school report places your child within that school's cohort, which is useful and different. The classified version is checkable against your child's own scripts, which is the property that makes a report worth reading.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-hydra-vill.closingHeading: Start from the syllabus, not from the service
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-hydra-vill.closingBody: The useful first step for a Hydra Village family costs nothing but a message and a weekend. Ask the school's exams officer for the syllabus code and tier for each subject, the exam centre and its Cambridge administrative zone. Open the published syllabus for each code on the board's own site and read the assessment overview. Then have your child sit one full past paper, mark it against the published scheme, and sort every lost mark into command term, accuracy, missing working or unknown content. Bring that to a free trial lesson and the tutor will confirm or correct it and name which component the next block should target.

intro.heading: What you are actually paying for when you book an IGCSE home tutor in Khalifa City
paragraphs: Khalifa City is a villa community, and villa communities price tutoring differently from tower communities. A tutor who agrees to drive to a house off the Khalifa City A roundabout is selling two things under one number: an hour of IGCSE teaching, and roughly forty minutes of driving, parking and gate access either side of it. Bestimate's 2026 UAE rate survey puts in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. The same survey puts a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300. The difference between those bands is the travel, not the teaching.

That gap matters more here than in most places, because the community sits between the island and the airport road rather than inside either. A tutor living in Al Bateen or Khalidiyah who takes a Khalifa City booking is committing most of an evening to one hour of paid work. Some price for it. Others accept the booking at a low rate and then quietly drop it in week three when a client closer to home appears. Families in Al Raha Gardens and Al Reef report the same pattern. In this corridor the cheapest in-home quote is reliably the least stable one.

The second thing the travel premium buys is a smaller shortlist. Insisting on somebody who can reach your villa by 16:30 narrows the field to whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive and still has a free evening. If your child needs Chemistry 0620 rather than general science help, or Edexcel 4MA1 rather than Cambridge 0580, that shortlist can empty entirely. Online delivery inverts the constraint: the lesson arrives at the desk over live video, so the limit on who teaches your child is the syllabus they know, not the traffic on the Sheikh Khalifa bridge at five o'clock.

This page prices the whole thing out. It publishes the AED bands by format with the source and date attached, does the monthly arithmetic most families actually budget against, names the four places money reliably disappears in this corridor, and covers the permit question nobody asks until after the first payment has cleared. It also states plainly what IB Gram does not sell: there are no home visits in Abu Dhabi, and no tutor will arrive at a Khalifa City gate. Home visiting is a service offered only in India.

One timing note before the numbers, because it changes what any of this is worth. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered in India only, so a tutoring budget built around a spring exam is a budget built on the wrong country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Everything below is priced against those windows rather than against a vague idea of exam season.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-khalifa-ci.programmesIntro: Khalifa City families mostly sit one of four things: Cambridge IGCSE, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the IB Middle Years Programme that runs to Year 11 at the IB schools in the corridor, or the Diploma Programme after it. The cost of support differs by programme because the assessment load differs, so each entry below says what the money is buying.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers, with syllabus codes that matter: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500, Economics 0455. Most subjects split into Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings. Tutoring cost tracks tier and paper count, not the subject name, which is why a quote should always ask which code and which tier your child is entered for.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Khalifa City schools publish their zone timetable each series; any revision plan a tutor builds should be checked against that document rather than a generic one found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other British-track route in the corridor, with codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics and 4CH1 Chemistry. Papers are structured differently from Cambridge and some subjects are available in a modular pattern, so past-paper practice does not transfer cleanly between the two boards. A tutor who prepares a child on 0580 material for a 4MA1 paper is teaching the right maths against the wrong question style.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes International GCSE series in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those lead times are why entry decisions in Khalifa City are made a term before anyone feels exam pressure.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The route taken at the IB continuum schools in and around Khalifa City. Assessment is criterion-referenced rather than paper-based, graded 1-8 against four criteria per subject, which parents coming from a British-track school often misread as softer. It is not softer; it is differently evidenced. Support usually targets the command terms and the criterion descriptors rather than past papers, because past papers barely exist.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving between an MYP school in Khalifa City and an IGCSE school in Al Raha or on the island hit a real content gap, especially in maths and the sciences. The gap is predictable and closable, and the transition map further down this page is the version of that work that costs the fewest paid hours.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, and the Diploma's cost profile is different from IGCSE: fewer total hours, concentrated in exploration design, data analysis and Paper 3 technique at Higher Level. Hourly rates for Diploma specialists run above IGCSE across the market.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB session or results date is published on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than no date. Confirm every Diploma deadline with your child's IB coordinator at the Khalifa City school, who holds the internal calendar that actually binds.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-khalifa-ci.subjectsIntro: The subject list below is the one Khalifa City families ask about most, with the syllabus code attached because the code is what determines the paper structure, the formula sheet and the mark scheme. Each note says where marks go missing rather than describing the subject in general terms.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Extended candidates lose most marks on functions, transformations of graphs and the longer trigonometry questions where a diagram has to be drawn before anything can be calculated. Method marks survive a wrong answer only if the working is legible and ordered, which is a teachable habit rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Higher tier rewards algebraic fluency more aggressively than Cambridge, and the question wording is noticeably different. Students who revise from 0580 papers arrive at 4MA1 able to do the maths but unprepared for how it is asked. Past-paper work must come from the right board.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Year 11 students as a bridge towards Diploma Mathematics or A-Level. Calculus arrives early and without the scaffolding of the main syllabus. The common failure is treating it as harder 0580 rather than a different course with its own technique demands.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism cost more marks than any other topic in this corridor, followed by the practical paper's handling of uncertainty and graph gradients. Many students can state the physics and still lose the mark for units, significant figures or an unlabelled axis.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic reaction pathways are where the grade is decided. The paper rewards precise language: a candidate who writes that a reaction is faster rather than naming the increased frequency of successful collisions has the idea and not the mark.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and deceptively approachable, which is why it is under-revised. Marks go on the extended-response questions about transport, homeostasis and inheritance, where a correct but unstructured answer scores a fraction of the available credit.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a double award, which means less time per topic and a syllabus that cuts specific sub-topics rather than simplifying everything. A tutor working from the single-science syllabus wastes hours on content this course does not assess.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended-response reading question carry the paper. Students in Khalifa City schools often read well and still lose marks for ignoring audience, form and purpose, which are explicitly credited in the mark scheme.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Assessed across reading, writing, listening and, in 0511, speaking. The exercises are formulaic and highly trainable; most of the available improvement sits in exam technique and timing rather than in general English ability.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline decide the grade. An analyse question answered with description earns little, no matter how much the student knows. Gulf-specific examples travel well in Paper 2 and are a cheap source of marks.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole assessment. Students who revise definitions score the knowledge marks and miss the application and evaluation marks, which together outweigh them. Practice has to be done on real case-study inserts.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Relevant to most non-Arab families in Khalifa City, because Arabic is mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. Progress depends on consistent short sessions rather than exam-term intensives, which makes it the one subject where spreading spend thinly is correct.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Khalifa City costs, line by line
paragraphs: The honest answer is a range, and the range contains two different products. Across Abu Dhabi, in-home one-to-one tuition is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 UAE rate survey, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300, and Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Budget platforms advertise far lower: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Those lower rates buy a capable university student, not somebody who has marked a 0625 paper.

Pull the bands apart and the travel premium is somewhere between AED 30 and AED 200 an hour. In Khalifa City that premium sits at the upper end, because the community is a twenty to thirty-five minute drive from Al Bateen, Khalidiyah and the Corniche where a large share of experienced tutors live, and the evening return is slower than the outbound run. At AED 250 an hour with a forty-minute round trip, you are paying roughly AED 80 of a specialist's time to sit in a car.

None of these figures are IB Gram prices. They are what the Abu Dhabi market charges, published here with sources and a read date so you can check them before you speak to anybody, including us. What IB Gram sells is one-to-one teaching over live video, quoted after a free trial lesson rather than before it. sections.heading: The travel premium, priced in Khalifa City minutes
paragraphs: A Khalifa City booking is a geography problem before it is a teaching problem. The community is spread across large plots with gated entries, and a tutor arriving by car needs time for the approach road, the gate, visitor parking and the walk to the door. Forty minutes of round-trip travel is a conservative estimate from the island, and closer to an hour from Khalidiyah during the school-run window. That time is real, it has to be paid for, and it comes out of the same hourly figure that was supposed to buy teaching.

The knock-on effect is on scheduling. An in-home tutor can serve two, at most three, Khalifa City families in an evening, so the 16:30 and 17:30 slots are allocated to whoever booked first and everyone else is offered 19:30 or nothing. Online, the same tutor can hold a 16:00 slot for a Raha Gardens child whose school day ends at 15:10 and a 20:00 slot for an Al Raha Beach household where both parents get home at 19:00, without either slot competing with the other.

The third effect is the one families notice last. Because travel caps how many clients a tutor can hold, in-home tutors specialise in whatever the nearest schools teach most of. That is fine for Extended maths. It is a problem for 0606 Additional Mathematics, 4CH1 Chemistry or Arabic as a first language, where the local pool may be empty and the family ends up paying a generalist specialist rate for generalist teaching. The comparison below prices the three formats against Khalifa City conditions rather than against a generic city.

sections.heading: Four places tutoring money disappears in this corridor
paragraphs: The first leak is paying for coverage instead of diagnosis. A family books ten hours, the tutor works forward through the syllabus from wherever the school happens to be, and nine of those hours are spent on material the child already had. The fix is cheap and almost nobody asks for it: hand over the marked mock script in the first session and let the tutor build the plan from the lost marks rather than from the contents page. A single marked paper is worth more diagnostic information than three hours of conversation.

The second leak is board drift. Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor run both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, sometimes in the same family, and past papers are freely available for both. A student revising 0580 papers for a 4MA1 exam is doing real maths against the wrong question style, and the first sign of trouble is a mock result that makes no sense given the hours invested. Ask which board and which code before the first session, and ask the tutor to name the paper structure back to you.

The third leak is the cheap quote that does not survive. In-home rates below the market floor are usually offered by somebody who has not yet priced the drive to Khalifa City, and the booking collapses in week three or four. Rebuilding a relationship with a new tutor costs two or three sessions of diagnosis that have already been paid for once. The fourth leak is spending in the wrong term: heavy hours in Year 10 autumn, nothing in the term that actually decides the grade.
bullets: Bring the marked mock paper to session one, not a list of topics
Confirm the board and syllabus code before any money changes hands
Treat a far-below-market in-home quote as a scheduling risk, not a bargain
Concentrate spend in the ten weeks before the series, not in the first term
Review after four sessions against the mock, and stop if nothing has moved

sections.heading: The monthly number parents in Khalifa City actually budget against
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutors quote and monthly totals are how families decide. Bestimate's UAE estimates for a weekly one-hour session land at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packaged offers in the market sit inside those bands: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. The in-home package costs roughly twice the online one for half the number of contacts.

Frequency usually matters more than rate. Two contacts a week at a mid-band rate generally outperform one contact a week at a specialist rate, because IGCSE content decays fast and a seven-day gap means the first fifteen minutes of every session are spent recovering last week's ground. A family with AED 1,200 a month to spend is almost always better served by two mid-band hours a week than by one premium hour, with the exception of Additional Mathematics and Higher-tier physics where depth beats frequency.

The other budgeting mistake is flat spending across two years. The grade is decided in the final two terms, and the useful shape is light support in Year 10, a step up after the Year 11 mocks, and an intensive block in the eight to ten weeks before the series. Spending the same amount every month for twenty-four months costs the same as that shape and delivers less, because the hours land when the student has nothing concrete to practise on.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision that changes what you spend
paragraphs: Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered, and the tier your child is entered for changes both the ceiling and the cost of support. Core caps the available grade and covers less content; Extended opens the full grade range and adds topics that need teaching rather than revising. A family paying for Extended support while the school has entered the child for Core is buying material that will never be assessed, and the reverse is worse: Core-level practice before an Extended paper produces a mock result nobody can explain.

The tier decision is the school's to make and it is usually made from mock performance, but parents are entitled to ask when it is made, on what evidence, and whether it can be revisited. In the Khalifa City corridor the decision typically lands between the autumn and spring mocks of Year 11. That timing is the single most useful piece of information for planning spend, because it tells you when the content list your tutor is working from becomes final.

Where tutoring genuinely changes the outcome is in the window before the decision. A student sitting on the Core and Extended boundary in maths or a science can often be moved across it with targeted work on the specific Extended-only topics, which is a short, well-defined job rather than a general improvement project. After the entry is made, support switches to paper technique within the chosen tier, and the hourly requirement usually falls.

sections.heading: Is the person you are paying permitted to tutor in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the rule is specific. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, administered through MoHRE. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers at government and private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

The practical consequence for a Khalifa City family is that the question is askable. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. A tutor who holds the permit can say so; a tutor who becomes vague when asked has told you something useful. The permit is about the individual, not the platform, and no agency can hold it on a tutor's behalf.

There is a second rule that catches families by surprise. ADEK's professional-ethics requirements for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against the current ADEK text, but the direction is clear: your child's own class teacher is the one person who should not be taking your money.

sections.heading: What no fee should ever buy: coursework and academic honesty
paragraphs: One corner of this market sells finished assessed work, and at least one competitor in the UAE search results advertises completed Internal Assessments at a price. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring. It is academic malpractice under IB rules and a disciplinary matter at every board, and the student carries the consequence while the seller carries none. No tutor may write an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a TOK essay, a Personal Project or any coursework component for a student, at any price.

What a tutor may do is substantial and worth paying for. Teaching the assessment criteria so the student knows what each one credits. Reading a draft and saying where the argument thins out. Questioning a research design until the student finds the flaw. Modelling a worked analysis on different data so the technique transfers. Checking that referencing is complete. All of that improves the mark legitimately, and all of it leaves the work demonstrably the student's own, which is the test every board applies.

The boundary matters for a second reason. IGCSE coursework components and Diploma internal assessments are submitted with declarations, and schools in the corridor run originality checks as a matter of routine. A paid draft that reads nothing like the student's class work is the easiest thing in the world to spot. A family that pays for genuine feedback gets a mark that stands; a family that pays for a document is buying a risk it cannot see and cannot withdraw once the submission is made.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the June and November series
paragraphs: Exam planning fails because families count forwards from today instead of backwards from the paper. The dates that bind are not the exam dates: they are the entry deadline, the coursework submission window and the mock that produces the tier decision, all of which fall months earlier. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered in India only, so it belongs nowhere in an Abu Dhabi plan.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The lead times are long and documented: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those gaps between sitting a paper and learning the outcome are the reason a resit decision has to be planned before the first result arrives, not after it.

Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Your child's Khalifa City school knows its zone; a generic timetable found online may not match it. Treat the school's published version as the only one that counts, link the official board timetable rather than any restatement of it, and build the eight-to-ten-week intensive block backwards from the first paper in your child's weakest subject.

sections.heading: Starting from Khalifa City without wasting the first month
paragraphs: The first month is where most tutoring budgets leak, and the cause is almost always a slow start. A family describes the problem in general terms, the tutor begins with general work, and four paid hours pass before anybody looks at an actual script. Shortening that is free. Send the marked mock paper, the school report and the syllabus code before the trial lesson, and the trial can be spent on the real diagnosis rather than on introductions.

The trial lesson is free and takes one hour, with no card details requested and no commitment attached. Its purpose is narrow: find out whether this tutor can explain the thing your child is stuck on, in a way your child follows. That is not a judgement a parent can make from a profile, and it is not a judgement anybody should pay AED 250 to make. If the answer is no, the next match is arranged without a fee and without a conversation about why.

After that the arithmetic is yours. Pick a slot that survives the Khalifa City school run rather than one that works only in a good week. Book two contacts a week if the series is close and one if it is not. Ask for the written note after each session so you can see what was covered without interrogating your child about it. Review after four sessions against the mock that started everything. If nothing has moved, change something, and say so early rather than at the end of the term.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE home tutor in Khalifa City cost per hour?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one tuition in Abu Dhabi is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 UAE rate survey, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. The difference between those bands is mostly travel, and in Khalifa City the drive from the island or Khalidiyah runs 35 to 60 minutes round trip. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a fixed rate, and delivers lessons online rather than at any UAE address.

faqs.question: Is online IGCSE tuition genuinely cheaper than a home visit in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: At the same teaching quality, yes, because the in-home rate includes a journey. Market figures put online qualified tutors at AED 150 to 300 and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500. The saving is not the main argument though. Travel caps how many Khalifa City families one tutor can serve in an evening, so the in-home pool is whoever lives nearby and is free at 16:30. Online, the constraint is the syllabus code rather than the Sheikh Khalifa bridge, which matters most for Additional Mathematics, Edexcel science codes and Arabic as a first language.

faqs.question: Why do the cheapest in-home tutoring quotes in Khalifa City keep falling through?
faqs.answer: Because the quote was priced before the drive was. A tutor living on Al Reem Island who agrees to AED 150 an hour for a Khalifa City villa is earning that for roughly an hour and forty minutes of committed time. When a client appears five minutes from home at the same rate, the Khalifa City booking is the one that gets rescheduled and then dropped, usually in week three or four. The cost to the family is not the rate; it is paying twice for the diagnostic sessions that a new tutor has to repeat from the beginning.

faqs.question: What should a Khalifa City family budget each month for IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's UAE monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Packaged offers in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. With a fixed budget, two mid-band contacts a week usually beat one premium contact, because a seven-day gap means the first quarter of each session is spent recovering ground.

faqs.question: Do the AED figures on this page include VAT?
faqs.answer: The figures here are market rates published by other providers, and whether each includes VAT is a question for the provider quoting it. The UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees is not stated on this page, because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation that is not held here. What you can reasonably ask any tutor or agency, including IB Gram, is a simple one: is the number you have quoted me the number I will pay, inclusive of any tax, and in dirhams rather than another currency.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working in Khalifa City need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, administered by MoHRE and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted here. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask your tutor directly, because the permit belongs to the individual rather than to any platform.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at their Khalifa City school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: They should not. ADEK's professional-ethics requirements for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than lifted from the policy text, so verify it against the current ADEK document. The reasoning holds regardless: the person who sets and marks the school assessment is the wrong person to be paid privately for preparing your child for it.

faqs.question: Is tutoring priced per hour or per lesson, and what if we stop after one?
faqs.answer: Ask, because the market does both and the difference is material. A ninety-minute lesson quoted as one session at AED 300 is AED 200 an hour; a sixty-minute lesson at AED 250 is dearer than it looks next to it. With IB Gram the first hour is a free trial with no card details taken, so stopping after it costs nothing. If you continue and then stop, there is no rolling term to exit and no fee attached to leaving. Any provider who cannot answer this in one sentence is worth a second look.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects cost the most to tutor in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Rates rise with scarcity rather than with difficulty. Extended sciences, Additional Mathematics 0606 and Arabic as a first language command the highest hourly figures in this corridor, because the number of tutors who can teach the actual syllabus rather than the subject is small. Mainstream Extended maths and English sit in the middle of the band. The practical consequence for a Khalifa City family is that the scarce subjects are exactly the ones where an in-home search fails and online delivery closes the gap, because distance stops being a factor in who is available.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Year 10 student in Khalifa City start with?
faqs.answer: One a week is usually right in Year 10, provided it is consistent and built on a marked script. The content load is still accumulating and the useful work is habit-forming: ordered working, command-term discipline, and getting past papers from the correct board into the routine early. The step up to two contacts a week belongs after the Year 11 mocks, when the lost marks are visible and the tier decision is settled. Starting at three sessions a week in Year 10 generally spends the budget before the term that decides the grade arrives.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi rise as the exam series gets closer?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens, which has the same effect as a price rise. In the eight to ten weeks before the June series, the tutors who know a specific syllabus code are already committed, and what remains is either a generalist at a specialist rate or a slot at an awkward hour. Families who book the intensive block a term ahead pay the ordinary rate for the right person. Those who start looking after the spring mocks pay whatever is left. The November series is quieter and easier to staff, which is worth knowing if a resit is likely.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put maths and physics with one Khalifa City tutor?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor who holds both 0580 Extended and 0625 Extended gives you continuity and a joined-up view of where the algebra is failing the physics. The limit is depth. Combinations that work well are maths with physics, or chemistry with biology. Combinations that rarely work are a science with English or Arabic, where the teaching skill is genuinely different. If one tutor is covering two subjects, ask which of the two they have actually taught to the exam rather than which they are comfortable with.

faqs.question: Will a tutor mark past papers, or is marking charged separately?
faqs.answer: Clarify this before you book, because it is where quoted rates stop being comparable. Marking a full Extended paper properly against the mark scheme takes thirty to forty-five minutes of unpaid time if it is not inside the fee. Some tutors include it, some charge for it, and some simply go through answers verbally in the session, which is not the same thing. Written feedback against the mark scheme is where most of the visible improvement comes from, so a slightly higher rate that includes marking is usually the cheaper arrangement overall.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE tutor be matched for a Khalifa City family?
faqs.answer: For mainstream codes such as 0580 Extended, 0625 or 0500, a match and a trial lesson usually happen within a few days, because online delivery means availability is not limited to tutors living near Khalifa City. Scarcer requirements take longer: Additional Mathematics, Edexcel-specific science codes and Arabic as a first language can take a week or more to staff properly. You will be told which situation applies rather than given a quick general match, since a fast poor match costs more than a short wait.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for a niche IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: You are told, which sounds unremarkable and is not: no competitor page studied for this search discloses a coverage limit at all. If no suitable tutor is available for your child's code, the options are a short wait for the right person, a different starting point such as examination technique while the subject specialist frees up, or a referral elsewhere. Where the specialist is based outside the UAE, that is stated up front and the session is timed to Gulf Standard Time, so the 16:30 or 20:00 slot works around a Khalifa City evening rather than around a foreign working day.

intro.heading: IGCSE tutor is a description, not a qualification
paragraphs: Madinat Zayed sits in central Abu Dhabi, close to Al Markaziyah and Al Danah, with the island's school network a short drive away. Finding somebody who advertises as an IGCSE tutor nearby takes minutes. Establishing whether that person has taught the board your child is entered for takes a conversation most families do not know how to have, and it is the conversation that decides whether the money produces marks.

The reason is that IGCSE is not one examination. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE cover overlapping content through different papers, with different tier names, different grade scales and different arrangements for science practical skills. Cambridge reports A* to G and splits several subjects into Core and Extended. Pearson reports 9 to 1 and splits mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Within Cambridge there are also separate syllabuses for the same subject, with Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 running different paper structures.

That means a tutor who has spent five years on Cambridge 0580 may be genuinely unfamiliar with Pearson 4MA1 question conventions, and a tutor who has taught Pearson science may not have seen a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper. Neither is a bad tutor. Both would be the wrong match for half the students in this catchment, and nothing on a profile page tells a parent which half they are looking at. The profile will say experienced IGCSE tutor, which is true in both cases and useful in neither, and a parent has no way to tell from the outside which board sits behind the claim.

Supply makes it harder. Abu Dhabi has many British-curriculum students and a finite number of adults who have taught any given syllabus recently, most of them in full-time employment with limited evening capacity, and professional-ethics rules are reported to bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school. The nearest advertised IGCSE tutor is therefore often the one who has never taught your child's code, and the one who has may be across the city or outside the emirate. None of that is visible from a listing, and it is why a parent is better served by a question than by a map. A single email to the school and ten minutes of questions to a tutor settle more than any amount of comparing profiles.

IB Gram deals with this by matching on the code and stating it, and by teaching one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time so that distance does not restrict the choice. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Where no specialist for a code is free, you are told, given a wait, and offered written alternatives rather than matched to whoever is available with the right-sounding job title.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-madinat-za.programmesIntro: Three routes matter for a Madinat Zayed family at this stage, and each sets a different requirement for a tutor's board knowledge.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with Core and Extended tiers in several subjects, A* to G grading, and science assessed through either an alternative-to-practical paper or a practical test depending on what the centre enters. Cambridge has revised assessment models including the balance of calculator and non-calculator papers, so the structure must be read at source for the series entered.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so a Madinat Zayed candidate sits June with November as the resit route. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1 and 4EA1, reported on the 9 to 1 scale, with mathematics tiered into Foundation, capped at grade 5, and Higher, running 9 down to 4 with a grade 3 safety net. Science practical skills are assessed inside the written papers in most routes rather than through a separate practical component.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs May and June and again November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and later revised, so plan from the live official version.

programmes.name: AS and A-Level, and the Diploma alternative
programmes.description: The two post-16 routes an IGCSE student moves into. A-Levels narrow to three or four subjects examined terminally; the IB Diploma takes six subjects with internal assessments and a 45-point total. The IGCSE grade and tier can close doors into either, which is why tier entry deserves attention in Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, plus five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-madinat-za.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are listed with the board distinction that matters for each, because that distinction is what a tutor either knows or does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Three codes, three paper structures. 0607 carries a graphics-calculator expectation and a different component mix from 0580; 4MA1 uses the 9 to 1 scale with Foundation capped at grade 5. A tutor should know which one your child sits before the first session, and which past papers follow from it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical paper or practical test; Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers. A tutor who has only taught one board may never have marked the other's experimental component, which is where a meaningful share of marks sits.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Similar content, different question conventions and different treatment of practical skills. Mole calculations and organic pathways dominate requests in this catchment, and qualitative analysis answers lose marks when the observation is omitted and only the conclusion is given.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy in both boards, with command terms deciding a large share of marks. The useful board-specific knowledge is how each one phrases extended-response questions and what its mark schemes reward in a six-mark answer.

subjects.name: English First Language
subjects.description: Summary writing, directed writing and reading comprehension, with coursework in some Cambridge routes. The examined skill is timed analysis rather than quantity of reading, and summary tasks lose marks when students quote instead of condensing.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate syllabus from First Language English, with 0511 carrying a speaking component. A student entered for this is assessed against different criteria, so preparing them as a first-language candidate wastes the hours entirely. Confirm the code before buying anything.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study papers where marks sit in application to the given business or economy rather than recited theory. Economics diagrams carry marks lost to missing labels, and evaluation questions need a judgement rather than two balanced paragraphs.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Skills questions on maps, graphs and data interpretation are entirely practisable and routinely under-practised. Case-study detail has to be specific: named places, figures and dates earn marks that general description does not.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based assessment where structure decides the mark. Candidates lose marks by describing a source rather than using it as evidence, and by writing narrative where an argument was required. Board-specific question stems matter here more than in most subjects.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two different subjects frequently confused by families. One is programming and computational theory; the other is applied software skills. Confirm which your child takes before looking for a tutor, because the required expertise barely overlaps.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Required in private schools regardless of the international curriculum, with separate class organisation for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. These sit on the timetable all year and are regularly the subjects a family plans around last.

subjects.name: Examination technique, board-specific

sections.heading: Answering the search, and the first thing to establish
paragraphs: Direct answer: an IGCSE home tutor in Madinat Zayed, through IB Gram, means a subject specialist matched to your child's board and syllabus code, teaching one-to-one over live video at an Abu Dhabi-friendly hour, with a free trial lesson used as a diagnosis. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. If someone physically in the room is the requirement, that is a different purchase and worth knowing now.

The first thing to establish is not a tutor but a fact: which board, which code, which tier, and for the sciences which practical route. One email to the examinations officer and the head of department produces all four. Until a family has that, every subsequent decision is provisional, including which past papers to download and whether the revision guide already on the shelf is the right one.

It is worth being blunt about how often this goes wrong. Families buy Cambridge revision guides for Pearson students, download 0580 papers for a 0607 candidate, and prepare a second-language English student as though they were sitting the first-language syllabus. None of those errors is detectable to a parent without the code, and none of them is caught by a tutor who was never told it.

Once the code is in hand, the question becomes whether a given tutor has taught it. That is testable in four questions, set out below, and the answers are specific or evasive within a few minutes. A family that runs those four will not confuse a confident tutor with a board-experienced one again, which protects every future booking as well as this one.
bullets: Get board, code, tier and practical route from the school in writing

sections.heading: The three-board problem, and why it is not a detail
paragraphs: In UAE schools three mathematics syllabuses dominate, and they are different examinations. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 tiers into Core and Extended on an A* to G scale. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 has its own paper structure and a graphics-calculator expectation. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, tiers into Foundation and Higher on the 9 to 1 scale, with Foundation capped at grade 5 and Higher running 9 down to 4 with grade 3 available as a safety net.

In the sciences the division is just as sharp. Cambridge 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology assess experimental skills through an alternative-to-practical paper or a practical test, depending on what the centre enters. Pearson 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 assess practical skills inside the written papers. A tutor who has only ever prepared students for one of these has never marked the other, and the experimental component is worth real marks.

In English the division is between syllabuses rather than boards. Cambridge 0500 and 0990 are First Language English; 0510 and 0511 are English as a Second Language, with 0511 carrying a speaking component. These are assessed against different criteria. In computing, Cambridge 0478 Computer Science and 0417 ICT are different subjects that families regularly conflate, and the expertise required barely overlaps.

None of this makes any tutor unqualified. It makes the word IGCSE insufficient as a description. A profile that says experienced IGCSE science tutor tells a parent nothing about whether this person has marked a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper, and that is the specific fact the family needs. The remedy is to ask for codes, which is why every tutor in our match is listed by code rather than by subject.

sections.heading: Four questions that establish board knowledge in ten minutes
paragraphs: A parent with no subject expertise can still test a tutor's board knowledge, because the answers are either concrete or they are not. Ask these four before paying anything, on a call or during the free trial lesson, and listen for whether the reply contains the examination or only reassurance.

First: which boards and syllabus codes have you taught, and in which years. A board specialist names codes without prompting. Second: how is practical work assessed in my child's board, and what does that paper ask for. A specialist describes the component precisely; a generalist talks about laboratory experience. Third: what are the tiers in this subject and what does each cap. A specialist knows whether Core or Foundation limits the grade and by how much. Fourth: show me where the marks are in a six-mark question in this board's scheme. A specialist can talk through the mark allocation; a generalist describes good writing.

There is a fifth, optional question that reveals a lot: which past papers should we be working from, and which should we stop using. A board specialist will tell you to put away the wrong-code materials on the shelf, which costs them nothing and saves the student weeks. A tutor who says all past papers are useful practice has not understood the problem this page describes.

Run these on us as well. The match we send states the tutor's codes, and the free trial lesson is where a family should spend ten of its sixty minutes on exactly these questions. A provider that resents the questions has told you something; a provider that has prepared for them has told you something better.

sections.heading: Who actually teaches each board in Abu Dhabi, and where the gaps are
paragraphs: Teacher supply follows school provision. Abu Dhabi has a large British-curriculum sector, so the overall pool of people who have taught IGCSE is reasonable, particularly for mathematics, the sciences and English. The gaps are narrower and more specific: a given code, in a given subject, during the weeks everybody wants it.

Cambridge coverage is generally better than Pearson coverage in this emirate, simply because more schools here have historically used Cambridge syllabuses, so more teachers have marked those papers. For Pearson codes the pool is thinner, and a family entered for 4MA1 or 4CH1 may need to look further than a family entered for 0580 or 0620. For Cambridge 0607 the pool is thinnest of all, because fewer schools use it.

Then there are the structural limits that apply regardless of board. Most experienced teachers are in full-time employment with limited evening capacity. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. And demand peaks in the same weeks every year, before mocks and before the June series.

The practical consequence for a Madinat Zayed family is to search by code and to search early. A booking made in October for a Year 11 student is a different experience from one attempted in April. If the code is unusual or the subject narrow, expect to be offered a tutor outside the emirate, and expect that to be stated rather than discovered.
