sections.heading: What to do when nobody is free, including the options that are not tutoring
paragraphs: Sometimes the right specialist is unavailable, and a good provider should say so and then name the alternatives, including the ones that make no money for anybody. There are more options here than families usually realise, and several of them are free.

The school is first. Most departments run clinics, revision sessions or drop-in help that families forget to ask about, and the teacher who marks the student's work knows the gap better than any external tutor. Second, peer study with a classmate sitting the same code: it costs nothing, and explaining a method to somebody else is one of the most efficient revision techniques available. Third, the student's own past-paper work marked against the published scheme, which is the single highest-value revision activity and requires no tutor at all once the student is shown how.

Then the paid options. A different qualified tutor on the same code at another time. A tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same board, disclosed before booking and scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. Shorter sessions at higher frequency as a stated holding pattern. A tuition centre group class, which is cheaper per hour and dilutes attention, and in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute to operate; ask about group size before agreeing. Or a named wait.

Publishing this list costs us bookings and is still correct. A family that gets a result from the school's own clinic will come back when the need is genuinely specialist, and a family sold an unsuitable tutor in a peak week will not come back at all. It is also the test of a provider: ask what we would recommend if you had no budget this term, and see whether an answer arrives.

sections.heading: Verifying the person before the first lesson
paragraphs: Competence and legitimacy are separate checks and both are quick. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified. Because the permit is free, a tutor without one has no cost excuse.

Beyond the permit, two claims should raise rather than lower suspicion. Nobody is an ADEK-approved or KHDA-approved tutor, because those bodies license and inspect schools rather than approving individuals. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval, a six-month completion window and annual renewal. And no tutor should be described as a Cambridge or Pearson examiner without evidence of current status, nor should examiner status be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

For completeness: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and no UAE office. We also publish no satisfaction percentages or star ratings, because a statistic without a sample size, a date and a method is not evidence, and two pages in this market show review totals that contradict each other.

sections.heading: Cost, starting from the cheapest competent option
paragraphs: A family worried about board specialism is often also worried that specialism means paying the top of the market. It does not. The cheapest competent option for many needs is free: the school's own clinic, a classmate on the same code, and self-marked past papers. Where paid help is right, the sensible entry point is the qualified band rather than the premium one.

Published figures read in October 2026: budget online tuition at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500; specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270; premium named or examiner-led tuition at AED 500 to 650 and above, BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly packages advertised include AED 799 for eight online sessions.

For IGCSE specifically, the qualified band at AED 150 to 300 covers nearly every genuine need: board-correct past-paper marking, tier judgement, alternative-to-practical technique and the extended-response work that separates grade bands. The premium band makes sense only where a family has already identified a narrow requirement precisely, and the budget band makes sense for supervision rather than teaching.

Two notes, as elsewhere on this site. These are market rates from named published sources, not IB Gram prices; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson once the code, tier and session length are known. And paying more does not improve a wrong-board match. A premium tutor working from the wrong past papers is the most expensive version of the exact problem this page exists to prevent.

sections.heading: Entries, zones and the resit route, for a candidate sitting here
paragraphs: Entries are made by the school as the examination centre, which means the school also controls tier deadlines and holds the correct timetable. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Work from the school's version, not a search result.

Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE and O Level, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only. A candidate in Madinat Zayed therefore sits June, with November as the resit route. A great deal of online advice is written for Indian candidates, and a revision plan built on a February window belongs to a different country.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates, cited so they can be checked, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables that are later revised, so plan from the live official version rather than a restatement.

The resit decision should be made from the component breakdown rather than from disappointment. Ask the examinations officer which paper and which question types lost the marks, check the actual grade requirement for the post-16 route, and then decide whether a November entry with targeted work would plausibly move it. A resit prepared the same way as the first attempt usually produces the same result.

sections.heading: What online delivery suits, and where it falls short
paragraphs: For IGCSE work the online format does the main job well. The correct board's past paper and its mark scheme sit open for both people. Working is built line by line in a shared space. An apparatus diagram can be annotated live. A six-mark answer can be marked in front of the student with the allocation explained. And the recording means the student can return to the explanation on the day the homework is actually attempted.

It falls short in three specific places, and they are worth naming rather than glossing. There is no person in the room, which matters most for younger students and those who struggle to stay engaged without presence. There is no laboratory; apparatus handling belongs to the school, and no private tutor in any format substitutes for it. And it cannot supply motivation a student does not have, which is true of in-home tuition as well but is easier to disguise there.

Where engagement is the actual problem, the fix is structural rather than format-based: shorter sessions more often, with smaller checkable tasks between them, and a parent who sees the weekly target rather than a general report. That is a scheduling change and it works in either format. A provider that responds to an engagement problem by selling longer sessions has misread it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. If you engage an independent in-home tutor in Abu Dhabi, ask for the MoHRE permit, ask the four board questions, and ask which past papers they intend to use. The three checks together take fifteen minutes and are the difference between buying teaching and buying a job title.

faqs.question: Does it really matter which board my child's IGCSE is with?
faqs.answer: Yes, enough to change what revision is useful. Cambridge and Pearson examine overlapping content through different papers, with different tier names, different grade scales and different arrangements for science practical skills. A student revising from the wrong board's past papers is practising question styles they will not meet, and in the sciences may be preparing for a component that does not exist in their board. Ask the school for the syllabus code in writing before buying any materials or booking any tutor.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor has taught my child's board?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which boards and syllabus codes have you taught, and in which years. How is practical work assessed in this board, and what does that paper ask for. What do the tiers cap in this subject. And where are the marks in a six-mark question in this board's scheme. A board specialist answers all four concretely; a generalist talks about laboratory experience and good writing. The difference is clear within ten minutes and needs no subject knowledge from you.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge International Mathematics the same as Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus 0607 and syllabus 0580 are separate Cambridge syllabuses with different paper structures, and 0607 carries a graphics-calculator expectation that 0580 does not. Both tier into Core and Extended and both appear in UAE schools, which is why the code rather than the board name is the thing to confirm. A student entered for 0607 revising from 0580 papers is preparing for the wrong examination, and the materials look convincingly correct to a parent.

faqs.question: Which boards are easiest to find a tutor for in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Cambridge codes generally, because more schools in this emirate have historically used them, so more teachers have marked those papers. Pearson codes such as 4MA1 and 4CH1 have a thinner pool here, and Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is thinnest of all because fewer schools use it. If your child is on an unusual code, expect to search beyond the district and expect to be offered a tutor outside the emirate, with the location stated before you book.

faqs.question: What free help should we try before paying for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Three things. The school's own clinic or revision session, because the teacher who marks the work knows the gap better than any outsider and these are often unadvertised. Peer study with a classmate on the same code and tier, since explaining a method is among the most efficient revision available. And the student's own past papers marked strictly against the published scheme, which is the single highest-value revision activity and needs no tutor once the student has been shown how to do it.

faqs.question: Our revision guide turned out to be for the wrong board. How much does that cost?
faqs.answer: Mostly time rather than money. The content overlap between boards is substantial, so the student has not learnt anything false, but they have practised the wrong question conventions and may have skipped a component their board actually examines. The fix is to put the wrong-code materials away, download the correct board's recent papers and schemes, and spend two or three sessions on the conventions that differ. A board specialist will tell you to do this unprompted.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches Cambridge handle a Pearson student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes well, sometimes not, and the honest answer depends on the subject. In mathematics the content overlap is large enough that a strong Cambridge tutor can adapt within a session or two, provided they work from Pearson papers. In the sciences the difference is structural, because the experimental component is assessed differently, so a tutor who has never seen that board's arrangement is at a real disadvantage. Ask which board's papers they intend to use, and listen to the answer.

faqs.question: Why is the nearest advertised tutor often the wrong one?
faqs.answer: Because proximity and board experience are unrelated. The adults advertising locally are the ones willing to travel to your district at the hour you want; the adults who have marked your child's board's papers are wherever they happen to live and work. On top of that, most experienced teachers are employed full-time with limited evening capacity, and professional-ethics rules are reported to bar school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which removes the nearest qualified person.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson need to establish for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Three things, and a parent should expect all of them in writing afterwards. Which specific errors are recurring, drawn from a marked paper rather than a conversation. Whether the tier looks right on that evidence, since Core and Foundation cap the grade available. And how many sessions the work genuinely needs, which should sometimes be two or three. If the lesson produces only encouragement and a recommended package, it has not diagnosed anything worth paying for.

faqs.question: Do we have to use the timetable the school gives us?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it matters more than families expect. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your child's school is the centre. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables that are later revised, so work from the live official version rather than a copy.

faqs.question: Can my child sit the February IGCSE exams to get an early result?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only. A candidate in Abu Dhabi sits the June series, with the November series available as the resit route, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. A good deal of advice online is written for Indian candidates and quotes a February window, so check that any plan you are given matches the series your school has actually entered your child for.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a tuition centre a reasonable alternative?
faqs.answer: It can be, with two questions asked first. How many students are in the group, because attention dilutes quickly beyond a handful and the per-hour saving stops being a saving. And what the centre's permit position is: an operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval, a six-month completion window and annual renewal. For board-specific technique work, one-to-one usually beats a group; for general content coverage, a small group can work.

faqs.question: How early should we book for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Term one, if the need is already visible. Demand peaks in the same weeks every year, before mock windows and before the June series, and the same board-experienced tutors are wanted across the city at once. A booking made in October is a different experience from one attempted in April, at the same rate. Starting early also means the first block can be diagnostic and unhurried rather than triage against a deadline that has already arrived.

faqs.question: What should I do if a tutoring company will not tell me where the tutor is based?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a reason to go elsewhere. The syllabus is identical wherever a tutor sits, so there is nothing to hide, and the only thing location genuinely changes is the available session times and local knowledge of your school's calendar. Several sites in this market route UAE families to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning it, and one shows a Dubai address on an Abu Dhabi page. The concealment is the problem rather than the geography.

intro.heading: Working out what IGCSE tuition will actually cost you
paragraphs: Almost every tutoring conversation in Abu Dhabi starts with an hourly rate, which is the least useful number available. An hourly rate tells you nothing about how many hours a Year 10 or Year 11 student actually needs, nothing about whether those hours are spent on the right paper, and nothing about the cost of discovering in March that the wrong board was being practised all along. Families in Masdar City, many of them working in energy, research and the free zone, tend to want the annual figure and the assumptions behind it.

So this page is built around money rather than reassurance. The published market rates are all here, named by the provider that quoted them, in dirhams and by tier. The monthly equivalents are here too, because a household budget runs monthly and a term is roughly four of those. The three common ways IGCSE tuition money gets wasted are set out explicitly, with what each one costs and how to spot it before the invoices stack up.

There is a geography point worth making first, because it affects the bill. Masdar City is a compact low-carbon district beside the airport, built around a university campus, a free zone and commercial offices. It has no private school inside it and its residential stock is apartments rather than villas, with parking held mostly at the district edge. A tutor driving in parks and walks at both ends of the hour, and that time is in the price whether or not it appears on the invoice.

Those two facts together explain the biggest single line item in the in-home option. The market quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Dubai rate table and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is travel. For a Masdar City address it buys a drive and a walk, and it also shrinks your choice of tutor to the people prepared to make that trip at five in the afternoon.

IB Gram's position is simple and worth stating before the tables. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Masdar City family the lesson happens over live video, one student and one teacher, with your child's own marked past papers on the screen. We target the home-tutor search because that is the phrase parents type, and then we answer it with the actual numbers rather than pretending the question was something else.

What follows, in order: monthly costs by tier, the three waste patterns, the board question that quietly decides whether your money is doing anything, the tier decision inside Cambridge subjects, what to ask about any quote, and the calendar that drives all of it. Nothing here is an IB Gram price list. Our fee is quoted after the free trial lesson, when there is a diagnosis to price against.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-masdar-cit.programmesIntro: Masdar City teenagers sit one of two IGCSE specifications, and a smaller group arrives from the Cambridge lower secondary route. The specification, not the year group, determines which papers are practised, so it is the first thing to establish before any money changes hands.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Identified by four-digit syllabus codes: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology. Several subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, which changes the grade ceiling and the paper set. Cambridge also assesses practical skills through a dedicated written paper in the sciences, which candidates with plenty of laboratory experience still answer badly.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge International runs its examinations for UAE centres in a June series and a November series. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your school's exams officer which zone it sits in before you plan a revision schedule.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Coded differently: 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology. Mathematics runs as two equally weighted papers with no coursework and a formula sheet that differs from Cambridge. Tiering does not map onto Cambridge's Core and Extended split, and the expected layout of a full-mark solution is not identical either.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and again in November. The pattern from the most recent completed cycle: the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, so read the official page rather than any summary.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, with Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. These years decide which tier a student is entered for, which in turn decides the grade ceiling, so they matter financially as well as academically. Work here is about algebraic fluency and written method rather than examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: This is where a Masdar City family can spend least and gain most. Support in Years 8 and 9 costs the same per hour as support in Year 11 but buys an entry tier rather than a rescue. A student entered for Extended because the groundwork was done has a higher ceiling available for the whole of IGCSE, and no amount of spending in Year 11 recovers a Core entry.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-masdar-cit.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Masdar City families pay for most often, with the component that decides the grade named in each. Use any one of them as an opening question to a prospective tutor: a specialist will discuss it without preparation.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson Edexcel 4MA1
subjects.description: The single most tutored subject in the emirate. Extended opens the top grade range and is what any student heading for A-level or Diploma mathematics needs. Marks go missing in algebraic fractions, graph transformations and the long multi-step questions late in the paper, where candidates abandon a question rather than bank the first two marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits do most of the damage, followed by anything requiring rearrangement of a formula under time pressure. The Cambridge practical-skills paper is answered poorly by students who have done the experiments but never been taught to write up uncertainty and error for a marker.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry separate grades, and they are a technique rather than a talent. Students who can balance equations and still cannot scale a calculation are missing one method, which is usually fixable in three or four sessions rather than a term.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem and command terms are the solution. Describe, explain and suggest demand different answers, and students who write everything they know on the topic score below students who answer the verb. Marked timed practice moves this faster than re-reading notes.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language and First Language English
subjects.description: Two different courses with different marking emphases, and families sometimes do not know which one their child is entered for. Directed writing and summary tasks reward format discipline: addressing the audience, the purpose and the word count is worth more than richer vocabulary.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A-level or Diploma mathematics and often added late. The calculus and trigonometry content is a genuine step up from 0580 Extended, and a student who was coasting on Extended will feel it immediately. Worth starting early rather than in the final two terms.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study papers reward structure. Candidates lose marks by describing a business situation rather than analysing it, and by never reaching an evaluative judgement where the question asked for one. The fix is a repeatable answer shape, taught in a handful of lessons.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Popular with Masdar City families given the district's technical employers. Pseudocode and trace tables cause more lost marks than programming does, because students solve the problem mentally and never write the intermediate steps the mark scheme is looking for.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education streams
subjects.description: These run alongside the international curriculum in UAE private schools by federal requirement, with separate classes organised by group and set languages of instruction. Support follows the school's own scheme of work, since additional or different content for the mandatory subjects needs Ministry permission.

sections.heading: The monthly number, not the hourly one
paragraphs: Convert everything into a monthly figure before you compare providers, because that is the number that lands in your account. Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session put a budget tutor at AED 240 to 600 a month, a mid-range tutor at AED 600 to 1,200, and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Those three bands are the entire decision for most families, and the difference between them over a two-year IGCSE course is substantial.

Package pricing in this market tells a similar story from the other direction. Published examples include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which works out well below the hourly rates advertised alongside it, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Both are real published figures. Notice that the in-home package buys eight contact hours for roughly twice the price of the online one, and that most of the difference is a car.

The arithmetic parents rarely do is the two-year one. An IGCSE course runs across Years 10 and 11, which is roughly eighteen teaching months. One subject at the mid band is somewhere around AED 10,800 to 21,600 across the course. Two subjects doubles it. That is a significant commitment, and it is the reason the waste patterns in the next section matter more than haggling over an hourly rate.

A sensible way to control it is to buy intensity where it changes an outcome rather than spreading it thin. One subject taught properly for a term beats three subjects seen fortnightly, because fortnightly contact becomes homework supervision by default. Masdar City families with two teenagers often run one subject each on consecutive evenings, which keeps one quiet room working twice and keeps the monthly figure predictable.

sections.heading: Three ways IGCSE tuition money gets wasted
paragraphs: The first and most expensive is paying for the wrong specification. A tutor who knows IGCSE mathematics generally but practises Cambridge 0580 questions with a Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 candidate is teaching real mathematics in the wrong format. The content overlaps enough that nobody notices for months. What differs is the paper structure, the formula sheet and the expected layout of a full-mark solution, and those are exactly what a tutor is for.

The second is paying for coverage when the problem is technique. A student who scores 55 per cent on a paper has usually not failed to learn half the syllabus; they have lost marks across many questions for a small number of repeating reasons. Re-teaching the whole course at AED 200 an hour is the most expensive possible response. Marking one paper properly and grouping the losses by cause costs one session and redirects the entire plan.

The third is buying frequency instead of focus. Three subjects at one fortnightly session each feels thorough and produces almost nothing, because a fortnightly hour has no continuity and degrades into checking homework. The same budget on one subject weekly produces a measurable change in that subject. Parents resist this because the weakest subject list has three items on it, but sequencing beats spreading.

There is a fourth, smaller leak worth naming: paying for travel you did not want. If the in-home option was chosen for supervision of a younger child, the premium is buying something real. If it was chosen because it seemed more serious, it is buying a car journey. For a Masdar City address with parking at the district edge, that is a particularly poor use of AED 50 to 200 an hour.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the question behind the invoice
paragraphs: Parents are often surprised that IGCSE is not one qualification. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel are separate boards with separate specifications, separate codes and separate papers, and a UAE school may use one for mathematics and the other for a science. The school's exams officer can confirm each subject in a single reply, and that reply is the most financially useful email you will send this year.

The differences that matter to a tutor are concrete. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, with different papers and a different grade ceiling; Pearson's tiering does not map onto that. The formula sheets differ. Cambridge assesses practical skills in the sciences through a dedicated written paper, which has its own technique. Mark schemes reward different levels of shown working, so the habit a tutor trains has to match the board being sat.

The calendars differ too, and this is where wrong information circulating online becomes expensive. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE centres. Its February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so a page quoting those dates to an Abu Dhabi parent is written for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May and June and November. Mixing those up wrecks a revision schedule.

If your child is moving between boards mid-course, which happens with school changes, that is the moment to pay for a specialist rather than a generalist. The content will mostly carry across. The paper craft will not, and a student who has learned to answer Cambridge questions well can lose marks on Pearson papers for reasons that have nothing to do with knowing the subject.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that changes the whole bill
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge subjects, the entry decision sets the grade ceiling. Core entry caps the available grades; Extended opens the top range and is what a student needs for A-level or Diploma progression in that subject. Schools make this decision from classroom evidence, typically in Year 10, and once an entry is made the ceiling is fixed regardless of what is spent afterwards.

That makes the financial logic of tutoring unusual. Money spent in Years 8, 9 and early 10 buys an entry tier. Money spent in the final two terms of Year 11 buys marks within a tier already chosen. The second is useful and is what most families buy. The first is cheaper per unit of outcome and almost nobody buys it, because the problem is not visible yet.

A Masdar City parent with a Year 9 student therefore has an option that a parent of a Year 11 student does not. A single term of focused work on algebraic fluency and written method, at mid-band rates, can be the difference between an Extended and a Core entry. The same spend a year later cannot change the entry at all.

If the entry has already been made at Core and the student is clearly capable of more, that is a conversation with the school rather than with a tutor. Schools can and do move students between tiers where the evidence supports it, but the evidence has to come from classwork and internal assessments. A tutor can help generate that evidence; a tutor cannot change an entry.

sections.heading: What a quote should tell you, and what to ask when it does not
paragraphs: A tutoring quote in this market is often a single hourly number with nothing attached. That is not enough to compare two providers, and the missing details are where the surprises live. Ask whether the price is per hour or per lesson, and how long a lesson is, because a 45-minute lesson quoted as an hourly rate is a 33 per cent increase in disguise.

Ask whether the quoted figure includes value added tax, and get the answer in writing. We do not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees as a general fact, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than a tutoring company's opinion. What any provider can and should tell you is whether the number they quoted you is the number you will pay.

Ask about cancellation, replacement and what happens after one lesson. If a tutor is unavailable for three weeks, is the slot held, refunded or filled by somebody else? If the match does not work, is there a replacement at no cost or a notice period to serve? These questions cost nothing to ask and they separate organised providers from improvised ones.

Finally, ask whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat a quoted penalty figure as unverified.

sections.heading: The in-home premium, priced for a district with edge parking
paragraphs: Masdar City is a useful place to examine the in-home premium, because the district makes the hidden costs visible. It is pedestrian-first by design. Vehicle access and parking sit largely at the perimeter, so a visiting tutor parks and walks at both ends of the hour. That is ten or fifteen minutes each way, unpaid in theory and priced in practice.

Add the drive itself. A tutor coming from Khalifa City, Mohammed Bin Zayed City or further is spending forty to sixty minutes in a car for a sixty-minute lesson. No supplier absorbs that indefinitely. It appears either as a higher hourly rate, which is what the AED 180 to 500 band reflects, or as a minimum booking of ninety minutes or two hours, which is what the AED 1,599 to 1,799 monthly packages reflect.

Apartment living adds a second constraint that nobody prices at all. A home visit assumes a room where an adult can work with a teenager undisturbed for an hour while the household continues. In a two or three bedroom apartment that room is usually occupied. Families discover this in week two and start moving the lesson to the kitchen table, which is not what the premium was for.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, so there is nothing to defend here; that service runs in India only. The comparison matters because it is the choice a Masdar City family is actually making. The same qualified teaching, delivered over live video at AED 150 to 300 an hour, draws on every specialist in the network rather than the subset willing to drive to the district edge at five in the afternoon.

sections.heading: Exam entries, equivalency and the costs nobody mentions
paragraphs: Tuition is not the only education cost attached to an IGCSE year, and the others shape when tutoring is worth buying. Entries are made by the school against the board's deadline, and the deadline sits months before the paper. Confirming subject, tier and board in writing with the exams officer is free and prevents the most expensive mistake available, which is a student prepared for a paper they are not entered for.

For context on fees generally, the Dubai authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi runs its own fee regime through ADEK. Neither affects a tutoring budget directly, but both matter if you are modelling total education spend across a Diploma or A-level pathway.

Then there is equivalency, which Masdar City families planning UAE university entry should understand early. On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A competitor page ranking for these queries says six subjects; five is what the official clarification states.

Equivalency is a Ministry process. IB Gram does not perform it, guarantee it or submit anything on your behalf, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. We mention it because a subject choice made in Year 9 can affect it, and a parent who knows the rule chooses the option block differently from a parent who does not.

sections.heading: What the free trial lesson is actually testing
paragraphs: A free trial is only worth something if it tests the right thing, and most do not. A trial that consists of a friendly chat about goals tests nothing. The trial should be a real lesson on a real piece of your child's work, because that is the only way to find out whether this tutor can teach this student this specification.

Three things should come out of it. First, a diagnosis: which marks are being lost and why, stated specifically rather than as a comment about confidence. Second, a view from your child, who has to spend an hour a week with this person and whose opinion is a better predictor of progress than any credential. Third, a short written note you can read afterwards, so the diagnosis exists in a form you can check against later.

What a trial cannot tell you is whether a grade will move, and any provider implying otherwise at that stage is guessing. What it can tell you is whether the tutor knows the specification, whether they can explain where the marks went, and whether your child engaged. Those three signals predict the next three months reasonably well.

Our trial carries no payment and no package, and if the match is wrong we change the tutor rather than asking you to persevere. That is not generosity, it is economics: a mismatched pairing produces no results, the family leaves, and everybody has wasted a term. Saying no after a trial costs you nothing, which is exactly what makes the trial informative.

process.title: Confirm the board and tier in writing
process.description: Email your child's exams officer and ask for the syllabus code and tier for each subject: Cambridge 0580 Extended, Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher, and so on. This single reply prevents the most expensive mistake in the market, which is a term of lessons practising the wrong paper format. It takes a day and costs nothing.

process.title: Decide the monthly number first
process.description: Work out what you can commit for the whole course rather than for a month, then choose intensity to fit. One subject weekly at the mid band is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month on published estimates. Knowing that figure before you talk to any provider stops a sales conversation from setting your budget for you.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: Not a report, not a summary. A returned past paper or mock with the marks on it. The first useful act is grouping those lost marks by cause, which routinely shows the problem is narrower and cheaper than feared: one topic, one command term, one habit in how working is set out.

process.title: Take the free trial and judge the hour
process.description: One real lesson on real work, no payment, no package. Listen for whether the tutor can name where the marks went and what the board expects. Read the written note afterwards. Your child gets a vote, and if the answer is no, we change the tutor rather than asking you to give it time.

process.title: Review every four to six weeks against the school's assessments
process.description: Progress is measured against your child's own school data, not our plan. If the next block should be paper technique rather than content, we change it. If the problem is solved, we reduce the frequency and say so, because a slot kept warm for the sake of continuity is money doing nothing.

whyPoints.title: Every price here carries its source
whyPoints.description: Each dirham figure on this page names the provider or rate table that published it and the tier it applies to, read in October 2026. Three of the six competitor pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars to families who pay in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: Specification matched before anything else
whyPoints.description: We establish the board, code and tier before matching a tutor, because a specialist on the wrong specification is an expensive way to learn real mathematics in the wrong format. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers, tier differently and reward different working.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium in the rate
whyPoints.description: Lessons are delivered over live video, so nothing in your price pays for a drive from Khalifa City or a walk in from the Masdar City perimeter. The same budget buys more teaching time, and the pool of specialists available to your child is not limited to those willing to make the journey.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you when to stop
whyPoints.description: A four-session diagnostic block is a legitimate purchase and sometimes the only one needed. If the plan your child leaves with can be followed without us, we say that instead of selling a term. A provider that never recommends less is not giving you advice.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated up front
whyPoints.description: When no UAE-based specialist is free for a subject, we say so at the enquiry and offer a network specialist teaching the same specification in Gulf Standard Time. You decide knowing the arrangement. Several providers in this market let families discover it afterwards, which is the part that damages trust.

whyPoints.title: Regulator facts, no borrowed credibility
whyPoints.description: We explain what ADEK, KHDA, SPEA and MoHRE each govern, because knowing which applies to your child is useful. We claim approval, accreditation or partnership from none of them, because IB Gram holds none. Implying otherwise is the commonest trust failure in UAE tutoring copy.

faqs.question: What should a Masdar City family budget each month for IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: On published estimates, one hour a week costs AED 240 to 600 a month with a budget tutor, AED 600 to 1,200 with a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist support in an exam year. Package pricing seen in this market includes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Most families with a Year 10 or Year 11 student land in the middle band for one subject. Two subjects roughly doubles the figure, which is why sequencing subjects usually beats running three at once.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor travel into Masdar City for lessons?
faqs.answer: Some in the market will, at a price. IB Gram will not, because we do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only. Masdar City is pedestrian-first with parking largely at the perimeter, so a visiting tutor parks and walks at both ends of the hour on top of the drive. The market quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online, and the difference is travel rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Why does the IGCSE exam board my child sits change the price I should pay?
faqs.answer: It does not change the rate, but it changes whether the money does anything. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are separate boards with separate codes, different tiering, different formula sheets and mark schemes that reward different amounts of shown working. A tutor practising Cambridge 0580 papers with a Pearson 4MA1 candidate is teaching genuine mathematics in the wrong format, and nobody notices for months. Confirm the code with the exams officer before paying for a single hour.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start IGCSE tutoring in Year 9 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 9 costs the same per hour and buys more. In tiered Cambridge subjects the entry decision sets the grade ceiling, and schools make it from classroom evidence around Year 10. Work on algebraic fluency and written method before that decision can be the difference between a Core and an Extended entry, which no amount of spending in Year 11 recovers. Year 11 tutoring buys marks inside a tier already chosen, which is useful but a narrower purchase.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does an IGCSE student actually need?
faqs.answer: For one subject, one hour a week through a term is the smallest arrangement that reliably changes anything, with practice happening between lessons. Fortnightly contact tends to degrade into homework checking because there is no continuity. In the four to eight weeks before a series, two or three shorter sessions a week on paper technique is more effective than one long one. More than that in a single subject usually means the problem was misdiagnosed rather than large.

faqs.question: What questions should I ask before accepting a tutoring quote in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Four. Is the price per hour or per lesson, and how many minutes is a lesson? Is the figure quoted the figure I will be charged? What happens if the tutor is unavailable or the match does not work, and is a replacement free? And does the tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? That permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Masdar City parents spend the most on?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, by a wide margin, then physics and chemistry. Mathematics attracts the spend because it gates A-level and Diploma progression and because the losses are visible in a mark. Physics follows because electricity and formula rearrangement defeat students who understand the ideas. Chemistry because moles and stoichiometry are a method rather than a talent. Given the district's technical employers, computer science requests are higher here than the emirate average, usually around pseudocode and trace tables.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach two IGCSE subjects to the same child?
faqs.answer: Often, and it can reduce the total bill while improving continuity. Mathematics with physics is the pairing that works most reliably, because the algebra underpins the physics. Chemistry with biology is common. Mathematics with English almost never sits with the same specialist. If the combination is not available we say so rather than putting a generalist on both subjects, because one strong specialist plus a second specialist beats two adequate matches on price-per-mark.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams held for a student at an Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs its examinations for UAE centres in a June series and a November series, with November serving as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge's February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so any page quoting February dates to an Abu Dhabi parent is written for a different country. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used.

faqs.question: How long after the exams do Pearson Edexcel results reach a UAE student?
faqs.answer: The pattern from the most recent completed cycle is the best guide. June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Those are backward-looking citations, which is what makes them checkable. For an upcoming sitting, read the board's own provisional and final timetable pages, because dates can be revised.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper tutor mean a worse result for my child?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but the bands buy different things. At AED 33 to 65 an hour you are buying supervision: someone to keep a student working through practice. That is genuine value for a Year 8 who will not start homework alone. At AED 150 to 300 you are buying teaching of the specification by someone who knows it. At AED 200 to 450 and above you are buying paper technique and criterion-level feedback. Matching the band to the actual problem matters more than the band itself.

faqs.question: Is online IGCSE tuition as effective for a Year 11 student as someone in the room?
faqs.answer: For exam-course work, usually yes. Both people annotate the same past paper, the tutor can see the working as it happens, and the session can be recorded for revision. Two conditions have to hold: a quiet hour and a stable connection, and in an apartment the first is the harder one. For a much younger child who needs physical presence to stay on task the answer is different, and we would say so rather than sell a format that will not work.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the Ministry equivalency count require?
faqs.answer: Five. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor page states six, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry process and no tutoring company performs or guarantees it.

faqs.question: Can we pause lessons during school holidays without losing the slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, with notice. A paused slot is held where the tutor's schedule allows, and we would rather pause than take money for sessions that will be half-attended across a long break. Some families use holidays the other way, running an intensive block when there is no homework competing for the evening, which is usually the best value week of the year. Either approach works; what does not work is drifting into a month of cancelled lessons nobody formally stopped.

faqs.question: What does the free trial lesson tell me that a profile page cannot?
faqs.answer: Three things. Whether the tutor can name where your child's marks are going, specifically, rather than commenting on confidence. Whether your child will talk to them, which predicts progress better than any credential. And whether the tutor knows the specification, which you can test by asking about the paper structure of the exact course. It carries no payment and no package, and if the answer is no, we change the tutor rather than asking you to persevere.

faqs.question: Is any particular grade outcome promised in return for the fee?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honest offers one. A grade depends on the student's work between lessons, the school's teaching, the tier they were entered for and how the papers go on the day. What we commit to is a named specialist on the correct specification, a diagnosis you can read, a written note after each lesson, review against your child's own school assessments, and a free trial before you pay. A provider promising a specific outcome in advance is selling certainty nobody in this market can produce.

With those two numbers you can compare quotes properly instead of being priced by whoever calls back first. Then send us the code, the tier, one marked paper and the evening windows that survive the school run. We will tell you what we would attack first, how long it should take, and what the free trial lesson will cover.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, a long commute, and one usable hour: planning IGCSE support in MBZ City
paragraphs: Mohammed Bin Zayed City is a large grid of residential zones on the mainland, and the school run out of it goes in several directions at once. Some children travel a few minutes to a school inside the community. Others go out towards Khalifa City and Al Raha, and a significant number cross onto the island for British-track secondary. The bus that serves three zones before it reaches yours is the single biggest variable in whether a tutoring arrangement survives a term.

The second variable is subject count. A Year 11 student here is commonly entered for eight to ten IGCSE subjects. That is a different planning problem from a Diploma student with six, because the family cannot buy support for all of it and should not try. Parents who book maths, physics and chemistry simultaneously in October generally run out of both money and child before the series arrives. The useful work is triage: three subjects where paid hours change the grade, and a plan for the rest that does not involve paid hours at all.

Those two variables interact badly with in-home delivery. A tutor driving to MBZ City from Khalidiyah or Al Reem Island has to leave before the traffic builds, which fixes the slot at a time your child may not be home, and it prices the journey into the hour. Market figures for in-home one-to-one in Abu Dhabi run AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 UAE survey, with independents reaching AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The gap is the drive.

Online delivery does not shorten the commute, but it stops the commute determining the timetable. A household whose child is home by 15:50 can hold a 16:15 slot. A household on a long route towards the island can hold a slot after 20:00 and keep it, because moving a session to the next evening costs nobody a journey. Both windows are available at the same rate, which is not true when somebody has to arrive.

This page is built around those practicalities. It sets out the realistic session windows from an MBZ City address, a triage method for a nine-subject week, what the November series is actually for and how to decide a resit before the first result lands, the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons that compete for the same evenings, and the Cambridge zone timetable rule that catches families every year. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India, and that position is identical on every country page we publish. What arrives at your child's desk is a shared whiteboard with their own worksheet open on it, not a car at the gate, and the practical consequence is that a slot can move without anybody rebuilding a route across the mainland.

Paper structure, question phrasing and formula provision all differ from Cambridge, so past-paper practice from the other board teaches the content in the wrong format.

programmes.description: Mohammed Bin Zayed City has a high share of mid-school transfers, often from Indian or Ministry curriculum schools into British-track provision. The arriving student usually has strong procedural mathematics and little experience of extended written answers, command terms or the style of structured science questions that an IGCSE paper uses.

The work is command terms, answer structure and paper technique rather than content, and the cheapest time to do it is the term after the transfer. abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-mohammed-b.subjectsIntro: With eight to ten subjects on a timetable, the question is not which subjects matter but which respond to paid hours. These notes say what each subject actually rewards, so triage can be done on evidence rather than on which teacher sent the most worrying email.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Responds strongly to tutoring because the lost marks are diagnosable per topic. Circle theorems, trigonometry with a drawn diagram and histograms with unequal intervals are compact and reliably examined, so they return more marks per hour than general revision.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Responds well, and usually for mathematical reasons rather than conceptual ones. Electricity and electromagnetism cost the most marks; after that it is uncertainty handling and graph gradients in the practical paper, plus units and significant figures.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic pathways decide the grade and both are teachable in a short block. The paper also rewards exact wording, so a student with the right idea and loose language is losing marks that precision recovers quickly.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Often the lowest-priority science for paid hours, because the content is learnable independently. The exception is extended-response structure on transport, homeostasis and inheritance, which is a short, high-value piece of teaching.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences in a double award, with specific sub-topics cut rather than everything simplified. A tutor working from the single-science syllabus wastes hours on content this course does not assess, so the syllabus version has to be confirmed first.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Responds to technique rather than reading. Directed writing and the extended reading response carry the paper, and marks go to candidates who address audience, form and purpose explicitly, which the mark scheme credits and most students ignore.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The highest-yield English option for paid hours, because the exercises are formulaic and highly trainable. Most of the available improvement sits in exam technique and timing rather than in general language ability.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Both assessed on application. Business Studies is entirely case-study driven, so practice must use real inserts. Students who revise definitions collect the smallest share of available marks and are often surprised by the mock.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Splits into theory and a practical programming element, and students are usually strong in one and weak in the other. Identifying which half is failing takes one session and determines whether paid hours are worth spending at all.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside any licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, and a subject where consistent short practice beats intensive blocks. It competes directly for the same evening hours that pre-examination science revision needs.

sections.heading: What the MBZ City commute does to a four o'clock session
paragraphs: Start from the bus, not the bell. Secondary schools serving these communities finish somewhere between 14:45 and 15:30, but a route that collects several Mohammed Bin Zayed City zones completes considerably later than that, and the last stop on a route can be forty minutes behind the first. Children travelling to island schools are in traffic in the returning direction at the worst time of the afternoon. A realistic home-arrival range across the community is 15:45 to 17:15, depending almost entirely on where in the grid you live.

That single fact explains most failed tutoring arrangements here. A family books 16:00 because it sounds right, the child is home at 16:40 for half of the term, the session runs short or late twice, and by the third cancellation the arrangement has effectively ended. The fix is to measure before booking: note actual arrival times for a week, then set the slot thirty minutes after the latest of them, or give up on the afternoon and take the evening window instead.

In-home delivery cannot flex around this. A tutor driving from the Corniche or Al Reem Island has to leave early enough to arrive, which fixes their availability to a single slot in the community, and the economics require them to fill it. Online, both windows exist at one rate, and a session that misses its start can move to the next evening without anybody recalculating a route. For a community with the journey profile of MBZ City, that flexibility is worth more than any individual tutor's reputation.

sections.heading: Triaging a nine-subject week
paragraphs: A Year 11 student entered for nine subjects cannot be tutored in nine subjects, and attempting it produces a tired child and an exhausted budget by February. Triage is the skill, and it is done on evidence rather than on which department has sent the most concerned email. The raw material is the set of marked mock scripts, which almost every family has and almost nobody reads carefully across subjects at the same time.

Rank the subjects on three questions. First, how far is the current mark from the target, in grade boundaries rather than percentages? A subject two marks below a boundary is a better investment than one twenty marks below. Second, is the loss diagnosable per topic, or is it spread evenly across the paper? Concentrated losses respond to tutoring; evenly spread losses usually mean the content was never learned and need a different remedy. Third, does the subject reward technique? English as a Second Language and mathematics do, strongly. Biology rewards independent learning more than paid hours.

The output should be a short written ranking: one or two subjects with a weekly slot, one or two with a short block and then nothing, and the rest left alone with a revision plan the student runs themselves. That is an uncomfortable conversation, because it means deciding that a subject will land where it lands. It is also the difference between a budget that changes three grades and one that changes none, and it is a conversation worth having in October rather than in April.

sections.heading: What the November series is actually for
paragraphs: Most UAE families treat the June series as the examination and November as a failure route, which wastes a genuinely useful option. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, and Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Both are full sittings. A student can be entered for a subject in November deliberately, to spread an unmanageable nine-subject load across two sittings rather than taking everything at once.

The resit case is also better handled early than late. Pearson's documented timings show why: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. By the time a June result arrives, a November entry decision has to be made quickly, and the student has been out of the subject for the whole summer. Families who decide in advance what result would trigger a November entry handle that week far better than families who start the conversation when the envelope opens.

One thing to be clear about: the February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates do not sit it, and any revision plan or tutoring package built around a spring sitting is built on another country's calendar. If a provider offers you a February entry for a child in Abu Dhabi, that is a reason to stop the conversation. Check your child's own exam centre's zone timetable, because clash dates and session windows differ between Cambridge's six administrative zones.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the week that is already full
paragraphs: Any honest plan for an MBZ City week has to account for the mandatory UAE subjects, which no competitor page in this market mentions. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why an international timetable in Abu Dhabi carries lessons a British timetable elsewhere does not, and why the evening has less room than parents assume.

Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed public account of how this is organised, and although KHDA's guidance governs Dubai schools, the structure it describes is the one families meet across the country. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with the advice that a mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes.

The consequence for planning is direct. After-school Arabic or Quran classes commonly occupy exactly the window a family had earmarked for maths, and Arabic itself rewards short, frequent practice rather than the intensive blocks that work for pre-examination science. Map the whole week before booking anything. Households that do this find one window that holds for a term; households that book the science slot first are renegotiating by week three, and renegotiated slots are the ones that quietly disappear.

sections.heading: Where the money goes, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most families actually start. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. Those rates buy a capable university student and are genuinely useful for homework accountability and keeping a reluctant student working. They are not useful for moving a grade boundary in Extended chemistry, and families who try tend to conclude that tutoring does not work rather than that they bought the wrong thing.

The next step is a qualified subject tutor working online, at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that sit IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's survey reaching AED 450 and beyond. Premium named tutors go higher again, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home delivery sits across the middle of that range with the journey added: AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's survey, independents to AED 500.

For an MBZ City household the practical reading is simple. A budget platform for accountability plus one mid-band specialist hour on the single subject that matters usually beats three in-home hours at the same total spend, and it survives the commute better. None of these figures is an IB Gram price list; they are what the market publishes, with sources attached so you can check them. Our own quote follows the free trial lesson, because a rate quoted before anybody has met your child is a guess with a number on it.

sections.heading: The honesty boundary, stated before you ask
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less independent coursework than the Diploma, but the boundary still matters and it is tested earlier than families expect. Some subjects carry coursework or practical components, and every school in this corridor runs originality checks as routine. A paid piece of writing that reads nothing like a student's class work is noticed immediately, and the consequence falls on the student. No tutor should write, draft or edit to submission any part of an assessed component, at any price or any deadline.

The related trap is past papers and mark schemes. Official syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, and reproducing or supplying them as downloads is copyright infringement. A tutor should reference them and link the official source. A provider offering a bundle of mark schemes as a selling point is telling you something about how else they treat rules, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure as well.

What a tutor should be paid for is clear enough to list. Teaching the content that was never learned. Marking a full paper properly against the published scheme and writing down which mark was lost and why. Drilling the technique that converts knowledge into marks. Teaching timing. Explaining command terms so an explain question is not answered with a description. All of that is legitimate, all of it moves grades, and none of it requires anybody to cross a line that puts a student's certificate at risk.

sections.heading: Starting without losing the first month
paragraphs: Most of the waste in tutoring happens in the first four sessions, and the cause is almost always that nobody looked at a script. A family describes the problem in general terms, the tutor starts from the beginning of the syllabus, and four paid hours pass before the actual lost marks are identified. Sending the marked mock before the trial hour fixes this for nothing, and it is the single most useful thing a parent can do.

For an MBZ City household, send four things: the board and syllabus code with the tier, the school name, the marked mock scripts for the subjects you are considering, and the real arrival times for a week rather than the school's finishing time. The last of those sounds trivial and determines whether the slot you choose survives. Then take the free trial hour over live video, with no card details taken and no commitment created.

After that, keep the arrangement narrow. One or two weekly slots, chosen from the triage ranking, with the rest of the subjects on a revision plan the student runs. Ask for a short written note after each session so progress is visible without interrogating your child at dinner. Review after four sessions against the mock that started it. If the targeted marks are not coming back, change the tutor, the subject or the diagnosis, and say so in week five rather than at the end of the term.
