faqs.question: What time can tutoring start for a child travelling home to MBZ City?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the route rather than the school. A child at a school inside the community can usually start by 15:45 to 16:00. A route out to Khalifa City or Al Raha pushes that to 16:15 or 16:45. A child crossing to an island school is often not home until 16:30 to 17:15, in which case the dependable slot is after 20:00. Measure actual arrival times for a week before choosing, and set the session thirty minutes after the latest of them rather than the average.

faqs.question: My child sits nine IGCSE subjects. How many should we tutor?
faqs.answer: One or two with a weekly slot, and perhaps one more with a short block that then stops. Nine parallel arrangements exhaust the budget and the child by February and typically move no grades. Rank the subjects from the marked mocks on three questions: how close is the mark to a grade boundary, are the losses concentrated in a few topics or spread evenly, and does the subject reward technique. Subjects that are learnable independently, and subjects already comfortably above target, should be left alone.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects give the best return on paid hours?
faqs.answer: Mathematics and English as a Second Language, consistently, because the lost marks are diagnosable and the exercises are highly trainable. Physics and chemistry follow, where electricity, moles calculations and organic pathways are compact blocks with reliable examination value. Biology usually gives less, because the content is learnable independently and only the extended-response structure needs teaching. Subjects where losses are spread evenly across the whole paper need content recovery rather than tutoring, which is a different and slower piece of work.

faqs.question: Is the November series only for resits?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge runs full June and November series, and Pearson runs May/June and November, so November is a complete sitting rather than a repair route. It can be used deliberately to split an unmanageable nine-subject load across two sessions, or for a subject missed after a mid-year transfer. It is also the fastest route for a grade that falls just below a university requirement. Decide in advance which result would trigger a November entry, because once the June result arrives the decision has to be made in days.

faqs.question: Can my child sit the February or March IGCSE series in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers the February and March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Any revision plan or tutoring package built around a spring sitting is built on another country's calendar, and a provider offering a February entry to a child in Abu Dhabi has told you something useful about their accuracy. Check your own school's zone timetable too, since Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones.

faqs.question: How much does in-home IGCSE tuition cost around MBZ City?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 UAE survey puts in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to 350 an hour across Abu Dhabi, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. A qualified online subject tutor sits at AED 150 to 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. Budget platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65. The gap between online and in-home is largely the journey, and from these communities the journey is long in both directions. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson and delivers online rather than at any UAE address.

faqs.question: Is a cheap online platform a waste of money?
faqs.answer: Not if you buy it for what it does. At AED 33 to 65 an hour, a budget platform provides accountability, routine and someone to keep a reluctant student working, which is genuinely valuable and much cheaper than a specialist. What it will not do is move a grade boundary in Extended chemistry or fix board-specific paper technique. Families who buy it expecting that conclude tutoring does not work, when they actually bought the wrong tier. Pairing a budget platform for routine with one mid-band specialist hour is a sensible combination.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to houses in Mohammed Bin Zayed City?
faqs.answer: Local independent tutors do, and the market prices the journey accordingly, which is why in-home quotes from the island or the Corniche run high for these zones. IB Gram is not among them: there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE from us, and visiting tutors are a service offered only in India. Lessons for MBZ City households run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is also why both the afternoon and late-evening windows are available at the same rate.

faqs.question: My child transferred from another curriculum into IGCSE. What needs fixing first?
faqs.answer: Answer structure and command terms, before content. Students transferring from Indian or Ministry curriculum schools usually arrive with solid procedural mathematics and little experience of extended written answers or of structured science questions that ask for explanation rather than recall. An explain question answered with a description earns a fraction of the credit, however well the student knows the material. That gap is specific, closes faster than families expect, and is cheapest to address in the term after the move rather than during Year 11 revision.

faqs.question: Does the after-school Arabic class affect when we can book?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and almost no provider raises it. Arabic is mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and after-school Arabic or Quran classes commonly occupy the 17:00 window families assume is free. Arabic also rewards short frequent practice, which competes with the evening hours a pre-examination science plan needs. Map the whole week before booking anything. Families who do find one window that holds for a term; families who book the science slot first are renegotiating by week three and drifting by week six.

faqs.question: Should a tutor supply past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: They should reference and link the official sources, not hand over bundles. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement; for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. A provider advertising a package of mark schemes as a selling point has told you how they treat rules generally. What a tutor should do is mark your child's attempt against the published scheme and write down which mark was lost and why.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the losses are content or technique?
faqs.answer: Read the marked script with the pattern in mind. If marks are missing from whole questions left blank or abandoned halfway, that is usually content or timing. If marks are missing from questions where the answer is broadly right but the credit was withheld, that is technique: no working shown, a command term misread, units omitted, or an explanation given where analysis was asked for. The two need different remedies, and a tutor who cannot tell you which it is after one session with the script is not reading it carefully.

faqs.question: Can we pause tutoring during school examination weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, though a short technique review often serves better than a pause. School examination weeks are when a student has the most immediate evidence of what is failing, and a thirty-minute session going over a just-sat paper is worth more than a full hour of new content. There is no rolling term to exit and no fee attached to a break, and because nobody is travelling to an MBZ City address a paused slot can be resumed in its original place without renegotiating anybody's route.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE tutor be matched for these communities?
faqs.answer: For mainstream codes, usually within a few days, because online delivery means the pool is not limited to tutors willing to drive out here. Coordinated Sciences 0654, Computer Science 0478 and Arabic as a first language take longer, as does any request tied to one narrow evening slot in the weeks before a series, when tutors who know a code well are already committed. You are told which case applies rather than given a fast general match that produces repeated diagnosis later.

faqs.question: What if we only want help for the final eight weeks?
faqs.answer: That is a legitimate and often efficient plan, provided the eight weeks start from a marked paper rather than from the beginning of the syllabus. Two or three sessions a week on one or two subjects, each ending with a timed section, with the topic list drawn from the lost marks in the most recent mock. Book it a term ahead if you can: the specialists who know a specific code are committed early, and families who start looking after the spring mocks are choosing from whoever is left.

Measure real arrival times for a week, rank the subjects from the marked mocks, and confirm the board, code and tier before any revision is planned. Then send the scripts and take the free trial hour over live video, with no card details and no commitment. Keep it to one or two subjects, and review after four sessions.

intro.heading: The question underneath the search
paragraphs: Parents in Mussafah rarely want a tutor who lives nearby for its own sake. They want certainty that the person sitting with their child has read the same syllabus the school is teaching from, has marked papers against that board's scheme, and will not spend six weeks teaching a structure the examiner does not reward. Proximity is a proxy for that certainty, and it is a poor one.

The honest supply picture for this part of Abu Dhabi is worth stating plainly. Mussafah's residential Shabiya districts sit south of the island, away from the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor where most international-curriculum schools and most specialist tutors are concentrated. Within a short drive of Shabiya the schools are mainly Indian and British curriculum, and the local tutoring pool reflects that. For Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 you will find people. For Pearson 4PH1 Physics, or Cambridge 0625 taught to the practical-method questions, or a Business Studies case-study paper marked to scheme, the pool thins quickly. That is a supply fact about this corner of the emirate rather than a judgement about the tutors who work here, and it is the reason a radius search produces such uneven results from a Shabiya address.

What makes this fixable is that syllabus knowledge does not need to be local. A tutor who teaches Cambridge 0620 Chemistry every week of the year knows where candidates lose marks on electrolysis questions whether they are in Shabiya or in Sharjah. A tutor selected because they will drive to Mussafah on a Tuesday evening knows whatever they happen to know. Those are different purchases, and the first one is what parents actually mean when they type the search. The distinction is worth holding on to, because it is the one that decides whether six weeks of paid sessions move a grade or simply fill an evening.

There is a specific trap in this district worth naming early. Mussafah households often have children in more than one system — one at an Indian-curriculum school nearby, one at a British-curriculum school in Khalifa City — and a tutor hired for the first is frequently asked to help the second. CBSE Class 10 mathematics and Cambridge 0580 Extended overlap in content and diverge completely in paper structure, command terms and mark-scheme behaviour. A competent CBSE tutor teaching 0580 without having read the syllabus will produce correct mathematics and mid-band marks.

IB Gram works as a matching platform, and for families in the UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Emirates; home visits are a service offered only in India. That means the match is made from everyone who teaches the syllabus rather than from everyone who can reach the postcode, and it is the reason this page can answer the syllabus question with a yes.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-mussafah.programmesIntro: International GCSE reaches Mussafah through two boards and two routes, and the differences between them decide what a tutor needs to know. The programmes below are the ones families here are actually enrolled in.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Syllabuses identified by four-digit code, with Core and Extended tiers available in several subjects. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Command-term conventions are published and consistent across subjects, which makes them teachable.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools reachable from Mussafah enter candidates with Cambridge, and tiering decisions at 0580 are made by the school well before parents start looking for support. Knowing whether your child is entered for Core or Extended changes what the final weeks should contain.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Examined in May/June and in November each year, with codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics and 4PH1 for Physics. Most subjects are single-tier, and the paper structure differs from Cambridge: two equally weighted maths papers both with a calculator, and a different convention for the longer extended-response questions.
programmes.countryNote: A minority of schools reachable from Mussafah use Pearson, and some families sit subjects split across boards. That split is the commonest cause of a mismatch here, because a tutor who defaults to Cambridge conventions teaches the wrong answer shape for a Pearson six-mark question.

programmes.name: The November resit route
programmes.description: Both boards offer a November series, so a missed grade does not mean a lost year. Entry is made through a centre, and a private candidate needs a centre that accepts external entries. November results follow in January: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Mussafah families tend to discover this route in the same August fortnight the results arrive, which compresses a decision that would be better made in advance. A resit block is paper technique plus the two or three topics that actually cost the grade, not a re-teach of the course.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects running alongside
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in private schools
programmes.description: Arabic language, Islamic education and social or moral studies are required in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond those subjects, but must follow the Ministry's general regulations.
programmes.countryNote: These sit alongside the IGCSE timetable rather than inside it, and they are a real part of a Mussafah student's week. Families planning IGCSE support sometimes forget that the Arabic stream has its own assessment calendar competing for the same evenings.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-mussafah.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Mussafah families request most, with the codes that identify them. Each note says what the paper actually tests and where candidates reliably lose marks, which is the knowledge a syllabus-aware tutor has and a generalist does not.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 decides most grades. Recurring losses sit in bounds and accuracy, similar shapes with area and volume scale factors, and multi-step problems where two ideas have to be linked. Working written badly costs method marks even when the answer is right.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, both with a calculator, which changes revision entirely against Cambridge. Higher tier asks more algebraic proof and more multi-stage ratio than textbook work suggests, and the scheme credits a clear method line most candidates never write.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical-method questions produce the widest spread. Candidates lose marks naming a control variable vaguely, and on the longer questions by describing an effect rather than explaining the mechanism behind it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry gate the whole paper, so a weakness there looks like general weakness. Electrolysis is the topic most often needing rebuilding from first principles rather than revising, and ionic equations are where careless notation costs marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: The content volume tempts reading over writing. Marks live in data-analysis questions and in comparisons with a stated measure. Command terms carry more weight here than in the other sciences: describe, explain and suggest expect different things.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510 and First Language 0500
subjects.description: Two genuinely different courses that families confuse. First Language rewards analysis of writer's technique and effect; Second Language rewards accurate register and task fulfilment. A tutor teaching the wrong one wastes a term.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Case-study papers punish general answers. Marks come from applying a named concept to the stimulus business and then judging it, and most candidates stop before the judgement. The six-mark evaluation questions are the trainable part.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram with a sentence of explanation scores where prose does not. Data-response questions reward reading the stimulus figures precisely rather than writing around them.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: The written paper rewards precision about algorithms, data representation and pseudocode conventions far more than coding ability. Trace tables are the single most reliable source of lost marks at this level.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the international curriculum as a mandatory subject in UAE private schools, with separate first-language and additional-language routes that are different courses. Support here is about reading fluency and written register.

sections.heading: Is there anyone near Mussafah who knows this syllabus? The honest answer
paragraphs: For common subjects, yes. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and English are taught widely enough across Abu Dhabi that a family in Shabiya can find competent help within a short radius, and plenty of it is good. For anything narrower the answer changes, and pretending otherwise is how families end up three sessions into an arrangement that will not work.

The reason is where the schools are. International-curriculum provision in Abu Dhabi concentrates on the island and along the Khalifa City to Al Raha corridor, and specialist tutors cluster where the students are. Mussafah's residential districts sit south of all of it. The schools within a short drive of Shabiya follow mainly Indian and British curricula, so the local pool is strongest in exactly the subjects where help is easiest to find anyway, and thinnest in Pearson science codes, Business Studies marked to scheme, and Computer Science 0478.

A second factor compounds it. Tutors in this market are chosen by families on availability and price far more often than on board knowledge, so the market has not had to specialise. A tutor can build a full timetable in Abu Dhabi without ever reading a Pearson syllabus, and will not be asked to. That is not dishonesty; it is what the demand signal rewards.

The practical consequence for a Mussafah parent is that a radius search quietly changes the question from who teaches this syllabus to who is available in this direction. Delivery over live video removes the radius, which is why IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes — home visits are an India-only service — and matches instead from everyone who teaches the specific code.

sections.heading: Why the syllabus code is the right question to ask
paragraphs: A four-digit number sounds like administrative detail and is actually the whole specification. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1 cover similar science and assess it differently: different paper counts, different weightings, different conventions for how an extended answer earns its marks, different formula provision. A tutor who knows one and assumes the other will teach a student to write answers that are correct and under-rewarded.

Mathematics is the clearest example because the calculator rule differs. Cambridge 0580 Extended splits into papers with and without a calculator, so part of the preparation is non-calculator fluency. Pearson 4MA1 has two equally weighted papers, both with a calculator, so the same hours are better spent on method presentation and multi-stage problems. A tutor teaching 4MA1 as though it were 0580 drills a skill the exam will not test.

Tiering is the third thing the code carries. Cambridge offers Core and Extended in several subjects, with different grade ceilings, and a student entered for Core should not be spending the final weeks on Extended-only content. Schools make the tiering decision and families often do not know which way it went. Asking the examinations officer takes one email and reshapes a revision plan.

Cambridge adds one operational detail that belongs in any honest calendar discussion: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the board states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong one. Your child's zone is a question for the school, not for a tutoring website.

sections.heading: How to test a tutor's syllabus knowledge in ten minutes
paragraphs: You do not need to be a subject specialist to run this test, and it is the single most useful thing a Mussafah parent can do before paying for anything. Ask four questions and listen for specificity rather than confidence.

First, ask which board and code your child is entered for, and see whether the tutor already asked you. A tutor who starts a conversation about IGCSE Physics without establishing 0625 or 4PH1 is working from a general subject picture. Second, ask them to describe the paper structure for that code: how many papers, what each tests, what the weightings are. A specialist answers this in one breath; a generalist describes the subject instead.

Third, hand them a marked script and ask what the pattern in the lost marks is. The answer you want names a behaviour — not writing a method line, answering a describe question as though it said explain, running out of time on the last two questions — rather than naming a topic as weak. Topic weakness is what a report card already told you. Fourth, ask what they would not take on. A tutor who claims every subject and every board at every level is telling you something about how the timetable is filled.

Those four questions also expose the CBSE-to-Cambridge mismatch that is common in this district. A strong CBSE mathematics teacher asked about 0580 Extended Paper 4 will often talk fluently about the content and vaguely about the mark scheme, which is exactly the profile that produces correct working and mid-band results.
bullets: Did the tutor ask for the board and code before you volunteered it
Can they state the paper structure and weightings for that code
Do they read a marked script as behaviour, not as topic weakness
Will they name a subject or board they do not take on

sections.heading: What happens when nobody covers the subject your child needs
paragraphs: Every tutoring platform has coverage gaps and almost none disclose them. The commonest failure in this market is quiet substitution: a request for Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry is answered with a Chemistry tutor who has taught Cambridge, nobody mentions the difference, and the mismatch surfaces in week four when a past paper comes back with marks lost on answer structure.

The honest options are narrower and better. A short wait for the right tutor, where the timetable allows it. A tutor with a strong adjacent specialism plus an explicit statement of what they do not cover, so you can decide whether that trade works for the time you have. Or a straightforward recommendation to look elsewhere, which costs nothing and preserves the week a family would otherwise lose.

Delivery over live video widens the pool considerably, because the constraint stops being who can reach the south mainland on a weekday evening and becomes who teaches the code. For most Cambridge subjects that produces a real match quickly. For Pearson science options and for a few minority-language courses, it still sometimes does not, and that should be said rather than papered over.
The table sets out how coverage actually looks for a Mussafah request, including the fallback position, so you can see where the thin spots are before you ask.

One more thing is worth saying about thin coverage: it is seasonal. Specialist availability in Cambridge science codes tightens sharply in the six to ten weeks before the June series, when every school's cohort is looking at once, and loosens again in the autumn term. A Mussafah family that asks in September for support running to June gets a far better match than one that asks in April, and the difference is availability rather than price.

sections.heading: The series a Mussafah IGCSE candidate is actually sitting
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series exists but is offered to candidates in India only, so no Mussafah student sits it and any revision plan built around those dates is built for the wrong country.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results following in January — November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June results come faster: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the next day. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well in advance, which is why any plan should link the live official timetable rather than rely on dates restated elsewhere.

Working backwards from a series is what turns a vague intention into a plan. Final entries go to the board months ahead through the school's examinations officer, so the subject list, tier and board are usually fixed before a family starts searching for help. Mock papers land the term before. Coursework and practical deadlines, where a subject has them, are school-set and earlier again. The adjustable part is how many marks a student collects from papers they are already entered for.

The November series matters more than families realise, because it converts a missed grade from a lost year into a second attempt a few months later. Knowing the route before August results arrive means a plan can start immediately rather than after three weeks of deliberation.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and where the honesty line sits at IGCSE
paragraphs: IGCSE has less assessed coursework than the Diploma, but where it exists the rules are the same and the pressure is similar. A tutor may teach the underlying skills, explain what the assessment criteria ask for, read what the student has written and say where it does not meet the standard, and teach method — how to structure an argument, how to present data from a practical, how to reference a source. A tutor may not write, rewrite or supply any part of an assessed piece, and may not invent data for a practical write-up.

The practical sciences are where this gets tested in a specific way. Students taught mainly online sometimes have thin hands-on experience, and the temptation is to supply plausible results for a write-up. That is a malpractice risk and it is also pedagogically useless, because the written papers ask about method, control variables, sources of error and improvements — all of which are learned by doing the experiment badly first and understanding why.

A related issue in this market is the sale of material that should not be sold. Reproducing or supplying board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads is a copyright problem, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure. The right behaviour is to reference the official source and link to it, which is also what a parent should expect of a tutor.

Asking a prospective tutor where the line sits is a useful filter in both directions. One who answers precisely has worked with schools. One who offers to help the student produce the piece is offering something that puts the qualification at risk.
bullets: Allowed: teaching skills, explaining criteria, feedback on the student's own work
Not allowed: writing any part of it, or supplying practical data
Practical papers test method and error, which only real experiments teach
Official syllabus and paper material should be linked, not distributed

sections.heading: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects competing for the same evenings
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must follow the Ministry's general regulations. In practice that means every Mussafah student following an international curriculum also carries a mandatory UAE subject load, and that load has its own homework and its own assessments.

In Dubai the detail is published clearly, and the principles are instructive even for Abu Dhabi families. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic education and social studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs for Arabic as a first language, Islamic education and social studies, and combined classes strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

Two further points shape what support is possible. Teachers of Islamic education and Arabic in Dubai must hold the relevant KHDA approval for those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. That is a genuine constraint on how tutoring material for these subjects can be described, and it is why honest support here focuses on reading fluency, written register and exam familiarity rather than on alternative content.

For an IGCSE planning conversation the relevant consequence is simpler: a Mussafah student's evenings are already partly committed. A revision plan that assumes a free weekday evening every day will not survive contact with the Arabic assessment calendar, and the fix is to agree the slot around it rather than to discover the clash in week three.

faqs.question: Is there really an IGCSE tutor near Mussafah who knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: For common Cambridge subjects such as Mathematics 0580 and English, yes, and locally. For Pearson science codes, Business Studies marked to scheme or Computer Science 0478, the pool within a short drive of the Shabiya districts is thin, because international-curriculum schools and the tutors who follow them cluster on the island and along the Khalifa City corridor. Matching over live video removes the distance constraint, so the question becomes who teaches the code rather than who will travel south on a weekday evening. Where even that leaves a gap, you are told before anything is agreed.

faqs.question: Why should a Shabiya parent ask for the code rather than the subject?
faqs.answer: Because the code is the specification. Cambridge 0625 Physics and Pearson 4PH1 cover similar science with different paper counts, different weightings, different conventions for extended answers and different formula provision. In mathematics the gap is sharper: Cambridge 0580 splits calculator and non-calculator papers, so non-calculator fluency is part of the preparation, while Pearson 4MA1 allows a calculator in both papers, making method presentation the better use of the same hours. A tutor teaching one as though it were the other produces correct work that the mark scheme under-rewards.

faqs.question: How does a Mussafah parent confirm the board and tier the school entered?
faqs.answer: Ask your school's examinations officer. Final entries go to the board months before the papers, and the officer holds the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject. Cambridge offers Core and Extended in several subjects with different grade ceilings, and families frequently do not know which way the school decided. The same email can confirm which of Cambridge's six administrative zones your centre sits in, which matters because the board states you must use the timetable version for your own zone and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one.

faqs.question: My child moved from a CBSE school to a Cambridge one. Can a CBSE tutor help?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the gap is predictable. CBSE Class 10 mathematics and Cambridge 0580 Extended overlap heavily in content and diverge in paper structure, command terms and how the mark scheme rewards working. A strong CBSE teacher will often talk fluently about the mathematics and vaguely about the scheme, which produces correct answers and mid-band marks. The fix is a short bridging block diagnosed against the new board's paper rather than the old one, teaching answer shape and command-term response. This is a common pattern in Mussafah households running two systems at once.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a home in Mussafah?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, and not anywhere in the UAE. Lessons for families in Mussafah and the Shabiya districts run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, including the free trial. The practical benefit is specific to this district: the specialist pool for international GCSE sits well north of here, so a visiting arrangement would mean choosing from whoever makes the trip rather than from whoever teaches the syllabus. Removing travel also means a 17:30 session starts at 17:30 rather than whenever the mainland road allows.

faqs.question: What four questions should I ask before paying an IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Ask which board and code your child sits, and notice whether the tutor asked you first. Ask them to state the paper structure and weightings for that code; a specialist does it in one breath. Hand them a marked script and ask what the pattern in the lost marks is — you want a behaviour named, such as missing method lines or answering a describe question as an explain, not a topic called weak. And ask what they will not take on. A tutor who claims every board and every level is describing how their timetable fills, not what they know.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a specialist for in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Pearson science codes — 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 — are the thinnest, because most schools reachable from Mussafah enter candidates with Cambridge and the market has not had to specialise. Business Studies 0450 and Economics 0455 marked properly to the case-study scheme are moderately scarce, and Computer Science 0478 is scarcer than its popularity suggests, because the written paper tests algorithms and pseudocode conventions rather than coding. Minority Group 2 languages are the hardest of all. For each of these the honest options are a short wait or a referral, not a substituted generalist.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams actually happen for a student in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to candidates in India only and does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For the most recent completed cycles: the November 2026 Pearson final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live official timetable your school holds.

faqs.question: Is the November series a realistic second chance for a Mussafah student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning it before results arrive makes it a better one. Both boards offer a November route, so a grade missed in June need not cost a full year. Entry goes through a centre, and a private candidate needs one that accepts external entries, which is worth checking early rather than in the August results week. A resit block is paper technique plus the two or three topics that actually cost the grade, not a re-teach of the two-year course. November results follow in January, as the 22 January 2026 date for the previous November series shows.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IGCSE practical write-up?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach how a practical write-up is structured, explain what the criteria or the paper expects, read what your child wrote and say where it falls short, and teach the science of control variables, sources of error and suggested improvements. A tutor cannot supply results your child did not measure, and should not. Beyond the malpractice risk it defeats the purpose: the written papers ask about method and error, and those are learned by running an experiment imperfectly and understanding why. Official board material should be referenced and linked, not reproduced or handed over as downloads.

faqs.question: How does the mandatory Arabic workload affect an IGCSE revision plan?
faqs.answer: It takes up evenings a revision plan might otherwise assume are free. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, and those subjects carry their own homework and assessments. In Dubai, KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic education and social studies, with combined classes prohibited, and requires Standard Arabic as the language of instruction in several of them. The practical step for a Mussafah family is to agree the tutoring slot around that calendar rather than discover the clash later.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does my child need for Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking tutoring page in this market states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process that no tutoring provider performs or guarantees, and tuition is not a requirement for it — check your own case on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tutors working with UAE students need a permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so figures circulating online are unverified. The route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: What does a good first session look like for a Year 11 student in Shabiya?
faqs.answer: It opens a marked paper and works through it question by question, sorting every lost mark into one of three groups: did not know it, knew it but wrote it badly, knew it but ran out of time. Those have different remedies, and families often spend a whole term on the first when most of the marks were in the second and third. By the end the tutor should name the two or three recurring losses and say what the coming weeks will drill. A first session spent on general discussion has told you nothing you did not already know from the report card.

faqs.question: Can we schedule around the school bus and still get a full session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the timing matters more than families expect. Mussafah students travelling to Khalifa City or island schools typically get home between 15:30 and 16:15, and a session straight off the bus runs at noticeably lower productivity than the same hour at 18:30. Most households here settle on a weekday window between 17:00 and 20:30, with a longer weekend slot for a full past paper sat to time, which needs two uninterrupted hours. Because the lesson is delivered over live video, the start time is the start time rather than an estimate dependent on traffic.

intro.heading: What a Saadiyat Island family is really asking when they search for a home tutor
paragraphs: Saadiyat Island is a short, well-built island with a small number of schools and a large number of families who commute off it every morning. That shapes tutoring more than anything academic does. A parent typing "IGCSE home tutor in Saadiyat Island" into Google is rarely asking for a teaching philosophy. They are asking whether anyone can be in front of their child between the end of the school day and the point at which homework, dinner and sleep take the evening back.

Work backwards from that. Most British-curriculum secondary schools serving the island finish their taught day between 14:45 and 15:30. Add the crossing to the mainland or the run back from a Khalifa City or Al Raha campus and a realistic arrival home is somewhere after 16:00. An in-home tutor booked for 17:00 has to leave their own location at roughly 16:15 to make it, and if your child's day has run long, the hour you paid for shrinks while the tutor sits in your kitchen waiting. Multiply that by two subjects a week across a two-year IGCSE course and the hidden cost is not money, it is lost contact time.

IB Gram does not solve that by sending someone faster. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Saadiyat Island families, lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, which removes the travel window on both sides. A 17:00 start means 17:00, and if your child's school has run a late co-curricular session, the lesson can move to 18:30 the same evening without anyone wasting a journey.

There is a second reason this matters on a small island. The pool of tutors who genuinely know Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1 or Cambridge Economics 0455 and who happen to live within twenty minutes of Saadiyat is tiny. The pool of tutors who know those syllabuses and can teach over video is not. Choosing by postcode means choosing from whoever is nearby. Choosing by syllabus means choosing the person who has marked that paper's command terms into the ground.

The rest of this page is written for the practical decision. It sets out when a session realistically fits around the island's school day, what the Abu Dhabi market charges for in-home and online IGCSE tuition in AED, how the Cambridge and Pearson exam series work for UAE candidates, what ADEK and the Ministry of Education actually govern, and where the honest limits of a tutor's role sit when coursework is involved. Figures quoted are market figures with their sources named. Nothing on this page is a price list for IB Gram.

These are the programmes an IGCSE tutor for this area is most often asked to cover, with what each one means for scheduling and for the entry your school makes.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses assessed by terminal written papers, with syllabus codes that tell you exactly what is being sat: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0455 Economics, 0470 History. Most subjects are tiered or split into Core and Extended routes, and the tier decides the grade ceiling. A tutor who does not know which tier your child is entered for is guessing at half the content.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a Saadiyat Island family that is a question for the school's exams officer, not for the internet.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other half of the British track in Abu Dhabi, with its own codes: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Pearson papers ask questions in a recognisably different register from Cambridge, and the mark schemes credit different things. Switching a student between boards mid-course without changing the past-paper diet is one of the quiet causes of a dropped grade.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Always read the live timetable on the Pearson site rather than a date restated on a tutoring page.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, where Checkpoint tests in English, mathematics and science give the only external read on a student before the real thing. Saadiyat Island parents often start tutoring here rather than in Year 11, because the gap that shows up as a grade 5 in IGCSE Mathematics is usually a Year 8 algebra gap that nobody had time to close.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. These are diagnostic rather than certificating, which makes them useful: a weak Checkpoint score in a specific strand tells a tutor precisely where to start, two years before the grade matters.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Where most Saadiyat Island IGCSE students go next if their school does not run the IB Diploma. The jump in reading load and in mathematical fluency between IGCSE Extended and AS is the steepest in the British track, and the students who cope are the ones whose IGCSE foundations were secure rather than crammed.
programmes.countryNote: The UAE Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency route asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, on top of the five IGCSE passes. That is worth knowing in Year 11, not Year 13.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-saadiyat-i.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask us to cover, with what each one actually assesses and where marks go missing. Entries are written for a parent deciding which subject to spend the first hour on.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework, and a grade ceiling set by tier. Extended marks are lost most often on algebraic fractions, transformations of graphs, bounds and compound percentage change. The fix is almost never more theory; it is timed past-paper work with the mark scheme open afterwards.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics or an IB higher level course. Introduces calculus, binomial expansion, trigonometric identities and matrices. Students who find 0580 comfortable can still stall here because the questions are multi-step and give no partial scaffolding.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism carry the most marks lost in Abu Dhabi cohorts, followed by the practical-skills paper where graph axes, best-fit lines and significant figures quietly erode a grade. Definitions must be written in the syllabus's own words; paraphrase scores nothing.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction conditions are the three places Extended candidates drop the most. The multiple-choice paper rewards fast recall of qualitative analysis tests, which is pure drill and responds quickly to tutoring.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The highest content volume on the science track, and the subject where command terms decide grades. "Describe" and "explain" carry different marks for the same knowledge. Genetics crosses and transport in plants reward structured diagram work rather than prose.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response are where marks sit, and both are taught skills rather than talents. Students in international schools often read widely and still lose marks for not answering the exact brief: audience, form and purpose are assessed explicitly.

subjects.name: English Literature (Cambridge 0475)
subjects.description: Passage-based questions reward close reference to language over plot summary. The common failure in Abu Dhabi cohorts is an essay that narrates the text accurately and never quotes it. Tutoring here is largely about building a quotation bank and practising timed paragraph structure.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the whole game: axes labelled, curves shifted in the right direction, equilibrium marked. Data-response questions ask for evaluation, and candidates who list advantages and disadvantages without reaching a judgement cap themselves well below the top band.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study driven, so marks depend on applying theory to the specific business in the paper rather than reciting it. Students who memorise definitions and ignore the case text routinely score in the middle band regardless of how much they know.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory covers data representation, networks and security; Paper 2 asks for pseudocode and trace tables. The trace table is the single most reliable mark-gainer on the paper and the single most commonly skipped piece of revision.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Arabic is required in Abu Dhabi private schools alongside the licensed international curriculum, and the first-language and additional-language routes are genuinely different courses with different expectations. Streaming a student into the wrong one is a common and fixable problem.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall plus skills: map interpretation, cross-sections, climate graph reading. Candidates lose marks for naming a case study without the specific figures that made it worth naming. A tutor's job here is largely building a tight, usable set of examples.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-saadiyat-i.regionsTitle: Where Saadiyat Island families actually come from, and where they go
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-saadiyat-i.regionsIntro: Saadiyat does not stand alone. Households move between it and the Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas corridors daily, and the school a child attends is often not on the island where they sleep. These are the areas that share Saadiyat's school run.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Beach-district and cultural-district villas and apartments, with a short internal road network and a single bridge route to the mainland. The island's own school provision is small, so most secondary students travel off it each morning.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-density towers reached from Saadiyat via the mainland, not directly. Reem families and Saadiyat families frequently share the same secondary schools, which means they share the same 15:00 finish and the same 16:30 earliest usable session.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A longer run from Saadiyat than the map suggests, because the route goes inland before it goes east. Yas has its own school provision, so cross-island tutoring groups rarely work; individual online scheduling does.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: The mainland coastal strip on the Abu Dhabi-Dubai road, close to several of the British and IB schools that Saadiyat students attend. Afternoon traffic on that corridor is the reason in-home tutors quote travel into their rate.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Villa community immediately inland of Al Raha Beach, heavily weighted towards British-curriculum families. The 15:00 pickup here and the 15:00 pickup for a Saadiyat household produce very different arrival times home.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The largest concentration of IB and British secondary places in the Abu Dhabi school map, and the destination for a significant share of Saadiyat Island's secondary students. A Saadiyat child at a Khalifa City school is typically not home before 16:15.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Older, close-in district with established international school provision and a shorter commute to the island than the Khalifa City corridor. Useful to know if you are choosing a school partly on the length of the afternoon.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Inland and further out, with its own cluster of schools. Families who move from Saadiyat to MBZ usually change schools too, which is when a transition gap in mathematics or science tends to appear.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Near the airport, popular with staff at the Khalifa City and Al Raha schools. Mentioned here because it is where a lot of in-home tutors in this part of Abu Dhabi are actually based, and that distance is what you pay for.

regions.name: The Corniche and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Central Abu Dhabi, where tuition centres cluster. A group class on the Corniche means a second commute at 17:00 for a Saadiyat family, which is the trade-off a one-to-one online session is designed to remove.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat Island and central Abu Dhabi
schoolClusters.note: The island's own provision is small and sits alongside the long-established central Abu Dhabi schools. Students we support in this cluster sit a mix of Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel entries, which is why an IGCSE tutor here has to ask for the syllabus code before the first lesson rather than after it.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: This is where most Saadiyat Island secondary students actually spend their day. The corridor carries the largest block of British-curriculum and IB places in the emirate, and the end-of-day times across these campuses are close enough that a 16:30 session start works for nearly all of them.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Yas Island and Al Reem Island
schoolClusters.note: The two island clusters either side of Saadiyat, both with growing secondary provision. Families moving between them mid-course are the group most likely to need a board-transition plan, because a move can mean a switch from Cambridge to Pearson or the reverse.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, fixed slot
modes.description: One or two sessions a week at the same time each week, held after the school run has finished. This is what most Year 10 families start with, because a fixed slot survives contact with a term timetable better than an ad-hoc arrangement does. The tutor works to your child's school scheme of work and the syllabus code the school has entered.

modes.title: Pre-series intensive
modes.description: A compressed block in the weeks before the June or November series, built around timed papers rather than new content. Sessions run more often and shorter, and the work is deliberately repetitive: sit the paper, mark it against the published scheme, rebuild the two topics that cost the most marks, repeat. Useful when the gap is exam technique rather than knowledge.

modes.description: A short, bounded block on one thing that has gone wrong: electricity in Physics, moles in Chemistry, algebraic fractions in Mathematics. Three to six sessions with a defined end point. Families on Saadiyat often use this after a mock result makes the problem specific, rather than committing to a year of weekly tuition on a hunch.

modes.description: Where a student needs support in two subjects, the sessions are placed on different evenings with the same weekly rhythm, so the week has a shape your child can predict. sections.heading: The Saadiyat Island school day, counted forwards to the first usable session
paragraphs: Most British-curriculum secondary schools serving Saadiyat Island end their taught day between 14:45 and 15:30, with co-curricular activities running until roughly 16:15 on the days a student has them. That is the single most useful fact for planning IGCSE support in this area, and no competitor page states it.

From a Khalifa City or Al Raha campus, a Saadiyat household is looking at a return journey that lands somewhere between 15:45 and 16:30 depending on the day and the route. From a school on the island itself, arrival home can be before 15:30. Those two cases produce very different evenings, and a tutor booked at a single fixed time for both is wrong for one of them. The practical answer is to set the slot against the school, not against the neighbourhood.

Our scheduling range for Abu Dhabi runs from 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and the reason is this arithmetic. A 16:00 start assumes a short commute and no activities. A 16:30 start works for an island school with activities or a mainland school without. A 18:00 or 18:30 start works for everything, and is also when a Year 11 student has eaten and is capable of sustained work. Later than 20:00 and the session is competing with sleep, which in an exam term is a false economy.

The table below sets out the pattern by school type rather than by named campus, because end-of-day times change and a parent should confirm theirs with the school office. What does not change is the shape: the further off-island your child's school, the later your usable window begins, and the more an in-home tutor's travel eats into it.
bullets: Confirm your school's actual finish time and activity days before fixing a slot
Leave at least 45 minutes between arriving home and starting a session
Avoid stacking two subjects on the same evening in an exam term
A 90-minute session suits mathematics and the sciences; 60 minutes suits essay subjects

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs in Abu Dhabi, and what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number a household budget actually feels. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Converted to an hourly rate, the published bands are these. Budget online and university-student tutors run AED 45-150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150-300, and Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, runs AED 180-500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200-500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors run AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

The gap between the online band and the in-home band is the travel premium, and it is worth being precise about what it pays for. It does not buy more teaching. It buys the tutor's journey, their waiting time, and the risk that the Abu Dhabi afternoon costs them a second booking. On Saadiyat Island, where the only road access is across a bridge, that premium is structurally higher than it is for a tutor working within Khalifa City. A family paying AED 350 an hour for an in-home session is typically paying AED 150-200 for teaching and the rest for logistics.

None of these are IB Gram's prices. They are published market figures, attributed above, and they are here so that a parent can judge a quote rather than accept one. IB Gram's own model starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about what the student actually needs, and we would rather you read the market table first.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit on Saadiyat Island
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search term implies, so it deserves a straight answer. IB Gram delivers IGCSE tuition to Saadiyat Island as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not sell home visits in the UAE at all. The case for that is not that video is inherently better teaching; it is that for this specific island, with this specific school run, the things video removes are the things that actually degrade a tutoring arrangement.

Travel is the first. A tutor who drives to Saadiyat for a 17:00 session has committed most of their afternoon to one hour of teaching, and that cost appears in the rate. The second is the tutor pool. Choosing an in-home tutor means choosing from people willing to make that journey, which on an island is a short list. Choosing online means choosing from people who teach Cambridge 0620 Chemistry at Extended tier as their main subject. For a Core-tier Year 10 student the difference may not matter. For an Extended-tier Year 11 student aiming at a grade 8, it decides the outcome.

The third is continuity. An in-home arrangement breaks when the tutor is ill, when your family travels, or when the road is closed. An online arrangement survives all three, and survives a family summer in another time zone, which in Abu Dhabi is not an edge case. The fourth is the record. A video lesson can be screen-shared, annotated and saved, so the worked solution to the problem that defeated your child in March is still there in May.

What video genuinely loses is the physical practical. A tutor cannot stand next to your child at a bench. For Cambridge 0625 Physics and 0620 Chemistry that is handled by working on the practical-skills paper itself, which is a written paper about method, graphs and error rather than a lab assessment. The school runs the laboratory work. The tutor makes sure the paper about it is answered properly.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects split into a Core route and an Extended route, and the split is not cosmetic. Core covers less content and caps the grade a candidate can be awarded. Extended covers the full syllabus and is open to the full grade range. The decision is made by the school, usually in Year 10, and it is reviewable, which is why a parent should understand it rather than discover it in a results envelope.

For mathematics, the practical consequence is that a Core candidate sits papers that never ask for the algebraic manipulation, the transformations or the harder trigonometry that Extended papers lean on. A student moved from Core to Extended in Year 11 therefore has real content to acquire, not just harder questions to practise. That is a tutoring job with a known size, and it is one of the most common reasons a Saadiyat Island family comes looking in October.

For the sciences, the Core and Extended distinction maps onto specific syllabus statements marked as supplementary. Electrolysis in Chemistry, electromagnetic induction in Physics and the detail of plant transport in Biology sit largely in the Extended material. A tutor who is working from a general Year 11 scheme rather than the actual syllabus document will cover these at the wrong depth in one direction or the other.

Pearson Edexcel handles the same problem differently, with tiered Foundation and Higher papers in mathematics and a single tier in most sciences. That is why the first question any competent IGCSE tutor asks is which board and which tier, and the second is to see a marked mock paper. Everything after that is diagnosis.

A tier change is a content change, not just a difficulty change

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June series and the November series. Cambridge offers a February/March series to India only, so an Abu Dhabi family should discount any page that mentions it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Those two facts between them settle most of the planning questions a Year 11 parent has.

Counting backwards from a June results day: results reach centres in August, final entries close months before the exam window, mocks fall in the spring term, and the last point at which a tier change is realistic is earlier still. For the November series, the pattern repeats shifted: the Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026.

What that means for tutoring is simple arithmetic. If you want eight weeks of timed-paper work before a June sitting, the tutor starts in the spring term, not after the mocks are returned. If a resit in November is the plan, the decision window opens the day the August results arrive and closes long before the exam itself. The November series is also the series a private candidate most often uses, and entering as a private candidate is an arrangement made with an exam centre, not with a tutor.

Dates in official timetables are revised, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series. Read the live timetable on the board's own site and confirm your centre's zone with your school's exams officer. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk.

sections.heading: ADEK, the Ministry of Education and what actually governs your child's school
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools sit under the Department of Education and Knowledge. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, according to the UAE government's own private-schools page, and publishes inspection outcomes. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority instead, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. ADEK is named by none of the competing tutoring pages we examined, which is a strange omission on a page aimed at Abu Dhabi parents.

What this means in practice is that your child's curriculum, fees and inspection record are an emirate-level matter. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the regulator's role goes well beyond inspection. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

A separate point, and an important one: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. MoHRE's own service page, "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Two things follow for a parent. Ask any tutor you hire privately whether they hold that permit, because it is free and there is no good reason not to. And treat any claim of regulator approval with suspicion: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, and says so plainly. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises, and nothing on this page should be read as implying one.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with IGCSE coursework
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework or a controlled assessment component, and every board treats the authorship of that work as non-negotiable. The student writes it. A tutor's legitimate role is to teach the skills the task assesses, explain the assessment criteria, discuss a plan, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. That is a real and valuable job, and it is also the boundary.

What a tutor must not do is produce the work. No tutor should write a coursework piece, supply a model answer to be submitted, rewrite a draft into its final form, or provide finished text of any kind for submission. One of the pages competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach, it puts the student at risk of a malpractice finding, and it is the reason we state our position in writing rather than leaving it implied.

The same applies to materials. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those documents belong to the boards, they are published on the boards' own sites, and a tutor's job is to teach your child to use them, not to hand over a copy. When a session needs a paper, it comes from the board's own published source.

There is one more boundary worth stating because it is specific to Abu Dhabi. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. We treat that as press-reported rather than quoted, and verify it against current policy. Either way, we do not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by a teacher at their own school.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule a Year 11 parent should know now
paragraphs: If your child may apply to a UAE university, the Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements for the British track matter from Year 10 onwards, because they constrain which subjects are worth entering. The published requirement, as reported in July 2026, is that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The part that catches families out is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A student who takes Arabic, Islamic Education and three other subjects has three towards the five, not five. One page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not the published rule.

On the American track the same article gives different gates: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. It states no IB points threshold, so no IB equivalency figure should be published without a source on the Ministry's own site, and this page does not publish one.

Two cautions. Equivalency and attestation are processes carried out by the Ministry and the relevant authority, not by a tutoring platform, and nothing here is performed or guaranteed by IB Gram. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Anyone telling you otherwise is selling urgency. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before you plan a subject list around it.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: A British-curriculum student in Abu Dhabi is not only sitting IGCSEs. Federal rules require private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed to deliver, and that occupies real timetable space alongside the IGCSE courses. Families planning tutoring around a Year 11 timetable often forget these subjects exist until a report flags one.

Dubai's regulator has published the clearest public specification of how this works, and the principles are instructive even for an Abu Dhabi family. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

The instructional-time rules are equally concrete. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is prohibited, which is a genuine constraint on how any tutor may describe support in these subjects.

What that means for a Saadiyat Island family is this. Arabic as a first language and Arabic as an additional language are different courses with different expectations, and a student in the wrong stream will struggle for reasons that have nothing to do with ability. Support in these subjects has to follow the school's own approved material rather than substitute something else. And if a report flags Arabic, the question to ask the school is which stream your child is in before you ask anyone for tutoring.
