process.title: Tell us the school, the board and the tier
process.description: The first message should say which school your child attends, which board the school has entered them for, which tier in each subject, and what time they are realistically home. Those four facts determine both the tutor and the slot, and getting them right at the start saves a wasted trial lesson.

process.title: Send one piece of marked work
process.description: A marked mock paper or a returned assessment is worth more than a description of the problem. It shows where marks were lost rather than where they felt lost, and it lets the tutor arrive at the first session with a diagnosis instead of a questionnaire.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video at no cost, with no card details required. Its purpose is to test the match: whether your child talks to this tutor, whether the pace is right, and whether the diagnosis holds up against the student in the room. If it does not, say so and we will try a different tutor.

process.title: Fix the slot against the school day
process.description: Using the school-run table above, pick a weekly time that survives an activity day. A slot that works only on a quiet Tuesday will break in the first fortnight. Most Saadiyat Island families settle on something between 17:30 and 18:30 Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Review at the end of each half term
process.description: After each session you get a short written note on what was covered and what comes next. At the half term, the question is whether the topic list is shrinking and whether timed-paper scores are moving. If the answer to either is no, the plan changes rather than continuing on momentum.

process.title: Decide the run-in before the mocks are returned
process.description: Eight weeks of timed-paper work has to be scheduled, not hoped for. The decision about whether to add a second weekly session for the run-in should be made during the spring term for a June sitting, not after the mock results arrive and the calendar has already closed in.

whyPoints.title: The slot is set by your school's finish time
whyPoints.description: Not by a tutor's availability or a centre's roster. We ask what time your child is actually home from their specific campus and work from there, which on Saadiyat Island is the difference between a session that happens and a session that gets cancelled twice a month.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, one student, one syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Every lesson is one-to-one. The tutor teaches to the specific code your school has entered, whether that is Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, and works from your child's own scheme of work rather than a generic plan for the year group.

whyPoints.title: No travel on either side
whyPoints.description: Lessons are delivered over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, which means no bridge crossing, no waiting in a kitchen, and no travel premium folded into the rate. It also means a session survives a closed road and a family trip abroad.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: The AED figures on this page are attributed to the competitors and rate surveys that published them, with the band stated. We would rather you could judge any quote you receive, including ours, than be told that rates are competitive and left to guess.

whyPoints.title: Coursework boundaries stated in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on your child's own draft. No tutor writes, rewrites or supplies work for submission, and we do not reproduce board papers or mark schemes. Saying this plainly is not a formality in a market where one competitor sells completed assessments.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims, because we hold none
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, and no office in the UAE. We name regulators to explain what they do, never to borrow their authority.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to homes on Saadiyat Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and Saadiyat Island is no exception; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Tuition for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. The practical effect is that no part of your fee pays for a bridge crossing or for a tutor waiting while your child finishes the school run, and the person teaching your child is chosen for knowing the syllabus rather than for living nearby.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session realistically start for a Saadiyat Island student?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the school is rather than where you live. A child at a school on the island itself is often home by 15:45, which makes 16:30 workable. A child at a Khalifa City or Al Raha campus is typically home between 15:45 and 16:30, so 17:30 or 18:00 is the honest earliest. On an activity day, add an hour to both. Our scheduling range for Abu Dhabi runs from 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and most families on the island settle somewhere between 17:30 and 18:30.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE home tutor in Saadiyat Island cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates for Abu Dhabi and Dubai put in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Bestimate's 2026 rate table quotes AED 180-350 for in-home, and independent home tutors quote AED 200-500. Those are market figures, not ours. The gap between the two bands is the travel premium, and on an island with a single road route it is structurally larger than it would be for a tutor working inside their own neighbourhood.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Abu Dhabi actually sit?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge IGCSE, UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge offers a February/March series to India only, so it does not apply to your child. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Which one your child sits is decided by the school's entry, and the school's exams officer can confirm both the series and the administrative zone your centre falls in. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's own risk.

faqs.question: Which schools do Saadiyat Island secondary students usually attend?
faqs.answer: The island's own secondary provision is small, so a large share of students travel to the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, where the biggest block of British-curriculum and IB places in Abu Dhabi sits, or to the long-established central Abu Dhabi and Al Bateen schools. Campuses such as Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, Al Yasmina Academy, Raha International School, The British International School Abu Dhabi and Repton School Abu Dhabi come up regularly. We name these as context for the school map only; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: My child is in Core tier mathematics and wants a grade 7. Is that possible?
faqs.answer: Not on the Core route, because Core caps the grade a candidate can be awarded. The honest answer is that the tier has to change first, and that is a decision for the school, usually reviewable during Year 10 and sometimes into Year 11. A move from Core to Extended is a content change rather than a difficulty change: Extended papers draw on algebraic manipulation, transformations and harder trigonometry that Core papers never ask for. Ask the school in writing which tier your child is entered for, by subject, before planning anything else.

faqs.question: Where exactly does an IGCSE tutor's help with coursework have to stop?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, explain the assessment criteria, talk through a plan and give feedback on a draft your child has written. A tutor must not write the piece, rewrite it into its final form, or supply text for submission. One page competing for these searches sells completed assessments outright, which puts the student at risk of a malpractice finding. We state our boundary in writing rather than leaving it to be assumed.

faqs.question: Does a private IGCSE tutor working with a Saadiyat Island family need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, so there is no good reason for a tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does my child need for UAE university equivalency?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education's British-track requirement, as reported in July 2026, is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competing page states six subjects, which is not the published rule. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring platform performs, so verify the current requirement on the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: Is online teaching workable for IGCSE Physics and Chemistry practicals?
faqs.answer: The practical component most IGCSE science candidates sit is a written paper about method, measurement, graphs and sources of error rather than a laboratory assessment, and that paper responds well to one-to-one work on a shared screen. Axes, best-fit lines, significant figures and the wording of a conclusion are where marks go missing, and all of those can be taught over video. The laboratory work itself belongs to the school. A tutor's job is to make sure the paper written about it earns the marks available.

faqs.question: What if no IGCSE specialist is free for the Saadiyat Island slot we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. For a narrow combination such as Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics at a 17:00 Gulf Standard Time start, the honest answer is sometimes that the match will take a few days or that the only workable slot is later in the evening. Where no suitable specialist is available at all, we say so. A tutor who does not know the syllabus code costs you the fee and a term of misdirected effort, which is worse than waiting.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan or when we travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the real advantages of video delivery. Sessions can shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, and they can follow a family that is out of the country for part of the summer or a half term, with the slot adjusted for the time difference. An in-home arrangement cannot do either without being paused. For a Year 11 student in the spring term, a paused month is the difference between finishing the timed-paper work and starting the exams halfway through it.

faqs.question: My child switched from Cambridge to Pearson Edexcel mid-course. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than most families expect. The content overlaps heavily, but the papers ask questions in a different register and the mark schemes credit different things, so a student revising from the wrong board's past papers is practising for a slightly different exam. The first thing a tutor should do is confirm the new code, switch the past-paper diet to match, and audit the content for the handful of topics that sit in one specification and not the other. That is usually a bounded job of a few sessions.

faqs.question: Do you publish a price list for Saadiyat Island?
faqs.answer: Not on this page. The AED figures above are published market rates attributed to the competitors and rate surveys that produced them, and they are here so that you can judge any quote you receive. IB Gram's own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about what your child needs, how many subjects are involved and how many weeks are left before the series they are entered for. Those three variables change the answer enough that a single headline number would be misleading rather than helpful.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor be matched for a Saadiyat Island family?
faqs.answer: For a mainstream subject at a common slot, usually within a few days. For Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology or English Language at an evening start, the pool is wide. For a narrower combination, or for an early slot that only works for a family whose child attends a school on the island itself, it can take longer. We would rather give you a date we can meet than a tutor who is merely free, and we will tell you which of those two situations you are in.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-saadiyat-i.closingHeading: Start with the school day, not with the search result
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-saadiyat-i.closingBody: If you remember one thing from this page, make it the arithmetic. Find out what time your child's school actually finishes, add the run back to Saadiyat Island, add forty-five minutes to eat and change, and you have the first hour in which tutoring can do anything useful. Then choose a tutor who knows the exact syllabus code your school has entered. IB Gram teaches Abu Dhabi students one-to-one over live video, inside that window, with a free trial lesson before any payment and market rates published with their sources so you can judge every quote you receive, including ours.

intro.heading: Comparing two neighbouring communities, and finding the same answer
paragraphs: Shakhbout City is a mainland villa community in the Khalifa City corridor, sitting between Khalifa City and Mohammed Bin Zayed City. It was built as family housing — compound streets, villas rather than towers — and most children here attend one of the international schools in that corridor. Families moving within Abu Dhabi routinely weigh it against the communities either side, and when they do they usually assume tutoring availability is one of the variables.

It is not, and this page exists to say so plainly rather than to pretend otherwise. The resident tutors who serve Shakhbout City also serve Khalifa City, Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Al Raha and Al Reef, because those communities sit within twenty minutes of each other and a tutor's route covers several of them in a week. There is one supply, and it is allocated by who asked first and who pays the travel.

What that means in practice is that a family comparing "tutors in Shakhbout City" with "tutors in Khalifa City" is comparing two search results drawn from one list. The names may differ because of how agencies tag their pages, and the people behind them overlap substantially. A quoted rate may differ by twenty or thirty dirhams depending on which end of the corridor the tutor lives in, and that difference is a petrol calculation rather than a quality one.

There are real differences between these communities, and they are worth naming: housing type, which schools are immediately adjacent, the curriculum mix those schools run, and how long the school run takes. Those affect your life considerably. They do not affect which IGCSE specialist is available to teach Cambridge 0620 Chemistry to a Year 11 student on a Tuesday evening.

Two things do change the answer, and both have nothing to do with geography. The first is which exam board your child is entered with, because Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel examine the same subjects with different papers, tiering and mark schemes. The second is the time your child is actually at a desk, which is a function of the school you chose rather than the house.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run in India only, and no tutor will travel to a Shakhbout City address or to any other address in this corridor. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, matched on syllabus code and tier. That removes the comparison entirely: the same specialist is available from any of these communities, and from the next emirate for that matter.

What follows is the comparison done properly: the two communities side by side, what genuinely differs between neighbouring Abu Dhabi communities, the board question, what changes if you move emirate, how a tuition centre in the next community compares with one-to-one online, and what each option costs in AED.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-shakhbout-.programmesIntro: Whichever community you live in, the qualification is what determines the tutoring. These are the IGCSE routes Abu Dhabi schools in this corridor enter students for.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International's IGCSE suite, identified by four-digit codes — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English First Language. Most subjects offer a Core tier with a reduced syllabus and a capped grade range and an Extended tier with the full content and full range, and the entry tier is decided by the school with you.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to a candidate sitting in Abu Dhabi. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international GCSE suite, identified by codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4BI1 Biology. Mathematics A is tiered as Foundation and Higher. Several subjects are available in a modular structure where units can be sat across series, which changes revision planning compared with a single terminal entry.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes and revises provisional timetables, so use the live official one.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Cambridge's O Level qualifications sit in the same June and November series and remain on offer for some subjects in some schools. Content overlaps heavily with the equivalent IGCSE while the assessment pattern differs, particularly in the handling of coursework and practical components.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer schools in this corridor enter O Level than IGCSE, but it appears, and it matters when a family moves house and school at the same time. A Year 10 student transferring between an O Level and an IGCSE entry in the same subject has a small content gap and a real paper-technique gap, which is a short, cheap piece of work if it is done at the point of transfer.

programmes.name: What the IGCSE grade set opens
programmes.description: The Year 11 grade set determines access to A Level, to the IB Diploma or to a career-related route, and each sixth form sets its own thresholds. Mathematics is the tightest gate: an Extended or Higher tier grade is normally required for A Level Mathematics or IB Higher Level maths.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools across this corridor run both A Level and IB Diploma sixth forms, which makes the grade set a genuine fork. Because the corridor's schools sit so close together, families here often change school between Year 11 and Year 12 rather than moving house, and the receiving school's thresholds are worth asking about a year early.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-shakhbout-.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects families across this corridor most often fund, with the specific place marks go. The syllabus code matters more than the community you live in.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics. Algebraic manipulation dominates the losses at the higher tiers, because almost every multi-step question routes through it and one slip costs a whole question.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics and radioactivity. Circuits are the standard breaking point, and the practical component rewards precise description of method and control variables.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, electrolysis and organic chemistry. Moles and ionic equations concentrate the marks; qualitative analysis rewards learned observations students rarely revise systematically.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Cells, transport, nutrition, respiration, coordination, inheritance and ecology. Large content, and the losses are command-term failures rather than knowledge gaps — describing where an explanation was asked for.

subjects.name: English First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, directed writing and composition. Marks go on failing to adapt register to the stated audience and on summary answers that reproduce rather than condense. A repeatable structure moves this grade fastest.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking for additional-language candidates. Gains come from accuracy drilling and exam technique rather than general conversation, and the listening paper responds to practice at speed.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Demand and supply, markets, the macroeconomy, business functions and finance. Diagram accuracy carries marks and is routinely sloppy; extended answers lose credit for listing without evaluating in context.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Data representation, hardware, networks, algorithms, programming and the practical components. Pseudocode and trace-table questions are reliable marks students treat as optional.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: These run alongside the international curriculum under the federal baseline. For Ministry equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and further options
subjects.description: Material overlapping early AS content: advanced algebra, series, identities and calculus foundations. A short, cheap bridge into sixth-form maths for a student already secure in the main syllabus.

sections.heading: Shakhbout City or Khalifa City: does the postcode change the answer?
paragraphs: Mostly no, and the reason is worth understanding before you spend time comparing. These communities sit within ten to twenty minutes of each other inside one continuous mainland corridor. A resident tutor living in Khalifa City will take bookings in Shakhbout City, Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Al Raha and sometimes Al Reef, because that is how a viable week is assembled when each session is an hour and the travel between them is short.

So the list of available tutors is effectively shared. What differs between two agency pages titled for two neighbouring communities is the page title, not the people. Where a rate differs by twenty or thirty dirhams, that is a petrol and time calculation reflecting which end of the corridor the tutor lives in, not a difference in what they know about Cambridge 0620 Chemistry.

Families still find real differences when they compare these communities, and it is worth separating them out honestly. Housing type and cost differ. Which schools are immediately adjacent differs. The curriculum mix those schools run differs, with Mohammed Bin Zayed City offering the broadest range in the emirate. Community facilities and the character of the streets differ. Those matter a great deal to how you live and almost nothing to which tutor teaches your child.

The one educational variable the address genuinely changes is the length of the school run, and even that is mostly a function of which school you chose rather than which community you live in. A Shakhbout City family with a child at a Khalifa City school has a ten-minute run; a Shakhbout City family with a child on Saadiyat has a forty-minute one. sections.heading: Why it is the same pool either way
paragraphs: The structural reason is worth spelling out, because it explains why the comparison cannot produce a different answer. Private tutoring in this emirate is supplied by individuals who assemble a week out of hour-long bookings. For that to be economic, the bookings have to be geographically close to each other, which pushes every tutor towards covering a cluster of neighbouring communities rather than specialising in one.

A tutor living in Khalifa City can plausibly fit four sessions into an evening across Khalifa City, Shakhbout City and the near edge of Mohammed Bin Zayed City. They cannot fit four sessions into an evening if two of them are on Saadiyat. So the supply naturally organises into corridors, and this corridor is one of the largest in the emirate.

The practical consequence for a parent is that local search results are a poor guide to quality and a reasonable guide to distance. Two tutors advertising for two different communities here may be the same person with two listings, or two people who would both take your booking. Neither fact tells you whether they teach your child's board at your child's tier, which is the thing that determines whether the hour works.

Which is the argument for changing the filter rather than the postcode. If the pool is shared across the corridor anyway, then the only remaining question is who teaches the qualification — and once you ask that, there is no reason to restrict the search to people who can drive to your villa. That is the whole case for online delivery here, and it is a logical consequence of the local supply pattern rather than a sales pitch.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: the difference that does change the answer
paragraphs: Having established that geography barely matters, here is the variable that genuinely does. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel examine the same subjects with different papers, different codes, different tiering vocabulary and different mark schemes. A tutor drilling Cambridge 0580 past papers for a student entered with Pearson 4MA1 is teaching useful mathematics and wasting the specificity you are paying for.

The differences are concrete. Cambridge tiers many subjects as Core and Extended; Pearson tiers Mathematics A as Foundation and Higher, and they are not identical in content or grade ceiling. Several Pearson subjects can be taken modularly with units sat across series, which changes the revision calendar entirely compared with a single terminal entry. Practical assessment in the sciences is handled differently, and the mark schemes reward differently phrased answers even where the physics is identical.

Find out by asking the school for the syllabus code rather than the subject name. Cambridge codes are four digits; Pearson codes carry a number and letters. Then give the code to anyone you speak to. A tutor who asks which tier applies and which paper pattern governs your child's exam year knows the qualification. A tutor who treats IGCSE as one thing has told you what you need to know at no cost.

One operational point with consequences, particularly for a private candidate. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong timetable. Through a school that is the school's responsibility. As a private candidate it is yours.

sections.heading: If you move emirate, the regulator changes
paragraphs: Families comparing communities inside Abu Dhabi sometimes end up comparing emirates, and that is the one relocation decision where the education framework genuinely changes rather than the house. The regulator differs by emirate, and so does the breadth of its remit.

Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai sits with KHDA, described as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The remit is not uniform, and this is the detail that catches families out. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — so curriculum and fee approval, not merely inspection, sits with the emirate regulator there. Dubai's KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under a second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total, which is a Dubai measure and not a national one.

For a tutoring decision none of this changes what you buy, because an online tutor serves any emirate identically. It changes what you ask the new school about: inspection history, fee policy, which board they enter and which tier they would place your child in. Those questions are free and more consequential than the tutoring.

sections.heading: A centre in the next community, or one-to-one online
paragraphs: The real alternative in this corridor is often not another home tutor but a tuition centre a few minutes' drive away, and the comparison deserves to be made on the right measure. Hourly rate makes a centre look decisively cheaper. Price per minute of attention directed at your child's specific error makes it look very different.

A group class at a fraction of the one-to-one rate may give a student five to fifteen minutes of individual correction in an hour, with the pace set by the group rather than by your child. That is good value for broad content coverage and shared revision, and poor value for a diagnosed weakness in moles calculations or circuit questions. The error families make is buying one-to-one for coverage and group classes for diagnosis, which is the arrangement exactly inverted.

Then there are the costs nobody quotes. A centre means two car journeys per session, usually at the hour this corridor's roads are busiest, which is a parent's time as well as a student's. It also means a fixed timetable, so a clash with a school activity is a paid session lost and not recovered. Across a school year that is several hours either kept or forfeited, and it belongs in the comparison alongside the headline rate.

And the direct answer on our own format, since this page targets a home-tutor search: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. No tutor will travel to a Shakhbout City address. In-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. The comparison below is between what the corridor offers and what we do.

The corridor-specific point is that the in-home premium here is smaller than on the islands, because the drive is shorter. That is genuinely a point in favour of in-home tutoring in this part of Abu Dhabi, and it would be dishonest not to say so. The gap is still a gap, though: somewhere between AED 30 and AED 200 an hour depending on where the tutor starts from, and across a school year of weekly sessions that is a real figure spent on a journey rather than on teaching.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do, and the permit question
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, and where it exists the boundary is the same. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the mark scheme rewards, question a method until the student finds its weakness, read work the student wrote and name which part undersells it, and teach honest description of a method. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or complete assessed work, produce a model answer to the live task for adaptation, or supply data the student did not collect.

There is an operator in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller, and it is not a service we offer at any fee. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link the official source.

On the permit question, which parents in this corridor ask more than most because so many tutors advertise locally: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted figure with suspicion. One Abu Dhabi-specific point: ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as prohibiting private and charter school staff from giving paid tuition to students at their own school, and the permit code of conduct is reported to bar the same. Treat that as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation or partnership and operates no UAE office.

sections.heading: Coverage, and the honest answer about where the tutors are
paragraphs: Since this page is about comparing locations, the fair thing is to state where our own tutors are. Common IGCSE subjects on both boards are well covered and a trial lesson is usually arranged within a few days to a week. Some subjects are thinner — less-taught languages, a few specialist options — and in those cases we say so before you pay rather than offering a near miss.

Where the right specialist for a subject is not UAE-based, you are told before the trial lesson and the reason is named, and the session is still scheduled in your evening in Gulf Standard Time rather than theirs. That disclosure matters because several providers in this market route UAE parents to contact numbers outside the country without ever stating where the teaching comes from, which a parent discovers only once lessons start at an odd hour.

Coverage also moves through the year. Slots in the main subjects tighten in the second term as families across the corridor and the Gulf reach the same point in the calendar, so the quickest route to a good tutor in February is to have asked in October. If you are reading this in the autumn term with a known weakness, that timing is the most useful line on the page.

And the comparison this page started with, concluded. Whether you live in Shakhbout City, Khalifa City or Mohammed Bin Zayed City, the same specialist is available at the same time for the same work, because nobody is driving. The variable worth optimising is the board and tier match, not the address.

faqs.question: Will I find more IGCSE tutors in Khalifa City than in Shakhbout City?
faqs.answer: More will be listed, and it is largely the same people. These communities sit ten to twenty minutes apart inside one mainland corridor, and a resident tutor assembles a week from short-travel bookings across Khalifa City, Shakhbout City and the near edge of Mohammed Bin Zayed City. So two agency pages titled for two neighbouring communities draw from one list. Where a rate differs by twenty or thirty dirhams, that reflects which end of the corridor the tutor starts from, not what they know about your child's syllabus.

faqs.question: What genuinely differs between Shakhbout City and the communities next to it?
faqs.answer: Housing character and cost, which schools sit immediately adjacent, the curriculum mix those schools run, and community facilities. Mohammed Bin Zayed City has the broadest curriculum range in the emirate, including Indian and Arab curriculum schools alongside British ones. Khalifa City has the densest concentration of international schools. Those differences matter considerably to how you live. None of them determine which IGCSE specialist is free to teach a Year 11 student on a Tuesday evening, which is the thing a tutoring decision turns on.

faqs.question: Does living closer to the school make tutoring easier?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the one educational advantage the address genuinely buys — though it depends on the school rather than the community. A Shakhbout City child at a Khalifa City school is home before four, which supports a 4.30pm session with a student who is still functioning. The same child at a Saadiyat school is home nearer five and needs an evening slot. We plan from the actual arrival time rather than the school's finish time, because the gap between them is where sessions get wasted.

faqs.question: Is the in-home premium smaller in this corridor than elsewhere in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. An in-home tutor serving Shakhbout City is usually travelling ten to twenty-five minutes rather than crossing the city, so less of the quoted rate is journey. The gap is still real: published bands put in-home at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, so somewhere between AED 30 and AED 200 an hour. Across a school year of weekly sessions that remains a substantial sum spent on a drive.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child sit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the syllabus code rather than the subject name. Cambridge codes are four digits — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology. Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1. The boards examine the same subjects with different papers, different tier vocabulary and different mark schemes, and several Pearson subjects allow modular unit entry, which changes revision planning completely. Give the code to any tutor you speak to; whether they ask about the tier and paper pattern tells you a great deal for nothing.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge Core the same as Pearson Foundation?
faqs.answer: No, and treating them as interchangeable is a common error. Cambridge tiers many subjects as Core and Extended; Pearson tiers Mathematics A as Foundation and Higher. The content coverage and the grade ceilings are not identical, the papers differ, and the mark schemes reward differently phrased answers. A tutor talking about Foundation tier when your child is entered for Cambridge Core is working from the wrong map, which is why the syllabus code rather than the tier name is the thing to establish first.

faqs.question: Does moving to another emirate change our child's education framework?
faqs.answer: More than moving between communities does. The regulator differs: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, KHDA in Dubai, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The remit differs too — Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, not just inspection. For tutoring nothing changes, since an online tutor serves any emirate identically; for school choice, a great deal does.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre a few minutes away better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, often not per useful minute. A group class at a fraction of the one-to-one rate may give your child five to fifteen minutes of individual correction in an hour, with the pace set by the group. It is good value for broad content coverage and poor value for a diagnosed weakness. A centre also adds two car journeys per session at the busiest hour and a fixed timetable, so a clash with a school activity is a paid session lost. Use the school's own revision provision before either.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost around Shakhbout City?
faqs.answer: Published market figures read in October 2026: budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 with the drive inside the fee, a named IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650. Monthly, Bestimate's 2026 estimates give AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for exam-year support. Ours follows a free trial.

faqs.question: Will anyone come to our villa in Shakhbout City?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We run no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time. The honest case for that in this corridor is not distance, since a visiting tutor would come from nearby. It is that an online match is made on the syllabus code and tier rather than on who can fit your villa into an evening route, and that the slot can move inside the week when the week demands it.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in this corridor need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applying through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published. Ask any local tutor to show you theirs before the first paid session.

faqs.question: Several teachers at our school tutor locally. Can we use one of them?
faqs.answer: It is not the shortcut it looks like, particularly in Abu Dhabi. ADEK's professional-ethics rules have been reported as prohibiting private and charter school staff from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat both as press-reported and check the current ADEK policy if it affects you. We will not arrange that, and a specialist in the same syllabus from outside the school is usually more candid about the gaps anyway.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my child's coursework?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the mark scheme rewards, question a method until the student finds its weakness, read work the student produced and name which part undersells it, and teach honest method description. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or complete assessed work, produce a model answer to the live task for adaptation, or supply data the student did not collect. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller.

faqs.question: Are board papers and mark schemes included in the fee?
faqs.answer: We link them rather than supply them. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyrighted material belonging to Cambridge or Pearson, and a folder of scans is redistribution of somebody else's property rather than a bonus for you. Papers come through your school's exams officer or the board directly. What a tutor adds is not the paper but the marking of your child's attempt against the real rubric and the naming of what went wrong, which no download can do for you.

faqs.question: When in the year should a Shakhbout City family start looking?
faqs.answer: Autumn if you can. Slots in the main subjects tighten in the second term as families across this corridor and the wider Gulf reach the same point in the calendar, so the quickest route to a good tutor in February is to have asked in October. Autumn is also the cheaper window academically: there is time to change a habit rather than patch a gap, and the tier decision for a Year 10 student has not yet been fixed. By the final term the only purchase available is damage limitation.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-yas-island.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses to Abu Dhabi students, including Yas Island families. Each plans a block against your school's own mock window and entry deadlines rather than against a generic revision timetable.

intro.heading: Two years with four decision points
paragraphs: An International GCSE course is twenty-two months long and contains four moments that actually decide the outcome. The tier decision, usually taken in Year 10 and reviewable for a while afterwards. The final entry, which closes months before the exam window. The mock examinations, which produce the first honest read on where a student will land. And the series itself, after which a narrow set of options opens briefly and then closes.

Everything else is content coverage, and content coverage is what the school does. That is the uncomfortable fact behind most tutoring arrangements on this island and everywhere else: a weekly session that re-teaches the current chapter a few days after the school taught it is not buying much, and it costs the same per hour as a session aimed at one of the four decision points.

The clearest example is the tier. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended, and Core caps the grade a candidate can be awarded. Pearson tiers into Foundation and Higher with the same consequence. A family that discovers in March of Year 11 that their child is capped has discovered it too late, because a tier change is a content change rather than a difficulty change and it needs months rather than weeks. A family that checks in Year 10 has options.

The second clearest is the mock. Mocks are usually treated as a verdict and they are far more useful as a diagnosis. A marked mock paper tells a competent tutor whether losses are clustered in two or three topics, which means a short bounded repair, or scattered as single marks across the whole script, which usually means method is not being written down, rounding is happening too early, or the student is running out of time. Those are different problems and the mock distinguishes them in minutes.

Yas Island adds one genuinely local scheduling factor, which is worth planning for rather than being surprised by. The island hosts large-scale events, including the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend at the end of the first term, and access and road management around those periods change what an evening looks like. For an in-home arrangement that is a cancelled session. For a lesson delivered over live video it is nothing at all, which is one of the more concrete arguments for the format on this particular island.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. What follows is the calendar in detail, with the Cambridge and Pearson dates we can source stated with their sources and nothing restated that a board might revise.

programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a UAE candidate. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong timetable.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other mainstream route in Abu Dhabi, tiered into Foundation and Higher where it applies, with longer unsignposted problem-solving items at Higher tier. Terminal written papers, so the final terms are necessarily about timed practice rather than new content.

The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so read the live version on Pearson's site.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before the International GCSE course, with Checkpoint tests providing the only external read on a student beforehand. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which gives a family three chances to see a strand-level weakness two years before it matters.
programmes.countryNote: On a calendar-led page this is the cheapest intervention available. A weak Checkpoint strand in Year 8 identifies the gap that will otherwise show up as a middling Year 11 mathematics grade, and closing it then costs a fraction of closing it in the final term.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The next step for Yas Island students at schools without the Diploma. The calendar reason to mention it here is that AS entry decisions are made in Year 11, before International GCSE results exist, which means subject choices are provisional and sometimes have to be revisited in August.
programmes.countryNote: The Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency route asks for one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, on top of five International GCSE passes at no less than E or grade 3. That constrains which subjects are worth entering, and it is a Year 10 conversation.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-yas-island.subjectsIntro: Each subject has its own pressure point in the calendar, and a household with a limited budget should know which ones peak when. These entries name the peak as well as the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: Peaks early and late: the tier decision in Year 10 and the timed-paper block after the mocks. Algebraic fluency has to be built across months, which makes it the one subject where early spending genuinely outperforms late spending.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism cost the most marks and are usually taught in the middle of Year 11, which means the gap appears just as revision begins. The practical-skills paper rewards graph discipline that can be drilled quickly and late.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles underpin everything and are taught early, so a Year 10 gap here compounds through two years of the course. Organic conditions and qualitative analysis tests are recall-heavy and respond well to a short block in the final weeks.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: The largest content volume of the sciences, which makes it the subject that absorbs the most revision time in the final term. Command-term discipline is the highest-yield work and can be taught at any point in the two years.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Spread evenly across the course with no single peak, which makes it the subject most often postponed indefinitely. Directed writing against a specific brief is a teachable skill that improves steadily rather than suddenly, so early work pays.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475)
subjects.description: Peaks with the set texts being finished, usually midway through Year 11. A quotation bank built across the year is worth far more than one assembled in the final fortnight, because it has to be recalled under time pressure.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy can be drilled quickly and late; evaluation technique cannot, because reaching a judgement is a habit of written argument. Families who leave Economics to the final weeks get the diagrams and not the top band.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is a technique rather than a body of content, which makes it unusually responsive to a short block at any point. Theory recited without reference to the case caps a candidate mid-band no matter how accurate it is.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are mechanical, teachable and the most reliable marks on the paper. They are also the revision most often skipped, which makes them an efficient target in a compressed block.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Sat in Year 11 alongside 0580, with content a year ahead of where students normally meet it. Needs sustained work across the year rather than a late block, and is the scarcest tutoring specialism in this market.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Case studies have to be learned with their specific figures, which is memory work best spread across months. Skills questions on maps and graphs can be drilled in a short block near the end.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed international curriculum under federal rules covering Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, and timetabled by the school across both years. Worth counting in the revision budget, because families routinely forget the hours it occupies.

modes.description: A short block early in the course aimed at the skills that compound: algebraic fluency in mathematics, mole calculations in chemistry, command-term discipline across the sciences. The cheapest tutoring a family will buy, because it prevents the expensive version later.

modes.description: The main event. A compressed block after the mocks in which papers are sat under conditions and marked together against the published scheme, with the two costliest topics patched between papers. Ninety-minute sessions, because the marking is where the learning happens.

modes.description: A short, targeted block between August results and the November series, aimed only at the papers being re-sat. The decision window is narrow and the work is specific, which makes it one of the easiest blocks to scope and one of the most often missed because families lose weeks deciding.

sections.heading: Years 10 and 11, term by term
paragraphs: Mapped across the two years, an International GCSE course has six phases and each one has a different job. Treating them as six identical weekly sessions is the sequencing error that costs the most, because it spends evenly on a course whose demands are concentrated at the beginning and the end.

Year 10 autumn is foundation. The school is establishing the course and the only tutoring with high marginal value is work on the skills that compound: algebraic manipulation, mole calculations, command terms. Year 10 spring is where the tier question becomes live and where a foundation gap is still cheap to close. Year 10 summer, almost universally wasted, is the best available window for consolidating anything shaky before the content accelerates.

Year 11 autumn is content completion plus the final entry decision, which closes months before the exam window and settles the board, the tier and the subject list. Year 11 winter is mocks, which are a diagnosis rather than a verdict. Year 11 spring is the run-in: timed papers, marking, and targeted repair, with no new content in the final fortnight.

After results in August there is a short phase that families frequently waste. A resit decision for the November series has to be taken quickly, and the work has to start within days rather than weeks. The table sets out the phases with the job each one carries and the cost of skipping it. Read it as a spending guide as much as a teaching one: two of the six phases carry most of the value, and a budget spread evenly across all six buys the least from each.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from a results day
paragraphs: The most useful planning exercise a Yas Island family can do takes fifteen minutes and nobody in this market publishes it. Start at results and work backwards, writing in what must already be true at each step. The exercise produces dates that are months earlier than most families expect, which is exactly why it is worth doing.

For Pearson, the sourced anchors are these: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series. For Cambridge, UAE candidates sit the June and November series, and each exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version.

Working backwards from an August results day: the exam window sits in the preceding summer term, the final entry closed months before that, the mock window fell in the winter, and the last realistic point at which a tier could be changed sat earlier still, in Year 10 or very early Year 11. Each of those steps has a thing that must already be done, and the table states them.

Because official timetables are revised, read the live timetable on the board's own site rather than any date restated on a tutoring page, including this one. Confirm your centre's administrative zone with the school's exams officer: Cambridge is explicit that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's own risk, and that is a sentence worth taking literally.

sections.heading: The November series, and what it is actually for
paragraphs: UAE candidates have two sittings available each year, which is a genuine advantage and is almost never discussed on tutoring pages. Cambridge runs June and November. Pearson runs May/June and November. The February and March series is offered to India only and should be ignored by an Abu Dhabi family entirely.

The November series serves three different purposes and they need different plans. The first is a resit of one or two papers after a June result, which is the most common use and the most time-critical, because the decision window opens with results in August and the work has to start within days. The second is a first sitting for a student who has moved countries or schools mid-course and is out of step with the local cohort. The third is a private candidate entry, arranged with an exam centre rather than with a tutor.

For a resit, the plan is unusually easy to scope. One or two papers, a known starting performance, and a fixed end date. What wastes it is indecision: families who spend four weeks of August and September deciding arrive in October with half the available time gone. The practical rule is to decide within a fortnight of results and start immediately, even if the entry is confirmed slightly later.

For a private candidate, the arrangements are with the exam centre. Entry, fees, identification and the timetable version all come from the centre, and a tutor has no role in any of it beyond the teaching. Anyone presenting themselves as able to arrange an entry should be treated with caution; that is a centre's function, and the Pearson and Cambridge sites explain the route.
