sections.heading: What to do with a mock paper
paragraphs: Mocks arrive in the winter of Year 11 and are usually read as a verdict, which wastes them. A mock is the single richest diagnostic document a family will have before the real thing, and it can be read in fifteen minutes by somebody who knows the specification.

The first question is whether the losses are clustered or scattered. Clustered losses in two or three topics mean a bounded repair of a few sessions. Scattered single-mark losses across the whole script usually mean something structural: method not written down, rounding at intermediate steps, or running out of time. Those three have completely different fixes and none of them is more content teaching.

The second question is about the end of the paper. Blank final questions alongside heavily worked early ones is a timing problem, fixed by practising question order and allocation rather than by learning more. Final questions attempted and scored poorly is a content problem in the strands those questions came from. The distinction is visible at a glance and decides what the next six weeks contain.

The third question is whether the tier is right. A Core or Foundation candidate who lost almost nothing is capped and should be in a review conversation with the school immediately, because the window for a change is closing. An Extended or Higher candidate scoring in the low band on the harder paper may be better served consolidating, which is again a school conversation rather than a tutor's decision. Either way the mock has told you something the grade alone did not.
bullets: Clustered losses mean a short repair; scattered losses mean something structural
Blank final questions are a timing problem, not a knowledge problem
A capped candidate losing almost nothing needs a tier conversation at once
Read the script, not the grade; the grade hides all of this

sections.heading: When Ramadan and the island's event calendar land in the plan
paragraphs: Two scheduling factors specific to this island and this country are worth planning for rather than absorbing as disruption. The first is Ramadan, which shifts approximately eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar and therefore passes through the whole academic year over a run of years, periodically sitting inside the Year 11 spring run-in.

School days shorten during Ramadan, which changes when a student is home, and late-afternoon concentration drops, which makes a ninety-minute timed paper at 17:00 a poor use of a session. Post-Iftar slots work far better for demanding work, and because lessons are delivered over live video a session can move to a later evening without any journey being involved. The sequencing opportunity is to put papers in post-Iftar slots and lighter review in the shortened afternoons. Eid then interrupts the following week or two, and a run-in built with that break accounted for survives while one built as eight consecutive weeks does not.

The second factor is local to Yas Island. The island hosts large-scale events, including the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend at the end of the first term, and access and road management around those periods change what an evening looks like for residents. Concerts and race weekends concentrate traffic at precisely the hours a tutoring session would run.

For an in-home arrangement that is a cancelled or heavily delayed session, repeated across several weekends a year. For a lesson delivered over live video it is not a factor at all. On a calendar-led page that is the most concrete argument the format has on this island: the plan survives the island's own event calendar, which an arrangement depending on a drive does not.
bullets: Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each year and periodically lands in the run-in
Put timed papers in post-Iftar slots and review in shortened afternoons
Build the Eid break into a run-in rather than discovering it
Yas Island event weekends cancel in-home sessions and do not affect online ones

sections.heading: The entry decision, and what closes with it
paragraphs: Final entries close months before the exam window, and when they close, several things become fixed that families assume are still open. The board, the subject list, the tier in each tiered subject, and the papers being sat. After that point the question is no longer what your child will sit but how well they will sit it, and tutoring should change accordingly.

That means the autumn of Year 11 is the last sensible moment for two conversations. The first is the tier conversation: ask the school in writing which tier your child is entered for, subject by subject, and whether a review is possible. The second is the subject-list conversation, which matters if a UAE university is a possibility, because the Ministry's British-track equivalency route counts five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 and excludes Arabic and Islamic education from that count.

A family whose child is taking Arabic, Islamic Education and three other subjects has three towards the five rather than five, and that is worth knowing while the entry is still being settled rather than afterwards. One page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six subjects, which is not the published rule. Equivalency is a Ministry process and nothing about it is performed or guaranteed by a tutoring platform, so verify the current requirement through the Ministry's own channel.

There is one more thing that closes quietly with the entry: the administrative zone of the exam centre, which determines the timetable version your child must use. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and states plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer for the zone and the timetable version at the same time as you ask about the tier.
bullets: Get the tier in writing, by subject, in the autumn of Year 11
Check the subject list against the five-subject equivalency count
Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the count of five
Ask the exams officer for the centre's administrative zone and timetable version

sections.heading: The eight-week run-in, and why it must be booked early
paragraphs: The run-in is the part of the calendar where tutoring earns most and where it is most often improvised. Eight weeks at two sessions a week is sixteen sessions, which at ninety minutes each is enough for roughly six full papers with their marking plus several targeted repair sessions. That arithmetic matters because it tells a family how many papers can realistically be covered and therefore which subjects can be supported at all.

The loop is the same in every subject: sit a paper under genuine conditions, mark it together against the published scheme, name the specific reason for every lost mark, patch the two costliest topics, repeat. The output is a ranked topic list, updated after each paper, which should visibly shorten. If it does not, the diagnosis was wrong rather than the student lazy, and the plan should change rather than continue to its end.

Booking matters because the calendar closes in. A family that decides to arrange a run-in after the mock papers come back finds six usable weeks rather than eight, five other subjects competing for the same hours, and a tired student. Booking during the autumn term as a deliberate decision is what makes the full eight weeks available, and it costs nothing to decide early.

The final fortnight is review only. No new content, no new topics, no new past-paper boards. A student who meets unfamiliar material in the last two weeks loses confidence at exactly the wrong moment, and the marginal value of that material is near zero against the cost. That is a planning decision, which is why it belongs on a page about the calendar rather than in a conversation in May.
bullets: Sixteen ninety-minute sessions is roughly six papers plus repair
The ranked topic list is the artefact; it must shorten
Book the run-in in the autumn term, not after the mocks
The final fortnight is review only, with no new material

sections.heading: Fitting the calendar into a Yas Island evening
paragraphs: A plan is only as good as the sessions it contains, and those have to fit the island's school run. Campuses serving Yas Island finish their taught day between about 14:45 and 15:30, with co-curricular sessions running later on some days. A student at a campus on the island itself is often home by 15:45; a student travelling to the Khalifa City or Al Raha corridor is typically not home before 16:15 and later still on an activity day.

Allowing three quarters of an hour at home, that puts the honest earliest start at 16:30 for an island campus and 17:30 for a mainland commute. Our Abu Dhabi scheduling range runs from 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time. Across a two-year plan the slots that survive are the ones at 18:00 and 18:30, because a slot that only works on an untroubled week will break inside a fortnight, and in a calendar-led plan a broken slot is a missed phase.

Session length should follow the phase. The run-in needs ninety minutes, because the working unit is a paper plus its marking. A Year 10 foundation block works in forty-five or sixty, because short repeated practice beats long explanation for fluency work. A tier-review session needs ninety, because a full higher-tier paper has to be sat. Choosing the duration before the purpose is a common and avoidable waste.

For context on cost, published market bands put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour with travel included against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 for in-home work, Unitors listing International GCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase at AED 270. Those are attributed market figures rather than our prices. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so no part of a rate pays for the island's roads.
bullets: 16:30 for an island campus; 17:30 for a mainland commute
Run-in sessions need ninety minutes; fluency blocks work in forty-five
The durable slots across two years are 18:00 and 18:30 Gulf Standard Time
A late finish or an island event moves the session instead of cancelling it

process.title: Tell us where you are in the two years
process.description: Year 10 autumn, Year 10 spring, Year 11 before entry closes, or Year 11 after mocks. The same symptom needs different treatment at each point, and this single fact changes the recommendation more than the subject does.

process.title: Send the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Cambridge or Pearson, the syllabus code, and the tier in each tiered subject. The school's exams officer can confirm all three in one email, along with the centre's administrative zone and the mock window.

process.title: Send the mock paper, not the grade
process.description: A marked mock with annotations. It distinguishes clustered losses from structural ones, shows whether the paper was finished, and reveals whether the tier is right. The grade alone tells a tutor almost nothing useful.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video at no cost and with no card details taken. Judge it on whether the tutor asked which phase of the course you are in and which series your child is entered for before discussing anything else.

process.title: Book the block with its end date
process.description: A Year 10 foundation block, a tier-review piece, a post-mock run-in or a November resit block. Each has a defined end. Agreeing the end at the start prevents a two-year weekly arrangement forming by default.

process.title: Check the ranked list every fortnight
process.description: In any paper-based block, the topic list should shorten. That is the measurable test and it is a better question than asking how revision is going, which always produces a positive answer regardless of what is happening.

whyPoints.title: Planned against your school's dates
whyPoints.description: Mock windows, entry confirmations and tier review periods are set per campus, and a plan built on them is a plan that can actually be executed. We ask for those dates before recommending a block rather than after.

whyPoints.title: The right block for the phase
whyPoints.description: Foundation work in Year 10, tier evidence while the decision is live, timed papers after the mocks, and a scoped block for a November resit. The same gap deserves different treatment at different points in the calendar.

whyPoints.title: Correct series information for UAE candidates
whyPoints.description: UAE Cambridge candidates sit June and November; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November. Pages quoting a February window at an Abu Dhabi parent are quoting another country's calendar.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: A foundation block, a run-in and a resit block all finish. Agreeing the end at the start is the difference between buying tutoring and acquiring a subscription, and the open-ended weekly arrangement is the most expensive pattern in this market.

whyPoints.title: The island's own calendar accounted for
whyPoints.description: Yas Island event weekends and Ramadan both change what an evening looks like. A plan that accounts for them delivers the hours it promises. Because lessons are over live video, a busy weekend moves a session rather than cancelling it.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and claims stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for Abu Dhabi families are delivered one-to-one over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. We hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office.

faqs.question: When should a Yas Island family start IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: It depends what they are buying. Work on skills that compound, such as algebraic fluency and mole calculations, belongs in Year 10 autumn, because a gap there compounds for two years. Tier evidence belongs in Year 10 spring while the decision is still reviewable. Timed-paper work belongs in the eight weeks after the mocks. A weekly session that re-teaches the current chapter a few days after the school taught it is the lowest-value hour available at any point in the course.

faqs.question: Which exam series will a Yas Island candidate sit?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge, the June series or the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it does not apply to a UAE candidate and any page quoting it is quoting another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. The school's entry decides which, and the exams officer can confirm both the series and the centre's administrative zone, which determines the timetable version your child must use.

faqs.question: When does the tier decision actually close?
faqs.answer: Practically, in Year 10 or very early Year 11, well before the final entry is confirmed. That matters because Core at Cambridge and Foundation at Pearson cap the grade a candidate can be awarded, and a move upwards is a content change rather than a difficulty change: Extended and Higher papers draw on material the lower tier never sets. A family that discovers the cap in March of Year 11 has discovered it too late, which is why the question belongs in Year 10.

faqs.question: What should we do with my child's mock paper?
faqs.answer: Read the script rather than the grade. Three questions answer themselves in fifteen minutes. Are the losses clustered in two or three topics, which means a short repair, or scattered as single marks, which usually means method is not written down, rounding happens too early, or the paper is not being finished? Were the final questions attempted or blank? And does a capped candidate who lost almost nothing need a tier conversation with the school immediately?

faqs.question: How does the November series work as a resit route?
faqs.answer: It is the main advantage UAE candidates have and it is time-critical. The decision window opens when August results arrive and the work should start within a fortnight, not after four weeks of deliberation. A resit is unusually easy to scope: one or two papers, a known starting performance and a fixed end date. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: Do Yas Island event weekends really affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: They affect an in-home arrangement considerably. The island hosts large-scale events, including the Grand Prix weekend at the end of the first term, and access and road management around those periods concentrate traffic at exactly the hours an evening session would run. Across a year that is several cancelled or heavily delayed visits. For a lesson delivered over live video it is not a factor, which on this island is one of the more concrete arguments for the format.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan for an Abu Dhabi Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the plan should assume it rather than react to it. Ramadan shifts roughly eleven days earlier each year, so it periodically lands inside the Year 11 spring run-in. School days shorten, changing arrival times home, and late-afternoon concentration drops. Put the timed papers in post-Iftar slots and the lighter review in the shortened afternoons. Build the Eid break into the run-in: eight consecutive weeks planned without it will lose a fortnight.

faqs.question: How many past papers does a run-in actually fit?
faqs.answer: About six, properly marked. Eight weeks at two sessions a week is sixteen sessions, and at ninety minutes each that covers roughly six full papers with their marking plus several targeted repair sessions. The arithmetic is worth doing in advance because it tells you how many subjects can realistically be supported. Twenty papers with their answers checked against a list teaches far less than six marked against the published scheme with reasons named for every lost mark.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to Yas Island homes?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, including Yas Island; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. On a calendar-led page the consequence is practical: a late school finish, an island event weekend or a family trip moves a session rather than cancelling it, so the plan delivers the hours it promised.

faqs.question: When does the final entry close and what closes with it?
faqs.answer: Months before the exam window, and when it closes the board, the subject list, the tier in each tiered subject and the papers being sat all become fixed. The administrative zone of the exam centre is settled too, which determines the timetable version your child must use. After that point the question is no longer what your child sits but how well, and tutoring should shift from coverage and tier questions to technique accordingly.

faqs.question: Why does the subject list matter for UAE university plans?
faqs.answer: Because the Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency route, as reported in July 2026, counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included in that count. A student taking Arabic, Islamic Education and three others has three towards the five. One page currently ranking in this market states six subjects, which is not the rule. Verify the current requirement through the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: What should the last two weeks before the exams contain?
faqs.answer: Review only. No new content, no new topics and no past papers from a different board. A student who meets unfamiliar material in the final fortnight loses confidence at the worst possible moment, and the marginal value of that material is close to zero against the cost. The useful work is re-reading the ranked topic list, re-sitting a paper already seen, and sleeping. That is a planning decision which has to be made in advance.

faqs.question: How long should an IGCSE session be during the run-in?
faqs.answer: Ninety minutes. The working unit in a run-in is a paper sat under genuine conditions plus the marking afterwards, and cutting the marking defeats the purpose because the marking is where the learning happens. Sixty minutes is right for a Year 10 fluency block, where short repeated practice beats long explanation, and forty-five can be enough for pure drill work. Decide the purpose first and the duration follows from it.

faqs.question: Should a Yas Island family use the summer break between Year 10 and Year 11?
faqs.answer: It is the most under-used window in the whole course. Content accelerates in Year 11 autumn, and a known weakness carried into that term gets worse rather than better because nothing slows down to accommodate it. A short block across those weeks consolidating algebraic fluency, moles or command-term discipline buys back time in a term that will not have any. Almost no family uses it, which is why it is worth naming.

faqs.question: What is the first thing to ask my child's school in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Five things in one email: the board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier in each tiered subject and whether a review is possible, the mock examination window, the final entry deadline the centre is working to, and the centre's Cambridge administrative zone. Those five answers let a whole year be planned backwards in an afternoon. Most families collect them piecemeal across the year and have them complete only once the decisions have closed.

intro.heading: What the words "near me" are actually asking for
paragraphs: A parent in Abu Dhabi typing that phrase is almost never asking about distance for its own sake. They are asking three questions in one breath: can someone reliable start soon, will they understand my child's school and syllabus, and will I be able to tell whether it is doing any good. Distance is a proxy for the first and has nothing to do with the second or third. The search engine answers the proxy. This page answers the questions underneath it.

Start with the geography, because in this emirate it is not a detail. Abu Dhabi spreads across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, Saadiyat and Yas, and the newer mainland communities out past Al Shamkha and Al Falah. A family in Al Reef looking for a Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 Chemistry specialist within a short drive is searching a pool of a handful of people, most of whom teach something else. The same family searching without the distance filter is choosing from everyone who has taught that exact code to Year 11 students.

So the honest answer to the search is this: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Abu Dhabi families are one-to-one over live video, in your child's own room, at a time set by your school run rather than by a tutor's route across the emirate. The reason that is a better deal rather than a lesser one is the pool, and the proof is in what the sessions produce.

Which brings this page to its real subject. The thing almost nobody discusses when they advertise tutoring is how a parent is supposed to know it is working. Children say the tutor is nice. Tutors say the child is engaging well. Three months pass and a mock result arrives that nobody saw coming. The fix is not more communication, it is evidence produced on purpose: the student's own answers, marked against the published mark scheme, with the mark and the reason recorded so the pattern of lost marks can be watched over six weeks.

That evidence is also the only honest basis for continuing. If the pattern of lost marks has not shifted in six sessions, the plan should change or stop, and a provider who cannot show you the pattern cannot tell you which. Nobody on this page promises a grade, and any tutor who does is describing something no teacher controls: grade boundaries move between series, and a student's performance on the day is theirs. What can be promised is that you will be able to see what changed, in your child's own handwriting, against the board's own marking criteria, week by week.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: The qualification on the certificate changes what the evidence should look like, because each one is marked differently. These are the four routes Abu Dhabi families are tracking, and what counts as proof of progress in each.

programmes.name: Cambridge International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written papers against four-digit syllabus codes: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English First Language, 0455 Economics. Several syllabuses are tiered, with Core and Extended papers leading to different grade ceilings. Evidence of progress here is concrete: a marked past-paper question, the mark awarded, and the specific mark-scheme point that was missed.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the widest provision across Abu Dhabi's British curriculum schools, so most families in the emirate are tracking a Cambridge code. The first thing to confirm before gathering any evidence is which tier the school has entered the student for, because a Core candidate marked against Extended papers will look much worse than they are, and that mistake is common in the first fortnight of tutoring.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes include 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Exams run in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel specialists per subject are a thinner pool inside Abu Dhabi than Cambridge specialists, which is exactly where a proximity search fails a family. The code matters more than the subject name for evidence purposes: a 4CH1 mark scheme rewards different phrasing from a 0620 one, so marked work has to be marked against the right document to mean anything.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, each subject carrying an internally assessed component. Evidence looks different here: alongside marked exam questions sit internal assessment drafts, where the only legitimate tutor contribution is feedback on work the student has already written.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session. IB exam and results dates are the one set of figures not published on these pages, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and nothing in this project has been confirmed from the board itself. For any specific date, ask your school's IB coordinator or read it on ibo.org rather than taking it from a tutoring site.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The post-IGCSE route in most British curriculum schools in the emirate. Evidence at this level is almost entirely about extended answers and multi-step problems, so the useful artefact is a marked long-answer question with the method marks separated from the accuracy marks, which is where most of the loss sits.
programmes.countryNote: This is also the qualification Ministry of Education equivalency asks for on the British track, alongside the IGCSE count. The published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. Verify the current wording through the Ministry's own channel; equivalency is a process the authorities run.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: Marks go missing in patterns, and the pattern is subject-specific. These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families book most, with the lost-mark pattern a first marked paper usually reveals in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Method marks lost to unshown working, and accuracy marks lost to premature rounding. A marked script separates the two, which matters because they need different fixes: one is a habit, the other is a technique. Tier confirmation comes first, since Core papers cap the grade available.

subjects.name: Physics (0625, 4PH1)
subjects.description: Units, significant figures and the maths of graphs. The characteristic loss is a correct physical idea written without the quantity it applies to. Electricity questions and the practical or alternative-to-practical component are where a marked script usually shows the clearest, most repairable pattern.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic mechanisms account for most of the loss, along with state symbols and balancing in equations. These are high-density marks: a student who fixes equation presentation alone often picks up several marks across a paper, which shows up quickly in six weeks of evidence.

subjects.name: Biology (0610, 4BI1)
subjects.description: Command-word failure dominates. A student who describes a graph when asked to explain it has lost the marks before content was ever in question. Marked scripts in biology are the clearest demonstration of why technique work outperforms content revision for many students.

subjects.name: English First and Second Language (0500, 0510, 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing against the task's audience and purpose, and analysis that quotes without explaining. The evidence here is a marked response with the band descriptors attached, so a parent can see which band the writing sits in and what the next band requires in concrete terms.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475, 4ET1)
subjects.description: Essays that narrate the text rather than argue about it. Progress is visible through successive marked essays on the same set text, where the shift from retelling to argument is measurable in the examiner's own language rather than in a tutor's impression.

subjects.name: Economics and Business (0455, 0450, 4EC1)
subjects.description: Evaluation marks left on the table and diagrams drawn without labels or shifts. Evaluation is a transferable technique, so a marked paper that shows no evaluation attempted is a cheap and fast repair compared with missing content.

subjects.name: History and Geography (0470, 0460)
subjects.description: Source utility answers that summarise rather than judge, and case-study detail left generic. The marked script shows this instantly: paragraphs with no named example score below paragraphs with one, regardless of how well written they are.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Three strands compressed, so the lost-mark pattern often differs by strand within the same paper. A marked script broken down by strand tells you which of the three actually needs the hours, which is usually a surprise to the family.

subjects.name: Additional and International Mathematics (0606, 0607)
subjects.description: A scarce tutor pool locally, which is precisely where proximity searching fails. 0607 carries a different structure and a graphic display calculator expectation, and marked evidence should show calculator-method marks separately from analytic ones.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (0478, 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode notation and trace tables, where the mark scheme is specific about form. A student who codes well can still lose heavily on notation, and a marked script is the only way a parent would ever discover that distinction exists.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508, 0544)
subjects.description: Taught alongside the licensed curriculum in every UAE private school. Marked evidence focuses on script accuracy and the structure of extended written responses. Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track Ministry equivalency.

sections.heading: Why searching by distance returns the wrong tutor in this emirate
paragraphs: A proximity search optimises for the one variable that has no effect on a grade. What decides whether a Year 11 student picks up marks is whether the tutor knows the specific paper: the syllabus code, the mark scheme's preferred phrasing, the tier the student is entered for, and the question types that recur. None of that correlates with how far away someone lives, and in a city shaped like Abu Dhabi the distance filter removes most of the qualified pool before you have looked at anyone.

Work through the arithmetic for one family. A student in Al Shamkha takes Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 Chemistry and needs help with moles calculations and organic mechanisms. The set of people who teach 4CH1 well is reasonably large. The set within a twenty-five-minute drive of Al Shamkha at 5pm on a weekday is very small, and most of them teach Cambridge 0620 instead, which is a different paper structure with a different mark scheme. The distance filter has just traded the thing that matters for the thing that is convenient.

There is a second cost that families notice later. An in-home arrangement is fragile in ways an online one is not. The tutor's car, the tutor's other commitments, the traffic on the airport road, a slot that can only exist because it fits a geographic route. When that breaks, the replacement is drawn from the same tiny local pool. An online arrangement that breaks is replaced from the whole pool, usually within the same week.

So the position taken here is explicit rather than buried. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at an Abu Dhabi address; home tutoring at a family's address exists only in the India service. What replaces it is a one-to-one lesson over live video at a time your school run allows, with a tutor chosen for the syllabus code on your child's entry. sections.heading: The evidence file: what you should be holding after six weeks
paragraphs: This is the part of tutoring almost nobody specifies, and it is the only part that lets a parent make a decision. After six weekly sessions you should be holding six marked scripts, each one a timed past-paper question the student attempted without help, each marked against the published mark scheme, each annotated with the mark awarded and the mark-scheme point that was missed. Together they are a record, and a record can be read.

What you are reading for is not the mark going up every week, because question difficulty varies and a harder question can produce a lower mark from a stronger student. You are reading for the pattern of loss changing. In week one a Chemistry student loses four marks to unbalanced equations and two to rounding. By week six, if the equation marks are still going, the teaching has not landed and the plan needs changing. If they have stopped and the loss has moved to a harder topic, that is progress even if the raw mark is flat.

Three further artefacts belong in the file. The lost-mark tally, which is just a running count by category: command word, working, units, content, presentation. The marks-to-boundary figure from the school's own mock, which is the only grade-shaped number in the file and should be treated as an estimate because boundaries move between series. And a one-line note after each session saying what was taught and what to do before next week, so the weeks between sessions are not blank.

The discipline that makes this work is comparability. Same subject, same mark scheme, same conditions, same marker. A file of six scripts marked six different ways tells you nothing. At the six-session point the whole file gets reviewed in one sitting with you, and there are only three honest outcomes: the pattern has shifted and the plan continues, it has not shifted and the plan changes, or it has not shifted twice and tutoring in this subject should stop.

sections.heading: How a mark scheme marks, and why your child's answer scored what it did
paragraphs: Parents often assume marks are lost through not knowing things. Marked scripts say otherwise. A large share of lost IGCSE marks come from answering a question that was not asked, from not showing the step that earns the method mark, from omitting a unit, or from writing a correct idea in a form the mark scheme does not credit. Those are all repairable in weeks, and none of them require learning new content.

Command words are the first and biggest category. Describe, explain, compare, evaluate, justify, state, suggest and calculate ask for different things, and the mark scheme allocates against what was asked. A biology student who describes a graph beautifully when the question said explain has not written a weak answer; they have written an answer to a different question. Fixing that is a matter of a few weeks of forced practice, with the command word underlined before anything is written.

Method and accuracy marks are the second. In maths and physics, marks are awarded for the steps, not only the final number, which means a student who writes only an answer forfeits the method marks even when the answer is right, and gains nothing when it is wrong. The habit fix is mechanical: write the formula, substitute, then evaluate, every time. A marked script makes the cost of skipping that visible in a way no amount of being told does.

The third category is presentation, and it is the cheapest of all. State symbols in a chemistry equation. Axes labelled with units. Significant figures carried to the end rather than rounded in the middle. A labelled shift on an economics diagram. A named example in a geography paragraph. Each is worth a mark or two, and across a full paper they often add up to more than a whole topic would. A student who fixes presentation in three weeks will see movement in the evidence file before any content work has begun.

sections.heading: Grade movement, described honestly
paragraphs: No tutor can promise a grade and nobody on this page will. Two things stand in the way, and both are outside anyone's control. Grade boundaries are set per series after the papers have been sat, so the mark needed for a 7 this summer is not necessarily the mark needed last summer. And performance on the day belongs to the student, who may be ill, nervous or unlucky with the question selection.

What can be described is distance. Ask the school for the student's mock mark and, where they will share it, the boundary the school used. The difference is the marks-to-boundary figure, and it changes the conversation from a vague hope into an arithmetic problem. Four marks short is a short technique block. Twenty-five marks short in the same subject is a different project, and pretending otherwise is how families end up disappointed by work that was always going to be insufficient.

Ranking subjects by that figure is the most useful thing a parent can do with an afternoon. Most families find one subject sitting a handful of marks below a boundary and one sitting far below. The first is cheap, fast and high-return. The second needs a longer plan or a decision to accept the grade and protect the others. Spending the available hours on the near-boundary subjects first moves more grades for the same money, and the evidence file is what tells you when a subject has moved far enough to stop.

Treat boundary figures as estimates throughout, and take them from the school or from a board's own published materials rather than from a tutoring page. This page publishes no boundary tables, no past papers and no mark schemes, because those documents belong to the boards and reproducing them is not ours to do. Your child's school has them, the boards publish them, and a tutor should be working from the official versions rather than from a copy.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi afternoon, and the time a session can realistically start
paragraphs: Session timing is the most underrated variable in whether tutoring works, and in Abu Dhabi it is almost entirely a function of where you live. A student who boards a bus at 6:40am and gets home at 3:30pm has a different afternoon from one picked up at 2:45pm ten minutes from school. The first will produce poor evidence at 4pm and good evidence at 5:30pm. The second is the reverse, because by 5:30pm the day is over.

The table below is the planning tool. It is drawn from what Abu Dhabi families actually report about their own routines rather than from traffic data, so treat it as a starting point for your household rather than a measurement. Its purpose is narrow: to pick the slot at which your child can do a timed, unaided question and have the result mean something. A marked script produced at the wrong hour is evidence of tiredness, not of ability.

The weekend is the other half of the answer and is routinely wasted. A full past paper under timed conditions takes an hour and a half to two hours, which does not fit a weekday evening after school, and compressing it ruins the evidence. Saturday morning is where that belongs, with the marking session following midweek. Families who split the work this way get a far more useful record than those who try to do everything in a weekday hour.

Because lessons are delivered over live video, the slot is set by the student's day rather than by a tutor's route. There is no arrival time, no parking, no travel buffer either side, and no minimum booking length imposed to make a journey worthwhile. For families in Al Reef, Al Shamkha and the outer parts of Khalifa City, that is the practical difference between a session at a sensible hour and a session squeezed into whenever a tutor could get there.

sections.heading: Working from the school's own assessments rather than around them
paragraphs: A tutor who ignores the school's assessment calendar generates a second, parallel version of the course, and the student ends up serving two masters. The better arrangement treats the school as the primary source of data. Its mocks, its unit tests, its predicted grades and its marked feedback are the richest evidence a family already has, and most of it goes unread beyond the number on the front.

Three things are worth asking the school for, and all three are usually given freely. The mark breakdown by question or by topic, rather than the total. The boundary the school applied when converting that mark to a grade, flagged as an estimate. And which assessment objectives the department thinks the student is weakest against. With those, a tutor can scope a block in one session instead of spending three sessions discovering what the school already knew.

Abu Dhabi's private schools are overseen by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection outcomes. Those reports are a useful read for a parent trying to understand the context their child is working in, particularly where a report comments specifically on assessment and feedback practice. ADEK is named here because it is useful to know what it governs; it does not inspect, license or endorse IB Gram, which holds no permit, centre or office in the emirate.

One boundary is worth stating here as well. Press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules describes a prohibition on school staff providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and notes that teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is secondary reporting, so verify it against ADEK's current published policy. The underlying principle is sound: the person marking your child's school work should not also be paid to prepare them for it.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the UAE calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: The UAE academic year has a shape that exam preparation has to be planned around, and it is a shape nobody writing about tutoring seems to mention. The spring term carries the heaviest load for a Year 11 student: mocks, coursework deadlines, and then the run-up to a May or June series. Ramadan falls within that window, school hours shorten, and the rhythm of a household changes for a month.

What that means in practice is that the hours available between February and April are fewer than the calendar suggests, and the hours available in October and November are more than families use. A twenty-hour block bought in the autumn sits on a student with capacity. The same twenty hours bought in March compete with mocks, with coursework and with fasting, and each hour achieves less. The cheapest intervention available to an Abu Dhabi family is simply doing the work earlier.

During Ramadan the sensible adjustment is to session timing rather than session content. Families commonly move to later evening slots after Iftar, or to a shorter session earlier in the day at the weekend, and keep the same tutor and the same subject throughout. Because lessons are online, shifting a slot is a scheduling message rather than a renegotiation with someone's driving route, and the evidence file continues uninterrupted, which matters when a six-week review is in progress.

Summer deserves one line too. Abu Dhabi's long break is where a Year 10 student either consolidates or slides, and families who travel across time zones often stop entirely for ten weeks. Two short sessions a week through July and August, aimed at holding technique rather than teaching ahead, keep the record continuous and avoid a September restart from a worse position than June ended on.

sections.heading: What happens when the evidence says this is not working
paragraphs: Most tutoring arrangements end badly by drifting rather than by decision: the sessions continue, the invoices continue, and nobody wants to be the one who says it has stopped helping. Having a record removes that problem, because at the six-session review the file either shows a shifted pattern of lost marks or it does not, and that is a fact rather than an opinion.

There are three legitimate reasons the pattern has not moved, and each has a different response. The match is wrong, in which case the tutor changes and the plan does not. The diagnosis is wrong, usually because the problem turned out to be reading speed, or an untreated gap two years further back, in which case the plan changes and the tutor may not. Or the frequency is wrong, which happens when a student is given one hour a week against a twenty-five-mark gap and nothing between sessions.

A fourth possibility deserves saying out loud, because providers rarely do: the subject may not be where the money should go. A student twenty-five marks below a boundary in one subject and four marks below in another will get more from fixing the second. The honest recommendation is sometimes to stop paying for the subject you asked about and start on the one you did not, and a provider that cannot bring itself to say that is not reading the evidence with you.

If no UAE-based tutor covers a syllabus in the slot you need, we will say so rather than filling the slot with whoever is free. The alternative offered may be a tutor based outside the UAE teaching in your time zone, disclosed before you book. Across the competitor pages reviewed for this project, not one discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying where delivery happens. A stated limit is more useful to a parent than a concealed one.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE home tutor near me actually find the right tutor in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It finds the nearest one, which is a different thing. What moves marks is whether the tutor knows the specific paper: the syllabus code, the tier, the mark scheme's preferred phrasing and the recurring question types. None of that correlates with distance, and in an emirate spread from Saadiyat to Al Shamkha the distance filter removes most of the qualified pool before you have looked at anyone. IB Gram does not visit homes anywhere in the UAE; lessons are one-to-one over live video, with the tutor matched to the code on your child's exam entry.

faqs.question: What evidence should I have after six weeks of IGCSE tutoring?
faqs.answer: Six marked scripts, each a timed past-paper question your child attempted without help, marked against the published mark scheme with the mark and the missed mark-scheme point recorded. Alongside them, a running tally of lost marks by category, a short note after each session saying what was taught and what to do before the next one, and a marks-to-boundary estimate from the school's own mock. That file is readable: either the pattern of loss has shifted by week six or it has not, and that is a fact rather than an impression.

faqs.question: How do you mark my child's work and what do I get to see?
faqs.answer: The last part of each session is a timed question the student does alone, which the tutor then marks against the published mark scheme rather than against a personal opinion. You receive the script itself, the mark awarded, and the specific mark-scheme point that was lost, usually the same evening. Over six sessions you also receive a tally grouping losses into command word, working, units, content and presentation, because the category is what decides where the next block of hours should go.

faqs.question: Can you tell me what grade my child will get?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who does is describing something no teacher controls. Grade boundaries are set per series after the papers have been sat, so the mark needed for a given grade this summer is not necessarily last summer's mark. Performance on the day belongs to the student. What can be described is distance: ask the school for the mock mark and the boundary it applied, treat the difference as an estimate, and track whether that gap closes. Four marks short and twenty-five marks short are different projects and should be funded differently.

faqs.question: Why does my child's mark go down on a harder past paper?
faqs.answer: Because question difficulty varies between papers and across topics, so a raw mark is not a clean measure of progress. This is exactly why the evidence file tracks the pattern of lost marks rather than the mark itself. A student who stops losing marks on unbalanced equations and starts losing them on a harder organic question has improved, even though the total may be flat or lower. If the same category of loss is still appearing in week six, that is the signal that the teaching has not landed.

faqs.question: How do I know the tutoring is working and not just keeping my child busy?
faqs.answer: Ask for the three things that make it checkable: a timed, unaided question marked against the published mark scheme every session, a tally of losses by category, and a review date set before the first session. Help given during a lesson proves only that the tutor can do the question. The unaided attempt is the evidence. If after six sessions the loss categories have not moved, the honest outcomes are a different tutor, a different diagnosis, a higher frequency, or stopping, and the file tells you which.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE session start if the school bus gets home at 3:30?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume. A student arriving home after 3:30pm from Al Reef or the outer parts of Khalifa City will produce a poor timed script at 4pm and a usable one at 5:30pm. Island families with short pick-ups are the reverse and do better at 4pm. Because lessons are delivered over live video there is no arrival time or travel buffer, so the slot is set by your child's day. Full timed papers belong on a Saturday morning, with the marking review midweek.

faqs.question: Do you work from my child's own school assessments?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are the richest evidence a family already holds. Three things are worth asking the school for and are usually given: the mark breakdown by question or topic rather than the total, the boundary the school applied when converting to a grade, and which assessment objectives the department thinks the student is weakest against. With those, a block can be scoped in one session rather than spending three sessions rediscovering what the school already knew. The school stays the primary source; the tutoring works to its calendar.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects lose the most marks to command words?
faqs.answer: Biology and Geography are the clearest cases, followed by Economics and Business. Describe, explain, compare, evaluate, justify, state, suggest and calculate ask for different things, and marks are allocated against what was asked. A student who describes a graph when the question said explain has written a good answer to a different question. The repair takes a few weeks of forced practice with the command word underlined before anything is written, and it shows up in the evidence file faster than any content work does.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change the IGCSE revision schedule?
faqs.answer: The adjustment is to timing, not to content. School hours shorten, household rhythms change for the month, and it falls inside the heaviest part of a Year 11 year alongside mocks and coursework deadlines. Families commonly move to a later evening slot after Iftar, or to a shorter weekend session earlier in the day, keeping the same tutor and subject so the evidence file stays continuous. The broader point is that hours bought in October and November are easier to schedule and more productive than the same hours bought in March.

faqs.question: Will my child's school know we are using a tutor?
faqs.answer: Only if you tell them, and telling them is usually worth it. A department that knows a student is getting extra support will often share the mark breakdown and the assessment objectives it is most concerned about, which makes the tutoring sharper and cheaper. There is no requirement to disclose private tuition to a school. What we would avoid is any arrangement where your child's own class teacher is paid to tutor them, since Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules as reported bar school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

faqs.question: What does a predicted grade mean and can a tutor change it?
faqs.answer: A predicted or forecast grade is the school's professional estimate, based on its own evidence, and it belongs to the school. Cambridge requires a forecast grade from the centre ahead of each series, and for a June sitting that submission falls in the spring term, earlier than most families expect; the exams officer at the school can give you the deadline for your centre. A tutor cannot change a prediction and should not try to. What a tutor can do is help the student produce better evidence for the school to look at before that submission closes, which is a different and legitimate route. If you disagree with a prediction, the conversation is with the department, supported by marked work.

faqs.question: How many past papers should my child do before the series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families imagine, done properly. A paper attempted under timed conditions, marked against the published mark scheme, and then reworked on the questions that were lost is worth more than five papers skimmed and self-marked generously. A reasonable shape for a final term is one full timed paper a fortnight on a Saturday morning, with the midweek session spent on the losses from it. Papers and mark schemes should come from the board or the school's own copies rather than from a tutoring site.

faqs.question: What happens if six weeks of evidence shows no movement?
faqs.answer: One of four things changes, and the file usually says which. The match may be wrong, so the tutor changes and the plan does not. The diagnosis may be wrong, often because the real issue is reading speed or a gap two years earlier, so the plan changes. The frequency may be wrong, which is common when one weekly hour is set against a twenty-five-mark gap. Or the subject may be the wrong place for the money, in which case the honest recommendation is to stop this subject and fund one nearer a boundary.

faqs.question: Is there a tutor in my area of Abu Dhabi who teaches Edexcel Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and that is the wrong question to optimise for. Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 specialists are a thinner pool per subject inside the emirate than Cambridge 0620 specialists, so an area filter often returns someone who teaches the other board's paper structure instead. Since lessons are delivered over live video, the search is by syllabus code across the whole pool rather than by postcode across a handful of people. If no UAE-based tutor covers your code in the slot you want, we will say so and name the alternative before you book.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Ask to see a marked script before you book anything
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-near-me.closingBody: The single most useful question a parent can ask any tutoring provider in Abu Dhabi is to see an example of a marked student script: the timed question, the mark against the published mark scheme, and the note explaining what was lost and why. A provider who can produce one is running the kind of arrangement you can audit. A provider who offers a verbal account instead is asking you to take three months on trust. Start with a free trial lesson, no card details taken, which ends with exactly that artefact for your own child, on your child's own syllabus code, at a time your school run allows.

intro.heading: The skill that separates a maths tutor from a mathematician
paragraphs: Al Bandar sits inside the Al Raha Beach development, within a short drive of several strong international schools, and a family here has no trouble finding somebody competent at mathematics. What is harder to find, and what actually changes an IGCSE grade, is somebody who can read a published mark scheme and explain why a particular script earned two marks out of four when the final answer was right. Those are different abilities, and only the second one is being bought when a family hires an exam-year tutor.

The reason is that IGCSE mathematics is not marked on whether the answer is correct. It is marked on specified method, specified accuracy and specified independent results, in a document the board publishes after every series. A candidate who computes three steps mentally and writes a correct final answer may earn full credit, or may earn nothing at all if the answer is wrong, because there is no visible method to award. A candidate who shows every line and makes an arithmetic slip at the end usually keeps most of the marks. Students are rarely taught this, and it is the single largest source of avoidable loss we see across Abu Dhabi.

So this page is about the mark scheme rather than about tutoring. It sets out the three kinds of mark on an IGCSE maths paper and how each is lost. It goes through Cambridge 0580 Extended topic by topic with the characteristic loss and the fix for each. It gives an eight-week past-paper regimen that a family can run with or without a tutor, because the regimen does most of the work and the tutor's job is to mark and diagnose. And it explains what the next step, whether A-Level or the IB Diploma, expects from an IGCSE maths grade.

What proximity cannot supply is this specific knowledge. A tutor living fifteen minutes away is a convenience; a tutor who has marked 0580 Paper 4 against the scheme is a capability. In a community with as many options as this one, the risk is not being unable to find anyone. It is choosing on availability and manner, because nothing in a profile distinguishes the two, and then spending a term having content re-explained to a student who already understands it.

One statement of model before the detail. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which also happens to be the format in which a shared mark scheme and a shared script are easiest to read together. We publish no rate card on this page: the trial lesson is free with no card required, and a quote follows the diagnosis.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 (Extended)
subjects.description: Method marks dominate the long structured questions, and accuracy marks are lost to early rounding carried forward. The non-calculator paper is where strong students most often lose marks on work they fully understand.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 (Core)
subjects.description: Independent marks on straightforward items carry the grade here, so question order matters more than ambition. The aim is to bank every reliable mark before fatigue, then attempt the harder items with whatever time remains.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: The graphics calculator changes what counts as method: a solution read from a graph still needs the reasoning written. The investigation component rewards a written argument, and bare correct answers score poorly against it.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two calculator papers graded 9 to 1, with marks lost mainly in the long multi-step questions at the back where candidates stop reading after the first clause. Follow-through marks make visible working even more valuable here.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Calculus, series and coordinate geometry taken alongside 4MA1 by stronger candidates. Almost all the tutoring value is in handling unfamiliar question structures, which is mark-scheme work rather than content coverage.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The same mark logic applies: rearrangement shown, substitution shown, units stated. Candidates lose marks describing when the command term says explain, and the practical paper punishes that more than the theory papers do.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations are marked like mathematics, with method credit for the route taken even when the arithmetic fails. Students who write only a final number are throwing away the most reliable marks on the paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Extended responses are marked against a list of acceptable points, so structure and coverage beat eloquence. Students who write a paragraph rather than distinct points routinely score below what they know.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: Diagram marks are independent and reliable, which makes them the first thing to secure. Evaluation marks require a judgement supported by the data, and that is a format to practise rather than a topic to revise.

sections.heading: How IGCSE maths marks are actually awarded
paragraphs: A published mark scheme allocates marks of three kinds, and understanding the difference changes how a student writes. Method marks are awarded for a correct approach, visible on the page, whether or not the arithmetic that follows is right. Accuracy marks are awarded for a correct value, usually conditional on the method mark having been earned and on the answer being given to the stated degree of accuracy. Independent marks are awarded for a particular correct result or statement on its own terms, without needing any preceding working.

Schemes also carry conventions that students benefit from knowing. A follow-through allowance credits later work that is correct given an earlier wrong value, which means a single slip need not destroy a whole question provided the subsequent working is visible. Or-equivalent notes accept alternative correct forms. A correct-answer-only note means no method credit is available, so on those items the value alone matters. Cambridge and Pearson use different letter notations for these, but the logic is the same in both.

The consequence is simple to state and hard to install. Write everything. A student who shows the rearrangement, the substitution and the evaluation collects method marks even on a question they finish wrongly, and benefits from follow-through on the parts afterwards. A student who works mentally and writes one line collects everything when they are right and nothing when they are not. Across a full paper that difference is routinely worth a grade, and it has nothing to do with how much mathematics the student knows. This is the entire argument for buying marking rather than teaching in Year 11.

sections.heading: Where Cambridge 0580 Extended marks go missing, topic by topic
paragraphs: After enough diagnostic papers the pattern stops being random. The same topics generate the same losses, and most of them are late additions to a scheme of work that were never consolidated. Bearings is the clearest example: students know what a bearing is and still lose marks for measuring from the wrong reference or omitting the three-figure form. Similar-shape scale factors is the second, where the area factor is the square and the volume factor the cube of the length factor, and candidates apply the length factor to all three.

Compound percentage change is third, usually because the reverse problem is treated as a forward one. Histograms with unequal class widths is fourth and is almost entirely a frequency-density problem. Vectors is fifth, where the notation rather than the geometry defeats students. Then algebraic fractions, where a sign error in the numerator ends an otherwise correct solution, and simultaneous equations with one non-linear equation, where candidates substitute correctly and then abandon the quadratic.

None of these requires many hours. Each is a recognisable question type with a recognisable loss and a short fix, which is why a well-aimed block of six to eight sessions can move a grade when a term of general revision did not. The table gives the loss and the fix for each, with a realistic session count. Use it as a checklist against your child's marked papers rather than as a curriculum: if a topic is not costing marks, it does not need sessions.

sections.heading: The eight-week past-paper regimen
paragraphs: This is the pattern that produces the most reliable improvement in the final stretch, and a family can run most of it without buying anything. The principle is one full paper a week, sat to the published duration, marked against the scheme within forty-eight hours, with the three largest loss categories carried into the following week as targets. The marking is the active ingredient. A paper sat and scored is a thermometer; a paper sat and classified is a plan.

Two scheduling notes for this belt. School runs here are short, so children are often home early enough for a 16:30 or 17:00 session, which makes a weekday slot genuinely workable rather than theoretical. But a full paper plus a walkthrough is a two-hour commitment, so the paper belongs at the weekend and the walkthrough in the weekday slot, not the other way round. And frequency has to fall during the school's own assessment weeks, because a student cannot run two revision programmes at once.

A word on what not to do. Do not shorten papers; the back of a paper is where pacing failures appear and a shortened paper hides them. Do not mark leniently; the scheme is the standard and a generous mark teaches nothing. Do not repeat a paper the student has already seen, except deliberately in the final week as a confidence item. And do not add new content after week five, because material learned that late tends to displace material already secure.

sections.heading: Non-calculator fluency: what to drill, and how
paragraphs: One of the two Cambridge 0580 papers is sat without a calculator, and for a generation of students who have had one since Year 7 that is the single most predictable source of lost marks. The losses are not conceptual. A student who can set up a correct percentage problem and cannot execute the division has understood the mathematics and will still score nothing for it, which is a particularly demoralising way to lose a grade.

The fix is frequency rather than duration. Ten minutes a day for a term rebuilds fluency; a ninety-minute session once a fortnight does not, because this is motor skill as much as knowledge. The content to drill is narrow and predictable: fraction arithmetic including mixed numbers, decimal multiplication and division, percentage increase and decrease including reverse problems, standard form, ratio division, squares, cubes and their roots, and simplification of surds where the syllabus requires it.

Two further habits belong here. First, estimation: a student who can tell that an answer should be about forty will notice when their working produces four hundred, and that noticing saves marks across both papers. Second, writing the intermediate values rather than holding them in memory, which is the same method-mark argument made earlier and matters more without a calculator because there are more intermediate values to lose. Candidates sitting Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 have a calculator in both papers and still benefit from this work, because fluency buys time at the front of the paper and time is what the long final questions need.

sections.heading: What A-Level and the IB Diploma expect from an IGCSE maths grade
paragraphs: In a belt where both routes are available within a short drive, the IGCSE grade is a selection document as well as a result, and it is a slightly misleading one. A grade can be assembled from reliable topic marks while a weakness in algebraic manipulation goes unnoticed, which is why some students with respectable IGCSE grades struggle immediately in Year 12. Mark-scheme work surfaces this, because it shows where the marks came from rather than only how many there were.

A-Level mathematics assumes fluent algebraic manipulation from the first week: rearrangement, indices, surds, quadratics and functions handled without hesitation. The IB Diploma splits into Analysis and Approaches, which makes the same assumption and adds proof and calculus, and Applications and Interpretation, which leans on modelling, statistics and interpretation and permits a calculator throughout at Standard Level. A student arriving from Cambridge 0607 Extended has met investigative writing already, which makes the Diploma exploration less alien than it is for a student arriving from 0580.

The practical advice for Year 11 in this community is to ask the tutor a specific question: from the marked papers, is the algebra secure enough for the next course? That is a different question from what grade is likely, and the answer is more useful. A student who scores well on data handling and mensuration while losing marks on algebraic fractions is being told something about Year 12, and acting on it in Year 11 is far cheaper than discovering it in the first term of a Diploma or an A-Level.

sections.heading: Why living nearby does not supply mark-scheme knowledge
paragraphs: Al Bandar is among the easiest places in the emirate to arrange an in-home tutor. Teaching staff live in numbers across Khalifa City and the Al Raha belt, journeys are short, and a family can have somebody at the table on a weekday evening without difficulty. It would be dishonest to argue that online wins here on logistics, so the argument has to be made on the thing this page has spent its length describing.

A local shortlist is deep in general competence and thin in specific mark-scheme experience. It will contain people who can teach mathematics clearly; it is far less likely to contain somebody who has marked Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Paper 2 against the scheme, and almost certainly will not contain a Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 specialist or someone who has prepared 0607 investigation candidates. Online widens the set to every specialist available, and at the published bands it costs less: in-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150.

The trade-offs of a screen deserve naming. A younger or easily distracted student is harder to supervise remotely. Written working has to reach the tutor, which means a tablet and stylus or a phone propped over paper, and both are worth testing in a free trial rather than assuming. Against that, reading a mark scheme and a script side by side on a shared screen is genuinely easier than passing paper across a table, which is a small advantage that happens to fall exactly where this page says the value is. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service available only in India.

sections.heading: What we measure, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: A page arguing that marking is the active ingredient should say how it reports. The unit is the classified loss: every mark lost on a timed paper is recorded as a method error, an accuracy error, a missed independent mark or genuine unknown content, and the same question types are re-sat after the targeted work. At six sessions you receive a written statement of what has moved and the three categories still costing the most marks. That is checkable against your child's own papers, which is the only property that makes a progress report worth reading.

If the match is wrong, the tutor changes at our cost, and the six-session review exists to make that an ordinary conversation rather than an awkward one. In a community where tutors often arrive by neighbour recommendation, the social cost of switching is the main thing keeping families in a mismatch. Nothing renews automatically either, so a household can take the free diagnostic and stop.

What we will not do is publish or supply board mark schemes, past papers, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. We publish no satisfaction percentage, score-improvement figure, student count or star rating, because none could be shown with a sample size, a date and a method. We claim no accreditation from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we have no premises in the UAE. And on the 0607 investigation, or any later Internal Assessment, a tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on your child's own work and never produces it.
