faqs.question: What makes an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Bandar better than someone who is simply good at maths?
faqs.answer: The ability to read a published mark scheme and explain why a particular script scored two out of four when the final answer was right. That is a distinct skill from explaining mathematics clearly, and it is the one that moves an exam grade. Ask any tutor to walk you through a marked question, naming where the method mark was available, where accuracy was lost and which independent marks were missed. A specialist does that fluently. A capable mathematician often cannot, and nothing in a profile distinguishes them.

faqs.question: How are marks awarded on a Cambridge IGCSE maths paper?
faqs.answer: In three kinds. Method marks go to a correct approach visible on the page, whether or not the arithmetic that follows is right. Accuracy marks go to a correct value, usually conditional on the method mark and on the stated degree of accuracy. Independent marks go to a specific correct result on its own terms, with no working required. Schemes also carry follow-through allowances, which credit later work that is correct given an earlier wrong value, and or-equivalent notes accepting alternative forms.

faqs.question: The answer is correct and the mark was withheld. What convention did my child break?
faqs.answer: Usually accuracy conventions rather than mathematics. The answer may be correct in value and wrong in form, or given to a different degree of accuracy than the question specified, or rounded early so the final figure is slightly off. Occasionally the question asked for a reason and received a calculation. These are reading and convention problems, they are the cheapest category in the whole subject to fix, and one or two mark-scheme walkthroughs usually change the behaviour permanently.

faqs.question: My child works things out mentally. Is that a problem for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a significant one. Method marks are awarded only for method the examiner can see, so a student who computes three steps mentally and writes one line collects everything when they are right and nothing when they are wrong. A student who shows the rearrangement, the substitution and the evaluation keeps most of the marks even when the arithmetic fails at the end, and benefits from follow-through on the subsequent parts. Across a full paper that difference is routinely worth a grade.

faqs.question: Which topics cost 0580 Extended candidates the most marks?
faqs.answer: A consistent set, mostly late additions to a scheme of work that were never consolidated. Bearings, where the reference direction or the three-figure form is wrong. Similar shapes, where the length factor is applied to area and volume instead of its square and cube. Reverse percentages solved as forward problems. Histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency is plotted instead of frequency density. Vector notation. Algebraic fractions, where a sign error ends an otherwise correct solution. Each is a short fix rather than a long one.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Year 11 student sit before the June series?
faqs.answer: One a week for the final eight weeks, sat to the published duration and marked against the scheme within forty-eight hours, is the pattern that produces the most reliable improvement. Volume beyond that adds little, because the active ingredient is the marking rather than the sitting. A paper sat and scored is a thermometer; a paper sat and classified into method, accuracy, independent and content losses is a plan for the following week.

faqs.question: Should past papers ever be shortened to fit an evening?
faqs.answer: No. The back of a paper is exactly where pacing failures appear, so a shortened paper hides the problem it was supposed to reveal. Schools in the Al Raha Beach belt finish early enough that a weekday session is workable, but a full paper plus a walkthrough is a two-hour commitment, so the paper belongs at the weekend and the walkthrough in the weekday slot. Mark strictly too: a generous mark teaches nothing, because the scheme is the standard the series will apply.

faqs.question: How should non-calculator practice be organised?
faqs.answer: Ten minutes a day rather than ninety minutes a fortnight, because fluency is a motor skill as much as knowledge. Drill fraction arithmetic including mixed numbers, decimal multiplication and division, percentage increase and decrease including reverse problems, standard form, ratio division, and squares, cubes and roots. Add estimation, so a student notices when working produces four hundred where forty was expected. Candidates on Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 have a calculator in both papers and still gain, because fluency buys time for the long final questions.

faqs.question: Does my child's school mark mocks the same way the board does?
faqs.answer: Usually closely, and the variation matters less than what is done with the result. A mock returns a score; a classified paper returns a plan. Whatever the school provides, the useful step at home is to take the marked script and sort every lost mark into method, accuracy, missed independent marks or genuine unknown content. That takes half an hour, requires no subject knowledge beyond the published scheme, and it is the most informative thing a parent in this belt can do for free.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE maths grade tell us whether my child is ready for A-Level or the IB?
faqs.answer: Only partly, which is why the marked papers matter more than the grade. A grade can be assembled from reliable topic marks while a weakness in algebraic manipulation passes unnoticed, and that weakness bites in the first weeks of A-Level mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches. Ask a tutor a precise question: from these marked papers, is the algebra secure enough for the next course? That answer is more useful than a predicted grade and it is actionable in Year 11.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the 0607 investigation component?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a fixed boundary. A tutor can teach what an investigative write-up has to contain, work a comparable example on a different problem, and give feedback on your child's own attempt against the published criteria. A tutor must not supply text for submission or edit a draft until the thinking has stopped being the student's. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and the malpractice consequences of that fall on the candidate rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: Can you send us the mark schemes and past papers?
faqs.answer: No, and nor should anyone else. We reference board materials and link to the official source rather than redistributing them, because reproducing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Cambridge and Pearson publish what is available on their own sites, and your child's school can advise on access. Working from the official document also means you are reading the current version rather than something that has since been revised.

faqs.question: Why choose an online tutor when in-home is easy in Al Raha Beach?
faqs.answer: Because the local pool is deep in general competence and thin in mark-scheme experience. It will contain people who teach mathematics clearly and is far less likely to contain somebody who has marked 0580 Paper 4 or 4MA1 Paper 2 against the scheme, let alone a 4PM1 specialist. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 online. Reading a scheme and a script side by side on a shared screen is also easier than passing paper across a table.

At six sessions you receive a written statement of what has moved and the three categories still costing most marks, which you can check against your child's own scripts. If the match is wrong we change the tutor at our cost.

intro.heading: Where your child is in the maths calendar decides what tutoring can do
paragraphs: The same request produces three completely different plans depending on when it arrives. A family asking in September of Year 10 is buying habit formation and a foundation audit. A family asking in January of Year 11 is buying targeted topic recovery ahead of a tier decision. A family asking six weeks before the first paper is buying technique and timing, and nothing else, because content teaching at that point competes with practice the student needs more.

Almost nobody frames it that way, which is why so much tutoring money is spent on the wrong activity at the wrong time. A tutor who begins at the start of the syllabus in February of Year 11 will reach the topics that are actually costing marks somewhere around the week of the examination. A tutor who drills timing in September of Year 10 is practising a skill the student has no content to apply it to. The calendar is the first question, not an afterthought.

The second thing families underestimate is how early the binding dates fall. The paper is the visible deadline and the least useful one for planning. Final entries are submitted by the exam centre months before the series opens, and the tier decision has to precede them. Mocks come one or two terms earlier and are the diagnostic for everything that follows. Those three dates, not the examination date, are what a plan should be built around. Ask the examinations officer for the entry deadline in writing, since it is rarely published to parents.

There is also a calendar fact specific to this country that reliably confuses families. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two: the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Any revision plan or tutoring package built around a spring sitting has been built on another country's calendar, and the mistake is common enough that it is worth checking in writing.

What follows is the whole cycle laid out: where you are now and what that implies, why the entry deadline is the real deadline, how to choose deliberately between June and November, the resit arithmetic that has to be settled before results arrive, and an eight-week countdown that works. Al Bateen's central position makes slots easier to hold than in the outer communities, which matters most in the final term. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India, and that position holds on every country page we publish. For a calendar-driven plan the useful consequence is that a disrupted week costs nothing to rearrange, because no journey was ever part of the arrangement.

subjects.description: A short block that can be closed late if necessary, which makes it useful filler in a compressed plan. Frequency density with unequal class widths is narrow, reliably examined and commonly weak.

subjects.name: Conditional probability
subjects.description: Another compact late-stage option. Tree diagrams where the second branch depends on the first are formulaic once the structure is understood, and the topic is often the weakest area on an otherwise solid script.

subjects.name: Vector proof questions
subjects.description: Needs practice rather than explanation, so it belongs in the eight-week countdown rather than in Year 10. These questions sit at the end of an Extended paper and separate strong candidates from middling ones.

subjects.name: Timed paper practice
subjects.description: The final-term staple, and useless earlier because a student needs content to apply the timing to. Full papers under proper conditions, marked against the published scheme, with time checked at the halfway point.

subjects.name: Error log maintenance
subjects.description: A running record of every mistake by category, kept by the student from Year 10 and reviewed weekly. The one revision habit that compounds across two years, and the cheapest diagnostic any tutor can work from.

subjects.name: Calculator discipline
subjects.description: Write the equation before the screen value, store rather than retype, round once, check angle mode. Installable in four to six sessions at any point, and the fastest available gain in the final term because the marks are already nearly earned.

subjects.description: Confirm with the school whether it applies. If it does, exact values, surds and fraction arithmetic need daily practice across months rather than a block of lessons, because the skill decays quickly without contact.

sections.heading: Where you are now, and what that makes possible
paragraphs: Before anything else, locate the student in the cycle. The honest capability of tutoring differs enormously between the start of Year 10 and six weeks before a paper, and a provider who offers the same plan at every point is not planning. The table below sets out what each stage can realistically achieve, which is also a guide to what you should refuse to pay for at that stage.

Early in Year 10 the available work is foundation and habit: algebraic fluency checked for speed rather than accuracy, calculator discipline installed before it matters, and an error log begun. None of it feels urgent, all of it is cheap, and it is the only point in the cycle at which a genuine foundation gap can be closed without displacing revision. Families who buy here buy the least and get the most.

By the middle of Year 11 the work is topic recovery, ranked from the autumn mock and timed to finish before the final mocks, because the final mocks produce the tier decision. In the final term the work changes again: content teaching largely stops and the recoverable marks are the ones being withheld rather than missed. Six weeks out, a tutor still working forward through the syllabus is spending your money on something that cannot pay back before the paper. Knowing that in advance is also a way of judging a provider, because the honest ones narrow their promises as the paper gets closer rather than widening them.

sections.heading: The entry deadline is the real deadline
paragraphs: The examination date is the visible deadline and the least useful one to plan from, because by the time it arrives every decision has already been made. The dates that bind are earlier and quieter. Final entries are submitted by the exam centre months before a series opens, and they fix the board, the code, the tier and the papers your child will sit. Once submitted, a tier change is generally not available, whatever the spring mock says.

Working backwards from the entry deadline rather than the paper changes the whole shape of a plan. The tier decision has to precede it, which means the mock that informs the tier decision has to precede that, which means any topic recovery intended to influence the tier has to be complete before that mock. For a boundary student in Al Bateen, that chain determines when tutoring is worth buying and when it is too late to affect the decision that matters most.

Ask the school three things in writing: when final entries are submitted, when the tier decision is made and on what evidence, and whether it can be revisited. Those answers take one email and they are the scaffolding for everything else. Also ask for the centre's own zone timetable when it is published, because Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version.

sections.heading: Choosing June or November deliberately
paragraphs: Both series are full sittings. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November, and Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November, so November is not a repair route unless a family treats it as one. Used deliberately, it is a way of spreading an unmanageable subject load across two sittings rather than taking everything at once, which for a student with nine or ten entries can be the single most useful decision of the two years.

The cases where splitting helps are recognisable. A student with a very large entry list and no capacity to revise all of it. A student who joined mid-year and genuinely has not been taught a subject's full content. A student whose strongest subjects could be banked in June, freeing the final months for the weakest. Each of those is a conversation with the school before entries are submitted, and each is impossible to arrange afterwards.

The decision also interacts with the timetable in a way worth checking. Clash arrangements differ between Cambridge's six administrative zones, so two students at different schools in these districts can face different constraints with the same subject list. Ask for your centre's zone timetable, look at the paper dates for the subjects under consideration, and raise any clash with the school early rather than discovering it in the week of the examination. Clashes are usually manageable when flagged a term ahead and genuinely disruptive when flagged a fortnight ahead, which is a difference entirely within a family's control.

sections.heading: Results-day arithmetic, settled in advance
paragraphs: Results arrive with a short window attached, and families who have not pre-decided spend it deciding. Pearson's documented timings illustrate the shape: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The gap between sitting a paper and learning the outcome is substantial, and the window between the outcome and a November entry decision is not.

The practical move is to agree a trigger before results arrive. Decide which result in mathematics would lead to a November resit, which would lead to accepting the grade, and which would lead to a remark request instead. Write it down. Then on the day the family executes a decision already made rather than arguing about one under pressure, which is the difference between restarting work in the same week and restarting it a month later.

The timing matters because of decay. A student who sat a June paper and then has an eight-week summer gap before resuming has lost fluency that will need rebuilding, and in a November sitting there is not much room for rebuilding. The strongest resit plans start within days of the result, work from the original script where a copy is available, and target the specific topics that cost marks rather than restarting the course. Remark and access-to-script options have their own deadlines, which the school's exams officer holds. Ask about them in the same conversation as the resit, because the two decisions interact and both are time-limited.

sections.heading: An eight-week countdown that works
paragraphs: Eight weeks is roughly what a family has between deciding to act and the first paper, and it is enough to move marks if the plan starts from a script. It is not enough to teach two years of content, and the attempt is why some students finish the period having covered everything and improved nothing. The structure below assumes two or three sessions a week and one full paper completed between sessions, which is what most students can actually sustain.

The first fortnight closes the two highest-priority topics from the marked mock, with a short timed section at the end of every session so timing work begins immediately rather than in week seven. The second fortnight adds a full paper, marked properly against the published scheme, and the feedback sets the next session's content. Week five is a checkpoint rather than more content: compare the pattern of losses with the original mock, and if it has not changed, change the plan rather than extending it.

Weeks six to eight are technique, question selection and finishing. No new topic after week six, because a topic met for the first time in the final fortnight is a liability rather than an asset. Full papers under proper conditions, with the student practising the first-few-seconds decision about whether to start a question and the discipline of returning to an abandoned one. Al Bateen's short commutes make this period easier to schedule than in the outer communities, which is the one point in the cycle where the district genuinely helps.

sections.heading: The error log, the one habit that compounds
paragraphs: If a family takes one thing from this page it should be the error log, because it costs nothing, it works at every stage of the calendar, and it makes every tutoring hour afterwards more productive. The student keeps a running record of every mistake, written by category rather than by topic: method not shown, rounded too early, misread the command word, arithmetic slip, did not know the content, ran out of time.

The categories are what make it useful. A log that says trigonometry, trigonometry, circle theorems is a topic list, which the school already has. A log that says method not shown, method not shown, method not shown is a diagnosis, and it points at a four-second habit rather than at a week of teaching. Over a term the distribution becomes obvious, and so does the fact that most students lose far more marks to two or three recurring behaviours than to unknown content.

For a tutor the log replaces the first ten minutes of every session. Instead of asking how the week went, they read the log, see where the errors concentrated, and adjust. For a parent it provides visibility without interrogating a teenager at dinner. Started in Year 10 it compounds over two years; started eight weeks out it still beats not having one, because the first week of entries alone usually tells a tutor more than a conversation would. It also costs nothing, needs no app and works equally well on paper, which is why it is the one recommendation on this page that has no caveat attached.

sections.heading: Mock weeks, Ramadan and the term that moves
paragraphs: A plan that assumes an undisturbed term will not survive one. Two features of the UAE school year reliably move things, and both are easier to handle when nobody is travelling to a lesson. Mock weeks come first: they are the best source of evidence in the cycle, and the right response is a short review of a just-sat paper rather than a pause or a full hour of new content. A paper reviewed the day after it was sat yields more than the same paper reviewed in three weeks.

Ramadan is the second, and it moves roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so its position relative to mocks and to a series changes from year to year. Schools in the UAE commonly shorten the day during the month, which reorganises the afternoon rather than freeing it, and household evenings reshape around Iftar. The productive approach is to agree the revised slot before the month starts, often post-Iftar, and to use the period for technique rather than new content.

The third disruption is ordinary: a changed school timetable, an exam week, a family trip. Because Al Bateen households are central, the afternoon slot is usually recoverable rather than lost, and because nobody travels to the house a session can move to the following evening in a single message. The rule that protects a plan is to move a slot after two disruptions rather than defending it through a third, which is when continuity and the arrangement both tend to break.

sections.heading: What a tutor should be doing at each stage
paragraphs: A useful way to judge any provider is to ask what they would do at your child's specific point in the calendar, and then check whether the answer changes depending on the stage. Somebody who describes the same programme for a Year 10 autumn request and a six-weeks-out request is selling a product rather than planning a response, and that is detectable in one conversation.

In Year 10 the right answer involves auditing fluency for speed, installing working and calculator habits, and setting up the error log, at low frequency. In mid Year 11 it involves ranking topics from the marked mock and closing them one at a time with a visible end point before the final mocks. Eight weeks out it involves counting the withheld marks on a script, building from that, and stopping new content at week six. Two weeks out it involves full papers and nothing else.

Ask also what they will not do, which is a shorter question with a more revealing answer. Official past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards and should be referenced and linked rather than supplied as downloads. No grade boundary should be quoted to you as a fixed figure, because boundaries move between series. And private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years; IB Gram holds no approval from ADEK, KHDA, Cambridge or Pearson, and no provider should claim otherwise.

faqs.question: When in the two years is IGCSE maths tutoring most worth buying?
faqs.answer: Early in Year 10 if you want the cheapest intervention, and mid Year 11 if you want the most targeted one. Year 10 is the only point at which a genuine foundation gap can be closed without displacing revision, and the work is fluency, habits and an error log at low frequency. Mid Year 11 is where topic recovery from the autumn mock can still influence the tier decision. Six weeks out, tutoring can still move marks, but only technique and timing rather than content.

faqs.question: What happens at the entry deadline that we cannot undo later?
faqs.answer: Because it fixes the board, the code, the tier and the papers your child will sit, and it falls months before the series. Once entries are submitted, a tier change is generally unavailable whatever a later mock suggests. The tier decision precedes the entry, the mock that informs it precedes that, and any topic recovery meant to influence the tier has to be finished before that mock. Ask the school in writing when entries go in and when the tier is decided.

faqs.question: Can my child sit maths in June and other subjects in November?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and for a student with nine or ten entries it can be the most useful decision of the two years. Both are full series: Cambridge runs June and November, Pearson runs May/June and November. Splitting the list means subjects are taught and revised in two waves instead of all at once. It has to be agreed with the school before final entries are submitted, and it is not arrangeable afterwards, so the conversation belongs early in Year 11.

faqs.question: What should we decide before results day?
faqs.answer: The trigger. Which maths result would lead to a November resit, which would lead to accepting the grade, and which would lead to a remark request instead. Write it down. Pearson's documented timings show why: June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results on 22 January 2026, and the window between a result and a resit entry is short. Families who have not pre-decided spend the first fortnight arguing rather than working.

faqs.question: How soon after a result should resit work start?
faqs.answer: Within days, because fluency decays over a summer gap and a November sitting leaves little room to rebuild it. Start from the original script where a copy is available, target the specific topics that cost marks rather than restarting the course, and confirm the November entry with the school before planning any revision, since an unconfirmed entry makes the plan theoretical. Ask the exams officer about remark and access-to-script options at the same time, because those deadlines are short and strictly applied.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks long enough to change a maths grade?
faqs.answer: Long enough to move marks if the plan starts from a marked script, and not long enough to teach two years of content. Close the two highest-priority topics in the first fortnight, add a full marked paper in the second, re-diagnose at week four rather than continuing, and spend the last three weeks on timing, question selection and finishing. Nothing new after week six, because a topic met for the first time in the final fortnight is a liability. Students who try to cover everything improve nothing.

faqs.question: What exactly is an error log and how do we keep one?
faqs.answer: A running record of every mistake, written by the student and recorded by category rather than by topic. Six categories cover most of it: method not shown, rounded too early, command word misread, arithmetic slip, content unknown, ran out of time. A log listing topics is just a topic list, which the school already has. A log listing categories is a diagnosis, and it usually shows that two or three recurring behaviours cost more marks than unknown content does.

faqs.question: Which timetable should we revise from?
faqs.answer: Only the one your child's own exam centre publishes. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable, which is unusually direct language and exists because the error is common. Two schools a few minutes apart in these districts can have different paper dates and different clash arrangements, so a neighbour's timetable is not a guide to your child's.

faqs.question: Can we sit the February or March maths series in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers the February and March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. A revision plan or tutoring package built around a spring sitting has been built on another country's calendar, and a provider who offers a February entry to a child here has told you something useful. Confirm the series with the school in writing before any planning begins.

faqs.question: How should a weekly slot survive mock weeks?
faqs.answer: By changing what it contains rather than by pausing. Mock weeks produce the best evidence in the whole cycle, and a short review of a paper sat yesterday is worth more than a full hour of new content. Reviewing the same paper three weeks later yields much less, because the student no longer remembers what they were thinking. If a pause is genuinely needed there is no rolling term and no fee attached, and because nobody travels the slot resumes in its original place.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change the maths revision plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the timing rather than the content priorities, and its position shifts roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so in some years it sits near mocks or a series and in others it does not. Schools commonly shorten the day, which reorganises the afternoon, and evenings reshape around Iftar. Agree the revised slot before the month starts, often post-Iftar, and use the period for technique rather than for new content. Nothing about that adjustment costs anything when nobody is travelling.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor to check they are planning rather than selling?
faqs.answer: Ask what they would do at your child's exact stage in the calendar, and then ask what they would do differently at a different stage. Somebody planning gives two clearly different answers: fluency and habits in Year 10, ranked topic closure in mid Year 11, withheld marks and timed papers eight weeks out. Somebody selling describes the same programme either way. It is a single question, it takes a minute, and the difference in the reply is unmistakable.

faqs.question: Will a tutor tell me what mark my child needs for a grade?
faqs.answer: They should decline, because grade boundaries move between series and are published by the boards after the event, so any figure quoted in advance will be wrong eventually. What can honestly be said from a marked script is relative: a student two or three marks below a boundary is a very different proposition from one twenty marks below, and the first justifies concentrated effort in a way the second does not. That comparison is more useful for planning than a number nobody can rely on.

faqs.question: Does living centrally help with the final-term schedule?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the one point in the cycle where the district genuinely matters. Short commutes from Al Bateen, Khalidiyah and Al Mushrif make a late-afternoon slot holdable through the weeks when two or three sessions a week are needed, where an outer-community household would be pushed into the evening. Because nobody travels to the house, both windows cost the same and a disrupted session moves in a message, which is what keeps a countdown intact.

faqs.question: Do you visit homes in Al Bateen for maths lessons?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE from IB Gram; visiting tutors are a service we offer only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on a shared whiteboard with the marked script or the current worksheet open, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. For a calendar-driven plan the practical advantage is flexibility: mock weeks, Ramadan and a changed school timetable all shift a session without anybody rebuilding a route across the island.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-falah.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IGCSE Mathematics to Al Falah students over live video: Cambridge 0580 at Core and Extended, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, and Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 at both tiers. The first session is a free diagnostic, because the point of this page is that the diagnosis decides what the money should buy.

intro.heading: Which hour is worth buying?
paragraphs: Nearly every IGCSE maths enquiry from Al Falah arrives in the same week of the year: the week the mock results come home. The instinct is to buy hours, as many as the budget allows, as soon as possible. It is the wrong first move, and it is expensive. In this subject the gap between a well-aimed six sessions and a badly aimed twenty is not a matter of degree; one moves a grade and the other produces a calmer student with the same result.

The reason is that IGCSE maths marks are lost in four distinct ways, and only one of them responds to re-teaching. A student can lose marks to genuine unknown content, which does need teaching. Or to method that was never written down, so a correct approach earned nothing. Or to arithmetic, mostly on the Cambridge non-calculator paper. Or to reading, where a question asked for a reason and received a calculation, or asked for three significant figures and received a decimal that was right two lines earlier. Those four need completely different interventions, at completely different costs, and a single past paper sorted against the mark scheme tells you which you are dealing with.

Here is the market, for reference, in AED with sources named. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified online subject tutor runs roughly AED 150 to 300, Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. Three of the six competitor pages measured for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars.

What those bands do not tell a parent is value, which is why the first table on this page prices interventions rather than hours. A six-session method-repair block at the middle band costs less than a quarter of a term of weekly sessions and is more likely to move a grade when the diagnosis says method. The same six sessions are worth little if the student genuinely has not learned the syllabus. Neither statement is a sales position; they are just the two situations, and they need to be told apart before any money moves.

One note on delivery. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. For Al Falah families, which sits well out towards the airport road, lessons are one-to-one over live video, and the in-home premium in a community this far from the island is largely the journey. We publish no rate card here. The trial lesson is free with no card required, and the quote follows the diagnosis so it is attached to a plan.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-falah.programmesIntro: The same budget buys very different value at different points in the course. Here is what each stage should be spending on, and roughly how much it takes.

programmes.name: The first IGCSE year
programmes.description: The cheapest year to intervene in and the least used. Content is being met for the first time, so a gap costs four sessions rather than fourteen, and the habit of writing visible method can be built instead of repaired. This is also the only year in which the tier decision can still be changed, which makes a small spend here worth more than a large one later.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Falah household this is also the easiest year to protect an evening in, because homework volume is lower and the commute has not yet collided with revision demand. Four to six sessions in Year 10 routinely replace a full term of Year 11 fees, and a family that uses them to test the tier is buying information rather than teaching.

programmes.name: The examination year
programmes.description: When nearly all spending happens, and when it is most likely to be misdirected. The right sequence is a diagnostic first, then whichever of the four error categories is largest, then timed papers with mark schemes read afterwards. The wrong sequence is a block of hours bought on the strength of a grade rather than a diagnosis.
programmes.countryNote: The weeks immediately after the winter break are the most productive revision weeks in a UAE school year, and families who begin in February have already spent them. In Al Falah, where the evening offers one usable block after a long commute, that lost time cannot be recovered by adding a second weekly session later.

programmes.name: The November series as a second attempt
programmes.description: A real option that is rarely costed properly. A resit is a narrow, well-defined target: one or two papers, known weaknesses, a short and intense plan. Support for it is usually cheaper than a full year of weekly sessions, because the diagnosis already exists in the form of a result.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge International runs June and November, and UAE candidates sit those two series; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. Entries for a resit go through a centre, so the first call is to the school's exams officer rather than to a tutor.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-falah.subjectsIntro: Maths is where the request starts, and the cost of the subjects usually added alongside it depends on how much overlap there is. These are the common combinations and what each one really needs.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 (Extended)
subjects.description: Two written papers of equal weight, one without a calculator. Most of the purchasable value sits in non-calculator fluency, visible method and the long questions at the back of each paper, which are technique problems rather than content problems.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 (Core)
subjects.description: A secure C rather than a reach for more, since the route is capped. Spending is best aimed at number, ratio, percentages, mensuration and data handling, plus a question order that banks reliable marks before fatigue.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: Graphics-calculator technique and the investigation component. Cost is driven by the written investigation rather than by content, and a student treating it as 0580 with extra buttons will lose most where the marks are easiest to earn.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two calculator papers graded 9 to 1. The cheapest version of this is to confirm the tier early, because preparing a Foundation candidate for a grade 7 is paying for something the entry cannot award.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 4MA1 by stronger candidates. Specialist availability is thinner, so the real cost includes a longer match time as well as a higher rate. Work is mostly technique against unfamiliar question structures.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The most economical subject to add to maths, because equation rearrangement and graph work transfer directly. Where physics marks are being lost to algebra, a maths block is cheaper than physics sessions and does more.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic and titration calculations are maths in a chemistry context, so a numerate student gains quickly. Organic naming and electrolysis products are the reliable marks worth securing early.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Data and statistics questions plus the structure of long extended responses. The cheapest improvement is writing timed answers rather than reading notes, which costs nothing and is the thing most students have never done.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Calculation marks are easy for a numerate student and evaluation marks are where everyone loses. Short, focused blocks on diagram accuracy and the explain-versus-evaluate distinction give better value than continuous support.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies alongside the IGCSE course
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools beside the licensed curriculum, and a cost in hours rather than dirhams. Any realistic Year 11 revision budget has to account for the timetable space they occupy.

sections.heading: Interventions ranked by what they fix and what they cost
paragraphs: This is the table most families would like before they spend and almost never get. It lists the interventions available in IGCSE maths, what each one actually treats, how many hours it takes and what that costs at the published mid band of AED 150 to 300 an hour. The figures are market rates from provider pages rather than IB Gram prices; our trial is free and our quote follows a diagnosis.

Read it alongside the honest caveat. Nothing in the right-hand column is a promise. An intervention that is well matched to the diagnosis has a good chance of moving a grade; the same intervention aimed at the wrong problem has almost none, which is the entire argument of this page. Nobody can promise a grade in an externally assessed qualification, and a provider who does is describing their marketing.

The pattern that emerges is consistent across the Abu Dhabi families we see. The cheapest items sit at the top, and they are the ones least often purchased, because they look too small to be serious. A tier check is an email. A full paper sat cold is a weekend. A mark-scheme walkthrough is one session. Those three cost almost nothing and they decide whether the expensive items are worth buying at all. The most expensive item, a term of weekly general support bought without a diagnosis, sits at the bottom for a reason. It is not that the teaching inside those hours is poor; it is that nobody has told the teaching where to aim.

sections.heading: Four checks that cost nothing and should happen first
paragraphs: The first check is the entry. Ask the school's exams officer, in writing, for the syllabus code and the tier for mathematics. Parents frequently do not have this, and it is not inattention: Abu Dhabi schools often write only IGCSE maths in reports. The code decides whether a calculator is permitted in every paper and whether an investigation component exists. The tier decides the maximum grade available, and Cambridge 0580 Core cannot award above a C while Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation caps at grade 5.

The second is a full past paper, sat at home, to the real duration, with a phone in another room. Most students who arrive after a bad mock have never done this voluntarily, and the attempt itself is diagnostic. The third is marking it against the mark scheme with the student present, sorting every lost mark into method, arithmetic, reading or unknown content. That half hour is the single most informative thing available to a parent in this subject, and it requires no subject knowledge, only the published scheme.

The fourth is the exam centre. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct version of the timetable for your zone is essential, and is explicit that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong version. The zone follows the centre rather than the home address, so ask the exams officer and get it in writing. Done together, these four checks cost nothing, take under two hours of a weekend, and frequently change what a family should buy. Occasionally they show that nothing needs to be bought.

sections.heading: The tier trap, priced
paragraphs: This is the most expensive misunderstanding in IGCSE mathematics, and it is entirely administrative. The route or tier a student is entered for sets a ceiling on the grade that can be awarded, independently of performance. Cambridge grades 0580 Core from C to G and Extended from A* to E. Pearson Edexcel caps 4MA1 Foundation at grade 5 and runs Higher from 9 to 4. A candidate on the lower option who answers every question correctly still cannot be awarded above the cap.

The cost of not knowing this is a whole term of fees spent preparing for a grade that was never available. We see it most often in the spring of Year 11, when a family has been buying weekly sessions since January in pursuit of a grade 7 while the entry is Foundation. Nobody involved acted carelessly. The school recorded the tier, the report said IGCSE maths, and the tutor taught what was asked. The question that would have surfaced it takes one line in an email.

The window matters as much as the fact. Tier changes are possible up to the point final entries are submitted, which sits months before the papers, and after that the ceiling is fixed. So the check belongs in Year 10 or the autumn of Year 11, not in the spring. If the tier turns out to be wrong for the student's ambitions, the conversation with the school is about evidence: a full paper sat at the higher tier under time is a stronger argument than a parental opinion, and it costs a weekend.

sections.heading: The four error categories, and which are cheap to fix
paragraphs: Sorting a marked paper into four categories is the whole method, and the categories differ enormously in what they cost to repair. Reading errors are the cheapest. A question asks for a reason and receives a calculation; asks for three significant figures and receives a decimal that was correct two lines earlier; asks for the answer in a particular form and receives it in another. One or two mark-scheme walkthroughs usually change this behaviour permanently, because the student has simply never seen what the examiner was waiting for.

Method errors are next, and they are the largest category in most Abu Dhabi diagnostics we run. The student can do the mathematics and writes one line, so when the final step fails, nothing is credited. Examiners award method marks only for method they can see. Six to eight sessions of insisting on written steps, with the marks pointed out each time, converts near-misses into partial credit across an entire paper. This is a habit intervention, which is why it works faster than content teaching and why it is so often skipped in favour of re-teaching topics the student already knows.

Arithmetic is third, and specific to the Cambridge non-calculator paper. Short daily drilling beats long weekly sessions here, and the gain shows on the calculator paper too because less time is lost on the early questions. Content is last and most expensive: genuinely untaught topics, usually bearings, similar-shape scale factors, compound percentage change, histograms with unequal class widths and vectors, because they arrive late in most schemes of work. Eight to fourteen hours is a realistic range, and this is the only category where buying a lot of hours is the correct response.

sections.heading: Group, centre, self-study or one-to-one: cost per useful hour
paragraphs: Cost per hour and cost per useful hour are different numbers. A tuition centre group class is cheap per student and cannot follow one student's gaps, which is precisely what the purchase is for when the diagnosis names three specific topics. Self-study is free and works well for arithmetic drilling and for sitting timed papers, and poorly for anything requiring feedback on method, since the student cannot see what they cannot see.

Online one-to-one sits in the middle of the published bands at AED 150 to 300 an hour, and every one of those minutes is spent on this student. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel, and from Al Falah the top of that range is realistic because the evening-peak journey is long. The useful comparison is not which is cheapest but which delivers the thing the diagnosis asked for, at the lowest total.

The practical answer for most families is a combination, which no provider has an incentive to recommend. Free self-study for the arithmetic drilling and the timed papers. One-to-one for the diagnosis, the method repair and the mark-scheme walkthroughs, which is where feedback is irreplaceable. A group class only if the student is broadly behind across the syllabus rather than specifically behind in a few places. Sequenced that way, a household spends less and buys more, which is the whole of the advice on this page. The one requirement is that somebody at home checks the self-study half actually happens, because an unsupervised drilling plan quietly becomes no drilling plan and then the paid hours go back to re-teaching.

sections.heading: What the monthly packages hide, and what the resit route costs
paragraphs: Monthly packages in this market sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are real figures and the headline is the least important part of them. What matters is in the terms: whether unused sessions roll over, how long the package remains valid, whether hours can move between subjects or siblings, and what happens if the tutor changes mid-package.

A package that cannot flex around the school's own assessment weeks, a family trip or Ramadan is cheaper per hour and more expensive per useful hour, because the sessions that cannot be moved are the sessions that are lost. Ask those four questions before committing to any monthly arrangement, including a cheap one. Ask also whether the quoted price includes any applicable tax; we do not state the VAT treatment of tuition in the UAE on this page because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation, and an unsourced tax statement is not something a page should hand a parent.

The resit route deserves a mention because it is frequently cheaper than families assume and rarely explained. Cambridge runs June and November and UAE candidates sit those two series; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. A resit is a narrow target with a diagnosis already attached, namely the result itself, so a short intense plan often costs less than a year of weekly support. Entries are made through a centre, so the first conversation is with the school's exams officer about entry deadlines and any entry fees they charge, which vary by centre and are not something this page will invent a figure for.

sections.heading: What we measure, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: A page this concerned with value owes a parent a statement of how progress is judged. The measure is timed questions. A cold paper at the start, every lost mark classified into the four categories, then the same question types repeated after the repair work. At six sessions you receive a statement naming what has moved and the three topics still costing the most marks. That is checkable, and it is deliberately not a report that the student seems more confident, because confidence is not a measurement and is the easiest thing in the world to produce.

If the match is wrong, the tutor changes at our cost. The most common quiet failure in this market is a family persisting politely with someone competent who is not right for their child, and a scheduled review removes the social awkwardness of saying so. Nothing renews automatically, and a household that wants only the free diagnosis can take it and spend nothing further.

What we will not publish is any statistic we cannot evidence: no satisfaction percentage, no score-improvement figure, no student count, no self-asserted rating. In the pages researched for this project, one provider showed two contradictory review totals on a single page and another showed a perfect score from twenty reviews next to a far larger claim about students taught. We also claim no accreditation: IB Gram holds no licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no premises in the UAE. On coursework the boundary is fixed: a tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on your child's own work, including on a 0607 investigation, and never produces it or supplies submittable text.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE maths sessions does an Al Falah student actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which of four error categories is costing the marks. Reading errors take one or two mark-scheme walkthroughs. Method errors, the largest category in most diagnostics, take six to eight sessions, because they are a habit rather than a knowledge gap. Non-calculator arithmetic takes four to six, spread as short drills. Genuinely untaught content takes eight to fourteen. Buying hours before the category is identified is the most common way money is wasted in this subject, and a single marked paper identifies it.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing that actually improves an IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: Three things that cost nothing. Asking the school in writing for the syllabus code and the tier, because a capped entry silently limits the grade. Sitting one full past paper at home to the real duration, which most students who arrive after a bad mock have never done voluntarily. And marking that paper against the published mark scheme with the student present, sorting every lost mark into method, arithmetic, reading or unknown content. Together they take under two hours of a weekend and frequently change what should be bought.

faqs.question: Why would a term of weekly tutoring not move my child's maths grade?
faqs.answer: Because most of those hours go on re-teaching content the student largely knows, when the marks are being lost to pacing, unwritten method and misread questions. A student who understands the syllabus and scores a C is usually losing partial credit across the whole paper rather than failing whole topics. Twelve hours of re-teaching produces slightly better understanding and the same grade. Twelve hours of method repair and timed papers with mark schemes read afterwards addresses the actual loss, and a diagnostic session tells you which case you are in.

faqs.question: Could my child be entered for a tier that cannot award the grade we want?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most expensive misunderstanding in this subject. Cambridge grades the 0580 Core route C to G and Pearson Edexcel caps the 4MA1 Foundation tier at grade 5. A candidate on the lower option who answers everything correctly still cannot be awarded above the cap. Tier changes are possible until final entries are submitted, which is months before the papers, so the check belongs in Year 10 or the autumn of Year 11. The email that surfaces it is one line long.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class good value for IGCSE maths in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It is cheap per student and cannot follow one student's gaps, so the answer depends on the diagnosis. If the student is broadly behind across the syllabus, a group class can work and is good value. If the losses are three named topics or one bad habit such as not writing method, group pace will not touch them and the saving is illusory. The sequence that avoids the mistake is diagnosis first, format second, which is also the order no provider has an incentive to recommend.

faqs.question: Can self-study replace a maths tutor for a Year 11 student here?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the split is worth knowing. Self-study is free and genuinely effective for arithmetic drilling and for sitting full papers to time, which are two of the most valuable activities available. It is poor for feedback on method, because a student cannot see what they cannot see, and that is exactly where a marked paper and a walkthrough change behaviour. Most households get the best value from a combination: free self-study for the drilling and the papers, paid hours only where feedback is irreplaceable.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home maths tutor dearer in Al Falah than nearer the island?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is inside the price. In-home one-to-one across Abu Dhabi is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, and the quotes sit lower in Khalifa City, where specialists are concentrated and drives are short, and higher out towards the airport road. Al Falah is at the expensive end of that geography. Online one-to-one sits at roughly AED 150 to 300. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service available only in India.

faqs.question: What should I check before committing to a monthly tutoring package?
faqs.answer: Four things, none of which appear in the headline price. Whether unused sessions roll over. How long the package stays valid. Whether hours can move between subjects or between siblings. And what happens if the tutor changes mid-package. Market packages sit around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, and a package that cannot flex around school assessment weeks, travel or Ramadan is cheaper per hour and dearer per useful hour.

faqs.question: Does the November series make a cheaper second attempt possible?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is rarely costed properly. A resit is a narrow target with the diagnosis already supplied by the result, so a short intense plan frequently costs less than a year of weekly support. Cambridge runs June and November, and UAE candidates sit those two series; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. Entries go through a centre, so the first call is to the school's exams officer about deadlines and any entry fee they charge.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the losses are reading errors rather than real gaps?
faqs.answer: Mark a full paper against the published scheme with your child sitting beside you and watch where the marks go. Reading errors have a signature: the working is correct and the answer is in the wrong form, to the wrong accuracy, or answers a different question than the one asked. Content gaps look different, with whole question types left blank or abandoned after one line. You need no subject knowledge to sort these, only the scheme, and reading errors are the cheapest category in the whole list to fix.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting IGCSE maths tutoring in February for June papers?
faqs.answer: It is worth starting, and you have missed the best weeks. The period immediately after the winter break is the most productive revision window of a UAE school year, and a February start concedes it. What remains still works if the plan narrows: method repair, non-calculator drilling and timed papers with mark schemes read afterwards, rather than an attempt to cover a syllabus. Trying to teach everything in the time left tends to produce a calmer student with an unchanged grade, which is the outcome families most regret paying for.

faqs.question: Do you quote a fixed price for IGCSE maths support?
faqs.answer: Not on this page, deliberately. A rate quoted before a diagnosis is a number attached to nothing, and the whole argument here is that the right purchase varies by a factor of ten depending on what is actually wrong. The trial lesson is free with no card required, the diagnosis names the largest error category, and the quote follows that with the hours counted. We also do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition, because that would require a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an assumption.

faqs.question: What if the tutor turns out to be the wrong fit for my child?
faqs.answer: We change them, at our cost, and the review at six sessions exists to make that easy to say. The most common quiet failure in this market is a family persisting politely with someone competent who is simply not right for their child, usually because raising it feels awkward. A scheduled review removes the awkwardness. Nothing renews automatically either, so a household can take the free diagnosis, use the written plan with the school, and spend nothing further.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Cambridge 0607 investigation without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a fixed boundary. A tutor can teach what an investigative write-up has to contain, work a comparable example on a different problem, and give feedback on your child's own attempt against the published criteria. A tutor must not supply text for submission or edit a draft until the thinking has stopped being the student's. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that exposes the candidate to malpractice proceedings rather than the seller, which is why our boundary is published rather than negotiable.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-falah.closingHeading: Spend two free hours before you spend anything else
abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-falah.closingBody: If your child is sitting IGCSE maths from an Al Falah school and the mock disappointed, do the free work first. Ask the school in writing for the syllabus code, the tier and the exam centre with its Cambridge zone. Have your child sit one full past paper at home to the real duration. Then mark it against the published scheme together and sort every lost mark into method, arithmetic, reading or unknown content. Bring that to a free trial lesson and the tutor will confirm or correct it and name the block worth buying. No card is required, nothing renews automatically, and if the diagnosis is all you need, take it and stop.

intro.heading: Two years, one long commute, and a tier decision early on
paragraphs: The IGCSE maths course runs over Year 10 and Year 11, and from Al Ghadeer those two years contain fewer usable evenings than a parent expects. There is no IGCSE school inside this border community, so a student here leaves early, travels out along the E11 toward Khalifa City, Al Raha or the island, and comes home somewhere between 16:30 and 17:45 depending on which direction the family chose. That journey is not dead time in the abstract; it is subtracted directly from the hours available to practise maths.

Inside those two years sits a decision most families only notice afterwards. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered: the Core tier covers less content and its papers cannot award the top grades, while the Extended tier covers more and can. Pearson's 4MA1 works the same way with Foundation and Higher tiers. Schools decide entries, usually during Year 10, on Year 9 attainment and classroom evidence. The decision is communicated rather than negotiated, and once a series entry is made the tier is fixed for that sitting.

So the honest shape of IGCSE maths support from this corridor is front-loaded. Work done in Year 9 and the first term of Year 10 changes the evidence the school is looking at, which is the only thing that changes a tier. Work done in the spring of Year 11 maximises the grade available inside the tier entered, which is worth doing and is a smaller prize. Families who understand that sequence spend their money in a different order from families who do not.

The content itself is unglamorous and highly trainable. Most lost marks in 0580 and 4MA1 come from a small set of repeated behaviours: working not shown so method marks are forfeited, rounding applied too early in a multi-step question, units ignored, and a diagram not drawn where a diagram would have made the geometry obvious. A student who fixes those four picks up marks across every topic on the paper, and none of it requires new mathematics. A student who writes one line of method per step, keeps unrounded values in the calculator, writes the unit beside every answer and sketches the triangle before reaching for a rule will collect marks on questions they are already able to do.

What follows is built for a commuting household. There is a two-year timeline showing where the pressure points actually fall. There is a paper-by-paper comparison of Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1, because the board changes what revision should look like. There is the tier question in full. There is the June series counted backwards. And there is a straight comparison of the tuition centres in Mohammed Bin Zayed City against one-to-one online, which is the real choice most families here are weighing. Lessons are delivered online and one-to-one; IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-ghadee.programmesIntro: Three stages matter for IGCSE maths in this corridor, and the earliest one carries the most leverage. The notes say what each stage decides and what it costs to fix later.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage that feeds the tier decision. Checkpoint tests, which Cambridge runs in March, May and October, are used by schools for setting and for judging whether a student should be entered for Core or Extended. The mathematics assessed is largely number, algebra and basic geometry, and weakness in algebraic manipulation here is the single strongest predictor of a Core entry.
programmes.countryNote: For a Al Ghadeer family this is the highest-return stage and the one almost nobody buys tuition for. A term of focused algebra work in Year 9 is cheap, fits the short evenings this corridor allows, and can move a borderline tier judgement. The same gap discovered in Year 11 cannot change the tier for that series and costs far more to work around.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Two years, assessed linearly at the end, with Core and Extended tiers each sitting a pair of papers. Extended adds functions, harder trigonometry, vectors and more demanding algebra. Candidates are expected to show method, and the mark scheme awards marks for correct working even where the final answer is wrong, which is why unshown working is so costly.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in this emirate sit the June series, with November as the resit route. The February/March series is offered to India only and should be ignored on any UAE page. Each Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, so take dates from your child's exams officer.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Pearson's international maths specification, tiered Foundation and Higher, each assessed by two written papers with a calculator permitted throughout. The content overlaps Cambridge substantially while the question style and the mark allocation differ, and the grading scale on the specification a school has adopted may be the 9 to 1 scale.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from the November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so plan from the live PDF rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger candidates, often as preparation for A Level Mathematics. The calculus and the harder trigonometric identities are genuinely new content rather than extensions of 0580, which is why a tutor comfortable with 0580 is not automatically useful here.
programmes.countryNote: 0606 is the hardest IGCSE maths request to staff in this emirate and we say so at enquiry rather than after payment. A Al Ghadeer family considering it should also count the evening cost: it is an additional subject carried on top of a full timetable, in a household where the commute has already taken ten hours out of the week.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-ghadee.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of the IGCSE maths course that cost Al Ghadeer candidates marks, listed by what actually goes wrong rather than by syllabus order.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: The foundation of the grade. A candidate who is slow rather than wrong at expanding, factorising and rearranging runs out of time on the longer paper regardless of how much of the syllabus they know. This is the highest-return area for tuition and the one that responds fastest to short daily drills.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Extended-tier content, including composite and inverse functions and transformations of graphs. Candidates lose marks by sketching without labelling intercepts and asymptotes, and by confusing the order of operations inside a composite function. Hours spent here are wasted on a Core-tier candidate.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Core at a basic level, Extended fully
subjects.description: Right-angled triangles appear in both tiers; the sine and cosine rules and non-right-angled work are Extended. The repeated failures are not drawing a diagram, using degrees when the calculator is in radians, and losing accuracy by rounding an intermediate angle before the final step.

subjects.name: Mensuration and geometry
subjects.description: Area, volume, surface area and circle properties. Marks go on unit conversion, particularly between cubic centimetres and litres, and on forgetting to include every face of a composite solid. These are checkable errors and a student can be trained to catch them in a single session.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Reverse percentages and compound interest cause more damage than their difficulty suggests, because candidates apply the forward method to a backward question. Ratio problems expressed in words are the other recurring loss, where the student divides in the wrong direction and never checks the answer for sense.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Cumulative frequency, box plots and histograms with unequal class widths. The histogram question is the one most often skipped or half-answered, because frequency density has to be computed rather than read off. Interpretation sentences also earn marks that candidates routinely leave on the table.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.levels: All tiers, deeper at Extended and Higher
subjects.description: Tree diagrams without replacement are the standard trap, along with confusing mutually exclusive and independent events. Candidates who draw the tree and label every branch before computing anything score consistently better than those who try to reason it out in their heads.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vector arithmetic is usually fine; proving that three points are collinear or that two lines are parallel is where marks go, because it requires a statement of reasoning rather than a calculation. This is a topic where showing working is literally the whole mark allocation.

subjects.name: Exam technique and method marks
subjects.description: Not a topic, but it behaves like the largest one. The mark scheme awards method marks for correct working even where the answer is wrong, so a candidate who writes only answers forfeits marks they had earned. Three weeks of insisting on written method usually produces a measurable change.

subjects.name: Calculator fluency
subjects.description: Knowing how to store an unrounded value, use the fraction and statistics functions and check an answer by a second route. Pearson permits a calculator on both papers, and candidates who are slow with the machine lose time they cannot recover elsewhere.

sections.heading: Where the two years actually go for a Al Ghadeer candidate
paragraphs: Year 10 and Year 11 feel long in September of Year 10 and very short by October of Year 11. The useful exercise is to lay the two years out and mark where the decisions and the pressure fall, because from a commuting household there is no slack to absorb a late start. A student losing two hours a day to the E11 has roughly ten hours a week less than a classmate who walks to school.

The first pressure point is the tier entry, settled during Year 10 on Year 9 evidence and classroom performance. The second is the Year 11 mock window, which is the first honest measurement of where the grade actually sits and the last point at which a serious change of plan is possible. The third is the final entry deadline, which sits months before the papers and after which nothing about the entry can be altered.

What families underestimate is how little of Year 11 is available. Between the mock window, the coursework and controlled assessment in other subjects, and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies load that every private school in the UAE carries, the spring term of Year 11 is close to full before any tuition is added. The hours that are genuinely free are in Year 10 and in the long breaks.

The table sets the timeline out with the action that actually matters at each stage. It is deliberately blunt about what can no longer be changed, because a parent planning in Year 11 should know which doors are closed before spending money as though they are open.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 side by side
paragraphs: Which board your child sits changes what revision should look like, and plenty of families do not know the answer. The exam entry statement from the school lists a syllabus code against each subject, and one message to the school office settles it. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1. It is entirely normal in Abu Dhabi for a student to sit Cambridge sciences and Pearson maths.

The structural differences matter. Cambridge 0580 assesses each tier across two papers, one of which does not permit a calculator. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers, which changes the arithmetic demand and the kind of mistakes candidates make. Pearson also allows modular entry in several subjects, so revision can peak at a different point in the year. The question style differs even where the content is identical, and past-paper practice on the wrong board teaches the wrong instincts.

There is a second-order effect families notice later. Because the calculator rules differ, a student who moves school mid-course between boards can arrive fluent in exactly the wrong habit, either reaching for a calculator on a paper that does not allow one or doing long arithmetic by hand on a paper where speed matters. Mid-course transfers happen often enough in this emirate to be worth asking about at enrolment.

Our practical rule is that we do not accept a booking against the subject name alone. Send the code and the tier, and the match is made against that. It takes one line in a message and it removes the commonest cause of wasted terms in this market.

sections.heading: The tier decision and the grade ceiling behind it
paragraphs: Tiering is the part of IGCSE maths that most affects a final grade and the part parents are least consulted on. In Cambridge 0580 the Core tier covers the shared core of the syllabus and its papers cannot award the top grades; the Extended tier covers the core plus the extension topics and the full range is available. Pearson's Foundation and Higher tiers work the same way. The school decides, usually in Year 10, on Year 9 attainment and classroom evidence.

The consequence reaches further than the IGCSE itself. A Core or Foundation entry is not adequate preparation for A Level Mathematics, and some university routes expect a high grade in a higher-tier maths qualification. A family that learns this in the spring of Year 11 has no options left. A family that asks in Year 9 what would have to improve for an Extended recommendation has a genuine decision and a term in which to act on it.

Tuition pitched at the wrong tier wastes money in both directions. Teaching functions, vectors and the sine rule to a Core candidate spends evenings on material that cannot appear on their paper. Teaching only core content to an Extended candidate leaves the hardest third of the course untouched until it is too late. We confirm the tier from the school's own paperwork before any paid session for exactly this reason.

If the tier is right and the grade is still short, the diagnosis is almost always behavioural rather than mathematical. Method not shown, rounding too early, units ignored, no diagram drawn. Those four account for the majority of the gap we see in candidates whose teacher reports that they understand the work.
