sections.heading: Counting backwards from the June series
paragraphs: The exam series is the one fixed point in the plan, so it makes sense to work backwards from it. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit June, with November available as a resit route. The February/March series exists but is offered to India only, which is worth saying plainly because pages written for a different market circulate those dates to UAE parents.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The clearest published illustration of the gap between a paper and a result is the November series: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from the equivalent November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day.

The milestone families most often miss is the final entry deadline, which falls months before the papers. Subject, tier and any resit are fixed at that point. The second is the zone timetable: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and it adds that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Take the timetable from the exams officer and from nowhere else.

The table is deliberately framed by milestone rather than by date, which is the only version that stays correct next year. For any actual date, Cambridge and Pearson publish live timetables and provisional timetables ahead of each series, and those are the documents to plan around.

sections.heading: Fitting maths practice around a two-emirate school run
paragraphs: The most useful thing a tutor can do for a Al Ghadeer candidate is not deliver more hours. It is to make the short daily practice land on the right thing. Maths improves through frequency, and frequency is the one resource a commuting household cannot buy more of. Twenty-five focused minutes on four evenings beats a single two-hour session, and it is also the only pattern a tired student will actually complete.

So the structure that works is one fixed session plus a set of questions for the days between. The tutor chooses those questions, which sounds trivial and is not: left to themselves, students practise the topics they can already do, because those are the ones that feel productive. A set of eight questions aimed at reverse percentages and histograms will do more than a hundred questions of comfortable algebra.

The journey itself can be used. Formula recall, converting between units, and the difference between a describe and an explain instruction are all things a passenger can rehearse. It is not a substitute for written practice and it is better than nothing, and from this corridor there is a great deal of nothing available.

Two UAE-specific adjustments belong in the plan. During Ramadan the school day shortens and sessions typically move to after Iftar, which works well when it is agreed in advance rather than improvised. And the long breaks are where a commuting student can do the volume of algebra work that term-time evenings cannot hold. Two weeks of that in a break is worth more than trying to find four extra weekday evenings in November.

sections.heading: A tuition centre in Mohammed Bin Zayed City or one-to-one online
paragraphs: This is the real decision most Al Ghadeer families are weighing, and the group rate makes it look settled before it is examined. A centre class can cost from roughly AED 100 per student an hour, against market rates of AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 for a specialist, with in-home one-to-one quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Those figures were published by the providers themselves and read in October 2026.

The arithmetic that matters is not cost per hour but cost per useful minute. A centre class works through a scheme of work covering the whole syllabus, so if your child's problem is histograms and reverse percentages, the hour may contain four minutes of what they needed. Measured that way, the cheap option can be the most expensive on the list. Group teaching is genuinely good value in one situation: every student in the room is on the same tier and stuck in the same place.

There is also the second school run. A centre in Mohammed Bin Zayed City means another journey, after a commute that has already taken an hour, in the evening traffic. For a Al Ghadeer household that cost is paid in the student's energy rather than in dirhams, and it is the reason centre attendance from this corridor tends to decay by the second month.

To be explicit about our own position: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. What we deliver here is one-to-one teaching over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the specification and tier rather than for how close they live to the E11 junction.

sections.heading: What to verify before paying an IGCSE maths tutor in this emirate
paragraphs: Three checks take five minutes and remove most of the risk. The first is the specification: ask which code and tier they teach and listen for 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher rather than IGCSE maths. The second is the permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years, and anybody tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. You can ask to see it.

The third is the school conflict. ADEK's professional ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE permit is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. The convenient arrangement, paying your child's own maths teacher, is the one to avoid. Verify the current wording on ADEK's own policy page before relying on it.

Two things worth knowing about claims. No fine schedule for unpermitted tutoring is published, so a provider quoting you a specific penalty figure is repeating something unverified. And there is no regulator approval scheme for individual private tutors: a business running a training institute with premises in Dubai needs a specific KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different thing entirely. IB Gram holds no regulator permit, accreditation or partnership.

Finally, ask what happens if it does not work. A provider who treats a tutor change as a normal review outcome rather than a complaint is one you can correct a mistake with cheaply, and at these rates the ability to correct a mistake cheaply is worth as much as the hourly figure.

process.title: Send the code and the tier
process.description: Cambridge 0580 Core or Extended, Pearson 4MA1 Foundation or Higher. Take it from the exam entry statement or ask the school office. We do not accept a booking against the subject name alone, because that single omission causes most of the wasted terms in this market.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson at a workable hour
process.description: A full session at no cost, online, scheduled after the school run lands rather than at the bell. Your child works questions from the correct tier while the tutor watches what happens when they get stuck, and you receive a written note naming the error pattern and the first six weeks of work.

process.title: Check the tier against the evidence
process.description: We say plainly whether the tier your child is entered for matches what the diagnostic showed. If it does not and there is still time, that is a conversation for Year 10 with the school. If the entry is fixed, the plan becomes maximising the grade available within it.

process.title: One session a week plus questions in between
process.description: A fixed weekday slot away from the maths homework night, with the tutor setting twenty to thirty minutes of targeted questions for the days between. The between-session set is chosen by the tutor, because students left to choose practise the topics they can already do.

process.title: Review on a marked paper at six weeks
process.description: A full paper under timing, marked against the published scheme, and a written review. That is the evidence for deciding whether to continue, change the focus or change the tutor. A tutor change is a normal review outcome and costs nothing.

whyPoints.title: Booked against a code, not a subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 Higher are different courses with different calculator rules and different question styles. Matching on the code rather than on maths in general is the single cheapest way to avoid a wasted term, and it takes one line in a message.

whyPoints.title: The tier checked before money is spent
whyPoints.description: Teaching functions and vectors to a Core candidate spends evenings on material that cannot appear on the paper. We confirm the tier from the school's own paperwork before the first paid session, which is a step almost nobody in this market takes.

whyPoints.title: Built for a commuting week
whyPoints.description: One fixed session scheduled after the car gets back, plus short targeted practice for the days between. A plan that assumes three free weekday evenings is a plan a Al Ghadeer household abandons in the second month, and the student usually blames themselves for it.

whyPoints.title: The between-session work is chosen for them
whyPoints.description: Students practise what feels productive, which is the topics they can already do. The tutor sets eight questions on reverse percentages and histograms instead, which does more than a hundred questions of comfortable algebra and takes a quarter of the time.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the board, not from us
whyPoints.description: We name the June and November series rather than restating dates that can be revised, and we point you to the exams officer's zone timetable. Cambridge warns it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone version, which is reason enough not to trust a tutoring page for a date.

faqs.question: When can an IGCSE maths lesson start for a student commuting out of Al Ghadeer?
faqs.answer: It depends on the direction of travel. A student at school within the border corridor can start around 17:00. One travelling to Khalifa City or Al Raha is usually home near 17:00, which makes 17:30 realistic. A student schooling on Abu Dhabi island or Saadiyat gets back closer to 17:45 and should start at 18:00. Allow twenty minutes after arrival: a lesson that begins the moment the car stops is a lesson nobody absorbs anything from.

faqs.question: Is my Al Ghadeer child sitting Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: The exam entry statement from the school lists a syllabus code against each subject, and one message to the school office will confirm it. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1. Do not assume one board across the timetable, because it is common in this emirate for a student to sit Cambridge sciences alongside Pearson maths. The code matters because the calculator rules and question style differ.

faqs.question: How much difference does the board make to IGCSE maths revision?
faqs.answer: More than the shared content suggests. Cambridge 0580 includes a paper without a calculator, so non-calculator arithmetic has to be drilled. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers, which shifts the error pattern toward speed and rounding instead. Pearson also allows modular entry at some centres, which changes when revision has to peak. Practising the wrong board's past papers teaches habits that cost marks on the paper your child actually sits.

faqs.question: What is the Core and Extended tier difference in Cambridge 0580?
faqs.answer: Core covers the shared core of the syllabus and its two papers cannot award the top grades. Extended covers the core plus extension topics, including functions, vectors and the sine and cosine rules, and the full grade range is available. Pearson's Foundation and Higher tiers work the same way. The school decides the entry during Year 10 on Year 9 evidence, and once the series entry is made the tier is fixed for that sitting.

faqs.question: Can tuition still change my child's tier if we start in Year 10?
faqs.answer: Early in Year 10, sometimes. A tier recommendation rests on attainment and classroom evidence, and a term of focused work on algebraic fluency and on showing method can change what the school is looking at. By the spring of Year 10 the entry is usually settled, and after the final entry deadline nothing about it can change for that series. The honest window is Year 9 into the first term of Year 10.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics cost Al Ghadeer candidates the most marks?
faqs.answer: Reverse percentages and compound interest, because candidates apply the forward method to a backward question. Histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency density must be computed rather than read. Tree diagrams without replacement. Vectors, where the marks are in the written reasoning rather than the arithmetic. And unit conversion in mensuration, especially between cubic centimetres and litres. All five are trainable and none of them requires new mathematics, only deliberate practice.

faqs.question: How much practice should happen between maths sessions?
faqs.answer: Twenty-five focused minutes on four evenings does more than one long weekly block, because maths improves through frequency rather than duration. The important detail is who chooses the questions. Left to themselves, students practise the topics they can already do, since those feel productive. A tutor-chosen set of eight questions on the actual weak topics will move the grade further than a hundred questions of comfortable algebra.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre class in Mohammed Bin Zayed City better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Only if the class matches your child's tier and the group shares their gap. Centre classes can start from roughly AED 100 a head against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, but a class working through the whole syllabus may give your child four useful minutes in an hour. Add a second evening journey from the border corridor and the energy cost is real. Measured per useful minute, the cheap option often is not.

faqs.question: When do Al Ghadeer candidates sit their IGCSE maths papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two, with November usually used as a resit route. The February/March series is offered to India only, so ignore any page quoting it at a UAE family. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For the actual timetable, use the copy your child's exams officer holds, since every Cambridge centre belongs to one of six administrative zones with its own version.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss the final entry deadline for a tier change?
faqs.answer: Nothing can be changed for that series once the deadline passes. Subject, tier and any resit are fixed at final entries, which fall months before the papers themselves. That is why the entry conversation belongs in Year 10 rather than in the spring of Year 11. If the entry is wrong and fixed, the useful work is securing the best grade available within the tier entered and planning a resit in the November series if a higher grade is genuinely needed.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE maths tutor to a home in Al Ghadeer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and a tutor travelling to the family's address is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Al Ghadeer students are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with past papers screen-shared and worked through together. The gain is that the tutor is matched to 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher rather than drawn from the small group willing to drive to this junction at dismissal.

faqs.question: Can maths sessions move during Ramadan for a family in this corridor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a fixed post-Iftar slot holds better than trying to keep the usual time. The school day shortens and the household rhythm changes, so planning the shift in advance works far better than cancelling week by week. The thing not to assume is that school deadlines move with it. Controlled assessment and mock dates set by the school stand, so the sensible plan front-loads work before the month rather than hoping for a quiet fortnight.

faqs.question: Should a Al Ghadeer student add 0606 on top of a long commute?
faqs.answer: It is strong preparation for A Level Mathematics and it is an extra subject carried on top of a full timetable. From a commuting household that cost is paid in evenings the family does not have, so it is worth being realistic. The calculus and harder trigonometric identities in 0606 are new content rather than extensions of 0580, so it also needs a tutor who has taught 0606 specifically, and that is the hardest IGCSE maths match to make in this emirate.

faqs.question: What should I check before paying an IGCSE maths tutor in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Ask which syllabus code and tier they teach and expect a specific answer. Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued free of charge for two years. Avoid paying a teacher from your child's own school, since ADEK's reported ethics rules and the permit's code of conduct both bar that. And ask what happens if the match does not work after three sessions.

faqs.question: Are there regulator-approved maths tutors in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No, and it is a claim worth treating as a warning sign. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in the emirate; it does not run an approval scheme for individual private tutors. In Dubai, KHDA permits training institutes with premises through a specific Educational Services Permit, which is a business licence rather than a tutor endorsement. What an individual tutor should hold is the MoHRE private tuition work permit. IB Gram holds no regulator permit, accreditation or partnership of any kind.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-ghadee.closingBody: Three lines in a message get a useful answer for a Al Ghadeer family: the syllabus code from the exam entry, the tier, and which way the school run goes. The first two decide who can teach your child properly. The third decides what time a lesson can honestly start, which from this corridor is usually 17:30 or later. The first session is free, runs online and one-to-one in Gulf Standard Time, and ends with a written note naming the topics costing marks and the twenty-five minutes of practice that should fill the evenings in between.

intro.heading: The same eight weeks does different work in October and in April
paragraphs: Families on Al Jubail Island reach this search at very different points in the school year, and that point matters more than almost anything else they will decide. An eight-week block of maths tuition starting in October of Year 10 can change which tier a student is entered for, which changes the grade ceiling, which changes what they can study after Year 11. The same eight weeks starting in April of Year 11 cannot change any of those things. It can improve technique and nothing structural.

This is the single most expensive misunderstanding in the Abu Dhabi tutoring market. Demand is heavily concentrated in the final term, which is also when the fewest specialists have capacity and when the least is still changeable. The families who get the most out of tutoring are not the ones who spend the most; they are the ones who spent in the autumn of Year 10 on something specific and then stopped when the gap closed.

So the structure of this page is a calendar. What the autumn of Year 10 can achieve, what the spring of Year 10 is for, how the autumn of Year 11 differs, what the winter mock window actually tells you, and what the final run from February onwards should and should not contain. Each section is written so a parent can find the month they are standing in and read what is still available to them. The honest version of most answers is narrower than a family hopes and more useful than a general promise.

The exam dates matter to all of it, and they are more often misunderstood than unknown. Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so advice built around a February exam window does not apply to a child sitting in Abu Dhabi, however widely it circulates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable having run to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

On delivery, so it is clear before anything else: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Al Jubail Island lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. From an island with no school on it, where every run crosses a bridge, that also means a weekly slot can be placed late enough to survive the school run and still be held in the same place forty weeks later. A slot placed once in September and never renegotiated is worth more than any amount of good intention in March.

programmes.name: The year before the course
programmes.description: Sets are usually finalised in this year and they shape the tier that follows. The content that matters is non-calculator number work, confident algebraic rearrangement and the habit of writing method. programmes.countryNote: Al Jubail Island's school-age population skews younger than the emirate average, so a good number of households here are at exactly this point with the IGCSE years still ahead. A short diagnostic block in Year 9 is worth more per dirham than anything available later.

programmes.name: First IGCSE year
programmes.description: The year in which structural change is still possible. The tier conversation is live, the content is being met for the first time, and a gap closed now does not have to be carried into a year with eight other subjects competing for attention. Rates are the same as in Year 11 and the effect is considerably larger.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools typically settle the tier recommendation during Year 10 and submit entries months before the papers. A family that produces a written diagnostic report during Year 10 has evidence to bring to that conversation; a family that raises it in Year 11 is usually too late.

programmes.name: Exam year
programmes.description: The year of technique rather than structure. The tier is fixed, the content is largely taught, and the available gains are in whole-paper timing, showing method, recognising question types and eliminating repeated errors. programmes.countryNote: The winter mock window drives the predicted grades a sixth form or an IB campus will read, which makes it the highest-stakes assessment of the year and the one most families treat as a rehearsal. abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-jubail.subjectsIntro: The parts of IGCSE maths that respond at different points in the year. Matching the work to the month is most of what a plan is for.

subjects.name: Non-calculator number fluency
subjects.description: Fractions, standard form, surds and index laws performed by hand at speed. Best addressed in Year 10 or early Year 11, because it is a motor skill built by short frequent repetition rather than by a late intensive block. On the Cambridge route it carries half the grade.

subjects.name: Algebraic rearrangement and quadratics
subjects.description: Completing the square, the quadratic formula, simultaneous equations with one non-linear, and algebraic fractions. The spine of the subject and the best predictor of a grade, so it belongs early. Insecurity here leaks into mensuration and probability.

subjects.name: Similar shapes and scale factors
subjects.description: Area scales with the square of a linear factor and volume with the cube. A single-session fix at any point in the year, and one of the few topics where a late intervention still pays, because the error costs a whole question each time it appears.

subjects.name: Trigonometry rule selection
subjects.description: Sine rule, cosine rule, area formula, bearings and three-dimensional work. Rule choice rather than application is where marks go, so the useful practice is rapid identification under timing. Responds well in the autumn of Year 11.

subjects.name: Graphs, functions and transformations
subjects.description: Sketching and reading quadratics, cubics and reciprocals, transformations of curves, and inverse and composite functions on the Edexcel Higher route. Mid-course work that sits comfortably in the winter term of Year 11.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability and Venn notation, where the structure rather than the arithmetic causes the loss. Short and responsive, so it fits well into a late plan when bigger content gaps cannot be closed.

subjects.name: Mensuration and bounds
subjects.description: Volume and surface area of composite solids, upper and lower bounds, and compound measures. A topic where premature rounding does most of the damage, which makes it worth revisiting right before the series rather than only early.

subjects.name: Showing method
subjects.description: A habit rather than a topic. Most marks on a multi-step question are method marks, so a correct answer with no visible route scores less than a wrong answer with a clear one. Takes about three sessions and one dissected paper, at any point in the year.

subjects.name: Whole-paper timing
subjects.description: Papers sat under exam conditions from the student's own specification, then dissected against the published scheme. February onwards, on weekend mornings, because a paper sat tired after a bridge crossing gives a misleading result.

subjects.name: The final-question problem
subjects.description: Students who consistently leave the last questions unattempted have a pacing problem rather than a knowledge problem, and it is diagnosable only from whole timed papers. A finishing strategy for the last ten minutes is late-stage work that genuinely pays.

sections.heading: Find the month you are standing in
paragraphs: The most useful question a family can answer before buying anything is where in the two-year course they are, because that determines what is still available to them. Structural change, meaning the tier and therefore the grade ceiling, is available in Year 10 and gone by the middle of Year 11. Content change is available until roughly February of Year 11. Technique change is available until the week before the papers. Nothing else is on the table at any point.

The table below maps the year to what each window can achieve. Read it once and the pattern is obvious: the value of a tutoring hour declines through the course while demand for it rises, and the crossover happens around the winter mocks. A family spending in October of Year 10 is buying options; a family spending in April of Year 11 is buying marks at the margin. Both are legitimate purchases and they are not the same purchase, and almost nobody says so.

There is one exception worth knowing about, and it is the fortnight after the winter mocks. That window is late in the course and unusually valuable, because the marked scripts produced in it are the only honest, specific, personal diagnostic a family will get before the real series. The complication is that school holidays frequently sit inside that fortnight, which is why the session has to be booked in November for a December date rather than discovered in January when every family in the emirate wants the same slot.

sections.heading: The next eight weeks, from four different starting points
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the natural unit for a tutoring plan: long enough to change something measurable, short enough to review honestly. What those eight weeks should contain depends entirely on where they start, and writing the plan down before the first session is what allows anyone to judge it afterwards.

From the autumn of Year 10, the eight weeks are a tier campaign. Weeks one and two diagnose, from marked school work, and produce a written list. Weeks three to six drill the two things the tier decision actually rests on, which are non-calculator number fluency and algebraic rearrangement. Weeks seven and eight re-test and produce a dated report the family can take to the head of maths. From the autumn of Year 11, the same eight weeks are topic repair, following the school's teaching order so nothing is taught in two competing versions, with method habits corrected throughout.

From the fortnight after mocks, the eight weeks begin with dissection and then attack the two or three error types the script revealed, with a second paper at week four to test whether the correction held. From February, the eight weeks are the paper programme: five whole papers under timing, marked against the published scheme, dissected in session, with a running error log and a finishing strategy for the last ten minutes. The table sets all four out side by side. Write the plan down in two or three lines and keep it. The point of a dated plan is not formality; it is that in eight weeks somebody can read it and say whether the thing it promised happened.

sections.heading: What a winter mock actually tells you
paragraphs: Most households read a mock result as a verdict and treat the preparation for it as optional, which gets both halves wrong. The preparation matters because the grades coming out of the mock window usually become the predicted grades a sixth form or an IB campus reads. The result matters far less than the script, because the script is the information.

A grade tells you the outcome. A marked paper tells you the mechanism, and the mechanism is what can be changed. Read by somebody who knows the specification, a mock script yields a specific list rather than an impression: four to six marks lost per paper to unshown method, two to premature rounding, a linear scale factor applied to a volume question, the cosine rule used where the sine rule was signalled, and the last two questions untouched because time ran out. That is five separate interventions, three of which take a single session each.

The timing constraint is the thing families underestimate. Within a fortnight the student still remembers what they were thinking at question seventeen and can recognise an error as their own choice rather than as an abstract possibility. Six weeks later the paper is cold, the memory has gone and the conversation turns general. Since the holidays usually fall inside that fortnight, the session has to be reserved in November. It is also the single busiest request in the Abu Dhabi tutoring calendar, so a family that plans it gets a specialist and a family that improvises gets whoever is left.
bullets: Mock grades usually become the predicted grades a sixth form reads
The script, not the grade, contains the actionable information

sections.heading: June, November, or move on: the resit decision
paragraphs: Some families face a resit decision, either because a grade came in below what a sixth form requires or because a subject was always going to need a second attempt. The decision is time-sensitive and it is usually made with less information than it deserves.

The mechanics first. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit June and November, so the November series is the natural resit route after a June result, and vice versa. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which means a November resit result arrives in January, well after most sixth-form terms have begun. That gap is the central practical fact in the decision and it is rarely explained.

The questions worth asking are therefore about sequencing rather than about ability. Does the destination sixth form or IB campus accept a January result, and under what conditions? Is the student carrying the resit alongside a full post-16 timetable, which is a genuine load? Is the gap in the original grade a content gap, which needs real teaching time, or a technique and pacing gap, which can be fixed in six weeks? And is maths the actual obstacle to the destination, or is it one of several? The table sets out the shape of each route. Ask the destination in writing rather than relying on a conversation at an open evening. Admissions positions on late results vary between campuses in the same emirate, and a written answer is what a family can actually plan around.

sections.heading: Ramadan inside a revision plan
paragraphs: Ramadan falls inside the IGCSE calendar every year and every weekly arrangement in the UAE has to deal with it. The families whose plans survive are the ones who decided in September what would happen, rather than the ones who renegotiated week by week once it arrived.

The practical adjustments are well understood. The school day shortens across the country and household rhythm moves towards the evening, so a session that worked at half past six often works better after iftar. Shorter and more frequent sessions suit a shortened day better than a single long block, which means two forty-minute sessions can achieve more than one ninety-minute one. Recall and fluency work suits this period; new difficult content does not.

For a Year 11 facing the June series the stakes are higher, because the interval between Ramadan and the papers is short and maths is cumulative. A four-week gap at that point is expensive and hard to recover from in the time remaining. The sensible plan is to move the slot deliberately, reduce the session length rather than the frequency, and schedule the lighter material into the month, saving whole timed papers for either side of it. Agreeing all of that in writing in September takes ten minutes and prevents a month of cancellations. One further practical note: tell the tutor the household's iftar timing rather than leaving them to guess it. A slot agreed against the actual timing holds, and a slot agreed in the abstract gets moved twice and then dropped.
bullets: Move the slot after iftar rather than cancelling week by week
Two shorter sessions beat one long block during a shortened day
Recall and fluency work suits the month; difficult new content does not
Keep whole timed papers for either side of it

sections.heading: The summer between Year 10 and Year 11
paragraphs: Ten weeks is a long time for a cumulative subject, and the summer between Year 10 and Year 11 is where more maths is quietly lost than anywhere else in the course. Al Jubail Island households travel, often for extended periods, and a student who stops maths entirely returns measurably weaker in exactly the fluency the tier decision rests on.

What decays is specific and predictable. Non-calculator arithmetic goes first, because it is a motor skill and motor skills fade without use. Algebraic rearrangement follows. Method habits loosen. Trigonometric rule selection, which was never secure, becomes a guess. What does not decay much is conceptual understanding, which is why a student can return in September appearing to know everything and still perform badly on a timed paper.

The remedy is small and it is almost never taken: two sessions a month across the summer, forty-five minutes each, aimed at fluency rather than at new content, delivered online wherever the family happens to be. Six sessions in total, which costs a fraction of the autumn remediation it prevents. The honest reason more families do not do it is that the cost of skipping it is invisible until November, by which point it has been absorbed into a general sense that Year 11 is harder than expected. Treat it as maintenance rather than as teaching. Nothing new is introduced, nothing is assessed, and the sessions are short enough that a student on holiday does not resent them, which is the only way six of them actually happen.
bullets: Non-calculator arithmetic decays first, because it is a motor skill
Conceptual understanding survives, which disguises the loss
Two short sessions a month, aimed at fluency rather than content
Online delivery means it happens wherever the family is travelling

sections.heading: Hiring mid-year, and the questions timing makes urgent
paragraphs: A family hiring in October has time to make a mistake and recover. A family hiring in February does not, which changes which questions matter most at the point of hiring. The specification and tier still come first, but two others move up the list.

The first is availability with a date. In the final two terms, the honest answer to can you cover this is sometimes no, and a provider who says yes and then assigns whoever has capacity is doing more damage in February than they would in October. Ask directly who will teach, by name, which courses and tiers they have taught, and whether the slot you need genuinely exists rather than being notionally possible. The second is what the first session will contain. In February there is no room for a get-to-know-you hour, so insist that the marked mock script is read before the session and that the hour starts on the error list.

The permit question still applies at any point in the year. An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, quoted figures are unverified. Treat the permit as a legal floor rather than a quality signal, because no UAE regulator approves individual tutors on teaching merit.
bullets: Ask who will teach, by name, and which tiers they have taught
Ask whether the slot genuinely exists or is only notionally possible
Insist the marked script is read before a February first session
The MoHRE permit is free, valid two years, and not a quality judgement

sections.heading: After results: what the grade is used for and when
paragraphs: A maths grade at sixteen gets read by three different audiences on three different timetables, and knowing which deadline is binding stops a family optimising for the wrong one.

Sixth forms and IB campuses read it first and read it as an entry gate. A-Level Mathematics commonly expects a grade 7 or an A; the sciences and economics expect a strong maths grade; IB Analysis and Approaches assumes Extended-level algebra from the first week. These decisions are made in the weeks after results, which is why a November resit landing in January can arrive after the relevant door has closed.

The Ministry of Education reads it later and differently. On the British track, equivalency requires a pass in five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competitor page in this market states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which contradicts the published rule and is exactly the sort of error a family can plan a year around. Equivalency is the Ministry's process, so confirm current requirements on moe.gov.ae rather than relying on any tutoring site. Work backwards from whichever of those three is binding for your child. A family optimising for an equivalency rule when the sixth-form gate is the real obstacle is solving the wrong problem carefully.
bullets: Sixth forms and IB campuses read the grade within weeks of results
A-Level Maths commonly expects grade 7 or A; IB AA assumes Extended algebra
MoE British-track equivalency counts five subjects at no less than E or grade 3
Arabic and Islamic education sit outside that count of five

process.title: Say which month and year group you are in
process.description: Year 10 autumn, Year 11 after mocks, six weeks before the papers. That single fact determines what is still changeable and therefore what the hours should be aimed at, and it is the first thing we ask rather than the last.

process.title: Send the specification code, the tier and a marked script
process.description: The code is on the front of any past paper the school issued; the tier comes from the head of maths. The marked script is what makes a first session a diagnosis. Together they take one email and a photograph.

process.title: Agree an eight-week plan in writing
process.description: What the eight weeks will attempt, what will exist at the end of them, and how it will be judged. A plan written before the first session can be reviewed honestly afterwards; an open-ended arrangement cannot be, which is how hours accumulate without anybody deciding to buy them.

process.title: Reserve the post-mock session in November
process.description: The fortnight after the winter mocks is the highest-value window in the course and the busiest week in the emirate's tutoring calendar, and school holidays usually sit inside it. Booking it before the mocks happen is the whole trick.

process.title: Review at eight weeks and decide deliberately
process.description: Set the plan, the error log and the most recent school evidence side by side. Either the evidence moved, in which case continue or taper, or it did not, in which case the plan changes or the hours stop. Inertia is the most expensive outcome available.

whyPoints.title: Plans written from the month you are in
whyPoints.description: An eight-week block in October of Year 10 is a tier campaign; the same eight weeks in April is technique work. Saying which one you are buying is the difference between a judged purchase and an open-ended one.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation while it is still open
whyPoints.description: Entry tier sets the grade ceiling and therefore the post-16 options, and evidence produced in Year 10 carries weight in that conversation in a way a parent's impression in Year 11 does not.

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts read while they are warm
whyPoints.description: Within a fortnight a student still remembers their own reasoning, and the script yields a specific error list rather than an impression. Reserved in November, because the holidays sit in the window.

whyPoints.title: The right series, not the wrong one
whyPoints.description: UAE Cambridge candidates sit June and November, not the India-only February and March series, and Pearson runs May/June and November with November results arriving in January. Resit planning turns on exactly that.

whyPoints.title: A calendar that includes Ramadan and the summer
whyPoints.description: The slot moves deliberately for Ramadan with shorter more frequent sessions, and thins rather than stopping over the summer, because non-calculator fluency is the first thing to decay in a ten-week gap.

whyPoints.title: No crossing, and a slot that holds
whyPoints.description: From an island with no school on it, a late online slot can be placed once in September and still be running in April, with no tutor's journey to absorb in either the fee or the schedule.

faqs.question: What can a maths tutor still change eight weeks before the June papers?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be worth doing, but the available gains have narrowed. By then the entry tier is fixed, so the grade ceiling cannot change, and most content has been taught. What remains is technique: showing method, pacing, recognising question types and eliminating two or three named repeated errors. Those are real and worth buying. What is no longer available is the structural change an autumn of Year 10 block could have delivered. Expect marginal gains honestly described rather than a transformation, and be wary of anyone promising otherwise.

faqs.question: What can eight weeks of maths tutoring achieve in the autumn of Year 10?
faqs.answer: The most of anything available in the course, because the tier is still open. A sensible eight weeks runs as a campaign: two weeks diagnosing from marked school work and producing a written list, four weeks drilling the two things the tier decision actually rests on, which are non-calculator number fluency and algebraic rearrangement, then two weeks re-testing and writing a dated report. That report is what a family takes into the conversation with the head of maths, and written evidence carries weight there in a way a parental impression does not.

faqs.question: When is the single best hour to buy in the whole two-year course?
faqs.answer: A session in the fortnight after the winter mocks, with the marked script on screen. That script is the only honest, specific, personal diagnostic available before the real series, and its value decays quickly: within two weeks the student still remembers what they were thinking at question seventeen, while six weeks later the paper is cold and the conversation turns general. The practical complication is that school holidays usually sit inside that fortnight, so the session has to be reserved in November rather than improvised in January.

faqs.question: Which exam series does an Al Jubail Island student sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series, with November as the alternate or resit route. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a February window does not apply to a child sitting in Abu Dhabi. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones, which the school's exams officer will know.

faqs.question: If my child resits in November, when will the result arrive?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect, and that gap is the central fact in the decision. On the Pearson route, November results reach students in January; the November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. A Cambridge November result also arrives weeks after the papers. Either way a November resit result reaches a student after most post-16 terms have already started, so the question to ask the destination sixth form or IB campus is whether they will accept a January result and on what conditions, before committing to the route.

faqs.question: Should a resit go in at the next series or wait a full year?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the original gap was content or technique. A technique and pacing problem can genuinely be fixed in the weeks available before a November series, particularly if a marked script from the first attempt is available to work from. A real content gap usually cannot, and attempting it alongside a full post-16 timetable tends to produce a second disappointing result. Waiting for the following June gives a full year of preparation and delays everything by a year, which is sometimes the right trade and sometimes not.

faqs.question: How should a maths plan handle the months around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: By moving deliberately rather than pausing, and by deciding in September what will happen. The school day shortens across the UAE and household rhythm shifts to the evening, so a session that sat at half past six often works better after iftar. Two shorter sessions suit a shortened day better than one ninety-minute block. Schedule recall and fluency work into the month and keep whole timed papers for either side of it. For a Year 11 heading into the June series a four-week gap is expensive and hard to recover.

faqs.question: Does stopping maths over the summer actually matter?
faqs.answer: More than it appears to, and the damage is specific. Non-calculator arithmetic decays first because it is a motor skill rather than an understanding, and algebraic rearrangement follows. Method habits loosen and trigonometric rule selection, if it was never secure, becomes guesswork. Conceptual understanding survives, which is what disguises the loss: a student can return in September seeming to know everything and still perform badly on a timed paper. Two short sessions a month across the summer, aimed at fluency rather than content, prevents almost all of it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come out to Al Jubail Island during exam term?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram, at any point in the year. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Some Abu Dhabi providers will, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure absorbs a round trip across the water. In exam term the stability issue matters even more than the cost one, because a late session depending on two bridge crossings is the one that gets moved when something goes wrong.

faqs.question: What should I insist on if we are hiring in February rather than October?
faqs.answer: Three things, because there is no time to recover from a bad start. That the marked mock script is read before the first session, so the hour begins on the error list rather than on introductions. That you are told who will teach, by name, and which specifications and tiers they have actually taught. And that the slot you need genuinely exists rather than being notionally possible, with a straight answer if it does not. In February an optimistic yes followed by whoever has capacity does far more damage than it would in October.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week makes sense in the final term?
faqs.answer: One for most students, with a second for six to eight weeks if a mock script showed two or three fixable error types. More than two a week in the final term is rarely a teaching decision; it is usually a response to anxiety, and it competes with the independent past-paper practice that actually moves a maths grade at that stage. The structure that works is one session dissecting a paper the student sat themselves, plus the student's own timed practice in between, tapering rather than intensifying as the series approaches.

faqs.question: What does the maths grade get used for, and on what timetable?
faqs.answer: Three audiences on three timetables. Sixth forms and IB campuses read it within weeks of results as an entry gate: A-Level Mathematics commonly expects grade 7 or A, and IB Analysis and Approaches assumes Extended-level algebra from the first week. Employers read it much later and loosely. The Ministry of Education reads it for equivalency, where the British track requires five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3 plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at E, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five.

faqs.question: Can the entry tier still be changed in the autumn of Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the window closes earlier than families expect. The entry, including the tier, is submitted by the school's exams officer months before the papers, and once submitted it is fixed for that series. Before that point a maths department will usually consider evidence, which is why a dated written diagnostic report from a specialist carries more weight in the conversation than an impression does. The questions to put to the school are what the current tier caps the grade at, what that closes after Year 11, and when the entry is submitted.

faqs.question: Which schools do your IGCSE maths students near Al Jubail Island attend?
faqs.answer: Families on and around the island travel to campuses on Saadiyat Island and Yas Island and across to Al Raha and Khalifa City. The names that come up include Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, West Yas Academy, Al Yasmina Academy, Reach British School and Amity International School Abu Dhabi, which between them use both Cambridge and Pearson specifications and run their mock windows across several different weeks. Those names describe the local education map only. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit, whatever time of year it is?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it does not vary by season. An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no official fine schedule is published.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-jubail.closingHeading: Tell us the month, and we will tell you what is still possible
abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-jubail.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Jubail Island, the most useful thing you can say first is where in the course your child is. Year 10 autumn means the tier is still open and an eight-week campaign can change the ceiling. After mocks means the script is the asset and the fortnight is short. February means technique, pacing and whole timed papers. Send the specification code, the tier and one marked script, and the free trial starts on the error list rather than on introductions. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-karama.tutorsIntro: These tutors prepare IGCSE mathematics candidates across central Abu Dhabi island, including Al Karamah, Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan. Each profile names the board and syllabus code, which is the comparison that decides whether a match is useful.

intro.heading: The comparisons nobody sets out for you
paragraphs: Al Karamah sits along Karamah Street in the middle of Abu Dhabi island, with Al Mushrif to the south and Al Nahyan to the north-east, and its families send children to a mix of British, Indian and international schools across the island and out onto the mainland. That mix is the first comparison worth making, because the school decides the board and the board decides the paper, and a maths tutor is only useful if they know which paper is coming.

The second comparison is the grade scale. Most IGCSE mathematics candidates are now awarded on a 9 to 1 scale, where 9 sits above the former A*, 7 is broadly comparable to the former A and 4 is broadly comparable to the former C, with some Cambridge syllabuses still reported on A* to G. Parents who grew up with letters frequently misjudge a number, treating a 5 as a near-miss on an A when it is nearer the middle of the range, and a plan built on that misreading aims at the wrong target.

The third is timing, and it is the comparison with the largest consequences. Support bought in Year 10 can still influence the Core or Extended entry decision, because schools generally confirm tiers in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the evidence of internal assessments. Support bought in February of Year 11 arrives after that decision, which means it is working inside a grade ceiling somebody else has already set. Identical sessions, bought a year apart, buy entirely different things, and nobody points this out at the time.

The fourth is the series. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in June and November, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in May/June and November. Which one a student sits, and whether November functions as a resit route or as a first sitting, changes the whole shape of the revision year. Several pages written for UAE parents get the series wrong, and an entry deadline is something a family acts on. The results tail differs between the two as well, which matters when a sixth-form or university place depends on a grade arriving by a particular month rather than merely arriving.

One comparison is simpler than families expect. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every session runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen, which removes the published AED 180 to 500 in-home band from the conversation and replaces it with the AED 150 to 300 band for qualified online subject tutors. The difference between those two numbers is a journey across the island at the worst hour of the day.
bullets: The school sets the board; the board sets the paper structure
On the 9 to 1 scale, grade 4 is broadly comparable to the former C
Year 10 support can still influence the tier entry; Year 11 cannot
UAE candidates sit June and November, never February or March
Delivery is online one-to-one; no UAE home visits

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-karama.programmesIntro: An Al Karamah family may have children on two or three different Year 10 and 11 routes at once, which makes the programme comparison practical rather than academic. The courses below are the ones genuinely in play in this part of Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 at 35 per cent and Paper 4 at 65 per cent. Compared with the Edexcel equivalent, the uneven weighting means revision should build towards sustained performance on one long paper rather than spreading evenly across two.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Tiered Foundation and Higher, examined through two papers of two hours each weighted equally. Compared with Cambridge, even coverage across the whole specification matters more and stamina on a single dominant paper matters slightly less, which changes how the final six weeks should be spent.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel International GCSE series run in May/June and November. For a sense of the tail between sitting and results: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge International Mathematics
programmes.description: Expects a graphics calculator and includes an investigation component, and is widely used by schools feeding into the IB Diploma. Compared with 0580 the content overlaps substantially and the assessment does not, because open-ended exploration is tested in a way 0580 never attempts.
programmes.countryNote: Al Karamah families whose children attend an IB-track school are the ones most likely to meet 0607, and the most likely to buy 0580 revision material by mistake. The code is on the entry confirmation and settles the question in a glance.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics
programmes.description: The feeder stage, with optional Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Compared with the IGCSE years it carries no certification weight, which is precisely why acting on a weak result here is so inexpensive relative to acting on a weak Year 11 mock.
programmes.countryNote: A weak Year 9 Checkpoint result preserves every option. The same weakness discovered in Year 11 has already influenced a tier entry, which is the comparison that makes early support the cheapest intervention available.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-karama.subjectsIntro: The entries below cover the IGCSE mathematics topics that generate requests from central Abu Dhabi island, described by what the examination demands rather than by textbook chapter.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and algebraic fractions at the upper tiers. Compared with every other topic this one determines whether a student can even start the longer questions, which is why it sits first on any repair list.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous systems
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic solving, including the formula and completing the square at the upper tier. Marks go missing when a quadratic is solved and only one root stated, or when an inequality direction is not reversed on multiplying by a negative.

subjects.name: Number, accuracy and bounds
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Significant figures, decimal places, upper and lower bounds and rounding within a chain of calculation. Premature rounding is the most expensive habit in the subject, because it removes accuracy marks from questions answered correctly.

subjects.name: Geometry, bearings and constructions
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems at the upper tier, loci and bearings. These are compliance marks: bearings stated to three figures, arcs left visible, theorem reasons named. Cheapest marks on the paper to recover and the most irritating to lose.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Right-angled work, then sine and cosine rules and triangle area at the upper tier, including three-dimensional problems. The recurring failure is selecting the wrong rule because the diagram was never labelled before calculation began.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound shapes
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Area, surface area and volume, extending to spheres, cones and frustums. Unit errors dominate the losses: a volume given in square centimetres earns nothing however correct the arithmetic behind it.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals and tree diagrams. Histograms with unequal class widths are among the most reliably lost marks in the whole specification, because frequency density is skipped under time pressure.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Sketching quadratics, reciprocals and exponentials, function notation, inverse and composite functions. Students who can plot cannot always sketch, and sketching from properties rather than from a table of values is the skill being assessed.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Column vectors and vector geometry in a plane. Proof-style questions reward writing a route in terms of the given vectors, and lose marks when a student states a conclusion without showing the path taken to reach it.

subjects.name: Investigation work, 0607 only
subjects.description: The component that distinguishes Cambridge International Mathematics from 0580. It rewards exploring a situation, noticing structure and explaining reasoning rather than producing one final answer, and students arriving from 0580 need practice specifically on open-ended work.

sections.heading: Which boards the schools around Al Karamah actually run
paragraphs: The first comparison to make is not between tutors but between schools, because the school determines which examination your child sits and therefore which tutor is useful. Central Abu Dhabi island carries a genuine mix. Long-established British-curriculum campuses in and around Al Mushrif and Al Bateen enter candidates for Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. IB-track schools on the islands and the mainland corridor frequently use Cambridge International Mathematics, code 0607, as a Diploma feeder. Indian-curriculum schools out on the mainland run CBSE alongside, in some cases, Cambridge provision.

That mix has a practical consequence families underestimate: schools sometimes use different boards for different subjects. A student can sit Cambridge mathematics and Edexcel sciences at the same school in the same year. Asking the office once, for one subject, does not answer the question for the rest. Ask subject by subject, and ask for the code rather than the board name, because the code is what identifies the paper.

The comparison between boards is real but narrower than it sounds. Both are widely accepted by universities and neither is harder in any general sense. What differs is architecture. Cambridge 0580 at Extended tier is a 35 per cent short-answer paper plus a 65 per cent structured paper. Edexcel 4MA1 at Higher tier is two papers of two hours weighted equally. Cambridge 0607 adds a graphics-calculator expectation and an investigation. Three different revision shapes from three codes that a shop assistant will happily sell you the same workbook for.

Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by ADEK, which publishes its own inspection outcomes. That is the only common scale on which two schools running different curricula can be compared, and it is named by almost none of the tutoring pages written for Abu Dhabi. Treat a rating as information about a school rather than about a particular class in a particular year.

sections.heading: IGCSE maths compared with the other Year 10 and 11 courses in the UAE
paragraphs: Al Karamah families frequently have a point of comparison from another system, either a sibling, a previous school or their own schooling, and the comparisons are rarely like for like. Setting the main alternatives beside IGCSE mathematics shows what is genuinely different rather than merely unfamiliar.

CBSE Class 10 mathematics, taught widely in Abu Dhabi's Indian-curriculum schools, is examined through a single board examination with internal assessment alongside, and its content emphasis sits heavily on algebra, trigonometry and coordinate geometry. Compared with IGCSE Extended the procedural demand is similar and the question style differs: IGCSE leans harder on multi-step contextual problems and on command-word precision, which is why a transferring student can know the mathematics and lose marks on the format.

American-curriculum mathematics in Years 10 and 11 is usually organised by course, Algebra II or Pre-Calculus for instance, with continuous assessment through the year rather than a single terminal series. Compared with IGCSE the pressure is distributed differently: a student used to grades accumulating from quizzes and projects finds a two-paper terminal examination a very different experience, and the revision skills required are not the same skills.

Then there is the question of what the mandatory UAE subjects add. Private schools in the country are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Those subjects occupy timetable space in every system, which is part of why a Year 11 week feels fuller than the examination entry list suggests, and why the workable tutoring hour in Al Karamah sits later in the evening than parents initially propose.

sections.heading: What a 9 to 1 grade actually means, compared
paragraphs: This is the comparison that causes the most quiet misjudgement in Al Karamah households. Most IGCSE mathematics candidates are now awarded on a 9 to 1 scale, and parents who grew up with letter grades, or who are familiar with percentage-based systems, routinely read the numbers wrongly in both directions.

The anchors are worth knowing. Grade 9 sits above the former A*, which means it is deliberately harder to achieve than the top letter grade was and is awarded to a smaller proportion of candidates. Grade 7 is broadly comparable to the former A. Grade 4 is broadly comparable to the former C, which is the point most systems treat as a standard pass. Some Cambridge syllabuses are still reported on an A* to G scale, so check which scale your child's subject uses rather than assuming.

Two misreadings follow from not knowing this. The first is treating a 5 as a near-miss on a top grade, when it sits around the middle of the range, and therefore under-reacting to a mock result that genuinely warrants attention. The second is treating a 7 as disappointing because it is not a 9, when it is broadly the former A and an entirely strong outcome for most onward routes. Both misreadings lead families to buy the wrong amount of support, in opposite directions.

The practical use of the scale is in target setting. A target expressed as a grade is nearly useless to a tutor; a target expressed as the specific marks currently being lost is immediately actionable. A student losing accuracy marks to premature rounding, method marks to unshown working and a cluster of statistics marks to frequency density is a student with a plan. A student who needs to go from a 5 to a 7 is a student with a wish.

sections.heading: Year 10 compared with Year 11: when support does what
paragraphs: The same number of sessions, bought twelve months apart, buys entirely different things. This is the comparison with the clearest financial and academic consequences, and most Al Karamah families make their purchase on the wrong side of it.

Support in Year 10 can still influence the tier decision. Schools generally confirm Core or Extended, or Foundation or Higher, in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the evidence of internal assessments, and a student whose algebra was repaired in the autumn of Year 10 presents a different picture by the time that decision is made. Because the lower tier caps the achievable grade, this is not a marginal effect: it can be the difference between a ceiling of around the middle of the scale and access to the full range.

Support in Year 11 works inside whatever tier was set. That is still worth buying, because examination technique, rounding discipline, method-mark habits and specific topic clusters all respond well within a term. What it cannot do is reopen a decision already made or teach content the student never met. The honest version of a February Year 11 plan targets the highest-value accessible topics and the cheapest marks on the paper, and says plainly that full coverage is not available in the time.

There is a third window worth comparing: the summer between Year 11 and Year 12. Four to six sessions aimed at the specific gap between an IGCSE grade and the demands of A Level or IB mathematics cost less and achieve more than a term of catch-up once the new course has started, because the new course does not pause. Families who skip it generally buy the same hours later, under more pressure, at a higher rate.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually sit across the papers
paragraphs: Comparing topics by how much teaching time they receive against how many marks they carry is the fastest way to find a student's cheapest available improvement. The two rarely match, and the mismatch is consistent enough across cohorts to be worth describing.

Number and accuracy receive very little explicit teaching and influence a large share of the marks on both papers, because rounding, significant figures and bounds affect answers in every topic. A single session on carrying full precision and rounding once, at the end, to the accuracy the question specifies, protects marks across the entire paper. Measured against the time it takes, nothing else on the specification comes close.

Statistics receives moderate teaching time and carries a concentrated cluster of marks that are routinely lost: histograms with unequal class widths, cumulative frequency interpretation and averages from grouped data. Geometry compliance is similar. Bearings written to three figures, construction arcs left visible, circle theorem reasons named by name. These are marks for following a convention, and they are the cheapest on the paper to recover.

At the other end sit the topics that absorb teaching time and deliver proportionately fewer marks for a struggling student: vectors, functions and transformations at the upper tier. They matter for the top grades and they are a poor first target for a student in the middle of the range. The sequencing conclusion is uncomfortable but consistent: repair accuracy, compliance and statistics first, and reach for the harder topics once the easy marks are reliably banked.

sections.heading: June compared with November: choosing a series
paragraphs: UAE candidates have two series available in each board, and families rarely compare them deliberately because the school usually decides. Understanding the comparison still matters, because it shapes the revision year and because the resit route depends on it.

For Cambridge, UAE centres sit June and November. The February and March series is offered to India only, and several pages written for UAE parents state otherwise, which is a date a family might act on. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, series run in May/June and November, with provisional timetables published ahead of each. In both cases entry deadlines sit months before the papers and are handled by the school's examinations officer.

The June series is the standard first sitting for most Al Karamah candidates, and November functions chiefly as a resit route. The results tails differ in a way worth planning around. As backward-looking illustrations: June 2026 Edexcel results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November resit therefore produces a result in the following January, which matters if a sixth-form or university application depends on it.

A specific Cambridge caution belongs here. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge's own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. If you are building a revision schedule from a timetable you downloaded yourself, confirm the zone with the examinations officer first. It is a five-minute check against a real and irreversible risk.

sections.heading: What the school provides compared with what one-to-one provides
paragraphs: A fair page has to compare buying support with using what you already have, because many Al Karamah families would be better served by the second. School fees already purchase a substantial amount of what parents go looking for.

A functioning mathematics department delivers the specification, sets and marks assessments, enters candidates, runs mock examinations and usually offers a clinic or departmental help at no additional cost. Across central Abu Dhabi island the teaching in the long-established campuses is generally strong. Buying a tutor to work through the textbook alongside that is paying twice for the same content, and it is only justified where the school's teaching has genuinely broken down, typically after a mid-year staff change.

What a class of twenty-five cannot provide is attention to one student's specific pattern of lost marks. A teacher marking twenty-five Paper 4 scripts can report a cohort trend; they rarely have the time to sit with one student and establish why that student in particular loses accuracy marks in the third line of every long question. That diagnostic conversation is what one-to-one actually sells, and it is worth separating from content coverage in your own mind before you buy anything.

Three questions settle it. What was the last assessment marked against, and which specific marks were lost. Has this class had a consistent teacher this year. Which specification topics remain to be taught this term. A department that answers those readily may have solved your problem for nothing. One that cannot has told you something useful about why your child is also unable to explain the difficulty.

sections.heading: Onward routes compared, from an IGCSE maths grade
paragraphs: The final comparison looks forward. An IGCSE mathematics grade is an input to a decision made a few months later, and Al Karamah families often discover the constraints after the entry has been made rather than before.

A Level Mathematics assumes IGCSE content is automatic and moves quickly from the start. The bridge is largely algebraic: surds, indices, manipulation at speed, and comfort with the pace of a course that does not revisit foundations. A student arriving from Extended or Higher tier with a grade 7 or above generally copes; one arriving from the middle of the range usually needs bridging work in the summer rather than discovering the gap in October.

The IB Diploma splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level. From 0580 Extended into Analysis, the missing pieces are proof, radians and sustained multi-step work, with proof the real conceptual step: IGCSE asks candidates to verify a result, the Diploma asks them to establish one. From 0607 the gap inverts, narrower on technology and wider on manipulation. Into Applications the relevant strength is interpretation of data in writing rather than algebra.

There are also applied and vocational routes where mathematics is embedded rather than examined separately, which suit some students very well and are rarely presented as a legitimate option. The comparison that matters is not which route is most prestigious but which structure a particular student performs in, and that is a judgement best made with a marked script and a frank conversation rather than with a prospectus.
