process.title: Get the code, subject by subject
process.description: Board, syllabus code and tier for mathematics specifically, because schools around Al Karamah sometimes use different boards across subjects. The code identifies the paper; the board name alone does not, and it is what makes a request fillable rather than approximate.

process.title: Establish which scale the grade is on
process.description: Most candidates are awarded 9 to 1, with grade 4 broadly comparable to the former C and grade 7 broadly the former A, while some Cambridge syllabuses still report A* to G. Knowing which prevents a mock result being under-reacted to or over-reacted to.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session at no cost and with no card required, built around past-paper questions rather than a conversation. You leave with a written read sorting lost marks by cause. If the match is wrong we rematch, which costs nothing in week one and a term in week six.

process.title: Target the cheapest marks first
process.description: Accuracy and rounding, geometry compliance and the statistics cluster, before vectors and functions. It is an unglamorous sequence and it is where the available marks actually are for a student in the middle of the range.

process.title: Review at eight sessions, comparing scripts
process.description: Put the first and last marked papers side by side and decide: continue, change focus, change tutor, or finish. Two scripts settle the question in minutes. An exchange of impressions never does, which is why the measure is agreed before the first session.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the code, not the board name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Edexcel 4MA1 are three different examinations with three different revision shapes. An Al Karamah student is matched to a tutor who prepares the specific code, which is the comparison that predicts whether sessions help.

whyPoints.title: The grade scale explained rather than assumed
whyPoints.description: Grade 9 sits above the former A*, 7 is broadly the former A and 4 broadly the former C, with some Cambridge syllabuses still on A* to G. Families who do not know that buy the wrong amount of support, in both directions.

whyPoints.title: Timing advice that costs us sessions
whyPoints.description: Year 10 support can still influence the tier entry; February of Year 11 cannot. We say so plainly even though the later, more expensive intensive is the easier sale, because the earlier purchase is the one that changes the ceiling.

whyPoints.title: Series facts checked against the boards
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit June and November; the February and March series is India-only. Cambridge allocates centres to six timetable zones and warns that the wrong version can cost a candidate an examination. Both statements come from the boards' own guidance.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the price
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not visit UAE homes; home visits are offered only in India. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online, and the gap is a cross-island drive rather than better teaching.

whyPoints.title: We point you back to the school first
whyPoints.description: Specification delivery, marking, mocks and a departmental clinic are already paid for through fees. If the department can answer what the last assessment was marked against, you may not need us at all, and that is a better outcome than a sale.

faqs.question: How do we find out which maths board the school around Al Karamah uses?
faqs.answer: Ask the office for the syllabus code for mathematics specifically, not just the board name. The three common answers in Abu Dhabi are Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, and schools in this part of the island sometimes use different boards for different subjects. The code is on the examination entry confirmation. It identifies the exact paper, which is what determines whether a tutor and a revision guide are the right ones.

faqs.question: What does a grade 5 in IGCSE maths actually mean?
faqs.answer: Roughly the middle of the range, around the former C and B boundary rather than a near-miss on a top grade. On the 9 to 1 scale, 9 sits above the former A*, 7 is broadly comparable to the former A, and 4 is broadly comparable to the former C. Parents who grew up with letters often under-react to a 5 because it looks higher than it is. Some Cambridge syllabuses still report A* to G, so check which scale applies before interpreting anything.

faqs.question: Does support in Year 10 really do something that Year 11 support cannot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the clearest timing comparison in the subject. Schools generally confirm Core or Extended, or Foundation or Higher, in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the evidence of internal assessments, and the lower tier caps the achievable grade. A student whose algebra was repaired in the autumn of Year 10 presents differently by the time that decision is made. Support bought in February of Year 11 works inside a ceiling somebody else has already set.

faqs.question: Which topics give the quickest improvement for a mid-range student?
faqs.answer: Accuracy and rounding first, then geometry compliance, then the statistics cluster. Rounding discipline protects marks across the whole paper and receives almost no explicit teaching. Bearings written to three figures, visible construction arcs and named circle theorem reasons are marks awarded for following a convention. Histograms with unequal class widths and cumulative frequency are a concentrated and reliably lost group. Vectors and functions matter for top grades and are a poor first target mid-range.

faqs.question: Can my son sit the November series instead of June?
faqs.answer: Both are available to UAE candidates in Cambridge and Edexcel, and November functions chiefly as a resit route rather than a first sitting. Note the results tail when planning: as previously observed, June 2026 Edexcel results reached students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. If a sixth-form or university application depends on the grade, a November resit produces it in the following January. Entry deadlines sit months earlier and the school's examinations officer holds them.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE maths sitting in the spring we could use?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge offers its February and March series to India only, so UAE candidates sit June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Several tutoring pages written for UAE parents state this incorrectly, which matters because an entry deadline is something a family plans around. Always confirm against the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than any restated date, including a date on this page.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone timetable warning, and does it affect us?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs between them. Cambridge's own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. Your school manages this in practice. If you are building a revision schedule from a timetable you downloaded yourself, confirm the zone with the examinations officer. Five minutes against an irreversible risk.

faqs.question: Our daughter came from a CBSE school. What will she find hardest in IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: The format rather than the mathematics. CBSE Class 10 builds strong procedural technique in algebra, trigonometry and coordinate geometry, and that transfers well. What does not transfer is IGCSE's reliance on multi-step contextual problems and on command-word precision, where show that, explain and calculate each require something specific. A student can know the content and lose marks consistently on presentation. A marked past paper makes the gap visible in one session.

faqs.question: How does IGCSE maths compare with the American curriculum our other child follows?
faqs.answer: The assessment structure differs more than the content does. American-curriculum mathematics in Years 10 and 11 is typically organised into courses such as Algebra II or Pre-Calculus, with grades accumulating across the year from quizzes, tests and projects. IGCSE concentrates almost everything into a terminal series of two papers. A student used to continuous assessment finds the examination skills unfamiliar: pacing, revising months of content and performing on a single day are genuinely different competencies.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for maths when the school's department is good?
faqs.answer: Only for what the department cannot give. A functioning department delivers the specification, marks assessments, runs mocks and usually offers a free clinic, all already covered by fees. What a class of twenty-five cannot do is work out why your child specifically loses accuracy marks in the third line of every long question. Buy the diagnosis and the technique work. Buying a tutor to repeat the textbook is paying twice for the same content.

faqs.question: How much bridging work is there between IGCSE maths and A Level?
faqs.answer: Usually four to six sessions over the summer, aimed at surds, indices, manipulation at speed and the pace of a course that does not revisit foundations. A student arriving from Extended or Higher tier with a grade 7 or above generally copes without help. One arriving from the middle of the range tends to need it, and buying it in July costs less and achieves more than discovering the gap in October while the new course is already moving.

faqs.question: Does living in Al Karamah rather than Al Mushrif change anything?
faqs.answer: Two small things and one large non-thing. Al Mushrif is more villa-heavy, so a study and a quiet hour are more likely; Al Karamah mixes villas with apartment blocks where the hour needs arranging. In-home quotes differ, because they track the tutor's address rather than yours. What does not change is the thing that decides the grade, which is whether the tutor prepares your child's exact syllabus code and tier.

faqs.question: Should we start with two subjects or one?
faqs.answer: One, almost always, and chosen from a marked paper rather than from which subject your child dislikes most. Mathematics tends to be the right first choice because its losses are process rather than knowledge, which makes them fast to repair. Two weekly sessions plus school homework plus mandatory subjects leaves little consolidation time, and consolidation is where learning settles. Add a second subject later if the evidence genuinely calls for it.

faqs.question: What are we entitled to see at the end of the very first lesson?

intro.heading: "Does anyone near us actually know this paper?" — the real answer
paragraphs: This is the question behind almost every IGCSE maths enquiry from Abu Dhabi island, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Somewhere within a short drive of Al Khalidiyah there is certainly a competent mathematician. Whether that person knows that Cambridge 0580 Extended is examined through a 35 per cent short-answer paper and a 65 per cent structured paper, or that Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher is two papers of two hours weighted equally, or that Cambridge 0607 expects a graphics calculator and an investigation, is a completely separate question. Proximity tells you nothing about it.

The distinction is not pedantry. The three codes demand different revision shapes. A paper worth 65 per cent of the grade rewards stamina across long multi-step questions, so revision has to include full-length practice rather than topic drills. Two equally weighted papers reward even coverage of the whole syllabus. An investigation paper rewards exploration and clear reasoning rather than a single right answer. A tutor who treats all of this as "IGCSE maths" will teach good mathematics and still leave your child unprepared for the specific paper in front of them.

The second thing worth knowing is that most lost marks in IGCSE mathematics are not caused by missing knowledge. They are caused by process. Working not shown on a multi-step question where method marks are awarded separately from the answer. Premature rounding that destroys every accuracy mark later in a chain. Eleven minutes spent on a four-mark question. A bearing measured but not stated as a three-figure bearing. These are diagnosable in one marked script and fixable in a defined number of sessions, which is why the first useful session involves a past paper rather than a plan.

So the search is answerable, just not by geography. Ask the school for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for mathematics specifically, because schools in the emirate sometimes use different boards for different subjects. Then ask any prospective tutor to name the papers and weightings under that code without looking them up. The answer takes four seconds and tells you more than a page of credentials.

On delivery, we are explicit rather than coy. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every session for an Al Khalidiyah family runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen, which suits mathematics particularly well because both people see the same working at the same size and the annotated question survives the lesson. It also means the tutor is chosen from everyone who prepares that code rather than from everyone willing to cross the island at six on a Tuesday.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-khalid.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics is usually taught as a list of topics and examined as a set of skills. The entries below are the areas Al Khalidiyah families most often ask about, described by what the examination actually demands rather than by chapter heading.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and simplifying, including algebraic fractions at the upper tiers. The usual loss is a sign error carried through four lines of otherwise correct work. Fluency here determines whether a student can attempt the longer questions at all.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous systems
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic solving, including the formula and completing the square at Extended. Marks go missing when a quadratic is solved correctly and only one root is stated, or when an inequality is solved but the direction is not reversed on multiplication by a negative.

subjects.name: Geometry, bearings and loci
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems at the upper tier, constructions, loci and bearings. Bearings must be stated as three figures, and constructions must show the arcs. Both are marks awarded for compliance rather than insight, which makes them the cheapest marks on the paper to recover.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, then sine and cosine rules and area of a triangle at the upper tier, including three-dimensional problems. The recurring failure is choosing the wrong rule because the diagram was not labelled before any calculation started.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound shapes
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Area, surface area and volume, including spheres, cones and frustums at Extended. Unit errors dominate: a volume given in square centimetres loses the mark however correct the arithmetic. Compound shapes reward a clearly annotated sketch.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals, and tree diagrams. Histograms with unequal class widths are among the most reliably lost marks in the whole syllabus, because frequency density is skipped under time pressure.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Sketching quadratics, reciprocals and exponentials, function notation, inverse and composite functions, and graph transformations. Students who can plot cannot always sketch, and sketching from properties rather than from a table of values is the skill being assessed.

subjects.name: Vectors and matrices
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry in a plane, and matrix operations where the specification includes them. Vector proof questions reward writing a route in terms of given vectors, and lose marks when a student jumps to a conclusion without stating the path taken.

subjects.name: Numerical accuracy and bounds
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Significant figures, decimal places, upper and lower bounds and the effect of rounding in a chain of calculation. Premature rounding is the single most expensive habit in IGCSE mathematics, because it quietly removes accuracy marks from questions the student answered correctly.

subjects.name: Investigation and modelling, 0607 only
subjects.description: The component that distinguishes Cambridge International Mathematics. It rewards exploring a situation, noticing structure and explaining reasoning, rather than producing one final answer. Students arriving from 0580 find it unfamiliar and need practice specifically on open-ended work.

sections.heading: Three maths codes, three different examinations
paragraphs: The first job in any IGCSE maths search from Al Khalidiyah is establishing which examination your child is actually entered for. There are three common answers in Abu Dhabi, and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge 0580 is the standard IGCSE Mathematics course. Cambridge 0607 is International Mathematics, built around a graphics calculator and including an investigation component, and widely used by schools that feed into the IB Diploma. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 is Mathematics A, tiered Foundation and Higher.

Each has its own architecture. In 0580 at Extended tier, Paper 2 carries 35 per cent and Paper 4 carries 65. That weighting shapes everything: a student who has only practised short questions is unprepared for the paper that decides two-thirds of the grade. In 4MA1 Higher, two papers of two hours are weighted equally, so even coverage matters more than stamina on a single long paper. In 0607, calculator technique and open-ended investigation are assessed in ways 0580 never tests.

Revision material follows the code, not the subject. A workbook bought for 0580 contains question styles that do not appear in 4MA1, and 0607 past papers assume a calculator a 0580 student may not own. Families regularly spend money on the wrong material because the shop assistant, or the website, treats IGCSE maths as one thing. Checking the code before buying anything is a five-minute step that saves real money.

A tutor should be able to recite the paper structure for your child's code immediately. Not approximately, and not after looking it up. That single question filters more effectively than any list of degrees, because paper structure is the thing a tutor who has prepared candidates simply knows.

sections.heading: Where 0580 Extended marks are actually lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: A grade is the sum of specific marks lost in specific places. Across Al Khalidiyah enquiries the same places recur, and naming them is what turns revision into repair. Almost none of them is about mathematical ability. Most are about a habit that was never corrected.

The largest cluster sits in numerical accuracy. A student rounds an intermediate value to two decimal places, carries it forward, and the final answer falls outside the accepted range. Every accuracy mark in that chain is gone, even though the method was right. The correction is mechanical: carry full calculator precision and round only at the end, stating the degree of accuracy asked for. It takes one session to teach and a fortnight to make automatic.

The second cluster is statistics, specifically histograms with unequal class widths and cumulative frequency interpretation. Frequency density gets skipped under time pressure, and a correct-looking bar chart scores nothing. The third is geometry compliance: bearings not written as three figures, construction arcs erased, circle theorem reasons not named. These are marks awarded for following a convention, which makes them the cheapest on the paper to recover and the most irritating to lose.

The fourth is the structure of Paper 4 itself. At 65 per cent of the grade, it is a long paper with multi-step questions that build. Students who have practised only topic exercises run out of stamina around question eight and leave marks on the page. The fix is full-length timed papers, marked to the official scheme, with time per question tracked. That is not glamorous work and it moves grades more reliably than new content does.

sections.heading: Revising for a paper worth 65 per cent of the grade
paragraphs: Weighting should change revision and almost never does. When one paper decides roughly two-thirds of the result, practising it in full is not optional. Yet most Year 11 revision in Al Khalidiyah consists of topic exercises, because topic exercises are what textbooks and revision apps supply and because they feel productive. They build knowledge and they do not build the thing Paper 4 tests, which is sustained accurate work across a long paper under time pressure.

The contrast with 4MA1 is instructive. Two equally weighted two-hour papers mean no single sitting dominates, so even syllabus coverage matters more and stamina matters slightly less. A 4MA1 student who has neglected one topic area pays for it twice. A 0580 Extended student who has neglected long-paper practice pays for it once, heavily, in the paper that counts most.

What works is uncomfortable and simple. Sit the full paper, timed, without notes. Mark it against the published mark scheme rather than impressionistically, because the mark scheme is where method marks are visible. Log every lost mark by cause, not by topic: rounding, misread question, time, missing method, genuine gap. Then teach to the causes. A log of causes usually shows that two or three habits account for most of the loss, which is a far more tractable problem than a list of weak topics.

Repeat the whole cycle rather than a single paper. Two timed papers eight weeks apart, both marked properly, give a parent something no impression can: evidence of whether the plan worked. If the second script has not moved, either the diagnosis or the match was wrong, and both are fixable before the series.

sections.heading: Command words, and why a right answer sometimes scores nothing
paragraphs: Mathematics parents assume command words are an English problem. They are not. An IGCSE maths paper distinguishes between show that, prove, find, calculate, work out, explain and justify, and the distinction decides whether a correct number earns the marks attached to it. Show that requires the stated result to be reached visibly, so a student who confirms it on a calculator without the steps scores nothing. Explain requires a reason in words, and a numerical answer alone does not satisfy it.

Method marks are the other half of the same issue. On a multi-step question the mark scheme typically awards marks for identifying the correct approach and separately for the accurate result. A student who does the whole thing mentally and writes one number can lose two of three marks while being entirely correct. This is the most common source of unnecessary loss in the subject, and the correction is a habit rather than knowledge: write the method even when it feels obvious.

Units, accuracy statements and context sentences sit in the same category. A volume answered in the wrong unit, an answer given to two decimal places when three significant figures were asked for, a probability left as an unsimplified fraction where the question specified a decimal. Each is a mark awarded for compliance with instructions, and each is lost by students who are perfectly competent mathematically.

The practical approach is to mark a student's own script with them, question by question, separating genuine mathematical gaps from compliance losses. Most Al Khalidiyah families are surprised by the ratio. On a typical first diagnostic, compliance and process account for a substantial share of the lost marks, and that share is recoverable within weeks rather than terms.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in the researched Abu Dhabi cluster omits this, and it is a real part of an Al Khalidiyah student's week. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why a Year 10 student sitting Cambridge or Edexcel examinations also carries mandatory subjects that do not appear on the IGCSE timetable at all.

Dubai's regulator has published the clearest public detail on how this works in practice, and it is useful as an illustration even for an Abu Dhabi family, with the caveat that Abu Dhabi provision sits with ADEK. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. It requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

The language rules are specific too. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

Two practical consequences. First, the mandatory subjects consume timetable space, which is part of why a Year 11 week feels fuller than the IGCSE subject count suggests, and that affects when a maths session can realistically sit. Second, for mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so support in those subjects is constrained in a way that maths support is not. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate regulator approval to teach them.

sections.heading: The permit question, and five ways to test a maths tutor by message
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a parent in Al Khalidiyah is entitled to ask about it directly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted to you with scepticism.

What the permit does not do is tell you whether someone can prepare a candidate for 0580 Extended. It is a right-to-work instrument, not a statement about teaching quality, and conflating the two is a mistake several tutoring sites encourage. Ask about the permit, then ask the questions that actually test competence.

The best of those questions concern paper structure and marking. Ask which code they prepare and what its papers are worth. Ask what they would do in the first session, where the right answer involves a marked diagnostic rather than a term plan. Ask how they mark: against the published scheme, or by impression. Ask what they would tell you if the plan was not working at week eight, because a tutor who has no answer to that has never had the conversation.

One Abu Dhabi-specific caution. Press reporting indicates ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct with a similar restriction. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, and do not pursue your child's own class teacher as a private tutor. An independent tutor also gives you an unconflicted second reading of how your child is doing.

sections.heading: From IGCSE maths into the Diploma or A Level: the gap nobody maps
paragraphs: The IGCSE maths grade is not the end of the decision. It determines which post-16 mathematics is realistically open, and the transition is steeper than most Al Khalidiyah families expect. One competitor page in the researched set has a single heading on the IGCSE-to-IB gap; nobody has a structured subject-by-subject version. The gap is real and it is specific.

From 0580 Extended into IB Analysis and Approaches, the missing pieces are usually algebraic stamina, radians, and the habit of proving rather than verifying. The Diploma's non-calculator Paper 1 at Standard Level, and its proof demands at Higher Level, assume manipulation fluency that an Extended grade 7 does not by itself evidence. From 0607 into Analysis and Approaches the gap is narrower on calculator technique and wider on algebra, because 0607 leans on technology.

Into Applications and Interpretation the picture inverts. Statistics, modelling and interpretation carry the course, so a 0580 student with solid data handling arrives better placed than one with strong algebra and weak interpretation. Into A Level Mathematics the bridge is largely algebraic: surds, indices, partial fractions where required, and the pace of a course that assumes IGCSE content is automatic.

The practical advice is to do the bridging work in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 rather than in the first term of the new course. Four to six sessions in July, aimed at the specific gap, cost less and achieve more than a term of DP1 catch-up, because the new course does not wait. Families who skip it generally buy the same hours later at a higher rate under more pressure.

sections.heading: What a short block of maths support can and cannot do before the series
paragraphs: Families in Al Khalidiyah often make contact with eight or ten weeks left and want to know whether it is worth starting. It usually is, provided the plan is honest about scope. Eight weeks at one session a week is eight to twelve hours of teaching, and that quantity has a clear ceiling and a clear floor.

Inside that window, three things are reliably achievable. One diagnosed content gap can be closed and re-tested, which for IGCSE mathematics is often a cluster like histograms or circle theorems rather than a whole topic. Examination technique can be rebuilt: rounding discipline, method-mark habits, question selection and pacing across a long paper. And compliance losses can be largely eliminated, which on a first diagnostic frequently account for a meaningful share of the marks missing.

What eight weeks cannot do is cover two years of content that was never taught, and no tutor should imply otherwise. If a Year 11 student has not met circle theorems, functions or vectors at all, the honest plan targets the highest-value accessible topics and the paper where marks are cheapest, and says plainly that full coverage is not available in the time. That is a more useful conversation than an optimistic one, because it lets a family decide between a maths block and a different priority.

The structure that makes this work is a measure agreed at the start. A timed paper in week one, the same style of paper at week eight, both marked against the published scheme, with an error log in between so no mistake is taught twice. If the second script has not improved, the plan or the match was wrong, and that is our problem rather than the student's.

faqs.question: How do I find out which maths code my child in Al Khalidiyah is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for mathematics specifically. It is on the examination entry confirmation and takes one email to confirm. The three common answers in Abu Dhabi are Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1. Do not assume the answer for maths matches the answer for science, because schools sometimes use different boards across subjects. Any tutor worth hiring will ask for this before the first session anyway.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0607 just a different name for 0580?
faqs.answer: No. 0607 is International Mathematics, built around a graphics calculator and including an investigation component, and it is widely used by schools feeding into the IB Diploma. 0580 is the standard IGCSE Mathematics course. Much of the content overlaps, but the assessment does not: 0607 tests open-ended exploration and reasoning in a way 0580 never does. Revision material bought for the wrong code is money wasted, so check the number on the entry confirmation before buying a single workbook.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 4 matter so much more than Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Because at Cambridge 0580 Extended it carries 65 per cent of the grade against Paper 2's 35. That weighting should change how a student revises and usually does not. Paper 4 is a long paper with multi-step questions that build, so it tests sustained accurate work under time pressure. Topic exercises build knowledge and do not build that. Full-length timed papers, marked against the published scheme with time per question tracked, are the only practice that addresses it directly.

faqs.question: My son gets the right answers and still loses marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly method marks and compliance. On a multi-step question the mark scheme awards marks for the correct approach separately from the accurate result, so a student who works it out mentally and writes one number can lose two of three marks while being entirely right. Add premature rounding, answers in the wrong unit, accuracy instructions ignored and bearings not written as three figures, and the total is substantial. All of it is habit rather than knowledge, and habit is fixable in weeks.

faqs.question: Does distance from Al Khalidiyah matter at all for a maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Only if you insist on someone physically present, and then it limits you to whoever is free and willing to cross the island that evening, with subject match becoming whatever is left. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. Our sessions run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, which for working through a past-paper question line by line is arguably clearer than two people sharing one printed page.

faqs.question: What does "show that" actually require in an IGCSE maths answer?
faqs.answer: Visible steps leading to the stated result. A student who confirms the result on a calculator without demonstrating the working scores nothing, however correct the result is. It is one of several command words that change what an answer must contain: prove needs a general argument, explain and justify need words rather than another calculation, and calculate expects the arithmetic shown. Marking a student's own script against the published scheme is the fastest way to see which of these is costing them.

faqs.question: Can my daughter resit IGCSE maths in February if June goes badly?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge offers its February and March series to India only, so UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. A resit after a summer sitting therefore points at November. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and your school's examinations officer holds the dates. Check the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than relying on a date restated by any tutoring website, including this one.

faqs.question: Do mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect when we can book maths?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, yes. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, which fills the timetable more than the IGCSE subject count suggests. A Year 11 week is therefore fuller than parents expect, and homework volume follows. In practice this pushes the workable maths slot later in the evening, which is also when most students produce better scripts, so the constraint is less damaging than it sounds.

faqs.question: How much bridging work is needed between IGCSE maths and the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: From 0580 Extended into Analysis and Approaches, usually four to six focused sessions over the summer, aimed at algebraic stamina, radians and non-calculator fluency. Higher Level needs more, because proof habits take longer to build than technique. From 0607 the gap is narrower on calculator work and wider on manipulation. Doing it in July costs less and achieves more than a term of DP1 catch-up, because the new course does not pause while a student consolidates.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting maths support with ten weeks left before the papers?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with an honest scope. Ten weeks at one session a week is around ten to fifteen hours, enough to close a diagnosed topic cluster, rebuild rounding and method-mark discipline, and remove compliance losses that often account for a meaningful share of missing marks. It is not enough to teach content never covered. We would sit a timed paper first so the block targets what the script actually shows rather than what anyone assumes.

faqs.question: Should we buy a group revision course instead of one-to-one maths?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the gap is broad or narrow. A group course is genuinely good value for general revision across a whole cohort shortly before a series. It is poor value when a student's problem is one cluster, such as histograms with unequal class widths, because a shared pace gives that topic a few minutes of an hour. Diagnose first with a marked paper, then choose the instrument. Buying the cheaper option for the wrong problem is not a saving.

faqs.question: Does the MoHRE permit tell us anything about teaching quality?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth being clear about that. The private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and establishes that a person may lawfully offer private lessons in the UAE. It says nothing about whether they can prepare a candidate for 0580 Extended Paper 4. Ask about the permit, then ask which code they prepare and what each paper is worth. The second question is the one that tests competence.

faqs.question: Our school says Core is right and we disagree. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Get evidence rather than have an argument. Ask for questions from both tiers to be set and marked against the published scheme, which can be done in two or three sessions, and take the marked scripts to the school. A student who handles Extended-style algebra but collapses on long structured questions has a stamina problem, which is fixable. A student who cannot access the Extended material at all is correctly placed. The entry decision belongs to the school either way.

faqs.question: What should the first session with a new maths tutor actually look like?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic, not a lecture. Past-paper questions attempted under something close to examination conditions, then marked against the published scheme in front of the student, with lost marks sorted by cause: rounding, misread question, missing method, timing, genuine gap. By the end you should have a short written list of causes rather than a list of weak topics. A tutor who arrives with a term plan has decided what your child needs before meeting them.

intro.heading: Knowing maths and knowing your child's maths specification are different things
paragraphs: Al Manaseer is not short of people who can do IGCSE maths. It sits in the middle of a dense, well-educated part of Abu Dhabi island, between Al Khalidiyah and Al Bateen, full of engineers, accountants, former teachers and graduate students who could solve every question on a Year 11 paper. The scarcity is not mathematical competence. It is knowledge of the specific assessment your child is sitting, and those two things are routinely confused by everybody involved in the transaction.

Here is the distinction in practice. A capable graduate can teach a student to factorise a quadratic. Only somebody who knows the specification can tell you that the Cambridge Extended tier sets a non-calculator paper worth half the grade, that most school practice happens with a calculator and that your child is therefore almost certainly weaker than their report suggests in exactly the half of the assessment nobody is rehearsing. The first person improves a skill. The second person changes a grade.

The same gap shows up everywhere. Which paper permits a calculator. Whether the tier caps the grade at C, at 5, at A star or at 9. Why area scale factors are squared and volume scale factors cubed, and why that single misunderstanding costs a whole question. What a mark scheme pays for when a student writes nothing down. Where the boundary sits between the Core and Extended content lists. A generalist will answer all of these plausibly and some of them wrongly, and a parent has no way of telling which is which without asking better questions. Each of those is a fact about the assessment rather than an opinion about teaching, which is what makes the gap testable in a short conversation.

So this page is mostly a set of questions. Ask them of any tutor, local or otherwise, and listen for precision rather than warmth. Then there is the honest second half: what IB Gram can actually cover at an Al Manaseer evening hour, and what it cannot. None of the competitor pages researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which makes their implied availability worth exactly nothing to a parent planning a year. Implied availability is cheap to publish and expensive to rely on.

On delivery, so it is clear from the start: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Al Manaseer lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That is also what makes specification-level matching possible, because the question stops being who knows 0580 and lives near Al Khalidiyah and becomes simply who knows 0580. Removing distance from the filter does not remove anything a parent values; it removes the one condition that has no bearing on the grade.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-manase.subjectsIntro: These are the specific areas where specification knowledge, rather than general mathematical ability, decides whether an hour of tutoring is worth anything.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Extended, the non-calculator paper
subjects.description: Half the Extended grade, sat by hand. Fractions, standard form, surds and index laws performed at speed without technology. School practice rarely rehearses it, so most students are weaker here than their report implies. A tutor who does not know this paper exists cannot plan around it.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Extended, the calculator paper
subjects.description: The other half, with longer multi-step questions carrying the heavier algebra, trigonometry, vectors and probability. The dominant loss is method marks on questions the student can answer, because nothing was written down. Training here is about writing, not knowing.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0580 Core
subjects.description: Graded C to G, with a narrower content list than Extended and its own pair of papers. Teaching a Core student from Extended material wastes their time on content they will never be assessed on, which happens whenever a tutor does not check the tier.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher
subjects.description: Grades 9 to 4 across two equally weighted papers with a calculator permitted on both. Expects confident algebraic manipulation, functions, graph transformations and vectors. Cambridge-trained tutors sometimes misjudge the balance here because the calculator rule changes what the papers test.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation
subjects.description: Grades 5 to 1, with a content list that overlaps Higher but stops short of its harder algebra and trigonometry. Knowing where that line falls is specification knowledge, and teaching past it is a common and expensive waste of a Foundation student's limited hours.

subjects.name: Similar shapes and scale factors
subjects.description: Area scales by the square of the linear factor and volume by the cube. A student applying the linear factor loses an entire question, and it is the single most predictable Extended-tier error. Fixable in one session by anyone who knows to look for it.

subjects.name: Trigonometry rule selection
subjects.description: Sine rule, cosine rule, area formula, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Mark loss comes from choosing the wrong rule rather than applying one badly, so useful practice is rapid identification under timing rather than repeated worked examples.

subjects.name: Algebraic fractions and quadratics
subjects.description: Completing the square, the quadratic formula, simultaneous equations with one non-linear, and algebraic fraction manipulation. Insecurity here leaks into topics that look unrelated, including mensuration and probability, which is why a diagnosis has to start with algebra.

subjects.name: Probability trees and set notation
subjects.description: The arithmetic is easy and the structure is not. Trees are usually drawn correctly then read along the wrong branch. Set and Venn notation differs in emphasis between the two boards, which is another place a tutor on the wrong specification gives sound but misdirected teaching.

subjects.name: Whole-paper timing in Year 11
subjects.description: Papers sat under exam conditions against the right specification's structure, then dissected against what that board's mark scheme rewards. Practising Cambridge timing for an Edexcel paper, or the reverse, teaches a pacing habit that does not transfer.

sections.heading: The questions that separate a maths graduate from a specification teacher
paragraphs: Ask these before you hire anybody, local or otherwise. They take about ten minutes and they are answerable precisely or not at all, which is the whole point. A tutor who knows the specification answers in specifics within a sentence. A tutor who does not answers in general terms about experience, confidence and rapport, and a parent who is listening for the difference can hear it immediately.

The questions are not difficult or hostile. Which specification does my child sit, and what is its code? Which of their papers permits a calculator? What does the tier they are entered for cap the grade at? Where do students on this specification most commonly lose marks, by topic? What would you want to see before the first session? None of these requires the tutor to have met your child. All of them require them to have taught the course.

The table below sets out what a precise answer sounds like next to a vague one. It is worth doing this even with a recommendation from a trusted neighbour, because informal hiring in dense Abu Dhabi districts runs on reputation rather than on specification, and reputation is usually built on a different child sitting a different paper. A tutor who was excellent for a Foundation-tier student two years ago may be the wrong person entirely for an Extended-tier candidate now. Ask them in that order, too. The specification question first, because every other answer depends on it, and the question about what the tutor wants to see last, because it reveals whether the first session will be diagnosis or small talk.

sections.heading: Why 0580 and 4MA1 are not interchangeable
paragraphs: The two specifications cover similar mathematics and assess it differently, and the difference is large enough to change a grade. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended, with Core graded C to G and Extended reaching A star. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, splits into Foundation at grades 5 to 1 and Higher at grades 9 to 4.

The structural difference that matters most is the calculator. On the Cambridge route each tier sets one paper without a calculator and one with, so half the grade depends on by-hand fluency. On the Edexcel route a calculator is permitted on both papers. A tutor who trained on Edexcel and is teaching a Cambridge Extended student will often under-rehearse non-calculator work simply because it was never half of anything in their experience, and the student's report will not flag it because school assessments usually mirror the school's own habits rather than the exam's.

There are smaller differences too: content boundaries between tiers, emphasis in set notation and vectors, question phrasing, and the pacing a mark scheme implies. None is dramatic in isolation. Together they mean that past papers from the wrong board build the wrong instincts about how long a six-mark question should take and what the examiner expects written down. The fix is trivial once anybody checks: look at a past paper the school issued, read the code on the front, and tell the tutor.

sections.heading: What we can cover at an Al Manaseer evening hour, and what we cannot
paragraphs: Every provider in this market implies unlimited availability and none of the pages researched for this project states a coverage limit. That makes their implied availability useless for planning. Here is the honest version for IGCSE maths specifically, which is one of the better-covered requests in the UAE.

IGCSE maths at Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher on both specifications is comfortably covered at Abu Dhabi evening hours, including the 6pm to 8pm window Al Manaseer households actually need. Non-calculator technique, whole-paper work and tier diagnostics are all straightforward to staff. Where it gets tighter is the narrow end: a particular tutor requested by name, a slot after 8.30pm, a weekend morning in the fortnight after mocks when every family in the emirate wants one, and Year 11 starts requested in April.

When a request cannot be met well there are three honest answers and you get whichever applies. A waiting time with a date attached. A named tutor who covers the specification solidly but is not the deepest specialist, with that limitation spelt out. sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, paper by paper
paragraphs: Mark loss in IGCSE maths is unusually predictable, which is exactly why specification knowledge pays. A tutor who has taught the course knows the error list before meeting the student and can test for each item in the first hour. A generalist discovers them one at a time over a term, at the family's expense.

The list is short. Unshown working is the largest single cause: on a multi-step question most marks are method marks, so a correct answer with no visible route scores less than a wrong answer with a clear one. Then premature rounding, which turns a correct method into a wrong answer. Then scale factors in similar shapes, where area is squared and volume cubed and students apply the linear factor. Then trigonometric rule selection. Then probability trees read along the wrong branch. Then non-calculator arithmetic that is secure with technology and absent without.

What makes this useful rather than merely interesting is that each item is diagnosable from a marked script in about fifteen minutes, and each is fixable in one to three sessions. A tutor who asks to see the last mock before the first session is planning to do that. A tutor who says send me nothing and we will see how it goes is planning to spend your first four sessions discovering what the script would have told them on day one. The useful consequence is that an IGCSE maths diagnosis is a short job rather than a long one. Anybody who needs a month to tell you what is wrong has not read the script.

sections.heading: What a tutor cannot know, and should ask the school
paragraphs: Specification knowledge has limits, and an honest tutor names them rather than guessing. Several of the facts that most affect a Year 11 maths plan are held only by the school, and a tutor who claims to know them without asking is making things up.

The school holds the entry tier and whether it can still be changed. The school holds the exams officer's knowledge of which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in, which matters because Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. The school holds its own assessment calendar, its mock dates, and the order it is teaching topics in. The school also holds whether a student is on a reduced subject load or has access arrangements.

So the first week of any sensible arrangement involves three questions sent to the school, not to the tutor: which specification and tier is my child entered for, when are the mocks, and in what order is the department teaching the remaining topics? Those three answers let a tutor build a plan that fits rather than one that competes. It is also a short email, and the number of families who never send it is the reason so many tutoring plans end up teaching a topic the week after the school assessed it. A tutor who says I will ask the school rather than guessing is demonstrating something useful about how the rest of the arrangement will run.

sections.heading: Permits, approved tutors, and which claims are verifiable
paragraphs: A search in a dense Abu Dhabi district surfaces agencies, platforms, centres and individuals advertising through building groups, and they are not all on the same legal footing. The rules are specific and checkable, which is more than can be said for most of the credentials advertised alongside them.

An individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts are unverified.

What no permit does is certify teaching quality. No UAE regulator approves individual private tutors on merit, so the phrase approved tutors, however it is dressed, should be read as marketing. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing with a renewal cycle and is also not an endorsement of anyone's teaching. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence, and no school named on this page is a client or a partner.

sections.heading: Why the IGCSE maths grade matters after Year 11
paragraphs: A maths grade at sixteen is read by more people than a family expects, and that is an argument for getting the tier and the specification right rather than for anxiety. Three audiences use it, and they use it differently.

Sixth forms and IB campuses use it as an entry gate. A-Level Mathematics commonly expects a grade 7 or A; the sciences and economics usually expect a strong maths grade too; IB Analysis and Approaches assumes Extended-level algebra from the first week. A Core or Foundation entry closes these regardless of how well the student performed within that tier, which is why the entry decision in Year 10 is a conversation about options rather than about this year's report.

The Ministry of Education uses it differently again. On the British track, equivalency requires a pass in five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page in this market states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which contradicts the published rule. Equivalency is the Ministry's process, not a school's or a tutor's, so confirm current requirements on moe.gov.ae before planning around them. Neither audience reads the tier, only the grade, which is precisely why the tier decision deserves attention while it is still open.

sections.heading: The fortnight after mocks, and why it is the best hour you will buy
paragraphs: If an Al Manaseer family buys only one session all year, it should be one session per weak subject in the two weeks after mocks, with the marked script on the screen. The reason is not sentiment. It is that a mock script is the only honest, specific, personal diagnostic available before the real series, and its value decays quickly.

Within a fortnight the student still remembers what they were thinking at question seventeen, and can recognise an error as their own rather than as an abstract possibility. A tutor who knows the specification can turn that script into a list: method not shown here, rounded too early there, cosine rule where the sine rule was signalled, ran out of time with two questions untouched. Each of those is fixable, and several of them are fixable in one session.

Six weeks later the paper is cold, the student has forgotten their reasoning and the conversation becomes general. The difficulty is that the school holidays usually fall inside exactly that fortnight, which is why the booking has to be made in November for December rather than discovered in January. It is also the single busiest request in the Abu Dhabi tutoring calendar, so a family that plans it early gets a specialist and a family that improvises gets whoever is left. One further argument for it: the session costs the same in December as in March and is worth several times more, which is unusual enough in this market to be worth acting on.

faqs.question: Is there anyone near Al Manaseer who actually knows my child's maths specification?
faqs.answer: There is no shortage of mathematical ability in this part of Abu Dhabi island, and a genuine shortage of people who have taught a specific IGCSE specification to a cohort. Those are different things. A capable graduate can teach factorising; only someone who knows the syllabus will tell you that Cambridge Extended sets a non-calculator paper worth half the grade and that your child has barely rehearsed it. The practical answer is to stop filtering by distance, filter by specification and tier instead, and ask the five questions on this page before hiring anybody.

faqs.question: What should I ask a maths tutor before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Five things, and they take ten minutes. Which specification does my child sit, with the code? Which of their papers permits a calculator? What does their entry tier cap the grade at? Where do students on this specification most commonly lose marks, by topic? And what do you want to see before the first session? A tutor who has taught the course answers each in a sentence. One who has not answers in general terms about experience and confidence, which is a different and much less useful kind of answer.

faqs.question: Does it genuinely matter whether a tutor trained on Cambridge or on Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Yes, mainly because of the calculator. Cambridge 0580 sets one paper per tier without a calculator, so half that grade rests on by-hand fluency. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers. A tutor whose experience is entirely Edexcel will often under-rehearse non-calculator work for a Cambridge student, not through carelessness but because it was never half of anything in their experience. Content boundaries between tiers, set notation emphasis and paper pacing differ too, and past papers from the wrong board build the wrong timing instincts.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our apartment in Al Manaseer?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Other Abu Dhabi providers do offer it, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure absorbs the journey. Al Manaseer lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and that is also what makes specification-level matching possible, because the pool stops being limited to people who live within a drive.

faqs.question: How do I find out which specification and tier my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Two routes, both quick. Look at the front of any past paper the school has issued, where the code is printed, or email the head of maths and ask for the specification code and the tier in writing. While you are sending that email, ask two more things: when the mocks are, and in what order the department is teaching the remaining topics. Those three answers are what let a tutor build a plan that fits the school rather than one that competes with it, and very few families ever ask for them.

faqs.question: Can you tell me whether my child's entry tier can still be changed?
faqs.answer: No, and any tutor who claims to know is guessing. The entry tier is held by the school and submitted by its exams officer to the board's deadline, months before the papers. Once submitted it is fixed for that series. Before that point a department will usually consider evidence, which is why a written diagnostic report from a specialist carries more weight in that conversation than a parent's impression does. The question to put to the school is what the current tier caps the grade at and what that closes after Year 11.

faqs.question: What are the most predictable ways IGCSE maths marks are lost?
faqs.answer: Unshown working leads by a distance: on a multi-step question most marks are method marks, so a correct answer with no visible route scores less than a wrong answer with a clear one. Then premature rounding, which turns correct method into a wrong answer. Then scale factors, where area scales by the square and volume by the cube and students apply the linear factor. Then choosing between the sine and cosine rules. Then probability trees read along the wrong branch. Each is diagnosable from a marked script in minutes and fixable in one to three sessions.

faqs.question: Why does a tutor want to see a marked paper before starting?
faqs.answer: Because the script contains information no report does. A grade tells you the result; a marked paper shows the mechanism. Where method stopped being written down, where rounding happened too early, which rule was chosen wrongly, whether the last two questions were untouched because time ran out. A specialist reading your child's script can produce a specific, prioritised list in about fifteen minutes. A tutor who asks for nothing in advance will find the same list eventually, over the first four sessions, at your expense.

faqs.question: Are there times of year you cannot cover an IGCSE maths request?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth saying rather than implying otherwise. Both specifications at all four tiers are comfortably covered in the 6pm to 8pm Gulf Standard Time window Al Manaseer households need. It gets tighter for slots after 8.30pm, for weekend mornings in the fortnight after mocks when every family in the emirate wants one, and for Year 11 starts requested in April, which frequently cannot be covered well at all. In each case you get a waiting time with a date, a named alternative with its limits stated, or an honest no.

faqs.question: What does it mean if a provider advertises approved tutors in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Usually nothing verifiable. No UAE regulator approves individual private tutors on teaching merit. MoHRE issues a work permit to an individual, which is a legal clearance granted free of charge for two years rather than a quality judgement. In Dubai, KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to a training institute with premises, which is also not an endorsement of anyone's teaching. For completeness, IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence, and no school named here is a client.

faqs.question: Should I trust a recommendation from a neighbour in our building?
faqs.answer: Trust it as a starting point and then check the specification. Informal hiring in dense Abu Dhabi districts runs on reputation, and reputation is almost always built on a different child sitting a different paper. A tutor who was excellent for a Foundation-tier student two years ago may be the wrong person for an Extended-tier candidate now, and nobody in that chain has done anything wrong. Ask the same five questions you would ask a stranger. A good tutor will not mind, and the answers take ten minutes.

faqs.question: How much of the final grade can realistically change in one term?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter, and nobody honest will promise a figure. What can be said is where the movement usually comes from. Non-calculator fluency on the Cambridge route is a trained motor skill and improves quickly with short, frequent practice. Showing method is a habit that breaks in about three sessions. Scale factors and rule selection are single-session fixes. Those together often move a student who was losing marks on questions they understood. What does not move quickly is a two-year content gap, which is why starting in April is the expensive option.

faqs.question: Does the IGCSE maths grade affect my child's options beyond Year 11?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and in two separate ways. Sixth forms and IB campuses use it as an entry gate: A-Level Mathematics commonly expects a grade 7 or A, and IB Analysis and Approaches assumes Extended-level algebra from the first week, so a Core or Foundation entry closes those routes regardless of how well the student did within the tier. Separately, the Ministry of Education counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 for British-track equivalency, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count.

faqs.answer: Families around Al Manaseer come from campuses in Al Bateen and on the western island and from larger British-curriculum schools further east, including the American Community School of Abu Dhabi, Al Bateen Academy, Cambridge International School Abu Dhabi, The British School Al Khubairat, International Community School Abu Dhabi and Abu Dhabi International School. Those names describe the local school map and nothing more. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any of them, and none of them is a client of ours.

faqs.question: If one session is all we can afford, when should we use it?
faqs.answer: In the two weeks after mocks, with the marked script in front of a tutor who knows the specification. That is the only honest personal diagnostic available before the real series, and its value decays fast: within a fortnight the student still remembers what they were thinking at question seventeen, and six weeks later the paper is cold and the conversation goes general. The complication is that the holidays usually sit inside that fortnight, so the booking has to be made in November rather than improvised in January.

intro.heading: Spend the free options first, then spend money on something narrow
paragraphs: Most pages about IGCSE maths tutoring begin by explaining why you need it. This one begins by listing what you should use before you pay anyone, because on Al Maryah Island the families who get most from tutoring are the ones who arrive at it last rather than first.

The order runs like this. The school's own revision provision, which you are already paying for through fees and which most students use inconsistently or not at all. Then past papers from the correct board, worked under timing and marked honestly against the real mark scheme — this is free, it is the single most diagnostic thing available, and it is skipped more often than anything else. Then a short block of targeted sessions on the two or three topics those papers expose. Only then a weekly one-to-one arrangement, and only if the pattern justifies it.

The reason to run it in that order is that the paid product is narrow and the free products are broad. A tutor's hour is worth a great deal when it is aimed at a named error on a named topic, and very little when it is spent covering the syllabus, which the school is already doing and which a past paper will tell you about for nothing. Families who reverse the order pay specialist rates for homework supervision, which is the commonest waste in this market.

When money does come in, here is what it costs. Published market rates in Abu Dhabi, read in October 2026, put budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 with the journey inside the rate, and a named IGCSE or A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions come out at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the mid range.

The in-home premium deserves naming on this island specifically. Al Maryah Island is roughly half a square kilometre of towers with no school inside it and few resident tutors, so an in-home match travels from the mainland across a bridge at the worst hour of the day. The gap between the online and in-home bands is money paid for driving. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — so for us the gap does not exist.

What follows is the maths-specific detail: which syllabus code your child is actually sitting, what the tier decision costs downstream, the four topics that eat most of the marks, how the calculator and non-calculator papers differ, and the arithmetic of a November resit. Each section is written so you can price a quote against it.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-maryah.programmesIntro: An IGCSE maths fee only buys specificity if the tutor knows which qualification is in front of them. These are the maths routes Abu Dhabi schools enter students for.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge's main IGCSE maths syllabus, code 0580, covering number, algebra, coordinate geometry, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, vectors and transformations, probability and statistics. It is tiered: a Core route with a reduced syllabus and a capped grade range, and an Extended route carrying the full content and the full grade range. The papers include both non-calculator and calculator components.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to a candidate sitting in Abu Dhabi. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns it is essential to use the correct timetable for your zone, stating it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Confirm the current paper pattern for your child's exam year through the school.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Pearson's main international GCSE maths qualification, code 4MA1, tiered as Foundation and Higher. Content overlaps substantially with Cambridge 0580 but the papers, the phrasing of questions and the mark schemes differ, and the calculator policy across the papers is not the same. Pearson also publishes further maths and additional maths qualifications taken by stronger cohorts.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so open the live official timetable rather than trusting a restated date.

programmes.name: Additional and further maths options
programmes.description: Some schools enter stronger students for an additional or further maths qualification alongside the main IGCSE, covering material that overlaps with early AS content: more advanced algebra, series, calculus foundations and trigonometric identities. It is a bridge into A Level or Higher Level maths rather than a separate track.
programmes.countryNote: Tutoring here is usually short and cheap because the student is already secure in the underlying IGCSE content. A handful of sessions on the genuinely new material is better value than a weekly arrangement, and it has the useful side effect of making the sixth-form maths choice easier to evidence when the school is deciding on places.

programmes.name: Where the maths grade leads
programmes.description: The IGCSE maths grade gates the sixth-form maths choice more tightly than any other subject. A Level Mathematics and IB Higher Level maths courses normally require an Extended or Higher tier grade at a decent level, and schools set their own thresholds. A Core or Foundation entry can close those doors before anyone has discussed sixth form.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools Al Maryah Island families use run both A Level and IB Diploma sixth forms, so the Year 11 maths grade is a genuine fork. This is why the tier decision is the highest-value place to put a small amount of tutoring money, and why spending in Year 10 beats spending in Year 11.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-maryah.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of IGCSE maths that absorb tutoring budget, with what each one actually costs in marks. Both boards and both tiers are covered.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. The single largest source of lost marks at Extended and Higher tier, because almost every multi-step question routes through it and an early slip propagates through the whole answer.

subjects.name: Number and non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form, bounds and estimation. Where a non-calculator paper is sat, this is where marks are quietly thrown away by students who are entirely capable of the mathematics.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangles, sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Bearings questions are reliably mishandled because students do not draw the diagram before calculating.

subjects.name: Geometry and mensuration
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems, surface area and volume of compound shapes. Compound-shape questions carry several method marks that are lost when working is not laid out in identifiable steps.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Straight lines, quadratics, reciprocal and exponential graphs, transformations and, at the higher tiers, function notation. Marks go on reading values off a graph without showing the construction lines the mark scheme expects.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms, tree diagrams and conditional probability. Histograms with unequal class widths are a predictable loss, and tree diagrams are usually drawn correctly then read wrongly.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry, translations, rotations, reflections and enlargements including negative scale factors. A small topic that appears every series and that students under-practise relative to its reliability.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem solving
subjects.description: Questions that combine two or three topics with no signposting. These separate the top grades, and the skill is planning the route before calculating rather than any individual technique.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Mode settings, fraction and surd entry, statistical functions, and recording enough working that a correct display earns full credit. One session here regularly returns more marks than a topic re-teach, and nobody charges for it because it is unglamorous.

subjects.name: Working presentation for the mark scheme
subjects.description: Writing the steps a marker needs to see. Students who do three steps mentally and write one line lose method marks they had earned. It is a habit, it takes about three weeks of insistence, and it is free marks.
