sections.heading: ADEK, the work permit, and who may legally teach your child
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools sit under ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by almost nobody in this market's content, which is odd, because it is the body whose inspection reports describe your child's school and whose professional-ethics rules shape what your child's own teacher may do outside school hours. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or endorsed by ADEK, and no tutoring platform should imply otherwise.

Private tutoring itself is regulated federally. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services. Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

One rule matters more than the paperwork for Abu Dhabi families. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current policy wording with ADEK before relying on it. The practical reading is simple: do not try to hire your child's own classroom teacher privately, however well that relationship works in school.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the maths
paragraphs: A Mushrif parent planning maths tuition is usually planning it into a week that already contains subjects the school has no choice about. Federal rules require private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside whatever international curriculum they are licensed for, and to follow the Ministry's general regulations on them. Those lessons occupy real timetable space, and for an Arabic-speaking student they occupy more of it, because the first-language route is a heavier course than the additional-language one.

This matters for scheduling rather than for maths content. A Year 11 student carrying nine IGCSE subjects plus the mandatory UAE subjects has fewer genuinely free evenings than the subject count suggests, and the two sessions a week that a pre-series paper clinic needs have to displace something. We would rather have that conversation before the first lesson than discover in week three that Thursday never works. Families often find that one maths session plus honest self-marking beats two sessions crammed into a full week.

It also matters for Ministry of Education equivalency, which is where the mandatory subjects and the international qualification meet. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. One competitor page in this market states that six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. We describe the process and point you to the Ministry; IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency, and no IB points threshold should be quoted without a Ministry source.

sections.heading: What happens in the week when no specialist is free
paragraphs: In the fortnight before a series, demand for Extended maths outruns supply, and the honest answer to a request in that window is sometimes no. What we will not do is fill the slot with a tutor who has never taught the paper and let the family find out in session two. The alternatives are better: a later weekday slot with the right person, a short diagnostic block that tells the student exactly what to work on alone, or a waiting list with a date on it rather than a vague promise.

A diagnostic-only block is more useful than it sounds. One session on a marked mock paper produces a ranked list of where the marks went, and a student in Year 11 can act on that list without a tutor present for every hour of practice. Several families have taken that and come back the following term for the rebuild, which is the right order. The expensive mistake is booking twenty hours in April to cover a problem that forty minutes of diagnosis would have identified in October.

If a different board's specialist is the only realistic match, we say so before you book, name the difference, and let you decide. A 4MA1 Higher teacher taking a 0580 Extended student will handle the content comfortably and will need to read the non-calculator paper properly first. That is a manageable gap when it is disclosed and a problem when it is hidden. Disclosure is the whole of the trust proposition here, and it is the one thing no competitor page in this market offers.

process.description: If the error log flattens and the student is working accurately, fewer sessions are the right recommendation, and we will make it. Tuition that continues because it has become a habit is money a family in this district would rather put towards the next subject.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IGCSE maths tutor living in Al Mushrif?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly somebody in the district teaches maths. Whether that person has taught your child's exact syllabus and tier to grade 8 or 9 standard, is free at five on a weekday, and holds a valid MoHRE private tuition work permit is a much narrower question, and the answer is often no. That is why we match on the syllabus code and deliver the lesson online over live video rather than drawing a radius around Mushrif Mall. The teaching relationship is still one-to-one; only the commute disappears.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits 0580, 0607 or Edexcel 4MA1?
faqs.answer: The code is printed on the statement of entry the school issues and on the front cover of every past paper the maths department distributes. If neither is to hand, the exams officer will confirm it in one email. It matters because the three routes test different things: 0580 bars the calculator in one paper, 4MA1 allows it in both, and 0607 assumes a graphic display calculator. Revision advice written for the wrong code wastes weeks, and we ask for the code before matching anyone.

faqs.question: My son is at the top of the Core group. Should he move to Extended?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the conversation belongs in Year 10 rather than Year 11. Core caps the grade available, so a student working comfortably at the top of it is limited by the route rather than by ability. Moving up is an entry decision the school makes as the exam centre, and it becomes awkward once final entries close. Bring the last two assessment papers to your child's maths teacher and ask directly what the cap is costing. A short diagnostic block can tell you whether the Extended content is reachable in the time left.

faqs.question: What does an online IGCSE maths tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The market splits into bands. Budget online tuition runs roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists reach AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those are the providers' own published figures rather than ours. For IB Gram's own arrangement, the trial lesson is free and the rate is confirmed in the match conversation.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tuition quoted higher than the same tutor online?
faqs.answer: Travel. An in-home one-to-one visit in this market is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online. The gap pays for the journey, the fuel and the cancelled session that cannot be refilled. On the central island that premium buys a short drive. Out towards Khalifa City it buys ninety minutes of somebody's evening, and the teaching is identical either way.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor working with my child need a permit in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Anyone tutoring privately without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted to you with caution.

faqs.question: Can we hire my daughter's own maths teacher from school privately?
faqs.answer: You should not, and in Abu Dhabi you probably cannot. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also restricts serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording with ADEK before acting on it. The practical effect is that the right tutor is somebody outside the school, which removes any conflict over marking her coursework or setting her mocks.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE maths exams for a candidate in the UAE?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in those two windows and offers the February/March series to India only, so an entry deadline found on an Indian revision site does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Both boards publish provisional timetables and both revise them, so take dates from the live timetable on the board's own site and confirm the version with your school's exams officer.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge timetable zone is my child's Abu Dhabi exam centre in?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the series timetable. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used. That makes the zone a genuinely important piece of information and one almost no parent is told. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in, then plan revision and travel from that timetable rather than from a generic one found online.

faqs.question: Where do strong maths students in this area lose marks most often?
faqs.answer: Not in the topics they find hard. The biggest single loss is method marks forfeited by doing arithmetic mentally and writing only the answer, which punishes quick students hardest. Second is the instruction: significant figures, units, exact form, answers left in terms of pi. Third is three-dimensional trigonometry, where the problem is drawing the triangle rather than using the rule. Fourth is surd and exact-form work on the non-calculator paper, and fifth is frequency density on histograms, which is a single-session repair almost nobody makes.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 in Al Mushrif realistically need?
faqs.answer: One a week through the autumn term, moving to two in the six to eight weeks before the series if the error log justifies it. Two from the start is usually a mistake: the student has no time to practise between sessions, so the tutor ends up re-teaching rather than correcting. A Year 11 here also carries the mandatory Arabic, Islamic studies and social studies lessons alongside nine or ten subjects, so the free evenings are fewer than the subject list suggests. Plan the slot against the real week.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a maths coursework task or an investigation paper?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the technique, question the reasoning and give feedback on what the student has already written. Nobody here produces the work itself. That boundary is not a policy preference: submitting work that is not the candidate's own is a malpractice matter with the board, and the student carries the consequence. For an investigation-style paper the useful support is structure, notation and how to justify a method, all taught against the published criteria rather than demonstrated on the student's actual submission.

faqs.question: Does my child need an IGCSE maths grade for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Maths is normally among the five because every British-curriculum school enters it. Verify the current requirement with the Ministry directly. IB Gram describes the process and does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not a requirement of it.

faqs.question: What happens if no Extended maths specialist is free when we ask?
faqs.answer: We tell you, which is not what the market usually does. The options are a later weekday slot with the right tutor, a short diagnostic block that gives the student a ranked list to work on alone, a waiting list with an actual date, or a tutor from the other board with the difference named before you book. In the fortnight before a series, demand for Extended maths outruns supply, and a disclosed limit is more useful to a family than a booking that quietly becomes a mismatch.

faqs.question: Is an online lesson genuinely as useful as somebody sitting at the table?
faqs.answer: For a Year 10 or Year 11 working through timed papers, yes, and often better, because the tutor is chosen for the paper rather than for the postcode. Both people see the same paper on screen, working is written live on a shared whiteboard, and the session is recorded in a note afterwards. Physical presence matters more for much younger children, who need an adult managing attention. For exam-year maths the binding constraint is the tutor's knowledge of the mark scheme, not the furniture.

intro.heading: Start with the specification, not the subject
paragraphs: Parents in Al Nahyan usually arrive at this search after a report card. A grade has slipped, or a mock paper has come back with a number that does not match what the student thought they knew. The instinct is to find someone good at maths. The more useful instinct is to find someone who knows which maths paper your child is sitting, because IGCSE Mathematics is not one qualification. It is at least three in common use across Abu Dhabi schools, and the differences are large enough to change what a student should practise this week.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the version most British-curriculum schools in the emirate use. It is tiered into Core and Extended, and a student sits two written papers. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a different animal, built around a graphic display calculator and carrying an investigation paper at Extended tier. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, splits into Foundation and Higher and is examined through two papers of equal weight, both with a calculator permitted. A student drilling non-calculator arithmetic for a 4MA1 entry is spending hours on a skill the paper will not test in isolation.

This is why the first conversation about an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Nahyan should be short and factual. Which board. Which tier. Which papers, on which dates. What the school's mock used. Whether the student has a formula sheet in the exam or has to recall the formulae. A tutor who cannot answer those within the first ten minutes is going to teach topics, which feels productive and moves grades slowly. A tutor who starts there can tell you by the end of a trial lesson which three topics are costing the most marks and roughly how long each takes to repair.

Al Nahyan sits inland on Abu Dhabi island, between Airport Road and Al Karamah, a dense district of mid-rise apartment blocks rather than villa compounds. Families here send children across the island and out to the Khalifa City corridor, so the school day ends anywhere between 2:30pm and 3:45pm and the journey home can add forty minutes. That geography is the practical reason tuition here works better over live video: a 5pm slot survives traffic, a tutor driving in from somewhere else does not. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi — home visiting is an India-only service — and on a subject like maths the trade is a good one, because the scarce resource is a tutor who has marked 0580 Paper 4 rather than a tutor who lives nearby.

The rest of this page is the detail: how the two main specifications differ, how the tiering decision is made and when it stops being reversible, where the marks actually go topic by topic, what the mark scheme notation means, how eight weeks of past-paper work should be structured, and what the Abu Dhabi market charges for all of it. Figures are attributed. None of them is our price list.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-nahyan.programmesIntro: Al Nahyan students reach IGCSE maths through a Cambridge Lower Secondary route, an Indian or American middle-school route, or a transfer from another system mid-way. Each arrives with different gaps, and the programme a student is in determines what a tutor should be fixing.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics
programmes.description: The three years that decide whether Extended tier is realistic. Lower Secondary covers number, algebra, geometry, measure, statistics and probability at a level that looks gentle next to IGCSE, and the gap opens in Year 9 when algebraic manipulation becomes the load-bearing skill. Students who leave Year 9 unable to rearrange a formula confidently will meet that same weakness in every IGCSE topic that follows.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools often make the Core or Extended recommendation during Year 9 on the strength of internal testing. For an Al Nahyan family, that means Year 9 is the cheapest year to buy tuition in: a term of work on algebraic fluency at that point changes which tier the school offers, and the tier decides the grade ceiling for the next two years.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Two written papers. At Core tier a student sits a short-answer paper and a structured paper graded C to G. At Extended tier the papers are longer and harder and the grade range runs A* to E. The syllabus content is number, algebra and graphs, coordinate geometry, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, vectors and transformations, probability and statistics, with Extended adding topics Core never sees.
programmes.countryNote: Extended 0580 is the standard entry at most British-curriculum schools on Abu Dhabi island, and the one a student needs if they intend to take Mathematics at AS and A Level or move into an IB Diploma maths course. A Core entry closes those doors quietly, which is why the tiering conversation matters more than any single topic.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Two papers of two hours, each worth half the qualification, both with a calculator allowed. Foundation tier is graded 5 to 1 and Higher tier 9 to 4, with the familiar numerical scale rather than letters. A formula sheet is provided, which shifts the emphasis from recall to selection and application. Content ranges across number, algebra, sequences, geometry, trigonometry, vectors and statistics.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools moved to Pearson specifications for the numerical grading and the modular resit routes available further up the system. For a family in Al Nahyan the practical consequence is that Pearson results arrive on a different schedule: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: An optional extra qualification sat alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for A Level Mathematics or a Higher Level IB maths course. It introduces calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and more demanding trigonometry a year early. Two papers, both calculator-permitted, with a noticeable jump in the algebra required to get started on a question.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Al Nahyan school offers 0606, it is usually taught in a small set and moves fast. Students who cope with Extended 0580 but find 0606 brutal are almost always missing algebraic stamina rather than the new content, and that is a diagnosable, fixable gap over a term of weekly one-to-one work.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-nahyan.subjectsIntro: Maths is the reason you are on this page, but the topics below are the ones that generate the marks. Each line is a place where Abu Dhabi students reliably lose marks on 0580 and 4MA1, with what a tutor should be doing about it.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and rearrangement
subjects.description: The skill every other topic rests on. Students who cannot change the subject of a formula without hesitation lose marks in mensuration, trigonometry, kinematics-style questions and simultaneous equations. Fluency here is built by volume of short exercises, not by long worked examples.

subjects.name: Quadratics: factorising, formula, completing the square
subjects.description: Extended 0580 and Higher 4MA1 both expect three routes into a quadratic and a judgement about which one the question wants. The common failure is reaching for the formula when the question says 'by factorising', which forfeits method marks even with a correct answer.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Sketching, reading intersections, describing translations and stretches in function notation. Marks go when a student describes a transformation in words where the mark scheme wants the notation, or sketches a curve with the wrong asymptotic behaviour.

subjects.name: Trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles
subjects.description: Sine rule, cosine rule, area formula and the ambiguous case. Three-dimensional trigonometry questions are where Extended candidates stall, usually because they do not draw the single relevant triangle out of the solid before starting.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound solids
subjects.description: Surface area and volume of cones, spheres, pyramids and frustums, plus similar-solid scale factors. The reliable error is applying a linear scale factor to an area or a volume. One clear lesson on the squared and cubed relationship usually ends the problem.

subjects.name: Vectors and column vector geometry
subjects.description: Adding and subtracting column vectors, magnitude, and proving points collinear using a scalar multiple. Students lose marks by writing a geometric argument in sentences when the mark scheme asks for a vector route, and by dropping the arrow notation.

subjects.name: Probability, tree diagrams and conditional cases
subjects.description: Without-replacement questions and two-stage trees. The marks are in labelling the branches and multiplying along them; the standard error is adding where the question requires multiplication, or forgetting that the second denominator has changed.

subjects.name: Statistics: cumulative frequency and histograms
subjects.description: Reading medians and quartiles from a cumulative frequency curve, and frequency density on unequal class widths. Histogram questions are among the highest-yield fixes available, because the frequency density calculation is mechanical once a student has seen it done twice.

subjects.name: Number: bounds, standard form and surds
subjects.description: Upper and lower bounds in a calculation, and exact-form answers. Extended candidates lose marks by rounding an intermediate value and carrying the error forward, which costs the accuracy mark even where the method was right.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic and exact answers
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 has a paper where no calculator is permitted; Pearson 4MA1 does not. This single difference changes a student's revision diet, and it is the first thing to establish before any practice schedule is written.

sections.heading: What a search for an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Nahyan is really asking
paragraphs: The literal answer: an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Nahyan is a specialist who teaches Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 to a student living in that district, almost always one-to-one and, in IB Gram's case, always over live video. The search word 'in Al Nahyan' describes where the student is, not where the teaching happens.

Behind the query there is usually a sharper question that parents do not type into Google: is my child on the right tier, and if the answer is no, how long do we have to change it. That question has a deadline attached, because a school's final entry decision is made months before the exam and a tier change after that point is awkward at best. A tutor who answers only the first question — can you help with maths — leaves the expensive part of the problem untouched.

The second unspoken question is about the mock result. An Abu Dhabi mock paper is usually a past paper from a recent series, marked to the official scheme by the class teacher. That makes it genuinely diagnostic, and it means the script itself is the most valuable document in the house. Before any tuition starts, the marked mock should be scanned and read question by question: not for the total, but for the pattern of where the marks stopped arriving. In most scripts, three or four recurring faults account for the majority of the lost marks, and two of them are usually technique rather than content.

That is the work this page describes. Everything below assumes the goal is a specific, diagnosable improvement on a named specification, delivered in weekly live video lessons to a household in Al Nahyan, with the figures and deadlines stated plainly enough that you can check them.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1: two specifications, two different revision diets
paragraphs: Most of the wasted effort in IGCSE maths tuition comes from treating the two main specifications as interchangeable. They are not. The table below sets them side by side on the points that change what a student should do on a Tuesday evening.

The calculator rule is the most consequential line in it. Cambridge 0580 includes a paper on which no calculator is permitted, so a 0580 candidate has to be fluent in exact-form arithmetic, surds, fraction manipulation and mental estimation. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers, so the same student would be better served spending those hours on calculator technique: storing intermediate values to avoid rounding errors, using the statistical functions, and checking that the machine is in degrees rather than radians.

The second consequential line is formula provision. Pearson supplies a formula sheet; Cambridge expects recall of a defined list. A 4MA1 student does not need to memorise the sine rule, but does need to recognise instantly which formula on the sheet a question is pointing at, which is a different skill and is trained differently. Tiering vocabulary also differs: Core and Extended for Cambridge, Foundation and Higher for Pearson, with different grade ranges in each case.

None of this is obscure. All of it is published on the boards' own sites, and the correct move for any Abu Dhabi family is to read the live specification and the current timetable there rather than trusting a summary. The point of the table is to show that the differences are large enough to matter, so the first question to any prospective tutor is which of these three documents they work from.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tiering decision, and when it stops being reversible
paragraphs: Tiering is the highest-stakes decision in IGCSE maths and it is usually made by the school, on internal evidence, in the middle of Year 10 or early in Year 11. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade. That cap then propagates: AS and A Level Mathematics generally expects an Extended or Higher grade behind it, and a student heading for an IB Diploma maths course at Higher Level will struggle without the Extended content, which includes topics Core never covers at all.

The decision is not arbitrary and schools are usually right. A student placed at Extended who cannot hold algebraic manipulation together will fail to convert the harder paper into marks and may score worse than they would have at Core. The honest framing for a parent is therefore not 'push for Extended' but 'find out what the school is seeing, and whether it is fixable in the time available'. That is a question with a factual answer, and the marked internal assessments contain it.

Where tuition changes a tiering outcome, it almost always does so in Year 9 or early Year 10, by building algebraic fluency before the content load arrives. A term of weekly one-to-one work at that stage is the single highest-leverage spend available in the whole IGCSE run. The same money spent in the final term before the exam buys exam technique, which is worth having, but it cannot buy back a tier.
The table sets out what to check, and what each answer implies. Take it to the maths department rather than to a tutor: the school holds the evidence and makes the entry.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks actually go, topic by topic
paragraphs: Lost marks in IGCSE maths are not evenly spread. Across marked Abu Dhabi mock scripts the same handful of faults repeats, and most of them are cheap to repair because they are procedural rather than conceptual. A student who understands similar solids perfectly but applies a linear scale factor to a volume is not confused about geometry; they are missing one rule, and one lesson ends it.

The highest-yield repairs, in rough order of how many marks they return per hour spent, are frequency density in histograms, scale factors in similar shapes, without-replacement probability trees, rearranging a formula where the subject appears twice, bounds in a division, and three-dimensional trigonometry where the first move is to extract the relevant triangle. None of these takes a term. Each takes a lesson plus practice, and together they routinely account for a double-digit mark swing on an Extended paper.

Conceptual gaps are a different category and they take longer. The common ones are function notation, where a student can evaluate but cannot interpret a transformation; vectors, where the geometric meaning never attached to the algebra; and anything requiring a proof or a justification, where students who can compute cannot explain. These need teaching rather than drilling, and the honest estimate is several weeks each rather than one lesson.

The practical method is to maintain an error log across every paper the student sits. Each lost mark gets one line: the question, the topic, and the category — content not known, method known but misapplied, technique or timing, misread the command. After three papers the pattern is unmistakable and the revision plan writes itself. Most students have never done this, and it is the single cheapest piece of exam preparation available.

sections.heading: Reading a mark scheme: method marks, accuracy marks and follow-through
paragraphs: Almost no IGCSE maths student has read a mark scheme, and it is the most useful document in the subject. Mark schemes are published by both boards after each series and they explain, line by line, exactly what earns credit. Once a student has read three of them, their written answers change shape permanently.

The notation is simple. A method mark is awarded for a correct approach even where the arithmetic fails afterwards, which means a student who writes nothing down and gets the answer wrong scores zero where a student who shows a correct method and slips at the last step scores most of the marks. An accuracy mark requires the right value, properly rounded. Follow-through credit allows a correct subsequent step to earn marks even when it is built on an earlier wrong answer — but only if the working is visible. Special-case credit covers specific common near-misses the examiners decided to reward.

The behavioural consequences are blunt and worth stating to a teenager directly. Write down the substitution before you evaluate it. Keep full accuracy in intermediate values and round only at the end. If a question gives you an answer to use in a later part, use it even if your own earlier answer differed. Never erase a wrong attempt that contains a valid method; cross it out instead, because crossed-out work can still be marked if nothing replaces it.

A tutor's job here is to mark the student's own scripts against the official scheme and show them where credit was available and not claimed. That conversation, repeated across four or five papers, converts more marks than most content teaching, and it is the part a generalist maths tutor is least likely to do.

sections.heading: Eight weeks of past-paper work, structured rather than accumulated
paragraphs: Most families reach for past papers at the point where there is no time left for anything else, and then use them badly: sit a paper, check the total, feel bad, sit another. Papers used that way measure a student repeatedly without changing them. Structured properly, the same eight weeks do real work.

A workable shape runs like this. Week one is diagnostic: one full paper under exam conditions, marked strictly against the official scheme, with every lost mark logged by category. Weeks two to four are repair, driven entirely by that log — the three or four highest-frequency faults, taught and then drilled on question sets rather than whole papers. Week five is a second full paper, which tests whether the repairs held. Weeks six and seven are timing and endurance: full papers to the clock, with a hard rule that no question is abandoned before the given working is attempted. Week eight is light, revisiting the error log and the formula list rather than introducing anything.

Two rules make the difference. Papers must be sat to time, because the fault most Abu Dhabi students discover in a timed paper is that they spend twelve minutes on a four-mark question and then leave eighteen marks unattempted at the back. And papers must be marked against the published scheme rather than self-assessed, because students systematically award themselves marks for answers that would earn none and miss method marks they actually earned.

Sourcing is a boundary worth naming. Specifications, timetables, past papers and mark schemes are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own sites, and that is where a family should get them. IB Gram does not reproduce or distribute board material; a tutor works through it with the student from the official source.

sections.heading: What IGCSE maths tuition costs around Al Nahyan, and what the hour buys
paragraphs: Published rates for maths tuition in the UAE vary by roughly a factor of ten, and the variation is not mostly about quality. It is about who is teaching, whether anyone is travelling, and how much marking happens between lessons. The table shows the bands visible in the market as read in October 2026, with the source of each, and what the hour is typically spent on at that level.

The useful way to read it is by what disappears as the price falls. At the budget end, the hour is usually spent going over homework the student has already attempted — valuable for confidence, limited for grade movement, and generally delivered by someone who has not marked a 0580 paper. In the middle band, the tutor teaches the specification and marks written work between sessions, which is where measurable improvement starts. At the specialist end, the fee buys judgement: which tier, which topics to abandon, which questions to practise, and what the mark scheme rewards.

In-home visiting carries its own premium in this market, quoted in survey data at AED 180 to 350 an hour and by independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. A meaningful share of that is the drive. For a household in Al Nahyan, travelling in from the mainland in the afternoon, the premium buys physical presence and costs both money and session time. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts monthly spend for a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Every figure here belongs to the market, not to IB Gram. sections.heading: Academic honesty in maths, and ADEK's rules on who may tutor
paragraphs: Maths has less coursework exposure than the essay subjects, but the honesty boundary still matters, and it sits in a predictable place. A tutor may teach content, model a method, mark a student's attempt against the official scheme and explain where credit was lost. A tutor may not sit beside a student during an assessed task, supply answers to live assessed work, or hand over a completed solution for submission. We will not do that, and a tutor who offers to is a liability to the student rather than a shortcut.

The regulatory position is worth knowing precisely because competitors leave it out. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals who tutor without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

In Abu Dhabi there is a further layer. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff are prohibited from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify that against the current ADEK policy document before relying on it, but the practical advice is simple: never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher.

IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and is not an approved centre of any kind. We are an independent matching platform. The regulators above are named here because knowing what each does helps a parent ask better questions, not because any of them endorses us.

whyPoints.description: Finish times across the island and the mainland corridor vary by more than an hour, and a sibling collection usually decides the slot. Sessions are set to what the household can actually sustain weekly, including post-Iftar timing during Ramadan.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths specification does my child in Al Nahyan actually sit?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the school, and it is the first thing to establish. Abu Dhabi schools commonly use Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1. The school's exams officer can confirm the code and the tier in one email. The codes are not cosmetic: 0580 includes a paper with no calculator, 4MA1 allows a calculator throughout and supplies a formula sheet, and 0607 is built around a graphic display calculator. Revision that suits one is partly wasted on another.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE maths tutor come to our apartment in Al Nahyan?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one IGCSE maths tuition over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE — home visiting is a service we run only in India. Independent home tutors in Abu Dhabi do visit, and the market prices that convenience at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on the source. What online delivery buys instead is choice: a tutor who teaches your child's exact specification, rather than whoever is free within a short drive.

faqs.question: How long does it take to move an IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong, and that is why the diagnosis comes first. Procedural faults — frequency density, scale factors, rounding too early, abandoning multi-part questions — are often worth a double-digit mark swing and take a lesson plus practice each. Conceptual gaps such as function notation or vectors take several weeks of teaching. A tier-level change in underlying fluency takes a term or more. No tutor can promise a grade, and a plan that cannot say which category your child's problem falls into is not a plan.

faqs.question: Is the non-calculator paper really that different to prepare for?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single biggest divergence between the main specifications. A Cambridge 0580 candidate sits a paper with no calculator and therefore needs fluent fraction work, surds, exact forms, mental estimation and confident long arithmetic. A Pearson 4MA1 candidate has a calculator on both papers and needs different habits: storing intermediate values to avoid rounding errors, using statistical functions correctly, and checking the angle mode. A student preparing for the wrong one of these has spent real hours on a skill their paper will not isolate.

faqs.question: When is it too late to change my child from Core to Extended?
faqs.answer: Practically, once the school has submitted its final entry. Entries close months before the paper is sat, and a change afterwards is difficult and sometimes impossible. There is a second, softer deadline: the Extended tier covers content Core classes may never have been taught, so a move needs enough time for that teaching to happen as well as the administrative change. Ask the maths department two questions — when the entry is submitted, and how much Extended-only content has been covered — and work backwards from the earlier of the two.

faqs.question: What does Additional Mathematics 0606 add, and does my child need it?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is an optional qualification taken alongside Extended 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics or a Higher Level IB maths course. It introduces calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and harder trigonometry a year early. It is not required for either route, but it makes the transition noticeably less abrupt. Students who manage Extended comfortably but find 0606 punishing are nearly always short of algebraic stamina rather than ability, which is a specific and fixable gap.

faqs.question: Which exam series can a candidate in Abu Dhabi actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two available to UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who sit the wrong version. Always read the live official timetable rather than a summary on any tutoring website, including this one.

faqs.question: Should we book weekly lessons or a short intensive block before the exam?
faqs.answer: Weekly lessons move content and fluency; an intensive block moves technique. If the mock showed topics genuinely not known, weekly work across a term is the honest answer, because content cannot be compressed indefinitely. If the mock showed the content broadly present but marks leaking through misread commands, early rounding and poor timing, a short block of timed papers marked against the official scheme does more in four weeks than a term of topic teaching would. The marked script tells you which case you are in.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover 0580 maths and a Cambridge science for an Al Nahyan student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A tutor who teaches Extended 0580 and Cambridge Physics 0625 can genuinely do both, and there is real value in one person seeing where the maths weakness is damaging the physics. What does not work is stretching a single tutor across four unrelated subjects to simplify scheduling. Where a second specialist is needed we say so, and where no UAE-based specialist covers a niche combination we will tell you that too rather than filling the slot.

faqs.question: How do we check that a private tutor in Abu Dhabi is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A tutor who deflects the question has answered it.

faqs.question: Can my child's own maths teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, that should be treated as closed. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates private and charter school staff are barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current ADEK policy document before relying on the detail, but the practical position is clear: arrange tuition with an independent specialist, not with the person who teaches and assesses your child in class.

faqs.question: What does the mark scheme notation on a returned paper mean?
faqs.answer: Method marks reward a correct approach even when the arithmetic afterwards fails. Accuracy marks require the correct value, rounded as asked. Follow-through credit allows a correct later step to score even when it rests on an earlier wrong answer, provided the working is visible. Special-case credit covers particular near-misses the examiners chose to reward. The behavioural lesson for a student is short: show the substitution, keep full accuracy until the end, use any answer the question gives you, and cross out rather than erase.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE maths rates in Abu Dhabi rise closer to the exam series?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens rather than headline rates moving much. In the weeks before a series the specialist tutors fill first, so families booking late choose from a smaller pool at the upper end of the published bands — roughly AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist support, per the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey. The practical consequence for an Al Nahyan family is that a decision made a term early costs the same and buys a better match. Booking in the final fortnight mostly buys exam technique.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with my child's maths coursework or assessed tasks?
faqs.answer: A tutor teaches the content, models methods, marks your child's own attempts against the published scheme and explains where credit was lost. A tutor does not sit alongside a student during an assessed task, supply solutions for live assessed work, or hand over finished work for submission. We decline that, because under board regulations it puts the student's own entry at risk. The boundary is not a technicality: the work submitted has to be the student's, and a tutor's value is in making that work better before it is submitted.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for our preferred time slot?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Demand for Extended 0580 and Higher 4MA1 specialists concentrates in the late-afternoon Gulf Standard Time window, which is exactly when Al Nahyan families want lessons. The options are usually a slightly earlier or later weekday slot, a weekend session, or a short wait for a named tutor. Where no UAE-based specialist covers the combination at all, we will tell you that and explain what the alternative looks like before you commit to anything.

intro.heading: Proximity is the wrong filter for an IGCSE maths tutor
paragraphs: A parent in Al Raha Beach types the search with a map in mind. Somebody within a fifteen-minute drive, ideally in the same community or in Al Raha Gardens, who can arrive after the school run. It is a reasonable instinct and it produces a poor shortlist, because the thing that determines whether a maths tutor is useful has nothing to do with where they sleep.

What determines it is the specification. A student at one Al Raha corridor school may be entered for Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended, sitting Papers 2 and 4. A student two kilometres away may be on Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 Extended, which requires a graphics calculator and ends with a compulsory investigation paper that 0580 does not have. A third may be on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, Higher tier, where both papers allow a calculator and each is worth half the grade. These are different courses that share a word.

The difference is not cosmetic. On 0580 Extended a calculator is permitted in both papers but the questions are written on the assumption that algebra carries the method, so a student who reaches for the calculator first is practising the wrong reflex. On 0607 the graphics calculator is mandatory and a correct answer without the required sketch or table loses marks. On 4MA1 Higher the back pages carry proof-style and vector questions that reward a written argument rather than a calculation. Three different sets of habits, three different first lessons.

The practical consequence is that a tutor who is excellent on 0580 Extended can waste six weeks of a 0607 student's time by drilling the wrong paper style, and will not know to teach the investigation at all. A tutor who has only taught 4MA1 will build a student's method around calculator availability, which is exactly the habit that loses marks on a 0580 Paper 2. None of that is visible from a profile that says IGCSE Maths.

So the first thing to do is not to search harder but to find out what your child is actually sitting. The information is on the exam entry statement the school issues, on a past paper header, or available from the head of mathematics in one email. A four-digit code and the word Core, Extended, Foundation or Higher is all you need. With that in hand the shortlist changes completely, and the geography stops mattering.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE maths specification is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This is the question that makes the search answerable. Four specifications account for almost all IGCSE maths entries in Abu Dhabi schools, and they differ in ways that change how a tutor works from the first session. The code is a four-character string on the exam entry statement, and it is also printed on the header of every past paper the school hands out.

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the most widely entered. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4. Paper 2 is short-answer and relentless, Paper 4 is structured and allows partial credit across a longer question. A calculator is permitted in all four papers, but the Extended questions are written on the assumption that algebra, not the calculator, carries the method.

Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is the one that catches parents out. It requires a graphics calculator, uses non-calculator and calculator papers in a different arrangement, and ends with a compulsory investigation paper. Schools that run an IB continuum often prefer it because the investigation and the graphing work map onto Diploma habits. A tutor who has never taught the investigation paper is not equipped for this course.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, uses two equally weighted papers with a calculator allowed in both. Specification B, 4MB1, is a different structure again. Pearson also offers Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 as the extension route where Cambridge offers Additional Mathematics 0606. Ask for the code, then read the table below.

sections.heading: Core, Extended, Foundation, Higher: what the tier decides
paragraphs: The tier is a bigger decision than most families realise, because it sets a ceiling. On Cambridge 0580, Core candidates can be awarded grades C to G and Extended candidates A* to E. On Pearson 4MA1, Foundation tier caps at grade 5 while Higher runs from 9 down to 4 with a safety-net 3. A student placed on the lower tier cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, and no amount of tutoring changes that arithmetic.

Schools make the tier decision for sound reasons, usually from Year 10 assessment evidence, and it is often right. The cases worth questioning are specific: a student whose weakness is arithmetic speed rather than conceptual understanding, a student who joined the school mid-course and was placed cautiously, and a student whose Year 10 results were depressed by something other than maths. Those are the three situations in which a diagnostic session earns its fee immediately.

The decision usually stays open until the entry deadline, which sits months before the exam window. That is the window in which evidence can change a placement, and it closes quietly. A parent who wants the tier reconsidered needs marked work showing the student handling Extended or Higher content, not a conversation about potential, and they need it before entries go in.

The reverse case matters too. A student struggling badly on Extended content who is moved to Core can convert a likely E into a secure C, which for the Ministry of Education's five-subject equivalency count is the difference between a subject that counts and one that is marginal. Tutoring aimed at the right tier beats tutoring aimed at the ambitious one.

sections.heading: What 'knows the syllabus' actually means in a maths tutor
paragraphs: Parents use the phrase constantly and providers repeat it back without content. It is worth defining, because it is testable in a single free trial lesson. A tutor who knows the specification can name the papers your child will sit and their weightings without looking them up. They know whether a calculator is available in each one. They know which topics are on the Extended syllabus but absent from Core, and which appear on 4MA1 Higher but not on 0580 Extended.

They also know the mark scheme, which is a separate kind of knowledge. IGCSE maths papers award method marks for work that leads towards a correct answer even when the final line is wrong, and they withhold marks for an answer that appears without the step that justifies it. A tutor who has marked or taught against the published mark schemes will stop a student mid-question to ask what the examiner can see, which is a habit no amount of content knowledge substitutes for.

And they know the sequence. Circle theorems before vectors is a different lesson from vectors before circle theorems, and neither is useful if simultaneous equations are still shaky. A tutor who knows the syllabus builds a route through it from where the student actually is, rather than following the textbook order because the textbook is in front of them.

You can test all three in a trial lesson by asking three questions. Which papers does my child sit and what are they worth. Which two topics should we do first, and why those. sections.heading: Where Abu Dhabi IGCSE candidates lose maths marks, topic by topic
paragraphs: Loss patterns in IGCSE maths are strikingly consistent, which is good news because it makes them addressable. The largest single cluster across both boards sits in algebraic manipulation: algebraic fractions, rearranging a formula where the subject appears twice, and solving a quadratic when the question did not announce that it was a quadratic. These are not conceptually difficult. They are unpractised.

The second cluster is in proportional reasoning. Reverse percentages, compound interest over a non-integer number of periods, direct and inverse proportion with a constant to find, and best-buy comparisons with awkward units. Students who can do forward percentage change confidently often cannot run it backwards, and examiners test the backwards direction deliberately.

The third is geometric reasoning, which is where Higher and Extended candidates separate. Circle theorems require a named reason, not just a correct angle, and vectors require an argument written in vector notation rather than a diagram with arrows. Pearson Higher papers place these towards the back, which means they also collide with the timing problem and get attempted badly or not at all.

The fourth is presentation. Marks are lost to unsimplified answers, to premature rounding carried through a multi-step calculation, to units omitted from a final line, and to working that skips the step the mark scheme needed. A tutor who fixes only these four habits, teaching no new content whatsoever, will usually move a grade boundary's worth of marks. It is also the fastest cluster to address, which makes it the sensible place to start after a disappointing mock rather than the place to finish.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: how to find out, and why the answer matters
paragraphs: Families often do not know which board their child is entered with, and the school rarely volunteers it in a form a parent notices. There are three reliable ways to find out. The exam entry statement names the board and the specification code. Any past paper the school issues carries the board's name and the code in the header. And the head of mathematics will answer the question in one line if asked directly.

Knowing the board matters for a reason beyond matching a tutor. Past papers are specification-specific, and a student revising from the wrong board's papers is practising the wrong question styles. A 0580 Extended candidate working through 4MA1 Higher papers will meet question formats that do not appear on their own paper and will miss the ones that do. The time is not wasted exactly, but it is spent at a poor exchange rate.

The boards also differ in how they release material. Both publish past papers and mark schemes through their own channels, and both treat that material as their copyright. A tutor should reference and link official material rather than distributing it, and a provider offering a bundle of papers as a download is not doing your child a favour. Use the school's access and the boards' own sites.

One more practical difference. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for forthcoming series well ahead of time, which is why any session plan should link the live official timetable rather than quoting a date that may be revised. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: how many IGCSEs count, and at what grade
paragraphs: This is the part of the British-curriculum route that competitor pages in this market almost entirely skip, and it changes which grades matter. For the Ministry of Education's equivalency of a secondary school certificate on the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. They must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for that count. That detail matters because at least one competing site ranking for these searches tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published clarification says. Getting the number right is worth more to a family than any amount of marketing copy.

Mathematics is almost always one of the five, which is why a borderline maths grade has consequences beyond the subject itself. It also explains why moving a student to the tier they can actually secure a grade on is sometimes better advice than keeping them on the ambitious tier. A secure C or 4 that counts towards equivalency is worth more than a marginal E that might not.

Equivalency is a process run by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authorities, not by a tutoring platform, and nothing on this page should be read as IB Gram performing or guaranteeing any part of it. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before acting, and treat tutoring as help with the grades rather than help with the paperwork.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside IGCSE maths
paragraphs: A family budgeting for IGCSE maths tuition should know what else is on the timetable, because the mandatory UAE subjects take real teaching time and occasionally real tutoring money. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Every emirate's requirement sits on that federal baseline.

In Dubai, KHDA's published guidance makes Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies mandatory in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The guidance also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

The language-of-instruction rules are specific. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students. For non-Arabs, Islamic Education and the Moral, Social and Cultural studies strand are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Schools must also ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Two further details are worth a parent's attention. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. And the use of any different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring in them can honestly be described.

sections.heading: Sitting the exams: the June and November choice
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so no Abu Dhabi candidate is sitting it and any page that tells a UAE parent otherwise is giving them a date they cannot act on. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

For most Al Raha Beach students the decision is made by the school: Year 11 sits the June window, with November available as the resit route. Where a student needs one subject improved rather than a whole set, the November series is the efficient option, and the tutoring block that supports it runs through the summer and the first weeks of the autumn term rather than in the spring.

Results timing is worth planning around because it drives the resit decision. Pearson's published pattern is instructive: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. A family deciding on a resit needs the tutoring conversation booked before results arrive, not after.

Private candidate entry is a separate matter. A student not entered through their own school pays entry fees directly and must find a centre that accepts private candidates, and the fee depends on the number of subjects. Get that quote in writing before planning the tuition around it, and always read the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than a restated date, because provisional timetables are revised.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE maths syllabus my child is sitting in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Three reliable routes. The exam entry statement the school issues names the board and the specification code. Any past paper handed out in class carries the board and code in its header. And the head of mathematics will confirm it in a single email if asked directly. You are looking for a four-character code plus a tier word, such as 0580 Extended, 0607 Extended, 4MA1 Higher or 4MA1 Foundation. That string determines which tutor is useful, which past papers your child should be revising from, and which paper styles the tutoring should drill.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge 0580 the same course as Cambridge International Mathematics 0607?
faqs.answer: No. They share a subject but differ structurally. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended uses Papers 2 and 4, both with a calculator permitted, and has no investigation component. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 requires a graphics calculator, arranges its calculator and non-calculator papers differently, and ends with a compulsory investigation paper. Schools running an IB continuum often prefer 0607 because the graphing and investigation work maps onto Diploma habits. A tutor who has only taught 0580 will not know how to prepare a student for the investigation paper at all.

faqs.question: Does it really matter whether a maths tutor lives near Al Raha Beach?
faqs.answer: Not for the quality of the teaching. It matters only if a tutor has to travel, and travel is what the in-home premium pays for: roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour in this emirate by Bestimate's rate work, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Distance also narrows the pool to whoever happens to be free nearby, which for a thin specification such as 0607 or Further Pure 4PM1 is close to nobody. IB Gram teaches over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so location is not a filter.

faqs.question: My child is on Foundation tier. Can tutoring get them to a grade 7?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider suggesting otherwise is misleading you. Pearson 4MA1 Foundation tier caps at grade 5 and Cambridge 0580 Core caps at grade C. The ceiling is set by the entry, not by the student's performance on the day. What tutoring can do on a capped tier is secure the top available grade, which matters for the Ministry of Education's five-subject equivalency count. If the ceiling itself is the problem, the conversation to have is with the school about the tier, and it has to happen before the entry deadline.

faqs.question: Can the tier my child was entered for be changed?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, until the entry deadline, which sits months before the exam window. What the school needs is evidence rather than ambition: marked work showing your child handling Extended or Higher content at a reasonable standard. The three cases most worth raising are a student whose weakness is arithmetic speed rather than understanding, a student who joined mid-course and was placed cautiously, and a student whose Year 10 results were depressed by something unrelated to maths. A diagnostic session can produce that evidence quickly.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics cost Abu Dhabi students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Four clusters account for most of it. Algebraic manipulation, especially algebraic fractions and rearranging a formula where the subject appears twice. Proportional reasoning run backwards, particularly reverse percentages. Geometric reasoning, where circle theorems need a named reason and vectors need an argument written in vector notation rather than a diagram. And presentation: premature rounding, missing units, unsimplified answers and working that skips the step the mark scheme required. The fourth cluster is pure habit, teaches in about two hours, and often returns a grade boundary's worth of marks.

faqs.question: Should my child revise from Cambridge papers if they are entered with Pearson?
faqs.answer: No. Past papers are specification-specific and the question styles differ. A 4MA1 Higher candidate working through 0580 Extended papers will meet formats that will not appear on their own paper and will miss the proof-style and vector questions that will. The time is not wasted exactly, but it is spent at a bad exchange rate during the months when time is scarcest. Use the correct board's material through the school's access and the board's own site, and ask any tutor to confirm which board's papers they are setting.

faqs.question: What is the investigation paper on 0607 and how is it prepared for?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 includes a compulsory investigation paper that 0580 does not have. It asks a student to explore a situation, find a pattern, form a conjecture and then justify or generalise it, with a graphics calculator available throughout. The commonest failure is stopping at the pattern. Preparation is a distinct skill rather than extra content: working through past investigations slowly, writing the justification out in full, and learning which calculator output needs to be reproduced on the page. A tutor who has not taught it will not know this.

faqs.question: Does a borderline maths grade affect my child's UAE certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: It can, because maths is almost always one of the subjects counted. The published clarification for the British track states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A marginal maths grade therefore puts one of the five at risk, which is part of why securing the top grade on an achievable tier can be better advice than staying on an ambitious one. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before acting on it.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi students sit IGCSE maths in November as well as June?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and both are open to UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. For most Year 11 students the school enters them for the June or May/June window, with November used as the resit route or to improve a single subject. If a resit is likely, book the tutoring conversation before results arrive rather than after, because the November preparation window is short.

faqs.question: Which schools around Al Raha Beach do the IGCSE students you support attend?
faqs.answer: They come from across the Al Raha and Khalifa City corridor and the island campuses, including Al Yasmina Academy, Yasmina British Academy, Raha International School, GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi, Reach British School, Emirates National School and Repton Abu Dhabi. Those schools describe the neighbourhood's educational context and nothing more. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement arrangement with any of them. Because lessons are online, which campus a student attends has no bearing on which specification specialist is available to them.

faqs.question: Will a tutor based outside the UAE know my child's school deadlines?
faqs.answer: They will if you tell them, and that is how it should work. School internal deadlines, mock windows and reporting dates are set by your child's school, not by the board, so a tutor learns them from the student's planner in the first session and works to them. What a tutor brings from outside is specification knowledge, which is set by Cambridge or Pearson and is the same in Abu Dhabi as anywhere. Where an IB Gram tutor is based outside the UAE we disclose it before you book, and lessons are timed to Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking alongside 0580 Extended?
faqs.answer: For a student heading towards A-Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, often yes, because it introduces differentiation, integration, logarithms and binomial expansion a year early and makes the post-16 start much less punishing. For a student still fighting 0580 Extended algebra, no; it adds abstraction to an unstable base. The practical difficulty is supply. Small numbers take 0606 in any Abu Dhabi year group, in-school capacity is thin, and specialist tutors for it are scarce enough that matching can take up to a week.

faqs.question: What does a tutor do about my child relying on the calculator for everything?
faqs.answer: Treat it as the diagnosis rather than a side issue. Heavy calculator dependence passes IGCSE and then collapses in the first term of A-Level or IB Diploma maths, which is why so many students who found IGCSE manageable struggle immediately afterwards. The fix is short, unglamorous and effective: non-calculator work on indices, surds and fraction arithmetic, done in short bursts across several weeks rather than in one block. On Cambridge 0580 the calculator is permitted in both papers, so nothing in the exam forces the habit to change.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE maths tutor be matched for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher, usually one to two working days, because the specialist pool for those two is the deepest. Core and Foundation tier matches take two to three days, since fewer tutors choose to specialise there. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 takes three to five working days because the investigation paper narrows the field. Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure 4PM1 can take up to a week. Where nobody suitable is free we give a date, disclose a non-UAE tutor, or say we cannot cover it.

intro.heading: The calendar decides more of this grade than the algebra does
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics has no coursework with either board. Two timed written papers carry the entire grade, which means there is no component where a student quietly banks marks over several weeks. Everything is produced under time pressure on two mornings, and everything that leads to those two mornings is a calendar problem rather than a mathematics problem.

The fixed points for a UAE candidate are published. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series; its February and March series is offered to India only, so a candidate in Abu Dhabi never sits it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

Results dates show the real rhythm. Pearson June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So November functions as a repair series producing a grade the following January, which works for a post-16 place that can hold a conditional and does not work when a firm grade is needed in September.

Before any of that comes the entry, and the entry is where families lose outcomes without noticing. Final entries are submitted months ahead of the papers, and once submitted the tier is fixed for that series: Core or Extended with Cambridge, Foundation or Higher with Pearson. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grade at C and a Pearson Foundation entry caps it at 5. Those decisions have deadlines, and the deadlines pass quietly, usually while everybody is thinking about revision rather than administration.
