sections.heading: The non-calculator paper is where the money goes
paragraphs: If your child sits 0580 and came home with a mock grade below expectation, the probability is high that the loss is concentrated on the non-calculator paper and that the cause is fluency rather than understanding. This is the most common and most tractable problem in IGCSE maths, and it is worth describing precisely because it is also the one most often treated with the wrong remedy.

What it looks like in a marked script: the method is right and the number is wrong. A reverse percentage treated as a forward percentage. A negative sign lost in expanding a bracket. A fraction division turned into a multiplication without flipping. Surds left unsimplified and then marked wrong on the final form. Standard form with the index off by one. Each costs between one and four marks, none of them indicates a gap in understanding, and together across a paper they routinely add up to a grade.

The wrong remedy is to reteach the topics. A student who can explain reverse percentages does not need a lesson on reverse percentages; they need twenty of them under time with a pen and no device. The right remedy is short, repetitive, timed, and boring, which is why tutors who are paid by the hour do not always propose it. Four sessions of mixed non-calculator work, with the errors logged by type rather than by topic, will usually show a measurable change in accuracy, and the log is the thing that tells a parent whether the money is working.

The same logic applies in reverse on the calculator paper. There, marks go missing to premature rounding, to answers written without working, and to calculator technique nobody ever taught - fraction mode, stored values, table mode as a checking tool. Neither problem is content. Both are habits. Habits are cheaper to fix than knowledge, and a family that understands the distinction will spend a fraction of what a family that assumes the worst will spend.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar decides everything about what a family should buy and when. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only, so it has no bearing on an Al Reef child and any page that quotes it to you has not checked.

Work backwards instead of forwards. The written papers are the fixed point. Before them sits the school's internal revision period and the mock window. Before that, and this is the deadline families forget, sits the final entry date, when the tier is locked and the argument about Core or Extended becomes academic. Before that sits the decision itself, which should be made on evidence - one full past paper marked at each tier - rather than on a teacher's instinct in October.

After the papers, the clock keeps running. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A family using November as a resit route is therefore waiting into the new year for a grade, which matters if a sixth-form or university application depends on it. The resit entry itself has its own deadline, usually weeks after results arrive, which is why a resit decision is made in days rather than in weeks.

Two practical rules follow. First, book tutoring against a milestone rather than against a term: ten weeks before the written papers is a meaningful block, a standing slot from September is mostly insurance. Second, take every date from the board's live timetable rather than from a tutoring page. Pearson publishes a provisional timetable ahead of each series and revises it; Cambridge publishes by administrative zone and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or a group room: the arithmetic from Al Reef
paragraphs: The home-tutor question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In-home one-to-one tutoring in Abu Dhabi is a real service, widely available, and for some families the right purchase. Published rates for it run roughly AED 180-500 an hour, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions are advertised at AED 1,599-1,799. What that premium buys is a person in the room: a child who will not open a laptop may well open a book for someone sitting at the table.

What it costs, out past the airport road, is tutor choice. The pool of people willing to drive to Al Reef on a weekday evening is small, and the pool who have taught 0580 Extended non-calculator work to grade-9 standard, or 0607's investigation paper, is smaller still. A family optimising for proximity is choosing from a short list; a family optimising for the paper is choosing from a long one. For maths specifically, where the diagnosis is paper-driven and the work is done on a shared screen with a past paper open, the case for proximity is weaker than in almost any other subject.

IB Gram's position is plain: home visits are not a service we sell anywhere in the UAE - that is offered only in India - and lessons for Al Reef families are delivered one-to-one over live video. Nobody will arrive at an Al Reef address from us. The reason to accept that is not loyalty, it is the trade in the table below: the travel premium removed from the rate, the whole hour spent teaching, a tutor matched to the syllabus code, and a session that can start at 17:00 because nobody is sitting on the airport road.

Group classes are the third option and the one most often bought on price alone. A tuition centre room of six to eight students is cheaper per hour than anything else here, and for a student whose gaps match the room's median it works. For a student with a specific, identifiable weakness - frequency density, bearings, reverse percentages - most of that time is spent watching other people's problems being solved. The honest version of the group-class pitch is that it is good value for broad coverage and poor value for targeted repair.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Maths at IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than most subjects, which makes the honesty boundary easier to state and no less important. A tutor teaches, explains, demonstrates, sets practice, marks it and gives feedback. A tutor does not produce work that is submitted as the student's own. That line is not a house style, it is the condition on which a qualification remains worth having.

In practice the pressure points are specific. Where a syllabus includes an investigation or modelling paper, as 0607 does, a tutor may teach the techniques, work through a published example and critique a student's draft reasoning. A tutor may not supply the investigation. Where a student moves on to IB Diploma Mathematics, the Internal Assessment exploration raises the same question with higher stakes: coaching on topic viability, on mathematical depth and on the criteria is legitimate, and anything resembling an exploration written for the student is a malpractice finding against the child.

This matters commercially because the market is not clean. One operator found in this sector sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a price, to students. A family handing over money for that is buying their child an academic-integrity investigation and risking the qualification itself. Any provider who answers the question will you write it for me with anything other than a flat no should be removed from the shortlist on that basis alone.

Two further boundaries are worth a parent's attention. Official syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards; a tutor should cite and link them rather than hand over reproduced copies. And a tutor should not be described as a current examiner unless that status can be evidenced, nor should examiner status be used to imply any access to marking, boundaries or unseen paper content. None of these is a hard question. All of them are questions worth asking in a first conversation.

sections.heading: ADEK, the permit, and what an Al Reef parent can actually verify
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are supervised by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which the UAE government describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes its own inspection outcomes, which is the place to read a school's rating - not a tutoring page. Dubai's equivalent is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Almost no competitor page in this market names ADEK at all.

Tutoring itself is regulated separately and by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, to government and private-sector employees, to unemployed residents, to university students and to school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Two Abu Dhabi-specific points follow. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. So the offer that sounds most attractive - your child's own maths teacher, privately, for a fee - is the one to decline. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before treating that as settled.

A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal again: in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of that kind and makes no claim to one; it is an online tutor-matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE. What a parent can verify is narrow but real - the permit position of an individual tutor, the school's rating on ADEK's listing, the syllabus on the board's own page, and the timetable on the board's own PDF. That list is short, and it is longer than what most pages in this search result will give you.

sections.heading: Maths, equivalency and the five-subject rule
paragraphs: Families in Al Reef planning a UAE university route eventually meet Ministry of Education equivalency, and maths is usually one of the subjects that decides it. On the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that trips people up is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page currently ranking in this market tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong, and it is the kind of error a family acts on by paying for an extra subject's tutoring. The published rule is five, Arabic and Islamic Education excluded, and the authority's own page is where to confirm it.

On the American track the requirements are structured differently: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics via at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma there is no figure published here and none should be taken from a tutoring page; confirm any IB points threshold on the Ministry's own site or with the emirate's attestation authority.

Two cautions belong with this. Equivalency and attestation are processes a family completes with the authority, not something a tutoring platform performs or guarantees on their behalf - IB Gram describes the rule and points at the official channel, nothing more. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Anyone framing it that way is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process, which is a reason to be sceptical of the rest of what they tell you.

process.title: Send the statement of entry, not a description
process.description: The first useful message from an Al Reef parent contains the syllabus code and the tier - 0580 Extended, 4MA1 Higher, 0607 Core. That single line does more to shape the plan than a paragraph about how the term has gone, because it fixes which papers exist and what the ceiling is.

process.title: A free trial lesson, before anything is paid
process.description: One trial session per student, with no card details taken to book it. The tutor spends it on diagnosis rather than on introduction: a short set of questions across strands, worked while the student explains the reasoning aloud, which is how fluency problems separate themselves from knowledge gaps.

process.title: One past paper, marked by question
process.description: Before the plan exists, a full paper is sat under exam timing and marked question by question, with every lost mark attributed to a strand and an error type. The output is a ranked list of marks at risk. That list is the purchase order for every session after it.

process.title: Hours bought against the list, highest marks first
process.description: Sessions work down the ranked list rather than through the syllabus. A strand worth eighteen marks across two papers is worked before one worth four, regardless of which feels more urgent. Written work is photographed between sessions and marked, so the following hour starts from evidence.

process.title: Re-test, then stop
process.description: After the top items are cleared, a second paper is sat and marked the same way. If the list is clear, the engagement ends rather than continuing on a monthly default. If it is not, the remaining items are re-ranked. Either way a parent sees the same measure twice, which is the only honest progress report available.

process.title: If the specialist is not free, you are told
process.description: Cover for 0607's investigation paper or 0606 calculus is thinner than cover for 0580 Extended. Where no suitable tutor has an evening slot that works from Al Reef, that is stated plainly along with when one is expected, rather than filling the slot with whoever is available.

whyPoints.title: The rate is published, even though it is not ours
whyPoints.description: This page prints the AED bands the UAE market charges, with each band attributed to the competitor or rate table that published it. Three of the six pages ranking for searches like this one publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars - a currency no Abu Dhabi family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Because delivery is online, the tutor is chosen from everyone who teaches 0580, 0607, 0606 or 4MA1 rather than from the smaller group willing to drive out past the airport. For a subject diagnosed from a marked paper and taught on a shared screen, that trade favours the paper every time.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium inside the hour
whyPoints.description: In-home rates in Abu Dhabi are quoted at AED 180-500 an hour partly because driving is inside the figure. Removing the drive removes that component and returns the full sixty minutes to teaching. The session can also start at 17:00 Gulf Standard Time, which an evening drive from Khalifa City cannot reliably manage.

whyPoints.title: Error logs, not progress adjectives
whyPoints.description: Marks lost are recorded by strand and by error type - sign slip, premature rounding, no method shown, question misread. A parent gets a list that changes between two marked papers rather than a sentence about confidence. It is less comfortable reading and considerably more useful.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on the student's own work and produces none of it. Given that at least one operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, the boundary is worth printing rather than assuming. It is also the reason a qualification keeps its value.

whyPoints.title: Short engagements are proposed on purpose
whyPoints.description: A diagnostic block aimed at a named paper is usually the right purchase and is cheaper than the standing retainer a family would otherwise book. Recommending fewer hours is against the commercial interest of an hourly business, which is roughly why so little of this market does it.

faqs.question: How much should an Al Reef family budget per hour for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in the UAE run roughly AED 150-300 an hour. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and Bestimate's rate table puts named IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above. Budget online options start lower - EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65. Those are the market's figures, not an IB Gram price list. For planning, the monthly number matters more than the hourly one: a weekly one-hour session sits around AED 600-1,200 a month in the qualified band.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class better value for my child than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether your child's gaps match the room's. A tuition centre class of six to eight is the cheapest option per hour and works well for broad pre-mock coverage. If the specific problem is frequency density on histograms or three-figure bearings, most of those hours are spent watching other students' problems being solved. The test is simple: if you can name the three strands costing your child marks, buy one-to-one time against them. If you cannot name them, a marked past paper is a cheaper next step than either option.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home maths tutor out past the airport road cost more?
faqs.answer: Because the drive is inside the rate. Al Reef is thirty to forty minutes from the Khalifa City and island clusters where most tutors are based, each way, so a tutor who accepts the run either prices at the upper end of the published AED 180-500 in-home band or fits only one session into the evening and charges accordingly. Tower communities like Al Reem allow three in-home sessions a night because travel is a lift ride. Nothing about that premium relates to how well someone teaches 0580 Extended.

faqs.question: Which 0580 paper is my child most likely losing marks on?
faqs.answer: Statistically the non-calculator paper, and usually for fluency rather than understanding. The marked script shows right method and wrong number: a reverse percentage computed forwards, a sign lost expanding brackets, a fraction division not flipped, standard form with the index off by one. Each costs one to four marks and together they add up to a grade. The remedy is short and dull - timed mixed non-calculator work with errors logged by type - and it is cheaper than reteaching topics the student already understands. Ask for the mock script before buying anything.

faqs.question: Where on my child's paperwork is the maths syllabus code printed?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry from the school carries the syllabus code, and that sheet is the only authoritative answer. Cambridge codes look like 0580, 0607 or 0606; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Maths A is 4MA1 and Further Pure is 4PM1. The difference is not cosmetic: 0580 sits one paper without a calculator, while 4MA1 permits one on both papers, so the preparation differs from the first session. If the school has not issued the statement yet, the head of mathematics will tell you, and it is worth asking before paying for an hour.

faqs.question: Should my child be entered at Core or Extended in Cambridge maths?
faqs.answer: Decide it on evidence, not instinct. Core is capped at grade C and sits a shorter pair of papers; Extended reaches A* and demands more content and more algebraic fluency. The sensible test is one full past paper at each tier, marked properly, before the school's internal entry deadline. A student scoring poorly on Extended but comfortably at Core may finish with a better outcome at Core; a student near the Core ceiling is wasting a grade there. Once final entries are lodged the decision is locked, which is why the paper has to be sat early.

faqs.question: How many weeks of maths tutoring do Al Reef families typically pay for?
faqs.answer: The purchase most families make is a weekly slot from September to June, which is thirty-odd sessions, most of them bought before any diagnosis existed. The purchase that usually works is a block of six to ten sessions timed to the mock result, worked against a ranked list of marks at risk, ending when the list clears. A short block costs a fraction of a year-long retainer. Recommending fewer hours is against the interest of an hourly business, which is part of why this market rarely suggests it.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth paying for alongside 0580?
faqs.answer: It is worth it when the destination needs it. 0606 introduces differentiation, integration, the binomial expansion and the factor and remainder theorems, and it genuinely eases the move into AS Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Schools usually run it as an option set or an after-school class, so teaching time per topic is thin and the support load falls at home. For most families a short block on calculus notation and technique is better value than a standing weekly slot across the whole syllabus.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and physics for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because the overlap is real: rearranging formulae, standard form, graph gradients and unit discipline appear in both and can be taught once. Where the physics requirement is specific - practical and data-handling skills, or a particular paper's extended response style - a second specialist is usually the better purchase even though it complicates the week. What matters more than the number of tutors is that both work to the right syllabus codes and that the sessions are sequenced so the heavier subject sits earlier in the evening.

faqs.question: What happens to our maths sessions during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Session times move. School days shorten across the UAE and household routines shift, so the standard adjustment is to run sessions after Iftar rather than in the late afternoon, or to move them to a weekend slot. Because lessons are delivered online there is no drive to plan around, which makes a post-Iftar slot genuinely workable rather than theoretical. Families who are travelling for part of the month usually pause and resume rather than attempt a reduced schedule, and the plan is rebuilt from the exam date on return.

faqs.question: Does my child need a maths tutor who actually lives in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: For maths, rarely. The subject is diagnosed from a marked past paper and taught on a shared screen with that paper open, so what matters is whether the tutor marks 0580 Extended non-calculator work or 0607 investigations routinely. Insisting on an Abu Dhabi address narrows the pool to people within driving distance of Al Reef, which is a short list. Local knowledge matters for school deadlines and timing, and that is held in the plan rather than in the tutor's postcode. Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time regardless.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to help with assessed maths coursework or an investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the techniques, work through a published example, and give feedback on the student's own draft reasoning. A tutor may not produce the work. That distinction holds for the 0607 investigation and modelling paper and, later, for the IB Diploma Mathematics exploration, where a piece written by someone else is an academic-integrity finding against the student rather than against the tutor. At least one operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Any provider who does not answer this question with a flat refusal should come off the shortlist.

faqs.question: Which five IGCSE subjects does MoE equivalency count for an Al Reef student?
faqs.answer: On the British track a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and maths is almost always one of them. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five. One page currently ranking in this market states that six subjects are required, which is wrong and could cost a family a year of unnecessary tutoring. A further requirement sits above it: one A Level at grade E or better, or two AS Levels at the same grade. Confirm all of it with the Ministry directly.

faqs.question: How can I check that a private maths tutor in Abu Dhabi is permitted to teach?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and covers school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published. Separately, ADEK's ethics rules have been reported as barring school staff from tutoring students enrolled at their own school.

faqs.question: When should we start if the June series is the target?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the written papers rather than forwards from today. A ten-week block before the papers, built on a marked mock script, is a meaningful intervention. Earlier than that, the useful work is the tier decision - one full paper sat at each tier before the school's internal entry deadline - because once final entries are lodged the ceiling is fixed. If you are inside six weeks, the plan narrows to full papers under timing plus the two or three strands carrying the most marks, and it is still worth doing.

faqs.question: What does the free trial maths lesson actually include?
faqs.answer: One session per student, booked without card details, spent on diagnosis rather than introduction. The tutor works a short set of questions across number, algebra, trigonometry and statistics while the student explains the reasoning aloud, which is how a fluency problem separates itself from a knowledge gap. You get back the strands at risk and a view on whether a short block or a longer engagement fits. If the answer is that your child's school marking already covers it, you are told that too.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-reef.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper, then decide what to buy
abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-reef.closingBody: The cheapest useful thing an Al Reef family can do about IGCSE maths costs nothing: find the syllabus code on the statement of entry, get the mock script, and have the lost marks attributed to strands and error types. Everything sensible follows from that list, including the possibility that a short block is enough and a year-long retainer was never needed. Book the free trial lesson, bring the code and the script, and the first conversation will be about which three strands are costing the most marks rather than about how many hours to sell you. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, from after the school run.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-reem-i.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE mathematics to Abu Dhabi students, including Al Reem Island households. Each works to the code the school entered and marks the student's own papers against the published scheme rather than ticking answers.

intro.heading: Most lost marks are not mathematical mistakes
paragraphs: Take any marked International GCSE mathematics paper from an Al Reem Island student scoring in the middle bands and separate the lost marks into two piles. The first pile is mathematics the student cannot do. The second is mathematics the student can do, written down in a way the scheme could not reward: an answer with no working, a correct method abandoned after an arithmetic slip, a value rounded two steps too early, a transformation named without its centre.

In almost every paper we see, the second pile is larger. That is the single most useful thing a parent can know before buying tutoring, because the two piles need completely different interventions. The first needs teaching. The second needs the mark scheme explained, which is quick, mechanical and almost never done, because it is not what tutoring is assumed to be about.

Mark schemes work in a way students are rarely told. Marks are typically split into method marks and accuracy marks, and the method mark is available for a correct approach even when the final number is wrong. Follow-through allows a student who made an error early to still earn marks for correct work afterwards, provided the work is visible. Both of those provisions are generous, and both are invisible to a student who writes only answers because that is what feels efficient under time pressure.

The content side matters too, and it is knowable. Cambridge 0580 at Extended tier covers a defined set of strands, and the supplementary statements marked as Extended-only are where the grade-deciding marks concentrate. Pearson 4MA1 at Higher tier covers substantially the same mathematics in a different order with a different question architecture. Knowing which strand a student is losing in, and on which paper, is a five-minute diagnosis from a marked script for anyone who knows the specification.

None of this is a criticism of schools, which have thirty students and a syllabus to finish. Mark-scheme literacy is the kind of thing that gets taught once in a revision assembly and then assumed. It takes about three sessions of one-to-one work on a student's own scripts to become automatic, and it is the only intervention in this subject that adds no new knowledge and still moves a grade.

The third element is the past-paper protocol, and this is where most revision goes wrong. A student who completes twenty papers without marking them properly has rehearsed their existing habits twenty times over. A student who completes six and marks each one against the published scheme, with the specific reason for every lost mark named, has learned six papers' worth of what the examiner actually rewards. The marking is the lesson. The paper is only the material.

Al Reem Island logistics come at the end, because they are the straightforward part. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled around the island's school run. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Market rates quoted later are published figures from named sources, not our prices.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Two written papers, no coursework, with Core and Extended routes. The Extended route adds supplementary content across every strand: harder algebraic manipulation, function notation and transformations, the sine and cosine rules, vectors and vector geometry, conditional probability, and histograms with unequal class widths. Those supplementary statements are where the marks that separate grades sit.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply to an Abu Dhabi candidate. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, says it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Tiered into Foundation and Higher, with two written papers at each tier. The Higher tier content overlaps heavily with Cambridge Extended, but the architecture differs: longer problem-solving items where the method is not signposted, and more questions where the student must choose an approach rather than follow a part (a) into a part (b).
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the day after. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so read the live version.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics B
programmes.description: A separate single-tier specification rather than a variant of Mathematics A, with a heavier algebraic emphasis and a question style closer to a traditional O Level paper. Entered by fewer schools, which makes it the code most often mistaken for Mathematics A by a tutor who was never told which one applies.
programmes.countryNote: If your child's Abu Dhabi school enters 4MB1, say so in the first message. It is the specification where a mismatch is both easiest to make and most costly, because the past-paper diet is genuinely different and a term of the wrong papers cannot be recovered in the final weeks.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Single tier, taken alongside 0580 by students heading for AS Level or an IB higher level route. Introduces differentiation and integration, the binomial expansion, trigonometric identities, matrices, vectors and functions at a level a year ahead of where most students meet them. Multi-step questions with no intermediate scaffolding are the defining feature.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school offers 0606, and where it is available it is the single best preparation for the jump to AS Level or to Analysis and Approaches at higher level. It is also the scarcest tutoring specialism in this market, in every community.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-reem-i.subjectsIntro: These are the mathematics strands an Al Reem Island Extended or Higher candidate is examined on, written as a tutor would diagnose them: what the strand contains and what the mark scheme rewards inside it.

subjects.name: Number, bounds and limits of accuracy
subjects.description: Standard form, surds, ratio, reverse percentages, compound growth and decay, and upper and lower bounds. In bounds questions involving division, the pairing that produces the maximum is not the one intuition suggests, and the scheme awards method for the correct pairing before any arithmetic.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, algebraic fractions, and rearranging a formula where the subject appears on both sides. The single largest loss area at Extended tier, and almost entirely mechanical. Method marks here are generous: a correct common denominator earns a mark even if the simplification goes wrong.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous systems
subjects.description: Quadratics by factorising, by formula and by completing the square; linear and quadratic simultaneous equations; inequalities and their regions. Students lose accuracy marks for rounding surds too early when the question wants an exact answer, and method marks for not writing the substitution.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, graph sketching and the four transformations. The recurring trap is the sign of a horizontal translation. Transformation description questions award marks per element, so naming the type without the centre or scale factor collects part of the marks and loses the rest.

subjects.name: Trigonometry beyond right angles
subjects.description: Sine rule, cosine rule, area of a triangle using two sides and the included angle, bearings and three-dimensional problems. The scheme awards a method mark for selecting the correct rule, so writing the rule down before substituting is worth marks even on a question that then goes wrong.

subjects.name: Mensuration and similar figures
subjects.description: Arcs, sectors, cones, spheres, and area and volume scale factors for similar shapes. Length, area and volume factors scale differently, and candidates routinely apply the length factor to a volume. The mark scheme separates the scale factor mark from the final value, so the error is partially recoverable if shown.

subjects.name: Vectors and vector geometry
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, addition and scalar multiples, and proofs of collinearity or of a point dividing a line in a given ratio. Short questions with unforgiving notation. The proof marks go to the stated vector route, not to the conclusion, so the conclusion alone earns nothing.

subjects.name: Probability, including conditional cases
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, probability without replacement, and set notation on Venn diagrams. Notation is examinable in its own right, so a candidate who computes correctly from a misread intersection symbol loses the lot. Method marks reward the correct product of branch probabilities before the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Statistics and data presentation
subjects.description: Cumulative frequency curves, interquartile range, box plots, and histograms with unequal class widths. Frequency density is the discriminating step: the division by class width earns its own mark, and skipping it while drawing a plausible bar earns nothing.

subjects.name: Sequences and nth terms
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic and geometric sequences and their general terms. Quadratic nth term questions carry method marks for the second difference step, which means a student who shows the differences and then mis-forms the expression still collects part of the marks.

subjects.name: Calculus (Additional Mathematics 0606)
subjects.description: Differentiation of polynomials and simple composite functions, stationary points and their nature, and integration as the reverse process including definite integrals. A year ahead of where this normally appears, with no partial scaffolding in the questions themselves.

subjects.name: Matrices and further algebra (0606)
subjects.description: Matrix multiplication, determinants and inverses, the binomial expansion, and trigonometric identities used to prove or solve. The identities strand rewards a stated starting identity, so showing which identity was used earns a method mark independently of the manipulation that follows.

sections.heading: How the mark scheme actually awards marks
paragraphs: Mathematics mark schemes do not award a single mark per question. They break a question into steps and allocate marks to those steps, typically distinguishing method marks for a correct approach from accuracy marks for a correct value. The consequence is that a student can earn most of a question's marks while producing the wrong final number, and can earn none of them while having done the mathematics correctly in their head.

Follow-through is the second provision students are rarely told about. Where a candidate makes an error early in a multi-step question and then works correctly from their own incorrect value, the scheme can award the later marks. That is generous, and it is entirely conditional on the working being visible. A student who makes one slip and then writes only a final answer loses every mark after the slip. A student who shows each step loses one.

Description questions work differently again, and they are where Abu Dhabi candidates lose marks most quietly. A transformation description is marked by element: the type of transformation, the centre or vector, and the scale factor or angle of rotation. Naming the type alone earns the element mark for the type and nothing else. Students treat these as one-mark recall questions and give one-third of the required answer.

Exact-answer conventions are the fourth category. Where a question asks for an answer in surd form, or to a given number of significant figures, or in its simplest form, the accuracy mark depends on the convention rather than on the value being close. Rounding at an intermediate step and carrying the rounded figure forward is the most frequent cause of a lost accuracy mark on an otherwise correct solution, and it is purely a habit.

sections.heading: The content map, paper by paper
paragraphs: Both Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 split their content across two papers, and the split is not random: the papers differ in calculator permission and in question length, which changes which strands appear where and how they are tested. Knowing the pattern lets a student allocate revision rather than cover everything twice.

The shorter, structured paper tends to carry a wide spread of topics in brief multi-part questions, which rewards breadth and speed. The longer paper carries fewer questions with more steps each, which rewards sustained working and is where method marks matter most, because there are more steps at which a slip can be followed through. A student who is strong on breadth and weak on sustained multi-step work will show a very different profile across the two papers, and that profile is visible from a marked pair.

At Extended tier the supplementary statements are the thing to find. Cambridge marks parts of each strand as additional content for Extended candidates, and those statements are disproportionately where the grade-deciding questions come from: function notation and composite functions, the sine and cosine rules, vector geometry, conditional probability, histograms with unequal class widths, and harder algebraic fractions. A revision plan that treats the whole syllabus evenly under-weights exactly this material.

The table maps strands against where the marks tend to sit and what each one needs from a candidate. Use it with a marked pair of papers rather than on its own: the diagnosis comes from the scripts, and the map tells you what to do about what the scripts show.

sections.heading: Cambridge Extended and Pearson Higher: the divergence that matters
paragraphs: The two specifications cover close to the same mathematics, which is why families assume the board does not matter. The architecture differs, and the architecture is what a student practises. Cambridge 0580 Extended papers lean towards structured multi-part questions in which part (a) builds the tool that part (b) uses, so the student is scaffolded through a long calculation and the method marks are distributed along a visible path.

Pearson 4MA1 Higher papers include longer items where the method is not signposted at all. The student reads a situation, decides what mathematics applies, and executes it without being told how many steps there are. That is a genuinely different exam skill. A candidate drilled exclusively on Cambridge-style scaffolding can find a Pearson problem-solving item disorienting while being perfectly capable of every technique inside it.

There is a second divergence in what is provided. The formulae supplied in the paper and the conventions around calculator use differ in detail between boards, which changes what a student must commit to memory. This is precisely the sort of thing that never surfaces in a tutoring conversation and costs marks in the hall. A tutor working to the code knows it; a tutor working to the idea of Year 11 maths does not.

Pearson's Mathematics B specification, 4MB1, diverges further again, with a heavier algebraic emphasis and a question style closer to a traditional O Level paper. It is a separate specification rather than a variant, and it is the code most often confused with Mathematics A. If your Abu Dhabi school enters 4MB1, the past-paper diet has to be 4MB1 from the first session.

sections.heading: The past-paper protocol
paragraphs: Past papers are the most recommended and least well used resource in International GCSE mathematics. The default pattern is to complete a paper, check the answers, feel reassured by the ones that were right and vaguely troubled by the ones that were not, and move on. That process produces practice without learning, and a student can repeat it twenty times with no change in grade.

The protocol that works has four steps and takes ninety minutes rather than sixty. The paper is sat under genuine conditions: timed to the real duration, no notes, calculator rules respected, and on a non-calculator paper genuinely without one. Then it is marked together against the published scheme, question by question. Then the reason for every lost mark is named specifically, not as carelessness but as the actual failure: the method was not written, the rounding happened too early, the description gave the type and omitted the centre. Then the two costliest items go on a ranked list.

The list is the artefact. It is updated after each paper, and across six weeks it should visibly shorten. If it does not, the diagnosis is wrong rather than the student lazy, and the plan should change. Asking a tutor to show you that list is a far better question than asking how the sessions are going, because the list is evidence and the answer to the other question is always positive.

A boundary on materials belongs here. We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They belong to the boards, are published through the boards' own channels and reach students through their school. A tutor's role is to teach a student to use those documents, not to hand over copies, and a provider offering a downloadable library of mark schemes is offering something that is not theirs to give.

sections.heading: Calculator discipline and what has to be memorised
paragraphs: A graphical or scientific calculator is a mark-losing device in the hands of a student who has not been taught to record method. On a calculator-permitted paper, a candidate can compute a correct answer in one keystroke sequence, write the number, and collect the accuracy mark while forfeiting the method marks that were available for showing the substitution. On a long question that is the difference between full marks and two out of five.

The discipline is simple and has to be practised rather than explained once. Write the rule or formula. Write the substitution with the actual values. Then compute. Keep full precision in the calculator memory and round only on the final line, to the form the question asked for. Students resist this because it feels slower, and under time pressure it is marginally slower, which is why it has to become automatic before the examination rather than being attempted during it.

There is also the question of what the paper supplies. Each board provides some formulae in the paper and expects others to be memorised, and the lists differ. A student who has assumed the cosine rule will be printed and finds it is not has lost a whole question for a reason that has nothing to do with mathematics. The only reliable answer is to check the front matter of a real past paper for your own specification, which takes two minutes.

For a non-calculator component, the discipline is different again: the arithmetic and algebraic fluency the paper assumes has to be built by short repeated practice over months, not weeks. A student who has done every exercise with a screen in front of them has never built it, and that gap is cheap to close in Year 10 and expensive to close in the final term of Year 11.

sections.heading: Reading a marked paper like a tutor
paragraphs: Parents can do a useful first pass on this themselves, and it takes fifteen minutes. Take the marked script and look first at the shape rather than the score. Are the losses clustered in two or three strands, or scattered as single marks across the whole paper? Clustered losses mean a bounded repair of a few sessions. Scattered single-mark losses usually mean something structural: method not being written, rounding habits, or timing.

Second, look at the final questions. Were they attempted? A paper where the last two questions are blank while earlier ones are heavily worked is a timing problem, and timing problems are fixed by practising question order and allocation rather than by learning more mathematics. A paper where the final questions were attempted and scored poorly is a content problem in the strands those questions came from.

Third, look for answers standing alone. Every bare final answer on a multi-step question is a place where method marks were available and forfeited. Count them. On a mid-band paper the total is often substantial, and it is the cheapest tranche of marks available to that student, because they already know the mathematics involved.

Fourth, look at the description and explanation questions specifically. Count how many elements the scheme wanted and how many the student gave. Transformation descriptions, reasons in geometry, and statements about what a statistic means are all element-marked, and students consistently supply the first element and stop. This is the pattern that a single mark-scheme literacy block fixes, which is why it is the block we most often recommend first.
bullets: Clustered losses mean a short repair; scattered losses mean something structural

sections.heading: The series, and when the paper work has to happen
paragraphs: UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting it at an Abu Dhabi parent has the wrong country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. The school's entry decides which applies, and the exams officer can confirm both the series and the centre's administrative zone.

The protocol described on this page has a cost in hours, and that cost has to be budgeted in advance. A full paper sat and then marked properly is roughly one ninety-minute session plus part of another, so six papers with their marking is nearer ten sessions than six. At two sessions a week that is five weeks, and it has to sit inside a term that also contains five other subjects' revision.

Working backwards from a June sitting, that means the paper block is booked in the spring term as a decision rather than assembled afterwards from whatever time remains. Mocks fall in the spring term and are the trigger for the ranked list, not for starting to think about one. For a November sitting the pattern shifts: the Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026.

Official timetables get revised and Pearson publishes provisional versions ahead of each series, so read the live timetable on the board's own site rather than any date restated on a tutoring page, including this one. Cambridge is explicit that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's own risk, which makes the zone a question worth asking the school rather than assuming.

faqs.question: What does a mark scheme reward that my child might be missing?
faqs.answer: Three things, usually. Method marks, which are awarded for a correct approach even when the final value is wrong, and which are forfeited entirely by a student who computes mentally and writes only an answer. Follow-through, which allows later marks after an early error provided every step is visible. And element-marked descriptions, where a transformation answer needs the type, the centre or vector, and the scale factor or angle, and supplying only the type collects one element's mark and loses the others.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's maths problem is knowledge or technique?
faqs.answer: Separate the lost marks on a marked script into two piles: mathematics they cannot do, and mathematics they can do but wrote down in a way the scheme could not reward. In most mid-band scripts the second pile is larger. Bare final answers on multi-step questions, intermediate rounding carried forward, and incomplete descriptions all belong to the second pile, and all of them are fixed mechanically rather than by more teaching.

faqs.question: Which Extended topics carry the grade-deciding marks at Cambridge 0580?
faqs.answer: The supplementary statements, which Cambridge marks as additional content for Extended candidates. In practice that means function notation and composite functions, the sine and cosine rules with area using two sides and an included angle, vector geometry and collinearity proofs, conditional probability, histograms with unequal class widths, and the harder algebraic fractions and rearrangements. A revision plan that covers the whole syllabus evenly systematically under-weights exactly this material.

faqs.question: Why does rounding too early cost marks in an IGCSE maths paper?
faqs.answer: Because the accuracy mark depends on the value being correct in the form the question required, and a figure rounded at an intermediate step and carried forward drifts. The fix is purely habitual: keep full precision in the calculator's memory, work to the final line, and round only there, to the stated significant figures or exact form. It is one of the few corrections that costs no additional knowledge and reliably recovers marks on otherwise correct solutions.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Year 11 student actually do?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most revision plans assume, and marked properly. Six papers sat under genuine conditions and then marked together against the published scheme, with the specific reason for every lost mark named, teaches more than twenty papers whose answers were checked against a list. The marking is the lesson and the paper is only the material. Six papers with their marking is nearer ten ninety-minute sessions than six, which is the budget to plan for.

faqs.question: Does the exam board really change how my child should revise?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the question architecture differs even where the content matches. Cambridge 0580 Extended papers often scaffold a long calculation through parts (a) and (b), so method marks sit along a visible path. Pearson 4MA1 Higher includes longer items with no signposting, where the student must choose an approach unprompted. A candidate drilled only on one style finds the other disorienting while being capable of every technique in it. Past papers must come from the entered board only.

faqs.question: What is Pearson 4MB1 and why does the code matter so much?
faqs.answer: Mathematics B is a separate single-tier specification rather than a variant of Mathematics A, with a heavier algebraic emphasis and a question style closer to a traditional O Level paper. It is entered by fewer schools, which makes it the code most often mistaken for 4MA1 by a tutor who was never told which applies. The consequence of the mistake is a term of practice on genuinely different papers, which cannot be recovered in the final weeks.

faqs.question: My child leaves the last questions blank. Is that a knowledge gap?
faqs.answer: Usually not. A script with heavily worked early questions and blank final ones is a timing problem, and timing problems are fixed by practising question order and time allocation rather than by learning more content. The diagnostic is simple: if the final questions are attempted and score poorly, it is content in those strands. If they are untouched while earlier questions are over-worked, the student never reached them, which is a different fix entirely.

faqs.question: Should sessions be sixty or ninety minutes for IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Ninety for paper work, sixty for everything else. A paper sat under conditions plus its marking does not fit into sixty minutes, and cutting the marking defeats the purpose, because the marking is where the learning happens. Sixty minutes suits strand repair, where the material is a focused topic, and mark-scheme literacy sessions built on scripts the student already has. Choose the purpose first and the duration follows from it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram teach at Al Reem Island apartments?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, including Al Reem Island; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, which also suits the protocol on this page: a paper can be annotated on a shared screen and the marked version kept, so the worked correction to a question that defeated a student in February is still available in May.

faqs.question: What time can a ninety-minute maths session start for an Al Reem Island student?
faqs.answer: A student at a campus on or near the island is often home by about 15:50, which makes a 16:30 start workable and leaves room for ninety minutes before dinner. A student commuting to the Khalifa City or Al Raha corridor is typically not home before 16:15, so 17:30 is the honest earliest and 18:00 is more durable. Our Abu Dhabi range runs 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and a late school finish moves a session rather than cancelling it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor tell us the grade boundaries for this series?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should. Grade boundaries are set by the boards after each series and published through their own channels, and no tutoring page should restate them or predict them. What a tutor can usefully do is work in raw marks: say how many marks a named habit is costing across a paper, and track whether that number is falling. That is actionable, checkable and does not depend on a boundary figure that nobody outside the board knows in advance.

faqs.question: Can you supply mark schemes and past papers for us to keep?
faqs.answer: No, and be cautious of anyone who offers a library of them as a download. Cambridge, Pearson and IB syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, are published through the boards' own channels, and reach students through their school. We cite and link them. The skill worth teaching is how to read a mark scheme critically, which outlasts any file a student could be handed.

faqs.question: Which Additional Mathematics topics does an Abu Dhabi 0606 candidate find hardest?
faqs.answer: Differentiation of composite functions and the nature of stationary points, integration as a reverse process with definite integrals, and the trigonometric identities strand where a proof has to start from a stated identity. The common factor is that 0606 questions are multi-step and give no intermediate scaffolding, so a student who is comfortable in 0580 Extended can still stall. Stating the identity or the rule first is worth a method mark independently of what follows.

faqs.question: What is the single cheapest improvement available to a mid-band candidate?
faqs.answer: Writing the method down. A mid-band script typically contains a substantial number of bare final answers on multi-step questions, and each one represents method marks that were available and forfeited on mathematics the student already knew. Teaching rule, then substitution, then computation, with rounding only on the final line, is a three-session job. It adds no knowledge and recovers marks immediately, which is why it is usually the first block we recommend.

intro.heading: The expensive decisions in IGCSE maths are not hourly rates
paragraphs: A family in Al Samha pricing IGCSE mathematics help will find the hourly rate easy to compare and almost everything else invisible. The rates, read in October 2026, are these. Budget online tuition, often delivered by university students: AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online: AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one with travel inside the rate: AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500. Specialists: AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium examiner-led tuition: AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Those numbers are worth having, and three of the six most visible competitors in this market publish none of them. But the decisions that actually move the total spend sit elsewhere. A tier entry that caps the grade below what the sixth form requires creates remedial cost that no hourly rate reflects. A resit adds a term of work in a year when the student has already started something else. A year of weekly sessions bought when six targeted ones would have done is the most common overspend in this subject, and it is invisible because the sessions are perfectly competent.

Geography adds one specific cost here. Al Samha sits in the north of the emirate off the Dubai road, and an in-home tutor coming from the city prices a journey of forty minutes or more each way. That is inside the quoted rate, and it is time nobody is taught in. For the same money an online arrangement buys more teaching and a wider choice of tutor, which in a subject where the syllabus code matters is the more useful trade.

There is also the cheapest route of all, which a page about cost should mention before any rate table. The maths teacher who marks your child's work already knows the gap. School departments run clinics, often unadvertised. The mock paper breakdown is a written diagnosis the family already owns. A classmate on the same code and tier is free. Two cycles of self-marked past papers will tell you whether paid help is needed and for what. The order matters: exhaust the free routes first, because they also tell you what to brief a paid tutor on.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-samha.subjectsIntro: Each item below is a thing families actually pay for, with a realistic session count attached. The counts are what make a budget possible.

subjects.name: Histograms with unequal class widths
subjects.description: Frequency density forgotten, so the whole question falls. Two sessions with a before and after test, and typically two to four marks a paper recovered. One of the clearest returns available in the subject.

subjects.name: Reverse percentages
subjects.description: Multiplying by 0.8 where the question requires dividing by 1.2. One session of structured practice fixes it permanently, and it appears in every series, which makes it among the cheapest marks a family can buy.

subjects.name: Bounds and accuracy
subjects.description: Rounding a bound and so defeating the question, or taking the lower bound where the upper is needed. One to two sessions, procedural, with a rule the student can apply without judgement.

subjects.name: Tree diagrams without replacement
subjects.description: The second denominator left unchanged, taking every later mark with it. Two sessions, and three to four marks commonly at stake in a single question, which is a strong return for a small block.

subjects.name: Transformation descriptions
subjects.description: Naming a rotation without centre or direction and forfeiting the attached marks. One session plus a checklist, and the marks come back immediately because the understanding was never missing.

subjects.name: Method-mark discipline
subjects.description: Writing the setup before evaluating on a calculator paper, so marks survive a wrong final value. One session plus a month of enforcement, and it protects marks across every paper the student sits.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency
subjects.levels: Where a non-calculator paper is sat
subjects.description: Fractions, index laws, surds and standard form at speed. Built in fifteen-minute timed blocks inside wider sessions, so it adds no extra cost, and it removes the arithmetic drag that causes students to abandon final questions.

subjects.name: Pacing and paper strategy
subjects.description: Leaving a stuck question and returning, and treating the last ten marks as reachable. Two sessions of timed sections, and often the single largest recoverable block for a student who understands the content.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Sign errors in subtracted brackets, factorising and algebraic fractions. Three to five sessions of mechanical practice rather than explanation, because the failure is procedural rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Genuine content gaps
subjects.description: Whole question types the student has never been able to attempt. This is the expensive category: a term of weekly work rather than a block, because the material is new rather than mislearnt. Worth identifying early precisely because it costs more.

subjects.description: Two to three sessions working past papers from both tiers and marking them honestly, producing written evidence a parent can take to the maths department. Cheap, bounded, and capable of preventing a far larger cost later.

subjects.description: Four to six sessions on the school's own paper styles before the mock window. Bounded and dated, which makes it easy to budget for, and it feeds the predicted grade a sixth form may act on.

sections.heading: The cheapest route to the grade, in the order it should be tried
paragraphs: Answering the search directly: an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Samha, through IB Gram, means a specialist matched to your child's syllabus code and tier, teaching one-to-one over live video at a time that fits the bus, with a free trial lesson used as a diagnosis. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, where the market rate here is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included.

The cheapest effective route is a sequence rather than a purchase. Start with the mock paper breakdown, which is a written diagnosis the family already owns and which names the papers and question types that lost marks. Ask the maths teacher for the two topics to prioritise. Attend the department clinic if there is one, because it happens before the bus leaves and costs no evening. Have the student mark one past paper strictly against the published scheme and classify every lost mark.

After that sequence, most families know exactly what they need, and in this subject it is usually a short list of procedural failures rather than a general absence of understanding. A student losing three or four marks a paper to histograms, reverse percentages and unwritten method lines needs perhaps six sessions in total. At the published qualified band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, that is a defined and modest spend with a measurable outcome.

The alternative, which is what most families actually buy, is a year of weekly sessions starting in September and ending with the series. Those sessions are usually competent and the student usually improves, but nobody can say which part of the improvement the money bought, and the total is several times the targeted figure. Naming that difference is the main purpose of this page.

sections.heading: What a wrong tier entry costs, and why it is the largest avoidable expense
paragraphs: Tier entry is made by the school as the examination centre and it sets a ceiling the student cannot pass however well the papers go. Cambridge Core caps the grades available below the top of the A* to G scale; Pearson Foundation tops out at grade 5, with Higher running 9 down to 4 and grade 3 available as a safety net. Those ceilings are not academic abstractions; they are the single largest avoidable cost in this subject.

Consider the sequence that follows a tier set too low. The student performs well, achieves the ceiling grade, and finds it below the entry requirement for the post-16 course they want. The remedies are all expensive: a November resit on the higher tier with a term of preparation while starting a new course, a change of post-16 plan, or a year repeated. Any of those costs more than the entire tutoring budget that preceded it.

A tier set too high has a different cost. A student who accesses few marks on the harder paper gains nothing from it and may finish with a weaker result than a confident performance at the lower tier would have produced. The money spent trying to stretch them to a paper they could not reach is money spent on the wrong target, and nobody involved notices until the results arrive.

The preventive spend is small. Two or three sessions working past papers from both tiers, marked honestly against the published schemes, produce written evidence a parent can take to the maths department while a change is still administratively possible. In Year 10 that evidence is actionable; in the spring of Year 11 it usually is not. This is the clearest case in the subject where a small early purchase prevents a large later one.

sections.heading: Group class, one-to-one and online: price against attention
paragraphs: A group class is genuinely cheaper per hour and genuinely less attention per student, so the comparison has to be made in both units at once. Tuition centres advertise group rates well below one-to-one bands, and for broad content coverage in a subject a student is simply behind in, a small group can work perfectly well.

Where a group stops working is the diagnostic part, which in IGCSE mathematics is most of the value. A tutor cannot mark one student's paper against the scheme and classify their individual error pattern while running a class of eight. The group gets the content; the individual gets whatever is left. For a student whose problem is a specific set of recurring failures, a group class is cheap and largely irrelevant.

There is also a regulatory dimension worth knowing before paying a centre. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained through initial approval first, with a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Ask a centre what it holds, and ask the group size before agreeing to anything.

The in-home column is the most expensive per unit of attention from this corridor, because the rate includes a journey of forty minutes or more each way and the start time is at the mercy of the road. Online one-to-one sits in the middle on price and at the top on usable attention, which is the argument for it stated without embellishment.

sections.heading: What a November resit actually costs, counted properly
paragraphs: A resit looks like an entry fee and a few weeks of revision. Counted properly it is more, and a family deciding in late August should see the whole figure rather than the visible part. Cambridge offers a November series as the resit route for a UAE candidate, and Pearson runs November as well as May and June; the November 2026 Pearson final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

The costs break into four. There is the entry itself, arranged through the school as the examination centre, so ask the examinations officer what applies in your case. There is the preparation, realistically a term of targeted work, which at the qualified band is a defined but non-trivial figure. There is the time cost, which is the real one: the resit term coincides with the start of a post-16 course, and in this corridor with the long bus run restored, so the hours have to come from somewhere already full.

The fourth is the opportunity cost of a resit that repeats the first attempt. If the preparation is the same as last time, the result usually is too. That is why the decision should be made from the component breakdown: which paper, which question types, and whether two or three specific fixes would plausibly cross the boundary. A breakdown showing marks lost to pacing and method lines points to a resit worth doing; one showing whole question types untouched points to a longer problem.

Weigh it against the alternatives honestly. Sometimes the right answer is a resit. Sometimes it is accepting the grade and choosing a post-16 route that takes it. Occasionally it is a different subject combination entirely. A provider that treats every resit as obviously worth selling preparation for has not done that arithmetic with the family.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths money disappears without producing marks
paragraphs: Six patterns account for most of the wasted spend in this subject, and they are different from the Diploma versions because the assessment is terminal rather than spread across two years.

The first is buying a year when six sessions would do. A student with three recurring procedural errors needs those errors fixed, not a weekly slot from September to June. The second is buying before the evidence exists: hiring in September on the basis of a feeling, rather than after the mock breakdown has named the papers and question types. The third is paying for content when the problem is pacing. A student who understands the material and abandons the last ten marks needs timed practice, not more teaching.

The fourth is two tutors in the same subject, which happens more often than families admit and produces contradictory methods that confuse a student under time pressure. The fifth is revision materials sold as a product. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are published by Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or redistributing them is a copyright matter, so any materials line on an invoice deserves a question. The sixth is an examination-skills course with no individual marking in it: generic technique advice is free on every board's own site, and the value is in somebody marking this student's paper.

All six are prevented the same way. Get the breakdown, name the targets, agree a session count, and set an exit criterion. That costs one free lesson and a short conversation, and it is the difference between a measurable purchase and a monthly habit.

sections.heading: The free diagnosis most families already own
paragraphs: The mock examination breakdown is the most valuable document in a Year 11 family's possession and it is routinely filed away unread. It names the papers sat, the marks lost in each, and in many schools the question-level detail behind them. That is a diagnosis produced by the people who teach your child, at no additional cost, and it is better evidence than a first paid session can generate.

Ask the examinations officer or the head of mathematics for the component breakdown rather than the grade. The grade tells you where the student stands; the breakdown tells you why, which is the part that determines what to buy. Then ask the teacher one specific question: which two question types would you prioritise. A specific question gets a specific answer, where a general request for feedback gets reassurance.

Add to that the department's own support. Clinics, surgeries and lunchtime help exist in most schools and are frequently unadvertised, and in this corridor they have the additional advantage of happening before the bus leaves, which means they cost no evening time at all. For a family where travel already consumes the week, that makes school-based help the highest-value hour available anywhere.

Then there is the free work the student can do alone: one past paper, attempted under timing, marked strictly against the published scheme, with every lost mark classified by topic and type. Two cycles of that and the family knows what paid help should target and roughly how much of it is needed. Recommending this sequence reduces what families spend with us, and it is the right order because a purchase made after it is a purchase that works.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost beside the other costs of the year
paragraphs: Families judge tutoring against the school fee rather than against other tutors, and that comparison is worth assembling properly. Write down the annual school fee, the annualised tutoring commitment at the tier under consideration, and what each is expected to deliver. Most families have never seen the second figure annualised, which is why a modest-looking hourly rate can become a surprising yearly total.

For context on the wider market: Dubai's private school sector in 2024-25 enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum students accounting for 37% of enrolment and the International Baccalaureate 7%. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Abu Dhabi fees are regulated separately by ADEK.

Those figures matter for a cost page in one specific way: they show that the British curriculum is the largest single cohort in this market, which means IGCSE tutoring is the most competitive and most heavily marketed segment of it. A parent is therefore being sold to more aggressively here than anywhere else in the education market, and the defence is the same as always: evidence first, targets second, session counts third.

One final caution. Tutoring is not required for school progression, for Ministry of Education equivalency or for university admission, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. Equivalency is administered by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, should be verified on their own pages, and is not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or speeds up.
