sections.heading: What money cannot buy here
paragraphs: No tutor can guarantee a grade. The result depends on a student's own work on a specific morning, and any guarantee offered should end the conversation rather than reassure. The same applies to a published success rate, satisfaction percentage or average score with no sample size, date or method behind it: that is a marketing device, and pages in this market show review totals that contradict each other within a single screen.

No provider should supply assessed work. IGCSE mathematics in the mainstream syllabuses has no coursework component, which removes the temptation, but the principle holds across every subject a family might buy help in: a tutor teaches, explains and gives feedback on work the student produced. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments to Diploma students, which is malpractice under IB rules and puts the student's own declaration in question.

No individual tutor is approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, because those bodies regulate schools rather than approving tutors. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them and has no UAE office. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific permit with a number that can be asked for.

And no amount of money buys compliance with the permit rules on a family's behalf. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years to a defined set of applicants. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, no fine schedule is published, and because the permit is free there is no cost reason for a working tutor to lack one.

faqs.question: What is the going rate for an IGCSE maths tutor in northern Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Read in October 2026, a qualified subject tutor working online is published at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online options run AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel included, and from this corridor that travel component is large. These are market figures from named sources rather than IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to fix one recurring maths error?
faqs.answer: Two or three for most procedural failures, with a before and after test on past-paper questions to confirm it has gone. Histograms with unequal class widths, reverse percentages, bounds, tree diagrams without replacement and incomplete transformation descriptions all fall into that category. A student losing three or four marks a paper to two or three such errors therefore needs about six sessions in total, which is a defined and modest spend rather than a monthly commitment.

faqs.question: What does it cost if the school enters my child on the wrong tier?
faqs.answer: More than the entire tutoring budget that preceded it. If the tier caps the grade below the sixth-form requirement, the remedies are a November resit with a term of preparation while starting a new course, a changed post-16 plan, or a repeated year. If the tier is set too high the student accesses few marks and gains nothing. Two or three diagnostic sessions in Year 10, producing written past-paper evidence for the department, is the cheap preventive purchase.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a centre better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour and less useful for the part that matters most. A group can cover content perfectly well for a student who is simply behind. What it cannot do is mark your child's paper against the scheme and classify their individual error pattern, which in IGCSE mathematics is where most of the value sits. Ask the group size before agreeing, and ask the centre what permit it holds; in Dubai an operation with premises needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute.

faqs.question: When is the right time to start paying for help in Year 11?
faqs.answer: After the mock breakdown exists, in most cases. Hiring in September on the basis of a feeling means several months aimed at whatever seems hardest rather than at what is actually losing marks. The breakdown names the papers and question types, and a self-marked paper confirms the pattern. The exception is a known content gap carried from Year 10, which is slow to close and therefore worth starting early rather than discovering in the spring.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home tutor cost more out here than in the city?
faqs.answer: Because travel is inside the rate and the journey from the city to this corridor is forty minutes or more each way, often into late-afternoon traffic. Published in-home bands are AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor. Some tutors decline the distance rather than price it, which leaves a northern family with a shorter list of willing tutors than a search suggests, and a higher chance that the available ones have not taught the right code.

faqs.question: Is a prepaid block of maths sessions worth it?
faqs.answer: Only if nothing expires and the sessions are genuinely used. Advertised monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions, which is good value if eight sessions get used and poor value if three do. Ask three questions before paying: does anything expire, what happens if we stop after one session, and who absorbs a late cancellation. A provider with clean answers to all three is less common than it should be.

faqs.question: What does a November resit really add up to?
faqs.answer: Four things. The entry, arranged through the school as examination centre, so ask the examinations officer what applies. A term of targeted preparation at the chosen band. The time cost, which in this corridor means finding hours in a term that already contains a new post-16 course and a restored bus run. And the risk that preparation identical to the first attempt reproduces the result. Decide from the component breakdown rather than from how the results felt.

faqs.question: Our child understands the maths but runs out of time. What should we buy?
faqs.answer: Timed practice, not more teaching, and it is one of the cheaper purchases available. Two sessions working sections against the clock, learning to leave a stuck question and return to it, and treating the final ten marks as reachable rather than lost. Paying for additional content delivery when the problem is pacing is one of the most common overspends in this subject, because the student appears to need teaching and actually needs a strategy.

faqs.question: Should we add a second tutor if progress feels slow?
faqs.answer: No. Two tutors in one subject produces contradictory methods that confuse a student under time pressure, and it doubles the cost while reducing clarity. If progress is genuinely slow after six to eight weeks, the right response is to re-examine the diagnosis and, if necessary, change the tutor rather than add one. A provider willing to be replaced is more useful than one willing to be supplemented.

faqs.question: Are revision guides and past paper packs worth paying for?
faqs.answer: Not from a tutor. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are published by Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or redistributing them is a copyright matter; the school can also provide them. If materials appear as a line item on an invoice, ask exactly what is being sold. What is worth paying for is somebody marking your child's paper against the scheme and classifying the losses, which is a service rather than a document.

faqs.question: After six weeks of IGCSE maths sessions, what evidence should show the spend is working?
faqs.answer: A fresh past paper, marked strictly against the published scheme, with the lost marks classified and compared against the original log. If the logged failures have gone, the money worked and the recommendation should be fewer sessions. If the distribution looks the same, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan should be redone rather than continued. Progress measured by how sessions feel is not evidence, and it is how a term passes without anything changing.

faqs.question: Can a technique or exam-skills course replace one-to-one help?
faqs.answer: Rarely, because generic technique advice is published free by the boards themselves and the value lies in somebody applying it to this student's paper. Before paying for such a course, ask one question: who marks my child's work, and how often. If the answer is nobody, or occasionally, the course is selling content that is already available at no cost. If it includes individual marking against the scheme, it may be worth the fee.

faqs.question: Under what circumstances would you advise cancelling the IGCSE maths sessions?
faqs.answer: When a fresh marked paper shows the logged failures have gone, which is the stated exit criterion for every block. Also when the diagnosis points elsewhere: a tier that needs changing rather than teaching, a pacing problem solvable in two sessions, a student too tired after a long bus run to use another commitment, or a gap the school's own clinic can close for nothing. A provider that never reaches that point is selling attendance rather than teaching.

What distinguishes a one-to-one arrangement from the cheaper models on this page is the marking of written work between sessions, which is where the grade movement comes from.

intro.heading: Six products, one search term
paragraphs: Search for maths help in Abu Dhabi and you will be offered six genuinely different things under roughly the same words. A group class at a tuition centre. A freelance tutor who visits. A booking through an international marketplace. A specialist agency arrangement. A low-cost online platform. And whatever intervention class the school itself runs. The prices differ by a factor of more than ten, and so does what you receive, but the advertising language is nearly identical across all six.

Al Shamkha is a settled mainland villa district on the south-eastern side of Abu Dhabi, roughly half an hour from the island on a clear afternoon run and longer when it is not. That geography matters for this comparison in one specific way: the models that involve somebody travelling are more expensive and less available here than they are in the island communities, so a family in Al Shamkha is pushed towards either the cheapest options or the online ones. Choosing between those on price alone is how the money gets wasted.

The useful way to compare is by asking what is included beyond the hour itself. That is where the models separate. A group class includes a teacher and a room and excludes any individual diagnosis. A marketplace booking includes a tutor's time and usually nothing between sessions. A specialist arrangement should include a written diagnosis, marked written work against the published scheme, and a stated review point. The hourly rate tells you very little; the inclusion list tells you nearly everything.

The second thing worth establishing is what kind of maths problem your child actually has, because the models are not equally good at the same faults. A procedural gap — frequency density, scale factors, rounding discipline — can be repaired in a group class if the teacher happens to cover it. A gap in underlying algebraic fluency cannot, because it requires volume of individually marked practice that no group format produces. Matching the model to the fault is the whole decision.

Delivery here, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Shamkha or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. From a mainland address that removes the travel loading and the travel risk, and it widens the choice of tutor from whoever will drive out here to everyone who can teach the specification.

What follows is the comparison itself with published figures and their sources, a table on group versus one-to-one by scenario, the five places money reliably disappears, the permit position for centres with premises, how sitting the papers as a private candidate actually works, a direct comparison of three mainland addresses, and the boundaries we work inside.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Two written papers, tiered Core and Extended, with one paper sat without a calculator and a defined list of formulae to recall. Extended adds functions, vectors and harder trigonometry. The grade range runs A* to E at Extended and C to G at Core, so the tier sets a ceiling before any teaching happens.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most common entry at British-curriculum schools in the emirate, which is why generic group classes are usually pitched at it. A student on any other specification sitting in that class is receiving teaching aimed at somebody else's paper, and the mismatch is invisible until a mock.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Two papers of two hours, equally weighted, calculator permitted throughout, formula sheet supplied, graded on the nine to one numerical scale with Higher covering nine to four. The skill rewarded is fast and accurate formula selection rather than recall, which is a different revision diet from the Cambridge route.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes its timetables and results schedule well in advance: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates matter for resits and application deadlines.

programmes.name: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607
programmes.description: A separate Cambridge specification built around the graphic display calculator, with investigation work at Extended tier. Not an easier or harder version of 0580 but a different design, which means calculator fluency is a taught skill from the beginning rather than an afterthought.
programmes.countryNote: The specification least well served by group teaching in this market, because very few generic classes are built around it. A family in Al Shamkha whose school uses 0607 should ask any provider directly whether they have taught it, and treat a vague answer as a no.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: An optional second qualification taken alongside Extended 0580 by students heading for A Level or Diploma mathematics. Early calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and harder trigonometry, both papers calculator-permitted, taught in a fast small set where one is offered.
programmes.countryNote: Almost never available as a group class anywhere in the emirate, because the cohort is too small to fill a room. For an Al Shamkha family this is the clearest case where one-to-one is not a premium choice but the only format in which the subject can be bought at all.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-shamkh.subjectsIntro: These are the faults that bring Al Shamkha families to this search, with an honest note on which provider model can actually repair each one. The distinction between procedural and fluency faults runs through all of them.

subjects.name: Frequency density and histograms
subjects.description: A procedural gap, mechanical once taught. Repairable in a group class if the teacher happens to cover it, and reliably repairable in one session of one-to-one work. One of the highest-yield single lessons in the whole syllabus.

subjects.name: Scale factors in similar shapes and solids
subjects.description: Another procedural gap: one rule about linear, area and cubed relationships. Any competent format fixes this, which makes it a poor reason to buy specialist tuition and a good reason to ask what else is wrong.

subjects.name: Algebraic fluency and rearrangement
subjects.description: A fluency gap, and the one no group format repairs. It requires volume of individually marked short exercises over months rather than explanation, which is why it is a Year 9 and Year 10 problem and an expensive Year 11 one.

subjects.name: Rounding and accuracy discipline
subjects.description: A habit rather than a gap. Students round intermediate values and carry the error into the final answer, losing accuracy marks on correct method. One instruction, consistently enforced across marked work, ends it.

subjects.name: Command terms and what each requires
subjects.description: Procedural and almost never taught explicitly. A question saying 'show that' wants a derivation; substituting the printed value back in scores nothing. Correctable in two sessions and worth more than most topic teaching.

subjects.name: Three-dimensional trigonometry
subjects.description: Partly conceptual. The first move is always to extract and redraw the single relevant triangle, and students who try to reason inside the solid rarely start. A group class can demonstrate this; only marked practice embeds it.

subjects.name: Probability without replacement
subjects.description: Procedural, with a specific trap in the changing denominator. Fifteen minutes of correctly drawn and labelled tree diagrams usually settles it, in any format, which again makes it a poor standalone reason to buy a term of tuition.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic and exact form
subjects.description: Specification-dependent and therefore the clearest example of why the model must know the code. A Pearson candidate drilled on this is wasting hours; a Cambridge candidate who skips it loses a paper's worth of fluency.

subjects.name: Vectors in column form
subjects.description: A translation problem as much as a mathematical one: students write geometric sentences where the mark scheme wants a vector route. Responds to marked written work, which is exactly what the cheaper models do not include.

subjects.name: Timing and question selection
subjects.description: Worth more marks than several topics and addressed by none of the cheaper models, because it requires full papers sat to the clock and marked against the published scheme. Four timed papers usually reveal and fix more than four content lessons.

sections.heading: Six ways to buy IGCSE maths help, compared
paragraphs: The table below is the comparison most families never see, because each provider compares itself to an unnamed alternative rather than to the actual options. The figures are published rates read in October 2026 and the sources are named. Nothing in it is IB Gram's price list.

Read the inclusion column rather than the price column. A group class at a tuition centre costs least per student and includes a teacher, a room and a scheme of work pitched at a typical candidate. It excludes individual diagnosis by design, because the format cannot provide it. A marketplace booking includes a tutor's time at whatever rate that tutor sets and typically nothing between sessions. A specialist arrangement should include a written diagnosis, marked written work and a review point, and if it does not then you are paying specialist rates for a marketplace product.

The verification column is the one to act on. Every model has a specific question that exposes whether it will work for your child: which syllabus code, who marks the written work, what happens if the match fails, and in the case of a centre with premises, which permit it holds. Those four questions take a single phone call each and they discriminate between the six options far better than any amount of reading about teaching philosophy.

One honest observation about the school's own intervention class, which is usually free and usually overlooked. It is taught by somebody who knows the exact specification, has seen the student's work, and has access to the department's own assessment data. For a procedural gap it is frequently the best available option at any price, and a family should exhaust it before paying anybody. Providers rarely mention this. It is true anyway.

sections.heading: Group class or one-to-one: what each can repair
paragraphs: The group-versus-individual question is usually argued on price and should be argued on fault type. Some maths problems are repairable in a room of fifteen students and some are not, and the difference is whether the repair needs individually marked written practice.

A group class delivers teaching. If a student's problem is that nobody has shown them how frequency density works, a competent group teacher showing the room how frequency density works solves it. If the problem is that the student cannot rearrange a formula quickly enough to start most questions, no amount of group teaching helps, because the fix is dozens of short exercises marked individually with errors identified. The teacher in a room of fifteen cannot do that, and it is not a failure of the teacher.

There is a second axis worth naming: whether the student will speak. Many students who are behind will not ask a question in front of peers, and a group class for them is an hour of watching somebody else learn. Conversely, some students work better with the social pressure of a class and go slack in one-to-one sessions. Parents usually know which of these their child is, and that knowledge is worth more than the price comparison.

The table gives a view by scenario. The honest recommendation column includes two rows where the answer is that paid tuition is not the right purchase at all, which is the information most worth having before spending anything.

sections.heading: The five places the money reliably disappears
paragraphs: Across this market the same five patterns waste tuition budgets, and all five are avoidable with information a family can obtain before paying anything. None of them involves a dishonest tutor; they are structural mistakes in how the purchase is made.

The first is buying a format that cannot fix the fault — most commonly a group class for a fluency problem, which produces a term of attendance and no grade movement. The second is buying without the specification, so that lessons are pitched at a generic IGCSE syllabus and a meaningful share of every hour addresses content the student's paper will not test. The third is spreading the budget across three or four subjects, which thins the written practice in all of them until the lessons are the only work being done and nothing consolidates.

The fourth is paying for travel rather than teaching. From an Al Shamkha address a visiting tutor's rate carries a journey, and published in-home figures of AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors reflect that. If the lesson could happen over video at the lower online band of AED 150 to 300, the difference is a transport subsidy and the money would buy more marks spent on marking.

The fifth is buying late. Demand peaks about eight weeks before the papers, which is precisely when tuition can do the least, because rebuilding fluency needs months and the week is already full. Late tuition genuinely improves timing, command-term discipline and rounding accuracy, which are real marks. It cannot deliver two years of practice volume, and a provider implying otherwise is selling the wrong thing to a worried family.

sections.heading: Centres with premises, and the permit that applies to them
paragraphs: If you are comparing a tuition centre with the online options, there is a regulatory distinction worth understanding, because the two are different legal animals and it affects what questions you should ask.

An individual private tutor in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the ministry's service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so a specific figure quoted as the penalty is invention.

An operation with premises and staff is different. In Dubai, a training institute requires an educational services permit from KHDA, obtained through an initial approval followed by permit and licence steps with a maximum period to complete them and an annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. Other emirates have their own routes through their own regulators: Abu Dhabi private schools sit with ADEK, Sharjah's with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the Ministry of Education.

The practical question for a parent comparing a centre near Khalifa City with an online arrangement is therefore simple: ask the centre which permit it holds and for its number. A legitimate centre answers immediately. Note also what cannot be claimed. IB Gram is an online matching platform with no premises in the UAE and holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and describing any tutoring service as approved by one of those bodies without the document to show is the most dangerous sentence available in this market.

sections.heading: Sitting the papers as a private candidate
paragraphs: Some Al Shamkha families end up needing this route: a student who has moved schools mid-course, one who wants an extra subject their school does not offer, or one resitting after leaving. It is a genuine option and it is administratively fiddly, so the order of operations matters.

The binding constraint is the centre, not the board. Entries are made through a centre registered with the board, and not every centre accepts private candidates. Those that do set their own fees and their own internal deadlines, which fall earlier than the board's. So the first step is to find a centre willing to take the entry, and only then to think about which series. Working the other way round is how families discover in week two of a series that no local centre will take them.

Subject availability is the second constraint. Specifications with practical or coursework components are harder or impossible to sit privately, which in mathematics is rarely an issue and in the sciences frequently is. Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June and a November series, the two available to UAE candidates, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version; Cambridge states that the correct zone timetable must be used and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

On cost, no figure appears on this page because entry fees are set by the centre rather than published universally, and a number invented here would be worse than useless to a family budgeting. Ask the centre for its total: the board entry fee, the centre's administration charge, and any late-entry loading. And ask what happens to the entry if the student is unwell on the day, because the answer differs between centres and is the question nobody thinks to ask until it matters.

sections.heading: Al Shamkha, Al Reef and Al Ghadeer: three addresses, one conclusion
paragraphs: This page is a comparison, so it is worth comparing the three mainland districts whose families face the same provider problem and seeing whether the answer differs. It does not, which is itself the finding.

Al Shamkha is settled villa housing with its own local provision and a half-hour run to the island. Al Reef sits on the Dubai-side corridor, nearer the Khalifa City centres. Al Ghadeer sits on the emirate boundary and some of its households use services on the Dubai side entirely, which gives it the widest nominal choice and the most confusing comparison. Three different geographies, three different sets of nearby options.

What is identical across all three is the structure of the decision. The group-class option is pitched at a generic specification in each case. The visiting-tutor option carries a journey in each case, priced into rates published at AED 180 to 350 and AED 200 to 500 depending on the source. The budget online option excludes marking in each case. And the fault types — procedural, fluency, technique, timing — are the same faults in the same proportions, because they are features of the qualification rather than of the neighbourhood.

So the conclusion from all three addresses is the same sequence. Exhaust the school's own intervention class, which costs nothing and is taught by somebody who knows the specification. Establish the syllabus code. Identify whether the fault is procedural or fluency-based by reading the last marked script. Then buy the narrowest thing that fixes it, which is often a bounded block rather than a term, and insist that marking of written work is included whatever the format.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor should produce every week
paragraphs: If the inclusion list is what separates the six models, it follows that a parent should know what the inclusion list looks like in practice. For a weekly one-to-one maths arrangement the weekly output is small and specific, and its absence is the clearest signal that an arrangement has drifted.

Each week there should be written work set, with an explicit instruction about what to show rather than just which questions to do. That work should come back marked against the published scheme for a real series, with the marks shown rather than a tick, so that a parent can see where credit was available and not claimed. The error log should be updated: one line per lost mark, categorised as content, method, notation or calculator, misread command, or ran out of time. And there should be a sentence about what next week addresses as a result.

That is four artefacts and none of them is onerous. Their value is that they are checkable by a parent with no mathematical knowledge at all. A marked script with eleven marks lost to command terms in October and three in December is evidence. A tutor reporting improved confidence is not, and in our experience that phrasing appears precisely when the written work has quietly stopped being set.

The same logic drives the review point. A date agreed at the start, at which the question is whether the named faults are recurring less often in marked work. The three honest answers are that the plan is working and can continue or taper, that the diagnosis was right but the cadence is too thin for the size of the gap, or that the diagnosis was wrong and needs redoing. A review that produces none of those three has not happened.

sections.heading: Claims we will not make, and work we will not do
paragraphs: A comparison page should be clear about its own limits, so here they are. IB Gram is an independent online matching platform. It holds no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. It is not a registered examination centre and has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. It cannot enter a candidate for an examination; only a centre can.

We publish no star rating, review count or satisfaction statistic. Doing so honestly would require producing the underlying data with its sample size, date and method, and a number without those is a sales device. Two providers in this market display different ratings on the same page, and one shows a figure in its markup that does not match the one a visitor sees; that is a structured-data problem as well as a credibility one.

On assessed work the boundary is firm and we state it to students. A tutor teaches, models methods, explains what a command term requires and marks the student's own attempts against the published scheme. A tutor does not supply answers for live assessed work, sit with a student during an assessment, or produce coursework for submission. A provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; we decline to produce assessed work at any price, and the consequences of buying it land on the student rather than the seller.

And on outcomes: no tutor can promise a grade or a grade improvement, and anyone offering one should be treated with real scepticism. Board material — specifications, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables — belongs to Cambridge and Pearson and is published on their own sites; we reference and link it rather than reproducing it. What we will commit to is a written diagnosis, marked written work, a stated review date and a straight answer about how much of the gap the remaining time can close.

whyPoints.description: The school's own intervention class is free and is frequently the best purchase available for a procedural gap. A group class can genuinely repair some faults. Both appear in the comparison on this page because a parent needs the full set, not our part of it.

whyPoints.title: Marking is the product, not the lesson
whyPoints.description: What separates a specialist arrangement from a marketplace booking is written work marked against the published scheme between sessions. We treat that as the deliverable and make it checkable by a parent with no mathematical background.

faqs.question: Which is better value in Al Shamkha, a group class or a private tutor?
faqs.answer: It depends on the fault rather than the price. A group class delivers teaching, so if the problem is that nobody has shown your child how a particular rule works, it can fix that. If the problem is weak algebraic fluency, no group format repairs it, because the fix is dozens of short exercises marked individually. Read the last marked script to establish which you have. And check whether your child will actually ask a question in a room of fifteen.

faqs.question: How much does a tuition centre class cost compared with one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Considerably less per student, and it is usually sold per term or as a package rather than hourly. The comparison that matters is what is included: a group class provides a teacher, a room and a scheme of work pitched at a typical candidate, and excludes individual diagnosis by design. Published online one-to-one rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to 150 for budget provision and AED 150 to 450 and above for specialist work, with marking included at the upper end.

faqs.question: Do visiting tutors charge more to come out to Al Shamkha?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, and the published ranges show why. In-home visiting in the emirate is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour in the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, with long journeys sitting at the upper end rather than the middle. A sixty-kilometre round trip for a single lesson has to be paid for somewhere. Against online specialist rates of AED 150 to 300, a meaningful part of that difference is transport.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tuition centre near Khalifa City before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which syllabus code the class is actually pitched at, because a generic IGCSE maths class usually targets the most common specification and not necessarily your child's. Who marks written work and against what. What happens if the class is the wrong level for your child. And which permit the centre holds, with its number: an operation with premises needs a permit from the emirate regulator, which is a different thing from an individual tutor's permit.

faqs.question: Is the school's own maths support class any good?
faqs.answer: Often it is the best option available at any price, and almost no tutoring provider will tell you so. It is taught by somebody who knows the exact specification, has seen your child's work and has access to the department's assessment data, and it is usually free. For a procedural gap that is a strong combination. Ask whether such a class exists and whether your child is in it before paying anyone, and treat its absence as the first question for the school.

faqs.question: Where do families in Al Shamkha most often waste tuition money?
faqs.answer: Five places. Buying a format that cannot fix the fault, typically a group class for a fluency problem. Buying without confirming the syllabus code, so lessons address a generic syllabus. Spreading a budget across three or four subjects until the written practice in all of them thins out. Paying a travel loading for a lesson that could happen over video. And buying eight weeks before the papers, when rebuilding fluency is no longer possible and only technique can improve.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE maths as a private candidate in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for mathematics, and the binding constraint is finding a centre rather than choosing a series. Entries are made through a centre registered with the board, not every centre accepts private candidates, and those that do set their own fees and internal deadlines earlier than the board's. So find the centre first. Subjects with practical or coursework components are harder to sit privately, which is rarely an issue in mathematics and frequently one in the sciences.

faqs.question: What does a private IGCSE entry cost through a centre?
faqs.answer: No figure appears here, because entry costs are set by the centre rather than published universally and an invented number would mislead a family budgeting. Ask the centre for the full total: the board entry fee, the centre's administration charge, and any late-entry loading. Ask also what happens to the entry if the student is unwell on the day, because the answer differs between centres and nobody thinks to ask until it matters.

faqs.question: How do I know whether a tutor is actually marking the written work?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it. A weekly arrangement should produce four things: work set with an instruction about what to show, that work returned marked against the published scheme with marks rather than ticks, an updated error log categorising each lost mark, and a sentence on what next week addresses as a result. All four are checkable by a parent with no mathematical background, and reports of improved confidence with nothing written are the signal that the marking has stopped.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor in another country need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: The UAE permit regime applies to private tutoring conducted in the Emirates, and the honest answer is that a family should ask any provider directly how its tutors are engaged and where they are based rather than accept a vague assurance. What we will state plainly is our own position: IB Gram is an online matching platform with no premises, office or branch in the UAE, and it holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson.

faqs.question: Which exam series can an Al Shamkha IGCSE candidate enter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two available to UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through the wrong version.

faqs.question: Is Additional Maths 0606 available as a group class anywhere nearby?
faqs.answer: Almost never, because the cohort is too small to fill a room anywhere in the emirate. That makes it the clearest case on this page where one-to-one is not a premium upgrade but the only format in which the subject can be bought at all. The difficulty students report in 0606 is usually algebraic stamina rather than the new calculus and logarithm content, which responds to volume of short marked practice rather than to re-teaching.

faqs.question: Should I buy tuition for three subjects at once before the papers?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the reason is arithmetic rather than principle. Tuition works through the marked written practice done between lessons, and your child's free evenings do not multiply when you add subjects. By the third or fourth subject the practice has thinned to the point where the lessons are the only work happening, and nothing consolidates. One subject funded properly moves a grade; three funded thinly cost three times as much and move none.

faqs.question: What does a review point actually look like in Al Shamkha?
faqs.answer: A date agreed at the start and a measure agreed with it, which is whether the named faults recur less often in marked work. Three honest answers are available at that point: the plan is working and can continue or taper, the diagnosis was right but the cadence is too thin for the gap, or the diagnosis was wrong and needs redoing. A review that produces a conversation about how the lessons feel has not taken place, whatever it is called.

Ask the school about its own support class first, because it costs nothing and the teacher knows the specification. Then establish the syllabus code and read the last marked script to see whether the fault is procedural, fluency, technique or timing. Then buy the narrowest thing that fixes it, with marking of written work included whatever the format. Lessons here run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE, and the trial is one lesson.

intro.heading: Two neighbourhoods, one answer: why the Al Wahda search and the Al Mushrif search end in the same place
paragraphs: Search for an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Wahda and you will find roughly the same results a parent in Al Mushrif, Al Nahyan or Al Bateen finds, with the area name swapped. That is not an accident of search engines; it is a fact about the market. Central Abu Dhabi is compact, the private schools in these catchments overlap heavily, and the pool of adults who can confidently teach Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher is small enough that it does not divide along neighbourhood lines at all. The honest version of this page says so, and then explains what does differ.

What differs between these areas is almost entirely logistics. Al Wahda is apartment-led and central, so a tutor travelling here faces a short hop but difficult parking. Al Bateen and Al Mushrif are more villa-led with longer school runs, pushing the first workable session later into the evening. Al Reem Island adds a bridge crossing that nobody enjoys at 5pm. None of that changes the syllabus, the tier decision or the grade scale. All of it changes the price and the start time of an in-home lesson, which is why a comparison between areas turns into a comparison between delivery formats.

The second thing that genuinely differs is which board each school sits. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 are not the same qualification, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, syllabus 4MA1, is a third. They differ in paper structure, in whether a calculator is permitted, in how the tiers are named and in the grade scale the final result is reported on. A parent who books a tutor without establishing this is gambling, and it is the single most common avoidable error in the first month of tutoring.

The tier decision is where real damage is done quietly. Cambridge splits 0580 into Core and Extended. Core caps the available grades; Extended opens the full range up to A*. Pearson splits 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher, with Foundation capping at grade 5 and Higher running from 9 down to 4, with a safety grade 3 available. A student entered on the lower tier in Year 10 because they were struggling can find in Year 11 that the grade they now need is not available to them. Tier entry is set by the school, confirm it early, and treat any mid-course tier change as a decision with a deadline attached.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one online tuition over live video, matched to the board and tier your child's school actually uses. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a comparison-minded parent, that is the point rather than a caveat: the question stops being which tutor is nearest to Al Wahda and becomes which tutor has taught the exact syllabus code your child is entered for, and the answer to that is the same whether you are searching from Al Wahda, Al Mushrif or the Corniche.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-wahda.programmesIntro: An IGCSE maths student in central Abu Dhabi is usually two years from a decision that matters more than the IGCSE grade itself: what comes next. The programmes below are the routes Al Wahda families actually choose between, and each one changes what Year 10 and Year 11 maths should be preparing for.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: A two-year terminal course examined by written papers with no coursework component in the mainstream mathematics syllabuses. Content covers number, algebra, coordinate geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, vectors and transformations, probability and statistics. Cambridge revised the 0580 assessment model, including the balance of calculator and non-calculator papers, so the paper structure should be confirmed on cambridgeinternational.org for the series your child is entered for.
programmes.countryNote: Central Abu Dhabi schools sit both boards, and some families discover the difference only when past papers arrive from the wrong one. Ask the department for the syllabus code and the tier in writing. Entries are made by the school as the examination centre, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, with a separate timetable version per zone that it is essential to use correctly.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme mathematics, after IGCSE
programmes.description: The Diploma splits mathematics into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Standard or Higher Level, with a 20% individual Exploration and, at Higher Level, a third paper. An IGCSE Extended or Higher-tier student arrives with solid algebra and almost no calculus, which is the predictable gap in the first term of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run a British route to Year 11 and then offer the Diploma, so an Al Wahda family may be choosing between staying on A-Levels at the same school and moving to a Diploma school on the island or towards Al Raha. That decision is easier to make in Year 10 than in the summer after the results arrive.

programmes.name: A-Level and AS-Level mathematics, after IGCSE
programmes.description: The common continuation for a student on the Cambridge or Pearson route. Pure mathematics dominates, with mechanics or statistics as applied content. A grade at IGCSE Extended or Higher tier is usually the entry condition, and schools often set a specific minimum. The step up in algebraic fluency is steep and shows in the first set of AS mock results.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. That makes the A-Level choice a regulatory matter as well as an academic one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics, the alternative route
programmes.description: The IB's middle-years route, assessed against four criteria rather than terminal papers. Students arrive at post-16 study with stronger investigation and communication skills and less experience of timed written examinations. Families comparing an IB continuum school with a British-curriculum school in central Abu Dhabi are really comparing these two assessment cultures.
programmes.countryNote: Some Al Wahda parents ask whether their child should sit IGCSE at all rather than continue through MYP. Both routes lead into the Diploma. The practical difference is that IGCSE produces an externally examined certificate at 16 that counts towards MoE equivalency, which matters to families who may apply to UAE universities.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-wahda.subjectsIntro: The list below breaks IGCSE mathematics into the parts an Abu Dhabi student is examined on, with the specific error that costs marks in each. A first session should narrow this to the two or three that are actually live rather than touring all of them.

subjects.name: Number and the four operations
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Fractions, decimals, standard form, upper and lower bounds, percentage change in both directions. Reverse percentages are the classic marks-loser: students multiply when they should divide. Bounds questions are the second, because rounding the answer defeats the purpose of the question.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging formulae, algebraic fractions and simultaneous equations. The sign error in a subtracted bracket accounts for more lost marks than any conceptual gap. Extended and Higher tier add harder factorising and manipulation of algebraic fractions, which rewards drilling rather than explanation.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and sequences
subjects.description: Linear and quadratic equations, the formula and completing the square, inequalities on a number line, nth-term rules for linear and quadratic sequences. Students who can solve a quadratic often cannot interpret which of the two roots the question wants, which is a reading failure rather than a maths one.

subjects.name: Coordinate geometry and graphs
subjects.description: Gradients, midpoints, parallel and perpendicular lines, sketching quadratics, exponentials and reciprocals, solving graphically. Perpendicular gradients and the negative reciprocal trip up a predictable share of candidates, and graph sketches lose marks for unlabelled axes and intercepts.

subjects.name: Mensuration and compound measures
subjects.description: Area, surface area and volume of prisms, cylinders, cones, spheres and composite solids, plus speed, density and pressure. The two routine errors are using a slant height where the vertical height is needed, and leaving an answer in the wrong unit after a cubic conversion.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and Pythagoras
subjects.description: Right-angled trigonometry, the sine and cosine rules, bearings, angles of elevation and depression, and three-dimensional applications at the higher tiers. Bearings cost marks through diagram errors rather than calculation, and students lose the cosine rule mark by rearranging it incorrectly under time pressure.

subjects.name: Transformations and vectors
subjects.description: Translation, reflection, rotation and enlargement including negative and fractional scale factors, plus column vectors and vector geometry. Describing a transformation fully, with centre, scale factor and direction, is worth marks that students forfeit by naming the transformation only.

subjects.name: Probability
subjects.description: Single and combined events, tree diagrams, Venn diagrams, and conditional probability without replacement. The replacement condition is the whole question in most tree-diagram items, and candidates who do not change the denominator on the second branch lose every subsequent mark.

subjects.name: Statistics and data handling
subjects.description: Averages from frequency tables, grouped data and estimated means, cumulative frequency, box plots, histograms with unequal class widths, and scatter diagrams. Histograms with unequal widths are the single most reliably mishandled topic at Extended and Higher tier because frequency density is forgotten.

subjects.name: Problem solving across topics
subjects.description: Multi-step questions that combine two or three topics and award method marks for a sensible route. Strong students lose marks here by jumping to an answer without writing the setup. Working whole past papers and marking them against the official scheme is the only reliable fix.

subjects.name: Calculator and non-calculator technique
subjects.description: Cambridge revised the 0580 assessment model and the balance of calculator and non-calculator papers, so confirm the structure for your child's series on the board's own site. Practising the wrong paper's habits wastes hours, and non-calculator fluency with surds, fractions and standard form takes weeks to build rather than days.

subjects.name: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: A separate Cambridge syllabus with a different paper structure from 0580, including a graphics-calculator requirement and an investigation paper at some tiers. Students entered for 0607 who revise from 0580 past papers are revising the wrong examination, and this happens more often than it should.

sections.heading: The one-street test: what actually changes between Al Wahda and the next neighbourhood
paragraphs: Answering the query directly: an IGCSE maths tutor in Al Wahda through IB Gram is a mathematics specialist matched to your child's board and tier, teaching one-to-one over live video at a time that fits an Abu Dhabi school day, with a free trial lesson first and no block of hours bought in advance. The same description applies in Al Mushrif, Al Nahyan and Al Bateen, which is the honest answer to a search phrased by neighbourhood.

Run the test yourself. Take two tutoring quotes, one for an Al Wahda address and one for an address ten minutes away, and compare them line by line. The syllabus is identical. The tier is identical. The papers and the grade scale are identical. The marks your child is losing in histograms and reverse percentages are identical. What changes is the journey, the start time and sometimes the price, and all three are properties of travel rather than of teaching.

That is why this page spends its effort on board, tier, cost and verification rather than on describing the neighbourhood back to you. A page that tells an Al Wahda parent about Al Wahda is spending words the parent does not need. A page that tells them their child may be entered for 0607 and revising from 0580 papers is spending words that change an outcome.

Where the neighbourhood does matter is the practical shape of the week. A dense central area with short school runs makes a 4pm slot workable. A villa community with a longer run makes 5.30pm more realistic. A bridge crossing makes an in-home tutor expensive and late. These are real constraints and they belong in the booking conversation, but they are scheduling facts, not educational ones, and online delivery removes most of them.

sections.heading: Which board is your child actually sitting: 0580, 0607 or 4MA1
paragraphs: Three syllabuses dominate IGCSE mathematics in UAE schools and they are genuinely different examinations. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 is the most widely sat. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a separate syllabus with its own paper structure and a graphics-calculator expectation. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is the main Pearson route, reported on the 9 to 1 grade scale rather than A* to G.

The consequences of guessing are concrete. A student entered for 0607 who revises 0580 past papers is practising the wrong paper structure and, in some components, the wrong skills. A student entered for 4MA1 Higher who revises Cambridge Extended material will meet unfamiliar question styles and a different mark distribution. Tutors who ask only for the school name and the year group are not in a position to catch this, which is why the syllabus code is the first thing we ask for.

Cambridge publishes the current assessment model for each syllabus on its own site, including which papers permit a calculator, and it has revised 0580 in recent years. Pearson publishes the structure for 4MA1 and its provisional and final timetables. Both should be read at source for the series your child is entered for rather than taken from a tutoring page, including this one. What belongs on this page is the instruction to check and the reason it matters.

One practical consequence for a household with two children at different schools in central Abu Dhabi: they may be sitting different boards. That is not a problem, but it does mean a single tutor covering both needs to have taught both, and it is a fair question to ask before booking. Two matched specialists are better than one generalist where either child's need is specific.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the tier decision and its ceiling
paragraphs: Tier entry is the decision most likely to cause regret, and it is usually made quietly by the school rather than discussed with the family. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended, with Core capping the grades a candidate can be awarded and Extended opening the range to A*. Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher, with Foundation topping out at grade 5 and Higher running from 9 down to 4, with a grade 3 available as a safety net.

The problem is timing. A student placed on the lower tier in Year 10 because they were struggling may improve substantially by the middle of Year 11, at which point the grade they now need may be outside the tier they are entered for. Tier changes are possible but they sit behind entry deadlines the school controls, and after that point the ceiling is fixed regardless of how the student performs on the day.

The reverse error is just as real and less discussed. A student pushed onto the higher tier to protect a school's grade profile can end up attempting a paper where they access few marks, when a confident performance at the lower tier would have produced a cleaner result. Neither tier is better. The right tier is the one where the student can reach the grade they actually need, and that judgement should rest on past-paper evidence rather than on optimism in either direction.

A short diagnostic block is the cheapest way to settle this. Two or three sessions working past papers from both tiers produce evidence a parent can take to the maths department. It converts a conversation about feelings into a conversation about marks, and it is a bounded piece of work with a clear finish rather than an open commitment.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs around here, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Most pages open with the premium tier and work down, which makes everything below look like a compromise. Starting at the other end is more useful. The cheapest live tuition advertised in this market is budget online work, often delivered by university students, from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For homework supervision and confidence at Year 9 or early Year 10, that tier can be genuinely sufficient, and saying otherwise would be dishonest.

The next step up is a qualified subject tutor working online, at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is the band most Year 11 families end up in, because the work has moved from supervision to teaching: tier judgement, past-paper marking, and the specific topics that separate a 6 from a 7. Above that sit IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led tuition at AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

In-home visits are priced differently because travel is inside the rate: AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for exam-year specialist work.

Two things a parent can verify rather than take on trust. First, every figure above is a market rate read from a named published source in October 2026; none of them is an IB Gram price, and ours is quoted after a free trial lesson when the board, tier and session length are known. Second, spending up the tiers does not fix a wrong diagnosis. A premium rate applied to a student whose real problem is frequency density in histograms buys an expensive route to the same gap.

sections.heading: Online against in-home across central Abu Dhabi, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Set the two cost columns beside each other and the travel premium is roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour depending on tier. For an Al Wahda family the journey being paid for is short; for a family in Mohammed Bin Zayed City or across the Al Reem bridge it is longer, and that is the main reason in-home quotes vary between neighbourhoods when nothing educational varies at all.

In-home tutoring has genuine advantages worth stating. A tutor in the room reads a student's body language, sees the page as it is written, and holds the attention of a younger or more distractible child better than a screen does. For a Year 7 student, that can be decisive. For a Year 11 student working past papers against a mark scheme, the decisive factor is whether the tutor has taught 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher before, and proximity has no bearing on that.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and this page will not imply otherwise in order to match a search phrase. What is on offer is live one-to-one video tuition into central Abu Dhabi: shared whiteboard, worked solutions built on the same screen both people are reading, past papers annotated live, and a recording the student can replay before the homework.

If you do engage an independent in-home tutor, ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and the permit is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for a working tutor not to hold one. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of any figure quoted to you.

sections.heading: Entries, series and results: the Cambridge and Pearson calendar for a UAE candidate
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a candidate in Abu Dhabi sits June, with November available as the resit route. This matters because a great deal of advice circulating online is written for Indian candidates and quotes a February or March window that does not exist for a student in Al Wahda.

Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each. It states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Since the school is the centre, the practical instruction is to work from the timetable the school issues rather than from whichever PDF a search returns.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and they are useful precisely because they can be checked. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and because provisional dates are revised, any session plan should link the live official timetable rather than a restatement of it.

Working backwards from that, the useful planning sequence for a Year 11 student in central Abu Dhabi is: tier confirmed and entry made by the school, mock window completed and marked, four to eight weeks of whole-paper practice, then the series itself. Ramadan sits inside the UAE academic year and moves earlier each year, shortening school hours and shifting energy to post-Iftar slots, so the heavy content work belongs before it and the consolidation work during it.

sections.heading: Why the IGCSE grade matters beyond the school: MoE equivalency on the British track
paragraphs: Families who may apply to a UAE university eventually meet the Ministry of Education equivalency process, and the IGCSE grade is part of it. On the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

One detail is worth more than the rest: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A competitor page currently ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced rule is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, and getting this right is a straightforward way for a parent to sanity-check any advice they are given.

What this means for maths specifically is that the subject almost always sits inside those five, and a tier that caps the grade below the requirement creates a problem that surfaces years later rather than immediately. It is one more reason to settle the tier question on evidence in Year 10 rather than hope in Year 11.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or speeds up; verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae or the relevant authority's own page before acting. And the IB points threshold for equivalency is not published in the source behind the British-track figures above, so no points figure should be quoted to you by anyone who has not read it on an official page.

sections.heading: Checks worth making before you pay anyone, in Al Wahda or anywhere nearby
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's regulator is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. For a school matter in Al Wahda, ADEK is the body, and ADEK's own site is where its inspection ratings belong.

No tutoring company should borrow a regulator's name as a credential. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no partnership with any of them. A page claiming otherwise is making a false statement about itself before it has taught your child anything, and the phrase to be most sceptical of is any variant of regulator-approved tutors.

A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. In Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Mentioning this is not a boast; it is a way of showing a parent what the real categories are so that marketing language stops working on them.

One Abu Dhabi-specific point. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document. The practical rule for a parent is to avoid engaging their child's own classroom teacher privately, however convenient the arrangement looks.

process.description: One full lesson, no card required and no hours bought in advance. The tutor works recent material to find the genuine gap, checks that the tier looks right on the evidence, and tells you plainly what they found, including when very little tutoring is needed.

process.description: Topics in priority order, how many sessions each is expected to take, and what the student does between lessons. Where the school's mock and entry dates are known, the plan runs backwards from those rather than from a generic twelve-week block.

process.description: Each session ends with one target. Every six to eight weeks the plan is checked against the error log, and when the log shows the recurring failures have gone, the honest recommendation is fewer sessions or none rather than a renewal.

faqs.question: Where do I get the syllabus code my child is actually entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the mathematics department for the syllabus code and the tier in writing, and keep the reply. Report cards and school websites often name the board without the code, and 0580 and 0607 are both Cambridge syllabuses with different paper structures. The examinations officer will also know, since the school makes the entry as the examination centre. This matters because past papers are not interchangeable between codes, and a student revising from the wrong set is practising question styles they will not meet.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE maths the same qualification as Cambridge International Mathematics?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, syllabus 0580, and Cambridge International Mathematics, syllabus 0607, are separate syllabuses with different assessment models, and 0607 carries a graphics-calculator expectation and a different paper structure. A student entered for 0607 who revises from 0580 past papers is preparing for the wrong examination. Both are Cambridge, both are tiered into Core and Extended, and both appear in UAE schools, which is exactly why the code rather than the board name is the thing to confirm before any tutoring starts.

faqs.question: What is the highest grade available on the Core and Foundation tiers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Core caps the grades a candidate can be awarded below the top of the A* to G scale, and Pearson Foundation tops out at grade 5 on the 9 to 1 scale. Higher tier at Pearson runs from 9 down to 4 with a grade 3 available as a safety net, and Cambridge Extended reaches A*. Confirm the current ranges on the board's own site for your child's series. The practical point is that tier entry sets a ceiling the student cannot pass however well the papers go, so the decision deserves evidence.

faqs.question: Can my child change tier partway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it sits behind an entry deadline the school controls as the examination centre. A student placed on the lower tier in Year 10 who has improved substantially may still be able to move, and a student struggling on the higher tier may be better served by moving down. Either way the conversation has to happen before the deadline, which is why a short diagnostic block producing past-paper evidence from both tiers is worth doing early. After the deadline the ceiling is fixed regardless of performance.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Al Wahda cost more or less than one in Al Mushrif?
faqs.answer: For online tuition there is no reason for a difference at all, and if a quote varies between two central Abu Dhabi addresses, the variation is travel being priced in. In-home rates genuinely do differ by area because the journey differs: a short central hop costs the tutor less than a run out to Mohammed Bin Zayed City or across the Al Reem bridge. Market in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online.

faqs.question: Which four maths topics show up most often in marked Year 11 papers?
faqs.answer: Four recur in marked papers. Histograms with unequal class widths, where frequency density is forgotten. Reverse percentages, where students multiply instead of dividing. Tree diagrams without replacement, where the second denominator is not changed and every later mark falls. And incomplete transformation descriptions, where a student names a rotation but omits the centre and direction and loses the marks attached to them. None of these is a conceptual failure; they are habits, and habits respond fast to targeted practice and an error log.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for a specialist rather than a cheaper online tutor?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the diagnosis. If a Year 9 student needs homework supervision and confidence, budget online tuition advertised at AED 45 to 150 an hour can be genuinely sufficient and paying more buys nothing. If a Year 11 student needs tier judgement, past-paper marking and the specific topics separating a 6 from a 7, a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 is the right band. Premium rates of AED 500 and above make sense only for a narrow need the family has already identified precisely.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE maths exams happen for a student in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so an Abu Dhabi candidate sits June with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable per zone, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version, so work from the timetable your school issues.

faqs.question: How many weekly maths sessions does a Year 11 student here usually start with?
faqs.answer: One sixty-minute session a week is the normal starting point, moving to two in the weeks around mocks or where the student is carrying gaps from Year 9 as well as current content. Beyond two a week the returns fall off sharply, because improvement in mathematics comes from the practice a student does between lessons and a crowded schedule removes the time for it. A tutor proposing four sessions a week at the first conversation is selling capacity rather than diagnosing a problem.

faqs.question: My child is predicted a 4 and needs a 6. Is that realistic in two terms?
faqs.answer: Often yes, provided the tier allows it and the work is targeted rather than general. Two terms is enough to convert habitual losses into marks: units and bounds, full transformation descriptions, frequency density, the second branch of a tree diagram, and writing a setup before reaching for the calculator. What is not realistic is re-teaching two years of content in that window. The first step is a marked past paper, because the gap between a 4 and a 6 is usually made of recoverable marks rather than missing understanding.

faqs.question: Do we lose anything by taking maths lessons online rather than in our home?
faqs.answer: For Year 10 and Year 11 mathematics, very little. Past papers are annotated live on a shared screen, the session starts at the minute booked rather than when traffic allows, and the recording can be replayed before the homework. What you give up is a person in the room, which counts for more with a younger or easily distracted child than with a Year 11 student. What you gain is a tutor chosen for having taught your child's syllabus code and tier rather than for living within a short drive.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover IGCSE maths for one child and IB maths for another?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking directly rather than assuming either way. Plenty of tutors teach both, and back-to-back online sessions for two children save a household real scheduling effort with no travel between them. But the examinations differ: IGCSE maths is tiered and terminal, while Diploma mathematics carries a 20% Exploration and a third paper at Higher Level. Ask which syllabus codes and which course levels the tutor has actually taught before deciding whether one person covers both.

faqs.question: How does the IGCSE maths grade affect a UAE university application later?
faqs.answer: On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. Maths almost always sits inside those five. A tier that caps the grade below what is needed creates a problem that appears years later. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae rather than relying on any tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: What should we ask an independent tutor before letting them teach our child?
faqs.answer: Four things. Which syllabus codes and tiers have you actually taught, and for how long. Can you show your MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years. Will you mark a past paper against the official scheme in front of us. And what would make you tell us to stop. A tutor comfortable with all four is usually a good sign; one who answers the first by naming a school rather than a code has told you something useful too.
