abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-zahiya.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE mathematics to Abu Dhabi students across the Cambridge and Pearson specifications and at both tiers. Matching is to a named syllabus code, because that is what the examiner marks against.

intro.heading: Timing is the variable nobody discusses
paragraphs: Almost every conversation about IGCSE maths tuition is about who. The more consequential question is when. The same money, the same tutor and the same child produce entirely different outcomes depending on which term of the two-year course you spend it in, and the difference is not marginal. Bought early it changes a tier; bought late it changes technique. Both are worth having and they are not substitutes.

Al Zahiyah, still widely called the Tourist Club Area, is the dense north-eastern corner of Abu Dhabi island. Families here send children across the island and out along the mainland corridor, and the practical consequence for maths specifically is the amount of homework capacity left in the evening. A child who gets home at four has a different week from one who gets home at ten past five, and maths is the subject where that difference compounds, because fluency is built by short frequent practice rather than by long sessions.

The second thing worth establishing early is which specification your child is actually entered for. Five are in common use across Abu Dhabi schools: Cambridge 0580 at Core and at Extended, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A coded 4MA1, Pearson Mathematics B coded 4MB1, and Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 as an optional extra. They differ on calculator rules, on whether a formula sheet is supplied, on tiering vocabulary and on grading scale. A tutor who does not ask which one is teaching the union of five courses.

Delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Zahiyah or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Independent tutors in the emirate do travel, and the market prices that at a loading we show with its source further down. For maths the relevant trade is that a specialist in the exact specification is scarcer than a competent mathematician within driving distance of Al Salam Street.

The rest of this page covers the things an Al Zahiyah parent can act on. A table of what a term of work achieves depending on when you start it, and what it cannot fix. The five specifications and what distinguishes each. The two grading scales and what the Ministry of Education actually counts for equivalency. Tuition cost set against other published figures in this market, including one that should alarm you. And how the regulators across the Emirates differ, because families move between them and assume the rules travel with the specification. There is also a short section on where twenty minutes of daily practice fits into an Al Zahiyah week, which sounds trivial and is the single strongest predictor of whether a maths grade moves at all. None of it requires you to understand the mathematics; all of it requires two dates from the school.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-zahiya.programmesIntro: An IGCSE maths grade is produced over roughly five years of schooling, not two, and the programme a student is in determines what tuition can still change. These are the stages where the decisions get made.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary mathematics, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Number, algebra, geometry, measure and data handling at a level that reads as straightforward beside IGCSE. The quiet work of these years is algebraic fluency: rearranging, expanding, factorising and substituting without conscious effort. Students who leave Year 9 doing these slowly meet the same delay in every IGCSE topic that builds on them.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools form their tier view during Year 9 on internal evidence. This is the only point at which tuition reliably changes a tier recommendation, which makes it the highest-value and least popular time to buy it. A parent told their Year 9 child is fine should ask specifically which tier the school currently expects to enter them for.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics, Year 10
programmes.description: The content year. Most of the syllabus is taught here and the tier is confirmed somewhere in it. A student who falls behind in Year 10 compounds the problem, because the course does not revisit topics; it assumes them. Half-term and end-of-year internal assessments are the evidence a school uses, which makes them worth reading rather than filing.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Zahiyah family, Year 10 is the term in which a genuine content gap can still be closed without competing against revision for everything else. A term of weekly work here achieves considerably more than the same term in Year 11, when the student is also preparing eight other subjects.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics, Year 11
programmes.description: Completion of the syllabus, mocks, and the final entry. Tuition in this year does two things well: it repairs specific diagnosed faults, and it converts known content into marks through timed practice and mark-scheme discipline. What it does not do is rebuild underlying fluency, because there is no longer room in the week.
programmes.countryNote: The school's final entry deadline sits months before the examination, and the tier is fixed at that point. An Al Zahiyah parent should ask for that date in the first term of Year 11 and treat it, not the examination, as the real deadline for any conversation about tiering.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: An optional second qualification sat alongside Extended 0580 by students heading for A Level or Diploma mathematics. Calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and harder trigonometry, both papers calculator-permitted. The content is new, but the difficulty students report is almost always algebraic stamina rather than the new ideas.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi school offers it, 0606 usually runs in a small fast set with limited support hours. It is the most common reason a strong Extended student suddenly needs tuition, and the fix is normally volume of short algebra practice rather than re-teaching the calculus.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-al-zahiya.subjectsIntro: These are the topic areas where Abu Dhabi IGCSE maths scripts lose marks most reliably, with what a tutor should do about each. The order roughly reflects marks returned per hour of work.

subjects.name: Histograms and frequency density
subjects.description: Unequal class widths, and the frequency density calculation that students either know or do not. Entirely mechanical once taught, and one of the highest-yield single lessons available anywhere in the syllabus.

subjects.name: Similar shapes and scale factors
subjects.description: Linear, area and cubed relationships between similar figures and solids. The reliable error is applying a linear factor to an area or volume. One rule, taught once, protects marks on every paper afterwards.

subjects.name: Bounds and accuracy in calculations
subjects.description: Upper and lower bounds propagated through a calculation, especially a division. Students also lose accuracy marks by rounding an intermediate value, which is a habit rather than a gap and responds to a single instruction consistently enforced.

subjects.name: Rearranging formulae with the subject twice
subjects.description: The point at which algebraic fluency either exists or does not. Students who manage simple rearrangement stall here, and the fix is volume of short exercises rather than explanation, which is why it is a Year 9 and Year 10 job.

subjects.name: Probability without replacement
subjects.description: Two-stage tree diagrams where the second denominator changes. Marks go to branches left unlabelled and to adding where the question requires multiplying along a path. Fifteen minutes of correctly drawn trees usually settles it.

subjects.name: Three-dimensional trigonometry
subjects.description: Where Extended candidates most often stop writing. The first move is always to extract the single relevant triangle from the solid and redraw it; students who try to reason inside the three-dimensional diagram rarely get started.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Sketching with correct asymptotic behaviour, reading intersections, and describing transformations in function notation rather than in words. The notation requirement is the marks, and most students describe when they should denote.

subjects.name: Vectors in column form
subjects.description: Addition, magnitude, and showing points collinear through a scalar multiple. Students write a sentence of geometry where the mark scheme wants a vector route, which is a translation problem rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic and exact form
subjects.description: Surds, fractions, exact answers and mental estimation, needed because 0580 includes a paper without a calculator. Pearson candidates do not need this diet, which is the clearest argument for confirming the specification first.

subjects.name: Calculator discipline and recorded working
subjects.description: Storing intermediate values, checking angle mode, and writing the substitution before evaluating it. Pearson and Cambridge 0607 candidates live on the calculator, and marks are lost to the machine rather than to the mathematics.

sections.heading: When in the two years does IGCSE maths tuition earn its money?
paragraphs: The answer is uncomfortable because it is the opposite of when families buy. Demand peaks about eight weeks before the papers, which is the point at which tuition can do the least. Supply of the thing that matters most — time to rebuild fluency — ran out a year earlier.

The mechanism is simple. Mathematics is hierarchical. Almost every Extended topic rests on confident algebraic manipulation, and manipulation becomes confident through volume of short practice over months. There is no shortcut, and a student in Year 11 preparing eight other subjects has no room in the week for the volume required. So a Year 11 intervention aims at the things that respond quickly: procedural rules, command terms, rounding discipline, timing. Those are real marks and often a double-digit swing, but they are a different category of gain.

The table states this plainly, including the final column, which is the one most providers leave out. A family that knows what a six-week block cannot fix will spend the six weeks well. A family that has been told it can fix everything will be disappointed in a way that was predictable from the start.

The practical instruction for an Al Zahiyah parent reading this in Year 9 or Year 10: ask the maths department which tier they currently expect to enter your child for, and ask when the final entry is submitted. Those two answers tell you how much time you have and what is still changeable. Nothing on this page is more useful than those two dates.

sections.heading: Five specifications, and why the one your child sits changes the plan
paragraphs: A single Abu Dhabi year group can contain students sitting five different mathematics qualifications. Parents discover this when two children at different schools compare homework and find the topics do not match. Teachers know it; tutoring websites mostly do not mention it, because the simpler story sells better.

The practical differences are concentrated in three places. First, the calculator rule. Cambridge 0580 includes a paper sat without one, so exact-form work, surds and mental arithmetic are load-bearing. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator throughout. Cambridge 0607 is built around a graphic display calculator and assumes fluency with it from the start. Second, formula provision: Pearson supplies a sheet, Cambridge expects recall of a defined list, and that changes whether memorisation or fast selection is the skill to train. Third, grading scale and tier names, which matter when a family tries to compare two children's reports or set a target.

The table sets out who sits what and what follows for revision. Treat the first column as something to confirm rather than guess: the school's exams officer can give you the exact code in one email, and that email is worth more than any amount of reading about IGCSE mathematics in general.

A note on 0607 in particular, since it is the one families understand least. Cambridge International Mathematics is not an easier or harder 0580; it is a different design, with investigation work at Extended tier and a calculator assumed throughout. A tutor whose experience is entirely 0580 will teach broadly correct mathematics against the wrong assessment shape, and the student will notice in the mock rather than in the lessons.

sections.heading: Two grading scales, and what the Ministry of Education actually counts
paragraphs: Cambridge reports IGCSE grades as letters, A* down to G, with Core capped below the top of the range. Pearson reports numbers, nine down to one, with Higher tier covering nine to four and Foundation five to one. These do not map onto one another cleanly and the attempt to convert between them at home produces more argument than information.

Where the scales stop being a domestic question and become an administrative one is Ministry of Education equivalency, which almost no tutoring site in this market explains and at least one gets wrong. For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that matters most to UAE families is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is simply not what the published rule says. For the American track the requirements are different again — English proficiency shown through an IELTS academic score of 5, a TOEFL iBT score of 61, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in SAT Mathematics.

Two cautions belong with this. No points threshold for the IB Diploma appears in the source material, so no Diploma equivalency figure should be quoted to you by anyone without a reference on the ministry's own site. And equivalency is a process performed by the authorities, not by a tutoring platform: IB Gram does not carry it out, guarantee it, or imply that tuition is required for it. Verify the current requirements through the official channel before acting on anything, including this page.

sections.heading: Tuition cost in context, in monthly figures
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a family decision, because nobody buys an hour. The question is what a term costs and whether that is the best use of the money against everything else a household spends on education. Monthly figures answer that; hourly ones invite a comparison nobody actually makes.

Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table estimates monthly spend for a single weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, the second of which carries the travel loading. All of these were read in October 2026, all belong to the market, and none is IB Gram's price list.

The last row of the table is there deliberately. A provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is a useful number for a parent to know, not as a purchase option but as a scale: roughly three months of genuine specialist tuition, spent instead on something that constitutes academic malpractice and whose consequences land on the student rather than the seller. We will not supply that, and the existence of the price is the clearest argument available for checking what a provider actually sells.

One piece of wider context, because it is dated and checkable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. That is Dubai rather than Abu Dhabi, where the fee process sits with ADEK, but it is the kind of published anchor worth knowing when weighing a tuition commitment against a school fee cycle. On VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE, we state no position: that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority.

sections.heading: Where the daily practice actually happens in an Al Zahiyah week
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject least well served by a single weekly session and most improved by short daily contact. Twenty minutes a day of focused practice beats two hours on a Saturday, and the reason is not motivational. Fluency is a retrieval problem: a skill recalled on six separate days is retained far better than the same skill practised for the same total time in one sitting.

In a dense island district the obstacle is the evening rather than the willingness. A Year 11 student arriving home at ten past five, with eight subjects' worth of homework, mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education on the timetable and a family apartment containing two other children, does not have an obvious twenty-minute window. Finding one is a scheduling exercise and worth doing explicitly rather than hoping.

The patterns that work in practice tend to be unglamorous. Twenty minutes before anything else, immediately after changing, while the student is still in school mode. Or the first twenty minutes of the morning for households where the child wakes early. Or a fixed ten minutes twice, which suits students who resist a single block. What does not work is leaving it to whenever there is time, because in an Al Zahiyah week there is no such moment and the practice silently becomes a weekend batch.

The content of that twenty minutes matters less than its existence, but the most useful version is retrieval rather than new work: five questions on a topic covered three weeks ago, done without notes. A tutor should be setting precisely that and marking it, which is what separates a weekly lesson that builds fluency from one that reviews whatever the school happened to set.

sections.heading: ADEK, fee approval and the regulator map across the Emirates
paragraphs: In Abu Dhabi, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and it publishes inspection outcomes. ADEK is named by almost none of the tutoring sites competing for this search, which is a striking omission in a market where parents treat inspection ratings as the primary school-choice signal.

The map matters because families relocate within the country and assume the rules travel. They do not. Dubai's private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Sharjah's are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map for UAE private schools.

The scope differs as well as the name. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates the regulator's remit extends considerably beyond inspection into what a school may teach and charge. A family moving between emirates mid-IGCSE should expect the administrative texture around their child's schooling to change even though the Cambridge or Pearson specification does not.

What none of this gives a parent is subject-level information. An inspection rating describes whole-school performance against a framework. It cannot tell you whether this year's Extended maths set has a specialist teacher, whether the department is carrying a vacancy, or whether your child is entered at the right tier. Read the rating, then ask those three questions of the school directly. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre.

sections.heading: The permit position, and what a maths tutor will not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity rather than an unregulated one, and the rules are published. A private tuition work permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The ministry's service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published — press reporting states that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties — so a specific figure quoted to you as the penalty is somebody's invention. In Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current ADEK document before relying on the wording.

On what a tutor does: teach content, model methods, explain what a command term requires, mark the student's own work against the published scheme, and show where credit was available and unclaimed. On what a tutor does not do: supply answers to live assessed work, sit with a student during an assessment, produce coursework for submission, or hand over board material. Specifications, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are published on their own sites; we work through them from the official source rather than distributing copies.

And on promises: no tutor can promise a grade or a grade improvement, and a provider offering one should be treated with real scepticism. Nor are our tutors described as current examiners for any board, because that status cannot be evidenced in a way a parent could check, and examiner language should never be used to imply access to marking or unreleased papers. What honest tuition offers is a diagnosis, teaching aimed at it, marked written work, and a straight answer about how much of the gap the remaining time can close.

faqs.question: When should an Al Zahiyah family start IGCSE maths tuition?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most do. Year 9 and early Year 10 are the only windows in which tuition can still change which tier a school enters a student for, because that decision rests on algebraic fluency and fluency is built by months of short practice. By term one of Year 11 the realistic gains are diagnosed procedural faults and mark-scheme discipline, which are genuinely worth a double-digit mark swing but are a different category. Six weeks before the papers, tuition buys timing and technique.

faqs.question: How many different IGCSE maths qualifications do Abu Dhabi schools use?
faqs.answer: Five in common circulation: Cambridge 0580 at Core and Extended tier, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A coded 4MA1, Pearson Mathematics B coded 4MB1, and Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 as an optional extra. They differ on calculator rules, formula provision, tiering vocabulary and grading scale. Your school's exams officer can confirm the exact code in one email, and a revision plan written against the wrong code wastes real weeks of work.

faqs.question: What is Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 and how is it different?
faqs.answer: It is a separate Cambridge specification built around the graphic display calculator, with investigation work at Extended tier. It is not an easier or harder version of 0580; it is a different design with a different assessment shape. A tutor whose experience is entirely 0580 will teach broadly correct mathematics against the wrong paper structure, and the student discovers that in the mock rather than in the lessons. Confirm which of the two your school uses before anything else.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education among the five subjects the ministry counts?
faqs.answer: No. For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. They must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. At least one ranking site in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is not what the rule says. Verify through the official channel.

faqs.question: What does a month of IGCSE maths tuition cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: In monthly terms, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table estimates roughly AED 240 to 600 for a weekly hour at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, the latter carrying the travel loading. Those figures were read in October 2026 and are the market's, not ours.

faqs.question: Is twenty minutes a day really better than a long weekend session?
faqs.answer: For mathematics, yes, and the reason is retrieval rather than motivation. A skill recalled on six separate days is retained considerably better than the same total time spent in one sitting. The practical difficulty in a dense Al Zahiyah household is finding the twenty minutes, which has to be placed deliberately — immediately after changing, or first thing in the morning — because left to whenever there is time it quietly becomes a weekend batch and loses most of its value.

faqs.question: How do Cambridge letter grades compare with Pearson number grades?
faqs.answer: They do not convert cleanly, and attempting the conversion at home causes more argument than information. Cambridge reports A* to G with Core capped below the top of the range; Pearson reports nine to one, with Higher covering nine to four and Foundation five to one. The comparison that means something is the same child against their own previous marked work on the same specification. For equivalency purposes the published rule names both scales explicitly, at no less than grade E or grade 3.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my Al Zahiyah child sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two available to UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through the wrong version. Take the timetable from the school.

faqs.question: Why is Additional Maths 0606 so much harder for a strong student?
faqs.answer: Because it introduces calculus, logarithms and binomial expansion in a fast small set, and the limiting factor is almost never the new ideas. It is algebraic stamina: 0606 questions require three or four manipulation steps before the new content even appears, and a student who manages Extended 0580 comfortably may still be doing those steps slowly. The fix is volume of short algebra practice rather than re-teaching the calculus, which is why it responds well to daily work.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools where we might move within the UAE?
faqs.answer: Five bodies, with different scopes. Abu Dhabi sits with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai sits with KHDA. Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

faqs.question: Should I pay for a completed assignment to save my child time?
faqs.answer: No, and the price tells you how the market views it. A provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, roughly three months of genuine specialist tuition. Buying one is academic malpractice and the consequences land on the student, not the seller. We decline to produce assessed work of any kind. A tutor teaches, questions a draft and marks practice work; anything beyond that puts your child's own entry at risk.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Al Zahiyah need a MoHRE permit even for online lessons?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and the ministry's service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask any tutor you are considering to show you theirs; the permit is a document, not an assurance.

faqs.question: What happens at the review point if the marks have not moved?
faqs.answer: We say so, name which part of the plan was wrong, and change it. The review looks at the error log and the marked papers rather than at how the lessons felt, which is why the log exists. The three honest outcomes are that the diagnosis was wrong and needs redoing, that the diagnosis was right but the cadence is too thin for the gap, or that the time remaining is not enough for the category of problem identified. All three get stated plainly.

faqs.question: Can tuition in Year 11 still change my child's tier in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the limiting factor is administrative as well as mathematical. The school's final entry is submitted months before the papers, and the tier is fixed at that point. Even before that deadline, moving a student up requires content the Core or Foundation class may never have been taught, so it needs teaching time as well as a form. Ask the department when entries close and how much Extended-only content has been covered, and work backwards from the earlier of the two.

intro.heading: Baniyas, Mussafah or Mohammed Bin Zayed City: the maths problem does not change with the postcode
paragraphs: Baniyas sits on the mainland side of Abu Dhabi, east of Mussafah and south of the island, and a parent searching for an IGCSE maths tutor in Baniyas is nearly always comparing it against the next community over. The honest finding, after watching the same conversation play out across Baniyas, Shabia, Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Shamkha, is that the geography changes the commute and almost nothing else. A Year 11 student who cannot rearrange a formula has the same gap whether the family lives in Baniyas East or Mussafah Shabia 11. The syllabus is set in Cambridge, not in the emirate, and the mark scheme does not know which community the candidate drove in from.

What the postcode does change is the supply of people able to teach the gap. Baniyas is residential rather than school-dense: much of the enrolment travels out to the Mussafah and Shabia school belt, to Mohammed Bin Zayed City, or across to Khalifa City. That travel pattern works in reverse for in-home tutoring. A tutor who lives within a twenty-minute drive of Baniyas is a small pool, and inside that pool the number who have taught 0580 Paper 4 to a full grade boundary is smaller again. Families then accept whoever is close rather than whoever knows the paper, which is the single most expensive decision available in this market.

Online one-to-one removes the constraint without pretending the constraint does not exist. Delivered over live video, a Baniyas family is choosing from every available specialist rather than from the drivers willing to come east after Maghrib. A student on Extended with a persistent problem in bearings, similar-shape scale factors and compound percentage change needs someone who has marked those questions, and that person may well be nowhere near the Abu Dhabi mainland. The lesson still starts at 17:30 Gulf Standard Time, which is the part the family actually cares about.

This page is therefore built as a comparison rather than a brochure. It sets Baniyas against the communities a parent is likely weighing it against, sets Cambridge 0580 against Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 because Abu Dhabi schools use both, sets the market's AED rates against one another from the cheapest tier upward, and sets the June series against the November series as a resit route. Where the answer is the same for Baniyas and for Mussafah, it says so instead of inventing a local difference.

One thing is worth stating at the top because competitor pages in this search leave it unsaid. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India. The phrase parents type is 'tutor in Baniyas', so that is the phrase this page uses, but the delivery is live online video, one-to-one, and the comparison table further down puts real AED numbers against both options so you can judge the trade yourself.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-baniyas.subjectsIntro: Baniyas requests cluster on maths, but a student rarely needs only maths. These are the subjects most often added alongside, with the specific thing each one is tutored for rather than a general description.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 (Extended)
subjects.description: The default request. Work concentrates on algebraic manipulation, the non-calculator paper, functions and transformations, and the long structured questions where a method mark is lost in line two and never recovered. Past-paper work is done under timed conditions with the mark scheme open afterwards.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 (Core)
subjects.description: Often the quieter crisis: a student capped at grade C who needs a secure C rather than a reach for A. Sessions target number fluency, percentages, ratio, mensuration and the data-handling questions that carry reliable marks, and they build a question order for the paper so the easy marks are banked first.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: Graphics-calculator technique first: using the calculator to solve, not to check. Then the investigation paper, which rewards a written argument and penalises a bare answer. Students who treat it as 0580 with extra buttons tend to lose most in the extended investigation task.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, calculator permitted in both, graded 9 to 1. Higher tier work focuses on surds, algebraic proof, vectors and the multi-step problems at the back of each paper. Tier decisions are checked early, because a Foundation entry caps the grade at 5.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 4MA1 by stronger students in Abu Dhabi schools that offer it. Content runs into calculus, series and coordinate geometry, so it functions as an AS bridge. Tutoring is almost entirely technique on unfamiliar question structures rather than content coverage.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Added by maths students more often than any other subject, because the algebra is the same algebra. Work targets equation rearrangement under pressure, graph interpretation, and the practical paper's command terms, where answers lose marks for describing rather than explaining.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are a maths problem wearing a chemistry coat, and they are where Baniyas students most often ask for help. Sessions cover mole calculations, titration arithmetic, electrolysis products and the organic naming rules that generate quick, reliable marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Tutored for the data and statistics questions, the rate-of-reaction graphs, and the long six-mark responses where structure decides the grade. Students who revise biology by reading rather than writing answers under time are the ones whose mocks under-report what they know.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455
subjects.description: Chosen by Baniyas students planning a commerce route into Abu Dhabi universities. The tutoring focus is diagram accuracy, the difference between explain and evaluate, and the data-response paper, where candidates quote the extract instead of using it.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies alongside the international course
subjects.description: Mandatory UAE subjects run beside the licensed curriculum in private schools, and they take real timetable space. Support here is scheduling and study-method work so these subjects do not quietly absorb the hours a Year 11 maths candidate needs for past papers.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-baniyas.regionsTitle: Baniyas and the communities families compare it with

regions.name: Baniyas

regions.note: The nearest dense school belt, ten to twenty minutes from Baniyas depending on the industrial-area traffic. Many Baniyas candidates sit their papers at centres here, which makes the exams officer in Mussafah, not in Baniyas, the person to ask about zone timetables.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Larger villa community with its own school provision and a heavy IGCSE presence. Families here face the same in-home tutor scarcity as Baniyas, and for the same reason: the specialists cluster near the island and Khalifa City.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Hydra Village

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the course
modes.description: The pattern for a Year 10 or early Year 11 student who is behind rather than in trouble. One sixty-minute session a week, aligned to the school's scheme of work so the tutor is a week ahead of the class rather than a month behind it. Over a term this closes a specific list of topics rather than revising everything shallowly.

modes.description: The exam-term pattern. One session on content repair and one on timed past-paper work, with the mark scheme read aloud afterwards so the student learns what the examiner is actually crediting. This is also where paper order, non-calculator discipline and time management per mark are built, because those are what separate a predicted grade from an achieved one.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE maths tutor in Baniyas actually has to cover
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths tutor in Baniyas teaches one of three syllabuses: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1. The first question in a first session is therefore which of those three your child is entered for, and at which tier. Parents frequently do not know, and it is not a failure of attention: schools in Abu Dhabi often describe the course as 'IGCSE maths' in reports and newsletters without naming the code. The code is on the exam entry statement, and the school's exams officer will confirm it in a sentence.

The tier matters more than the code. On Cambridge 0580 the Core route is graded C to G and the Extended route A* to E, so a student on Core cannot be awarded an A regardless of how well they perform. On Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 the Foundation tier caps the grade at 5 while the Higher tier runs 9 to 4. A student aiming for an A-Level or Diploma maths route who is sitting the lower tier has a problem that no amount of tutoring in the final term can fix, because the ceiling is administrative rather than academic. Checking the entry in Year 10, while a move is still possible, is the single highest-value thing a parent in Baniyas can do.

Beyond codes and tiers, the content split is stable across all three. Number and arithmetic fluency, algebra and manipulation, functions and graphs, geometry and mensuration, trigonometry, vectors and transformations, probability and statistics. Tutoring that works does not march through that list in order. It starts with a full past paper sat under time, classifies every lost mark as a method error, an arithmetic slip, a misread question or genuine unknown content, and then spends the available weeks on whichever category is largest. For most Baniyas students who arrive after a weak mock, the largest category is method, not content, which is why more revision of the same notes rarely moves the grade.
bullets: Ask the school for the syllabus code and the tier in writing
Confirm which exam centre your child is entered at, and its Cambridge administrative zone
Sit one full past paper cold before buying any tutoring
Classify lost marks before choosing topics to revise

sections.heading: Baniyas against the next community over: what the postcode changes and what it does not
paragraphs: Here is the comparison this page exists to make. A parent in Baniyas, a parent in Mohammed Bin Zayed City and a parent in Al Shamkha are searching for the same thing and are usually told something vague about local coverage. The measurable differences between those communities are travel time, school density and the size of the in-home tutor pool. The differences that affect a grade are none of those. The syllabus, the papers, the mark scheme and the grade boundaries are identical for every candidate in the emirate, and in-home proximity has no effect on any of them.

What proximity does affect is what a family can realistically buy. In a community with few resident specialists, an in-home arrangement means either a long-travelling tutor charging a travel premium or a nearby generalist teaching a subject they do not examine. The second option is cheaper and much more common, and it is where money quietly disappears: twelve sessions with someone who can do the maths but has never read the 0580 mark scheme produces a student who is more confident and no better at scoring. Online removes the geography from the decision entirely, so the only variable left is whether the tutor knows the paper.

The table below sets out the comparison honestly, including the places where Baniyas is at a disadvantage. It is not an argument that Baniyas is a better place to study maths than Al Raha Beach. It is an argument that for this particular purchase the postcode is not the variable worth optimising, and that a family who accepts a nearby generalist because the drive is short has made the one trade that reliably costs a grade.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, since Abu Dhabi schools use both
paragraphs: Baniyas families often discover mid-course that the school down the road teaches a different IGCSE maths qualification from their own, and ask which is easier. Neither is easier in any way a parent can act on. They are different assessment designs with different risks, and the practical question is only ever which one your child is entered for, because the preparation differs in specifics that matter.

Cambridge 0580 Extended is assessed by two written papers of equal weight, and one of them is sat without a calculator. That single design feature drives most of the tutoring work, because a student who has used a calculator for every piece of arithmetic since Year 7 loses marks on exactly the questions they can do. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, which shifts the risk to the long multi-step problems at the back of each paper, where a correct method collapses because the candidate stopped reading after the first clause. Cambridge grades 0580 as A* to G; Pearson grades 4MA1 on the 9 to 1 scale, and a parent comparing two children's reports across the two systems should not assume a 7 and an A are the same thing.

Then there is the calendar. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE candidate plans around June with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For both boards, confirm the current syllabus specification and the live timetable on the board's own site rather than relying on a page like this one, because specifications are revised and we would rather send you to the source than restate a date that has moved.

sections.heading: Where Baniyas students lose IGCSE maths marks, in the order we see it
paragraphs: After enough diagnostic papers the losses stop looking random. The most common single cause is method collapse in multi-step questions: the student knows every individual step and still scores two out of five because the working is unreadable, a line is skipped, or an intermediate value is rounded early and carried forward. Examiners award method marks for visible correct method, and invisible correct method earns nothing. This is a habit problem, and habits respond to tutoring faster than content gaps do, which is why a block of six sessions sometimes moves a grade that a year of revision did not.

Second is non-calculator arithmetic on Cambridge 0580. Fractions, decimals, standard form, surd simplification where it appears, and percentage reverse problems. Students who have met these only with a calculator in hand treat the non-calculator paper as a different subject. The repair is drilling, in short bursts, not a lecture: ten minutes of mental and written arithmetic at the start of each session for a term rebuilds the fluency, and the gain shows on both papers because confidence on the early questions changes the pace of the whole hour.

Third is the cluster of topics students skip because they came late in the course and were never consolidated: bearings, similar-shape area and volume scale factors, compound percentage change, histograms with unequal class widths, and vectors. These carry predictable marks every series, and almost every student who arrives from a Baniyas school with a grade C mock has left most of them untouched. Fourth, and most fixable of all, is reading: the question asks for a reason and receives a calculation, or asks for an answer to three significant figures and receives a decimal that was correct two lines earlier. A mark-scheme walkthrough after every timed paper is the cheapest intervention in this whole list.
bullets: Write every step; an invisible method earns no method marks
Round only at the final answer and state the degree of accuracy asked for
Drill non-calculator arithmetic in short daily bursts, not in long sessions
Treat bearings, scale factors and histograms as guaranteed marks, not optional extras

sections.heading: What the Abu Dhabi market charges, cheapest tier first
paragraphs: Most pages in this search publish no price at all. Three of the six competitor pages measured for this project quote nothing, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Abu Dhabi family transacts in. So here is the market, in AED, from the cheapest tier upward, with the provider type that charges each band named and the figures attributed to the sources they came from rather than presented as ours.

At the bottom, university-student and budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. This tier can be good value for a Year 9 or Year 10 student who needs company while practising, and poor value for a Year 11 candidate who needs someone who has read the mark scheme. The middle band, a qualified subject tutor working online, runs roughly AED 150 to 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's Dubai rate table showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500.

Above that, IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted at roughly AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate showing AED 200 to 450 plus for exam-year specialists. Premium named or examiner-led tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED publishing AED 650. On a monthly basis the market shows packages around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page: the trial lesson is free, and a quote follows the diagnosis rather than preceding it.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for a Baniyas address, with the numbers attached
paragraphs: This is the comparison a parent searching for a tutor in Baniyas is actually making, so it deserves numbers rather than opinion. The in-home option costs more per hour in every published rate table, because travel is inside the price. From a Baniyas address the travel is not trivial: a specialist based on the island or in Khalifa City is looking at a round trip that eats more time than the lesson, and that time is billed, either openly as a premium or quietly as a shorter session.

The second cost is the pool. Choosing in-home from Baniyas means choosing from tutors willing to drive to Baniyas on a weekday evening, which is a different and much smaller set than tutors who can teach 0580 Extended well. Online inverts that: the family chooses the subject specialist and the travel question disappears. There are genuine losses in going online, and it is worth naming them rather than pretending otherwise. A young or easily distracted student is harder to supervise on screen. Written working is harder for a tutor to see unless the student uses a tablet or a document camera. Both are solvable, and both should be tested in the trial lesson rather than assumed.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and that is a deliberate model choice rather than a coverage gap: home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Saying so plainly matters, because two of the competitor pages in this search route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without ever stating where the tutor sits. sections.heading: The June series counted backwards, which no competitor page does
paragraphs: Every page in this search talks about exam preparation and none of them names a session, a deadline or a results point. That is strange, because the calendar is the only thing that makes a tutoring plan concrete. A Baniyas family deciding in which week to start is really asking how many teaching weeks remain before the papers, and that number is knowable.

Work backwards. The Cambridge final-entry deadline sits months before the papers, and it is set by the school's exams officer rather than by the family, so a tier change has to happen before it closes. Mocks usually fall a full term before the series, which makes them the last useful diagnostic with enough runway to act on. The exam window itself consumes revision time rather than creating it. Results reach centres before they reach candidates, and the window for a review of results or a remark opens immediately afterwards and closes quickly. For the November series, which is the resit route for UAE candidates, Pearson's published pattern is instructive: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Two cautions. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, because it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after reading the wrong version; a Baniyas student sitting at a Mussafah centre must use that centre's zone. And the February/March series is offered to India only, so no Abu Dhabi revision plan should reference it. Always open the live official timetable on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com rather than trusting a restated date, including the dates on this page.

sections.heading: ADEK, the regulator map, and what a school report does not tell you
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi, including every school a Baniyas family is likely to use, are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. This matters to a tutoring decision in a specific way: the school's internal report tells you how your child is doing against that school's cohort, while the inspection framework tells you something about the school itself, and neither tells you how your child would score against a Cambridge grade boundary. Only a past paper sat under time does that.

The regulator map across the UAE is worth knowing if your household straddles emirates, which many Baniyas and Al Ghadeer families do. Dubai private schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK. Sharjah sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not merely inspection sits at emirate level there.

One mandatory-subject point affects Year 11 timetables directly. Across UAE private schools, Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum. In Dubai, KHDA's published guidance requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. The same federal baseline applies nationally: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies. For a Baniyas maths candidate the consequence is practical rather than political, since those lessons occupy timetable space, and a revision plan that ignores them overestimates the hours available.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE, and how can you check?
paragraphs: This question goes unanswered on almost every page in this search, and it has a clear answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and it is granted free of charge for two years. If anyone quotes you a permit fee, that is a signal about them rather than about the rules.

Eligibility is broader than parents expect. The permit covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no page should quote an amount, and several that circulate online do.

Two further points apply specifically in Abu Dhabi. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct has been reported as barring the same thing. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document before relying on it. The practical consequence is that marketing which offers you your child's own class teacher privately is offering something an Abu Dhabi family should decline. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram is an online matching platform with no UAE premises, and it holds no regulator accreditation; it would be a serious misrepresentation to suggest otherwise.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a maths tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Maths looks like the safest subject for this question and it is not, because the coursework element arrives later. An IGCSE maths candidate has no Internal Assessment on 0580 or 4MA1, but Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 carries an investigation component, and any student continuing into the IB Diploma will write a mathematics exploration worth a fifth of the final subject grade. So the boundary has to be set in Year 10, before it is being tested under deadline pressure.

The boundary is simple to state. A tutor teaches, explains, models technique, sets practice, marks it and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not produce your child's assessed work, does not supply text to be submitted, and does not edit a draft to the point where the thinking is no longer the student's. That is not squeamishness: one page in this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student at risk of malpractice proceedings, not the seller. Buying it is the student's exposure.

In practice the honest version is more useful anyway. On a 0607 investigation a tutor can teach what an investigative write-up has to contain, show a worked example on a different problem, and give feedback on the student's own attempt against the criteria. On an IB mathematics exploration, the assessment criteria are published by letter with their mark allocations, and a tutor can teach what each criterion rewards so the student writes to it. We also do not publish or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

process.title: Tell us the code, the tier and the problem
process.description: A short message naming the syllabus code if you have it, the tier, the last mock grade and the target. If you do not have the code, say which school your child attends in the Baniyas catchment and we will ask the right question in the first session instead of guessing.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a working session, not a sales call. The tutor sets two or three questions pitched at the tier, watches the method rather than the answers, and tells you at the end which of the four error categories is costing the most marks. The trial is free with no card required.

process.title: A written plan with a topic order
process.description: After the trial you receive the topics to address, in the order they will be taught, with the reason each one is in that position. For a Year 11 candidate it also states how many teaching weeks remain before the June series and what each block has to achieve.

process.title: Weekly sessions in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: A fixed evening slot after the Baniyas school run, usually between 16:00 and 21:00. Rescheduling is a message rather than a logistics problem, because nobody is travelling. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing on request.

process.title: Review every six sessions, change if needed
process.description: At the six-session mark the tutor reports what has moved and what has not, measured on timed questions rather than impressions. If the match is wrong we change the tutor; a family who feels obliged to persist with a poor match is the failure mode this review exists to prevent.

whyPoints.title: The specialist is chosen before the geography
whyPoints.description: A Baniyas family searching locally is choosing from the people willing to drive east on a weekday evening. Choosing online means choosing by syllabus code and tier instead, which is the variable that actually affects the mark. The travel question stops being part of the decision.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure here has a source

faqs.question: Can we get an IGCSE maths tutor in Baniyas who comes to the house?
faqs.answer: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and lessons for Baniyas families are delivered one-to-one over live video instead. The Abu Dhabi in-home market does exist and is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, so the premium is real. The bigger difference is the pool: in-home from Baniyas means choosing among tutors willing to drive east midweek, while online means choosing the person who actually teaches your child's syllabus code and tier.

faqs.question: Does living in Baniyas rather than Khalifa City change my child's IGCSE maths result?
faqs.answer: No. The syllabus, the papers, the mark scheme and the grade boundaries are identical for every candidate in the emirate, so the address has no effect on the mark. What the address changes is supply. Baniyas is residential rather than school-dense, so the pool of nearby subject specialists is small, and families often accept a nearby generalist because the drive is short. That trade is where grades are lost. Delivered online, the geography drops out of the decision entirely and the only remaining variable is whether the tutor knows the paper your child is sitting.

faqs.question: Which maths syllabus is my child in a Mussafah or Baniyas school actually sitting?
faqs.answer: It is one of three: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1. Schools in Abu Dhabi often write only 'IGCSE maths' in reports, so parents frequently do not know. The code appears on the exam entry statement, and the school's exams officer will confirm it in one email along with the tier. Ask for both, in writing. The code decides whether a calculator is permitted in every paper and whether an investigation component exists, and the tier sets the grade ceiling, so no revision plan is reliable without them.

faqs.question: What is the grade ceiling if my child is entered for 0580 Core instead of Extended?
faqs.answer: Cambridge grades the 0580 Core route C to G, so an A is not available on that entry no matter how the candidate performs. The Extended route runs A* to E. Pearson Edexcel works the same way with different labels: the 4MA1 Foundation tier caps at 5 while Higher runs 9 to 4. This is an administrative ceiling rather than an academic one, which is why it has to be checked in Year 10 while an entry change is still possible. A student aiming at an A-Level or IB Diploma maths route who is sitting the lower tier has a problem late tutoring cannot solve.

faqs.question: Why does the non-calculator paper cause Baniyas students so much trouble?
faqs.answer: Because most students have used a calculator for arithmetic since Year 7, and Cambridge 0580 assesses one of its two equally weighted papers without one. The questions themselves are not harder; the candidate simply cannot execute work they genuinely understand. Fractions, decimals, standard form and reverse percentages are the usual casualties. The repair is short daily drilling rather than long sessions, and it pays twice: the fluency gain also changes the pace of the calculator paper, because less time is spent on the early questions and more remains for the long ones at the back.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Year 11 candidate in Baniyas usually need before June?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the diagnostic finds, and the honest range is wide. A student whose losses are mostly method and reading errors often moves a grade in six to ten sessions, because habits respond faster than content gaps. A student with four or five untaught topics needs a term or more, typically one content session and one timed-paper session each week. We do not promise a grade, and anyone who does should be treated with caution. What we will give you after the trial is a count of remaining teaching weeks and what each block has to achieve.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tutoring eight weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a narrowed plan. Eight weeks is not enough to teach a syllabus, and it is enough to repair method, drill non-calculator arithmetic and sit timed papers weekly with the mark scheme read afterwards. The first session sits a full paper cold, and every lost mark is classified as a method error, an arithmetic slip, a misread question or unknown content. The largest category gets the weeks. Trying to cover everything in eight weeks produces a calmer student with the same grade, which is the outcome parents most regret paying for.

faqs.question: What do Abu Dhabi families actually pay for IGCSE maths support?
faqs.answer: Published market rates, cheapest first: budget online and university-student tutors from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified online subject tutor runs about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium examiner-led tutoring reaches AED 650 at BartyED. Those are market figures from provider pages, not IB Gram prices; our trial is free and a quote follows the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit, and what should I ask to see?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Ask any tutor to show the permit, and treat a quoted permit fee as a warning sign. Working without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published.

faqs.question: Could my child's own maths teacher at a Baniyas catchment school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: It has been reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars the same arrangement. Verify the current wording against the ADEK policy document before relying on it, because press reporting is not the policy itself. The practical answer for a Baniyas family is to decline any offer of your child's own class teacher privately, and to ask instead for a tutor with no connection to the school your child attends.

faqs.question: When do UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE maths, and is there a March option?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February/March series is offered to India only, so no Abu Dhabi revision plan should reference it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, since it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after reading the wrong version. Confirm your centre's zone with the exams officer and open the live timetable on the board's own site.

faqs.question: My child sits exams at a Mussafah centre but we live in Baniyas. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters for the timetable rather than for the teaching. The centre, not your home address, determines which Cambridge administrative zone applies, and Cambridge is explicit that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. So ask the Mussafah centre's exams officer which zone it sits in, and build the revision calendar on that version. The journey itself is worth a dry run in exam week so the morning of the first paper holds no surprises.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Cambridge 0607 investigation task?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the academic-honesty boundary. A tutor can teach what an investigative write-up has to contain, work a comparable example on a different problem, and give feedback on your child's own attempt against the published criteria. A tutor does not supply text for submission and does not edit a draft until the thinking stops being the student's. One page ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that exposes the student to malpractice proceedings rather than the seller, which is why our boundary is published rather than quietly flexible.

faqs.question: How does an online maths lesson actually work when the student needs to show working?
faqs.answer: Working is the whole subject, so this is the right thing to test in the free trial. Most students write on a tablet with a stylus into a shared whiteboard, which the tutor sees stroke by stroke and can annotate. The alternative is paper under a phone or document camera, which works and is clumsier. Either way the tutor watches the method as it forms, which is often more diagnostic than seeing a finished page. If neither arrangement suits your child, the trial is where you find that out before any money is committed.

faqs.question: Can a Baniyas family shift session times during Ramadan or school assessment weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sessions shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan on request, and families often reduce frequency during the school's own assessment weeks and increase it afterwards. Because nobody is travelling, a reschedule is a message rather than a logistics problem, which is a practical advantage from a Baniyas address where an in-home tutor's cancelled journey is usually chargeable. We would rather a family paused for a fortnight and resumed than paid for sessions a student attended exhausted.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's exact subject and tier?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting quietly. For a narrow combination, such as Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 at a specific evening slot, the match can take longer, and in that case you are told the expected wait and offered the nearest alternative with the difference explained. Non-UAE-based specialists teaching the same syllabus are part of the roster and the lesson runs in Gulf Standard Time either way. Concealing a coverage limit is how families end up with an approximate match, which is the thing this page spends most of its length arguing against.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-baniyas.closingHeading: Start with one paper, not with a package
abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-baniyas.closingBody: If your child is in a Baniyas catchment school and the maths grade has slipped, the cheapest useful next step costs nothing. Ask the school for the syllabus code and the tier in writing, then book a free trial lesson and let the tutor set two or three questions at that tier and watch the method. At the end you will know which of the four error categories is costing the most marks, how many teaching weeks remain before the June series, and whether the current entry is right. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled after the school run. If the diagnosis is all you want, take it and stop there.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-corniche.tutorsIntro: Corniche mathematics enquiries arrive in two kinds: a tier question and a weeks-left question. Both are answerable with the school's own dates and a marked paper, and we match from the answer to a tutor who teaches that specification weekly.

intro.heading: Four dated decisions, and a weekly routine
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics has no coursework with either board. Two timed written papers carry the whole grade, which removes every opportunity to bank marks slowly and makes everything that leads to those two mornings a scheduling problem. Four decisions sit on that path, each with a date attached, and all four are routinely made by default rather than by anybody choosing. Three of them are owned by the school rather than by you, which means they are settled by a single email or not at all.

The first is the tier. Cambridge enters candidates at Core or Extended and Pearson at Foundation or Higher, and the entry caps the grade: C with Cambridge Core, 5 with Pearson Foundation. That ceiling is fixed for a series once final entries are submitted, which happens months before the papers. Most families learn about it at confirmation, by which point the upper-tier content has not been taught.

The second is the series. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson runs May, June and November, and its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The third is whether to use November as a repair route: November 2025 Pearson results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a resit produces a grade the following January rather than the same summer.

The fourth is less obvious and purely practical: what a normal week looks like from January onwards. Most students revise in bursts triggered by anxiety, which produces long unproductive evenings and no measurable progress. A plain weekly shape, with one timed section, one error-correction session and one rest day written into it, outperforms twice the hours spent reactively.

The Corniche is apartment living along the waterfront, with schools a short drive inland towards Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and Al Khalidiyah. Journeys are short, which means the limiting factor is the week rather than the road. It also means tower logistics matter: visitor parking, reception and lift waits consume paid minutes that no hourly rate itemises, and mathematics wants two sessions a week rather than one, so whatever that access cost is, it applies twice.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to the Corniche is one-to-one teaching over live video. The rest of this page covers the dated decisions, the formulae sheet, the weekly cycle, the two papers and their different demands, the entry choice, the final weekends and what each phase costs. Every figure carries its source and the month it was read, because a date or a price a parent acts on has to be checkable.
