abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-corniche.programmesIntro: The British mathematics pathway has three stages and the decisions available narrow at each one. Knowing which decisions are still open is more useful than knowing which topics are weak.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 mathematics, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Fractions, negatives, index laws and basic rearrangement are built here and assumed by both IGCSE specifications. Nothing is examined, so nothing feels urgent, and that is precisely the problem: a Year 10 student who rearranges slowly loses time in every question for two years rather than marks in one topic.
programmes.countryNote: Corniche Key Stage 3 students attend schools a short drive inland and are commonly home before 15:15 with the lightest workload in the house. Two short sessions a week on manipulation alone, at the budget end of the market, is the highest-return mathematics spend available to a family here and almost nobody buys it.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics, year one
programmes.description: Half the specification taught and the tier provisionally decided. This is the only stage where all four dated decisions are still fully open, which makes it the cheapest and most influential point to involve anybody. Habits also form here: shown working, units, diagram discipline on bearings and vectors.
programmes.countryNote: Email the school this term and ask three things in writing: the tier your child is provisionally entered for, the maximum grade it allows, and the last date a change can be submitted. Those three answers are worth more to a Corniche family than any amount of comparing local tutors.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics, examination year
programmes.description: Final entries fixed, mocks sat, study leave, then two papers in the June or November series. From January the useful work is conversion rather than coverage: shown working, pacing, mark-scheme reading and a shrinking error list. Content teaching keeps its value only where a topic is genuinely unseen.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools release students for parts of mock season, which gives Corniche families a daytime window that does not exist in normal term. Because journeys inland are short, that fortnight is unusually usable here, and the marked script is at its freshest at the same moment.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-corniche.subjectsIntro: These are the areas that decide an IGCSE mathematics grade, with the point in the calendar where each is best addressed.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Should be automatic before January, because nearly every upper-tier question routes through it. A student rearranging slowly loses time across the whole paper rather than marks in one topic, which makes this the first thing any calendar-led plan secures.

subjects.name: Reverse percentages
subjects.description: The most reliably mishandled topic at this level: students multiply where they should divide and lose every mark in the question. A one or two-week fix at any point in the year, and therefore ideal work for the fortnight immediately after mocks.

subjects.name: Similar shapes and scale factors
subjects.description: Length, area and volume scale by different powers of the ratio and the length factor gets applied to all three. Self-contained, appears regularly, and clears in about a week of deliberate practice, which makes it a reliable early win in a short plan.

subjects.name: Upper and lower bounds
subjects.description: Choosing the correct bound in a division or subtraction. Taught once in Year 10 and rarely revisited, so it is almost always worth one deliberate week in the Year 11 autumn before past papers begin in earnest.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules with three-figure bearings measured clockwise from north, plus the ambiguous case of the sine rule that many students do not know exists. Rewards practice over several weeks, so it belongs before Christmas rather than in April.

subjects.name: Cumulative frequency and histograms
subjects.description: Histograms with unequal class widths need frequency density and students plot raw frequency instead. Statistics topics are good late work because they are self-contained and do not depend on earlier material being secure.

subjects.name: Probability trees
subjects.description: Without replacement is where the marks sit, because the second branch denominators change. Students draw the tree correctly then reuse the original denominators, producing a plausible answer and no credit. Two weeks of annotated practice removes it.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vector arithmetic and fully described transformations: a rotation needs centre and direction, an enlargement needs scale factor and centre. Descriptive precision is the mark, which makes this a two-week fix at any point.

subjects.name: Shown working as a habit
subjects.description: Multi-stage questions award method marks for visible steps, so computing mentally and writing one line forfeits most of them. This is a habit rather than a topic and takes two to four weeks to install, which is why it cannot be left to April.

subjects.name: Pacing
subjects.description: Marks divided by minutes gives a rate a student can act on mid-paper. Combined with the discipline of abandoning a stuck question and returning to it, this is often worth a grade boundary on its own and takes about two sessions to teach.

sections.heading: The dated decisions, in the order they expire
paragraphs: Most mathematics problems presented to us as teaching problems are partly decision problems with deadlines nobody noticed. The table below lists them in the order they expire, with who owns each and what missing it costs. None requires a tutor to resolve; all of them require somebody to ask, and the asking is usually a single email to the school office.

The tier is the most consequential. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grade at C and a Pearson Foundation entry at 5, and the cap is fixed for a series once final entries are submitted months ahead of the papers. The school is usually right about the tier; the problem is that the decision is handled as administration, so a family finds out at confirmation rather than while it could still change.

Access arrangements sit alongside it and are more final still. Where a student needs them, they must be applied for with supporting evidence before the entry deadline and cannot be arranged retrospectively. A known need that has never been discussed in writing is the most avoidable loss on this list, and it is also the one families are least likely to raise unprompted.

The last item, the weekly routine, has no external deadline and expires anyway. A student who has not established a workable weekly shape by the end of January will spend the spring revising reactively, in long unproductive evenings triggered by anxiety. That is a decision about habits rather than dates, and it is the one a tutor can most directly help make.

sections.heading: What the formulae sheet gives you, and what it does not
paragraphs: Both boards print some formulae on the paper and expect others to be held in memory, and the two lists are not the same. This is one of the most practically useful things a student can establish early, because it tells them exactly what to commit to memory and, equally importantly, what not to waste effort memorising. Almost nobody checks.

The general shape, which should be verified against the current syllabus document for your child's code, is that the less intuitive results tend to be provided and the foundational ones are not. Trigonometric rules for non-right-angled triangles and the volumes and surface areas of the more complex solids are commonly printed. Circle formulae, Pythagoras, the basic trigonometric ratios, gradient and midpoint, and compound growth are commonly expected from memory.

Both boards have revised their printed lists in recent years, which is why this page describes the pattern rather than restating a list that may have changed. Open the current syllabus document on the board's own site, find the formulae page, and print it. Then have your child annotate it: provided, memorise, and not needed at this tier. That exercise takes twenty minutes and saves weeks of misdirected memorisation.

The second half of this is knowing how to use what is printed. A student who has never practised with the sheet in front of them loses time locating a formula under pressure, and a student who has practised only with it loses marks when a required result is not on it. Every timed practice section should be done under the real conditions, with the real sheet, from January onwards.

sections.heading: The weekly cycle that works from January onwards
paragraphs: From January the question stops being what to revise and becomes when. Most students revise reactively, in long evenings triggered by anxiety, which feels like effort and produces very little that is measurable. A written weekly shape, repeated, outperforms twice the hours spent unplanned, and it also makes it obvious when a week has been lost rather than discovering it a month later.

The shape below is deliberately modest, which is the point. It contains one timed section, one error-correction session, two short practice slots, a tutoring session and a genuine rest day. A plan with no rest day in it is a plan that will be abandoned, and the abandonment usually takes the useful parts with it. Written down, it also lets a parent see at a glance whether the week happened.

Two features matter more than the rest. The timed section comes before the error correction rather than after, because the errors have to exist before they can be worked on. And the error log is cumulative rather than weekly: the same sheet grows and shrinks across the whole spring, which is the only honest measure of whether the plan is working.

On the Corniche this routine is easier to run on video than in person, because it wants two contacts a week. Two visits a week means two rounds of visitor parking, reception and lift waits, and a tutor arriving ten minutes late twice weekly is a real share of what you are paying for. The hour starting on the hour matters twice as much when there are two of them.

sections.heading: Two papers, two different revision jobs
paragraphs: The two boards structure their mathematics papers differently and that changes what revision should look like. Cambridge 0580 separates its papers so that a candidate sits one without a calculator and one with. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both of its papers. Neither board includes coursework, so these two papers carry everything.

For a Cambridge candidate this means two distinct jobs. Non-calculator practice has to be deliberate and regular: fraction arithmetic, long multiplication, surds, estimation and exact values all have to be genuinely automatic, because under time pressure slow mental arithmetic consumes the minutes needed for the harder questions. That practice cannot be introduced in April and expected to work.

For a Pearson candidate the risk inverts. With a calculator available throughout, the temptation is to reach for it on work that should be instant, losing seconds repeatedly across a hundred marks. The compensating discipline is estimation: a student who sanity-checks a calculator answer against a rough mental estimate catches the keying errors that otherwise pass unnoticed and cost whole questions.

Both candidates share one structural fact worth planning around. With no coursework anywhere in the subject, pacing is a first-order skill rather than an afterthought. Marks divided by minutes gives a rate; writing that rate at the top of the paper gives a student something to check against mid-question; and practising abandonment, leaving a question with a mark or two taken and returning later, is what converts the rate into marks.

sections.heading: June now or November later
paragraphs: Where a student is clearly short of the grade they need, the entry itself becomes a decision rather than a given, and it is a decision with a date. Sitting in the June series produces a result in August; using November produces one the following January, as happened when November 2025 Pearson results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those two timings suit very different situations.

November works where a post-16 place can hold a conditional grade, and mathematics is one of the better subjects for it. The content is already taught, the gap is usually technique, and technique responds quickly to a focused three-month build. A student who sat June with eight weeks of poorly directed revision behind them is in a materially better position in November with twelve well-directed weeks.

November does not work where a firm grade is needed in September, which is the common case for a school's own sixth form entry. In that situation the realistic options are an enquiry about results, submitted by the school within a board deadline on defined grounds, or acceptance and a conversation about which post-16 courses remain open with the grade achieved.

Cambridge candidates in the UAE have the same two series available: June and November. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not available here, whatever a generic revision website lists. Always check the live official timetable on the board's own site, and note that Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with different timetables.

sections.heading: The last five weekends
paragraphs: In the final stretch the weekdays belong largely to school, and the weekends become the only blocks of time a student controls. Most families leave them unplanned, which means they are either lost entirely or filled with undirected re-reading. Planning five weekends specifically is a small piece of work with a measurable return.

The structure below allocates each weekend a job. Full paper, then review. Full paper, then the highest-frequency errors. Then the papers stop and pacing takes over, because by that point a student who has done four full papers under timing knows their content position and what remains is execution. The last weekend does almost nothing deliberately, which parents find counter-intuitive and students need.

Two things get dropped across all five weekends. Topics that appear rarely and are not understood should be abandoned rather than learned badly; the hours are worth more on high-frequency marks. And re-reading notes should stop entirely, because at this stage it produces a strong feeling of progress with almost no measurable return. Both decisions feel wrong and both reliably raise the final mark.

A note on honesty about limits. Five well-used weekends plus a sensible weekly routine can move a grade boundary. They will not move three, and no provider can guarantee a grade or an improvement, including us. What a diagnostic session can give you is a realistic estimate based on the script in front of us, which is more useful than a promise.

sections.heading: Corniche logistics, Ramadan and the weeks that are not there
paragraphs: A plan built on calendar weeks rather than teaching weeks will break. Most Abu Dhabi private schools run three terms with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break towards the end of March, and the spring break falls squarely inside the period this page describes as the from-January routine.

Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year and currently falls in the spring, increasingly overlapping the weeks before the May and June papers. Schools shorten the day, which frees the afternoon, but the freed afternoon is a weak window for mathematics specifically because arithmetic accuracy degrades sharply when a household is fasting and preparing. A post-Iftar slot, commonly 20:30 to 22:00, works considerably better.

The Corniche logistics point is worth stating plainly because it is specific to this kind of housing. Visitor parking in a waterfront tower is often full at the hour tutors arrive, reception takes minutes, and lifts at five in the afternoon are slow. For a subject that wants two contacts a week, that access cost doubles, and it appears in nobody's quoted rate. Online delivery removes it entirely.

Count the real weeks before agreeing anything. Take the paper date, subtract the spring break, subtract study leave, subtract Ramadan if your household reduces sessions then, and subtract travel you already know about. Most Corniche families find the usable figure four to six weeks below their first estimate, and a weekly routine designed for sixteen weeks that actually has ten fails in a predictable way.

sections.heading: What each phase costs, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Mathematics support costs more per grade point in the spring than in the Year 10 autumn, which is market behaviour rather than a judgement. Demand concentrates before papers, the formats families want then are intensive, and specialists able to work on a named paper are the scarcest part of the market. The same outcome bought earlier simply costs less.

The Abu Dhabi bands, with sources named, run as follows. University-student tutors online advertise from around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik on their own pages. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase quoting around AED 270. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named tutors have been quoted to AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. None of these figures is our price list. They are the market, published with attribution so that any quote you receive, including ours, can be measured against something.

What we will not claim: no provider can guarantee a grade, a score or an improvement, including us. No regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram, we hold no ADEK or MoHRE approval, and there is no Abu Dhabi office. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and we will show you how to verify a tutor's.

process.title: Ask the school the three tier questions
process.description: In writing: which tier in each examined subject, the maximum grade it allows, and the last date a change can be submitted. Those three answers settle the most consequential dated decision in the two years, and they are worth more than any amount of comparing local tutors.

process.title: Print the formulae page from the syllabus
process.description: Open the current syllabus document for your child's code on the board's own site, find the formulae page and print it. Have your child annotate it: provided, memorise, not needed at this tier. Twenty minutes of work that prevents weeks of misdirected memorisation.

process.title: Send the marked mathematics paper
process.description: We classify every lost mark as content, question wording, unshown working or timing. In mathematics the working category is usually larger than families expect and the cheapest to fix. The tally decides the plan and routinely contradicts what the student assumed.

process.title: Write the weekly cycle down
process.description: One timed section, one marking session, two short practice slots, a longer weekend block and a genuine rest day. Written down, it is obvious when a week has been lost. A plan with no rest day in it will be abandoned and will take the useful parts with it.

process.title: Review the error log at the halfway point
process.description: The log is cumulative across the whole spring, not weekly, which makes it the only honest measure of progress. If the recurring errors have not stopped by the halfway point, we change the tutor, the focus or the diagnosis rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: Dated decisions raised before they expire
whyPoints.description: Tier, access arrangements, series and the weekly routine all have deadlines, and three of the four are owned by the school rather than by you. We list them in the order they expire and tell you exactly what to ask for in writing.

whyPoints.title: The formulae sheet separated out
whyPoints.description: Both boards print some formulae and expect others from memory, and the lists differ and have been revised. We work from your child's current syllabus document rather than a revision guide, which prevents weeks of memorising things that will be printed anyway.

whyPoints.title: A written weekly routine, with a rest day
whyPoints.description: Reactive revision feels like effort and produces little that is measurable. A plain repeated weekly shape outperforms twice the hours, and including a genuine rest day is what stops the whole plan being abandoned in week three.

whyPoints.title: Board differences planned around
whyPoints.description: Cambridge separates a non-calculator paper; Pearson allows a calculator on both. Those are two different revision jobs: deliberate mental arithmetic for one, estimation discipline for the other. We match on the code so the right job gets done.

faqs.question: What should we ask an IGCSE maths tutor in the Corniche before booking?
faqs.answer: Which specification they teach weekly, whether a calculator is permitted on both of your child's papers, and what the grade ceiling of your child's tier is. All three are published facts, so hesitation is itself the answer. Then ask what the first session will produce: a good answer is a classification of lost marks you can check against the script, and a vague one tells you the engagement will be hours rather than a plan.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor into a Corniche tower?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard, so every line of working is visible and saved. The logistics argument is sharper for mathematics than for other subjects, because it wants two sessions a week, which doubles the parking, reception and lift cost of any visiting arrangement.

faqs.question: Which maths formulae does my child actually have to memorise?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board and the code, and both have revised their printed lists in recent years, so check the current syllabus document on the board's own site rather than a revision guide. The usual pattern is that less intuitive results are provided, such as the sine and cosine rules and the volumes of more complex solids, while foundational ones are expected from memory: circle formulae, Pythagoras, the basic trigonometric ratios, gradient and midpoint, and compound growth.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether we practise with the formulae sheet?
faqs.answer: It matters in both directions. A student who has never practised with the sheet in front of them loses time locating a formula under pressure, and a student who has practised only with it loses marks when a required result turns out not to be on it. Every timed section from January onwards should be done under real conditions with the real sheet, which also makes the annotation exercise of provided, memorise and not needed genuinely useful.

faqs.question: What should a normal revision week look like from January?
faqs.answer: One timed section under examination conditions, one session marking it aloud and classifying the errors, two short practice slots on the highest-frequency error, a longer weekend block, a short Sunday recall, and one genuine rest day. The timed section comes before the marking, because the errors have to exist before they can be worked on. Written down, this beats twice the hours spent reactively and makes a lost week obvious immediately rather than a month later.

faqs.question: Is a rest day really worth building into a Year 11 plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the item most often cut first. A plan with no rest day in it gets abandoned, and the abandonment takes the useful parts with it rather than just the excess. One day a week with nothing scheduled makes the other six sustainable from January through to the papers, which is five months. Students who maintain a modest routine for five months reliably outperform students who maintain an ambitious one for three weeks.

faqs.question: Which maths paper should we worry about more?
faqs.answer: The one your board makes harder for your child, and that differs. Cambridge separates its papers so a candidate sits one without a calculator, which exposes slow mental arithmetic; that paper needs deliberate non-calculator practice from the autumn. Pearson permits a calculator on both, which creates the opposite risk: reaching for it on work that should be instant and losing seconds across a hundred marks. The Pearson discipline is estimation, to catch keying errors.

faqs.question: Can a Corniche school still move my child up a maths tier this term?
faqs.answer: When final entries are submitted, which is months before the papers. Up to that point a Cambridge Core or Pearson Foundation entry can in principle be changed; afterwards the grade ceiling of C or 5 is fixed for the series. Ask the school in writing for the tier in each examined subject, the maximum grade it allows and the last date a change can be submitted. Those three answers are routinely available and almost never volunteered.

faqs.question: Should we consider November rather than June?
faqs.answer: If the gap is technique rather than content and a post-16 place can hold a conditional grade, yes, and mathematics is one of the better subjects for it. The content is already taught and technique responds quickly to a focused three-month build. November results arrive the following January, as happened when November 2025 Pearson results reached students on 22 January 2026. It does not work where a firm grade is needed in September, which is the common sixth-form case.

faqs.question: Is there a February maths sitting for Abu Dhabi students?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so no candidate in the UAE sits it however many revision websites list its deadlines. UAE candidates sit June and November with Cambridge, and May, June or November with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Check your own school's timetable on the board's site, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and the timetable differs between them.

faqs.question: How should the final five weekends be used?
faqs.answer: Give each one a job. Five out: a full Paper 1 under timing, marked on the Sunday. Four out: a full Paper 2, then drill the two highest-frequency errors. Three out: a paper from a different series, marked aloud. Two out: timed sections only, focused on pacing. One out: one short section, then rest. Across all five, re-reading notes stops entirely and rare topics still not understood are abandoned deliberately rather than learned badly.

faqs.question: My daughter's answers are right but marks are missing, so what now?
faqs.answer: Working that is not visible. Multi-stage questions allocate method marks to steps, so computing mentally and writing a single line collects the answer mark and forfeits the rest. On a paper with several such questions that habit alone can be worth a grade boundary. It takes two to four weeks to install as a habit rather than a rule, which is why it belongs in the autumn and not in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change how we should plan maths revision?
faqs.answer: It changes the hour rather than the plan. Schools shorten the day, which frees the afternoon, but arithmetic accuracy degrades sharply when a household is fasting and preparing, so the freed afternoon is a weak window for mathematics specifically. A post-Iftar slot, commonly 20:30 to 22:00, works considerably better and is easy to staff on video because nobody is driving. Families who prefer to pause can do that; decide in advance rather than losing the weeks.

faqs.question: How many real weeks are left before the maths papers?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the calendar implies. Subtract the spring break, which most Abu Dhabi schools take towards the end of March. Subtract the weeks your school reserves for study leave. Subtract Ramadan if your household reduces sessions. Subtract travel you already know about. Most Corniche families find the figure four to six weeks below their first estimate, and a weekly routine designed for sixteen weeks that actually has ten will fail in a predictable way.

faqs.question: What if you cannot staff two maths sessions a week for us?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and sometimes offer one plus set work rather than pretending two are available. The spring is the tightest part of the Abu Dhabi year and Corniche households compete with Al Reem, Al Bateen and Saadiyat families for early-evening slots. Common tiers usually match within a few days; a fixed weekday pair of hours can take longer. Being told early leaves you time to try elsewhere while it still matters.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-corniche.closingBody: Ask the school for the tier, the grade it caps at, and the last date it can change. Print the formulae page from the current syllabus. Send us both along with the most recent marked paper, and we will tell you which dated decisions are still open, which topics to clear and which to abandon, and what a weekly routine should look like from January. Then your child meets a specialist in that specification on a free trial lesson, live online, one to one, twice a week where the week allows.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-eastern-m.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below teaches one IGCSE mathematics specification rather than mathematics broadly. That matters because the two main boards differ on calculator rules, tiering and the shape of their longest questions, and past papers from the wrong board feel productive while teaching the wrong habits.

intro.heading: Find the code before you find the tutor
paragraphs: The most useful ten minutes a parent in this neighbourhood can spend on IGCSE mathematics is not spent looking for a tutor. It is spent emailing the school's examinations officer and asking, in writing, for the syllabus code and tier on their child's entry. The answer comes back as something like Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher, and it determines everything that follows: which papers are sat, whether a calculator is allowed in each, what the highest available grade is, and which past papers are worth the student's evenings.

This matters more in Abu Dhabi than in most places, because the school mix here is unusually varied. Within a short drive of the mangrove channel there are British-curriculum schools entering Cambridge, others entering Pearson, and IB continuum schools where mathematics looks nothing like either. Families with two children at two schools quite often have two different boards in the house, and a well-meaning tutor working from the wrong specification will drill question styles that will not appear on the paper.

Once the code is known, the subject becomes tractable. IGCSE mathematics has no coursework on either main board. The whole grade sits in written papers, which means every mark is recoverable by practice and technique rather than by a submission deadline that has already passed. That is genuinely good news, and it is why mathematics responds faster to focused tutoring than almost any other IGCSE subject.

IB Gram delivers that tutoring to UAE families one-to-one over live video rather than by visiting homes; in-home teaching is a service we run only in India. For mathematics the online format has a specific advantage: a shared screen means both people write on the same working, so a tutor sees the exact line where a method collapsed rather than a finished answer. Marks in this subject are lost inside the working, and the working is what a shared screen exposes.

The rest of this page is the mathematics itself. The two boards side by side. What the tier decision does to the grade ceiling and when it closes. The six topics that generate most of the lost marks in marked papers from this emirate. Why the non-calculator paper behaves differently from the calculator one. How to build a past-paper diet that improves a mark rather than filling an evening. And what the Abu Dhabi market charges, attributed, so the spending decision is made with real numbers.

One last framing point before the detail. Mathematics is the IGCSE subject where tutoring has the clearest mechanism, because there is no coursework mark to protect, no practical to arrange and no essay style to acquire. There is a specification, a set of papers and a mark scheme, and the distance between a student's current mark and their possible mark is made of identifiable, listable mistakes. Nothing on this page asks you to take that on trust: the first session produces the list, and you read it.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-eastern-m.programmesIntro: Mathematics support divides by year group far more cleanly than by ability, because what a tutor can do is bounded by how much of the specification has been taught and how close the entry deadline is. These are the three stages that generate requests from this part of the island.

programmes.name: Year 9: before the course starts
programmes.description: The cheapest place in the pipeline to fix mathematics, and the least popular. Year 9 is where algebraic fluency either becomes automatic or does not, and a student who leaves it without confident manipulation of indices, brackets, fractions and rearrangement will spend two years paying interest on that gap. Fortnightly support here costs less than weekly rescue work in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 is also the last comfortable moment to influence set placement, which in most Abu Dhabi schools feeds directly into the tier decision later. Children arriving from a CBSE or American curriculum frequently land in a lower set for presentation reasons rather than content reasons, and that is fixable at this stage.

programmes.name: Year 10: content delivery
programmes.description: Most of the specification is taught in this year, and usually taught once. Tutoring here is consolidation: closing topics covered during an absence, a move between schools or a term with a supply teacher. The end-of-year internal examination typically doubles as the tier recommendation, which makes the spring of Year 10 the moment when evidence matters most.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools vary in how firmly they treat that internal examination. Some revisit the tier in the autumn of Year 11; others do not. Asking which policy applies, before the examination rather than after it, is the difference between a decision you can influence and one you are informed of.

programmes.name: Year 11: the examination year
programmes.description: Teaching time ends at study leave, and everything after the mock is paper technique against mark schemes. The work that reliably moves a grade here is narrow: claiming method marks, non-calculator accuracy, reading multi-part questions properly and the two or three recurring topics that cost the same marks in every paper the student sits.
programmes.countryNote: Entries are submitted months before the papers, so by the time most families start searching for a tutor the tier is already fixed. Where a student is on the wrong tier and it is genuinely too late to change, the honest plan is to maximise the available ceiling and consider the November series rather than to pretend the ceiling is not there.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-eastern-m.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is one subject on the timetable and four or five different skills on the paper. The list below separates them the way a diagnostic session does, because a student is almost never weak at all of them at once.

subjects.name: Number and non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, standard form, bounds and ratio, done accurately without technology. From the current Cambridge 0580 structure a non-calculator paper sits at both tiers, and students who have leaned on a calculator for three years lose marks here first and most.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. The single biggest predictor of an IGCSE maths grade, and the skill most often assessed indirectly inside a question about something else. Weak manipulation shows up as a correct method abandoned halfway.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Sketching, transformations, intersections and reading information from a curve. Students lose marks by producing an accurate plot and then failing to answer the question asked about it, which is a reading problem rather than a graphing one.

subjects.name: Geometry, trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems at the higher tiers, right-angled and non-right-angled trigonometry. Marks go on stating the reason as well as the answer, and on diagrams drawn badly enough to mislead the student who drew them.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, averages from tables, cumulative frequency and histograms. Usually the most recoverable topic on the paper: the techniques are few and mechanical, and a student who has avoided them can bank a block of marks in two sessions.

subjects.name: Calculus and advanced algebra
subjects.description: Differentiation, turning points and harder algebraic fractions where the specification includes them. The content that separates the top grades, and the content most often taught last and therefore least practised before the papers.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem solving
subjects.description: The final parts of long questions, where two topics are deliberately combined. Students fluent in each topic separately still lose these marks, and no amount of single-topic revision fixes it. The remedy is a diet of combined questions.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken alongside IGCSE by students heading for A Level Mathematics or an IB Higher Level course. Useful as a bridge, demanding in Year 11, and worth taking only where the main specification is already secure.

subjects.name: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: A different Cambridge specification from 0580, with a graphing-calculator requirement and an investigation paper at the Extended tier. Some IB continuum schools in the emirate use it, and families sometimes find out only when past papers look unfamiliar.

subjects.name: Examination technique as a taught skill
subjects.description: Timing, question order, showing working, units, significant figures and checking. Not a soft skill: in marked papers from this emirate it accounts for more lost marks than any single topic, and it is trainable in a small number of sessions.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-eastern-m.regionsTitle: School destinations from the mangrove channel
abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-eastern-m.regionsIntro: Nobody goes to school inside Eastern Mangroves, so the relevant geography is where the children travel to and what that does to the evening. These are the directions families on this stretch actually commute in.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Bateen

sections.heading: What an IGCSE maths tutor in Eastern Mangroves is for
paragraphs: An IGCSE maths tutor in Eastern Mangroves, as parents here use the phrase, is a mathematics teacher working one-to-one with one child on the specification that child is entered for. IB Gram provides that over live video to families on this part of Abu Dhabi island. There are no home visits in the UAE; in-home tuition is something we run only in India. For mathematics specifically the online format costs nothing and gains something, because the shared screen puts both people inside the same working rather than on either side of a finished answer.

What the tutor is for is narrower than most families expect, and that is the point. IGCSE mathematics on both main boards is assessed entirely by written papers, with no coursework component. Every mark on offer is recoverable through practice and technique. So the job is diagnostic before it is instructional: find the three or four repeatable ways this student loses marks, name them, and remove them one at a time with evidence at each stage.

That is a different service from supervised homework, which is what a good deal of tutoring in this market actually is. Homework supervision keeps a student afloat and changes very little about their paper. A diagnosis changes the paper. The distinction is visible in the first session: a tutor who asks for marked work before teaching anything is doing the first job, and a tutor who opens the textbook at the current chapter is doing the second.

The practical consequence for a family here is that the first question to answer is not who, but which: which code, which tier, which topics. Those three facts turn a vague worry about mathematics into a short list of things to fix, and they are all available for free before any money is spent.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson Edexcel 4MA1
paragraphs: Two specifications dominate IGCSE mathematics in Abu Dhabi schools, and the differences between them are not cosmetic. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 tiers into Core and Extended, and the current syllabus includes a non-calculator paper alongside a calculator paper at each tier. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, tiers into Foundation and Higher, sits two papers at each tier and permits a calculator throughout.

The grade ranges differ too, and this is where a tier error becomes expensive. Cambridge Core access grades C to G, while Extended accesses A* to E. Edexcel Foundation accesses grades 5 to 1, while Higher accesses 9 to 4 with a safety-net grade 3 available. A student capable of a 7 who sits a Foundation entry cannot be awarded one, and no amount of preparation changes that arithmetic.

There is a third specification worth knowing about. Cambridge International Mathematics, code 0607, is a separate qualification with a graphing-calculator requirement and, at the Extended tier, an investigation paper. Several IB continuum schools use it because it dovetails with Diploma mathematics. A family whose past papers suddenly look unfamiliar should check whether this is the code on the entry rather than assume a printing error.

The reason to care about all of this is practice efficiency. Past papers from the wrong board teach the wrong instincts: a student drilled on calculator-permitted questions walks into a non-calculator paper with no arithmetic stamina, and a student drilled on Cambridge-style structured questions can be unsettled by Edexcel's longer unbroken problems. Same mathematics, different examination.

sections.heading: The tier decision and the ceiling nobody sees
paragraphs: Tier is decided by the school, on evidence, to a board deadline that falls months before the papers. By the time a family notices a problem and starts looking for a tutor, the entry is frequently already submitted. That sequence is worth understanding, because it changes what a parent should ask for and when.

Before entries close, the useful thing a tutor produces is evidence. Two timed sections and a diagnostic session generate marked work that shows whether a student can access the harder paper. A conversation with the school backed by that evidence is a different conversation from one backed by a parental impression. Schools in this emirate are generally reasonable about tier where the evidence exists; they are understandably firm where it does not.

After entries close, the work changes shape. On a lower tier the plan is to maximise the available ceiling and secure every mark on offer, which for a capable student is a realistic and often comfortable outcome. On a higher tier that was over-ambitious, the plan is to bank the accessible marks at the front of the paper rather than to spend revision time on content the student will not reach. Both plans are honest. Neither is the plan a family wants to hear about in April.

The November series matters here. Both main boards run a November session, which functions as the resit route after a summer result. For a student on the wrong tier, a June entry taken as a baseline followed by a targeted November resit is sometimes a better overall plan than a frantic spring, and it is worth raising with the school early rather than treating it as a failure option.

sections.heading: Six topics that decide most IGCSE maths grades
paragraphs: Marked papers from students in this emirate concentrate their lost marks in a small number of places. The table below is the list we start from in a diagnostic session, with what actually goes wrong and the intervention that fixes it. None of these are obscure corners of the specification; they are mainstream topics where the loss is procedural rather than conceptual.

The pattern across all six is the same. The student understands the mathematics and loses the marks in the execution: a method not written down, a unit omitted, a graph read carelessly, a reason not stated. That is why diagnosis beats revision. A student told to revise algebra will reread algebra; a student shown that they consistently lose the last two marks of multi-part questions will change what they write.

The second thing the table makes clear is how fast some of these are to fix. Probability and statistics in particular is mechanical: a handful of techniques, applied consistently, worth a reliable block of marks. Students who have quietly avoided the topic for two years can bank most of it in two sessions, which is the best return available anywhere on the paper.

What takes longer is algebraic fluency, because it is a habit rather than a technique. That one needs weekly drilling across a term, and it is the reason Year 9 and Year 10 support is better value than Year 11 rescue work even though far fewer families buy it.

sections.heading: Why the non-calculator paper behaves differently
paragraphs: Cambridge candidates on the current 0580 syllabus sit a non-calculator paper, and it exposes something no calculator-permitted paper can: whether a student actually owns the arithmetic. Students in this market frequently do not, through no fault of their own. They have had a device within reach since primary school, and the habit of reaching for it hides a gap rather than filling it.

The symptoms are specific. Fractions added by decimal conversion and rounded early. Percentages computed by a remembered button sequence rather than a method. Standard form handled by trusting a display. Surds and indices treated as unfamiliar notation rather than as rules. None of this shows up in class, where the calculator is on the desk, and all of it shows up under examination conditions.

The fix is unglamorous and quick: short timed drills with every intermediate step written down, repeated until accuracy stops depending on concentration. Ten minutes at the start of each session for a term outperforms an hour of theory, because the problem is not knowledge, it is fluency. Students resist this because it feels remedial, and they stop resisting when the paper marks move.

Edexcel 4MA1 candidates permit a calculator in both papers, which changes the emphasis rather than removing it. Their equivalent risk is over-reliance in the other direction: using the device for steps that should be mental, losing time, and failing to notice an answer that is obviously the wrong order of magnitude. Estimation as a checking habit is the skill to drill there.

sections.heading: A past-paper diet that moves a mark rather than filling an evening
paragraphs: Most students do past papers badly, and the way they do them badly is consistent. They work through a paper untimed, with notes open, checking answers question by question, and finish feeling reassured. That activity has almost no effect on an examination mark, because none of the conditions that produce the mark were present.

A paper that teaches something has four properties. It is timed, strictly. It is attempted without notes. It is marked against the published scheme rather than against an answer key, so the student sees where method marks sat. And the marking is followed by a specific action: three lost-mark answers rewritten in full, not just read over. That last step is where the learning actually happens and it is the step almost everyone skips.

Frequency matters less than people assume. One properly conducted paper a fortnight, fully processed, beats a paper a week skimmed. In an eight-week block we would normally use three full papers: one at the start as diagnosis, one at the midpoint to test whether the diagnosis was right, and one near the end for timing and stamina. Between them the work is targeted question types rather than whole papers.

Sequencing is the last piece. Papers from the same series are not equivalent in difficulty, and working through them chronologically mixes up two variables at once. Better to work by question type across several series, then use whole papers only when the point is timing and endurance.

sections.heading: Rates, value and what not to buy
paragraphs: Published figures in this market, read in October 2026, give a reasonable picture of what Abu Dhabi families are choosing between. At the entry level, EdFlik advertises online sessions from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit higher: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IGCSE, IB and A Level tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase listing around AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits including travel run from about AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table placing the usual band at AED 180 to 350.

The cheapest tier is not automatically poor value, but it buys a different product. At entry-level rates a family is usually buying homework supervision and company, which has real worth for a disorganised student and very little effect on a paper mark. The qualified band buys somebody who knows the specification. The specialist band buys somebody who knows the paper, the mark scheme and the tier decision. Matching the tier of purchase to the actual problem is the whole of value in this market.

Where money is most often wasted is in buying length instead of accuracy. A term of weekly general maths sessions, bought because the report card was poor, costs several thousand dirhams and frequently fixes nothing identifiable. Three sessions on one diagnosed topic cost a fraction of that and produce a visible change in the paper. Families here should ask for the short option first and be suspicious of anyone who does not offer it.

IB Gram publishes no tariff on these pages. The rate depends on tier, subject scarcity and session length and is quoted after a free trial lesson. Every figure above belongs to the named provider or survey that published it, not to us.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE maths specification my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer rather than the class teacher, and ask in writing for the syllabus code and tier. You are looking for something like Cambridge 0580 Extended, Cambridge 0607 Extended or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher. It is the most useful single fact in the whole process: it determines which past papers help, whether a calculator is permitted in each paper, and what the maximum grade available actually is. Families here with children at two schools often discover each child is on a different board.

faqs.question: What is Cambridge 0607 and why do some Abu Dhabi schools use it instead of 0580?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 is a separate specification from 0580, built around a graphing calculator and including an investigation paper at the Extended tier. Several IB continuum schools choose it because its style dovetails with Diploma mathematics, particularly the Applications and Interpretation route. For a parent the practical consequence is that 0580 past papers are the wrong practice material, and a tutor who has not checked the code will supply them without realising. Confirm the code before buying anything.

faqs.question: If my child sits the Cambridge Core maths tier, what is the best grade possible?
faqs.answer: Core accesses grades C to G, while Extended accesses A* to E. That ceiling applies however well the papers are answered, which is why the tier decision carries more weight than any revision plan. Pearson Edexcel works similarly: Foundation accesses grades 5 to 1 and Higher accesses 9 to 4 with a grade 3 safety net. If your child is capable of more than the tier allows, the time to make that case is before the school submits entries, with marked evidence rather than an opinion.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get my child's tier changed?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should claim they can. The tier decision belongs to the school and is submitted to a board deadline months before the papers. What a tutor can do is produce the evidence a school needs in order to reconsider: two timed sections and a diagnostic session, marked against the published scheme, showing whether the student can access the harder paper. Schools in this emirate are generally reasonable where that evidence exists and firm where it does not, which is a fair position.

faqs.question: My child scores well in Year 11 class tests and badly in the mock. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because class tests follow the topic just taught and mock papers do not. A student revising one chapter at a time performs well on questions that signal their own topic, then meets a paper where the signal is removed and two topics are combined. The marks lost are in the final parts of long questions. The fix is practising deliberately mixed questions rather than more single-topic exercises, which is a different activity from revising harder.

faqs.question: Does the non-calculator paper really change how we should revise?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially, if your child sits Cambridge 0580. Arithmetic fluency that a calculator has been hiding for years becomes visible: fractions, percentages, standard form, indices and surds, all without a device. The remedy is short timed drills with every intermediate step written out, ten minutes at a time, repeated until accuracy no longer depends on concentration. Edexcel 4MA1 candidates use a calculator in both papers, so their equivalent weakness is failing to estimate and notice an answer of the wrong magnitude.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a home at Eastern Mangroves?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. Mathematics here is taught one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, which suits the subject: both people write on the same working, so the tutor sees the exact line where a method broke down instead of a finished answer. What you give up is a person in the room. What you gain is a tutor matched to your child's syllabus code rather than to your neighbourhood.

faqs.question: How many past papers should my child do before the June series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families imagine, done properly. Three fully processed papers in an eight-week block does more than eight skimmed ones: one at the start for diagnosis, one at the midpoint to test whether the diagnosis held, and one near the end for timing and stamina. Between them, work by question type across several series rather than chronologically. A paper only teaches something if it is timed, closed-book, marked against the published scheme and followed by rewriting three lost answers in full.

faqs.question: Is a cheap online maths tutor at AED 50 an hour worth considering?
faqs.answer: It depends what the problem is. At entry-level rates advertised in this market, from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, a family is generally buying homework supervision and structure. For a disorganised student who works well with company, that has genuine value. For a student losing method marks on multi-part questions, it will not help, because diagnosing that needs somebody who knows the mark scheme. Match the level of purchase to the actual problem rather than to the budget, and ask for the diagnosis first.

faqs.question: What is the fastest topic to improve before the papers?
faqs.answer: Probability and statistics, almost every time. The techniques are few and mechanical — tree diagrams, averages from frequency tables, cumulative frequency, histograms — and a student who has quietly avoided them for two years can bank most of those marks inside two sessions. Compare that with algebraic fluency, which is a habit built over a term. If time is short, taking the mechanical marks first is the rational order, and it also rebuilds confidence before the harder work starts.

faqs.question: Should we consider the November series rather than rushing June?
faqs.answer: It is worth raising with the school early rather than treating it as an admission of failure. Both main boards run a November session, and for a student on an unsuitable tier or missing a chunk of the specification, sitting June as a baseline and targeting a focused November resit can produce a better final grade than a panicked spring. Pearson's November results have historically reached students in January. Discuss timing and entry costs with the examinations officer before deciding.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor working with an Eastern Mangroves family need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so a page quoting a specific amount is not citing anything.

faqs.question: Does the IGCSE maths grade matter for a UAE university application later?
faqs.answer: It forms part of the picture rather than deciding it. For the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. Mathematics is also a prerequisite for many degree programmes in its own right. Verify the current requirement with the Ministry; we describe the process and do not carry it out.

faqs.question: What should the first maths session with an Eastern Mangroves student produce?
faqs.answer: A written list of three or four named error types, drawn from marked work rather than from conversation. Not a reassurance that your child is bright, and not a plan to work through the textbook. You should be able to read the list and recognise your child in it, and your child should be able to say what their weakest topic is without prompting. If the first session produces none of that, the tutor is supervising rather than teaching and the block will not move a grade.

We will match a mathematics specialist who teaches that exact specification, run a free trial lesson on one of your child's own questions, and recommend the smallest block that fixes what the marked work shows — two or three sessions where that is enough. Teaching runs one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time for families at Eastern Mangroves and across Abu Dhabi island.

Ask each of them which code and which tier they have taught and marked, because on this subject that answer predicts the value of the hour better than any other detail.

intro.heading: Budget the job, not the hour
paragraphs: Almost every conversation about an IGCSE maths tutor starts with a rate and then stalls, because a rate on its own answers nothing. AED 200 an hour for six hours is AED 1,200; AED 200 an hour for a year is closer to AED 7,000. What a family on Hudayriyat Island actually needs to know is how many hours the particular problem takes, and that depends on which problem it is. Tier misplacement, a specific topic gap, weak non-calculator arithmetic and poor exam technique are four different jobs with four different costs.

The market bands are easy enough to state. A qualified subject tutor working online in the UAE is published between roughly AED 150 and 300 an hour; Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150. Budget-tier online provision runs lower — EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 — and buys a textbook walk-through rather than mark-scheme knowledge. Specialist IGCSE and A-Level tutors are quoted from AED 200 to 450 and upward, and in-home arrangements from AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, and not an IB Gram price list.

Set against hours, those bands behave differently than they look. A fluency problem in Extended tier algebra typically needs short, frequent practice rather than long sessions, so a mid-band tutor at AED 200 an hour over eight weeks is a modest total. A tier problem discovered in March of Year 11 cannot be solved by hours at all; it needs a conversation with the school that should have happened a year earlier. Paying specialist rates for the first job is unnecessary, and paying any rate for the second is money spent on the wrong thing entirely.

Hudayriyat Island adds one specific distortion. The island is reached by bridge from Al Bateen, the residential handovers here are recent, and there is no established local teaching community, so an in-home tutor is travelling from the mainland or from along Abu Dhabi island. That travel is inside the rate whether or not the invoice says so, and it also narrows the list to whoever will make the crossing twice a week in the right specification and tier. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

What follows is a page built around the hours. It names the four jobs families on this island actually buy, says roughly how long each takes and why, sets Core against Extended and Foundation against Higher so the tier conversation can happen with evidence, and explains what the papers reward well enough that you can judge a tutor's answers rather than take them on trust. Every AED figure carries its source, and the exam series are named by month so nothing on the page goes stale.

One framing that helps more than any rate comparison: ask what the job is before asking what the hour costs. A single diagnostic session against a marked past paper tells you which of the four jobs you are buying, and buying the wrong one well is more expensive than buying the right one at a premium.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-hudayriya.programmesIntro: Hudayriyat Island families sit IGCSE mathematics through one of two boards, with Cambridge's earlier stages feeding into it and A Level sitting above. The stage and the board together decide what a maths tutor is actually working on.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge's main IGCSE mathematics syllabus, entered at Core or Extended tier. Core covers a reduced content set with a lower grade ceiling; Extended covers the full set and is the entry route for A Level mathematics. Both tiers are examined through written papers with no coursework component, which means paper technique carries the whole mark and there is nowhere else to recover it.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi centres belong to one of Cambridge's six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Take the timetable from your own school's exams officer, not from a general calendar found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Pearson's international GCSE mathematics, graded 9 to 1 and entered at Foundation or Higher tier. Two written papers, with the calculator permitted throughout, which changes the balance of skills compared with Cambridge. The formula provision and the style of the longer questions differ enough that past papers from the other board are of limited use.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results arrive in January — November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Plan from the live official timetable on qualifications.pearson.com, because provisional versions are revised.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Taken alongside the main syllabus by students heading for A Level mathematics, physics or engineering. Calculus, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities arrive here before A Level, which makes it the single best preparation available and also the course where confident Extended students most often stall. Worth real tutoring hours if the A Level route is already decided.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school offers it, and availability varies between campuses even within the same district. A Hudayriyat Island family whose school does not run it, but whose child intends to take A Level mathematics, should treat the bridging work in Year 11 as a deliberate purchase rather than an optional extra.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage before IGCSE, assessed through Checkpoint tests. These results are the earliest honest indicator of whether a child is on a Core or an Extended trajectory, and they arrive while the gap is still cheap to close. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: For cost purposes this is the most important programme on the page. A Year 8 Checkpoint result acted on costs a handful of general-rate sessions. The same gap discovered in a Year 11 mock costs specialist-rate hours under time pressure and may no longer be fixable before the entry deadline.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-hudayriya.subjectsIntro: An IGCSE maths tutor working with a Hudayriyat Island student spends their hours in a small number of places. These are listed with the honest hour cost of each, because that is what determines the bill rather than the rate.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentage fluency
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Reverse percentages, compound interest and ratio problems carry marks across the whole paper and are the most common source of silent errors in otherwise competent students. Cheap to fix: short, frequent practice over a few weeks rather than extended sessions. A fluency job, typically six to ten hours spread thinly.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and rearranging
subjects.description: Factorising, algebraic fractions, simultaneous equations and changing the subject of a formula. These are the skills every later topic depends on, so a weakness here looks like a weakness everywhere. Typically the largest single hour commitment on an Extended tier plan, and the one that pays for itself fastest.

subjects.name: Trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles
subjects.description: The sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Students who are fine with SOHCAHTOA frequently collapse here because the problems require a decision about which rule applies before any calculation starts. A topic job: often four to eight hours, with a clear endpoint.

subjects.name: Graphs, functions and transformations
subjects.description: Quadratic and reciprocal graphs, intersections, gradients and the transformation sequences. Marks are lost on sketching rather than on calculation, because the harder questions use a sketch as the setup. Teachable in a defined block, and worth doing before the mock rather than after it.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability, cumulative frequency and histograms with unequal class widths. The histogram question is the reliable mark-loser at Higher and Extended tier. A short topic job, but one that is frequently skipped in revision because it looks easy on the surface.

subjects.name: Geometry, circle theorems and similarity
subjects.description: Circle theorems need to be learned as named results with named conditions, and students lose marks by seeing a configuration and guessing. Similarity and congruence proofs reward a method. Four to six hours closes most of the gap, provided the student writes reasons rather than answers.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic and surds
subjects.description: Cambridge's non-calculator paper exposes arithmetic that a calculator has been hiding for years. Surd manipulation, index laws and standard form are the specific points of failure. Pure fluency work, cheap per hour and ineffective in long sessions: fifteen minutes daily beats two hours weekly.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem solving at the back of the paper
subjects.description: The final questions chain three or four techniques with no intermediate confirmation. Students lose marks by abandoning rather than by error. This is an exam-technique job rather than a content one, and it responds to full timed papers with marking, not to topic exercises.

subjects.name: Method marks and the presentation of working
subjects.description: A substantial share of recoverable marks sit in working that is legible, ordered and shows the intermediate step. Students who do mental arithmetic and write only the answer lose method marks on questions they understood. The fastest improvement available to most candidates and almost never taught explicitly.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics: calculus and identities
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities, taken alongside the main syllabus. Confident Extended students stall here because the abstraction level rises rather than the difficulty. Worth specialist rates if A Level mathematics is the destination.

subjects.name: Tier diagnosis and course placement
subjects.levels: Core versus Extended · Foundation versus Higher
subjects.description: Not a topic but the most consequential piece of work a tutor does. One marked past paper at each tier settles whether a student is correctly entered, and the answer has to reach the school before the final entry deadline. One or two hours, and it occasionally saves a year of misdirected sessions.

subjects.name: Bridging into AS and A Level Mathematics
subjects.description: A Level assumes Extended or Higher tier content as a starting floor. A student entered for Core or Foundation has a structural gap to close before AS is realistic, and a student from Extended tier still needs algebraic fluency at a higher standard. A defined summer block rather than an open-ended commitment.

sections.heading: What each maths job actually costs, in hours and in AED
paragraphs: A qualified subject tutor working online in this market is published between roughly AED 150 and 300 an hour. Multiply that by the hours a specific job takes and the picture becomes usable. A topic block of six sessions is somewhere between AED 900 and 1,800. A fluency pattern spread over two months, using short sessions, often lands lower in total than a single month of long weekly lessons. An exam-technique block of eight full papers with marking is the biggest single item, and also the one with the most predictable return.

The job that costs least and saves most is diagnosis. One or two hours produces a written answer to whether the student is correctly entered for their tier and which topics are genuinely insecure. Families who skip it tend to buy a weekly slot in October and discover in March that the problem was placement. Two terms of weekly sessions at mid-market rates is roughly AED 3,000 to 6,000 in total; the diagnostic that would have redirected it is a rounding error against that.

Two jobs are routinely mispriced in opposite directions. Fluency work is bought at specialist rates when it needs frequency rather than expertise — a competent tutor at the lower end of the qualified band is the right purchase, and the money should go into more frequent, shorter sessions. Conversely, Additional Mathematics and the multi-step problem solving at the back of an Extended paper are bought at budget rates when they genuinely need somebody who has marked the paper, and the hour is wasted at any price.

The table below prices the common jobs by hours rather than by rate, with the market band applied so the total is visible. The rates are other providers' published figures read in October 2026. IB Gram quotes its own pricing after a free trial lesson and against the actual plan, because a single hourly figure applied across every tier and job is how competitor pages end up contradicting themselves within one page.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the decision that costs the most money
paragraphs: Tier placement is the most expensive variable in IGCSE mathematics and the one families understand least. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended. Pearson 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher. The lower tier in each pair covers less content and carries a lower grade ceiling, so a student entered at the lower tier cannot reach the grades the higher tier makes available, regardless of how well they perform on the day.

The consequences run forward. A Level mathematics, and by extension engineering, physics, economics and many other university routes, assume the higher tier content as a starting point rather than an aspiration. A student entered for Core or Foundation who intends to take A Level mathematics has a structural problem, and it is a problem that gets more expensive the later it is identified, because closing it eventually competes with new A Level content for the same hours.

The entry deadline is the hard edge. Final entries are made by the school's exams officer months before the papers, and a tier change has to be agreed before that date. Once entries are in, the tier is fixed for that series. This is why the diagnostic conversation belongs in Year 10 or very early Year 11 rather than after the mocks, and why a tutor who raises it in the first session is worth more than one who quietly works within whatever tier they were handed.

What a tutor can usefully contribute is evidence. A past paper at each tier, marked honestly, converts a conversation about potential into a conversation about marks, and schools respond to marks. The table below sets the two pairs out side by side so a parent can walk into that meeting knowing what is actually being decided.

sections.heading: Where the money gets wasted on this island specifically
paragraphs: The first waste is paying a travel premium for a maths lesson that gains nothing from physical presence. In-home arrangements in this market are quoted between AED 180 and 500 an hour with the drive inside the rate, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online. For a Year 10 student working through past papers with a shared screen and a visible worked solution, the premium buys a car journey across the Hudayriyat bridge and nothing that appears in the marking.

The second is buying hours in the wrong shape. Non-calculator arithmetic does not improve during a two-hour weekly lesson; it improves through short daily practice that somebody checks. Families who buy long sessions for a fluency problem spend more and get less, and then conclude that tutoring does not work for their child. The tutor's job on a fluency problem is partly to set up and police a pattern rather than to fill the hour.

The third is the unexamined monthly package. Plans circulating in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four in-home visits of two hours. Both look tidy and both conceal the same three things: the effective hourly rate, what a cancellation costs, and what happens to unused sessions. Ask for all three in writing before committing to a term.

The fourth is specific to maths and almost universal. Working from the wrong board's past papers wastes every hour of every session. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 differ in tier names, calculator rules, formula provision and question style, and a tutor who has not asked which specification your child sits is not going to discover the mismatch on their own. Ask for the code, not the board name, and get it from the school's exams officer.
