sections.heading: What the Cambridge and Pearson papers actually reward
paragraphs: Marks in IGCSE mathematics are not distributed the way students assume. A large share of recoverable marks live in method rather than in answers, which means the presentation of working is worth real points. A student who performs a step mentally and writes only the result loses method marks on questions they fully understood, and that loss is invisible to them because they believe they got the question right. Correcting this habit is the fastest grade movement available to most candidates.

Command vocabulary matters more than it appears to. Show that, prove, hence, and verify each require something different, and hence in particular means the previous part must be used. Students who restart a question from scratch after a part marked hence have thrown away the structure the examiner built for them. These conventions are rarely taught explicitly and are quick to teach once named.

The back of the paper is where tier-appropriate students lose grades. Those questions chain three or four techniques with no confirmation along the way that the route is correct, and most candidates abandon rather than err. The skill is tolerance for ambiguity under time pressure, and it is trained by doing complete papers rather than topic exercises. Any tutoring plan that never has the student sit a full paper under timing is incomplete.

Cambridge's non-calculator paper deserves separate mention because it exposes arithmetic a calculator has been concealing. Surd manipulation, index laws and standard form are the specific failure points, and they are pure fluency rather than comprehension. Pearson's calculator-throughout structure removes that exposure and introduces a different one: students who trust the display and never sanity-check a result.

sections.heading: The June and November series, read backwards from the money
paragraphs: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to candidates in India only, so a UAE family planning around those dates would be preparing for a window their child cannot enter. That mistake has a real cost attached, which is why it belongs in a section about money rather than only in a calendar.

Read backwards, the cheap decision points all sit early. A Checkpoint result in Year 8 or a Year 9 internal assessment, acted on with a short topic block at general rates, costs a fraction of the same gap addressed in the spring of Year 11 at specialist rates with the entry deadline already passed. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and those results are the earliest honest signal a parent gets.

The expensive decision points cluster in the final two terms, and they are expensive partly because everybody wants the same hours. Demand for tier-experienced maths tutors across Abu Dhabi concentrates in the months before the June series, which tightens availability and firms up rates. A family that books an exam-technique block in advance pays for the block; a family that books it in the last fortnight pays for scarcity, if the slot exists at all.

Results and resits carry their own arithmetic. For Pearson, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January timing matters: a November resit entered after disappointing June grades produces results in the middle of the university application cycle rather than before it, which changes what a resit is worth. Confirm every date with the school's exams officer and the live official timetable.

sections.heading: ADEK, the tutoring permit, and what a parent is entitled to ask
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes inspection ratings. Dubai's regulator is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A Hudayriyat Island family is inside the ADEK system.

Tutoring is permitted separately. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The MoHRE service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor's failure to hold one is not a cost question. Anyone providing private lessons without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Abu Dhabi adds a conflict rule: ADEK's professional-ethics expectations restrict private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable bar. Hiring your child's own maths teacher privately is not a route to pursue here.

IB Gram holds no ADEK permit, no KHDA permit and no board accreditation, and makes no claim to any. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a licence issued to a specific kind of entity. What a parent can reasonably ask us for is the tutor's permit position, the specification and tier they have taught, and a free trial lesson before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor may and may not do, and what we will not sell you
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics carries no coursework component at either board, which removes the academic-honesty problem that dogs other subjects. There is still a boundary worth stating. A tutor may teach, set problems, mark work, explain a mark scheme's reasoning and work through a past paper question. A tutor may not sit an assessment, complete work submitted as the student's own, or supply material a board has not released. Providers in this market who sell completed assessed work for other subjects exist, and the consequence of buying from them falls on the candidate.

Board material is the second line. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them and point to the official source rather than reproducing or distributing them. A provider handing over a bundle of copied board documents is telling you how it treats rules generally, and that is worth noticing before you hand over a term's fees.

The third is the claim boundary, which is where most of this market falls down. There is no self-asserted star rating on this page, no percentage of students achieving anything without the underlying data, and no tutor described as an examiner without the board, component and years behind it. Competitor pages in this cluster publish contradictory ratings within a single page and a review count that cannot be reconciled with their own student numbers.

And one promise that will not appear anywhere here: a grade. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any provider offering one is either misunderstanding the assessment or misrepresenting it. What can honestly be offered is a diagnosis, a plan with a stated hour count, marked work that shows whether the plan is working, and the willingness to change the match or say the problem lies elsewhere.

sections.heading: Starting from Hudayriyat Island: four messages and a free lesson
paragraphs: Tell us four things and the match becomes straightforward: the school, the specification code and tier, the most recent assessment mark with the paper if you have it, and the times that genuinely work once the bridge crossing and the school run are accounted for. The specification code is the one families most often cannot supply and the one that matters most, and the school's exams officer can confirm it in a minute.

The first lesson is a free trial with no card required. Spend it on diagnosis rather than on a sample lesson: ask for a past-paper question worked and marked live, and ask at the end which of the four jobs this is — tier, topic, fluency or technique. A tutor who names it and estimates the hours is giving you a budget. A tutor who offers a weekly slot without naming the problem is giving you a subscription.

Pricing follows the trial and the plan rather than preceding them, because the hour count is what determines the total and the hour count depends on the diagnosis. For comparison while you decide, the published market figures used throughout this page were read in October 2026: AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, AED 200 to 450 and upward for specialists, AED 180 to 500 in-home with travel included, and monthly packages at AED 799 online or AED 1,599 to 1,799 in-home.

Two last honest notes. If no tutor with the right specification and tier experience is free in the slot you need, we will say so and give a date rather than filling it with a generalist, and if the available specialist is based outside the UAE we disclose that before anything is booked, with sessions timed to Gulf Standard Time. And enquiry forms here collect a child's year group, school, board and subject because a match needs them; we do not ask for grades, documents or photographs at that stage, and the privacy policy linked on every page explains deletion, which is a UAE obligation under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021.

process.title: Get the specification code from the school
process.description: Not the board name — the code. Cambridge mathematics is 0580, Pearson Specification A is 4MA1, and Additional Mathematics is separate again. Ask the exams officer for the code and the tier your child is entered for. Five minutes here prevents a tutor working from the wrong past papers, which wastes every hour that follows.

process.title: Buy the diagnosis before the hours
process.description: One or two sessions against marked papers at both tiers, producing a written answer on tier fit and insecure topics. This is the cheapest useful purchase in the market and it determines which of the four jobs you are buying. Families who skip it frequently spend two terms on the wrong problem.

process.title: Pick the shape that matches the diagnosis
process.description: A topic block, a fluency pattern, an exam-technique block and full-course weekly support cost very different totals and do very different work. The shape should follow the diagnosis rather than default to a weekly slot, because a weekly slot aimed at a nameable gap is the most common overspend on this page.

process.title: Agree the hours and the terms in writing
process.description: Ask for the number of sessions, the effective hourly rate, what a cancellation costs and what happens to unused sessions, all in writing before the block starts. Any provider unwilling to answer those four in writing is not worth a term's commitment, whatever the headline rate looks like.

process.title: Fix a slot the student can do arithmetic in
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time. After the bridge crossing and the school run, the realistic windows for Hudayriyat Island families are straight after the commute or well after dinner, and for mathematics the later option is usually better. Accuracy, not comprehension, is what tiredness destroys.

process.title: Re-test at the end of the block
process.description: A block finishes with unseen questions on the same topic, marked. That is the only honest way to know whether the hours worked. If the re-test shows no movement, the next step is a different tutor or a conversation with the school about tier, not another block of the same thing.

whyPoints.title: Priced by the job, not by the hour
whyPoints.description: This page publishes the hour counts the common maths jobs take and applies the market band to them, so a family can see a total rather than a rate. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote dollars. A rate without an hour count is not information.

whyPoints.title: The tier question raised first
whyPoints.description: Core against Extended, Foundation against Higher, is the most consequential variable in IGCSE mathematics and it has a deadline attached. Tutors here raise it in the first session and produce marked evidence for the school conversation, rather than quietly working inside whatever tier they were handed.

whyPoints.title: Specification, not just board

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE maths tutor cost for a Hudayriyat Island family, in total rather than per hour?
faqs.answer: It depends on the job. A tier diagnosis is one or two hours. A single topic block is four to eight. An algebraic manipulation rebuild is ten to sixteen, and an exam-technique block of full timed papers is eight to twelve. Applying the published market band of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online tutor, a topic block lands roughly between AED 600 and 2,400 and a diagnosis between AED 150 and 600. In-home rates in this market run AED 180 to 500 with travel inside them. Those are other providers' October 2026 figures; IB Gram quotes after a free trial.

faqs.question: Is my child on the right tier for Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1?
faqs.answer: A marked past paper at each tier answers it in about two hours, and the answer has to reach the school before final entries are submitted. Cambridge splits into Core and Extended, Pearson into Foundation and Higher, and the lower tier in each pair caps the grade available regardless of performance. The consequence runs forward: A Level mathematics assumes the higher tier content as a floor. Once the entries are in, the tier is fixed for that series, so this conversation belongs in Year 10 or very early Year 11 rather than after the mocks.

faqs.question: Why does working from the wrong board's past papers matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because the two specifications differ in the things that decide marks. Cambridge 0580 includes a paper without a calculator; Pearson 4MA1 permits the calculator throughout. The tier names differ, the formula provision differs, and the style of the longer questions differs. A student drilled on Cambridge non-calculator arithmetic while sitting a Pearson paper has spent hours on an exposure that does not exist for them, and vice versa. Get the specification code from the school's exams officer and give it to the tutor before the first session rather than after it.

faqs.question: My child's arithmetic is weak. Is a long weekly session the answer?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most common misallocation in IGCSE maths tutoring. Arithmetic, surds and index laws are fluency rather than comprehension, and fluency responds to frequency. Fifteen or twenty minutes of practice most days, set and checked, outperforms a two-hour weekly lesson and costs less in total. Part of the tutor's job on a fluency problem is designing and policing that pattern rather than filling an hour with it. Families who buy long sessions for this problem spend more, see less movement, and often conclude tutoring does not work for their child.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a house on Hudayriyat Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a recording. For maths specifically this costs almost nothing in teaching quality: past-paper work with a visible worked solution on a shared screen is the same lesson it would be at a kitchen table. What it saves is the drive across the bridge, which in this market is quoted inside rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour.

faqs.question: How many marks am I losing by not writing out working?
faqs.answer: More than most students believe. A substantial share of recoverable marks in both specifications sit in method rather than in the final answer, so a candidate who does a step mentally and writes only the result loses marks on questions they genuinely understood. The loss is invisible to them, which is why it persists. Correcting the habit is usually the fastest grade movement available and takes very few sessions: the tutor marks the student's own script against the published criteria and shows exactly where a written intermediate step would have earned a mark that was forfeited.

faqs.question: What are the hardest topics for Extended and Higher tier candidates?
faqs.answer: Trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles is the first, because the problem requires choosing which rule applies before any calculation begins, and students fine with SOHCAHTOA have never had to make that decision. Circle theorems are second, because they must be learned as named results with named conditions rather than recognised by shape. Histograms with unequal class widths are a reliable mark-loser that looks easy. And the multi-step questions at the back of the paper defeat tier-appropriate students who abandon rather than err, which is technique rather than content.

faqs.question: Can we sit an IGCSE maths exam in February or March in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to candidates in India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. This matters practically because general online calendars sometimes show the India dates, and a family revising towards a window their child cannot enter has lost real time. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct zone timetable, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version.

faqs.question: Is a November resit worth the money after disappointing June grades?
faqs.answer: It depends on the application timeline rather than on the maths. For Pearson, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026. A November entry therefore produces results in the middle of the university application cycle rather than before it, which changes what the improved grade can actually be used for. Work that out with the school and the universities concerned immediately after results rather than in the new year, and treat the short intensive block plus entry fees as the cost of the decision.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor in Abu Dhabi need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The MoHRE service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone offering private lessons without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since it costs nothing there is no reasonable explanation for its absence.

faqs.question: Can my child's maths teacher at their Abu Dhabi school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Not while the child is enrolled at that teacher's school. ADEK's professional-ethics expectations for private and charter school staff restrict teachers from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours also need the permit. The practical effect in Abu Dhabi is that some of the nearest and most obviously suitable maths teachers are the ones a family cannot lawfully hire, which is one reason the local search for a tutor feels unproductive.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth paying specialist rates for?
faqs.answer: If A Level mathematics is the destination, yes. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics introduces differentiation, integration, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities before A Level, which makes it the best available preparation and also the course where confident Extended tier students most often stall, because the abstraction level rises rather than the difficulty. This is one of the few places on this page where a budget-rate tutor is poor value at any price: the hour needs somebody who has taught and marked the paper. Not every Abu Dhabi school offers it, so check with yours.

faqs.question: What should I ask before committing to a monthly maths package?
faqs.answer: Four things, in writing. What is the effective hourly rate once everything is inside the price? What does a cancellation cost, and how much notice avoids the charge? What happens to sessions the family does not use? And how many sessions does the provider think this specific job needs? Packages circulating in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home visits, and both look tidy while concealing the same three answers. A provider who will not put them in writing is not worth a term.

faqs.question: What if no tutor with our tier and specification is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a realistic date rather than putting somebody without that experience into the slot. Demand for tier-experienced maths tutors across Abu Dhabi concentrates in the months before the June series, which is exactly when most families start looking, so the tightest combination is a fixed weekday evening in the spring term. Where no UAE-based tutor with the right specification is available, the alternative is a tutor based elsewhere teaching the same specification over the same platform on Gulf Standard Time, disclosed before anything is booked.

faqs.question: Can a tutor guarantee my child a grade 7 or above in IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who offers one is misrepresenting how the assessment works. Grades depend on the paper, the tier, the student's performance on the day and the boundaries the board sets afterwards, none of which a tutor controls. What can honestly be offered is a diagnosis naming the problem, a plan with a stated number of hours, marked work that shows whether the plan is moving the marks, and a willingness to change the tutor or say the issue lies with tier placement instead. Treat any guarantee in this market as a reason for scepticism rather than reassurance.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-hudayriya.closingHeading: Name the job, then look at the rate

If the honest answer is a tier conversation with the school rather than a block of sessions, you will have saved considerably more than the lesson was worth. abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-hydra-vil.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE mathematics to Abu Dhabi students at both tiers and across the Cambridge and Pearson specifications. Each works from the published mark schemes for recent series rather than from a generic scheme of work, because the mark scheme is what actually awards the marks.

intro.heading: The mark scheme is the most useful document in the subject
paragraphs: Almost no IGCSE mathematics student has read a mark scheme, and it is the single most informative document available to them. Mark schemes are published by Cambridge and Pearson after each series on their own websites, and they set out, line by line, exactly what earns credit on every question. A student who reads three of them writes differently for the rest of the course, and the change is immediate rather than gradual.

The reason it matters so much in mathematics is that credit is structured rather than binary. There are marks for a correct approach even when the arithmetic afterwards fails, marks that require the exact value in the exact form, and credit that follows through an earlier mistake provided the working is visible. A student who writes nothing down and reaches a wrong answer scores zero on a question where a student with the same understanding and worse arithmetic scores most of the marks. That is not a matter of fairness; it is how the instrument works, and it is learnable in an afternoon.

Hydra Village is a small gated villa community on the mainland side of Abu Dhabi, out towards Al Shamkha and Al Reef, with no school inside it. Every student here travels, mostly into the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, which makes the afternoon long and the daily study window narrow. For mathematics that matters more than for most subjects, because fluency is built by short frequent practice and a narrow window has to be used deliberately rather than hoped for.

Delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Hydra Village or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a page about mark-scheme forensics the relevant point is that the valuable skill is reading a script against a published scheme, and the person who can do that for your child's exact specification is scarcer than somebody willing to drive out past Al Shamkha at five in the afternoon.

The rest of this page is diagnostic material a parent can use without knowing any mathematics. The mark scheme notation in a table, with the behaviour each convention implies. The nine topic errors that cost the most marks in Abu Dhabi scripts, ranked roughly by how many marks each returns per hour of repair. An eight-rung algebra ladder with a test question for each rung, so you can find where a student actually stands. The three topics students skip. A marking routine that makes past papers useful rather than merely repeated. And the boundaries we work inside.

Two notes on sources. Specifications, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are published on their own sites; we reference and link them rather than reproducing them, and a tutor works through them with a student from the official source. And Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series, with the February and March series offered in India only, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-hydra-vil.programmesIntro: The specification determines which mark scheme applies, and the schemes differ in detail even where the mathematics is identical. These are the routes in use across Abu Dhabi schools.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Two written papers per tier, one of them sat without a calculator, with a defined list of formulae to recall. Extended tier adds functions, vectors, harder trigonometry and more demanding algebra, and carries the full grade range while Core is capped below the top grades.
programmes.countryNote: The non-calculator paper is the single feature that most changes a student's practice diet, and it is the one most often overlooked by families who assume all IGCSE mathematics is the same. Exact-form answers, surds, fraction work and estimation all have to be fluent unaided for an 0580 candidate.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Two papers of two hours, equally weighted, with a calculator permitted throughout and a formula sheet supplied, graded on the nine to one numerical scale. The skill rewarded is fast and correct formula selection rather than recall, which is a genuinely different thing to train.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes its timetables and results schedule well ahead. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge International Mathematics 0607
programmes.description: A separate Cambridge specification designed around the graphic display calculator, with investigation work at Extended tier. Not a harder or easier 0580 but a different design, in which calculator fluency is examined rather than assumed.
programmes.countryNote: Mark schemes for 0607 reward recorded calculator use in a way 0580 schemes do not, so a student taught entirely from 0580 material will under-record their working. This is one of the clearest arguments for confirming the code with the exams officer before anything else.

programmes.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
programmes.description: Optional, sat alongside Extended 0580 by students heading for A Level or Diploma mathematics. Calculus, logarithms, binomial expansion and harder trigonometry a year early, with both papers calculator-permitted and a visible jump in the algebra needed before the new content appears.
programmes.countryNote: The difficulty students report here is almost always the top rungs of the algebra ladder rather than the calculus itself. A 0606 question typically needs three or four manipulation steps before the new idea arrives, and a student doing those slowly runs out of time rather than out of understanding.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-hydra-vil.subjectsIntro: Below are the specific errors that recur in marked Abu Dhabi scripts, with what each costs and how quickly it responds. The ordering reflects marks returned per hour of repair rather than difficulty.

subjects.name: Frequency density on unequal class widths
subjects.description: Entirely mechanical once taught and reliably skipped in revision. A histogram question with unequal widths is free marks for a student who has seen the calculation twice and a guaranteed loss for one who has not. The highest-yield single lesson in the syllabus.

subjects.name: Scale factors between similar shapes and solids
subjects.description: One rule covering linear, area and volume relationships. The reliable error is applying a linear factor to an area or a volume. Taught once, it protects marks on every paper thereafter and takes under half a lesson.

subjects.name: Rounding an intermediate value
subjects.description: A habit rather than a gap. Students round partway and carry the error forward, losing accuracy marks on correct method. One instruction, enforced across four pieces of marked work, ends it permanently.

subjects.name: Answering 'show that' with a numerical check
subjects.description: Substituting the printed value back in and demonstrating that it works is verification rather than derivation, and scores nothing. Two sessions on command terms fixes this and several related faults at once.

subjects.name: Probability without replacement
subjects.description: A changing denominator on the second branch, and multiplication along paths rather than addition. Fifteen minutes of correctly drawn and labelled trees settles it for most students.

subjects.name: Bounds propagated through a division
subjects.description: Upper and lower bounds where the student must decide which bound goes where. Counter-intuitive the first time and mechanical afterwards, which makes it a single-lesson repair with a reliable return.

subjects.name: Three-dimensional trigonometry
subjects.description: The first move is always to extract and redraw the relevant triangle out of the solid. Students who attempt to reason inside the three-dimensional diagram rarely begin, which reads as a hard topic and is a method habit.

subjects.name: Transformations described in words
subjects.description: Mark schemes want the transformation named precisely with its parameters, and often in function notation. A student who describes the movement in a sentence has understood it and not claimed the marks.

subjects.name: Vectors as geometry instead of algebra
subjects.description: Showing points collinear through a scalar multiple, with the arrow notation retained. Students write a geometric argument where the scheme asks for a vector route, which is a translation problem rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fraction and surd work
subjects.description: Needed because 0580 includes a paper sat without a calculator. A student who has practised everything with a device has quietly outsourced the exact skill that paper examines, and will meet the consequence in the examination hall.

subjects.name: Bearings and compass-based questions
subjects.description: Three figures, measured clockwise from north, and a sketch before any trigonometry. Skipped in most revision because it feels old-fashioned, and it appears regularly with marks attached to the convention itself.

subjects.name: Unrecorded calculator work
subjects.description: Method marks are awarded for what appears on the page, not for what appeared on the screen. Three sessions of marked work in which the operation must be written down is usually enough to end this for good.

sections.heading: Decoding the mark scheme notation
paragraphs: Published mark schemes use a compact notation that looks forbidding and takes about ten minutes to learn. Once a student knows it, they can read their own marked script and see precisely where credit existed and was not claimed, which is a different and better experience than looking at a total.

The notation varies slightly between boards and the principles are the same. A method mark rewards a correct approach. An accuracy mark requires the right value in the right form. An independent mark is available for a specific statement or step regardless of what surrounds it. Follow-through credit allows later work built on an earlier wrong answer to score, provided the working is visible. Special-case credit covers particular near-misses the examiners decided to reward. Some marks are dependent on an earlier one having been earned; some answers are acceptable within a stated tolerance; some are marked correct answer only.

The behavioural consequences are blunt and worth saying to a teenager in exactly these words. Write down the substitution before you evaluate it. Keep full accuracy in intermediate values and round only at the end. If the question gives you an answer to use in a later part, use it even if your own earlier answer differed. Never erase a wrong attempt that contains valid method — cross it out instead, because crossed-out work can still be marked if nothing replaces it. And write down what you did on the calculator, because a screen is not a page.

The table sets out each convention with the behaviour it implies. A tutor's job with it is specific: mark the student's own scripts against the official scheme for a real series and show them, question by question, the marks that were available and not claimed. That conversation across four or five papers converts more marks than most content teaching, and it is the part a generalist mathematics tutor is least likely to do.

sections.heading: Nine errors, ranked by marks returned per hour
paragraphs: Lost marks in IGCSE mathematics are not evenly distributed. Across marked Abu Dhabi scripts the same errors recur, and most are procedural rather than conceptual, which is why they are cheap to repair. A student who applies a linear scale factor to a volume is not confused about geometry; they are missing one rule.

The ranking in the table is by return on effort rather than by frequency or difficulty. Frequency density tops it because it is both common and completely mechanical: two demonstrations and some practice and it is gone. Scale factors follow for the same reason. Rounding discipline is third because it costs marks across every topic simultaneously, so one habit change pays out repeatedly rather than in one place.

Lower down the list the repairs get longer. Three-dimensional trigonometry needs a method habit established, which takes a couple of sessions and some supervised practice. Transformations in function notation and vectors as algebra are translation problems — the student understands the mathematics and does not express it in the form the scheme requires — and those take three or four pieces of marked writing each. None takes a term, which is the point: a well-aimed short block addresses most of the table.

What is not on the list is anything conceptual, and that is deliberate. Genuine conceptual gaps exist and they take weeks, not lessons: function notation where a student can evaluate but not interpret, or algebraic fluency underneath everything. Those need teaching rather than drilling and they belong in a term arrangement. A family who attacks the nine procedural errors first will know afterwards whether a deeper problem remains, which is a far better position than guessing at the start.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper: arithmetic that has to be unaided
paragraphs: Cambridge 0580 includes a paper sat without a calculator, and this is the largest single divergence between the specifications in common use in Abu Dhabi. Pearson 4MA1 permits a calculator on both papers. A student preparing for the wrong one of these has spent real hours on a skill their paper will not isolate, or has failed to build one it will.

What the non-calculator paper actually requires is a specific and narrow set of competences, all of which are trainable. Fluent addition, subtraction, multiplication and division with fractions, including mixed numbers. Simplifying surds and rationalising simple denominators. Standard form arithmetic without a device. Percentage work in both directions, including reversing a percentage change, which is where students most often guess. Long multiplication and division performed rather than estimated. And rough estimation, used to check whether an answer is plausible before moving on.

The failure pattern is predictable and almost never addressed. A student has done two years of homework with a calculator to hand, because homework is calculator-agnostic and the device is faster. They are then surprised by a paper that removes it. The remedy is equally simple and almost never applied: for the final months, a fixed proportion of practice must happen with the calculator physically out of the room. Students resist this and it is the single most effective change available to an 0580 candidate.

The reverse case matters too. A 4MA1 or 0607 candidate should be spending that time on calculator technique instead: storing intermediate values rather than retyping rounded ones, checking the angle mode before any trigonometry, using the statistical functions correctly, and above all recording on the page what was done on the device. Method marks follow what is written, not what was displayed, and this is the most common avoidable loss in calculator-permitted scripts.

sections.heading: The algebra ladder: finding the rung a student stalls at
paragraphs: Algebraic fluency is not a single thing that a student either has or lacks. It is a sequence of skills in a fairly fixed order, and a student who struggles with Extended mathematics has almost always stalled at an identifiable rung and is compensating above it. Finding the rung takes about twenty minutes with the right questions and makes the difference between a targeted term and a vague one.

The ladder runs roughly as follows. Substituting values into an expression accurately. Collecting like terms and expanding a single bracket. Expanding and simplifying a double bracket. Factorising a simple quadratic. Rearranging a formula where the subject appears once. Solving simultaneous equations by elimination and substitution. Factorising and manipulating algebraic fractions. And rearranging a formula where the subject appears twice, which is the rung most Extended candidates stall at and the one 0606 assumes completely.

The diagnostic value is in the order. A student who cannot rearrange a formula with the subject twice but handles everything below it needs a specific, finite piece of work. A student who stumbles at double brackets is in a quite different position and will meet that weakness in every quadratic, every area problem and every rearrangement for the rest of the course, which is a term of repair rather than a block.

The repair mechanism is volume rather than explanation, which is why this work belongs in Year 9, Year 10 or the summer rather than in the final term. Fluency comes from performing a skill many times across many days, and the week of a Year 11 student preparing eight subjects does not contain the required volume. The table gives each rung with a test question shape, so a parent can run the diagnostic themselves before paying anybody.

sections.heading: Bearings, transformations and vectors: the three topics students skip
paragraphs: Every cohort skips the same three topics in revision, and examiners keep setting them. Bearings feel old-fashioned, transformations feel like primary-school geometry, and vectors feel abstract and optional. All three appear with marks attached, and all three are quick to secure because the marks are largely in conventions rather than in difficulty.

Bearings have exactly two rules worth memorising: three figures always, and measured clockwise from north. A student who writes a two-figure bearing or measures from the wrong reference loses marks on an otherwise correct trigonometric calculation. The method habit is to sketch the situation with north marked before touching any trigonometry, which takes ten seconds and prevents the most common error in the topic.

Transformations are a notation problem. Mark schemes want the transformation named with its parameters — the specific translation, the centre and scale factor, the mirror line, the angle and direction of rotation — and on Extended papers often in function notation. A student who describes the movement in a sentence has understood the geometry and has not claimed the credit. Three marked pieces usually fixes it, because the student is not learning geometry; they are learning to write what they already see.

Vectors are the same translation problem one level up. Showing that two points are collinear requires demonstrating that one vector is a scalar multiple of another, written as vectors, with the arrow notation retained. Students write a convincing geometric argument in prose and score a fraction of the marks. The fix is to practise the specific route the scheme rewards, four or five times, against the published mark scheme rather than against intuition about what should count.

sections.heading: A past-paper routine that actually changes something
paragraphs: Past papers are the most abused resource in this subject. The common pattern is to sit a paper, check the total against a boundary somebody found online, feel the appropriate emotion and sit another. Papers used that way measure a student repeatedly and change nothing, and a student can lose a whole term to the illusion of productive revision.

The routine that works has four steps and is tedious in a way that is hard to sell. Sit the paper to time, with no interruptions and the correct calculator rule applied. Mark it against the official published mark scheme for that series, strictly, awarding only what the scheme awards. Log every lost mark on one line: question, topic, and category — content not known, method known but misapplied, notation or calculator, command word misread, rounding or form, or ran out of time. Then rework only the questions where the category was method or content, and leave the others to the behavioural fixes.

The marking step is where honesty matters. Students systematically award themselves credit for answers the scheme would not accept, and simultaneously miss method marks they genuinely earned. Both errors make the log useless. If a student cannot mark their own work strictly, somebody else has to do it, and that is a large part of what a tutor is actually for in the final months.

After three papers the log is unmistakable. Two or three categories will dominate, and the plan writes itself: attack those, ignore the rest, and re-measure on the fourth paper. There is also a useful second-attempt rule worth applying: a question answered wrongly should be re-attempted from blank a week later rather than read through, because reading a worked solution produces recognition and re-attempting produces the retrieval the examination actually requires.

sections.heading: Hydra Village: a gated community and the twenty-minute slot
paragraphs: Hydra Village has no school inside it and no tuition provision, which means two things for a mathematics plan. Every student commutes, so the afternoon is long and the evening study window is narrow. And there is no local in-person option worth considering, because there is no reason for an IGCSE mathematics specialist to live in a small gated community out towards Al Shamkha.

On the window: the method is to measure rather than estimate. Record when your child actually walks in for five consecutive days, take the latest of those, and add fifteen minutes for changing and eating. From here that usually places a weekly session at five o'clock or later. Booking earlier produces a rescheduling habit, and a rescheduling habit ends an arrangement by about week six, which then gets attributed to the tutor rather than to the arithmetic.

On the daily practice, which matters more in mathematics than in any other subject: twenty minutes on six days beats two hours on a Saturday, because fluency is a retrieval problem and six separate recalls build it far better than one long session. In a household where the afternoon is consumed by travel, that twenty minutes has to be placed deliberately. The patterns that survive are immediately after changing, while the student is still in school mode, or first thing in the morning for early risers. Left to whenever there is time, it becomes a weekend batch and loses most of its value.

On the in-person option: published in-home visiting rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, read in October 2026, with the longest journeys at the upper end. Set against published online rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor, the difference from a community like this one is largely transport. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case, since home visiting is an India-only service for us, and the figures explain why we are comfortable saying so.

sections.heading: Sources, the permit and what we decline
paragraphs: This page leans heavily on mark schemes, so the sourcing position matters. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are published on their own websites. We do not reproduce or distribute them; a tutor works through them with a student from the official source, which is also the only way to be certain the version in use is current. A site offering a downloadable library of current board material is doing something a parent should decline.

We also publish no grade boundary. Boundaries are set after each series in light of that series' papers and candidate performance and published afterwards, so a fixed threshold on a tutoring page is a fabricated certainty. On dates, Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered in India only, and Pearson runs May/June and November. The Pearson dates cited on this page are backward-looking citations kept with their dates because that is what makes them checkable.

On tutors and permits: any paid private tutor in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with the ministry's own service page listing no fee and a two working day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so a figure quoted as the penalty is invention.

On status and what we will not do: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and holds no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. We decline to produce assessed work of any kind, to supply answers for live assessed tasks, or to sit with a student during an assessment. Our tutors are not described as current examiners for any board, no tutor can promise a grade, and we publish no rating or satisfaction statistic, because stating one honestly requires the sample size, the date and the method.

faqs.question: What does M1 or A1 mean on my child's marked IGCSE maths paper?
faqs.answer: A method mark rewards a correct approach even where the arithmetic afterwards fails, so it is earned by the substitution or setup being written down. An accuracy mark requires the correct value in the required form, which is where exact answers and rounding discipline matter. There are also independent marks for specific steps, follow-through credit for later work built on an earlier error where the working is visible, and dependency, where one mark requires another having been earned first.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when their final answer is right?
faqs.answer: Usually form or working. An accuracy mark requires the value in the form the question demanded, so a decimal where an exact answer was asked for scores less than it should. And on calculator-permitted papers, method marks follow what appears on the page rather than what appeared on the screen, so work done correctly on a device and not recorded earns little. Both are habits rather than gaps and both respond to three sessions of marked practice.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths error is cheapest to fix?
faqs.answer: Frequency density on histograms with unequal class widths, closely followed by scale factors between similar shapes and solids. The first is an entirely mechanical calculation that students either know or do not, and one lesson plus practice settles it. The second is a single rule covering linear, area and volume relationships and takes under half a lesson. Both appear regularly with marks attached, and both are routinely skipped in revision because they feel minor.

faqs.question: How do I find out where my child's algebra actually breaks down?
faqs.answer: Run an eight-rung ladder: substituting accurately, collecting terms and one bracket, double brackets, factorising a simple quadratic, rearranging with the subject appearing once, simultaneous equations, algebraic fractions, and rearranging with the subject on both sides. Twenty minutes, one question per rung. Most Extended candidates stall at the last rung, which is a finite repair. A stall at double brackets is a different and larger problem that will show up in every quadratic.

faqs.question: Should my Hydra Village child practise without a calculator?
faqs.answer: Only if they sit Cambridge 0580, which includes a paper taken without one. In that case yes, and specifically with the device physically out of the room for a fixed share of practice, because two years of calculator-assisted homework quietly outsources the exact skill that paper examines. A Pearson 4MA1 or Cambridge 0607 candidate should spend that time on calculator discipline instead: angle mode, stored values and recording on the page what was done on the device.

faqs.question: What is the right way to use IGCSE maths past papers?
faqs.answer: Four steps. Sit the paper to time with the correct calculator rule applied. Mark it strictly against the official published scheme for that series. Log every lost mark on one line with its category: content, method, notation or calculator, command word, rounding or form, or ran out of time. Then rework only the method and content questions. After three papers two or three categories dominate and the plan writes itself. Checking the total against a boundary found online achieves nothing.

faqs.question: Why does 'show that' get no credit for substituting the answer back in?
faqs.answer: Because the question asks for a derivation and substitution is verification, which is a different thing. Demonstrating that the printed value satisfies an equation shows the value works; it does not show how it was obtained, which is what the marks are for. This is one of the most common losses in Extended scripts and it is a vocabulary problem rather than a mathematical one. Two sessions on command terms usually fixes it along with several related faults.

faqs.question: Are bearings and transformations really worth revising?
faqs.answer: Yes, and every cohort skips both. Bearings have two rules — three figures, measured clockwise from north — and a method habit of sketching with north marked before any trigonometry. Transformations are a notation problem: schemes want the transformation named with its parameters, often in function notation, and a student describing the movement in a sentence has understood it without claiming the marks. Three marked pieces each is usually enough.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to Hydra Village for IGCSE maths lessons?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors in the emirate do travel and IB Gram does not. We teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not offer home visits in Hydra Village or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Published in-home rates run from AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on the source, against roughly AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor, and from a small gated community most of that difference is transport.

faqs.question: How much daily maths practice does a Year 11 student need?
faqs.answer: Twenty minutes on six days is worth considerably more than two hours in one sitting, because fluency is a retrieval problem and six separate recalls build it better than one long session. In a Hydra Village household the difficulty is placing the twenty minutes, since the afternoon is consumed by travel. The patterns that survive are immediately after changing while the student is still in school mode, or first thing in the morning. Left to spare time, it becomes a weekend batch.

faqs.question: Why is Additional Maths 0606 so hard for a good 0580 student?
faqs.answer: Because 0606 questions typically require three or four manipulation steps before the new calculus or logarithm content appears, and the limiting factor is the top rungs of the algebra ladder rather than the new ideas. A student who is comfortable but slow at rearranging with the subject on both sides will run out of time rather than out of understanding. The fix is volume of short algebra practice rather than re-teaching the new content.

faqs.question: Will you give us past papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: No. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are published on their own websites, which is also the only place you can be certain the version is current. A tutor works through them with your child from the official source. Boards revise specifications, and an unofficial downloaded copy can be two syllabuses out of date without saying so anywhere on it.

faqs.question: What score does my child need for a grade 7 or an A in IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: No figure can be given honestly, because grade boundaries are set after each series in light of that series' papers and candidate performance, and published afterwards. They move between series, so a fixed threshold on any website is invented certainty. The useful target is behavioural rather than numerical: fewer marks lost to rounding, form, command words and unrecorded working, which is measurable from one paper to the next and entirely within the student's control.

faqs.question: Should my child re-read a wrong answer or redo the question?
faqs.answer: Redo it from blank, about a week later. Reading a worked solution produces recognition — the feeling that the method is familiar — which the brain mistakes for the ability to reproduce it unprompted. Re-attempting from nothing produces retrieval, which is what the examination requires. This second-attempt rule is one of the cheapest improvements available to a revision routine and almost nobody applies it, because reading feels like progress and redoing feels like failure.

intro.heading: Why the school run decides whether IGCSE maths tutoring works in Khalifa City
paragraphs: Khalifa City is a commuting community in both directions. Children leave early for schools in Al Raha, on the island, in Mohammed Bin Zayed City and sometimes further, and they come back on a bus that does not arrive when the bell rings. Secondary finishes commonly fall between 14:45 and 15:30, and a bus route that collects three communities can add thirty to fifty minutes to that. By the time a child is home, changed and fed, the usable window has moved to somewhere between 16:00 and 17:00, or has disappeared into an activity.

That window is the real constraint on tutoring in this area, and it is why so many arrangements collapse in the second month rather than the first. An in-home tutor driving from Al Reem Island or Khalidiyah has to leave before the traffic builds to make a 16:00 start, which means they can serve one Khalifa City family in that slot and everybody else is offered 19:30. Families accept 19:30, discover that their Year 11 child cannot do algebra at 19:30 after a full day, and quietly stop.

Online delivery does not make a tired child alert, but it removes the journey from the equation on both sides. A 15:45 start becomes possible because nobody has to arrive, and a session can shift to the following evening without anyone recalculating a route. For a household in Al Raha Gardens with a short run, that means mathematics gets the alert hour. For a household in Al Reef with a long bus route, it means the realistic slot is after 20:00 and it can be held consistently rather than negotiated weekly.

The second thing to settle before any slot is booked is which examination your child is actually sitting. Khalifa City schools run both Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1, and both tier their entries. Past papers are freely available for both boards, which is exactly how students end up practising the right mathematics against the wrong question style. The warning sign is a mock result that makes no sense given the hours invested.

This page is organised around those two decisions. It sets out the slots that genuinely work from a Khalifa City address, the differences between 0580 and 4MA1 that change what revision should look like, the topics that cost the most marks in each tier, the term-by-term shape of a two-year plan counted backwards from the June and November series, and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons that sit in the same week and are rarely factored in. IB Gram runs no home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India, so every slot described here is a live video lesson rather than a doorstep arrival.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-khalifa-c.programmesIntro: Three routes produce the IGCSE maths cohort in the Khalifa City corridor, and each one arrives in Year 10 from a different place. The programme a child has come through matters more than their current mark, because it tells you which parts of the foundation are solid.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Tiered into Core and Extended, with Extended opening the full grade range and adding content rather than simply asking harder questions. Assessment is by terminal written papers with no coursework. Extended candidates face longer multi-step questions where a diagram usually has to be produced before anything can be calculated, and where method marks survive a wrong final answer only if the working is ordered and legible.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Your Khalifa City school publishes the version that applies to it. Any revision schedule should be built from that document rather than from a timetable found through a general search.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
programmes.description: Tiered into Foundation and Higher, with two written papers rather than the Cambridge paper pattern. Higher tier rewards algebraic fluency more aggressively and words its questions differently, so a student who has revised entirely from 0580 material arrives able to do the mathematics and unprepared for how it is asked. Formula provision also differs, which changes what has to be memorised.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those lead times are why a resit decision has to be planned before the first result lands.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Run to Year 11 at the IB continuum schools in and around Khalifa City, assessed against four criteria and graded 1 to 8. Students who transfer into an IGCSE school mid-key-stage arrive strong on investigation and reasoning and light on procedural speed, because MYP credits the quality of mathematical thinking more than fast, accurate manipulation under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Mid-key-stage transfers between the corridor's IB and British-track schools are common, and the resulting gap is specific rather than general: indices, surds, algebraic fractions and the structured paper technique that an IGCSE examination assumes. It is a short, well-defined job if it is tackled in the term after the move rather than in Year 11.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-khalifa-c.subjectsIntro: IGCSE mathematics is one grade built from several separate skills, and tutoring is organised by the skill that is failing rather than by the subject as a whole. These are the areas Khalifa City students lose marks in most often.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and handling algebraic fractions. The foundation everything else rests on, and the usual reason a capable student stalls in Year 11: the algebra is correct but slow, so questions get abandoned halfway.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Transformations, inverse and composite functions and graph interpretation. Marks go when a sketch is required first and the student calculates instead, or when a transformation is applied in the wrong order.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled work at Core, extending to the sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems at Extended. The highest-value topic for targeted tutoring, because the method is formulaic once a correct diagram exists.

subjects.name: Geometry and mensuration
subjects.description: Circle theorems, similarity, surface area and volume of compound solids. Circle theorems in particular are learnable in a few hours and routinely under-taught, so they return marks faster than almost anything else on the syllabus.

subjects.name: Number and ratio
subjects.description: Percentages, compound interest, standard form, bounds and ratio problems. Easy marks lost to rounding too early, to misreading a reverse percentage, and to giving an answer to an accuracy the question did not ask for.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Averages from grouped data, cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal intervals and tree diagrams. Histogram frequency density and conditional probability account for a disproportionate share of lost marks at Extended.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and the four transformations. The proof-style vector questions at the end of an Extended paper are where strong candidates separate from middling ones, and where practice has the clearest effect.

subjects.name: Calculator and non-calculator technique
subjects.description: Knowing which paper permits what, how to use memory and fraction functions efficiently, and how to show enough working that method marks survive. Quickly taught and worth several marks spread across a whole paper.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: The optional bridge into Diploma or A-Level mathematics, introducing calculus and advanced algebra a year early. Taken alongside 0580 Extended by stronger Year 11 students, and the best preparation available for Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language 0544
subjects.description: Included because it sits in the same week as maths for almost every Khalifa City student. Arabic is mandatory in UAE private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and it competes for the same evening hours a maths plan needs.

sections.heading: The Khalifa City school day, and the only slots that actually hold
paragraphs: Work backwards from dismissal rather than forwards from a preferred time. Secondary schools serving this corridor commonly finish between 14:45 and 15:30. A bus collecting Khalifa City, Al Raha and sometimes Al Reef adds thirty to fifty minutes on top, and arrival varies by route rather than by school, so two children at the same school can be home forty minutes apart. After changing and eating, the earliest reliable start for most households is 15:45 to 16:15, and for long routes it is closer to 17:00.

The second window opens after 20:00, once evening activities and family dinner are out of the way. It is a genuine window and it holds well, provided the work is chosen for it. A tired Year 11 student can practise circle theorems, work through a past-paper section with a diagram already drawn, or drill calculator technique. The same student cannot absorb algebraic fractions for the first time at 20:30, and booking new content into that slot is the most common reason a plan is abandoned in month two.

What falls between those two windows is the dead zone: 17:00 to 19:30, occupied by sport, Arabic or Quran classes, siblings' schedules and the second school run. An in-home tutor needs that zone to make the economics work, because driving to Khalifa City for a single 16:00 lesson is not viable. Online, the two real windows are both available at the same price, which is the whole practical argument for the format in this particular community.

sections.heading: 0580 or 4MA1: find out before you book anything
paragraphs: Both boards are taught in this corridor, sometimes in neighbouring schools and occasionally within one family. Cambridge tiers 0580 into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel tiers 4MA1 into Foundation and Higher. The mathematics overlaps heavily. The examinations do not. Question wording differs, the paper structures differ, formula provision differs, and the mark schemes credit different things, which means past-paper practice is only useful if it comes from the right board.

The failure is quiet, which is what makes it expensive. A student revises diligently from freely available papers, performs well on them, and then produces a mock result that nobody can explain given the hours invested. The usual cause is not weak mathematics but practice against unfamiliar question styles, particularly in the longer multi-step questions where the two boards set up a problem differently. Ask the school which board, which code and which tier, in writing, and give that answer to any tutor before the first session.

The tier question matters nearly as much. Extended and Higher open the full grade range and add content rather than simply asking harder questions. A family paying for Extended support while the school has entered the child for Core is buying material that will never be assessed. The reverse is worse. The entry decision usually lands between the autumn and spring mocks of Year 11 in this corridor, and parents are entitled to ask when it is made and on what evidence. Getting that answer in writing early is the cheapest thing on this page, because it fixes the content list a tutor works from for the rest of the course.

sections.heading: The topics that return the most marks per hour
paragraphs: Not all revision is equally productive, and with a limited weekly window the choice of topic matters more than the number of hours. Circle theorems are the clearest example: a well-defined set of rules, recognisable question types, and a reliable source of marks at Extended and Higher, usually under-taught because schools cover them once and move on. Three focused hours here often shows up in a mock more visibly than ten hours of general revision.

Trigonometry behaves similarly. Once a student reliably draws a correct labelled diagram before touching the formula, the sine and cosine rule questions become procedural. The failure is almost never the trigonometry; it is starting to calculate before the geometry is clear. Histograms with unequal class widths and conditional probability on tree diagrams are two more compact, high-yield topics, each learnable in a short block and each responsible for a disproportionate share of lost marks.

The topics that absorb time without returning much are the broad ones. General algebra practice spreads effort thinly across a skill that needs daily repetition rather than a weekly hour. Number work is usually already secure. The sensible plan is to take the marked mock, list the lost marks by topic, and spend the window on the three compact topics with the largest losses, leaving algebra to short daily drills the student does alone between sessions. That split matters because a weekly hour is a teaching resource rather than a practice resource, and spending it on something that needs daily repetition converts expensive time into cheap time.

sections.heading: Working with the school's own material, not against it
paragraphs: A tutor running a parallel syllabus creates a second workload, and a Year 11 student in Khalifa City does not have room for one. The useful arrangement is narrower: the tutor works from the school's scheme of work, the current worksheet, and the marked mock script, and spends the hour on whatever that material shows is failing. Parents can make this happen by sending the worksheet before the session rather than after, which takes a minute and changes what the hour is worth.

The marked mock is the single most valuable document in the arrangement, and it is often not shared because nobody thinks to ask. It shows whether a mark was lost to missing content, to invisible method, or to running out of time, and those three causes have three different remedies. A tutor working without it spends two or three paid hours reconstructing by conversation what the script would have shown in ten minutes.

Second marking is worth more than it sounds. A full Extended paper marked properly against the scheme takes thirty to forty-five minutes, and the written feedback is where most visible improvement comes from. Ask whether marking is inside the fee or charged separately, because a slightly higher rate that includes it is usually the cheaper arrangement. Ask also for a short written note after each session, so you can see what was covered without interrogating your child about it at dinner. A note naming the topic, the marks lost and the next target takes a tutor two minutes and gives a parent something to check against the following mock.

sections.heading: Two years, counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Spending evenly across Year 10 and Year 11 costs the same as spending well and achieves less. The grade is decided in the final two terms, and the shape that works is light, consistent support in Year 10 to build habits, a step up after the Year 11 mocks once the lost marks are visible and the tier is settled, and an intensive block in the eight to ten weeks before the first paper. The alternative, heavy hours in Year 10 autumn and nothing in the spring of Year 11, is a common and expensive mistake.

The dates that bind are earlier than the examinations. Final entries are submitted by the centre months before the series opens, and the tier decision has to precede them. Mocks come one or two terms before the papers and are the diagnostic for everything after. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered in India only, so a plan built around a spring sitting is built on the wrong country's calendar.

Pearson's documented lead times show why resit planning happens early. The November 2026 final International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Build the intensive block backwards from the first paper on your school's zone timetable, and link the board's live timetable rather than trusting any restatement of it, including this one.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the week maths has to fit into
paragraphs: Any realistic plan for a Khalifa City week has to account for the mandatory UAE subjects, which almost no tutoring provider mentions. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is the reason an international-curriculum timetable in Abu Dhabi carries lessons that a British or American timetable elsewhere does not.

Dubai's regulator has published the most detailed public version of how this works, and while KHDA's guidance applies to Dubai schools, it illustrates the structure families meet across the country. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes.

The practical consequence for a maths plan is competition for evening hours. Arabic in particular rewards short, frequent practice rather than intensive blocks, which is the opposite of what works for pre-examination mathematics. Families who map the whole week before booking a maths slot generally find one window that holds for a term. Families who book the maths hour first and then discover the Arabic class tend to be renegotiating by the third week, and renegotiated slots are the ones that quietly disappear.

sections.heading: Booking a slot that survives the term
paragraphs: The test of a tutoring slot is not whether it works in a good week but whether it works in a bad one. Pick the time that holds when the bus is late, when a sibling has a fixture, and when a parent is still on the Sheikh Zayed bridge at 18:30. A slot chosen for an average Tuesday gets cancelled three times a term, and three cancellations is usually where continuity breaks and the arrangement ends.

Before the trial, send three things: the board and code, the marked mock script, and the current worksheet. The trial hour is free, runs over live video, takes no card details and creates no commitment. Its only purpose is to find out whether this tutor can explain the specific thing your child is stuck on in a way your child follows. That is not a judgement anybody should pay a market hourly rate to make.

After four sessions, check against the mock that started the plan. Either the lost marks in the targeted topics are coming back or they are not. If they are not, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes, which may mean a different tutor, a different frequency or a different slot. Saying that early costs nothing. Saying it at the end of term costs a term, and in Year 11 there are not many terms left to spend. The same applies to the slot itself: if it has been cancelled twice, change it rather than hoping the third week goes better.
