faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE maths session realistically start in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: Two windows work from this corridor. If the school is inside the community or the bus route is short, a 15:45 to 16:15 start is reliable and is the best hour of the day for new content. If the route is long, towards Al Reef or across to the island, the dependable slot is after 20:00, and the work has to suit a tired hour: past-paper sections, circle theorems, calculator technique. The 17:00 to 19:30 stretch is usually taken by activities, Arabic classes and second school runs, and slots booked there get cancelled.

faqs.question: Which maths code do Khalifa City schools enter students for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly and get it in writing, including the tier. Khalifa City schools run both Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580, tiered Core and Extended, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1, tiered Foundation and Higher. Past papers for both are freely available, which is how students end up revising diligently against the wrong question style. The warning sign is a mock result that makes no sense given the hours invested. Give the board, code and tier to any tutor before the first paid session rather than after it.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics give back the most marks per hour of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Circle theorems first: a compact, rule-based set of question types that schools cover once and move past, and the clearest return available at Extended or Higher. Trigonometry next, once the habit of drawing a correct labelled diagram before calculating is fixed, after which the sine and cosine rule questions become procedural. Histograms with unequal class widths and conditional probability on tree diagrams are two more short, high-yield blocks. General algebra is better handled by short daily drills than by the weekly hour, because it needs repetition rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Is an evening maths session after 20:00 worth paying for?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the content suits it. A tired Year 11 student can work through a past-paper section, practise circle theorems with the diagram already drawn, or drill calculator technique productively. The same student cannot meet algebraic fractions for the first time at 20:30. Evening arrangements fail when new content is booked into them, not because the hour is late. For long bus routes in Al Reef or multi-community routes through Al Raha, a consistent evening slot beats an optimistic afternoon one that gets cancelled.

faqs.question: Should a Khalifa City student revise from both boards' past papers?
faqs.answer: No. Use the board your child is entered for, and nothing else, until the final weeks. Cambridge and Pearson word questions differently, structure papers differently and provide different formulae, so practice from the wrong board teaches the right mathematics in the wrong format. If you want extra material late in the course, individual topic questions from the other board can be used for drill, but full papers should always come from the correct one. Confirm the code with the school before building any revision set.

faqs.question: When does the school decide Core or Extended, and can we influence it?
faqs.answer: In this corridor the decision usually lands between the autumn and spring mocks of Year 11, based on mock evidence, and it belongs to the school. Parents can reasonably ask when it is made, on what evidence, and whether it can be revisited. If your child is sitting on the boundary, the useful window is before the decision: targeted work on the specific Extended-only topics is a short, well-defined job. After the entry is submitted, support shifts to paper technique within the chosen tier, and the hours required usually fall.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor need to mark full past papers, or is going through answers enough?
faqs.answer: Marking properly against the scheme is where most of the visible improvement comes from, and it is not the same as going through answers verbally. A full Extended paper takes thirty to forty-five minutes to mark well, which is why some tutors include it in the rate and others charge separately. Ask before you book. Written feedback that names which mark was lost and why gives you and your child something to act on, where a spoken walkthrough in the session tends to leave no record by the next week.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a Year 11 student in this area need?
faqs.answer: One reliable hour a week through most of Year 11, rising to two in the eight to ten weeks before the series once the mock has shown exactly which marks are missing. Two sessions from the start of the year usually spends the budget before the term that decides the grade, and a Khalifa City student is already carrying several hours of homework a night plus Arabic and activities. Consistency matters more than frequency: one hour that happens every week beats two that happen most weeks.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to homes in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: Some local tutors do, and the market prices it accordingly: in-home one-to-one in Abu Dhabi is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 UAE survey, with independents reaching AED 500. IB Gram is not one of them. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE from us; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India. Khalifa City lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is also why both the afternoon and the late-evening window are available rather than only one.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor help with maths and physics in the same week?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and it is a sensible pairing, because weak algebra usually shows up in physics before anyone links the two. A tutor holding both 0580 Extended and 0625 Extended can tell you whether a physics problem failed on the physics or on the rearrangement. Ask which of the two subjects they have actually taught to the examination rather than which they are comfortable with. Pairings that rarely work are a science with English or Arabic, where the teaching skill is genuinely different.

faqs.question: How does the Arabic class affect when maths tutoring can happen?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and almost no tutoring provider mentions it. Arabic is mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and after-school Arabic or Quran classes commonly occupy the 17:00 window that families assume is free. Arabic also rewards short, frequent practice, which competes directly with the evening hours a pre-examination maths plan needs. Map the whole week before booking a maths slot. Families who do this find one window that holds for a term; families who do not are renegotiating by week three.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first maths session?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they take five minutes to gather. The board, code and tier in writing from the school. The most recent marked mock script with the teacher's annotations left on it. The current worksheet or topic the class is working through. The script shows whether marks were lost to content, to invisible method or to timing, which are three different problems with three different remedies. Without it, two or three paid hours go on reconstructing by conversation what the paper would have shown immediately.

faqs.question: Is a weekend double session better than two weekday hours?
faqs.answer: For an intensive block before the series, often yes: two hours on a Saturday is long enough for a full past paper and proper feedback in one sitting. For year-round support it is weaker, because a seven-day gap lets content decay and the first part of each session goes on recovery. The strongest pattern for a Khalifa City family with no usable weekday window is a weekend double plus a short midweek check by message, which keeps some rhythm without needing an evening slot that does not exist.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE maths tutor be matched for Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: For 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher, usually within a few days, because online delivery means availability is not limited to tutors living near Khalifa City. Additional Mathematics 0606 takes longer, as does a request tied to a specific evening slot in the weeks before a series, when the tutors who know a code well are already committed. You will be told which situation applies rather than offered a quick general match, since a fast poor match means paying for the same diagnosis twice.

faqs.question: What if the slot we choose stops working after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Change it, early and without apology. Term patterns shift: activities start, bus routes are redrawn, mock weeks land. Because nobody is travelling to a Khalifa City address, moving a weekly slot costs nothing and does not require a tutor to redraw a route across the emirate. The arrangement that fails is the one where a family keeps a broken slot out of politeness, cancels three times, and then stops altogether. Say it in week two, not at the end of the term.

intro.heading: Does anyone near Madinat Zayed actually know your child's maths syllabus?
paragraphs: The honest answer is that plenty of people near Madinat Zayed know mathematics, and considerably fewer know the specific syllabus your child is entered for. Those are different claims. A graduate engineer can solve every question on a Cambridge 0580 Extended paper. Whether they know that Core caps at grade C, that one paper in each tier is now sat without a calculator, or that Edexcel's 4MA1 grades on a 9-to-1 scale while Cambridge grades A* to G, is a separate matter — and it is the matter that decides whether an hour of tuition lands on the right thing.

There are five syllabuses in regular use across Abu Dhabi schools and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 runs in Core and Extended tiers. Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 is a different course with a graphic display calculator built into its assessment and an investigation component, used by schools heading towards the IB Diploma. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 is a stretch course sat alongside 0580 Extended. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, 4MA1, runs Foundation and Higher tiers across two calculator papers. Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 sits above it.

So the first thing worth doing costs nothing. Find your child's statement of entry, or ask the school's examinations officer, and write down the syllabus code and the tier. Parents in Madinat Zayed routinely discover at this point that the child they thought was sitting Extended is entered for Core, or that the school moved from Cambridge to Edexcel between cohorts. Either discovery changes what tuition should cover, and finding it out in Year 10 rather than in the spring of Year 11 is the difference between a plan and a rescue.

The second thing worth doing is testing a prospective tutor on that code specifically. Ask which paper in their tier is non-calculator. Ask what the grade ceiling is on Core and whether it can be lifted. Ask what happens to a Higher-tier Edexcel candidate who scores below the tier's bottom grade. A tutor who knows the syllabus answers in a sentence each; a tutor who knows maths in general gives you a reassuring paragraph without a single specific. That five-minute conversation is worth more than any rate comparison.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE maths tuition to Madinat Zayed as one-to-one lessons over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The practical consequence for this particular question is the useful one: the pool of tutors who know 0607's investigation paper, or 4PM1's calculus content, is small in any one neighbourhood and reasonably large across a time zone. Removing the drive removes the reason to compromise on the syllabus.

The mathematics here is the foundation the IGCSE assumes: negative numbers, fractions, index laws, basic algebraic manipulation and the four operations without a calculator. A Checkpoint result is diagnostic rather than certificated, and it is the cheapest early warning a family will get.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools licensed by ADEK vary in how seriously they run Checkpoint, and some skip it entirely. For a Madinat Zayed family the useful question is not the Checkpoint score but whether the school has already streamed the year group into future Core and Extended groups. That streaming often happens in Year 9 and it quietly sets a grade ceiling two years before anyone mentions one.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Syllabus 0580, in Core and Extended tiers. Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4, each paper carrying half the grade. From the current syllabus, one paper in each tier is sat without a calculator, which is the change most families have not registered. Confirm the exact durations and components on cambridgeinternational.org, because Cambridge revises them between syllabus cycles.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any advice built around a spring sitting does not apply in Abu Dhabi. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that the correct zone timetable must be used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after using the wrong version. Take dates from your school, not from a tutoring site.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
programmes.description: Syllabus 0607, a genuinely different course from 0580 rather than a variant of it. A graphic display calculator is integral to the assessment, the content leans towards modelling and functions, and the course is structured to feed the IB Diploma. Schools in Abu Dhabi with an IB Diploma pathway often choose it deliberately. A tutor who teaches 0580 well is not automatically useful here.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single most common syllabus mismatch in Abu Dhabi tuition. A Madinat Zayed family books a tutor for 'IGCSE maths', the tutor arrives with 0580 Extended material, and the student is sitting 0607 Extended with a graphic display calculator they are expected to use fluently. Nothing is dishonest about it; the booking simply never named the code. This is why the code matters more than the subject name.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Specification 4MA1, Mathematics A, in Foundation and Higher tiers. Two papers of two hours, each worth half the grade, with a calculator permitted on both. Grades run 9 to 1, with Foundation capped and Higher reaching down to a safety grade below its nominal floor. Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 sits above it for students heading to A-Level maths or an engineering pathway.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Where most Extended and Higher-tier candidates go next, and the reason tier choice at IGCSE is not a cosmetic decision. A-Level Mathematics assumes algebraic fluency that Core and Foundation candidates were never required to demonstrate, so the step up from a capped tier is steep. Further Mathematics assumes more again.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states six subjects are needed; the sourced figure is five.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-madinat-z.subjectsIntro: Maths is rarely the only entry a Madinat Zayed family wants help with. These are the IGCSE subjects most often added, with the syllabus code and the specific place marks are lost in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Two papers, each half the grade, with one sat without a calculator in the current syllabus. Extended adds functions, calculus-adjacent gradient work, vectors and more demanding trigonometry. Core candidates lose most marks on multi-step problems; Extended candidates lose them on algebraic fractions and on questions requiring a proof-like argument.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: A graphic display calculator is assumed throughout and there is an investigation component. Modelling, functions and data handling carry more weight than on 0580. Students lose marks by producing a correct calculator output and failing to interpret it, which is exactly the habit the IB Diploma will test later.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two two-hour calculator papers, graded 9 to 1. Higher tier rewards speed as much as knowledge, because the paper is long and the final questions carry the top grades. Foundation candidates most often lose marks on ratio, proportion and percentage change in unfamiliar contexts rather than on the arithmetic itself.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606) and Further Pure (4PM1)
subjects.description: Stretch courses sat alongside the main entry, introducing calculus, series and more formal algebra. They are the clearest signal that a student is heading for A-Level mathematics. Marks are lost to notation and to unexplained steps, because both specifications expect working that reads like an argument.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: The subject most damaged by weak maths. Rearranging formulae, handling standard form and reading logarithmic scales are mathematical skills examined through physics. Practical assessment differs by board and by school, and the alternative-to-practical paper has its own distinct technique.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, empirical formulae and titration arithmetic are where the marks concentrate and where maths weakness shows. Organic chemistry is the other recurring wall. Students who can recite reaction conditions but cannot calculate a yield are scoring in the wrong half of the paper.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: High content volume with a statistics and data-interpretation strand that catches students who chose biology to avoid numbers. Marks are recoverable in command-term discipline: describe, explain and compare each demand a different structure, and answering the wrong one wastes a correct fact.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455 / Edexcel 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest source of recoverable marks: axes labelled, curves shifted rather than described, equilibrium identified. Data-response questions reward arithmetic on percentage change and index numbers, which returns the maths problem to a subject chosen to escape it.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510/0511)
subjects.description: Widely sat across Abu Dhabi and frequently the subject that decides whether a student clears five passes for equivalency. The reading paper rewards precise lifting of information; the writing paper rewards register control. Both are trainable in a term, which makes it the highest-yield entry for a borderline candidate.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate provision for Arab and non-Arab students. These subjects are not counted among the five required for British-track Ministry of Education equivalency, which surprises many families planning their entries.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: West along the island, with a dense school corridor and a mix of Cambridge and Edexcel entries between neighbouring schools. Families here are the ones most likely to find two children on different boards in the same household.

regions.name: The Corniche
regions.note: Waterfront towers with the shortest school run on the island. The earliest realistic tuition slot in the emirate sits here, which matters for a Year 11 candidate also carrying a November entry.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: An established villa district inland from the Corniche with several long-standing private schools. A number of them have switched board between cohorts, so the syllabus code in an older sibling's file is not a safe guide for the younger one.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Bridge-access towers where the afternoon crossing lengthens sharply after 15:30. Online sessions remove the question of whether a tutor can make a second crossing in a working afternoon.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A large off-island villa community with its own cluster of international schools and a heavy Edexcel presence. A tutor serving Khalifa City and Madinat Zayed in one afternoon is serving one of them badly.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Dense mainland housing with the widest spread of curricula and budgets on this list. The AED 45 to 150 end of the maths tuition market is most visible here, and the variation in what it delivers is widest.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Low-rise waterfront and villa communities near the airport corridor. Strong school access, and a long enough drive to the central grid that cross-area in-home tutoring rarely holds across a full term.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Several well-known international schools and a later finish than the central island. Madinat Zayed students enrolled there arrive home later and start tuition later, which pushes the realistic slot past 17:30.

schoolClusters.city: Central Abu Dhabi island — Madinat Zayed, Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and the Corniche
schoolClusters.note: The island's established school corridor, 10 to 20 minutes from Madinat Zayed depending on the hour. Boards are mixed across this cluster: some schools run Cambridge IGCSE, others Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a few enter different subjects with different boards in the same year group. Named here as local context only, with no affiliation implied.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: The off-island corridor, where much of the emirate's newer provision sits and where Pearson Edexcel entries are common. A Madinat Zayed family enrolled here has a 25 to 40 minute afternoon drive, which is the usual reason a weekly in-home session slides later through the term.

Working appears on a shared whiteboard line by line, past papers are annotated by both parties at once, and the session is recorded. sections.heading: The five IGCSE maths syllabuses in Abu Dhabi use, and why the code decides everything
paragraphs: A parent asking for an IGCSE maths tutor in Madinat Zayed is asking for one of five fairly different things. Cambridge 0580 is the mainstream course, tiered Core and Extended, with one non-calculator paper in each tier under the current syllabus. Cambridge 0607, International Mathematics, assumes a graphic display calculator throughout and carries an investigation element. Cambridge 0606 is a stretch paper sat alongside Extended. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 runs Foundation and Higher across two calculator papers graded 9 to 1. Further Pure 4PM1 sits above it.

The practical consequence is that the same request produces four different lesson plans. A 0580 Extended student needs non-calculator fluency drilled weekly. A 0607 student needs calculator technique plus interpretation, because the examiner marks what the output means. A 4MA1 Higher student needs pace, since the two-hour papers are long and the last questions carry the top grades. A 4PM1 student needs notation discipline. A tutor given only the words 'IGCSE maths' will default to whichever of these they know best.

Finding the code takes one message. The statement of entry lists it, and the school's examinations officer can confirm it in a line. Families in this area regularly discover that a sibling two years older sat a different board, because schools do switch between cohorts and specification codes change on the same subject name. Checking costs nothing and it is the single highest-value thing a parent can do before spending anything on tuition.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: the ceiling nobody mentions
paragraphs: Tier is the decision with the longest shadow and it is usually made by the school, quietly, in Year 9 or early Year 10. On Cambridge 0580, Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above grade C however well they perform; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and reach A*. On Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, Foundation is capped partway up the 9-to-1 scale while Higher reaches 9 and extends a grade below its nominal floor as a safety net.

This matters because a capped tier closes doors a family has not yet thought about. A-Level Mathematics, most engineering foundation routes and several UAE university programmes expect a grade that a Core or Foundation entry cannot produce. A student sitting Core and achieving the ceiling grade has done well and is still, administratively, below the threshold for the next course. Nobody says this at the point the entry is made, because at that point it is a reasonable and often correct decision.

The useful move is to test the ceiling before it is set rather than argue about it afterwards. Three or four sessions of timed Extended-tier questions, marked against the published scheme, tell you honestly whether the higher tier is reachable and what would have to change for it to be. That is a stronger case to take to a head of department than a report grade or a parent's impression. If the answer is that Core is right, a family has bought certainty rather than a year of doubt.

sections.heading: How to tell in five minutes whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Ask closed questions with checkable answers. Which paper in my child's tier is sat without a calculator? What is the highest grade available on this entry? How many papers are there and what is each worth? Which topics appear only on Extended? A tutor fluent in the specification answers each in a sentence. A tutor who knows mathematics generally answers with reassurance, enthusiasm and no specifics, and that difference is audible within a minute.

Then ask a diagnostic question rather than a credential question. Not 'how much experience do you have' but 'what would you look at first if my child scored well on the calculator paper and badly on the non-calculator one?' The right answer names by-hand fluency, exact values, index laws and fraction work, and proposes short weekly practice rather than more content teaching. A vague answer here is the single most reliable warning sign available to a parent.

Third, ask what they will not do. A tutor who knows the rules will tell you, unprompted, that they do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because those are the awarding body's copyright and the correct route is the official site or the school. They will also say they do not produce assessed work. A tutor who offers you a folder of mark schemes on the first call is telling you something about how they operate.

Finally, ask about the series. Which window is your child entered for, and what changes between June and November? A tutor working with Abu Dhabi families knows that the February/March series is India-only, that November is the resit route here, and that the entry deadline sits months ahead of the paper. One who answers that question with a date they have read off a blog is guessing with your child's timetable, and the exams officer at the school is the only person whose dates are authoritative.
bullets: Which paper in this tier is non-calculator?
What is the grade ceiling on this entry, and can it be changed?

sections.heading: Where IGCSE maths marks are actually lost in Abu Dhabi cohorts
paragraphs: Algebraic fractions are first, and they are first on both boards. Adding, simplifying and solving with algebraic fractions appears in the upper half of Extended and Higher papers, it is taught once, and it is rarely practised to fluency. A student who hesitates here loses a cluster of marks in the questions that separate the top grades, and the fix is mechanical practice rather than explanation.

Second is the non-calculator paper, which is a newer problem than most families realise. Students who have had a calculator in hand since Year 7 arrive unable to work with surds, exact trigonometric values or index laws by hand. The paper exists specifically to find that out. Rebuilding takes around eight weeks of short weekly practice and it cannot be compressed into the fortnight before a mock.

Third is pace on the Pearson Edexcel Higher papers. Two hours is a long time to maintain accuracy, and the final questions hold the top grades. Students who have only ever done exercise sets never discover that they run out of time, because exercises are untimed. Fourth is command-term carelessness: 'show that' requires working, 'write down' does not, and 'give your answer to three significant figures' is a mark.

Fifth, and specific to Abu Dhabi timetables, is a thin November and December, when mandatory UAE subject assessments compete with IGCSE coursework in the same weeks. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are required in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the week has a fixed number of hours in it. A Madinat Zayed family who notices maths slipping in late November is usually looking at a timetable collision rather than at a sudden loss of ability, and the response is scheduling rather than panic.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a spring sitting does not apply to a student in Madinat Zayed. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Those are the two windows your child's year has to be planned around.

Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, which is the fact that catches families out. A decision taken in April about a summer sitting is usually already past the window, and a private-candidate entry is harder again because it has to go through a centre that accepts external candidates. The school's examinations officer holds the real dates. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after using the wrong one.

Counted backwards from a sitting, the sequence is stable even when the dates are not. The last six to eight weeks belong to whole papers under timing, marked against the published scheme. Before that sits the mock window, which is the most useful free diagnostic a family will get. Before that, the tier must be fixed and any entry change made. For reference on how far ahead results sit: the November 2026 Pearson timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: What the Abu Dhabi market charges, starting from the cheapest end
paragraphs: Begin where most families begin, at the bottom. A university-student or graduate tutor working online is advertised from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. For a Core or Foundation candidate who needs arithmetic drilled and company while doing it, that band can be entirely adequate. What it does not reliably buy is specification knowledge — which paper is non-calculator, which topics are Extended-only, what the grade ceiling is — and on a tiered entry that knowledge is the whole game.

The next band up is where specification fluency starts. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270; Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits are quoted higher again, at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with the difference paying for a car rather than for better teaching.

Thinking in months rather than hours makes the decision easier. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000-plus for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages seen in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published figures, quoted with their sources so you can check them; they are not an IB Gram price list. We quote after a free trial lesson, once the code and tier are known.

sections.heading: After the IGCSE: Ministry of Education equivalency and the five-subject rule
paragraphs: Families in Madinat Zayed planning a UAE university route need to know what the Ministry of Education counts, because it is narrower than most people assume and one competing tutoring page states it wrongly. On the British track, students must submit proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. That single clause changes entry planning for a large number of UAE-educated students, because a child with seven passes including Arabic and Islamic Education may have fewer counting subjects than the certificate suggests. One ranking competitor publishes a requirement of six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five, excluding those two. Confirm your own case against the Ministry's own channel rather than any tutoring site, including this one.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and no tutoring is required for it. What a tutor can do is make sure the entries that will count are the ones a student is strong in, which is a planning conversation worth having in Year 10 rather than after results. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, with at least 450 in SAT Mathematics required before applying.

sections.heading: ADEK, your school report, and the question to ask at parents' evening
paragraphs: Private schools serving Madinat Zayed are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is a different authority from Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority, from the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and from the federal Ministry of Education that supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Guidance written for Dubai does not describe your child's school.

An inspection band describes a whole school rather than a department, and a strongly rated school can still be thin in Extended-tier maths in a particular year — usually because an experienced teacher left and the timetable absorbed the gap. That is the most common real reason a Madinat Zayed family starts looking, and naming it changes the request from general maths help to cover for a specific tier and board. A school report tells you less: a report grade is a prediction against a cohort, while a mock sat under real timing and marked against the published scheme tells you where the marks went.

So the question for parents' evening is not 'how is she doing in maths'. It is: which syllabus code and tier is she entered for, what was her mock score broken down by paper, and is the non-calculator paper the weaker one? Three answers, all free, and together they define what tuition should buy. On credentials, note that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, and private tutors need the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. IB Gram claims no regulator accreditation and holds none.

Ask for the mock score split by paper, not a single grade
Ask whether the non-calculator paper is the weaker one

process.title: Send the syllabus code and tier
process.description: 0580, 0607, 0606, 4MA1 or 4PM1, and whether the entry is Core, Extended, Foundation or Higher. It is on the statement of entry, and the school's examinations officer can confirm it in a line. That one detail is what separates a useful first session from a polite one, and it is the whole premise of this page.

process.title: Sit a free trial lesson with the matched tutor
process.description: Sixty minutes, no charge, with the tutor who would actually teach. It is a working session: questions from your child's own tier, under time, with the tutor watching the working rather than the answer. Ask them the five specification questions from this page while you are there.

process.title: Get the diagnosis in writing before any package
process.description: After the trial you should have a short written statement of what is weak, split by paper where possible, and what the first eight sessions will target. A provider who cannot produce that is selling hours. This is also when a rate is quoted for your child's tier and session length, against the market bands published above.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot around the Abu Dhabi afternoon
process.description: Slots run from 16:00 Gulf Standard Time for students finishing on the central island, with later options for those travelling back from Khalifa City, Saadiyat or Al Raha. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing. Same tutor, same hour each week — consistency moves a maths grade more than intensity does.

process.title: Re-test on a whole paper every six weeks
process.description: A full past paper under real timing, marked against the published scheme, with the component split compared to the previous one. If the non-calculator paper has not moved in twelve weeks, the plan is wrong and should change. This is also the point at which a family decides whether to continue paying, which is how it should work.

process.title: Decide the series and the resit route early
process.description: Whether the target is the June series or the November series changes everything about pacing, and the decision belongs with the school's examinations officer rather than with a tutor. Resit decisions are best taken in the week results arrive, not in October when the entry window has narrowed.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: 0580 Extended, 0607 Extended and 4MA1 Higher are three different jobs. Matching starts from the syllabus code and tier on the statement of entry, because a tutor fluent in one of those specifications is not automatically useful on another, however strong their mathematics.

whyPoints.description: Core and Foundation entries carry a grade ceiling that closes off A-Level Mathematics and several university routes. We say so before a package rather than after results, and we will run a timed diagnostic from the higher tier so the decision is made on evidence rather than on a report grade.

Three of six competitor pages researched publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams. A number you can check beats a reassurance you cannot.

whyPoints.description: Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them and link the official site; we do not host or distribute them. A tutor offering a folder of mark schemes on the first call is telling you how they operate.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE maths syllabus my child in Madinat Zayed is entered for?
faqs.answer: The syllabus code is printed on the statement of entry the school issues, and the examinations officer can confirm it in one message. You are looking for 0580, 0607 or 0606 for Cambridge, or 4MA1 or 4PM1 for Pearson Edexcel, together with the tier — Core, Extended, Foundation or Higher. Do not assume it matches an older sibling's: schools switch board between cohorts and specification codes change on the same subject name. Checking costs nothing and it is the highest-value thing a parent can do before spending anything on tuition.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and 0607 for my child?
faqs.answer: They are different courses rather than variants. 0580 is the mainstream syllabus, tiered Core and Extended, and under the current syllabus one paper in each tier is sat without a calculator. 0607, International Mathematics, assumes a graphic display calculator throughout, carries an investigation component, and leans towards modelling and functions because it is structured to feed the IB Diploma. A tutor who teaches 0580 well may be of limited use on 0607. This is the most common syllabus mismatch in Abu Dhabi tuition bookings.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended, or Foundation to Higher?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but only before entries are finalised, and the window is earlier than families expect. The school's maths department makes the recommendation and the examinations officer holds the deadline. The strongest case you can bring is evidence: three or four sessions of timed questions from the higher tier, marked against the published scheme, which shows honestly whether the grade is reachable and what would have to change. A report grade or a parent's impression carries much less weight in that conversation than a marked paper does.

faqs.question: Why does the non-calculator paper matter so much now?
faqs.answer: Because it is newer than most parents realise and it finds a specific weakness. Under the current Cambridge 0580 syllabus, one paper in each tier is sat without a calculator, which exposes students who have had a device in hand since Year 7. Surds, exact trigonometric values, index laws and fraction arithmetic all have to be secure by hand. Rebuilding that fluency takes roughly eight weeks of short weekly practice and cannot be compressed into the fortnight before a mock. A mock split that shows a strong calculator paper and a weak non-calculator one is diagnosing this exactly.

faqs.question: Does my child in Abu Dhabi sit the Cambridge February/March series?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International offers the February/March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, with November functioning as the usual resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after using the wrong version. Take every date from your school's examinations officer rather than from a tutoring website.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE maths tutor in Madinat Zayed cost per month?
faqs.answer: Thinking monthly is more useful than hourly. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000-plus for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published figures with their sources named, not an IB Gram price list. We quote after a free trial, once the code and tier are known.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutor in Abu Dhabi ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth saying so. For a Core or Foundation candidate who needs arithmetic drilled regularly and company while doing it, a graduate tutor at the AED 45 to 150 band — EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 — can be entirely adequate. What that band does not reliably buy is specification knowledge: which paper is non-calculator, which topics are Extended-only, where the grade ceiling sits. On a tiered entry, that knowledge is most of the value, which is why the band above it exists.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE maths topics do Abu Dhabi students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fractions first, on both boards — they sit in the upper half of Extended and Higher papers, are taught once and rarely practised to fluency. Then non-calculator technique: surds, exact values and index laws by hand. Then pace, particularly on Pearson Edexcel's two-hour Higher papers, where the final questions hold the top grades and are frequently unreached. Then command-term carelessness: 'show that' requires working, significant-figure instructions carry marks. All four respond faster to short weekly practice than to more content teaching.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel maths for Abu Dhabi schools?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we match to one specification rather than claiming general coverage. Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 at Foundation and Higher, and Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1. Schools around Madinat Zayed use a mix, and a few enter different subjects with different boards in the same year group, so the code on the statement of entry decides the match. We do not supply any board's syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes.

faqs.question: Which schools near Madinat Zayed sit IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: The central island corridor within a short drive includes schools such as Abu Dhabi International School, Cambridge High School Abu Dhabi, Al Ittihad National Private School and Emirates Private School; the off-island corridor adds Al Yasmina Academy, GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi, Raha International School and Brighton College Abu Dhabi. Boards are mixed across those schools and provision changes between intakes, so confirm the current position directly with the school. All are licensed and inspected by ADEK. IB Gram has no affiliation with any school named here.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE grades will the Ministry of Education actually count for my child?
faqs.answer: On the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five, which catches out families whose child has seven passes including both. One ranking competitor publishes six as the requirement; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own case with the Ministry and your emirate's attestation authority, not with a tutoring site.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE maths coursework or an investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the mathematics an investigation needs, question the method, and give feedback on work the student has already produced. A tutor cannot write it, redraft it to completion, or supply mathematics for the student to transcribe as their own. The Cambridge 0607 investigation component is assessed work and the same boundary applies. The simple home test: if your child cannot explain each step unprompted, the work is not theirs and the mark is not safe. We also do not distribute board mark schemes or past papers.

faqs.question: Can sessions fit around school hours, prayer times and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the online format is what makes it practical rather than merely tolerable. Slots run from 16:00 Gulf Standard Time for students finishing on the central island, with later options for those travelling from Khalifa City, Saadiyat or Al Raha. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, and a family travelling between terms keeps the same tutor on the same clock. A tutor driving across the island at half past four cannot offer that, because their schedule is set by traffic rather than by your child's day.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the series — is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the plan has to change shape. Eight weeks is enough for whole papers under timing, command-term discipline, and targeted work on two or three recurring topics — algebraic fractions, ratio in unfamiliar contexts, or non-calculator fluency if the mock split points there. It is not enough to cover a syllabus, and any provider promising that is selling you a fiction. Start with one timed paper marked against the published scheme, and let the component breakdown decide where the remaining hours go.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for my child's exact syllabus and tier?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of filling the slot. Cambridge 0607 Extended and Pearson Edexcel 4PM1 are the narrowest pools on this page, and in a busy term the honest answer is sometimes a two to three week wait for the right match, or an interim tutor for general algebra while the specialist slot opens. Neither is hidden and neither is charged as though it were the match you asked for. None of the competitor pages researched for this page discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: The commute decides the maths week before the maths does
paragraphs: Masdar City was designed as a clean-technology and research district near Abu Dhabi International Airport, built around a university campus, with a street plan that deliberately keeps vehicles out of its pedestrian core and a residential population that is small and professional. There is no private school inside it. Every school-age child leaves the district each morning and returns each afternoon, and that one fact shapes a tutoring week more than any argument about method.

The direction of travel matters. The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor is the nearest school belt and the usual choice, which is fortunate: the journey is short enough that a student can be at a desk by four o'clock and an afternoon maths session is realistic. Families who have enrolled further out, on the islands or across the city, are looking at a longer run in both directions and an evening slot instead.

There is a smaller, local complication worth naming. Masdar City's core is pedestrianised, so the last leg of an afternoon is often a walk or a shuttle from a car park or transit point rather than a drive to the door. It adds minutes at exactly the point where minutes matter, and it is the sort of detail a tutoring page written from a template would never mention.

An in-home tutor has to land inside the same window, having driven in from wherever they live — in practice the Khalifa City corridor or Al Reef — and then park outside the pedestrian core and walk. A session that starts fifteen minutes late still costs the full hour. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. Lessons are live one-to-one video, which removes the arrival problem rather than managing it.

Maths is the subject where this matters most, because maths needs a surface, a pen, a calculator and a student who is not still catching their breath. A child handed a laptop on a sofa ten minutes after walking in will not do useful algebra. Thirty minutes between arrival and the session, and a table rather than a bed, are worth more than most things a tutoring page would try to sell you.

One more thing families here get wrong is buying hours without a plan. An open-ended weekly session finds its own content, which usually means whatever homework is due, and that is supervision purchased at a specialist rate. A term plan costs nothing to write and changes what the same hours are worth, which is why half of this page is a calendar rather than a sales argument.

The rest of this page is that plan: which slots each school cluster actually leaves available, what belongs in each term of Year 10 and Year 11 for a June series, which topics are worth a paid hour and which ones the school is already covering adequately with provision you have funded, what the Abu Dhabi market charges for each kind of purchase in AED, and the boundary around assessed work. Read it and you will be able to price and place any tutoring offer in this city.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge syllabus 0580, covering number, algebra, coordinate geometry, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, vectors and transformations, probability and statistics. It is tiered into a Core route with a reduced syllabus and a capped grade range and an Extended route carrying the full content and full grade range, with both non-calculator and calculator components.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to a candidate sitting in Abu Dhabi. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: Pearson code 4MA1, tiered as Foundation and Higher. The content overlaps substantially with Cambridge 0580 but the papers, command terms, mark schemes and calculator policy differ, so revision is not transferable between the two in detail even where the mathematics is identical.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes and revises provisional timetables, so use the live official one rather than any restated date.

programmes.name: Additional and further maths options
programmes.description: Some schools enter stronger cohorts for an additional or further maths qualification alongside the main IGCSE, covering material that overlaps early AS content: more advanced algebra, series, trigonometric identities and calculus foundations. It is a bridge into sixth-form maths rather than a separate track.
programmes.countryNote: In a district where many parents work in engineering and research, this option comes up often and is usually a good idea for a secure student. The tutoring is short because the underlying IGCSE content is already solid — a handful of sessions on the genuinely new material, not a weekly arrangement.

programmes.name: What the maths grade gates
programmes.description: The IGCSE maths grade constrains the sixth-form choice more tightly than any other subject. A Level Mathematics and IB Higher Level maths courses normally require an Extended or Higher tier grade at a reasonable level, with each school setting its own threshold, and a lower-tier entry can close those routes early.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Khalifa City corridor and on the islands run both A Level and IB Diploma sixth forms, so the Year 11 maths grade is a genuine fork for a Masdar City family. That is why the Year 10 tier decision, not Year 11 revision, is where a small amount of tutoring money does the most work.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-masdar-ci.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of IGCSE maths worth a paid hour, with what each costs in marks. Both boards and both tiers covered.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and solving. The largest single loss at the higher tiers, because almost every multi-step question routes through it and one early slip costs the whole question rather than a mark.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.levels: Where a non-calculator paper is sat
subjects.description: Fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form, bounds and estimation without a machine. Capable students lose marks here simply because they have never revised with the calculator off the desk.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and bearings
subjects.description: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangles, sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional work. Bearings questions are lost almost entirely to not drawing and labelling the diagram first.

subjects.name: Geometry and mensuration
subjects.description: Angle reasoning, circle theorems, surface area and volume of compound shapes. Compound shapes carry several method marks that vanish when the working is not laid out in identifiable steps.

subjects.name: Graphs and functions
subjects.description: Straight lines, quadratics, reciprocal and exponential curves, transformations and function notation at the higher tiers. Marks go on reading values from a graph without the construction lines a marker expects.

subjects.name: Probability and statistics
subjects.description: Averages from tables, cumulative frequency, histograms, tree diagrams and conditional probability. Histograms with unequal class widths recur every series and are reliably under-practised.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry, translations, rotations, reflections and enlargements including negative scale factors. A small, dependable topic that students neglect relative to how often it appears.

subjects.name: Multi-step problem solving
subjects.description: Questions combining two or three topics with no signposting. These separate the top grades and the skill is planning the route before calculating, which is taught by doing rather than explained.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Mode settings, fraction and surd entry, statistical functions, and recording enough working that a correct display earns full credit. Usually the highest-return single session available and almost never offered.

subjects.name: Working presentation
subjects.description: Writing the steps a marker needs. Students doing three steps mentally and writing one line discard method marks they had earned. Three weeks of insistence fixes it permanently, at no content cost.

sections.heading: What the Masdar City school run leaves for a maths session
paragraphs: Start with the arrival time, not the school bell. A school in the Khalifa City or Al Raha corridor finishing around 3.15pm puts a Masdar City student home by roughly 3.50pm, allowing for the last pedestrian leg into the district's core. That supports a 4.30pm maths slot with a student who is still functioning, which is a genuine advantage over most of this emirate.

Push the school further out and the arithmetic changes quickly. Mohammed Bin Zayed City adds fifteen to twenty minutes. Yas Island is a cross-city run in both directions. Saadiyat is further again. By the time a family is enrolled on the islands, a six o'clock start is the first option that is not a fiction, and a school bus route rather than a car adds more.

The practical rule is arrival plus thirty minutes. That half hour is not politeness; it is the difference between a maths session and a session about being tired. Maths specifically punishes a rushed start, because an error in the first ten minutes propagates: a lost sign or a mode left in radians costs the next three questions rather than one mark.

There is also a case for shorter and more frequent rather than long and weekly, particularly for the longer commutes. Two forty-minute sessions beat one eighty-minute session for a tired student, and algebraic fluency responds better to frequent correction than to a long block anyway. That option exists because nobody is driving to a route.

sections.heading: The pedestrian core, and why in-home timing is worse than it looks
paragraphs: Masdar City was planned to keep vehicles out of its core, which is pleasant to live in and awkward for anyone arriving to work. A visitor does not pull up at the door. They park or arrive at a transit point and walk the last stretch, carrying whatever they brought, which for a maths tutor is papers and a calculator.

Add that to the journey. A resident tutor in the Khalifa City corridor or Al Reef driving in at half past four faces the airport-road traffic and then the walk. Fifteen minutes of slippage is routine, and a session that starts fifteen minutes late still costs the full hour. Over a term of weekly sessions that is several hours of teaching paid for and not received.

There is a second-order effect that families notice only after a few weeks. A tutor whose week is built around a driving route cannot move your Tuesday to a Thursday, because the route is the business. So the one thing that would help — shifting the session when a school activity or an exam week collides with it — is the thing the format cannot deliver.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run in India only, and no tutor will travel to a Masdar City address. The lesson happens on live video at the agreed minute, and the slot can move inside the week when the week demands it.

sections.heading: What belongs in each term of Year 10 and Year 11
paragraphs: Families buy an open-ended weekly hour and let it find its own content, which is why so much IGCSE maths spending achieves so little. A term plan costs nothing to make and changes what the hours are worth. Here is the shape that works, assuming a June series.

Year 10 is for content security and the tier decision. The autumn term is algebraic fluency, because everything later routes through it. The spring term is the tier conversation with the department, backed by four to six sessions on the specific content that separates Core from Extended or Foundation from Higher. The summer term is consolidation and the first full past paper, sat under timing, which establishes a baseline nobody has to argue about later.

Year 11 is for technique and papers. The autumn term is the remaining topic gaps, found from that baseline paper rather than guessed at. The winter is mocks, and mocks matter more as diagnostics than as predictions — a mock script is the best teaching material of the whole year. The spring is timed papers, error patterns, calculator discipline and working presentation, in that order of return.

The final four weeks should contain no new content at all. Timed papers, marked properly, with the repeating errors drilled. A family starting in those four weeks is buying the last stage without the first three, which is why late spend feels so expensive relative to what it delivers.

A November-series candidate shifts the whole plan back by roughly five months, and a resit candidate compresses it: the content is already covered once, so the work is error patterns and timing rather than teaching. Either way the principle holds — decide what each block is for before buying it, and the hours stop drifting.

sections.heading: Which topics are worth paying for, and which the school covers well
paragraphs: Not every weakness needs a tutor. Schools teach the syllabus competently and run revision provision you have already funded through fees, and for broad content coverage that provision is usually adequate and always cheaper. What schools do less well, through no fault of anyone, is individual error correction — a class of twenty-five does not permit a teacher to watch one student's working habits for an hour.

So the paid hour should go where individual attention is the active ingredient. Working presentation, because it needs someone watching every line and refusing to accept compressed steps. Calculator discipline, because it needs someone looking at the machine in the student's hand. Algebraic fluency, because it needs short frequent correction rather than explanation. Diagram habit on bearings and three-dimensional trigonometry, for the same reason.

What the school handles adequately: first teaching of each topic, broad revision of content, past-paper availability, and the mechanics of entry and timetabling. Buying tutoring for those is buying a second copy of something you already own.

There is one more category worth naming: topics that recur every series and get under-practised because they feel minor. Histograms with unequal class widths, vectors, transformations with negative scale factors, conditional probability from a tree diagram. These are reliable marks and a short block on them is excellent value precisely because neither the school nor the student prioritises them.

The test for whether to pay is worth stating as a question. Would an hour of someone watching this student work, one to one, change the outcome more than an hour of them revising it alone with the school's materials? If yes, buy the hour. If no, the school's provision and a past paper will do the job for nothing, and the money is better held back for the term when the answer changes.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and why it belongs in Year 10
paragraphs: In maths the tier sets a ceiling. A Core or Foundation entry caps the available grade; an Extended or Higher entry does not, but places harder algebra, trigonometry and multi-step problem solving in front of a student who may not be ready, with a real risk of a worse outcome than a secure lower-tier entry.

The cost of a capped entry lands in Year 12. A Level Mathematics and IB Higher Level maths courses normally require an Extended or Higher grade at a reasonable level, and sixth forms set their own thresholds. A Masdar City family choosing between an A Level sixth form and an IB Diploma sixth form in the Khalifa corridor will find both ask for it. Reopening a closed door means a resit series and another year's planning.

The timing argument is simple. A tier decision is made in Year 10 and absorbed as a fact. Four to six sessions placed before it is fixed, aimed at the content that separates the tiers, is a small defined cost protecting a large one. The same money in Year 11 buys general revision after the ceiling is already set.

Ask the department two questions and pay nothing for the answers: which tier is my child provisionally entered for, and what specifically would have to improve for the other tier to be viable. The second answer is a precise tutoring brief, obtained free, and it tells you whether to spend at all.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do, and how we handle papers
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the Diploma, but where it exists the boundary is identical and the consequences are as serious. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the mark scheme rewards, question a method until the student finds its weakness, read work the student produced and name which part is underselling it, and teach honest description of a method.

A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or complete assessed work, produce a model answer to the live task for adaptation, or supply data the student did not collect. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is an integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student, and it is not something we do at any fee.

On papers and mark schemes, we reference and link rather than redistribute. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyrighted material belonging to Cambridge or Pearson. A provider handing over a folder of scans is redistributing someone else's property, not adding value. Papers come through your school's exams officer or the board; what a tutor adds is the marking of your child's attempt against the real rubric.

One regulatory note parents ask about. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility extending to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted figure with suspicion. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation or partnership of any kind and operates no UAE office.

sections.heading: Making online maths work from a Masdar City desk
paragraphs: Maths over video works on one condition, and it is worth getting right in the first session rather than discovering in week four. The tutor must see handwritten working as it happens — a camera angled at paper, or a tablet and stylus. Without that the session becomes dictation and the one thing that needed watching, the student's own method, is invisible.

With it, the format has genuine maths advantages. A shared whiteboard retains every worked line, so last week's quadratic can be reopened rather than reconstructed from a notebook. The exact past-paper question is pasted onto the board instantly. Two methods can sit side by side. And the student writes on their own paper in their own hand, which is precisely what the exam will ask of them, rather than watching someone else write.

A Masdar City apartment supplies the rest without effort: reliable connectivity, a quiet building, and no visitor to admit through a pedestrianised core. What we ask for is a table rather than a bed, headphones, the correct calculator on the desk, and that camera on the paper. All four are free and all four change the quality of the hour.

The gain in selection is the real point. Rather than asking who can drive the airport road and walk in by five, we ask who teaches Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher and can read a marked script. From this district that reordering is the whole of the advantage.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE maths session start for a Masdar City student?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school, since none sit inside the district. From Al Raha Gardens, Al Raha Beach or Al Reef the journey is fifteen to twenty-five minutes and a 4.30pm start works. From Khalifa City or Shakhbout City, 4.30pm to 5pm. From Mohammed Bin Zayed City, 5.30pm. From Yas or Saadiyat, 6pm or later. We plan from arrival plus about thirty minutes, because maths punishes a rushed start: a sign lost in the first ten minutes costs the next three questions.

faqs.question: Does Masdar City's pedestrian core affect tutoring arrangements?
faqs.answer: It does, and nobody mentions it. The district was planned to keep vehicles out of its core, so the last leg of any arrival is a walk or shuttle from a car park or transit point rather than a drive to the door. For a family that is a few extra minutes at the end of the school run. For an in-home tutor it is a few extra minutes of slippage on top of the airport-road drive, and a session starting fifteen minutes late still costs the full hour. Online removes the problem entirely.

faqs.answer: Most use the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, which is the nearest belt and short enough to keep an afternoon tutoring slot realistic — a genuine advantage in this part of the emirate. Families wanting a particular programme rather than a short journey enrol on the islands or across the city, which moves the slot to the evening. Because our lessons are online, the direction of the commute changes which slot is available but not which tutor is, so no family is limited by where they enrolled.

faqs.question: What should each term of Year 10 and Year 11 maths actually contain?
faqs.answer: Year 10 autumn is algebraic fluency, because everything later routes through it. Year 10 spring is the tier decision with four to six sessions on the content that separates the tiers. Year 10 summer is a full past paper under timing, which gives a baseline. Year 11 autumn closes the topic gaps that baseline revealed. Winter is mocks used as diagnosis. Spring is timing, error patterns, calculator discipline and presentation. The final four weeks are timed papers only, with no new content at all.

Four to six sessions placed in Year 10, before the entry is fixed and aimed at the content separating the tiers, is a small cost protecting an expensive decision. faqs.answer: As teaching material, by a wide margin. A mock prediction is one data point on one day; a mock script is a page-by-page record of how your child answers under timing, which is the best diagnostic available all year and free. One session spent working through a marked mock, naming the repeating errors and what each costs, is usually worth more than three sessions of general revision. Families who file the mock and move on have thrown away the most useful thing the autumn produced.

intro.heading: One hour a week, and how to spend it on IGCSE maths
paragraphs: Almost every family in Mohammed Bin Zayed City arrives at the same constraint: there is one usable hour in the week for mathematics, maybe two, and no amount of good intention produces a third. The bus arrives when it arrives, Arabic or Quran class takes an afternoon, something takes the weekend, and the honest planning question is not how much tutoring to buy but what that single hour should contain.

Most of the hour gets wasted in the same way. A tutor who has not read a marked script works forward through the syllabus from wherever the class happens to be, and the first three or four weeks go on material the student already had. Meanwhile the actual lost marks sit in four topics the tutor has not reached yet. Reading the mock first costs nothing and is the difference between an hour that moves a grade and an hour that keeps a child company.

The second waste is treating all topics as equal. They are not, and not because some are harder. Some are compact, rule-based and reliably examined, which means a short block of work converts directly into marks. Circle theorems are the clearest case. Others are broad skills that need daily repetition rather than a weekly lesson, and spending the one available hour on general algebra practice converts expensive time into something a free worksheet would have done.

The third waste is the board. This corridor runs both Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, and past papers for both are freely available online. A student who revises diligently from the wrong board's papers does real mathematics in the wrong format and then produces a mock result nobody can explain. Confirm the code and tier in writing from the school before any revision set is built, and hand that answer to whoever teaches your child.

What follows is a method rather than a sales pitch. It explains how to read a marked script so you can tell content problems from technique problems, ranks the topics by how quickly they return marks, separates the calculator disciplines from the non-calculator ones, lays out an eight-week block before a series, and states where a tutor has to stop on coursework and official materials. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India, so every session described here reaches your child's desk over live video rather than arriving at a gate. One more thing worth saying before the method: none of what follows depends on hiring anybody. A parent who reads the script, ranks the topics and sets a slot from measured arrival times has already done the part that most arrangements get wrong, and a tutor is then being paid for teaching rather than for diagnosis a family could have supplied for free.
