abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-mohammed-.programmesIntro: Three starting points feed IGCSE mathematics in this part of Abu Dhabi, and each produces a recognisable profile of strengths and gaps. Knowing which one applies saves a diagnostic session.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
programmes.description: Tiered into Core and Extended, with Extended opening the full grade range and carrying additional content rather than merely harder questions. Assessed by terminal written papers with no coursework. Longer Extended questions typically require a correct diagram or a structured setup before any calculation is possible, and ordered working is what protects method marks when the final answer goes wrong.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm the current paper pattern and calculator rules for your child's entry with the school rather than assuming, because syllabus versions change and schools do not always flag it to parents. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
programmes.description: Tiered Foundation and Higher, with a different paper structure from Cambridge and noticeably terser question wording. Higher tier leans harder on algebraic fluency, and formula provision differs, which changes what has to be committed to memory. Students who revise from Cambridge material arrive able to do the mathematics and unready for how it is asked.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Link the live official timetable rather than relying on restated dates.

programmes.name: Transfers into IGCSE from other systems
programmes.description: Common across these zones, usually from Indian or Ministry curriculum schools. The arriving student generally has strong procedural arithmetic and algebra and little experience of the structured, multi-step question style an IGCSE paper uses, or of showing working in a form that earns method marks rather than simply reaching an answer.
programmes.countryNote: That gap is about presentation and question-reading rather than content, which is good news because it closes in weeks rather than terms. The cheapest time to do it is immediately after the transfer. Left to Year 11, it competes with revision for the one available hour and gets squeezed out by whichever topic feels most urgent.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-mohammed-.subjectsIntro: This list is ordered the way a plan should be: by how quickly a topic converts a weekly hour into marks. The ordering matters more than the content descriptions, because with one hour a week the sequence is the strategy.

subjects.name: Circle theorems
subjects.description: The highest-return topic available. A closed set of rules, recognisable question shapes, and reliable examination presence, usually taught once by the school and never revisited. Three focused sessions typically show up in the next mock more visibly than ten hours of general revision.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled work at Core, with sine and cosine rules, bearings and three-dimensional problems at Extended. Once a student reliably draws and labels a diagram before touching a formula, the questions become procedural. The failure is almost never the trigonometry itself.

subjects.name: Histograms and grouped data
subjects.description: Frequency density with unequal class widths accounts for a disproportionate share of lost statistics marks and is learnable in one or two sessions. Cumulative frequency and interquartile range questions sit next to it and respond equally quickly.

subjects.name: Conditional probability
subjects.description: Tree diagrams where the second branch depends on the first, and without-replacement problems. Compact, formulaic once the structure is understood, and routinely the weakest topic on an otherwise solid script.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, vector geometry proofs and the four transformations. The proof-style vector questions at the end of an Extended paper are where strong candidates separate from middling ones, and they reward practice on past questions more than explanation.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions and graph interpretation. Marks go when a sketch was required first and the student calculated instead, or when transformations are applied in the wrong order, both of which are habits rather than knowledge gaps.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Expanding, factorising, rearranging and algebraic fractions. Essential and poorly suited to a weekly hour, because it needs daily repetition. Better handled as short drills the student runs alone, with the tutor checking the pattern of errors rather than teaching the technique repeatedly.

subjects.name: Number, ratio and percentages
subjects.description: Usually the most secure area on a script, and therefore the lowest priority for paid hours. The exceptions are reverse percentages and bounds, which are narrow, commonly misread and quick to fix in a single session.

subjects.name: Non-calculator technique
subjects.levels: Where the entry includes a non-calculator paper
subjects.description: Exact values, surd handling, fraction arithmetic under time pressure and mental estimation. Confirm with the school whether your child's entry includes a non-calculator paper, since that determines whether this work is essential or irrelevant.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Memory and fraction functions, storing values instead of retyping them, correct angle mode, and showing enough working that method marks survive. Quick to teach, never taught, and worth several marks spread across a whole paper.

sections.heading: Reading the mock script: symptom, cause, remedy
paragraphs: A marked mathematics paper is the most informative document a family holds and the least read. It does not simply show a mark. It shows the pattern of how the mark was lost, and the pattern tells you which of three different problems you are dealing with, each needing a different and differently priced remedy. Fifteen minutes with the script before buying any hours is the highest-return effort available in this whole process.

Look for three signatures. Whole questions blank or abandoned halfway through usually mean content that was never learned, or a timing collapse in the second half of the paper; check whether the blanks cluster at the end. Questions where the answer is broadly right but marks were still withheld mean technique: no working shown, a command word misread, units omitted, an explanation given where a calculation was wanted. Questions attempted correctly but with arithmetic slips throughout mean something else again, usually calculator habits or working too fast.

Those three have almost nothing in common as pieces of work. Content gaps need teaching, which is slow and takes a sequence of sessions. Technique problems need a habit installed, which takes four seconds per question and a few weeks of enforcement. Slips need process: store values rather than retyping, round once, check mode. A tutor who cannot separate the three after one session with the script is not reading it, and a parent who can has already done most of the diagnostic work themselves.

sections.heading: A topic ladder ordered by recoverable marks
paragraphs: With one hour a week, sequence is strategy. The right order is not the syllabus order and it is not easiest-first; it is the order in which a short block of work converts into marks on the next paper. Compact, rule-based topics with reliable examination presence come first, because they can be closed and then left alone. Broad skills that need daily repetition come last, because a weekly hour is the wrong instrument for them.

Circle theorems lead the ladder for Extended and Higher candidates. The rules are finite, the question shapes recur, and schools characteristically teach the topic once and move on, leaving it available as a gain for a year. Trigonometry follows, where the only real intervention is making the diagram-first habit automatic. Histograms with unequal class widths and conditional probability on tree diagrams come next: each is narrow, each is reliably examined, and each is frequently the weakest area on an otherwise competent script.

At the bottom of the ladder sit general algebraic manipulation and number work. Algebra matters enormously and responds badly to a weekly lesson, because what it needs is twenty minutes a day rather than sixty minutes a week; the sensible arrangement is drills the student runs alone with the tutor reviewing the error pattern. Number and ratio are usually the most secure part of a script already, with reverse percentages and bounds as narrow exceptions worth a single session. Spending the scarce hour at the bottom of this ladder is the most common planning error in this market.

sections.heading: Two different disciplines: with a calculator and without
paragraphs: Confirm first with the school whether your child's entry includes a non-calculator paper, because the answer determines whether half of this section applies. Syllabus versions and paper patterns change, schools do not always communicate the change clearly, and a tutor working from the wrong assumption spends weeks on the wrong discipline. Get it in writing alongside the code and the tier, in the same message.

If a non-calculator paper applies, the work is specific: exact-value arithmetic, surd handling, fraction operations under time pressure, and estimation sharp enough to notice when an answer is implausible. None of that is conceptually hard and all of it decays without practice, so it needs short, frequent drilling rather than a single lesson. The common failure is a student who can do every technique slowly and runs out of paper time in the second half.

On a calculator paper the discipline is almost the opposite, and it is where the quickest marks live. Write the equation or expression being evaluated before producing the value, because the examiner awards method marks for what is visible and an answer alone collects the smallest share on a multi-part question. Store intermediate results rather than retyping them, since transcription is where silent errors enter. Round once, at the end, to the form the question specified. Check the angle mode before the first trigonometry question rather than after it goes wrong. None of those four habits is difficult, and none of them is taught at school, which is why they stay available as easy marks for years. The way to measure the gain is to take a marked calculator paper and count the marks withheld on questions where the final answer was correct, because that total is the ceiling on what this work can recover.

sections.heading: Eight weeks before a series, week by week
paragraphs: An intensive block works when it starts from a marked paper and ends at the series. It fails when it starts from the beginning of the syllabus, because eight weeks is not enough to teach two years and the attempt leaves the last fortnight with no past-paper practice at all. The shape below assumes two or three sessions a week and a student who will complete one full paper between sessions, which is the realistic commitment most families can sustain.

The first fortnight is the topic ladder: the three or four highest-priority topics from the mock, closed one at a time, with a short timed section at the end of every session so timing work starts immediately rather than in week seven. The middle fortnight adds full papers, marked properly against the published scheme, with the feedback driving the next session's content. By week five the pattern of remaining losses should look different from the pattern in the original mock, and if it does not, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan needs changing rather than extending.

The last three weeks are timing, question selection and the discipline of finishing. Full papers under exam conditions, marked, with the student practising the decision of whether to start a question in the first few seconds and when to abandon and return. Nothing new is introduced after week six, because a topic met for the first time in the final fortnight is a liability rather than an asset. The block ends at the first paper, with no automatic continuation into whatever comes next.

sections.heading: Who may tutor, and the two questions to ask
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE operates under a permit system that most families never hear about. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here; an amount circulating online could not be verified against any official source. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system. The permit attaches to the person rather than to any platform, so it is a question for the individual teaching your child and not for whoever introduced them.

The second question concerns your child's own school. ADEK's professional-ethics requirements for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported rather than lifted from the policy text, so verify it against the current ADEK document before relying on the exact wording. The principle is sound regardless, and asking both questions takes under a minute. It is also worth stating plainly that IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from ADEK, KHDA, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and any provider claiming such approval is making a claim worth checking.

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and the line nobody mentions
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics carries no coursework, so the academic-honesty question looks simpler here than on the Diploma side. It does not disappear. It moves to materials. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them as downloads is copyright infringement. A tutor should reference them and link the official source; a provider advertising a bundle of mark schemes as a selling point has told you how they treat rules in general.

There is a related point about what mark schemes are for. They exist to show what earns credit, which is genuinely useful teaching material, and they do not exist to be memorised as answers. A student who has worked through a mark scheme with a tutor and understands why a method mark is awarded has learned something durable. A student handed a folder of worked answers has learned to recognise familiar questions, which is a strategy that fails the moment the question changes.

Grade boundaries deserve the same caution. They move between series, they are published by the boards after the event, and no figure should be quoted to a parent as if it were fixed. What is honest and useful is the relative statement: a student two or three marks from a boundary is a different proposition from one twenty marks away, and the first justifies concentrated effort in a way the second does not. That comparison can be made from a marked script without anybody publishing a number that will be wrong next year.
bullets: Official papers and schemes referenced and linked, never supplied as downloads
Mark schemes used to teach what earns credit, not memorised as answers
No grade boundary quoted as a fixed figure; they move between series
Marking done on your child's own attempt, with the lost marks named in writing
A provider selling bundles of official material is a reason to look elsewhere

sections.heading: Telling in four sessions whether it is working
paragraphs: Four sessions is enough to know, and setting that review point in advance is what stops an arrangement drifting for a term. The test is not whether your child enjoyed the sessions or whether the tutor seemed knowledgeable. It is whether the specific topics identified from the mock now produce correct answers on questions the student has not seen before, under no time pressure. That is a concrete, checkable thing, and it is either true or it is not.

Ask for the running list: which topics from the original ranking have been closed, which are in progress, and which have not been started. A tutor working properly keeps that list anyway and sharing it costs nothing. If after four sessions nothing has moved off the outstanding column, the problem is either the diagnosis, the sequence or the match, and all three are fixable. Extending the arrangement unchanged and hoping is the one response that reliably wastes money.

Where the match is wrong, say so early and without apology. The arrangements that fail are the ones where a family keeps a poor fit out of politeness for half a term, cancels twice, and then stops without explaining why. A replacement match with a repeated trial costs nothing here, and the honest version of that conversation in week five is far cheaper for everyone than the silent version in week fifteen. For an MBZ City household, the slot itself deserves the same treatment: if it has been cancelled twice because the bus was late, move it rather than hoping.
bullets: Set the four-session review before the first paid hour, not after

faqs.question: What should go into one weekly hour of IGCSE maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: The highest-priority topic from the marked mock, worked until it produces correct answers on unseen questions, then the next one. Compact rule-based topics first: circle theorems, trigonometry with a drawn diagram, histograms with unequal class widths, conditional probability. End every session with a short timed section so timing work starts in week one rather than week seven. General algebra should not occupy the hour; it needs twenty minutes a day of drills the student runs alone, with the tutor reviewing the error pattern rather than reteaching.

faqs.question: How do I read my child's marked maths paper myself?
faqs.answer: Look for three signatures. Whole questions blank or abandoned means content never learned, unless the blanks cluster at the end, in which case it is timing. Questions where the answer is broadly right but marks were still withheld means technique: no working shown, a command word misread, units omitted. Correct method with wrong arithmetic means calculator habits or working too fast. Those three need teaching, a four-second habit, and a process change respectively, at very different costs, so the distinction is worth fifteen minutes of your time.

faqs.question: Which maths topic should we start with if there is only time for one?
faqs.answer: Circle theorems, for an Extended or Higher candidate. The rule set is finite, the question shapes recur, examination presence is reliable, and schools characteristically teach the topic once and never revisit it, which leaves the marks sitting there for a year. Two or three focused sessions usually show in the next mock more clearly than ten hours of general revision. If circle theorems are already secure, trigonometry is next, where the only real intervention is making the diagram-first habit automatic.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a non-calculator maths paper?
faqs.answer: Ask the school and get it in writing, because the answer changes half the revision plan and paper patterns are revised from time to time without parents being told clearly. If a non-calculator paper applies, the work is exact values, surds, fraction arithmetic under time pressure and estimation, and it needs short frequent drilling because the skill decays. If it does not, that time belongs to calculator discipline instead. A tutor working from the wrong assumption can spend weeks on the wrong half of the subject.

faqs.question: My child's answers are right but the marks are missing. What is happening?
faqs.answer: The method is not visible. On a calculator paper, solving something on screen and writing only the result collects the answer mark and forfeits the method marks, which are usually the larger share on a multi-part question. Writing down the equation or expression being evaluated before producing the value takes a few seconds and recovers them. The second common cause is rounding at an intermediate step, which pushes the final answer outside tolerance. Store values in the calculator and round once, at the end, to the form the question specifies.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks enough to improve an IGCSE maths grade?
faqs.answer: Enough to move marks, provided the block starts from a marked paper rather than the front of the syllabus. Two or three sessions a week, the top three or four topics from the mock closed in the first fortnight, full papers marked against the published scheme in the middle, and the last three weeks on timing, question selection and finishing. Nothing new after week six, because a topic met for the first time in the final fortnight is a liability. Eight weeks spent re-teaching two years achieves very little.

faqs.question: Can we revise from both Cambridge and Edexcel papers?
faqs.answer: Not for full papers. Use only the board your child is entered for, because question wording, paper structure and formula provision all differ, and practice from the wrong board teaches the right mathematics in the wrong format. Individual topic questions from the other board are acceptable as extra drill late in the course, where the topic is identical and the phrasing is not the point. The warning sign of board drift is a mock result that makes no sense given the hours the student has clearly put in.

faqs.question: How much should a Year 11 maths tutor cost around here?
faqs.answer: Market rates rather than ours: Bestimate's 2026 UAE survey puts in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to 350 an hour across Abu Dhabi, with independents reaching AED 500, and a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. Budget platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65, which buys accountability rather than grade movement. The difference between online and in-home is largely the journey, and from these zones the journey is long in both directions. IB Gram quotes after the free trial.

faqs.question: Should marking of past papers be included in the fee?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it is where quoted rates stop being comparable. Marking a full paper properly against the published scheme takes thirty to forty-five minutes, and written feedback naming which mark was lost and why is where most of the visible improvement comes from. Some tutors include it, some charge separately, and some go through answers verbally in the session, which leaves no record by the following week. A slightly higher rate that includes written marking is usually the cheaper arrangement once you count the hours.

faqs.question: What if the bus means we keep cancelling the session?
faqs.answer: Move the slot rather than defending it. Two cancellations is the signal, not the third. Because nobody is travelling to a Mohammed Bin Zayed City address, a weekly time can shift to a later evening or a different day without anybody recalculating a route, and the tutor loses nothing by the change. Families who keep a broken slot out of politeness usually stop altogether within a month, which costs far more than one awkward message asking to move to 20:15 instead of 16:30.

faqs.question: Should a tutor be handing us folders of official exam material?
faqs.answer: They should link the official sources rather than hand over bundles. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement; for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. A provider advertising a folder of mark schemes as a selling point has told you something about how they treat rules generally. What a tutor should do is mark your child's own attempt against the scheme and write down the lost marks.

faqs.question: Why will nobody tell me what mark my child needs for a grade 7?
faqs.answer: Because grade boundaries move between series and are published by the boards after the event, so any figure quoted in advance is a guess that will be wrong next year. What can be said honestly from a marked script is the relative position: a student two or three marks below a boundary is a very different proposition from one twenty marks below, and the first justifies concentrated work in a way the second does not. That comparison is more useful for planning than a number that cannot be relied on.

faqs.question: My child transferred from another curriculum. Is maths the problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not the mathematics itself. Students arriving from Indian or Ministry curriculum schools typically have strong procedural arithmetic and algebra, and little experience of the structured multi-step question style an IGCSE paper uses or of showing working in a form that earns method marks. The gap is presentation and question-reading rather than content, which closes in weeks rather than terms. It is cheapest to address immediately after the transfer, before it gets squeezed out by whichever topic feels most urgent in Year 11.

faqs.question: How many sessions before we can tell whether it is working?
faqs.answer: Four, and the review should be agreed before the first paid hour. The test is whether the specific topics identified from the mock now produce correct answers on questions the student has not seen before, with no time pressure. Ask for the running list of closed and outstanding topics, which a tutor working properly keeps anyway. If nothing has moved off the outstanding column after four sessions, change the diagnosis, the sequence or the tutor instead of extending the arrangement and hoping.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my children if they are in different years?
faqs.answer: Yes, in separate sessions, and it is often convenient to run them back-to-back on one evening. What does not work is teaching two children together unless they share both the board and the tier, because the papers diverge too far for shared practice to help either of them. A Year 10 Core student and a Year 11 Extended student in the same hour means one is being carried and the other is being held back. Separate slots, one point of contact, reviewed per child.

intro.heading: The Mussafah school day, and the hour that is left over
paragraphs: Mussafah is the densest school belt on the Abu Dhabi mainland and one of the most awkward to run an evening around. The residential ME zones and Shabia sit alongside the industrial districts, bus routes are long because they loop through several communities, and a family whose working parent commutes to the island adds another forty minutes at each end. The result is a tightly compressed evening: the child is home somewhere between 14:45 and 16:30 depending on the school and the route, food and prayer have to happen, school homework is set for the same night, and the block left for anything else runs from roughly 17:00 to 20:30.

An IGCSE maths tutor in Mussafah who ignores that arithmetic sets a 16:00 session and then wonders why attendance drifts. The schools here finish earlier than the island independents in many cases, but the bus home is the variable nobody controls. Two students at the same school can arrive fifty minutes apart because one is first off the route and the other is last. The practical fix is not a stricter rule; it is choosing a slot with the bus time already known, and treating the first fifteen minutes of a late arrival as recoverable rather than lost.

This page therefore treats scheduling as a subject in its own right. It sets out which schools Mussafah and Shabia families use, what board each cluster tends to run, what time the day actually ends, and which evening slots hold up across a full term. It then does the maths teaching properly: the Cambridge 0580 paper structure, where the time goes inside each paper, what a week of preparation looks like for a Year 11 candidate, and what the Abu Dhabi market charges so you can judge value rather than guess at it.

Mussafah also has a curriculum pattern worth naming, because it changes what a first session has to do. A large share of families here move between Indian-curriculum schooling and the British route, and a student who has arrived into IGCSE from a CBSE or ICSE background has specific gaps rather than general weakness: notation differences, a heavier emphasis on procedural speed, and much less experience of the structured multi-part question that Cambridge builds every paper around. That transition is mapped in a table further down rather than treated as a vague adjustment period.

One statement before anything else, because competitor pages in this search leave it unsaid. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address. Home visits are a service offered only in India. For Mussafah the delivery is one-to-one live video, which happens to suit the traffic pattern here better than a car does: an in-home tutor crossing Mussafah Industrial at 17:30 is the reason so many in-home arrangements quietly become fortnightly.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-mussafah.programmesIntro: Three programme contexts cover nearly every Mussafah request, and the school day affects each one differently. Here is what each needs locally, including the slot that tends to work.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The two-year course ending in external papers. Cambridge 0580 runs a Core route graded C to G and an Extended route graded A* to E; Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 runs Foundation capped at grade 5 and Higher running 9 to 4. Tier is set by the school, usually during Year 10. Tutoring in Year 10 is about securing the right tier; in Year 11 it is about converting what the student knows into marks under time.
programmes.countryNote: Mussafah and Shabia schools enter candidates with both boards, sometimes within the same corridor, so the first question for a family here is which code appears on the entry statement. Many Mussafah students also sit their papers at a centre inside the same belt, which makes the local exams officer the person to ask about the Cambridge administrative zone for the timetable.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics
programmes.description: The graphics-calculator syllabus, used by schools continuing into the IB Diploma. It adds an investigation component and rewards modelling and written reasoning rather than procedure alone. A student arriving here from a procedure-heavy background usually finds the calculator work straightforward and the written investigation uncomfortable, which is where the tutoring time goes.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer Mussafah schools run 0607 than run 0580, so a family whose child moves to an island or Khalifa City IB school for Diploma years may meet it for the first time in Year 10. If that move is planned, building graphics-calculator fluency a term early removes most of the friction from the transfer.

programmes.name: Indian curriculum into IGCSE mathematics
programmes.description: Not a programme so much as the most common Mussafah starting point. A student from a CBSE or ICSE background typically arrives with strong procedural speed and a notation mismatch, little experience of the structured multi-part question, and no habit of showing method for method marks. Six to eight sessions usually closes the gap, and the gain shows first in mock papers rather than in classwork.
programmes.countryNote: Because Mussafah hosts both Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools within a short radius, mid-year transfers between the two are routine here in a way they are not on the island. A transition plan that names the specific notation and question-format differences is faster than general revision, and the table later on this page sets them out subject by subject.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-mussafah.subjectsIntro: Maths is the request, but Mussafah families often add one science or Economics in the same term. Each entry below names the specific thing it is tutored for.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 (Extended)
subjects.description: Algebraic manipulation, the non-calculator paper, functions and transformations, and the long structured questions where a method mark disappears in line two. Papers are sat to full duration and the mark scheme is read afterwards.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 (Core)
subjects.description: Securing a solid pass rather than reaching for a top grade. Number fluency, ratio, percentages, mensuration and data handling, plus a question order for the paper so the reliable marks are banked before the harder items.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: Graphics-calculator technique used to solve rather than to check, then the investigation component, which rewards a written argument. Bare answers score poorly here even when they are right.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two calculator papers of equal weight on the 9 to 1 scale. Higher-tier work targets surds, algebraic proof, vectors and the multi-step problems at the back of each paper, where candidates stop reading after the first clause.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 4MA1 by stronger candidates. Calculus, series and coordinate geometry make it an AS bridge, and tutoring is mostly technique against unfamiliar question structures rather than content coverage.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The subject most often added by maths students here, because the algebra is identical. Equation rearrangement under time, graph interpretation and the command terms on the practical paper are the focus.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations, titration arithmetic, electrolysis products and organic naming. Students who can do the chemistry and not the arithmetic are common, and that is a maths intervention wearing a chemistry label.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Data and statistics questions, rate graphs, and the six-mark extended responses where structure decides the grade. Revision by reading rather than by writing timed answers is the usual failure.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Popular with Mussafah students planning a commerce route. Calculation questions on costs, revenue and ratios are where maths students gain easy marks, and evaluation is where everyone loses them.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies alongside the main curriculum
subjects.description: Mandatory UAE subjects occupy real timetable space in private schools. Support here is study method and scheduling, so these lessons do not absorb the hours a Year 11 maths candidate needs for timed papers.

sections.heading: What time does the Mussafah school day actually end, and where does a session fit?
paragraphs: The published finish time is not the answer. What matters is when your child is through the door, fed, and able to think. Across the Mussafah and Shabia belt that lands somewhere between 14:45 and 16:30, and the spread is caused almost entirely by the bus. Routes loop through Shabia, the ME zones, Mohammed Bin Zayed City and sometimes Baniyas, so two children from the same classroom can be home three-quarters of an hour apart. A family that books a 16:00 session on the strength of a 14:30 bell will spend the term apologising for late starts.

Then the evening has fixed claims on it that no tutor should be competing with: food, prayer, and the school's own homework. School work set for tomorrow has to win, because a student who skips it to attend tutoring arrives at school behind and the tutoring gets blamed. That leaves a realistic window from roughly 17:00 to 20:30 on a school night, and inside that window the earlier half is better for a younger student while Year 11 candidates generally hold concentration later.

The table below is the practical scheduling guide for this belt. It assumes nothing about your particular bus route, so treat the first row as the question to answer before you book: find out, from the school or from a week of observation, what time your child is actually home. Everything else follows from that one number. Because sessions are delivered over live video, moving a slot is a message rather than a logistics problem, which is the practical reason online scheduling survives a Mussafah term and a travelling arrangement often does not.

sections.heading: Which schools Mussafah families use, and what board each cluster tends to run
paragraphs: The Mussafah and Shabia belt carries a mix of Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools inside a small radius, with Mohammed Bin Zayed City immediately east adding more. That density is the reason mid-year transfers between curricula are ordinary here and comparatively rare on the island, and it is why a Mussafah tutoring request so often begins with a student who changed system in Year 9 or Year 10.

For maths specifically, the board matters more than the school's reputation. Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel entries exist across this belt, and in some cases a school will run one board for mathematics and another for a science. A parent cannot infer the code from the school name, and the report will usually just say IGCSE. Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code and the tier in writing; it is a one-line answer and it determines whether a calculator is permitted in every paper, whether an investigation component exists, and what the grade ceiling is.

Schools are named on this page to describe the catchment, and nothing more. IB Gram has no relationship with any of them. That caution exists because several pages in this search list twenty or more schools under a heading implying partnership, and at least one competitor lists a school that does not appear to exist. If you ever see a tutoring provider claim a school relationship, ask what the relationship is; if it is real, it will have a name and a document behind it.

sections.heading: Inside the Cambridge 0580 papers: where the hour goes and where the marks go
paragraphs: A Mussafah student who revises topics but never times a paper is preparing for a test that does not exist. The 0580 Extended route is assessed by two written papers of equal weight, one of which is sat without a calculator, and the pacing problem is as important as the content. Candidates lose marks at the back of each paper not because the final questions are unreachable but because twenty minutes were spent earlier on arithmetic that should have taken four.

The structural work in a session is therefore a pacing plan: how many minutes a mark is worth, which question types to attempt first, when to leave an item and return. Most students discover that their natural order is wrong. They begin at question one and work forward, which puts the reliable mid-paper marks after the fatigue sets in. Reordering the attempt so secure topics are banked first routinely gains marks without any new content being taught at all, and it is the fastest intervention available in the final eight weeks.

The second structural issue is visible method. Examiners award method marks for method they can see, and a candidate who computes mentally and writes one line earns nothing for a correct approach that failed at the last step. This is cultural as much as technical, and it is particularly common among students who arrived from a procedure-heavy curriculum where speed was rewarded and layout was not. Rebuilding the habit takes a few weeks of insisting on written steps in every session, and it converts near-misses into partial credit across the whole paper.

sections.heading: A Year 11 week in Mussafah that actually survives contact with the school run
paragraphs: Revision plans fail here for a scheduling reason rather than a motivational one. A plan that asks for ninety minutes of maths on five evenings cannot coexist with a late bus, school homework and two mandatory UAE subjects on the timetable. So the week below assumes the opposite: that the available maths time on a school night is thirty to forty-five minutes, that one session with a tutor is sixty minutes, and that the weekend carries the long work.

The design principle is that timed papers happen when there is time to mark them. A full Extended paper plus a mark-scheme review is a two-hour job, which is a weekend job, not a Tuesday job. Weeknights are for short, specific repair: fifteen minutes of non-calculator arithmetic, one past-paper question type, one set of corrections from the last marked attempt. Short and daily beats long and weekly for fluency, and fluency is what the non-calculator paper actually tests.

The second principle is that the school's own calendar wins. During the school's internal assessment weeks, frequency drops and the focus moves entirely to what the school is testing, because a student cannot run two revision programmes at once. After those weeks, frequency rises again. Families who try to hold a fixed plan through everything tend to abandon the whole thing in week six, which costs more than a planned pause ever does. The third principle is that one night a week carries nothing at all. A deliberately empty evening is not slack in the plan; it is the reason the plan is still running in March, and in this belt, where the bus arrival time is outside anyone's control, the empty night also absorbs the weeks when a route runs late twice.

sections.heading: Why in-home slots slip in Mussafah, and what online costs instead
paragraphs: Mussafah has a traffic profile that punishes travelling tutors. The industrial districts generate heavy late-afternoon movement, and a tutor crossing from the island or Khalifa City into Shabia at 17:30 is committing an hour each way on a bad day. That cost does not disappear; it is either billed as a travel premium or absorbed by a shorter session, and over a term it shows up as cancellations. Published market figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500.

An online qualified subject tutor sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour on the same published figures, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The gap between those bands is the travel, not the teaching. Where online genuinely costs you something is supervision and visibility: a younger or distractible student is harder to manage on screen, and a tutor needs to see written working, which means a tablet and stylus or a phone propped over paper. Both are worth testing in the free trial rather than assuming.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all. Home visits are available only in India, and saying that plainly is the point of this paragraph, because two of the competitor pages measured for this project route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without ever stating where the tutor sits. sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context for a Mussafah household
paragraphs: A rate per hour is not a budget. What a family needs is the shape of the spend across a term and a year, and how it sits next to the other education costs already in the household. So here is the market, in AED, with the provider that published each band named, set against the realistic number of sessions rather than a single hour.

At the budget end, university-student and entry-level online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Monthly packages in the market sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Specialist IGCSE and IB tutors are quoted at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

The useful conclusion is about sequencing rather than about which band is correct. A diagnostic block of four to six sessions at the mid band costs less than a term of weekly sessions at the budget band and tells you something the budget band cannot: which of the four error categories is costing marks. Families who buy a long cheap block first and a diagnosis second almost always pay twice. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page; the trial lesson is free with no card required, and a quote follows the diagnosis.

sections.heading: Moving from an Indian-curriculum school into IGCSE maths
paragraphs: This transition is the most common reason a Mussafah family calls, and treating it as general weakness wastes the first month. A student arriving from a CBSE or ICSE background usually brings real strengths: procedural speed, comfort with algebraic manipulation, and a large bank of practised question types. What is missing is specific, and naming it is most of the work.

The first gap is the structured multi-part question. Cambridge and Pearson build papers around items that run (a), (b), (c) with each part depending on the last and marks allocated to steps rather than to answers. A student used to standalone questions and final answers writes too little and loses method marks. The second gap is notation and vocabulary: command terms such as show that, hence, state and justify carry precise expectations, and treating them as decoration costs marks on questions the student can do. The third is the non-calculator paper on Cambridge 0580, which is a surprise to anyone whose previous course permitted a calculator throughout.

The fourth gap is the least visible and the most expensive: the mark scheme as a document. Students who have never read one assume marks are awarded for correctness. They are awarded for specified method, accuracy and sometimes a particular form of answer. Reading two mark schemes properly, with a tutor explaining each award, changes how a student writes for the rest of the course. sections.heading: UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, and why the subject count matters
paragraphs: Mussafah families planning a UAE university route eventually meet equivalency, and the detail is worth getting right because one competitor page ranking for these searches publishes the wrong subject count. For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The point that trips families up is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A student who assumed those two were part of the five can arrive at application with four qualifying subjects rather than five, and that is a scheduling decision made two years earlier. It is worth checking the entry list in Year 10 against the count, which is a five-minute exercise with a two-year payoff.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB Diploma, we do not publish a points threshold, because no figure has been verified on the Ministry's own site, and an unsourced number on an equivalency page is the kind of error a family acts on. Verify every line on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority. Equivalency is a process the authority runs; IB Gram neither performs it nor influences it, and no tutoring is required for it.

sections.heading: Progress reporting, and the honesty boundary on assessed work
paragraphs: A parent paying for weekly sessions is entitled to know whether they are working, measured on something other than the tutor's impression. The measure used here is timed questions: a cold paper at the start, classified errors, and a repeat of the same question types after the repair work. That produces a statement a parent can check, such as which three topics are still losing the most marks, rather than a report that the student is more confident. We publish no satisfaction statistics or score-improvement figures, because we could not show the underlying data, and any provider quoting such a number should be asked for the sample size, the date and the method.

At the six-session mark the tutor reports what has moved and what has not. If the match is wrong, the tutor is changed. That matters more than it sounds: the most common way tutoring fails is a family persisting politely with a tutor who is competent and not right for the student, usually because changing feels awkward. Building the review into the schedule removes the awkwardness.

On assessed work the boundary is fixed. IGCSE mathematics on 0580 and 4MA1 carries no Internal Assessment, but Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 carries an investigation component and any student continuing to the IB Diploma will produce a mathematics exploration worth a fifth of the subject grade. For those, a tutor teaches what the criteria reward, works a comparable example on a different problem and gives feedback on your child's own attempt. A tutor does not supply submittable text or edit a draft until the thinking is no longer the student's. One page in this search sells completed Internal Assessments; the risk of that purchase falls on the student, who faces malpractice proceedings, not on the seller. We also reference and link board papers and mark schemes rather than redistributing them.

process.title: Find out what time your child is actually home
process.description: Before anything else, establish the real arrival time for your bus route across a normal week. In this belt it varies by up to fifty minutes between children at the same school, and it is the number that decides whether a 17:00 or a 18:30 slot will survive the term.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the last mock
process.description: Name the syllabus code if you have it, the tier, the most recent mock grade and the target. If the code is unknown, tell us the school and we will ask the right question in the first session rather than assuming Cambridge when the entry is Pearson Edexcel.

process.title: Free trial lesson, used as a diagnostic
process.description: A working session rather than a sales call. The tutor sets questions pitched at the tier, watches the method rather than the answers, and names which of the four error categories is costing the most marks. No card is required and nothing follows automatically.

process.title: A written plan with the slot fixed
process.description: You receive the topic order with the reason for each position, the number of teaching weeks remaining before the June series, and a fixed weekly slot chosen around the bus time. Fixing the slot is not administrative tidiness; it is what stops weekly tutoring becoming fortnightly.

process.title: Review at six sessions and adjust
process.description: The tutor reports what has moved on timed questions and what has not, and the plan changes accordingly. Frequency drops during the school's own assessment weeks and rises afterwards, and sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan on request.

whyPoints.description: Slots are chosen after the real arrival time is known, which is the difference between a plan that survives a Mussafah term and one that quietly collapses in week six. A slipped slot is the most common reason tutoring stops working in this belt.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code is established before the teaching
whyPoints.description: Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel entries exist across this school belt, and a report that says only IGCSE is not enough to plan from. We ask for the code and the tier in writing, because the calculator rules, the components and the grade ceiling all follow from them.

whyPoints.title: The curriculum transition is mapped, not waited out
whyPoints.description: Students arriving from Indian-curriculum schooling have specific gaps: multi-part questions, command terms, non-calculator fluency, visible method and mark-scheme literacy. Naming them takes six to eight sessions; treating it as general weakness takes a year.

whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The in-home market is real and priced, and this page shows those figures so you can compare.

whyPoints.description: Progress is reported on timed questions every six sessions, with a tutor change if the match is wrong. No satisfaction percentages, no score-improvement claims, no guarantees, because none of those could be evidenced.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE maths session realistically start in Mussafah?
faqs.answer: For most families in Shabia and the ME zones, 17:00 is the earliest slot that holds up across a full term, and 18:30 is often better for a Year 11 candidate. The limiting factor is the bus, not the bell: routes loop through several communities, so two children from the same class can be home three-quarters of an hour apart. Establish your real arrival time over a normal week before booking. If your child is home before 15:15, a 15:30 start works. Sessions run over live video, so moving a slot later is a message rather than a logistics problem.

faqs.question: Do you send a maths tutor to a house in Shabia or the ME zones?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are offered only in India. Lessons for Mussafah families are one-to-one over live video instead. The local in-home market exists and is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor on the same published figures. The extra buys travel through the industrial roads at the worst hour of the day, which is also why in-home arrangements in this belt tend to slip to fortnightly.

faqs.question: My child moved from a CBSE school into IGCSE maths. What is actually missing?
faqs.answer: Usually five specific things rather than general weakness. Experience of multi-part structured questions where marks sit on steps. The precise expectations behind command terms like show that and hence. Non-calculator fluency, because one Cambridge 0580 paper is sat without one. The habit of writing visible method, since method marks are only awarded for method the examiner can see. And mark-scheme literacy, which changes how a student writes for the rest of the course. Six to eight sessions normally closes that list, and the gain shows in mock papers before it shows in classwork.

faqs.question: Which maths board do Mussafah and Shabia schools enter candidates with?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the syllabus code and the tier, in writing. Both boards are used across the Mussafah belt, sometimes within the same corridor and occasionally with different boards for different subjects in one school, so the school's name tells you nothing. Reports usually say only IGCSE. The code matters because 0580 sits one paper without a calculator while 4MA1 permits one in both, and the tier matters because it sets the grade ceiling. Everything in a revision plan depends on those two facts.

faqs.question: Is a weekend double session as good as two weekday sessions?
faqs.answer: It is less ideal and much better than a weekday slot nobody can keep. Spacing matters for retention, so two separated sessions beat two consecutive ones. But in households with shift work or an island commute, weekday evenings often cannot be protected, and a plan built on an impossible slot fails in week six. The weekend pattern puts one content session and one timed-paper session inside the weekend, keeps midweek to one short task, and still delivers the full-paper work that only the weekend has room to mark.

faqs.question: How long should a Year 11 student in Mussafah spend on maths each night?
faqs.answer: Thirty to forty-five minutes on two or three school nights, not ninety minutes on five. The long work belongs to the weekend, because a full timed paper plus a mark-scheme review is a two-hour job. Weeknights are for short specific repair: fifteen minutes of non-calculator arithmetic, one past-paper question type, and corrections from the last marked attempt. Short and daily builds the fluency the non-calculator paper tests. Plans that demand long weeknight sessions collide with school homework and the mandatory UAE subjects, and they are abandoned rather than adjusted.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well in class tests and badly in mock papers?
faqs.answer: Almost always pacing and structure rather than knowledge. Class tests are short and topic-specific; a full IGCSE paper is long, mixed and front-loads easy marks that students overspend time on. The usual pattern is twenty minutes lost early on arithmetic that should take four, leaving the reliable mid-paper marks to fatigue. Reordering the attempt so secure topics are banked first gains marks without any new content. The second cause is invisible method, where a correct approach that fails at the last step earns nothing because nothing was written down.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE maths tutoring cost over a term in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: On published market rates, twelve weekly sessions with a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour works out at roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600 for a term. The budget online band of AED 45 to 150 an hour puts the same twelve sessions at AED 540 to 1,800, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above cost more. Market monthly packages sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are provider figures, not IB Gram prices; our trial is free and a quote follows the diagnosis.

faqs.question: Should we buy a cheap block of sessions first and see how it goes?
faqs.answer: It usually costs more in the end. A long block at the budget band tells you nothing about why marks are being lost, so families buy a diagnosis second and pay twice. The cheaper sequence is a four-to-six session diagnostic block at the mid band, which ends with a written statement of which error category is costing the most marks and whether the tier is right. If that diagnosis is all you want, stop there and take it to the school. There is no obligation to continue, and no card is required for the trial.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor who knows the Mussafah schools specifically?
faqs.answer: They need a tutor who knows the syllabus and the mark scheme. Local school knowledge is useful at the margins, mainly for aligning with the school's scheme of work and its internal assessment dates, and that information comes from your child's own reports rather than from the tutor's postcode. The variable that changes a grade is whether the tutor has taught and marked the specific paper your child sits. Choosing a nearby generalist because the drive is short is the one trade in this market that reliably costs marks.

faqs.question: Which series do Mussafah candidates sit, and when do results arrive?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in June and November, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only and should never appear in an Abu Dhabi revision plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. As a guide to the rhythm, Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always open the live official timetable on the board's own site, because provisional dates are revised.

faqs.question: Does the exam centre my child sits at change the timetable we should use?
faqs.answer: Yes, for Cambridge. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Many Mussafah students sit at a centre inside the same belt, so the question goes to that centre's exams officer rather than to the family. Get the zone in writing, build the revision calendar on that version, and do a dry run of the journey before the first paper.

faqs.question: For a Mussafah student, is Arabic part of the five subjects the Ministry counts for equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at not less than grade E or 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A student who assumed otherwise can reach application with four qualifying subjects, and that is a choice made two years earlier at option time. Check the entry list against the count in Year 10. Verify every line on moe.gov.ae, because requirements change and a tutoring page is not the authority. Equivalency is a process the authority runs, and no tutoring is required for it.

faqs.question: Are your Mussafah tutors permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years; MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask any tutor to show the permit, and treat a quoted permit fee as a warning sign. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and has no UAE premises.

faqs.question: What evidence will I get that the maths sessions are moving marks?
faqs.answer: By timed questions rather than by impressions. A cold paper is sat at the start, every lost mark is classified as method, arithmetic, reading or unknown content, and the same question types are repeated after the repair work. At six sessions you receive a statement of what has moved and which three topics still lose the most marks. If the match is wrong, the tutor changes. We publish no satisfaction percentages or score-improvement figures, because we could not show you the sample size, date and method behind them.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-mussafah.closingHeading: Fix the slot first, then fix the maths
abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-mussafah.closingBody: If your child is at a Mussafah or Shabia school and the maths grade has slipped, two short steps come before any spending. Find out what time the bus actually gets home across a normal week, and ask the exams officer for the syllabus code and the tier in writing. Then book a free trial lesson in the slot that real arrival time allows. The tutor will set questions at that tier, watch the method rather than the answers, and tell you which error category is costing the most marks and how many teaching weeks remain before the June series. Lessons are one-to-one over live video. If the diagnosis is all you need, take it and stop.

intro.heading: Is there anyone on Saadiyat Island who actually knows your child's maths syllabus?
paragraphs: The honest answer is: probably not, if you insist on proximity. Saadiyat Island has a small resident population relative to the Abu Dhabi mainland and a small number of schools. The subset of adults living within a twenty-minute drive who teach Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier week in and week out, and who know which questions the Extended papers actually set, is very small. The subset who teach Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is smaller still.

That is not a problem with the island. It is what happens when you filter a specialist skill by geography. Filter instead by syllabus code and the picture inverts: there are plenty of people who teach 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher as their main work, and video removes the only reason they could not teach your child. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, because the honest alternative is better. Home visits are a service we run only in India.

The reason this matters more in mathematics than almost anywhere else is tiering. Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended, and the two routes sit different papers with different content and different grade ceilings. Pearson 4MA1 tiers into Foundation and Higher. A tutor working from a generic Year 11 plan will teach topics your child will never be examined on and skip topics that carry marks, and the hourly rate will look identical either way. The first question any competent IGCSE maths tutor asks is the code and the tier. If that question does not come up, you are talking to a generalist.

There is a second specificity worth naming. Cambridge and Pearson ask questions in a recognisably different register. Cambridge 0580 Extended papers lean on structured multi-part questions with incremental marks. Pearson 4MA1 Higher papers include longer problem-solving items where the method is not signposted. A student who has spent a year on the wrong board's past papers will be competent and still underperform, and nobody will be able to say why. Matching the paper diet to the entry is the cheapest correction available in Year 11.

What follows is the coverage answer in detail. Which codes we cover and how quickly, what happens when no specialist is free for a given slot, how the two boards' mathematics specifications differ in practice, where Extended and Higher candidates actually lose marks topic by topic, and how a session fits around a Saadiyat Island school run. Where money is mentioned it is a published market figure with its source named, not an IB Gram price.

One more thing is worth saying plainly before the detail begins. A tutor who knows the specification will tell you within one session what the problem is and roughly how many hours it will take to fix, because the losses on a marked paper point at named topics rather than at general weakness. A tutor who does not know it will describe the problem back to you in the words you used, and will keep doing so for as long as you keep paying. On a small island that distinction is easy to miss, because the local option feels like the convenient one and the question of whether they teach 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher never gets asked.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-saadiyat-.programmesIntro: An IGCSE maths tutor in this part of Abu Dhabi is asked for four distinct specifications, and they are not interchangeable. Here is what each one is, with what it means for who can teach it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The most widely entered maths specification in Abu Dhabi's Cambridge schools. Two written papers, no coursework, and a split into Core and Extended routes. Extended covers the full syllabus and is open to the top grades; Core covers less and caps the award. The supplementary syllabus statements are where Extended marks concentrate, and a tutor who has not read them will pitch the work wrongly.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so it does not apply to an Abu Dhabi candidate. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: A separate, single-tier course taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level Mathematics or an IB higher level route. It introduces differentiation and integration, binomial expansion, trigonometric identities, matrices and vectors a year early. Questions are multi-step with little scaffolding, so students who find 0580 Extended comfortable can still stall here. This is the scarcest IGCSE maths specialism in the Abu Dhabi market.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school offers 0606, and a Saadiyat Island student who wants it sometimes has to take it as an additional entry. Where a school does run it, it is the single best preparation available for the jump to AS Level or to Analysis and Approaches at higher level.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A
programmes.description: The other mainstream route in Abu Dhabi, tiered into Foundation and Higher. Two written papers at each tier. Higher papers include longer problem-solving items where the method is not signposted, which is a different exam skill from Cambridge's structured multi-part style even where the underlying content matches almost exactly.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so read the live timetable on Pearson's own site.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics B
programmes.description: A distinct specification rather than a variant, single-tier, with a heavier emphasis on algebraic manipulation and a question style closer to a traditional O Level. Entered by a smaller number of schools, which makes it the specification most often mistaken for Mathematics A by a tutor who was not told the code. The consequence is a term of practice on the wrong papers.
programmes.countryNote: If your child's school enters 4MB1, say so in the first message. It is the one International GCSE maths code where a mismatch is both easy to make and expensive, because the past-paper diet is genuinely different from Mathematics A.

abu-dhabi/igcse-maths-tutor-in-saadiyat-.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the subject here, but the topics are what a tutor is actually hired for. These are the strands Abu Dhabi Extended and Higher candidates most often need, with where the marks go missing in each.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and fractions
subjects.description: The single largest source of lost marks at Extended tier. Simplifying algebraic fractions, changing the subject of a formula with the subject appearing twice, and expanding triple brackets accurately. Errors here are mechanical and respond to short repeated practice rather than explanation.

subjects.name: Quadratics and the formula
subjects.description: Completing the square, the discriminant, and solving by formula with surds left exact. Students lose marks for rounding too early and for giving one root when two exist. Cambridge marks method generously here, which means showing the substitution is worth real marks even when the arithmetic slips.

subjects.name: Graph transformations and functions
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, and the effect of each transformation on a sketch. The common failure is confusing a horizontal translation's sign. A tutor's job is a small, memorised set of rules tested until they are automatic.

subjects.name: Trigonometry beyond right angles
subjects.description: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle, bearings and three-dimensional problems. Marks are lost to unlabelled diagrams and to using the wrong rule when two sides and a non-included angle are given. Drawing the triangle first is the habit worth drilling.

subjects.name: Bounds, rounding and limits of accuracy
subjects.description: Upper and lower bounds in calculations, especially division, where the bound that produces the maximum is not the one students expect. A small topic that appears reliably and is almost always taught too quickly in class.

subjects.name: Compound measures and percentage change
subjects.description: Reverse percentages, compound interest, exponential growth and decay, speed and density. The reverse percentage is the single most common error in the whole specification: students divide by the wrong figure and lose every mark in the question.

subjects.name: Vectors and transformations
subjects.description: Column vectors, magnitude, and proving three points are collinear. Transformation questions reward precise description: the type, the centre or vector, and the scale factor or angle. A partial description scores a partial mark, which students rarely realise.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams, conditional probability without replacement, and Venn diagram notation. The notation is examinable in its own right, and candidates who can do the probability still lose marks for misreading an intersection symbol.

subjects.name: Statistics and cumulative frequency
subjects.description: Histograms with unequal class widths, frequency density, cumulative frequency curves and interquartile range. The frequency density calculation is the discriminating step and is the one most often skipped in revision because it looks like a presentational detail.

subjects.name: Calculus (Additional Mathematics 0606)
subjects.description: Differentiation of polynomials and simple composite functions, stationary points, and integration as the reverse process with definite integrals. A year ahead of where most students meet it, which is why 0606 candidates need a tutor who teaches it rather than one who last saw it at school.

sections.heading: Coverage, honestly: which maths codes we can staff and how fast
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal the fact that delivery is not local at all. We would rather state ours. For mainstream International GCSE mathematics at a common evening slot, a match is usually available within a few days. For narrower specifications, or for an early slot that only suits a student at a school on Saadiyat Island itself, it takes longer, and sometimes we will tell you that we cannot staff it well.

The variables are the code, the tier and the time. Cambridge 0580 at Extended tier in an 18:00 Gulf Standard Time slot is the easiest match in this market. Pearson 4MA1 Higher is nearly as straightforward. Pearson 4MB1 is a smaller pool because fewer schools enter it. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics is the scarcest, because it requires a tutor who teaches calculus to sixteen-year-olds routinely rather than one who remembers it.

What we will not do is fill a slot with a tutor who does not teach that code. A tutor who covers the wrong specification costs you the fee and a term of misdirected effort, and the second cost is much the larger of the two. If the honest answer is that the match will take a week, we say a week. If the honest answer is that we cannot cover a particular combination at the time you need, we say that too, and you are free to look elsewhere with the code written down.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 against Pearson 4MA1: what actually differs
paragraphs: The two specifications overlap heavily in content and differ sharply in examination style, which is why a board mismatch is invisible in a progress report and visible in a results envelope. Both split the cohort by ability: Cambridge into Core and Extended, Pearson into Foundation and Higher. Both sit two written papers with no coursework. Both examine the same core strands of number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics.

The differences start with question architecture. Cambridge 0580 Extended papers tend towards structured multi-part questions where part (a) sets up part (b), and the marks are allocated incrementally, so a student who makes an early error can still earn method marks downstream. Pearson 4MA1 Higher includes longer unsignposted problem-solving items where the student has to choose the method with no prompt. A candidate drilled only on structured questions finds these disorienting even when every individual technique is secure.

The second difference is emphasis at the margins. Pearson's Mathematics A specification treats some algebraic and graphical work in a slightly different order, and its Mathematics B specification, 4MB1, is heavier on algebraic manipulation again. The practical consequence for a tutor is not a different curriculum but a different revision priority, and the only way to get that right is to work from the specification the school has actually entered.

The third is the calculator convention and the formulae provided, which differ in detail between boards and change what has to be committed to memory. This is the sort of thing that never comes up in a tutoring conversation and costs marks in an exam hall. A tutor working to the code knows it. A tutor working to "Year 11 maths" does not.
