sections.heading: The whole spend stack after a weak mock, in AED
paragraphs: Almost nobody in this market shows a parent the full cost of acting on a mock result, which is strange, because it is the only figure that answers the question actually being asked. The stack has four lines. School fees are already committed, and in Dubai they have been held flat for 2026-27 under a decision KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026, part of an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Tuition is the line families focus on. Resit entry fees, set by the centre, are the line that moves the total most when a tier decision goes wrong. Materials are small but not nothing.

Tuition prices out as follows, from published market sources. Budget online tuition runs AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. A qualified subject tutor online sits between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Exam-year and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, per Bestimate's rate table, with TutorChase at AED 270; premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

The entry line is the one to establish early, because it is set by the centre and not published anywhere a search will find. Exam centres in the emirate publish their own fee schedules and revise them between series, so the correct action is to ask your school's exams officer, or an external centre, for the current schedule in writing. A family that budgets for tuition and forgets the entry fee discovers it at the worst possible moment, which is after the tier decision has been made.

Put those lines next to each other and the arithmetic usually points the same way: the cheapest intervention after a mock is the one that prevents a resit. A single diagnostic session that settles the tier question correctly is a smaller number than a term of teaching, and a much smaller number than a term of teaching followed by a November entry.

sections.heading: The mock is the tier decision, and the tier decision carries the grade ceiling
paragraphs: Families tend to read a mock as a rehearsal. Schools read it as evidence for an entry decision, and that difference explains most of the frustration in the fortnight afterwards. In tiered subjects, the centre must submit each candidate at Core or Extended, and once the entry is made the tier is fixed. Core carries a lower grade ceiling; Extended carries a higher one and assumes algebraic and analytical fluency that the Core papers never test. The mock is the last substantial piece of evidence before that submission.

Getting it wrong is expensive in both directions. A candidate entered at Core who was capable of Extended has a capped grade that may close a sixth-form route, and reopening it means a resit entry in a later series. A candidate entered at Extended who was not ready can score below what a Core entry would have produced, because the Extended paper allocates marks to content they never reached. Neither outcome is fixed by more teaching after the entry closes.

The right way to settle it is a full Extended paper, sat under timed conditions and marked strictly, read against the grade boundary the school used for the mock. That gives three usable facts: the raw mark, where the marks were lost, and how far the candidate sits from the boundary that matters. A conversation about confidence gives none of them, and a tutor's opinion offered without a marked paper is worth exactly as much.

One practical note: schools differ considerably in how willing they are to revisit a tier decision after mocks, and some have already submitted by the time mock marks are released. The question to ask the exams officer is simple and should be asked in writing before the mock, not after: when is the internal cut-off, and will a mock result change a tier entry?

sections.heading: What a mock percentage does not tell you about a grade
paragraphs: Mock marks arrive as percentages and get read as grades, and the translation is where most families go wrong. Grade boundaries are set per series by the board, after the papers have been sat, and they move. A school marking a mock has to pick boundaries from somewhere, usually a previous series, and that choice can shift a candidate a whole band either way. A mock percentage is therefore a position relative to one set of historical boundaries, not a prediction.

This matters commercially because the size of a perceived gap drives the size of the spend. A parent told their child is two grades off will buy more than a parent told they are four marks below a boundary, and those can be the same script. Asking the school which boundaries it applied, and what the raw mark was, converts a frightening grade into an arithmetic question. Frequently the answer is that a handful of marks are in play, and a handful of marks is a cheap purchase.

The second translation problem is component weighting. A candidate can score poorly overall while performing adequately on the paper that carries the most marks, or the reverse, and the overall percentage conceals both. Where a school releases a component breakdown, that is the document worth reading. Where it does not, ask for it; most will provide it when the request is specific.

None of this means a mock is unreliable. It means a mock is a measurement with a known error bar, and the correct response is proportionate rather than panicked. Boards publish grade thresholds for past series on their own sites, and reading your child's raw mark against those is a free and more informative exercise than most things a family could buy that week.
bullets: Grade boundaries are set per series after the papers are sat, and they move between series
A mock grade depends on which historical boundaries the school chose to apply
Ask for the raw mark and the component breakdown, not just the converted grade
A gap of a few marks is a cheap fix; a gap of a whole band may not be

sections.heading: The six weeks after a mock, costed week by week
paragraphs: A post-mock plan should be bounded, and the easiest way to bound it is to write it against the centre's internal entry cut-off. Six weeks is the usual gap between a mock result and the point where the tier and subject list are fixed, and six weeks of one subject at one session a week is a number a family can see the whole of before agreeing to it. Open-ended arrangements are where the cost gets away from people.

Week one is diagnostic and nothing else: the marked paper read question by question, the raw mark set against the boundary the school used, and a written answer on the tier question. Weeks two and three take the largest cluster of lost marks, with a short marked set each week to confirm the diagnosis was right. Week four is a timed section under exam conditions, which either shows the repair held or shows it did not.

Weeks five and six do one of two things depending on that result. If the repair held, they attack the second cluster and finish with a full timed paper. If it did not, they change approach rather than repeating it, because repeating an approach that failed is the most expensive thing on this page. Either way the family ends the six weeks with marked evidence rather than an impression, and a defensible answer to the tier question.

The figures below use the mid-market monthly estimate of AED 600 to AED 1,200 for one subject at weekly sessions and the specialist band of AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above, both from Bestimate's Dubai rate table. They are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list. Our route is a free trial lesson, on the condition that it is a single lesson, followed by a consultation where the subject, the tier and the cut-off date are established before any hours are quoted.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE mock marks actually go, paper by paper
paragraphs: In Mathematics the losses are predictable enough to check before you look. Algebraic fractions, upper and lower bounds, three-dimensional trigonometry and the unstructured questions at the end of the Extended paper. Beneath those sits a steady band of presentation marks: no method line on a method-marked question, a value rounded two steps early, a missing unit on a rate or density answer. That band is usually worth more than families expect and costs very little to recover.

In Physics, electricity and electromagnetism take the largest share, and practical-skills questions take the next. An ammeter drawn in the wrong branch, an anomalous point identified without a reason, a relationship described as increasing rather than named as proportional. In Chemistry, moles and stoichiometry dominate, with organic conditions and the qualitative-analysis tables following. In Biology the losses are almost entirely in command-word discipline and in answer length mismatched to mark allocation.

In the written subjects the pattern is structural. English candidates summarise where they were asked to use evidence. Economics and Business candidates define correctly and never apply to the stimulus. Computer Science candidates write good code and lose marks on trace tables and pseudocode conventions. Each of these is a narrow repair with a small price attached, which is precisely why reading the script first saves money.

The purpose of listing these is to make the first paid session efficient. A tutor who knows where to look turns a diagnostic hour into a plan; one who starts from the syllabus turns it into a conversation. That difference compounds over a six-week block.
bullets: Mathematics: algebraic fractions, bounds, 3-D trigonometry, unstructured final questions
Physics: electricity, electromagnetism, circuit diagrams, anomalous-result reasoning
Chemistry: moles under time pressure, exact organic conditions, analysis tables
Written subjects: application to the stimulus, command words, and controlled structure

sections.heading: Mock season and the entry clock: who holds which deadline
paragraphs: A mock mark only matters because of what it sits in front of. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, and the February/March series is offered to India only, so an Abu Dhabi candidate's realistic windows are summer and autumn. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Before each of those, a board deadline closes, and before the board's deadline the centre's internal cut-off closes. The second is the one that affects your family.

Entries are made by the centre, which for nearly every candidate is the school. The exams officer decides the internal cut-off, which subjects and option codes go on the entry, and at which tier. A parent cannot submit an entry directly. That makes the exams officer the most important person in the fortnight after mocks, and a written exchange with them more valuable than a week of revision.

There is one administrative detail specific to Cambridge that is almost never mentioned and occasionally costs a candidate an exam. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the centre which zone it sits in before building a revision calendar.

If the mock makes a June grade unlikely, the November series is a genuine alternative rather than a failure. The papers are set to the same standard, the series is open to UAE candidates, and Pearson's record shows November results reaching students in January, with November 2025 results arriving on 22 January 2026. Weighing a cheaper, better-targeted November block against an expensive spring intensive is a legitimate budgeting decision and one almost nobody presents to parents.

sections.heading: Group class, tuition centre or one-to-one: what each price actually buys
paragraphs: The market after mocks offers four models at four price points, and it is worth being clear about what distinguishes them, without naming or disparaging particular businesses. A tuition centre group class is the cheapest per hour because the cost is shared, and it works where a cohort has the same gap, which after mocks is rarely true: the whole point of a script is that two candidates with the same mark have different problems. Group teaching cannot act on a script.

A freelance independent tutor is next, and the range is wide because the category is wide. The published rates run from AED 33 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, and the rate correlates loosely with whether the tutor marks to the mark scheme. The relevant question is not qualifications in the abstract but whether they will mark a paper and show you the breakdown.

An agency or platform sits above that, charging for matching, replacement and administration as well as teaching. Whether that is worth paying for depends on how much you value being able to change tutor without starting again, and on whether anyone verifies the tutor's marking. The category also includes operations that conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking number, which is worth checking rather than assuming.

The fourth model is a tuition operation with premises, which in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. That is a specific permit issued to institutions with premises, and no tutoring business should describe itself as holding regulator status it does not. Separately, individual private tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Asking a tutor whether they hold it is a reasonable question with a free answer.
bullets: Group class: cheapest per hour; cannot act on one candidate's script
Freelance tutor: widest price range; ask whether they mark to the mark scheme
Agency or platform: pays for matching and replacement; verify where delivery happens
Centre with premises: a different legal animal, requiring its own permit in Dubai

sections.heading: How lessons run, and who regulates the school behind the mock
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing and the marked mock script open during the session. Gulf Standard Time lessons are set around the Abu Dhabi school week: late afternoon where the school run is short, 5pm or later for the Khalifa City and Mohammed Bin Zayed City catchments, and weekend blocks where weekday evenings are already committed. During Ramadan the same sessions move to post-Iftar timing without changing the plan.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. The cost argument for online delivery is on this page in numbers rather than adjectives: in-home rates in the emirate are quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to AED 500 by independent home tutors, and the advertised in-home monthly package sits at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 against AED 799 online. Across six weeks that gap buys several marked papers.

Private schools in Abu Dhabi are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's regulator is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so regulator powers vary by emirate.

One caution that applies directly here. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours needs the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document. The practical point stands: the teacher who marked the mock is not the person to buy lessons from.

process.title: Get the three documents
process.description: The marked mock paper, the raw mark with the component breakdown, and the centre's internal entry cut-off date in writing. Those three determine both the plan and its cost. A family that has all three before the first paid session buys considerably less than one that has none of them.

process.title: Free trial lesson spent on the script
process.description: One free trial lesson with the subject specialist, on the condition that it is a single lesson, used to read the mock paper question by question and set the raw mark against the boundary the school applied. You keep the written marks-lost list and the tier recommendation whether or not you book further.

process.title: Agree a bounded total, not an open arrangement
process.description: Sessions per week, number of weeks to the cut-off, and the total at the market rate stated up front. A post-mock plan has a natural end point, so there is no reason for it to be open-ended. If the honest estimate says the gap is too large for the weeks available, we say that instead of selling the hours.

process.title: Weekly teaching with marked checks
process.description: A fixed weekly slot, each session anchored to a marked piece rather than to a topic list, with a short marked set between sessions and a timed section at the halfway point. After each marked item you get the breakdown and a short written note of what moved.

process.title: A written tier recommendation before the cut-off
process.description: By week four you get a plain statement, in writing, of what the marked evidence supports at Core or Extended, with the raw marks behind it. You can hand that to the exams officer. The entry decision remains the centre's and we do not present it as ours.

process.title: The honest fallback
process.description: If no specialist is free for your subject at the hours you need, we say so and offer a different slot, a later start or a referral elsewhere. The weeks after mock results are the single tightest period of the year for Extended-tier science supply in this emirate.

whyPoints.title: The whole stack, not the hourly rate
whyPoints.description: This page prices school fees already committed, tuition, the resit entry fee set by the centre and the materials, because that is the sum a household actually faces. Three of the six pages ranking in this market publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to UAE parents.

whyPoints.title: The tier decision treated as the point
whyPoints.description: A mock exists to inform an entry decision with a deadline attached, and that decision carries the grade ceiling. We give a written recommendation backed by raw marks before the centre's cut-off, and we are explicit that the entry belongs to the centre rather than to us.

whyPoints.title: A bounded total agreed up front
whyPoints.description: Post-mock plans have a natural end point, so the number of weeks and the total are stated before anything starts. If the marked evidence says the gap is too large for the weeks available, the honest answer is a November entry rather than an expensive spring.

whyPoints.title: Every figure traceable
whyPoints.description: AED bands here come from Bestimate's Dubai rate table and from published competitor rates, each with the publisher named and the month it was read. We publish no IB Gram price list on this page because the figure depends on subject, tier and weeks remaining.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated as a limit
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on the student's own work. We do not produce coursework, and syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson, so we link them rather than hosting them. Some sites in this market sell the opposite outright.

whyPoints.title: Regulator facts, correctly attributed
whyPoints.description: ADEK supervises private school licensing in Abu Dhabi, KHDA in Dubai, SPEA in Sharjah and the Ministry of Education in three further emirates. We name what each does and link the source. ADEK appears on none of the competitor pages researched for this market.

faqs.question: My child's IGCSE mock mark was low. What should I buy first?
faqs.answer: One diagnostic session on the marked paper, and nothing else until it is done. A mock mark is a single number that supports no decision, while the script shows whether the marks went on command words, method presentation, a genuine content gap or questions never attempted. Those four have completely different costs, and the most common expensive mistake is buying a term of teaching for what turns out to be a technique habit. Ask the school for the marked paper, the raw mark and the component breakdown first.

faqs.question: Does the mock decide whether my child sits Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: It is the main evidence for that decision, and the decision is made by the centre in the entry rather than in the exam hall. Core carries a lower grade ceiling; Extended carries the full range and assumes algebraic fluency the Core papers never test. The useful test is a full Extended paper sat under timed conditions and marked strictly against the boundary the school applied. Ask the exams officer, in writing and before the mock, when the internal cut-off falls and whether a mock result can change a tier entry.

faqs.question: How much does post-mock IGCSE tutoring cost per month in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions at AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages in the market sit at AED 799 per month for eight online sessions. Those are market figures rather than an IB Gram price list. The number that actually varies is the subject count, so settle that from the script before comparing quotes.

faqs.question: Why does a mock percentage not translate cleanly into a grade?
faqs.answer: Because grade boundaries are set per series by the board after the papers have been sat, and they move. A school marking a mock has to borrow boundaries from somewhere, usually a previous series, and that choice can shift a candidate a whole band. Ask which boundaries were applied and what the raw mark was. Frequently a frightening grade turns out to be a handful of marks below a threshold, which is a cheap problem rather than an expensive one.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a tuition centre good value after mocks?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest option per hour because the cost is shared, and it works where a group has the same gap. After mocks that is rarely the case: the whole value of a script is that two candidates with identical marks usually have different problems, and group teaching cannot act on an individual script. Where a group class suits a family's budget, pair it with a single diagnostic session so at least the revision is pointed at the right thing.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE resit entry cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The centre sets it, and centres revise their fee schedules between series, so no honest answer can be published on a page like this. Ask your school's exams officer, or the external centre you would use, for the current schedule in writing. The reason to do this early is that the entry fee belongs in the budget alongside tuition: a family that funds a spring of teaching and then meets the entry cost in the autumn has planned only half of the spend.

faqs.question: Should we give up on June and aim at November instead?
faqs.answer: It is a legitimate option rather than a defeat, and often the cheaper one. The November series is a full sitting examined to the same standard and open to UAE candidates, with Pearson's November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. A better-targeted November block usually costs less than a panicked spring intensive and produces a stronger grade. The cost is a January result, which any sixth form or university holding a conditional place needs to be told about early and in writing.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher tutor them privately after mocks?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi that is the wrong door to knock on. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy, but the direction is clear enough that no family should be arranging it.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in the UAE need a permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free. Private tutoring is regulated through the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and official guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to recover a mock grade band?
faqs.answer: It depends which of the four causes the marks fell into, which is why the diagnostic comes first. A command-word or presentation habit is typically two or three sessions plus marked sets to maintain it. A pacing problem can be largely addressed in one session with timed practice done independently. A genuine content gap is measured in weeks per topic and is the only one that justifies a six-week block. Buying the block before the diagnosis is how families overspend.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school's exams officer after mock results?
faqs.answer: Five things, all short. When is the centre's internal entry cut-off. Which subjects and tiers are currently on the entry. Which grade boundaries were used to convert the mock marks. Whether a mock result can still change a tier decision. And which Cambridge administrative zone the centre sits in, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone. Ask by email so you have the answers in writing.

faqs.question: Is an in-home tutor worth the extra after a weak mock?
faqs.answer: The extra is the journey. In-home one-to-one in the emirate is quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to AED 500 by independent home tutors, and the advertised in-home monthly package runs AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 against AED 799 for eight online sessions. Over a six-week post-mock block that gap buys several marked papers. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case; home visits are a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two subjects to keep the cost down?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is a reasonable question to ask rather than a corner to cut. Where two subjects share a skill that is costing the marks, such as presentation discipline in Mathematics and Physics, one tutor can address both efficiently. Where the marks are going to subject-specific content, such as organic conditions in Chemistry, the saving disappears because the teaching has to be done by someone who marks that paper. Decide it from the two scripts rather than from the budget.

faqs.question: How quickly can sessions start after mock results are released?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days, because delivery is online and there is no travel to arrange. The honest exception is the two or three weeks immediately after mock results in the emirate, when demand for Extended-tier Physics, Chemistry and Additional Mathematics peaks and a particular evening slot may not be free. Where that happens we say so and offer a different time, a later start or a referral rather than filling the hour with a tutor who cannot mark the paper.

abu-dhabi/igcse-mock-exam-preparation.closingBody: A mock result is information, and information bought cheaply is worth more than teaching bought early. Get the marked paper, the raw mark and the component breakdown from the school, ask the exams officer for the internal entry cut-off in writing, then spend one session having the script read question by question. That hour tells you whether the gap is a habit, a timing problem or real content, and those three carry very different totals in AED. Book a free trial lesson with the subject specialist, keep the written marks-lost list, and agree a bounded plan only if the evidence says one is needed.

intro.heading: A November sitting is a budget and a calendar, not an open-ended plan
paragraphs: Families searching for IGCSE October November exam preparation in Abu Dhabi are almost never starting from scratch. They have a June grade that fell short, a subject dropped mid-year, a mid-cycle arrival from another school system, or a private candidate who needs one certificate before a university offer firms up. Every one of those situations has the same two hard edges: an entry deadline that sits months before the first paper, and a results date in January that somebody else is waiting on. Work out those two dates first and the rest of the plan writes itself.

That is why this page leads with money rather than motivation. A November push is a defined block of hours with a known finish, which makes it one of the few tutoring decisions in Abu Dhabi you can actually cost in advance. Market rates in the emirate for qualified subject tuition run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online, with IGCSE and specialist exam-year work quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list.

What moves the number in this emirate is specific. Abu Dhabi's IGCSE cohort is spread across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and the newer mainland communities, and the supply of Extended-tier Physics, Chemistry and Additional Mathematics specialists inside the emirate is thinner than the demand for them between September and November. A tutor who can mark a Paper 4 to the mark scheme and tell you which assessment objective the marks came off costs more per hour than one who re-teaches the topic from the textbook, and needs fewer hours to do the job. The per-hour rate is the wrong figure to optimise; the total to the certificate is the right one.

The second thing that moves the number is how late you start. A November plan begun in early September has time to run diagnostically: two marked papers, a topic list ranked by marks lost, then rebuilding. The same plan begun in mid-October becomes triage, which means more hours per week, weekend sessions, and a higher weekly cost for a smaller gain. Nothing about an IGCSE resit Abu Dhabi families book in week six of term is cheap, and the honest version of this page says so rather than implying a late start is equivalent.

Delivery is the last variable. IB Gram runs one-to-one online IGCSE tutor Abu Dhabi sessions over live video. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address — home visits are a service we offer only in India — and the in-home market in the emirate is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour precisely because the travel is priced into the lesson. Buying online removes that premium and removes the twenty-minute radius constraint on who can teach your child, which on a November Chemistry or Additional Mathematics entry is the difference between a specialist and whoever was free.

abu-dhabi/igcse-october-november-exam-pr.programmesIntro: A November entry sits inside a longer path, and the sensible plan treats it that way. These are the stages Abu Dhabi families are usually moving between when they search for a November sitting, and what the November window means at each one.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The two years before IGCSE decide whether a child arrives in Year 10 able to handle Extended-tier algebra and quantitative chemistry. Checkpoint tests are sat in March, May and October and are diagnostic rather than certificating. Most of the damage that shows up as a November resit three years later was done here, in algebraic fluency and in the habit of writing a method rather than an answer.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools following the Cambridge pathway typically run Checkpoint in the primary and lower secondary phases before streaming for IGCSE in Year 9. Families arriving mid-phase from another system often find the streaming decision has already been made on data they never saw, which is worth asking about before Year 10 begins.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is examined in a June series and a November series, with Core and Extended tiers in subjects such as Mathematics 0580 and Physics 0625. The November series is a full sitting in its own right, not a lesser version of June, and the papers are set to the same standard. What differs is the preparation window: a November candidate usually has one term rather than two years.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi centres are allocated to one of Cambridge's six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your centre which zone it sits in before you plan a single revision week.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year, with subject codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics and 4PH1 for Physics. Several Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November subjects are modular in structure, which changes how a resit is planned: a candidate may be re-sitting one paper rather than a whole qualification, and the cost drops accordingly.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so a November plan made in Abu Dhabi should be built against the live official timetable PDF rather than a date quoted on a tutoring site. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, the step after
programmes.description: A November IGCSE grade usually exists to clear a condition: an AS subject choice, a sixth-form place, or a university condition. That means the November work should be taught towards the next course rather than towards the paper alone. A Mathematics resit aimed at AS Mathematics should cover algebraic manipulation to a depth the IGCSE paper never demands, because the next course does.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi sixth forms set their own entry grades and many publish them on their admissions pages. Where a November grade is the condition, the January results date matters more than the grade itself: it determines whether a candidate joins Year 12 in September or mid-year, and whether the school holds the place.

abu-dhabi/igcse-october-november-exam-pr.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often book for a November sitting, with what the paper actually asks and where November candidates in particular lose marks. The pattern is consistent: the content is known, the exam technique is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Extended-tier marks are lost on algebraic fraction manipulation, bounds, similar-shape ratios in three dimensions, and the multi-step problems that carry no scaffolding. November candidates typically know the methods and lose marks on presentation: unlabelled working, no units, and answers rounded before the final step.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism account for a disproportionate share of lost Extended marks, followed by the practical-skills questions on graph drawing and anomalous-result identification. A resit candidate who re-reads notes without drawing circuit diagrams by hand usually sits the same paper twice and gets the same grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the single largest mark sink at Extended tier, with organic reaction conditions and the qualitative-analysis tables close behind. The fix is arithmetic fluency under time pressure, not more theory, and it responds quickly to marked practice in the eight weeks before November.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Biology rewards precision of language more than any other science at this level. Marks go on osmosis and water potential, enzyme-graph interpretation, and the command-word distinction between describe, explain and suggest. Candidates who write long answers to short-mark questions lose time they need for the data questions.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics / Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by candidates heading for A Level Mathematics, and the subject where a November entry is most often a tactical decision rather than a repair. Calculus notation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities carry the marks, and the paper assumes an algebraic speed that IGCSE Mathematics alone does not build.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: The reading and writing components reward structure over vocabulary. November candidates lose marks on the summary task by copying rather than compressing, and on the directed-writing task by ignoring the audience and register specified in the prompt. Both are coachable inside six weeks.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: The directed-response and composition papers are marked on reading comprehension as much as on writing. Marks are lost where candidates summarise the passage instead of using it as evidence, and where the composition runs to length without a controlled structure. Timed practice with a marked rubric moves this faster than redrafting.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: The data-response and extended-answer questions carry the grade, and both are lost on application rather than knowledge. A candidate who defines a term correctly and then fails to apply it to the stimulus material scores the knowledge mark and nothing above it. Past-paper marking exposes this within two sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory marks concentrate in data representation, logic circuits and the fetch-execute cycle; programming marks go on trace tables and pseudocode conventions. November candidates often arrive strong on code and weak on the written conventions the mark scheme expects, which is a fast repair.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies alongside IGCSE
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, and those lessons keep running through a November revision block. A realistic plan treats them as fixed timetable load rather than something a candidate can quietly drop.

abu-dhabi/igcse-october-november-exam-pr.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi's IGCSE families are not evenly distributed, and where a household sits changes what the school week looks like far more than it changes the syllabus. These notes are about session timing and school supply, which is what a November plan actually turns on.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-density towers with a short commute to the island schools, which means a 4pm start is realistic on most weekdays. The constraint here is sibling scheduling in apartments rather than travel, and a fixed weekly slot holds better than a flexible one.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A large villa catchment feeding several British-curriculum schools, with a school run that can add forty minutes each way during term. November sessions here usually land at 5pm or later on weekdays, with the main teaching block on Saturday morning.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Close to the Khalifa City school cluster and the Abu Dhabi-Dubai road, so families here often combine a weekday evening slot with a weekend double session. Extended-tier science demand in this corridor outruns local supply between September and November.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A smaller cohort attending a short list of island schools, with the shortest school runs in the emirate. That makes earlier weekday sessions workable, which matters on a November plan where the useful teaching weeks are few and each one counts.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: A newer catchment with a growing Year 10 and Year 11 population and a commute that is short in the morning and slow at 3pm. Families here tend to book two shorter weekday sessions rather than one long one, which suits paper-by-paper revision.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: A mainland catchment with a wide spread of school choices and longer travel to the island. This is where buying online instead of in-home changes the arithmetic most, because the travel premium in the in-home market is real money for a short November block.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Governed by the same emirate authority as the capital but an hour inland, with a smaller pool of IGCSE specialists physically present. For an Extended-tier November entry in Al Ain, live video is usually the only route to a subject specialist at all.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Saadiyat schools
schoolClusters.note: The island cluster carries a mix of British and international curricula, and its Year 11 cohorts sit both Cambridge and Pearson papers depending on the school's registration. November entries from this cluster are most often single-subject science or mathematics repairs rather than full retakes.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas corridor
schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of IGCSE candidates in the emirate, and the cluster that generates most November demand for Extended-tier Physics and Chemistry. Session timing here is dictated by the school run rather than by the syllabus, and plans that ignore that fail in week three.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: A wide geography with fewer subject specialists physically present, which is why online delivery is the default rather than a compromise. Families here are often the ones who discover a November entry window exists only after June results arrive.

abu-dhabi/igcse-october-november-exam-pr.modesIntro: Three ways to run a November block, each with a different cost profile and a different failure mode. The right one depends on how many weeks are left and how many subjects are in play, not on which sounds most thorough.

modes.title: Single-subject November sprint
modes.description: One subject, two sessions a week, eight to ten weeks, built around marked past papers rather than syllabus coverage. This is the most common November booking in Abu Dhabi and the easiest to cost: the total is the per-hour rate multiplied by a number you can see from the start. It works when the content is broadly known and the marks are being lost on technique.

modes.title: Two-subject parallel plan
modes.description: Two subjects taught by two specialists rather than one generalist covering both. The cost is higher per week and lower per mark gained, because an Extended-tier Chemistry paper needs someone who marks Chemistry. Families often resist this and then split the budget across subjects anyway in week five, having lost a month.
bullets: Separate specialists per subject, with a shared written progress record
Workload balanced so the weaker subject gets the longer sessions

modes.title: Private candidate support block
modes.description: For a candidate not entered through their own school, where the registration logistics matter as much as the teaching. The work covers the syllabus, the paper structure and the components a private candidate IGCSE Abu Dhabi entry can and cannot include. The registration itself is made with the centre, not with us; we help a family ask the right questions of it.

sections.heading: Who actually sits the November series, and why it matters to the budget
paragraphs: A November International GCSE entry serves four quite different candidates, and the cost of preparing each is different. The first is a June resit: one or two subjects where the grade fell below a sixth-form or university condition. The second is a sequenced entry, where a school deliberately splits a candidate's subjects across two series to reduce the June load. The third is a mid-cycle arrival who joined an Abu Dhabi school after the June entry deadline had closed. The fourth is a private candidate sitting outside a school roll entirely.

The resit is the cheapest of the four to prepare, because the content has been taught once and the diagnostic information already exists in the form of a June result and, usually, a component breakdown. Eight to ten hours of marked past-paper work with a specialist frequently does more than thirty hours of re-teaching, and the honest version of a cost estimate says so. The sequenced entry is next cheapest, because the school is managing the syllabus and the tutoring is topping up a known gap.

The mid-cycle arrival and the private candidate are where the number rises. A candidate who moved from another system in September is not resitting; they are meeting a syllabus, a tier and a paper format for the first time in one term. A private candidate carries the same teaching load plus the registration work and, in several subjects, a different option code because the practical or coursework component is not available externally. Both of those are real hours and should be in the estimate from the start rather than discovered in October.

The practical consequence is that nobody should quote you a single figure for IGCSE October November exam preparation in Abu Dhabi without first asking which of these four you are. Any site that gives you a price before it asks that question is pricing the hour rather than the job.

sections.heading: The November series counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: Almost every competitor page in this market names no exam session at all, which is strange, because the calendar is the part a parent can act on. The useful way to read a November entry is backwards from the date somebody else needs the grade. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Those two facts set the shape of every November plan: papers in the second half of autumn term, results in the second half of January.

Working back from the papers, the entry deadline is the next fixed point, and it is set by the board and administered by the centre. A parent does not make an entry; a centre does. That single fact catches out more Abu Dhabi families than any syllabus question, because a household can be entirely ready to pay for an entry and simply miss the window during which their school is willing to make it. Ask your school's exams officer for its internal cut-off date, which always precedes the board's.

Then there is the zone question, which is specific to Cambridge and almost never mentioned. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. A revision plan built on a timetable downloaded from the wrong zone can put a candidate in the wrong room on the wrong day. Confirm the zone with the centre, in writing, before building a week-by-week plan.

The last backward step is the teaching. Count the usable weeks between the start of the plan and the first paper, subtract the half-term break and any school assessment week, and that is the real number. In Abu Dhabi that figure is usually between seven and ten weeks for a plan starting in September, and four to six for one starting in October. The plan should be built on the real number, not the nominal one.

sections.heading: What a November push costs in Abu Dhabi, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market and work up, because that is the order a budget actually gets built in. The cheapest published option is budget online tuition from a university-student tutor, which EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. At that rate a two-session week for ten weeks is a small number, and for a Core-tier candidate who needs company and structure rather than diagnosis, it can be enough. For an Extended-tier paper where the marks are being lost in a mark scheme nobody has read, it usually is not.

The next band up is a qualified subject tutor working online, which market sources put between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. This is where most November resits are bought, and the arithmetic is straightforward: sixteen hours at AED 200 is a knowable total, and it buys marked papers rather than company. Above that sit specialist exam-year rates of AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, per Bestimate's Dubai rate table, with TutorChase quoting AED 270; premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes.

In-home delivery in the emirate carries a travel premium that is visible in the published numbers: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500 an hour, against monthly packages seen at AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The premium is not a quality signal. It is a fuel, parking and Abu Dhabi traffic charge, and on a ten-week November block it is money that could have bought four more marked papers.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page, and the reason is that the figure depends on subject, tier and how many weeks are left. The route is a free trial lesson and a consultation, where the subject, the tier and the real number of usable weeks are established before anybody quotes hours. What we will not do is quote a per-hour number that makes the page look cheap and then discover in week two that the job needs twice the hours.

sections.heading: Why a resit is a different teaching job from a first sitting
paragraphs: The instinct after a disappointing June grade is to start the syllabus again. It is the wrong move, and it is the main reason a second sitting produces the same grade as the first. A candidate who sat the paper in June has already met every topic; what they have not had is a reading of where the marks actually went. Re-teaching content that was understood wastes the one resource a November plan is short of, which is weeks.

The alternative is to treat the first two sessions as forensic. A full past paper, sat under timed conditions, marked strictly against the published mark scheme, and then read question by question with the candidate present. What emerges is almost never a list of topics. It is a list of behaviours: rounding too early, not writing the formula before substituting, answering explain questions with describe answers, abandoning multi-step questions after the first wrong step, running out of time because the first long question took fifteen minutes. Each of those is a repair with a known cost in hours.

That reading is also what turns an IGCSE resit Abu Dhabi families are nervous about into a plan they can see the end of. A candidate who learns that eleven of their lost Physics marks came from graph work and anomalous-result identification has a target. A candidate who is told to revise Physics does not. The second framing is the one most of this market sells, because it is easier to deliver and impossible to measure.

There is a limit worth stating plainly. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and any page that offers one on a November resit is selling a thing nobody owns. What marked past-paper work can do is remove the specific, countable, repeated errors between a candidate and the next grade band, and report honestly when the remaining gap is a content gap that needs more weeks than the calendar has left.

sections.heading: Where November candidates lose marks, paper by paper
paragraphs: Across Extended-tier mathematics and science, lost marks cluster in a small number of predictable places, and a November candidate has the advantage of knowing which ones already applied to them. In Mathematics, the heaviest losses sit in algebraic fractions, upper and lower bounds, three-dimensional trigonometry and the unstructured multi-step problems at the end of the paper. Candidates lose further marks to presentation: no method shown on a method-marked question, premature rounding, and missing units on a rate or density answer.

In Physics, electricity and electromagnetism take the largest share, and the practical-skills questions take the next. Drawing a circuit with the ammeter in the wrong place, failing to identify which plotted point is anomalous and say why, and describing a relationship as going up rather than naming it as directly proportional all cost marks that have nothing to do with understanding. Chemistry concentrates its losses in moles and stoichiometry, organic reaction conditions, and the qualitative-analysis tables that reward memorised precision.

In the written subjects the pattern shifts from arithmetic to command words. Describe, explain, suggest, evaluate and justify each have a mark-scheme meaning, and an answer written to the wrong one scores against the wrong objective. Biology candidates write explanations where a description was asked for and lose nothing in accuracy but everything in credit. Economics and Business candidates define the term and never apply it to the stimulus. English candidates summarise where they were asked to use evidence.

IGCSE past paper marking is the only reliable way to find out which of these applies to one candidate, which is why it is the first thing a November plan should buy. A plan that begins with a syllabus checklist begins by assuming the answer.
bullets: Mathematics: algebraic fractions, bounds, 3-D trigonometry, unstructured multi-step problems
Physics: electricity, electromagnetism, graph work, anomalous-result identification
Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry, organic conditions, qualitative analysis tables
All subjects: command-word mismatch, premature rounding, missing method lines

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the components a November entry has to watch
paragraphs: A November entry is not always a straight copy of the June one, and the component structure is where that shows up. In several science subjects the practical assessment is examined through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory session, and which route applies depends on the option code the centre enters. A candidate who revises for a practical that is not being sat, or who ignores an alternative-to-practical paper that is, has made a planning error that no amount of teaching fixes in November.

In subjects with a coursework component, a private candidate usually cannot submit it externally, and the centre will enter an option code without it. That changes the weighting of the written papers and sometimes the content they cover. The IGCSE Extended tier Abu Dhabi candidates sit under one option code is not identical to the one sat under another, and the first conversation with a centre's exams officer should establish exactly which codes are going on the entry.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November entries add a further wrinkle where the qualification is modular: a candidate may be resitting a single paper and carrying forward the rest. That is a cheaper and faster job than a whole-qualification resit, and it is worth confirming before buying hours on the assumption that everything must be retaken. Cambridge's structure differs, and the carry-forward rules are set by the board rather than by the centre.

None of this is material a tutoring site should reproduce. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, and the correct behaviour is to cite and link them rather than host them. What a tutor can legitimately do is read the live syllabus with you, name the components your centre has entered, and build the teaching around them.

sections.heading: How lessons actually run: online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time
paragraphs: Every lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing and the candidate's own marked scripts on screen. There is no group class and no recorded course. Gulf Standard Time lessons are scheduled around the Abu Dhabi school week, which in practice means weekday slots from late afternoon and a longer weekend block, and during Ramadan the same sessions shift to post-Iftar timing without changing the plan.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and no sentence on this site should suggest otherwise. That is a straightforward statement of what we sell rather than an apology for it, and the comparison in the cost table above is the argument: the in-home market in the emirate is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour because the journey is priced in, and a ten-week November block pays that premium ten times over for nothing that reaches the mark scheme.

The second argument is supply. An Extended-tier Chemistry or Additional Mathematics specialist who can mark to the mark scheme is a scarce resource in Abu Dhabi between September and November, and a family buying in-home tuition is choosing from whoever can reach their address inside a reasonable drive. Buying online removes the radius and leaves only the question of who can teach the subject, which is the question that was supposed to be asked in the first place.

Practically, that means a family in Al Ain and a family on Saadiyat Island are choosing from the same pool. Where no specialist is available for a niche subject at the hours a family needs, we say so and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than filling the slot. That disclosure is in the process section below, because a page that never mentions a coverage limit is concealing one.

sections.heading: ADEK, your school, and who owns the entry
paragraphs: In Abu Dhabi, private schools are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. Dubai's equivalent is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the Ministry of Education supervises private schools directly. Knowing which authority governs your child's school matters because inspection reports, fee approvals and complaint routes all sit with it.

What the regulator does not do is own your child's exam entry. That belongs to the centre registered with the board, which for most candidates is the school itself. The exams officer decides when internal deadlines fall, which option codes are entered, and whether the school is willing to enter a candidate for a series at all. A family planning a November sitting should treat that conversation as the first task in the plan, not an administrative detail at the end of it.

For a candidate without a school route, an external centre takes that role, sets its own fee schedule, and has its own internal cut-offs. Centres publish their own charges, so ask for the current fee schedule in writing rather than relying on a figure quoted elsewhere. Private candidate IGCSE Abu Dhabi entries are routine, but they are administered by the centre and the responsibility for getting the codes right sits with the family.

One caution, because it is enforced here. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and a teacher tutoring outside school hours needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is clear: do not ask your child's own classroom teacher for paid lessons.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE exams in the November series in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November each year. Both are open to UAE candidates. The entry itself is made by a centre registered with the board, which for most children is their own school, so the first step is asking your school's exams officer whether it will enter your child for November and what its internal cut-off date is. External centres take that role for candidates without a school route.

faqs.question: Is the November IGCSE series only for resits?
faqs.answer: No. A November entry is a full sitting examined to the same standard as June, and four quite different candidates use it. Resits are the most common, but schools also sequence subjects deliberately across two series to reduce the June load, mid-cycle arrivals use November when they joined after the June deadline closed, and private candidates sit outside a school roll entirely. The preparation cost differs sharply between those four, which is why no sensible estimate is given before establishing which one applies to your child.

faqs.question: When do November IGCSE results reach students in the UAE?
faqs.answer: In the second half of January. Pearson's published record is the clearest guide: November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026. The practical consequence is that a November entry does not produce a grade before the winter break, so if a sixth form or university is waiting on the result, plan for a January confirmation rather than a December one. Always read the board's live timetable and results pages, because published dates are revised between series and a date quoted on a tutoring site is not authoritative.

faqs.question: How much should we budget in AED for a November IGCSE push?
faqs.answer: Work from the total rather than the hourly rate. Market rates in the emirate run from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour for budget online tuition, per Tutopiya and EdFlik, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for exam-year specialists, with TutorChase at AED 270. A single-subject resit typically needs eight to sixteen hours; a mid-cycle arrival meeting the syllabus for the first time needs far more. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Does our Abu Dhabi school enter my child for November, or do we?
faqs.answer: The centre does, and for most candidates the centre is the school. Parents cannot submit an entry directly to Cambridge or Pearson. Your school's exams officer sets an internal deadline that lands before the board's, decides which option codes go on the entry, and may have a policy on whether it enters candidates for November at all. If the school will not, an external centre can, with its own fee schedule and its own cut-offs. Get all of this in writing before buying tuition hours against an entry that does not yet exist.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge zone timetable and why does it matter for us?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the exam timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For an Abu Dhabi family this is a five-minute question with a serious downside if skipped: ask the centre which zone it sits in, then build the revision plan from that timetable. Do not plan from a timetable found through a general search.

faqs.question: Can we change from Core to Extended before the November entry closes?
faqs.answer: Tier is part of the entry, so it is decided before the centre's deadline rather than in the exam hall. Moving a candidate from Core to Extended raises the grade ceiling and raises the content load, particularly in Mathematics and the sciences, where Extended papers assume algebraic fluency Core does not test. The decision should be made on a marked Extended paper rather than on ambition. If a marked paper says the candidate is three topics short with eight weeks left, that is a real answer, and the centre needs it before its cut-off.

faqs.question: Does a November grade replace the June grade on the certificate?
faqs.answer: Each series produces its own result, and how multiple attempts appear and which grade a university or sixth form uses is set by the board's rules and the receiving institution's policy rather than by a tutor. Most institutions look at the highest grade achieved, but that is a policy question to put to them in writing. Ask your centre's exams officer how the board records a second attempt for your specific qualification, and ask the sixth form or university directly which attempt it will use for a conditional offer.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a two-subject November plan usually take?
faqs.answer: Two to four teaching hours a week per subject, plus unsupervised past-paper time, is the usual shape for a ten-week block. That is deliberately modest, because the limiting factor in November is not teaching hours but the candidate's capacity to absorb marked feedback while school continues. Abu Dhabi candidates are also still carrying Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies lessons alongside their international curriculum, which is fixed timetable load. A plan that ignores that collapses in week three, usually by cancelling the weekend session first.

faqs.question: Will a November resit delay a university application?
faqs.answer: It can shift the timing, because a November entry produces a grade in January rather than in August. For applications where the IGCSE grade is a stated condition, that means the condition clears in the new year, and the receiving institution needs to know the result is pending rather than missing. Tell them early and in writing. Nothing about tutoring changes that timeline, and no page should imply that tuition is required for an admission decision; it is a teaching service, not a route through an institution's process.

faqs.question: Can my child prepare for November while starting Year 12?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes, and it is one of the more common bookings in the emirate. A candidate who has moved into Year 12 is carrying new AS or IB content while repairing one IGCSE subject, which argues for a small number of focused hours rather than a broad revision programme. The useful plan marks one past paper early, targets the two or three behaviours costing the most marks, and protects the new course. Trying to re-teach a whole IGCSE syllabus alongside a Year 12 timetable is where this goes wrong.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel for a November sitting?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction matters more than most families expect. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE use different subject codes, different paper structures and, in several subjects, different approaches to practical assessment, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE November entries can be modular where Cambridge's are not. A tutor who does not know which board your child sits is guessing at the paper. Confirm the board and the option code with the centre, and the teaching is built from that syllabus rather than a generic one.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for our subject in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Specialist supply for Extended-tier Physics, Chemistry and Additional Mathematics is thinnest between September and November, which is exactly when November candidates want it. Where we cannot staff a subject at the hours you need, the options are a different slot, a later start, or a referral elsewhere, and we would rather say that than put a tutor in front of a candidate who cannot mark the paper. No competing page in this market states a coverage limit, which is not the same as not having one.

faqs.question: How do lessons fit around ADEK school hours and Abu Dhabi traffic?
faqs.answer: Because lessons run over live video, travel disappears from the schedule and only the school week constrains it. In practice that means weekday slots from late afternoon for island and Saadiyat families, 5pm or later where the Khalifa City or Mohammed Bin Zayed City school run is long, and a weekend teaching block where weekday evenings are already full. During Ramadan the same sessions move to post-Iftar timing. The plan is written around the real week, including half-term and school assessment weeks, before any hours are agreed.

intro.heading: Why nobody will give you a straight price, and what to ask instead
paragraphs: Three of the six UAE tutoring pages reviewed for this project publish no price at all. One of them has a frequently asked question that asks what tuition costs and then declines to answer it. The two that do quote figures quote them in US dollars, which is not a currency any Abu Dhabi family transacts in. That is the market you are shopping in, and it is why a parent ends up calling four providers and getting four incompatible answers.

The reason the price is withheld is usually mundane rather than sinister. An hourly rate for a Year 11 Cambridge Physics 0625 student starting in January, needing paper-technique work on the alternative-to-practical, is a genuinely different number from a Year 10 Business Studies 0450 student starting a two-year run in September. Quoting one figure for both would be wrong for both. The failure is not in having a range; it is in refusing to explain which end of the range a particular family is at and why.

So this page does the opposite. It publishes the bands that providers in this market have themselves published, names which provider publishes which band, and then sets out the seven variables that decide where inside the band a quote lands. Subject scarcity, level, session length, exam proximity, number of subjects, tutor credential and format. Six of those seven are things a parent can influence. One of them, scarcity, is the reason online delivery changes the arithmetic in Abu Dhabi specifically.

Abu Dhabi matters to this calculation in a way most tutoring pages ignore. The emirate is spread out: the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, Saadiyat and Yas, and the newer mainland communities out towards Al Shamkha and Al Falah. An in-home tutor crossing that at 4pm is paid for the drive whether anyone says so or not, usually through a travel-inclusive rate and a minimum booking length. Published in-home bands sit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and most of that gap is movement, not teaching.

A final framing note. Every AED figure on this page is a market figure attributed to the provider that published it, with the tier it describes. None of them is an IB Gram price list. IB Gram quotes against the actual subject, board, level and frequency after a free trial lesson, because the honest answer to what IGCSE tuition costs is that it depends on six things, and a published rate card would be wrong for most of the families reading it. Treat any figure here as a reference point for comparing the quotes you collect yourself, and check the provider's own page for the current number before you rely on it, since rate pages in this market are revised without notice and at least one competitor contradicts its own published prices on a second page of the same site.
