Many syllabuses are tiered, with Core and Extended papers, and a Core entry caps the available grade. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with centres allocated to one of six administrative timetable zones.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge provision is widespread across Abu Dhabi's British curriculum schools, which is why Cambridge-specialist tutors are the least scarce and therefore the least expensive to book at the qualified-tutor tier. Tiering is the cost question most parents miss: a student entered for Core papers has a ceiling, and finding that out in Year 11 is more expensive than checking the entry in Year 10.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes run 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4MB1 Mathematics B, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A, 4EC1 Economics, 4HI1 History. Exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel specialists in a given subject are a smaller pool in Abu Dhabi than Cambridge specialists, which pushes quotes towards the upper half of the qualified-tutor band for subjects where paper structure genuinely differs. This is the clearest case for online delivery on cost grounds: the board specialist you need may not live in the emirate at all, and a travel-inclusive in-home rate cannot solve that.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subject groups, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS, with an internally assessed component in each subject. Priced above IGCSE across the market: Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, a gap that reflects the narrower pool of tutors who know a specific subject's internal assessment criteria.
programmes.countryNote: For an Abu Dhabi family, the relevant cost planning point is the two-year shape. A Diploma run is 18 to 24 months of intermittent support rather than a six-week sprint, so the sensible comparison is total spend across DP1 and DP2 rather than an hourly rate. Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The post-IGCSE route in most British curriculum schools in the emirate, and the qualification UAE Ministry of Education equivalency asks for on the British track alongside the IGCSE count. Priced with the specialist band because subject depth narrows the tutor pool sharply, particularly in Further Mathematics, Physics and Economics.
programmes.countryNote: The equivalency rule is the reason to price A-Level support into a plan early. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the five, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. Verify the current wording on the Ministry's own channel before planning around it.

abu-dhabi/igcse-online-tuition.subjectsIntro: Rates vary by subject more than most providers admit, and the variation is about tutor scarcity rather than difficulty. These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families price most often, with what drives the number in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580, 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The least scarce subject and therefore the cheapest to book well. The cost question is tiering: Core papers cap the grade, so a student aiming above a 5 needs the Extended entry confirmed before any money is spent on tuition. Two sessions a week in the January to April run is the common shape.

subjects.name: Physics (0625, 4PH1)
subjects.description: Priced above maths because the pool of tutors comfortable with both the written papers and the practical or alternative-to-practical component is smaller. Electricity and the maths of graphs are where the marks go. Online delivery is where the board specialist is usually found rather than the nearest available physics graduate.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 4CH1)
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and moles calculations carry most of the lost marks, and both are teachable in a short block, which makes chemistry one of the better value subjects to buy tuition in late. A six to eight week block before the series is often enough, rather than a year of weekly sessions.

subjects.name: Biology (0610, 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy rather than technique-heavy, so parents frequently overbuy. The marks are usually lost on command words and on describing a graph instead of explaining it. That diagnosis changes the spend: fewer sessions aimed at answer construction rather than weekly content coverage.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed, which makes tutor matching harder and the rate higher per hour but usually cheaper in total than three separate subject tutors. Worth asking any provider whether one tutor can genuinely cover all three strands at the level needed, because many cannot.

subjects.name: English Language (0500, 0510, 4EA1)
subjects.description: Two very different products at the same price point. First Language work is directed writing and analysis technique; Second Language is accuracy, range and the listening and speaking components. Booking the wrong one is the most common wasted spend in this subject.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475, 4ET1)
subjects.description: Set-text dependent, which is the cost trap: a tutor who has not taught your child's specific texts spends paid hours reading them. Always confirm the text list before the first session. Essay structure and quotation use are where the marks move, and both transfer across texts.

subjects.name: Economics and Business (0455, 0450, 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, evaluation marks and data response. Evaluation is the single most profitable thing to buy tuition for in these subjects, because it is a transferable technique rather than content, so a short block has outsized effect on the grade.

subjects.name: Additional and International Mathematics (0606, 0607)
subjects.description: A genuinely scarce tutor pool in Abu Dhabi, so expect quotes in the specialist band. 0607 International Mathematics carries a different structure from 0580 and a graphic display calculator expectation, which is the detail to confirm a tutor actually knows before booking.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (0478, 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the practical component. Scarce enough that rates sit above the science subjects, and the one area where a tutor who codes professionally but has not taught the syllabus is a false economy, because the mark scheme is specific about notation.

subjects.name: Arabic (0508, 0544)
subjects.description: Taught alongside the licensed curriculum in every UAE private school. Rates sit in the qualified-tutor band and availability in Abu Dhabi is reasonable. Note that Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the five subjects counted for British-track Ministry equivalency.

subjects.name: History and Geography (0470, 0460)
subjects.description: Source skills and structured extended writing. Like Literature, these are option-dependent: confirm which papers and options your child's school has entered before paying for a tutor, since preparation for the wrong option is money spent on content that will not be examined.

abu-dhabi/igcse-online-tuition.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Abu Dhabi changes what in-home tuition costs them and barely changes what online tuition costs. These are the communities where that difference is largest.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Large villa communities a long drive from the island. A travel-inclusive in-home rate quoted here sits near the top of the published band, and the minimum booking is usually longer to make the journey worthwhile.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Further out again, near the airport road. Families here report the widest gap between online and in-home quotes in the emirate, and the longest wait for a subject specialist to be available at all.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short distances to several schools and a concentrated tutor market, so in-home quotes are closer to the online band here than anywhere else. The scarcity premium still applies to Edexcel and Additional Maths specialists.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise apartments where the practical constraint is a quiet room rather than travel. Online tuition costs the same as it does on the mainland; headphones and a fixed study corner are the real setup cost.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: A dense Year 10 and 11 population in one corridor. The common cost-saving move here is two siblings on consecutive slots with the same tutor, which halves the scheduling overhead without sharing a lesson.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A newer family population with many mid-year arrivals, which means a lot of transfers into Year 10 part-way through a two-year course. Catch-up blocks are priced by weeks remaining, not by the hour alone.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Bateen
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods with long-standing schools nearby and the emirate's deepest local tutor market. Even so, a specific board specialist for a scarce subject is usually found online rather than locally.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Mainland communities where in-home availability for a named syllabus is thin. Online delivery removes the scarcity premium that distance creates, which is the whole of the cost argument in these two areas.

schoolClusters.city: The island: Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and Al Rawdah
schoolClusters.note: Long-established schools running Cambridge and Edexcel programmes, with the densest concentration of Year 10 and 11 students in the emirate. Families here are usually comparing three or four providers at once, which is the right way to find out where in the band a quote actually sits.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi
American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas Island
schoolClusters.note: The mainland corridor holds much of the emirate's secondary population across a wide spread of curricula. Travel-inclusive in-home quotes rise sharply across this corridor, and it is where online delivery changes the arithmetic most clearly for a scarce subject.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Reem and the newer communities
schoolClusters.note: Newer schools serving fast-growing residential areas, with intakes that change composition year on year. Mid-year transfers into Year 10 are common, and those are the families for whom a weeks-remaining calculation matters more than an hourly rate.

abu-dhabi/igcse-online-tuition.modesIntro: The shape of the booking changes the total far more than the hourly rate does. These are the three shapes that make sense for IGCSE, and what each one actually costs over a term.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across the course
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, one slot a week from September through to the series. The highest total spend and the lowest cost per mark when a student is genuinely behind on content rather than on technique. Thirty weeks at one hour is the planning unit, and the market's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run from roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end to AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.
bullets: Same tutor and slot each week in Gulf Standard Time
Plan in terms rather than months so holidays are counted honestly
Ask what happens to a session you cancel with 24 hours' notice
Best value where content, not technique, is the gap

modes.title: Pre-series block of six to ten weeks
modes.description: A concentrated run aimed at paper technique and the two or three topics the mocks exposed. Total spend is a fraction of a full-year plan and the effect on a grade is often larger, because most lost IGCSE marks are technique rather than ignorance. The booking is made against a named list of topics and papers, not an open-ended weekly slot.
bullets: Six to ten sessions, scoped from the mock paper, not from the syllabus
Every session ends on a timed question under exam conditions
Priced by the block so the total is known before you start
Right choice when the student knows the content but loses marks

modes.title: Fortnightly review alongside school
modes.description: A lighter arrangement for a student who is coping but drifting. One session every two weeks spent marking the student's own work against the published mark scheme and fixing the recurring error. Lowest total cost of the three and the easiest to scale up if the mock results say so.
bullets: One hour a fortnight, roughly 15 sessions across a school year
Session is driven by the student's own marked work
Scales to weekly in January without changing tutor
Cheapest way to keep a second or third subject monitored

sections.heading: What IGCSE online tuition costs in Abu Dhabi, in AED
paragraphs: Published market rates for IGCSE tuition in the UAE run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the student-tutor end to AED 650 for a premium named provider, with a qualified subject tutor working online sitting around AED 150 to 300. Those figures are the providers' own published numbers, listed below with the provider that publishes each band. They are market rates, not IB Gram prices.

Read the table by what the rate includes rather than by the number alone. A budget online rate typically buys supervised homework and little diagnostic work. A qualified-tutor rate buys a tutor who knows the syllabus code and the mark scheme, and who will send you the student's marked work. An in-home rate includes the drive, which in a city as spread out as Abu Dhabi is a material share of the hour, and usually comes with a minimum booking length to make the journey viable.

The premium bands exist for scarcity, not for quality in any measurable sense. A provider quoting AED 650 an hour is pricing a named individual whose availability is limited. For a tiered Cambridge Mathematics 0580 candidate who needs twenty hours of Extended paper technique, that premium buys nothing the qualified-tutor band does not. For a scarce syllabus such as 0607 International Mathematics or 0478 Computer Science, the scarcity is real and the quote will reflect it regardless of which provider you ask.

One important caution. Do not read any of these bands as a quote for your child. The variables in the next section move a number inside the band by a factor of two, and the only honest way to get a figure is to describe the subject, board, level, start date and frequency and have someone price that. IB Gram's own approach is a free trial lesson and then a quote against the real brief, with no card details taken to book the trial.

sections.heading: The seven things that move your number inside the band
paragraphs: A quote is the product of seven variables, and six of them are things a family can change. Knowing which is which is the difference between negotiating and guessing. The table sets out each factor, which direction it pushes the rate, and roughly how much, based on the spread between the published bands above.

Scarcity is the one you cannot argue with and the one online delivery actually solves. There are fewer Pearson Edexcel 4PH1 specialists than Cambridge 0625 specialists, and fewer 0607 International Mathematics tutors than 0580 tutors, in Abu Dhabi and everywhere else. An in-home provider facing that scarcity either charges the premium or sends a generalist. An online provider can widen the pool instead, which is the one structural cost advantage of the format rather than a marketing claim about it.

Exam proximity is the factor families control least well. A Year 11 student starting in February needs the same twenty hours as one starting in October, compressed into ten weeks instead of thirty, and compressed hours are harder to schedule and therefore priced higher. The saving available here is entirely about starting earlier, which is advice nobody wants in October and everybody wants in March.

Session length and frequency interact in a way that is worth planning around. A 90-minute session is usually priced below one and a half times the hourly rate, so the cost per contact hour falls, but IGCSE attention is poor past about 75 minutes. Two 60-minute sessions a week will outperform one 120-minute session at the same total price for almost every student. Buying the cheaper cost per hour is not the same as buying the cheaper cost per mark.

sections.heading: Hourly, package or term: the same tuition at three different totals
paragraphs: Providers in this market sell the same hours under three structures, and the headline rate tells you almost nothing about which is cheapest for you. Pay-as-you-go has the highest sticker rate and the lowest risk. Monthly packages drop the effective rate and move the risk onto you, because an unused session in a month that contained a school trip and a bout of flu is money spent on nothing. Term blocks sit in between and are the easiest to plan against a school calendar.

Market examples make the arithmetic concrete. A monthly package of eight online sessions at AED 799 works out near AED 100 a session, which looks excellent against a qualified-tutor hourly band of AED 150 to 300. It is excellent, if eight sessions happen. At five sessions it is AED 160 each and the advantage has gone. The question to ask before buying any package is what happens to an unused session, and the answers range from full rollover to outright expiry.

The in-home package figures in the market, AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions, are worth decoding for a different reason. That is eight contact hours a month, so roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour, in the middle of the published in-home band. The structure is not a discount so much as a way of selling the two-hour minimum that travel requires. For an IGCSE student, two-hour blocks are the wrong shape: the last forty minutes of a two-hour after-school session rarely earns its place.

The comparison that actually decides this is cost per contact hour over a realistic number of weeks, including the weeks nothing will happen. Count the Abu Dhabi school calendar honestly: the winter and spring breaks, the exam weeks, the family travel, and the mock period when a student has no capacity for anything else. A thirty-week plan is usually a twenty-four-week plan, and pricing it as thirty is how a package stops being a saving.

sections.heading: What you stop paying for when the lesson is online
paragraphs: The gap between the published in-home band of AED 180 to 500 and the online qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300 is not a quality gap. It is mostly transport, and in Abu Dhabi transport is expensive in time rather than money. A tutor travelling from the island to Khalifa City in the late afternoon spends a substantial part of the hour in the car, and that time appears in the rate whether the invoice itemises it or not.

Four specific costs disappear with online delivery. The drive itself, which is why in-home quotes rise with distance from the island. The minimum booking length that exists to make the drive worthwhile, usually ninety minutes or two hours. The scheduling rigidity, because an in-home tutor can only serve families whose slots fit a geographic route. And the scarcity premium, because the pool of available tutors shrinks to whoever is willing to drive to Al Reef at 5pm.

What does not disappear is the need for a working setup, and this is the honest cost of the online format. A student needs a quiet place, headphones, a device with a camera, and a way of showing written working, which in practice means a tablet with a stylus or a phone camera pointed at a page. Families in Al Reem Island apartments usually find the quiet place is the hard part. Budget for solving that properly once rather than losing fifteen minutes of every session to it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring at a family's address is a service offered only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an Abu Dhabi address. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation, and the reason is in the table above: for the same money, a family in Al Shamkha can work with the specialist their child's syllabus needs rather than the generalist who is willing to make the drive.
bullets: The travel element is the largest single difference between the two bands
In-home minimum bookings exist for the tutor's journey, not the student's attention span
Online removes the local-availability premium on scarce syllabuses

sections.heading: How many subjects to buy tuition in, and in which order
paragraphs: Most families overspend by buying breadth. A student taking nine IGCSEs and struggling in five does not need five tutors; they need the two subjects closest to a grade boundary fixed first, because a grade moved is worth more than five subjects marginally improved. The order is a cost decision, and it is the single largest saving available on this page.

The method is simple and takes an evening. Take the mock results and write down, for each subject, how many marks sit between the student's score and the next grade boundary. Boundaries move between series, so use the school's own reported boundary or the published one from a recent series as an estimate rather than a fact. Then rank the subjects by marks-to-boundary, cheapest first. A subject four marks short is a different investment from one twenty-five marks short.

Then overlay technique against content. A subject where the student knows the material and loses marks on command words, diagram labelling or showing working is cheap to fix: six to eight sessions of paper technique. A subject where two whole topics are missing is expensive: that is a term of weekly work. Spending the first block on the cheap fixes buys two grade movements for the price of one expensive one, and it does so before the series rather than after it.

The subjects to protect rather than improve are the ones Ministry of Education equivalency depends on. The published British-track rule asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five. A student comfortably above that in six subjects has a different risk profile from one sitting on the line in two. Check the current wording on the Ministry's own channel; equivalency is a process the authorities run, not something a tutoring service performs or can influence.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: what the board does to the cost
paragraphs: Parents rarely choose the board; the school does. It still affects the quote, because the two boards structure papers differently and the pool of tutors fluent in each is different. Cambridge is the more widespread provision in Abu Dhabi's British curriculum schools, so Cambridge specialists are easier to find at the qualified-tutor band. Edexcel specialists in a given subject are a thinner pool locally, which pushes quotes upward unless the search widens beyond the emirate.

Two structural differences matter for what a tutor actually has to know. Cambridge runs tiered syllabuses in several subjects, where Core and Extended papers lead to different grade ceilings; a tutor who does not check which entry a student holds can prepare them for papers they will not sit. And Cambridge centres are each allocated to one of six administrative timetable zones, with the board stating plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

On the Pearson side, exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any date you plan around should be read from the live official timetable rather than from a tutoring page, including this one.

The practical cost advice is short. Confirm the board, the syllabus code and the tier before you pay for anything, in writing from the school if possible. Then ask any prospective tutor which code they teach and what the paper structure is for that code. A tutor who answers the second question precisely is worth the qualified-tutor band; one who answers it generally is being priced as a specialist for generalist work.

sections.heading: The entry deadline sits months before the exam, and missing it costs more than tuition
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake in this whole process is not overpaying for tuition. It is an administrative one: a missed entry deadline, a wrong tier, or a private-candidate registration that was never completed. Pearson publishes the shape of this clearly for its November 2026 series: the final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, entries close months earlier in the year, and results do not reach students until the following January, with November 2025 results landing on 22 January 2026. The Cambridge June series carries the same gap, with entries closing in the spring term and the date that binds your candidate printed on the statement of entry the centre issues.

Read that sequence again as a cost calculation. Entries close roughly ten weeks before the first paper. A family that decides in January to move a child from Core to Extended papers may be too late, and the ceiling on the grade is then fixed regardless of how much tuition is bought between January and the exam. Checking the entry in October is free. Discovering the tier in February costs a grade.

The same logic applies to private candidates, which is the route for a student not entered through their school, for a retake, or for an extra subject the school does not offer. A private candidate pays an entry fee to an examination centre, and that fee has nothing to do with tuition. It is a separate cost, paid to a different party, on the centre's own deadline, and centres set their own administrative charges on top of the board's fee. Ask the centre for the total in writing.

IB exam dates are the one area where no figure should be taken from a page like this. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Abu Dhabi schools sit the May session; for any specific date, ask your child's IB coordinator or read it on ibo.org. Cambridge and Pearson dates above are sourced from the boards' own pages, and should still be checked against the live timetable before anyone plans around them.

sections.heading: Tuition cost in context, and where Abu Dhabi families waste money
paragraphs: Tuition is the second education cost in a UAE household, and it behaves differently from the first. School fees in the emirate are set and approved through the regulator's own processes, billed per term, and effectively fixed once a place is accepted. Tuition is discretionary, variable and almost entirely under a family's control, which is why it is where overspending happens: nobody audits it.

Four patterns account for most of the waste. Buying weekly tuition in a subject where the problem is technique, so paying for thirty sessions when eight would have done. Buying tuition for the wrong qualification, usually by booking a First Language English tutor for a Second Language candidate or preparing the wrong Literature texts. Buying a package and using half of it. And buying a premium named tutor for a non-scarce subject, where the band above AED 300 purchases availability rather than anything that appears on the mark scheme.

The fifth, which is less obvious, is buying too late. Compressed hours cost more per hour and deliver less per hour, because a student in March is also sitting mocks, finishing coursework and losing sleep. The same twenty hours bought between October and January are cheaper to schedule, cheaper to price, and land on a student with capacity to absorb them. The calendar is the cheapest lever on this page and the least used.

On tax, one line only, because more than that would be guessing. The UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees is not stated here, since doing so responsibly needs a Federal Tax Authority citation. What a family should do is ask any provider whether a quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive of VAT and get the answer in writing before committing. A quote that does not say is not a quote.
bullets: Technique problems need a block of six to ten sessions, not a year of weekly ones
Confirm board, syllabus code, tier and text list in writing before the first session
Ask what happens to unused sessions before buying any monthly package

process.title: Send the brief, not the subject
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier, current mock mark, the marks-to-boundary gap and the weeks remaining. That is six lines and it produces a real quote instead of a band. Providers who cannot price against that brief are quoting an average rather than your child's situation.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the diagnostic in it
process.description: The trial is a real session on a real past paper question, not a sales call. You get the tutor's written read on where the marks are going and whether the gap is content or technique. No card details are taken to book it, and nothing is owed if you stop there.

process.title: Agree the shape before the rate
process.description: Weekly across the course, a six-to-ten-week pre-series block, or a fortnightly review. The shape decides the total far more than the hourly figure does, so settle it first. Then price the shape, including what happens to a session cancelled with 24 hours' notice.

process.title: Measure against the mark scheme, not against effort
process.description: Each session ends on a timed question marked against the published mark scheme, and you receive the mark and the reason. Over six weeks the pattern of lost marks either shifts or it does not, which is a clearer basis for continuing or stopping than how the sessions felt.

process.title: Review the spend at the mock results
process.description: Mocks are the natural audit point. Re-rank the subjects by marks-to-boundary, drop what is now safe, and move the hours to whatever is still short. Most families find at least one subject they can stop paying for, which funds the one that still needs work.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and the tier it describes. Three of the six competitor pages reviewed publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. A parent comparing quotes needs the bands and the attribution, not a promise of affordability.

whyPoints.title: The scarcity premium removed
whyPoints.description: Online delivery widens the tutor pool past the people willing to drive to Al Reef at 5pm. For a scarce syllabus such as 0607 International Mathematics or Pearson 4PH1, that is the difference between a specialist at band rate and a generalist at specialist rate.

whyPoints.title: Priced on the brief, not on a rate card
whyPoints.description: A quote follows the subject, board, tier, start date and frequency, after a free trial lesson. A published rate card would be wrong for most families reading it, which is why we do not keep one, and why we will tell you when a cheaper shape of booking would serve you better.

whyPoints.title: The administrative traps named
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines sit months before papers, Cambridge centres sit in one of six timetable zones, and a Core entry caps a grade. Those three facts cost families more than any hourly rate, and no competitor page reviewed for this project mentions a single one of them.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on the student's own work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, mark and give feedback on the student's own answers. They do not write, redraft to completion or produce coursework, Internal Assessments or Extended Essays. In a market where one provider sells completed Internal Assessments outright, this is worth stating rather than assuming.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based tutor covers a syllabus in the slot you want, we say so and offer the alternative, which may be a tutor based outside the UAE teaching in your time zone. That is disclosed before you book rather than discovered afterwards.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE online tuition cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market bands run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a student or graduate tutor, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, and from AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Subject specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named providers reach AED 650. Those are the providers' own figures rather than IB Gram prices. Where your quote lands inside a band depends on subject scarcity, tier, exam proximity and frequency.

faqs.question: Why do two tutors quote different rates for the same IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: Because the subject name is not the product. A Cambridge 0625 Physics tutor and a Pearson 4PH1 Physics tutor are preparing different papers, and the pool fluent in each differs in size. On top of that sit tier, exam proximity, session length, number of subjects and credential. A quote twice another is usually explained by two of those, most often scarcity and proximity. Ask each provider which of the seven factors they are pricing. One that can answer is quoting your child's situation; one that cannot is quoting an average and hoping.

faqs.question: Is online IGCSE tuition cheaper than a home tutor in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: On the published bands, yes: qualified online tutors sit at AED 150 to 300 an hour against AED 180 to 500 for in-home one-to-one with travel included. Most of that gap is the journey rather than the teaching, and in an emirate as spread out as Abu Dhabi the journey is substantial. In-home delivery also usually carries a minimum booking of ninety minutes or two hours so the drive pays for itself, which inflates the total beyond the hourly difference. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE tuition rates go up closer to the May exam series?
faqs.answer: Effective rates do, for two reasons. Compressed hours are harder to schedule, so availability tightens and quotes move to the top of the band. And the same twenty hours delivered in ten weeks rather than thirty lands on a student who is also sitting mocks and finishing coursework, so each hour achieves less. The calendar is the cheapest lever available to a family: buying the block in the autumn term costs less and works better than buying it in March. That is unwelcome advice in October and the most requested advice in March.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we actually pay for tuition in?
faqs.answer: Usually two, not five. Take the mock results and write down how many marks separate the student from the next grade boundary in each subject, then rank them cheapest first. A subject four marks short is a different investment from one twenty-five marks short. Overlay technique against content: a subject where the material is known and marks go on command words or working takes six to eight sessions, while two missing topics take a term. Fixing two cheap gaps buys two grade movements for less than one expensive one.

faqs.question: Does a longer session cost less per hour?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and that is not the same as being better value. A 90-minute session is typically priced below one and a half times the hourly rate, so the cost per contact hour falls. IGCSE attention, though, degrades noticeably past about 75 minutes, and the last stretch of a two-hour after-school session rarely earns its place. Two 60-minute sessions a week will outperform one 120-minute session at the same total spend for most students. Buy the cheaper cost per mark rather than the cheaper cost per hour.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying per session?
faqs.answer: Only if you use the sessions. A market package of eight online sessions at AED 799 works out near AED 100 each against a qualified-tutor band of AED 150 to 300, which is a real saving at eight sessions and no saving at five. Count the Abu Dhabi school calendar honestly before committing: winter and spring breaks, mock weeks, family travel. A thirty-week plan is usually twenty-four weeks in practice. Ask what happens to an unused session, because the answers in this market range from full rollover to outright expiry.

faqs.question: What is not included in an hourly IGCSE tuition rate?
faqs.answer: Three things, commonly. Exam entry fees, which are paid to an examination centre rather than a tutor and carry the centre's own administrative charges on top of the board's fee. Materials, where a provider expects the student to have the textbook and past papers. And cancellation, where a session called off at short notice may still be billed. On tax, ask in writing whether a quoted AED figure is inclusive or exclusive of VAT; a quote that does not say is incomplete, and the UAE treatment of tuition fees is not something to take from a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel subjects cost different amounts to tutor?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, often yes, because of supply rather than difficulty. Cambridge provision is more widespread locally, so Cambridge specialists in a given subject are easier to book at the qualified-tutor band. Pearson Edexcel specialists are a thinner pool per subject in the emirate, which pushes quotes upward unless the search widens beyond it. That is the clearest cost case for online delivery: the 4PH1 or 4CH1 specialist your child needs may simply not live in Abu Dhabi, and a travel-inclusive in-home rate cannot create one.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to sit IGCSE exams as a private candidate in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: That cost sits entirely outside tuition and is set by the examination centre, not by any tutor. A private candidate pays the board's entry fee plus whatever administrative charge the centre adds, on the centre's own deadline, which falls ahead of the board's. Pearson's November 2026 series is sat on a final timetable running late October to 19 November 2026, with entries closing months earlier in the year and the centre's internal cut-off sitting ahead of that again. Ask the centre for the total in writing, per subject, and confirm the deadline before paying for any tuition aimed at that series.

faqs.question: Does the quoted AED rate include VAT?
faqs.answer: That is a question to put to each provider in writing, and the answer belongs in the quote. This page does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an opinion from a tutoring site. What a family can do is insist that any figure quoted says explicitly whether it is inclusive or exclusive, and that any provider claiming to charge VAT shows a tax registration number. A quote that is silent on this is not comparable with one that is not.

faqs.question: How do we avoid paying for tuition we do not need?
faqs.answer: Audit at the mocks. Re-rank every subject by marks-to-boundary, drop whatever is now comfortably safe, and move those hours to what is still short. Most families find at least one subject they can stop paying for, which funds the one that still needs work. The other three savings are structural: diagnose technique against content before buying a weekly slot, confirm the board, code, tier and text list in writing, and start the block in the autumn rather than in February when the same hours cost more and achieve less.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one online IGCSE session?
faqs.answer: Sharing a one-to-one session rarely works, because the whole value is that the teaching follows one student's errors. What does work, and is common in the Al Raha and Khalifa City corridors, is two consecutive slots with the same tutor on the same evening. The administrative overhead halves, the tutor already has both students' context, and multi-subject or multi-student bookings generally attract a lower effective rate. If a genuinely shared lesson is what you want, ask about small-group provision and compare it honestly against one-to-one for your child.

faqs.question: How many weeks of IGCSE tuition does a grade change take?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the gap is technique or content, and no honest provider will promise a grade. Where a student knows the material and loses marks on command words, diagram labelling or not showing working, six to eight focused sessions can move a mark total meaningfully. Where two topics are genuinely missing, that is a term of weekly work. The useful measurement is not weeks but the pattern of lost marks on timed questions marked against the published mark scheme: if that pattern has not shifted in six sessions, the plan should change rather than continue.

faqs.question: Which details turn an IGCSE price band into a real quote?
faqs.answer: Six lines. The board and syllabus code, for example Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1. The tier, Core or Extended. The current mock mark and, if the school will share it, the marks to the next boundary. The weeks remaining to the series. The number of subjects you are considering. And your realistic weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time. A provider who prices against that is quoting your child. A provider who answers with a single hourly figure before reading it is quoting an average.

faqs.question: Is group IGCSE tuition in Abu Dhabi worth the saving?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is what the student's problem is. Group provision is cheaper per student and works reasonably for content coverage, where several students need the same topic taught. It works poorly for technique repair, because the teaching has to follow one student's specific pattern of lost marks and a group cannot do that. A sensible mixed plan is group or school support for content and a short one-to-one block for paper technique, rather than paying one-to-one rates for something a class could deliver.

abu-dhabi/igcse-online-tuition.closingHeading: Get a number that belongs to your child
abu-dhabi/igcse-online-tuition.closingBody: The bands on this page are the market's, published by the providers named, and they are wide for a real reason: a Year 10 Business Studies 0450 student starting in September and a Year 11 Physics 4PH1 student starting in February are not the same purchase. Send the six lines, board, code, tier, mock mark, weeks remaining and your realistic weekly slot, and take a free trial lesson with no card details required. You will get a written read on whether the gap is technique or content, a recommended shape of booking, and a price for that shape. If a cheaper shape would serve your child better, we will say so before you pay for the expensive one.

intro.heading: The code on the entry form decides everything else
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools choose examination boards by department, not by school. A Year 11 student can be entered for Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 and Cambridge First Language English 0500 in the same series. Those are three different examinations with three different paper structures, three different mark tariff conventions and three different sets of command words. A tutor who starts work without asking which is which is, in effect, guessing at half the job.

The reason this matters so much at IGCSE is that the marks are unevenly distributed and the distribution is public. In the Cambridge separate sciences, roughly a fifth of the total sits in the practical or alternative-to-practical paper, a component most classrooms rehearse two or three times in two years. In Business Studies and Economics the final evaluation lines of the long questions are the single largest unclaimed block. In Mathematics the method marks inside multi-step questions are worth more than the final answers. None of this is secret, and all of it is actionable within a handful of sessions.

What an online format changes is who can be matched to that work. A geographic search in Khalifa City returns tutors who can teach Mathematics and Biology and almost nobody who can mark Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 to the published scheme. Matching on the code instead of the postcode is the difference between covering a subject and covering the examination. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because in-home visits are a service we offer only in India.

The second thing the format changes is what happens on screen. A past paper is shared, the student writes, and the tutor annotates in the same document. There is no waiting a week for a script to come back. A wrong-length answer is interrupted at the third line and rewritten, which is the specific correction that converts subject knowledge into marks. That is the whole mechanical argument for one-to-one, and it works identically whether the tutor is in the next district or another time zone.

This page is organised by what the papers actually assess. Mathematics first, then the separate sciences, then English, then the pattern of mark loss across the rest of the subject list, then the board comparison, then the federally required subjects that run alongside everything else, then how a session is run from an Abu Dhabi household. If you only read one section, read the one covering your child's weakest subject, and bring the code to the consultation. The questions at the end answer the ones families actually ask the exams officer, and a few they should ask and usually do not.

abu-dhabi/igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: IGCSE is tiered, and the tier is part of the specification rather than a classroom setting decision. These are the structures an online tutor has to work inside for an Abu Dhabi student.

programmes.name: Cambridge Core tier
programmes.description: A reduced content specification with its own pair of papers and a capped grade ceiling, typically C on the Cambridge letter scale. Core papers ask shorter questions with lower tariffs, and the technique that pays is accuracy and completeness rather than extended explanation.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi schools the Core entry is often used for students who arrived mid-course from another system, which means some Core candidates are capable of Extended work and have never sat an Extended paper. A single marked Extended paper settles the question.

programmes.name: Cambridge Extended tier
programmes.description: The full specification with access to the top grades. Extended papers carry longer multi-step questions, more marks for method and command words that require explanation and evaluation. Nearly all the online tuition Abu Dhabi families request sits at this tier.
programmes.countryNote: The marginal Extended candidate - entered at the higher tier and working at the bottom of its range - is the most common enquiry in the emirate, and the one where component-level work rather than general revision changes the outcome.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: A single-tier qualification in most subjects, graded 9 to 1, with Mathematics A offered at Foundation and Higher. Papers are structured differently from Cambridge equivalents and some subjects are available in a modular pattern, which changes when marks are banked.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run Edexcel in one or two departments and Cambridge elsewhere, so a student may face both grade scales in the same results envelope. Sixth forms in the emirate read both, but the conversion is not always applied consistently.

programmes.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 and Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 are taken alongside the main Mathematics entry by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Further Mathematics. Content overlaps the start of an A Level course.
programmes.countryNote: These are the thinnest codes in the Abu Dhabi tutor market by a wide margin. A family searching within a twenty-minute drive will usually find nobody; matching on the code rather than the district is the only route that works.

abu-dhabi/igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names the specification, what the papers assess and where the marks actually leave the page. This is the list an online tutor should be able to discuss before taking a booking.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Assessment splits between a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper at both tiers. Extended marks concentrate in multi-step algebra, trigonometry in three dimensions, and probability with conditional structure. The commonest loss is an unsupported final answer in a four-mark question, which forfeits the method marks the student had already earned.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, graded 9 to 1. Higher tier questions are often set in longer applied contexts than Cambridge equivalents, so reading and extracting the mathematics is a skill in itself. Vectors, iteration and compound measures are where Abu Dhabi students most commonly stall.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical or alternative-to-practical paper, the last worth around a fifth of the total. Electricity, waves and momentum carry the mark loss; the multiple-choice paper punishes carelessness with units and prefixes more than any other component.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, electrolysis products and organic reaction pathways are the three heaviest losses. Students who can recite a definition and cannot apply it to an unfamiliar substance score predictably on recall questions and predictably badly on the applied ones.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Large content, low conceptual difficulty, and marks decided almost entirely by command-word discipline. Transport, homeostasis and inheritance questions are answered descriptively when they ask for explanation, which costs a mark a question across a full paper.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Two equally weighted papers: reading, and directed writing with composition. Reading marks are lost on the summary and analysis questions where candidates narrate instead of selecting evidence. Writing marks turn on register and structure far more than on grammar.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
subjects.description: A separate qualification from First Language English, with reading and writing, listening and speaking components. The entry decision matters more than the tuition: sixth forms read 0500 and 0510 differently, and a misplaced student is capped before the course begins.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450, 0455)
subjects.description: Case-study and data-response papers where the gap between a middle and a top grade is application to the stimulus. The final evaluation lines of the long questions are the largest block of marks that candidates routinely leave unattempted.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory and Paper 2 algorithms and problem solving. Students who code fluently in a lesson lose marks writing pseudocode under timed conditions, and trace tables are the highest marks-per-hour gain anywhere in the specification.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460, 0470)
subjects.description: Skills-based papers with case-study requirements. Geography marks hang on using the resource provided rather than general knowledge; History marks hang on source utility and on answering the question asked rather than narrating the period.

sections.heading: Mathematics: 0580 against 4MA1, and what each paper rewards
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where board and tier choices have the largest mechanical effect on the grade available, and the one where an online tutor can waste the most time working from the wrong assumption. Cambridge 0580 is tiered: Core candidates sit a different pair of papers from Extended candidates and the grade is capped. Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 is offered at Foundation and Higher and graded on the 9 to 1 scale. Those are not minor differences in presentation; they change which topics appear at all.

What the papers reward is also different in texture. Cambridge Extended questions tend to be compact and multi-step: a short stem, several marks, and a method that has to be visible. Edexcel Higher questions are more often set in extended applied contexts, so a student has to read a situation, extract the mathematics and then solve it. A student strong at technique and weak at reading will underperform on Edexcel relative to Cambridge, and the reverse is also true.

The marks lost are consistent across both. Unsupported answers in multi-step questions forfeit method marks that were already earned. Premature rounding inside a chain of calculations loses accuracy marks at the end. Bearings, transformations and vector descriptions are marked on precision of language as much as on the diagram. And the non-calculator paper exposes arithmetic fluency that a calculator has been hiding since Year 7, which is why diagnostics are set on it first.

A session on Mathematics should therefore start with the paper, not the topic. The tutor sets a section of the actual paper the student will sit, marks it to the published scheme, and identifies whether the loss is content, method presentation or arithmetic. Those three faults have different fixes and different timescales, and conflating them is the usual reason a term of weekly tuition produces no movement.

sections.heading: The separate sciences, and the fifth of the mark nobody rehearses
paragraphs: Cambridge Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 share a structure that is worth understanding before buying any tuition in them. Candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper at their tier, and a practical component: either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. That practical component is worth around a fifth of the total mark, and it is assessed on paper in both forms. It asks the candidate to read a method critically, identify a control variable, criticise a results table, plot accurately and draw a conclusion the data supports.

Almost no school timetable rehearses it properly. Practical lessons in Years 10 and 11 are about doing the experiment, which is a different skill from answering questions about somebody else's experiment under timed conditions. The result is a component carrying twenty per cent of the grade that most candidates meet two or three times before the series. For a tutor it is the highest ratio of available marks to teaching hours anywhere in the IGCSE science specifications.

The multiple-choice paper is the second underestimated component. It is marked without method credit, so a unit error or a prefix slip costs the whole mark, and the questions are designed around precisely those slips. Drilling forty multiple-choice questions with the student explaining each distractor aloud is dull and extremely effective, and it is the sort of work a one-to-one session can sustain and a class of twenty-eight cannot.

The theory paper is where content gaps show, and the gaps are predictable. Electricity and waves in Physics. Moles, electrolysis and organic pathways in Chemistry. Transport, homeostasis and inheritance in Biology. A diagnostic across those topics in the first session will usually locate the problem within twenty minutes, which is why a first lesson spent on introductions is a wasted hour.

sections.heading: English: 0500 against 0510, and the entry that sets a ceiling
paragraphs: The most consequential English decision in an Abu Dhabi school is not how the subject is taught but which code the student is entered for. Cambridge First Language English 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510 or 0511 are separate qualifications with different papers, different ceilings and different value to a sixth form. A student entered for 0510 who reads comfortably at first-language level has a placement problem that no amount of tuition addresses, and it is worth checking in Year 10 rather than discovering in Year 12.

Within 0500, the two papers behave differently under tuition. The reading paper responds quickly: the summary question and the analysis question have specific, teachable techniques, and candidates who narrate rather than select can usually be retrained in four or five sessions. The directed writing and composition paper moves more slowly, because register, structure and control of length are habits built over months rather than techniques applied in an exam.

Edexcel English Language A 4EA1 is structured differently again, with its own anthology and coursework option in some centres. The practical consequence for a tutor is that the texts matter: a student working on an anthology extract needs a tutor who has read it, not a general essay coach. That is one of the clearest cases for matching by specification rather than by subject name.

Across all three codes the same two marks are left on the table. Candidates write answers of the wrong length for the tariff, and they answer the question they expected rather than the one printed. Both faults are correctable in a one-to-one session because they need interrupting mid-sentence, and both are invisible in a class where work is marked a week later.

sections.heading: Where the marks go in everything else, in order of size
paragraphs: Outside the core subjects the pattern of mark loss is remarkably consistent, and knowing it changes what a family asks a tutor to do. In Business Studies 0450 and Economics 0455 the largest single block of unclaimed marks sits in the final lines of the long questions, where the command word is evaluate or discuss and the candidate has produced two lists and no judgement. Four to six marks a question, several questions a paper, and it is teachable in a handful of sessions because it is a structure rather than a body of knowledge.

In Computer Science 0478 the loss is almost entirely in Paper 2. Students who write working code in a lesson produce pseudocode under timed conditions that would not run, and trace tables - a mechanical, entirely learnable skill - are attempted without method. Both are drillable, and neither gets rehearsed often in a crowded classroom.

In Geography 0460 the marks hang on using the resource printed on the paper rather than on general knowledge of the topic, and in History 0470 on source utility and on answering the question asked rather than narrating the period. Both faults are diagnosable from one marked script. In Accounting 0452 the loss is presentational: a correct figure in the wrong column scores nothing, and candidates practise calculation while losing marks on layout.

The practical point is that these are component-level faults, not subject-level weaknesses. A student is rarely bad at Economics; they are routinely losing the evaluation marks in Economics. Naming the fault at that resolution is what makes a four-session block worth buying, and it is the first thing a tutor should produce from a diagnostic.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel, and why your child may sit both
paragraphs: Two boards dominate British-curriculum entries in Abu Dhabi, and plenty of students sit papers from both in one series. The differences that matter to a tutor are structural rather than reputational. Cambridge tiers Mathematics and the separate sciences into Core and Extended with different papers; Edexcel offers a single tier in most subjects and Foundation and Higher in Mathematics A. Cambridge grades A* to G; Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1. Cambridge runs June and November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; Pearson offers International GCSE in May/June and November.

The administration differs in a way worth knowing. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. That is a parent-facing risk, not an abstraction: check the zone timetable your child's centre uses rather than a generic one found online.

Entry deadlines sit a long way ahead of the papers on both boards. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and final entries for June close in the spring term, months before the first paper; because every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the version of the timetable that applies to your child comes from the school, and Cambridge warns that it cannot take responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any date should be checked against the live official timetable rather than a restatement of it.

For tuition purposes the conclusion is simple. Ask for the board and code by subject, in writing, from the exams officer. Then ask the tutor to work from that specification and that board's past papers. A student preparing for Edexcel on Cambridge papers will meet a question style they have never practised in the room where it counts.

sections.heading: How an online session actually runs from an Abu Dhabi household
paragraphs: The mechanics are worth describing because families imagine something more passive than what happens. A past paper from the student's own board is shared on screen at the start of the session. The student works on it, typing or writing on a tablet, while the tutor watches the working appear. Nothing is screen-shared from a slide deck; the document in view is the paper being sat. That alone changes the session from a lecture into supervised practice.

When an answer goes wrong, the correction happens immediately. A four-mark explanation that opens with a one-line description is interrupted at the third line, the command word is reread, and the answer is rewritten there and then. This is the single mechanical advantage of one-to-one tuition in any format, and the reason a class cannot replicate it: in a group of six the same answer is marked and returned a week later, by which point the habit has been practised five more times.

What the household needs to provide is modest and specific. A surface at the right height, a door that closes, a device with a camera and a stable connection, and either a printed paper or a stylus. Headphones help in an apartment. A second screen is useful but not necessary. Families on Al Reem Island and in central districts usually find that reorganising a corner of a room improves the mark record more than an extra session would.

The written output arrives after the session rather than being promised for later. An annotated paper, a short note naming what was covered and what to practise, and an updated component record carrying the raw mark and the paper reference. Because the work happened in a shared document, producing all three is a by-product rather than an extra task, which is why online engagements tend to leave a better paper trail than visiting ones.
bullets: The document on screen is the paper being sat, not a slide deck
Wrong-length answers are interrupted and rewritten in the session

sections.heading: What an online tutor cannot do, stated plainly
paragraphs: There are limits worth naming before a family pays for anything. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, because in-home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. No tutor will arrive at an Abu Dhabi address, and a page that implied otherwise would be selling something we do not have. For a young or very distractible student, the absence of an adult in the room is a real cost rather than a detail, and a parent who needs that supervision should buy it from somebody who sells it.

Bench practical work remains the school's job. A tutor can rehearse the alternative-to-practical paper, which is where the marks are, and can talk a student through a method, but cannot supervise an experiment over video and should not pretend to. Where a Cambridge centre enters candidates for the practical test rather than the written alternative, the school's laboratory time is the preparation and the tutor's contribution is recording, presentation and interpretation.

Nor can a tutor supply board materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and reproducing or distributing them is copyright infringement. We reference them, cite the official page, and link out. A provider offering a drive full of mark schemes is handing you somebody else's property and a reason to doubt everything else they say.

On internally assessed work the boundary is firm. A tutor teaches the skills the component assesses, explains the published criteria, marks a student's own draft against them and asks questions that make the student revise their own reasoning. Content, prose and finished pieces are not supplied by anyone other than the candidate. Services advertising completed assessed work are selling the student a malpractice risk they will carry alone, and the correct response is to leave the provider rather than negotiate the scope.

process.description: The tutor names the component to be worked on, the specification points still unsecured in the board's own wording, and a target mark on a named paper type. It is written down before the second session, so progress is checkable by anyone.

process.description: Sessions are spent on past questions from your child's board, annotated live. Answers of the wrong length are interrupted and rewritten. Each session produces an annotated document, a short note and an updated component record.

process.description: The component record is read every six or seven weeks and one of three decisions follows: continue, change the component, or stop because the target is met. Where the evidence points at the entry rather than the teaching, we say so.

whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched to Cambridge 0580 or Edexcel 4MA1, to 0625 or 4PH1, not to Mathematics or Physics. The code determines the papers, the tiering and the mark distribution, and working from the wrong one wastes a term.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Around a fifth of a Cambridge science mark sits in the practical or alternative-to-practical paper, and most classrooms rehearse it two or three times in two years. It is the highest marks-per-hour component in the qualification and we treat it that way.

whyPoints.title: Live annotation, not a weekly delay
whyPoints.description: Work happens in a shared document, so a wrong-length answer is corrected at the third line instead of a week later. That immediate correction is the one thing one-to-one buys that no group format can replicate.

faqs.question: Where is the IGCSE syllabus code printed, and why does it decide the tuition?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer or check the entry confirmation; the code is also printed on any past paper the department has issued. Boards are chosen by department, so a single Abu Dhabi school may enter candidates for Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and Edexcel 4MA1 Mathematics in the same series. Get it in writing per subject. It matters because the papers differ in structure, tiering and mark allocation, and a tutor working from the wrong specification prepares for questions that will not appear on the paper.

faqs.question: How much of the Cambridge science grade sits in the practical paper?
faqs.answer: Around a fifth of the total, in either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Both are assessed on paper: reading a method critically, identifying a control variable, criticising a results table, plotting accurately and drawing a conclusion the data supports. Most school timetables rehearse it two or three times in two years, because practical lessons focus on doing experiments rather than answering questions about somebody else's. It is the highest ratio of available marks to teaching hours in the whole specification.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor prepare my child for the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the components the format handles best. The paper asks candidates to criticise a written method, spot the variable that was not controlled, redraw a badly presented table, plot points accurately and interpret a trend. All of that happens on paper and rehearses perfectly on a shared screen with past questions. Bench technique stays with the school; the paper skills, which are where the marks actually are, are what a tutor drills.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge Core and Extended tier?
faqs.answer: They are different papers from a different amount of content, and the grade available differs. Core covers a reduced specification with shorter, lower-tariff questions and caps the grade, typically around C on the letter scale. Extended covers the full content with longer multi-step questions, more method marks and command words demanding explanation and evaluation. The decision is usually made in Year 10 and reviewed once against mock performance, and a marked Extended paper is the evidence a school can act on.

faqs.question: Does my child lose anything by sitting Edexcel instead of Cambridge?
faqs.answer: No. Both are recognised qualifications and sixth forms in Abu Dhabi read both. The practical differences are structural: Edexcel is single tier in most subjects and graded 9 to 1, Cambridge tiers maths and the sciences and grades A* to G, and the question styles differ. Edexcel Higher Mathematics tends to set longer applied contexts, Cambridge Extended tends to set compact multi-step stems. A student should practise on the board they will sit, which is the whole reason to confirm the code.

faqs.question: Where do most students lose marks in IGCSE Business Studies and Economics?
faqs.answer: In the final lines of the long questions, where the command word is evaluate or discuss. Candidates produce two lists of points and stop without a supported judgement that refers back to the stimulus, leaving four to six marks on several questions in the same paper. It is a structure rather than a body of knowledge, which means it responds to a short block of targeted sessions. A diagnostic script usually shows the pattern within one paper.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 2 the problem in Cambridge Computer Science 0478?
faqs.answer: Because writing algorithms under timed conditions is a different skill from coding in a lesson. Students who build working programmes on a computer produce pseudocode on paper that would not run, miss initialisation, and attempt trace tables without a method. Trace tables in particular are mechanical and entirely learnable, and they are among the highest marks-per-hour gains in the specification. Both faults need interrupting and redoing in the moment, which is what a one-to-one session can sustain.

faqs.question: Is First Language English or English as a Second Language the right entry?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student, and the decision deserves checking rather than inheriting. Cambridge 0500 First Language English and 0510 or 0511 English as a Second Language are separate qualifications with different papers and different ceilings, and sixth forms read them differently. A student reading comfortably at first-language level who is entered for 0510 is capped before the course starts. Raise it with the school in Year 10, when the entry can still be changed without disruption.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix a command-word problem?
faqs.answer: Usually four to six sessions, which makes it the cheapest substantial gain available at IGCSE. The fault is that candidates describe when the paper says explain, and stop before the judgement when it says evaluate. The fix is mechanical: read the tariff, decide the shape of the answer, then write. It needs interrupting mid-sentence and rewriting repeatedly, so it responds to one-to-one work and barely moves in a group where scripts come back a week later.

faqs.question: What should the first online session with an IGCSE tutor contain?
faqs.answer: A real past paper from your child's own board, or two sections of one, sat under something close to timed conditions and marked against the published scheme. The output should be a raw mark, a question-by-question breakdown and a named fault: content gap, method presentation or exam technique. A first session spent on introductions and learning styles has told you nothing you can act on, and it is an hour you cannot get back in an exam year.

faqs.question: Can a tutor send us past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who offers a folder of them is distributing somebody else's property. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. We reference them and link to the official pages, and we work from material your child's school has legitimately issued. Reproducing board material is copyright infringement, and for unreleased papers it is a malpractice exposure for the candidate as well.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge publish six different exam timetables?
faqs.answer: Because every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. For a parent this means checking the timetable your child's own centre uses rather than a generic one found online, and treating any date restated on a third-party site as unverified.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, Computer Science Paper 2 and Arabic First Language 0508, in roughly that order. A search within a twenty-minute drive of most districts returns nobody who can mark those papers to the published scheme. This is the clearest practical argument for matching by specification rather than by location, and it is also why we state coverage before a booking rather than after one.

faqs.question: What does my child need at home for an online IGCSE lesson?
faqs.answer: A surface at the right height, a door that closes, a device with a working camera and a stable connection, and either a printed paper or a stylus for a tablet. Headphones help in an apartment. A second screen is useful rather than necessary. Families in tower districts often find that reorganising a corner of a room improves the mark record more than an additional session would, which is worth trying before buying more hours.

abu-dhabi/igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Bring the code and we will tell you the truth about coverage
