abu-dhabi/igcse-resit-tutor.programmesIntro: A resit rarely sits alone. Most Abu Dhabi families booking IGCSE resit support are also managing the next stage, whether that is a sixth-form A-Level block, an IB Diploma start, or a second IGCSE sitting alongside it. These are the programmes the work connects to.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two boards, two specifications, two sets of paper codes. Cambridge tiers many subjects into Core and Extended with different grade ceilings; Pearson generally runs a single tier with higher-tier content built in. A resit candidate must be entered against the same specification code they intend to be examined on, which is why the code belongs in the plan from the first lesson.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a deep British-curriculum sector under ADEK, so most resit candidates here are entering through a school centre rather than a standalone examination centre. Where a student has left the school, the entry has to be arranged with a centre willing to take external candidates, and that decision drives which series is realistic.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, the usual reason for the resit
programmes.description: Sixth-form entry conditions are the single most common trigger for an IGCSE resit. A school may require a grade 6 in the subject to be taken at A Level and a grade 5 in English and Mathematics for any offer. The resit therefore has a target number, not a vague ambition, and the plan should be built backwards from that number.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi sixth forms differ on whether they accept a November or March resit grade after the academic year has begun. Ask the admissions office in writing which series they will accept and by what date, then choose the series. Doing it the other way round is how a family ends up with a grade that arrives too late to be useful.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Students moving from IGCSE into the Diploma often resit a science or Mathematics because the Diploma subject they want has an attainment expectation attached. The resit then doubles as preparation: the algebra that limits a 0580 grade is the same algebra that limits Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run the Diploma alongside a British lower school, so a student can resit an IGCSE in November while already sitting in DP1 classes. That is workable, but it needs the revision block scheduled around internal assessment deadlines rather than dropped on top of them.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency track
programmes.description: For the British track, the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.
programmes.countryNote: That five-subject rule is the reason a resit sometimes matters even when a university offer does not depend on it. A student holding four qualifying IGCSEs and one ungraded result has an equivalency problem, not an admissions problem, and the fix is usually one targeted resit. Verify current requirements on the Ministry's own channel before acting.

abu-dhabi/igcse-resit-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families most often resit, with the syllabus code that decides what the paper looks like and the component where the marks usually went. The code matters: 0580 and 4MA1 are both called Maths and they are not the same examination.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Extended Paper 4 is where resit candidates lose most ground: multi-part structured questions on functions, transformations and probability trees that reward method marks. Core candidates often lose a whole grade to number work and percentage reverse problems. The fix is method writing, not more topics.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Higher tier Papers 1H and 2H both run 2 hours and both carry calculator access, which changes revision priorities away from arithmetic and towards algebraic fluency, vectors and circle theorems. Students who switched boards mid-course often sit the wrong paper style and lose marks to unfamiliar question phrasing.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and the thermal physics questions account for a large share of lost marks, and the practical-skills paper punishes students who have never written a method with a named control variable. Resit work concentrates on circuit reasoning, graph interpretation and the difference between describe and explain.

subjects.name: Physics (Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2 split the content, so a resit candidate who collapsed on one paper may only need half the specification rebuilt. Forces and motion calculations with unit conversion, and the magnetism and electromagnetism section, are the recurring weak points in Abu Dhabi cohorts.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and moles calculations between them decide most Extended grades. Students can usually name functional groups and still cannot write a balanced equation under time pressure. Sessions drill stoichiometry to automaticity before touching anything qualitative.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Biology resits are usually a writing problem rather than a knowledge problem. The specification rewards precise terminology and the mark scheme accepts a narrow set of words. Work focuses on transport in plants, homeostasis and the long-answer questions where a vague answer earns one mark instead of four.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Many Abu Dhabi students sit ESL rather than First Language English, and the resit hinges on the summary task and the extended writing register. Marks are lost to length, not accuracy: a 150-word answer where the task wanted 120 is penalised for relevance before it is read for grammar.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: The directed writing and composition components carry the grade, and resit candidates almost always need structural work rather than vocabulary work. A composition with three strong paragraphs and no planning loses to a plainer piece that answers the question it was set.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: The case-study paper requires application to the given business, and resit candidates lose marks by writing textbook answers that never name the company in the stem. Evaluation marks are the cheapest available and the most often skipped entirely.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455 and Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the grade. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns marks that no amount of prose recovers. Resit work rebuilds the six core diagrams until they can be drawn from memory, then attaches the analysis to them.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science (Cambridge 0653 and 0654)
subjects.description: Students resitting these often did so because one of the three sciences dragged the grade. The component report shows which, and that is where every hour should go. Rebuilding all three equally is the most common wasted resit plan in this subject.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 2 algorithm and programming questions are where resit candidates lose ground, specifically pseudocode that does not compile in a reader's head. Trace tables and dry-run practice recover marks faster than revisiting the theory in Paper 1.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE resit actually changes on the certificate
paragraphs: A resit produces a new result for that subject in that series. The original result does not disappear from a student's records, but a university or sixth form looking at an application reads the grade the student presents, and in practice the higher grade is the one that gets used. For the Ministry of Education equivalency count, what matters is holding five accredited subjects at no lower than grade E or grade 3, and a resit that lifts a failing subject into that range solves the problem directly.

What a resit does not do is change the specification. If your child sat Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Extended, the resit is against 0620 Extended with the same components and the same weightings. There is no reduced paper for resit candidates and no partial entry on the Extended tier. That is why the component report is the whole basis of the plan: the examination is identical, so the only variable is what the student does differently in it.

Tier changes are the one structural decision available. A Cambridge candidate on Extended can be entered for Core instead, which caps the grade at C or grade 5 depending on the subject's grading scale but makes that ceiling far more achievable. Whether that trade is right depends entirely on what the grade is for. A student who needs a 5 in Mathematics for a sixth-form offer may be better served by a secure Core entry than by a second Extended attempt that lands in the same place as the first.

Families sometimes ask whether a resit looks bad. In the Abu Dhabi schools we deal with, it does not. Admissions teams read a resit as a student who identified a problem and fixed it, which is a more useful signal than a first-attempt grade that nobody can explain. What does read badly is a resit entered without a plan and sat with the same preparation as the first attempt.

sections.heading: Choosing the series: the calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: Every resit decision is a calendar decision first. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and each centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones. Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. That is a real risk for a family arranging entry through an unfamiliar centre.

The table below uses Pearson's published November 2026 International GCSE series as the worked example, because November is the window most resit candidates are actually choosing and it shows how far ahead of the paper the real deadlines sit. The papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026; entries for them closed months earlier in the year, and the centre's own internal cut-off closed earlier again. Results reach students the following January, which is the date a conditional sixth-form offer has to be checked against before the entry is filed. A family that starts planning in October for a November paper is planning for a series it can no longer enter, and should be counting backwards towards May/June instead.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable on the Pearson qualifications site is the only version worth planning against; restating a date that can still be revised is how families end up revising for the wrong week.

Working backwards from the paper is the whole method. Count the weeks from today to the examination window, subtract the two or three weeks before the paper when nothing new can be learned, and what remains is the teaching time available. If that number is under eight weeks for a two-grade jump in a science, the honest answer is to target the following series and use the time properly rather than enter early and repeat the result.

sections.heading: Entering as a private candidate in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: If your child is still enrolled at the school where they sat the first attempt, entry is usually straightforward: the examinations officer adds them to the series and the fee appears on the school account. The complication arrives when the student has left, has changed curriculum, or when the school declines to re-enter them. In those cases the student becomes a private candidate and must find a centre willing to accept external entries for that specification.

Abu Dhabi has a deep private-school sector licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Not every licensed school is an examination centre for every board, and a centre that runs Cambridge is not automatically a centre that will take a Pearson entry. The practical question to ask is narrow: do you accept external candidates for this exact syllabus code in this series, and what is your internal cut-off date?

Private-candidate entry carries its own fees, set by the centre rather than by the board, and those fees are separate from the board's entry fee. Centres also differ on whether they will host components that need a laboratory or a speaking examination, which rules some specifications out entirely for external candidates. Check the component list against what the centre can actually deliver before paying anything, because an entry that cannot sit Paper 5 is not an entry at all.

One scheduling point specific to this emirate: confirm the zone timetable the centre uses, not the one a friend at another school quoted. Cambridge allocates centres to administrative zones and publishes a timetable per zone, and two Abu Dhabi centres do not have to be in the same zone. The date your child sits the paper is the date their centre's timetable says, and that is the date the revision plan has to end on.

sections.heading: Where the marks went the first time, subject by subject
paragraphs: The component report is the most under-used document in the IGCSE system. It tells you which paper lost the grade, and that single fact reorganises the entire revision plan. A student who scored adequately on a short-answer paper and badly on an extended-response paper has a writing and timing problem. A student who lost marks evenly across both papers has a content problem. The two need almost nothing in common, and treating them the same is why so many resits land on the same grade.

Where the school can request the original script, that is worth doing. Cambridge and Pearson both operate access-to-script services through the centre, and reading the real answers removes all guessing. We do not reproduce or supply board papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents; the centre requests the script and we work from what your child wrote, against the published assessment objectives that the board makes available on its own site.

The table below sets out the patterns we see most often in Abu Dhabi resit candidates, by syllabus code. These are the recurring failure modes, not a prediction about your child, and the first diagnostic session exists precisely to establish which of them applies. What makes them useful is that each has a known fix with a known number of hours attached, which is what lets us tell a family honestly whether the target grade fits in the time remaining.

One pattern cuts across every subject: command-term misreading. A student who answers describe when the question said explain loses marks they could already have earned. The mark schemes are consistent about this, and it is the cheapest grade movement available in a resit, which is why it comes first in almost every plan we write rather than last.

sections.heading: What resit support costs in Abu Dhabi, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Resit tuition sits at the upper end of the market, because the work is specification-specific and time-bounded. Market rates in the UAE run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online and university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist. Premium named or examiner-led tuition has been advertised at AED 650. Those are market figures published by providers and rate trackers, not IB Gram prices.

Three things move the number in this emirate specifically. The first is format: in-home rates carry travel, and in Abu Dhabi travel between the mainland communities and the island is a genuine cost, which is why in-home bands sit AED 50 to 150 above online for the same tutor quality. The second is proximity to the series, because availability tightens in the eight weeks before a paper and the specialists are booked first. The third is subject scarcity: a resit in Mathematics has a wide tutor pool, a resit in Cambridge Art and Design or a less-entered language has a very narrow one.

Package structures seen in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. A resit plan is usually denser than a weekly habit, so budget against total hours rather than against a monthly figure.

For context, Abu Dhabi school fees are set and approved through the emirate's regulatory process, and in Dubai the KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the variable line in a family's education budget, which is exactly why a resit plan should state a total hour count up front rather than running open-ended. IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages; the first lesson is free with no card required, and pricing is confirmed in the consultation.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and what carries over
paragraphs: This is the question families ask last and should ask first. Whether a coursework or practical mark carries into a resit depends on the specification, and the answer changes what the resit actually involves. Some components can be carried forward from a previous series; others must be sat again. The centre's examinations officer can confirm this against the current syllabus for the exact code, and that confirmation should happen before the entry is made rather than after.

Where a practical or coursework component must be re-taken, a private candidate has a real problem, because not every centre can host it. A Cambridge science specification with a practical-skills paper needs a centre with the apparatus and the willingness to run it for an external candidate. A language with a speaking component needs an examiner. If the centre cannot deliver the component, the entry has to move to a centre that can, and that decision changes both the timetable and the fee.

Where a mark does carry forward, the resit narrows to the written papers and the plan gets correspondingly tighter. That is the best case for a resit candidate: a known weak paper, a fixed number of weeks, and no coursework to rebuild. It is also where the biggest grade movements happen, because every available hour goes into the component that actually lost the marks.

On the coursework itself, the boundary is absolute and worth stating plainly. A tutor teaches, explains, models technique, and gives feedback on work the student has written. A tutor does not write, complete or redraft assessed coursework, and no IB Gram tutor will do so. Providers in this market sell completed assessed work; that is a malpractice trigger for the student and the reason we say what the boundary is rather than leaving it implied.

sections.heading: Resits, equivalency and what the Ministry actually counts
paragraphs: A resit sometimes matters for reasons that have nothing to do with a sixth-form offer. For the British track, the UAE Ministry of Education requires a student to pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last point catches families out. A student holding five IGCSEs where two are Arabic and Islamic Education is holding three for equivalency purposes, not five, and needs two more qualifying subjects. One competitor page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced requirement is five accredited subjects excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Getting the count right is the difference between one targeted resit and a year of unnecessary work.

For the American track the Ministry sets test requirements instead: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in the sourced material we hold, so we publish none; verify any IB figure against the Ministry's own channel.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation. We describe the requirement, point to the authority, and make sure a resit plan is aimed at a subject that actually counts. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, university admission or school progression, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling urgency rather than teaching.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, not left open. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's own service page for this is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone, including us.

Two further points matter for a resit. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. So a plan built around your child's own class teacher tutoring them privately is not a plan we will arrange, and you should be cautious of anyone offering it. Verify current wording against the live ADEK policy document.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal again: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no regulator permit or accreditation and does not claim one. We are an online tutor-matching platform with no UAE office, and we say so because several pages in this search result imply otherwise.

sections.heading: The twelve-week resit plan, and what happens if the subject is scarce
paragraphs: Twelve weeks is the shape most resit plans take, because it is long enough to rebuild two or three topics properly and short enough that a family can hold the schedule. Weeks one and two are diagnosis: component marks read, one full paper sat under timing, a ranked topic list produced with marks attached. Weeks three to eight are the rebuild, one or two sessions a week, each ending with a question set returned before the next lesson. Weeks nine to twelve are paper discipline, where content stops and timing starts.

The measure of progress is marks recovered on repeat questions, not topics ticked off. A student who could not earn the last four marks on a structured question in week two and earns three of them in week seven has moved; a student who has covered nine topics and still loses the same marks has not. That distinction is why the plan gets reviewed every fourth session and rewritten when the evidence says to, rather than run to completion because it was written down.

Availability is where most platforms stop being honest, so here is the position. For a mainstream resit subject in Abu Dhabi, a specialist match usually takes two to four working days. For a narrow specification, a less-entered language, or a creative subject with a coursework component, it can take longer, and in the eight weeks before a series it takes longer still because the specialists fill up first. If we cannot cover a subject at the standard a resit needs, we say so rather than putting a general tutor in front of a specification they have never marked.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match may be a tutor based elsewhere teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which for an online lesson changes nothing about the lesson and everything about the pool available. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we run only in India, and the comparison table on this page exists so you can judge that trade on its merits rather than on our description of it.

process.title: Send the statement of results
process.description: The first useful document is the component breakdown, not a description of how the year went. Send the statement of results, the subject and the exact syllabus code, and the target grade with the reason behind it. That is enough to tell you whether the target fits the time left.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: One lesson at no cost and with no card required. The tutor works through the weakest component with your child and finishes with a written statement of what cost the grade. If the fit is wrong, you have lost an hour and gained a diagnosis.

process.title: Confirm the series and the centre
process.description: Before any teaching plan is fixed, settle which series you are entering and which centre is taking the entry, with the centre's own cut-off date and zone timetable in writing. The teaching plan is built backwards from that examination date, not forwards from today.

process.title: Agree the hour count
process.description: The plan states a total number of hours against the ranked topic list, so you are agreeing to a block of work rather than an open-ended arrangement. If the honest hour count does not fit the series, we say so and recommend the next one.

process.title: Weekly work with marks tracked
process.description: Fixed slot, question set after every lesson, written feedback returned before the next. Marks recovered per topic are recorded, and the plan is reviewed every fourth session against that record rather than against the calendar.

process.title: Hand over to paper discipline
process.description: In the final six weeks the work changes shape: full papers under timing, marked against the published mark scheme, review sessions spent only on lost marks. Timing strategy per paper is written down and practised rather than discussed.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts from the real paper
whyPoints.description: A resit plan built on a tutor's own diagnostic test ignores the most informative document you have. We start from the component marks and, where the centre can request it, the original script, because that removes guessing about which paper lost the grade.

whyPoints.title: Syllabus codes, not subject names
whyPoints.description: 0580 and 4MA1 are both called Maths and they examine differently. Every plan names the code, the tier and the components, so the practice your child does matches the paper they will sit rather than a generic version of the subject.

whyPoints.title: The hour count is stated up front
whyPoints.description: Resit work is time-bounded, so the plan carries a total hour estimate against a ranked topic list. If the target grade does not fit the weeks remaining before the entry deadline, we tell you that before you pay for anything.

whyPoints.title: A wider specialist pool than any commute allows
whyPoints.description: Because lessons are online and one-to-one, the match is made from tutors who have taught that specification to examination rather than from tutors who can reach your community by 5pm. For a scarce specification that difference decides whether a match exists at all.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is explicit
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, models and gives feedback on your child's own work. No IB Gram tutor writes or completes assessed coursework. Providers in this search result sell finished assessments; we state the boundary because the student carries the malpractice risk, not the seller.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated honestly
whyPoints.description: Mainstream resit subjects match in two to four working days. Narrow specifications take longer, and inside eight weeks of a series they take longer again. When we cannot cover a subject properly we say so instead of filling the slot with a generalist.

faqs.question: Can my child resit just one IGCSE subject, or does the whole set have to be taken again?
faqs.answer: One subject is fine. IGCSE results are reported per subject, so a candidate can be entered for a single syllabus in a later series and leave everything else as it stands. That is the most common resit in Abu Dhabi: one science or Mathematics standing between a student and a sixth-form offer. The entry is made against the specific syllabus code, and the only thing that has to be re-sat is whatever that specification requires, which may include a practical or coursework component. Confirm the component list with the centre before entering so the revision plan matches the papers actually being taken.

faqs.question: Which exam series should an Abu Dhabi resit candidate enter, November or June?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the date the grade is needed. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. If a sixth form needs the grade before the academic year starts, June is usually the answer. If the student has already started Year 12 and the offer is conditional, November can work provided the school has confirmed in writing that it will accept a January results date. Check your centre's zone timetable, because Cambridge allocates centres to six administrative zones with different versions.

faqs.question: Does a resit grade replace the original grade on the certificate?
faqs.answer: A resit produces a new certificated result for that subject in that series. The earlier result still exists in the student's record, but in practice sixth forms and universities read the grade the applicant presents, and the higher one is the one that gets used. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, what counts is holding five accredited subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, so a resit that lifts a subject into range solves the requirement directly. Verify current rules on the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: Can my child sit an IGCSE resit as a private candidate if their school will not re-enter them?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it takes arranging. The student becomes a private candidate and needs a centre willing to accept external entries for that exact syllabus code in that series. Not every school licensed by ADEK is a centre for every board, and a Cambridge centre will not necessarily take a Pearson entry. Ask three questions in writing: do you accept external candidates for this code, what is your internal cut-off date, and can you deliver every component including practicals or speaking papers. Centre fees sit on top of the board entry fee and are set by the centre.

faqs.question: How many weeks of tutoring does a one-grade IGCSE improvement usually take?
faqs.answer: Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does should be treated with real scepticism. What can be said is the shape of the work. A one-grade move in a science or Mathematics typically needs eight to twelve weeks of one or two weekly sessions, with the last four to six spent entirely on timed papers. Two grades usually needs a full term or the next series. The variable is not effort but how many of the lost marks came from content versus timing and command-term misreading, and the first diagnostic session exists to establish exactly that.

faqs.question: What does specialist IGCSE resit tuition cost per hour in Abu Dhabi in 2026?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not IB Gram prices: roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online or university-student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE or A-Level specialist, and AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is priced in. Premium named tuition has been advertised at AED 650. Resit work sits in the specialist band because it is specification-specific and time-bounded. Ask any provider for the total hour count rather than the hourly rate, because that is the number that matters.

faqs.question: Does a coursework or practical mark carry over into a resit?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specification, and this is the question to settle before entering rather than after. Some components can be carried forward from a previous series; others must be sat again. The centre's examinations officer can confirm the position against the current syllabus for the exact code. Where a practical or speaking component must be re-taken, a private candidate needs a centre with the apparatus or the examiner to deliver it, which rules some specifications out entirely at some centres. If a mark does carry forward, the resit narrows to the written papers and the plan gets considerably tighter.

faqs.question: Will a resit grade still count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A certificated resit result is a certificated result, so a subject lifted into range counts. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. Equivalency is handled by the authority, not by IB Gram, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

faqs.question: My child needs a grade 5 in Mathematics 0580 for sixth form. Is one term realistic?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the component report tells you whether. If the first attempt was Extended and the marks were lost mainly on Paper 4 structured questions, a term of method-writing discipline plus functions and probability work is a realistic route to a 5. If marks were lost evenly across both papers, the content base needs rebuilding and a term is tight. A Core entry is the other option: it caps the grade but makes the cap far more achievable, and if the offer asks for a 5 rather than a 7 that trade is worth putting on the table.

faqs.question: Is there any Cambridge IGCSE sitting between November and June that an Abu Dhabi resit could use?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers UAE centres a June series and a November series, and nothing in between: the February and March series some families read about online is offered to India only, and the Checkpoint tests that run in March, May and October are Primary and Lower Secondary assessments, not IGCSE. So the earliest paper available after a set of August results is the November sitting, with entries closing over the summer on the centre's deadline, and the next one after that is June, with entries closing in the spring term. That gap is what makes the resit decision a calendar decision: five months to November, or roughly twelve to the following June, with the extra time usually worth more than it looks when a grade boundary is two or three marks away. Confirm with your centre which series it enters candidates for and which zone timetable applies to it.

faqs.question: Should a resit candidate move from Extended down to Core, or stay on Extended?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the grade is for. A Cambridge candidate entered for Core faces a lower grade ceiling but a far more achievable one, because the papers are shorter in content reach and the questions are more direct. If a sixth-form offer needs a 5 and the first Extended attempt landed at 3, a secure Core entry can be the better bet. If the subject is being continued to A Level and the department expects a 6 or 7, Core closes that door and a second Extended attempt with proper diagnosis is the right call.

faqs.question: How do we see the actual paper our child sat to know where the marks went?
faqs.answer: Through the centre. Cambridge and Pearson both operate access-to-script services requested by the examinations officer, not by the family directly, and the statement of results already gives you marks by component without any request at all. Start with the component breakdown, because it tells you which paper lost the grade and that one fact reorganises the whole plan. We do not reproduce or supply board papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents; we work from what your child wrote and cite the board's own published material by link.

faqs.question: Can my child resit with Pearson Edexcel if the first attempt was Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Switching boards is possible, since the two are separate qualifications, but it usually makes the resit harder rather than easier. Pearson International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 and Cambridge 0580 cover similar mathematics with different paper structures, question phrasing and tiering, so a student switching boards is learning a new examination on top of fixing the original problem. The switch is worth it only where a centre will take one board and not the other, or where a component the student struggles with does not exist on the other specification. Otherwise, resit the specification they know.

faqs.question: Do resit lessons happen at our villa in Khalifa City, or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a resit that matters in your favour, because the specialist pool stops being tutors who can reach Khalifa City through the evening traffic and becomes tutors who have taught and marked the exact specification your child is re-sitting. Screen sharing also means the marked paper and the question set sit in front of both of them in the same window.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the subject we need to resit?
faqs.answer: We tell you. For mainstream resit subjects in Abu Dhabi a specialist match usually takes two to four working days; for a narrow specification, a less-entered language or a creative subject with coursework it can take longer, and inside eight weeks of a series it takes longer again because specialists fill first. Where no UAE-based tutor covers the specification, the match may be a tutor elsewhere teaching into Gulf Standard Time, which for an online lesson changes the pool and not the lesson. We would rather decline a subject than put a generalist in front of a specification they have never marked.

abu-dhabi/igcse-resit-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the component marks, not the calendar
abu-dhabi/igcse-resit-tutor.closingBody: A resit is a solvable problem with a deadline attached, and the two things that decide it are which component lost the grade and how many weeks remain before the entry closes. Send the statement of results, the syllabus code and the target grade, and the first lesson is free with no card required. The tutor will finish it with a written statement of what cost the grade and an honest hour count for fixing it. If the target does not fit the series, we will say so and point you at the next one rather than sell you a plan that lands on the same grade twice. Lessons are one-to-one, online, and timed to your week in Abu Dhabi.

abu-dhabi/igcse-revision-classes.tutorsIntro: These tutors mark, date and return every piece of timed work, then open the next session with the script rather than with a conversation. The point of a revision class at IGCSE is to make progress visible on paper, which is the one thing a parent can actually check.

intro.heading: How to tell whether IGCSE revision is working
paragraphs: Most parents judge revision by atmosphere. The student seems more settled, the tutor sounds confident, the weekly message says good progress. None of that is evidence, and in a nine-month IGCSE run it is possible to spend a great deal of money on an atmosphere. The evidence is a stack of marked papers with dates on them, and this page is about reading that stack.

Start with the right unit of measurement. An IGCSE grade is built from separate papers with separate weightings, so an overall percentage hides the thing you need to see. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 has different papers at Core and Extended tier. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 has a theory paper, a multiple-choice paper and a practical component. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1 with its own paper structure. A student can hold a steady overall mark for six weeks while one component quietly collapses and another improves, and that is invisible unless somebody records the components separately.

So the first thing a revision class should produce is a table, not a report. Date, paper, component, raw mark, available mark, and the error category. Error category is the part almost nobody keeps, and it is the most useful column: knowledge gap, method error, command-term misread, arithmetic slip, or ran out of time. Four weeks of that column tells you whether the tutoring is addressing the actual failure mode or teaching content the student already had.

What movement looks like is worth being concrete about, because expectations drive bad decisions. A genuine four-week movement on a single component is a few marks, repeated across two different papers of the same format, with the dominant error category changing. A single good score is noise; students have good days. A flat four weeks with the same dominant error every time is not a reason for more hours, it is a reason to change what the hours contain, and sometimes to change the tutor. We would rather say that than sell a fifth month.

There is one prerequisite to all of this that costs nothing and gets skipped constantly. Before any script is worth marking, confirm the board, the specification code and the tier for each subject in writing, and confirm the series and the Cambridge administrative zone with your school's exams officer. A student revising Extended-tier papers who is entered at Core tier is producing marks that describe a paper they will never sit, and the family will spend four months reading a record that cannot mean anything. Ten minutes of paperwork makes the next four months of evidence interpretable.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE revision to Abu Dhabi families as one-to-one online tuition on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only. For evidence-led revision the online format helps directly, because scripts are shared, annotated and stored rather than left in a folder in a bag, and a parent can look at week two next to week nine without organising anything.

abu-dhabi/igcse-revision-classes.programmesIntro: IGCSE revision in Abu Dhabi spans two boards and two tiers, and the evidence you collect differs across them. Here is what is actually being revised in each case.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Individually certificated subjects assessed by externally marked papers, with many subjects tiered into Core and Extended. Mathematics is 0580, Physics 0625, and the syllabus code matters because the paper structure and the grade ceiling follow the tier rather than the subject. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For an Abu Dhabi family this is a five-minute check with the exams officer and the single highest-consequence item in the whole revision plan.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board widely taught in the emirate, with its own specification codes such as 4MA1 for International GCSE Mathematics A. Pearson exams are available in May and June and again in November each year, and some specifications are structured differently from the Cambridge equivalent, which changes what revision has to rehearse.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's dated calendar is useful precisely because it is published: the November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official PDF.

programmes.name: Core and Extended tiering
programmes.description: Not a board but the decision that shapes the evidence. Core tier covers less content and caps the attainable grade; Extended covers more and opens the top grades. A revision plan built on the wrong assumption about tier is revising the wrong papers, and the mark evidence will look inexplicable until somebody checks.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools make tier decisions at different points in Year 10 and sometimes revisit them in Year 11. Ask which tier your child is entered for, in writing, and ask when the entry becomes final. The answer determines which past papers the revision should be using and therefore whether the marked evidence means anything at all.

programmes.name: Private candidate entry
programmes.description: Where a student is not entered through a school, entry goes through a centre that accepts external candidates, and some subjects are harder to sit privately because of coursework or practical components. The revision evidence is the same; the administration is not, and the deadlines sit months before the papers.
programmes.countryNote: This matters in Abu Dhabi for students between schools, students schooling at home, and students adding a subject their school does not offer. Identify the accepting centre before building a revision plan, because a well-revised candidate with no entry has nothing to sit.

abu-dhabi/igcse-revision-classes.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families most often book revision in, with the component the marked evidence usually indicts.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Marks leak through method omission rather than wrong answers. The error column fills with method error and arithmetic slip, and both are drillable. Extended-tier candidates lose most in the later algebra and trigonometry questions where working is not shown.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The practical component and the extended-response questions produce the most recoverable marks. Students give correct conclusions without the reasoning step the mark scheme requires, which is a writing fault rather than a physics one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic naming dominate the error log. Multi-step calculations lose a mark early and then propagate, so the useful evidence is which step failed rather than whether the final answer was right.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume with command-term precision on top. Marked scripts show full knowledge expressed in the wrong verb, which scores nothing. The error category here is almost always command-term misread.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading-paper marks are won by selecting evidence precisely and lost by summarising. Writing-paper marks move with structure and register. Both are measurable week to week once the marking is done against the criteria rather than impressionistically.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Textual detail under timing is the whole game. The evidence to watch is quotation accuracy and the number of distinct points made, both countable, both improvable in four weeks.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-application marks separate the grades. Students define a term and then do not apply it to the stimulus, which caps answers in the knowledge bands. The error log shows this as a method error, not a gap.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram marks are the cheapest in the paper and the most frequently dropped, usually through unlabelled axes or a missing equilibrium point. Measurable within two weeks because the fix is mechanical.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger candidates and still the subject where timing fails most often. The evidence to collect is how many questions were reached, not just how many were right.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Productive skills decide the grade while receptive practice dominates most revision. Marked writing in the required text types, corrected at sentence level, is the only evidence that moves here.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode convention accuracy and the theory paper's extended answers. Students who code well in a real language still lose convention marks, which the error log exposes immediately.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Named case studies with figures and dates, plus skills questions on maps and graphs. The skills questions are the quickest measurable gain because they are pattern-based.

abu-dhabi/igcse-revision-classes.regionsIntro: Where you live in the emirate changes what evidence you can realistically collect, because it changes how many sessions fit in a week and when the student is still awake enough to sit a timed paper.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi Island
regions.note: Short school runs mean a 16:30 start works, so a timed paper can be sat at home on a weekday rather than only at weekends. That makes weekly evidence collection genuinely sustainable here.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A 20-40 minute commute from the island schools pushes weekday starts to 17:30 or later. Most families here sit the timed paper on a Friday or Saturday morning instead, which works as long as it is actually timed.

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Students are typically home by 15:45, the earliest in the emirate, which allows a session and a separate timed paper in the same week without either being squeezed.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools with shorter results histories, so school-side mock evidence is sometimes thinner. Families here often rely more on tutor-marked papers to see where a student stands.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Long mainland commutes compress the evening. Weekend timed papers are the norm, and during Ramadan the whole pattern moves post-Iftar, which is workable if agreed in advance.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Ninety minutes inland under the same regulator, with few resident IGCSE specialists in the sciences. Online delivery is how an Al Ain family gets a 0625 Physics specialist rather than a general science tutor.

sections.heading: The evidence table a revision class should hand you
paragraphs: A revision class should produce a running record you can read without the tutor present. Date, paper and component, raw mark out of the available mark, and the dominant error category. That is five columns and it takes two minutes to update after each marked piece. No competitor page researched for this project publishes anything like it, and it is the single most useful artefact in the whole arrangement.

The error category column is what makes the record diagnostic rather than decorative. Five categories cover almost everything at IGCSE: knowledge gap, where the content was never learned; method error, where the approach was wrong or working was not shown; command-term misread, where the student answered a different question; arithmetic or transcription slip; and timing, where questions were not reached. Each one implies a different intervention, and only the first is fixed by teaching more content.

Read the record by looking for a change in the dominant category rather than a rise in the mark. A student whose scripts move from knowledge gap to timing has made real progress even if the total has not moved yet, because timing is the last fault to fall and the quickest to fix once the content is secure. A student whose scripts show command-term misread in weeks one, three, five and seven has not been taught the fix, and more hours of the same will not deliver it.

The table below shows what a readable four-week record looks like. It is an illustrative record of the kind a revision class should produce, not a published result: we do not publish student outcome statistics on these pages, because any statistic without the number of students, the date and the method behind it is a claim rather than evidence, and this market is full of those.

sections.heading: Why component scores beat an overall percentage
paragraphs: An IGCSE subject grade is assembled from papers with different weightings, and that assembly is where the useful information lives. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 separates theory, multiple-choice and practical work. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 has a different paper structure at Core tier than at Extended. Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A, specification 4MA1, has its own arrangement again. An overall percentage averages all of that into a number that cannot tell you where to spend the next ten hours.

The practical consequence appears in week six of most revision plans. A student holds a steady total for a month and the family concludes nothing is happening, when in fact one component has improved by a useful margin and another has fallen, and the two cancel. Or the reverse: the total rises while the weakest component stays exactly where it was, because the student is getting better at the paper they were already good at. Neither is visible without separate component records, and both change what the tutoring should do next.

This is also how you decide whether a revision class is worth continuing. If the component you bought the class to fix has not moved across four separately marked attempts at the same format, the class is not working on that component, and the right conversation is about content and approach rather than about more hours. We will raise it rather than wait for the family to notice, because a tutoring plan that quietly does not work is the most expensive thing in this market.

One qualification. Comparing a mark on a Paper 2 to a mark on a Paper 4 tells you very little, and comparing across boards tells you less. Evidence only works when the format is held constant deliberately. That is why the sequence above repeats the same paper type: the point of a second attempt at the same format is to make the first one interpretable.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE IGCSE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May and June and again in November each year. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only and is not a route available to a candidate sitting in this emirate, which matters because advice written for an Indian audience circulates widely here.

Cambridge adds a logistical trap worth the five minutes it takes to close. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and it says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and work only from that version. This is the highest-consequence item on the entire revision plan and it costs nothing.

Pearson's published dates show why entry deadlines sit so far ahead of the papers. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; the November 2025 results landed with students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so the right habit is to work from the live official PDF rather than from any restatement, including this one.

Build the revision record against the series rather than the calendar month. Sixteen weeks out is topic repair, twelve weeks out is component technique on the weakest paper, eight weeks out is full papers under conditions, and the final fortnight is error-pattern drilling and logistics with nothing new introduced. Write the known losses in first: travel, Ramadan timing, and the school's own mock weeks, which will take time out of the plan whether you plan for them or not.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, and why the revision differs
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi schools use both boards, and some families have children on different boards in the same house. The subject names look identical and the papers are not, so revision material has to match the specification your child is actually entered for. Using Cambridge 0580 past papers to revise for Pearson 4MA1 produces practice that is useful in content and misleading in format, and format is half of what a revision class is selling.

The first thing to establish is the specification code, not the subject name. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics is 0580 and Physics is 0625; Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1. Those codes appear on the school's entry paperwork and on the exam timetable, and they determine which past papers, mark schemes and examiner reports are relevant. Exactly one syllabus code appeared across an entire cluster of researched competitor pages, which tells you how rarely this gets checked.

The structural differences show up in the evidence. Where a specification is modular, a student may sit components at different points, which changes what a mark in February actually represents. Where a subject is tiered into Core and Extended, the grade ceiling differs and so do the papers, so a strong Core mark and a weak Extended mark can describe the same performance. And where a science has a practical component or an alternative written paper in its place, revision for that component is a specific skill rather than general subject knowledge.

Practically: ask the school for the board, the specification code and the tier for every subject in the revision plan, in writing, and ask when entries become final. Then check that the past papers in use match all three. It is a ten-minute task that decides whether every marked script you collect for the next four months means anything. We do not supply or reproduce papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents; we cite them and link to the board's official page, which is lawful and keeps the student on the current version.

sections.heading: What a four-week movement actually looks like
paragraphs: Expectations drive decisions, so it is worth being concrete about the size and shape of real progress. A genuine four-week movement on one component is a measurable rise across two separately marked attempts at the same paper format, with the dominant error category changing between them. One good score is not a movement; students have good days and bad papers, and a single data point cannot distinguish between the two.

The sequence that recurs in marked scripts goes knowledge gap, then method error, then timing, then slips. That order is not arbitrary. A student cannot show method until the content is there, cannot run out of time until they are attempting everything, and cannot be undone by arithmetic until the method is sound. So a record that walks down that list in four weeks is working even if the raw mark has moved modestly, and a record where the dominant category never changes is not working regardless of what the raw mark does.

This is also how to decide about changing tutor, which parents are often reluctant to raise. If the component you bought the sessions to fix shows the same dominant error at weeks one, three, five and seven, the issue is the content of the sessions, not their quantity. Adding a second weekly session to a plan that is not addressing the fault doubles the cost of not addressing it. Ask what specifically will be different next week, and ask it as a question about the error category.

We publish no success statistics on these pages, and the absence is deliberate. A percentage without the number of students behind it, the date, and the method by which it was calculated is a marketing claim, and several providers in this market publish exactly that, sometimes contradicting themselves within one page. What we will commit to is the record: dated scripts, separated components, a named error category each time, and an honest reading of the trend including when it says stop.

sections.heading: What IGCSE revision costs in Abu Dhabi, and what the evidence is worth
paragraphs: Rates first, briefly, because the evidence argument only matters once the price is known. Published UAE market figures as read in October 2026 put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 33-65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65; qualified subject tutors online at roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150; and specialists at roughly AED 200-450 and above. In-home one-to-one in the UAE runs roughly AED 180-500 including travel. Those are other providers' published rates, not an IB Gram price list.

What the marking is worth is the part nobody prices. A ninety-minute session with a full paper marked against the scheme and returned with an error category involves real work outside the lesson, and it is in the rate whether anyone itemises it or not. A cheaper arrangement where scripts are self-marked against a downloaded scheme is a legitimate product and a different one: it gives the student a score and tells nobody why the marks went. If a quote is at the bottom of the band, ask who marks the work, and the answer usually explains the price.

The cheapest sensible first purchase is a diagnostic block: three sessions, three marked papers across different components, and a written error analysis, with no obligation beyond that. At the qualified-tutor band that is roughly AED 675-1,350 for four and a half hours. It frequently shows that less tutoring is needed than the family assumed, or that the problem sits in one component rather than one subject, which is the difference between a four-session purchase and a four-month one.

For context on where this sits in a household's education spend, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. Abu Dhabi fee regulation sits with ADEK and works separately, but the household shape is the same: fees are fixed, tutoring is variable, and the variable cost is the one worth scoping tightly to a named component with a record attached.

sections.heading: Online delivery, and the honest case for it on evidence grounds
paragraphs: Parents searching for revision classes in Abu Dhabi usually picture a classroom or a tutor at the table, so it is worth answering that directly. In-home tutoring is a substantial market here with published prices of roughly AED 180-500 an hour, most of the premium over online being travel. Tuition centres run group classes on a fixed timetable, and the family does the driving twice per session. Both exist and both work for some students.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Revision for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. The evidence argument for that is specific rather than general. Scripts annotated on a shared screen are stored and timestamped, so week two sits next to week nine without anyone keeping a folder. The error log lives in one place both the tutor and the parent can open. And sessions do not disappear because of traffic on the Sheikh Zayed bridge or a sandstorm, which matters when the whole method depends on weekly continuity.

The second argument is about who teaches. A 0625 Physics specialist who has marked hundreds of practical-component answers is findable online and often is not findable within a drive of Al Shamkha or Al Ain. For evidence-led revision this is the whole point: the error category only becomes useful if somebody can read it precisely, and reading an error log in Cambridge Physics is a specialist act, not a general teaching one.

One in-home advantage deserves naming rather than ignoring. A student who will not start work without a person physically present sometimes performs better with a local tutor regardless of that tutor's subject depth. If that describes your child, say so at the outset. The honest answer may be a local presence for accountability plus a short online component block with a specialist, which costs less than buying either at full length and produces better evidence than buying neither.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: A parent can check whether a tutor is permitted to work, and it is worth doing. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two implications follow. The permit is free, so a provider citing permit costs as a rate driver is inventing one. And no fine schedule is published for tutoring without a permit, so no amount should be quoted to you; the ministry did not specify fine amounts, as reported in the press, and a figure circulating as a maximum could not be verified, so it is left out of this page on purpose.

On the school side, private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and inspected by ADEK, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project. It regulates schools, publishes inspection ratings, and approves no individual tutor. A tuition business with premises and staff is a separate matter again: in Dubai that requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal.

One boundary before you book. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct makes the same point. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, but do not plan around hiring your child's own subject teacher. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, MoE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership, and claims none.
