faqs.question: How do I know whether my child's IGCSE revision classes are actually working?
faqs.answer: Ask for the record rather than the impression. You want dated scripts showing the paper and component, the raw mark against the available mark, and a named error category for each piece. Progress shows as a rise across two separately marked attempts at the same paper format, with the dominant error changing between them. One good score is not progress; students have good days. If the same dominant error appears at weeks one, three, five and seven, the sessions are not addressing the fault and adding hours will not change that.

faqs.question: What error categories should a tutor be recording on my child's IGCSE papers?
faqs.answer: Five cover almost everything at this level. Knowledge gap, where the content was never learned. Method error, where the approach was wrong or working was not shown. Command-term misread, where the student answered a different question from the one asked. Arithmetic or transcription slip. And timing, where questions were not reached at all. Each implies a different intervention, and only the first is solved by teaching more content. The useful signal over four weeks is which category dominates and whether it changes, because that tells you more than the raw mark does.

faqs.question: Why does the tutor keep setting the same IGCSE paper format every week?
faqs.answer: Because a second attempt at the same format is what makes the first one interpretable. A mark on a Paper 2 and a mark on a Paper 4 are not comparable, and a mark on a Cambridge paper is not comparable to one on a Pearson paper, so switching format each week produces data that cannot show a trend. Holding the format constant for three or four attempts lets you see whether the component actually moved. Once it has, the format changes deliberately, to check whether the improvement transfers rather than being specific to one paper.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series do students in Abu Dhabi sit?
faqs.answer: The June series and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in June and November, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May and June and again in November. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so advice written for an Indian audience about a spring sitting does not apply to a candidate entered in this emirate. Confirm your dates against the live official timetable rather than any restatement of it.

faqs.question: What is the Cambridge zone timetable and why does it matter for my child?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in, then work only from that version and discard any other. It is the highest-consequence item in a revision plan, it costs nothing to check, and almost no tutoring page in this market mentions it.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child is on Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel for revision?
faqs.answer: It matters more than the subject name does. The specifications differ in paper structure, question style and sometimes in assessment pattern, so Cambridge 0580 past papers are useful content practice and misleading format practice for a Pearson 4MA1 candidate. Get the board, the specification code and the tier in writing from the school for every subject in the plan, then check that the past papers in use match all three. Exactly one syllabus code appeared across an entire cluster of competitor pages researched for this project, which suggests this check is rarely made.

faqs.question: How much does a marked IGCSE paper add to the cost of a revision class?
faqs.answer: It is inside the rate rather than itemised, and it is a real part of what separates the bands. A ninety-minute session plus a full paper marked against the scheme and returned with an error category involves substantial work outside the lesson. Published UAE rates run roughly AED 33-65 an hour at the budget end, where scripts are usually self-marked, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor who marks them, and AED 200-450 and above for specialists. If a quote sits at the bottom of the band, ask who marks the timed work; the answer normally explains the price.

faqs.question: Can a three-session diagnostic block really tell us anything useful?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the three papers cover different components rather than repeating one. Three marked scripts and a written error analysis establish which component is actually weak, which error category dominates, and whether the problem is one paper or the whole subject. That frequently narrows a planned four-month purchase to a four-session one, or occasionally shows the opposite. At the qualified-tutor band it costs roughly AED 675-1,350 for four and a half hours, which is the cheapest way to avoid committing a term's budget on an assumption.

faqs.question: My child scores well in school tests but badly in timed IGCSE papers. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Usually that the content is there and the execution is not, which is the easier problem of the two and the one timed practice fixes. School tests are often shorter, sometimes use familiar question wording, and rarely reproduce the full paper's time pressure. The evidence to collect is how many questions were reached, not just how many were right, because an unreached question and a wrong answer look identical in a total. If timing is the dominant category across three marked papers, the plan should be full papers under conditions rather than more teaching.

faqs.question: Is Core or Extended tier the right entry, and does revision change with it?
faqs.answer: The tier decides the content, the papers and the attainable grade ceiling, so it changes the revision entirely. A strong Core mark and a weak Extended mark can describe the same performance, and revising from the wrong tier's past papers makes every marked script uninterpretable. Ask the subject teacher which tier your child is entered for, in writing, and ask when the entry becomes final, because some Abu Dhabi schools revisit tier decisions during Year 11. Then check that the practice papers match. It is a ten-minute task with four months of consequences.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals handled if the revision is online?
faqs.answer: The practical component or its alternative written paper is a distinct skill with its own question patterns, and it is revisable in writing because that is how it is assessed. What a tutor works on is apparatus description, variable control, table and graph construction, uncertainty and the reasoning the mark scheme wants to see. The physical work itself happens in the school laboratory, under the school's arrangements, and no online session substitutes for it. Confirm with the science department which route your child's specification uses, because leaving that component unrevised is one of the commonest omissions.

faqs.question: Should we add a second weekly session if the marks are not moving?
faqs.answer: Not until you know why they are not moving. If the dominant error category has been identical across four marked attempts, doubling the sessions doubles the cost of not addressing the fault. The right question is what specifically will be different next week, asked as a question about the error category rather than about effort. Sometimes the answer is a different tutor, and we would rather say so than take a second booking. A second session genuinely helps where the record shows timing as the main fault, because that responds to volume of full timed practice.

faqs.question: Can my child revise two IGCSE subjects with one tutor to save money?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the shared error log is the reason it can work well. Two subjects on alternating weeks produces one data point per subject every fortnight rather than one a week, so trends take longer to read, but the log frequently reveals that one error category, usually command-term misreading or not showing method, is costing marks in both. Fixing it once helps twice. Where one subject has a genuine content gap and the other does not, splitting the plans is better, because alternating weeks is too slow to close a gap.

faqs.question: Do tutors running IGCSE revision in Abu Dhabi need a permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and, according to u.ae, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so no amount should be quoted to you. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in the emirate and approves no individual tutor.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram tell me what grade my child will get after a revision term?
faqs.answer: No, and no honest provider can. A revision plan changes what a student can retrieve under time, how accurately they read a command term and how they spend the minutes in a paper. It does not produce a predictable grade, and any page offering a guaranteed grade or a percentage improvement is either misunderstanding the assessment or hoping you will not check the arithmetic. We publish no outcome statistics at all, because a figure without the number of students, the date and the method behind it is a claim rather than evidence.

faqs.question: What should we do in the final fortnight before the papers?
faqs.answer: Stop adding content. The last two weeks are for error-pattern drilling on the categories the record identified, light retrieval, logistics and sleep. Confirm the correct zone timetable with the exams officer, check the equipment and the centre arrangements, and reduce session length rather than extending it. Introducing new topics in the final fortnight competes with consolidation and usually costs marks rather than earning them. If the record shows a knowledge gap still dominant at two weeks out, the honest move is to triage which topics are worth the remaining time.

abu-dhabi/igcse-revision-classes.closingHeading: Ask for the record, then decide
abu-dhabi/igcse-revision-classes.closingBody: If you are choosing IGCSE revision classes in Abu Dhabi, make the record the condition of the purchase. Get the board, specification code, tier, series and Cambridge zone in writing from the school. Then ask any provider for dated scripts with components separated and a named error category on each piece, and ask who marks the timed work. Start with a three-session diagnostic block rather than a term, because it often shows the problem is narrower than it looked. A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor comes first, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so you see the marking before you commit.

abu-dhabi/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.tutorsIntro: These tutors have taught both ends of this move, which is what makes the gap map possible. They know which IGCSE habits earn marks in Year 11 and cost marks in DP1, and a session is spent unlearning those rather than covering content again.

intro.heading: The gap is specific, so name it before buying anything
paragraphs: Most transition courses sold in this market are general: study skills, organisation, time management, a gentle introduction to the Diploma. Those are not useless and they are not the gap. The gap between a Year 11 IGCSE paper and a DP1 paper is specific, it is different in every subject, and it is almost entirely about what the question asks you to do rather than about what you know. A student can finish IGCSE with excellent grades and lose marks steadily for a whole term in DP1 without any content being missing.

Three things change at once. First, the command terms. IGCSE papers reward description and recall generously; Diploma papers reward analysis, evaluation and justification, and they allocate marks to the reasoning rather than to the conclusion. A student who writes a correct answer without the argument that earns the marks has produced exactly what IGCSE trained them to produce. Second, the length and shape of the expected answer. An IGCSE extended response and a Diploma extended response are different genres, and nobody tells students that.

Third, the internally assessed work arrives, and it arrives marked against named criteria with published allocations rather than against a teacher's judgement. Writing to a criterion on purpose is a learnable skill and it is not one IGCSE develops, because most IGCSE subjects have no coursework at all. Add Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which together feed up to three bonus points through a published matrix, and the first term of DP1 asks for several things the student has literally never been asked for.

There is a fourth change that is specifically an issue in this emirate. The Mathematics route decision, between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation and between Higher and Standard Level, is usually made on an overall IGCSE grade when it should be made on component evidence. A strong 0580 Extended grade earned on the questions a student always gets right, with the long multi-step questions at the end unattempted, points a different way from the same grade earned by working through them. That is a five-minute check with the component breakdown and it decides two years.

So the right shape for a transition course is a short, finite block aimed at named gaps, not a term-length programme. Six to ten sessions over the summer, each one spent on a specific thing the Diploma will ask for that IGCSE did not: criterion writing, command-term discipline in the subjects chosen, the particular calculation or argument style that the intended Higher Level courses demand. It ends. If it has not ended, it was not a transition course; it was the beginning of two years of tutoring sold under a different name.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online sessions on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only. For a transition block that matters practically, because the work is subject-specific and Abu Dhabi, with fewer IB World Schools than Dubai, has a thin resident pool in exactly the Higher Level subjects a student is about to start.

abu-dhabi/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.programmesIntro: This move spans two systems, and each side of it assesses differently. Here is what the student is leaving and what they are joining.

programmes.name: IGCSE, the starting point
programmes.description: Individually certificated subjects assessed by externally marked papers, with many subjects tiered into Core and Extended. Cambridge codes include 0580 for Mathematics and 0625 for Physics; Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics A is 4MA1. Most subjects have no coursework component, so a student arrives at the Diploma with two years of pure examination practice and no experience of criterion-marked submitted work.
programmes.countryNote: IGCSE is the dominant pre-16 route in Abu Dhabi's British-curriculum schools, which means the majority of the emirate's Diploma intake makes exactly this transition. Ask the school for component marks and the tier for each subject before DP1 starts, because that is the only evidence that tells you where the real gaps sit.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, the destination
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject grade combines externally marked papers with an internally assessed component marked against named criteria. The total runs to 45 including up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Higher Level courses carry roughly 240 recommended teaching hours against roughly 150 at Standard Level.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the available Diploma combination is constrained by each school's timetable blocks, and a smaller cohort means fewer parallel options in each subject group. Ask which Higher Level courses have actually run for two consecutive years, because a course in a booklet is not a course with a teacher and a cohort.

programmes.name: MYP, the alternative route in
programmes.description: The IB's own pre-Diploma programme, assessed against four criteria per subject on an eight-point scale, with the Personal Project in the final year. Students arriving in DP1 from MYP have criterion-writing experience that IGCSE students do not, and usually weaker timed-examination technique, which is the mirror image of the IGCSE profile.
programmes.countryNote: In a mixed DP1 class, which is the norm in this emirate, the teacher is managing both profiles at once. That is useful to know: the IGCSE student's first-term marks often dip relative to classmates for reasons that are entirely about criterion literacy and will correct, provided somebody names the cause rather than treating it as a slide.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: DP courses taken as individual certificates alongside a career-related study, Personal and Professional Skills, service learning and a reflective project. The certificates are graded 1 to 7 in the same way as Diploma subjects, so the same transition gaps apply to them.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing about at transition stage, because for a student whose IGCSE evidence does not support three Higher Levels this is an alternative rather than a failure. Provision is thinner in Abu Dhabi than full Diploma provision, so availability needs checking rather than assuming.

abu-dhabi/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.subjectsIntro: This is the actual gap in each subject: the IGCSE habit that stops working and what the Diploma asks for instead. These are the things a transition session should be spent on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The IGCSE habit that fails here is answer-hunting without written method. Diploma marking pays for the argument, and at Higher Level the extended investigative paper asks the student to follow an unfamiliar multi-step problem with no worked example in sight, which no IGCSE paper required.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The gap is verbal rather than numerical. A student trained to compute and stop must now justify a model choice and comment on its limitations in language the criteria reward. Marks are lost in the sentence after the correct calculation, which is a new experience.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: IGCSE rewarded recall of named processes; the Diploma asks why, and pays for the mechanism. Calculation chains get longer, so an early slip propagates further, and the internally assessed investigation introduces experimental design marked against criteria the student has never seen.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The mathematical load rises sharply and the extended-response genre changes. An IGCSE answer that stated the correct outcome scored; a Diploma answer must show each reasoning step, and students lose a term's marks before anyone explains that the steps are the marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume roughly doubles and command-term precision becomes decisive. Outline, explain, distinguish, evaluate and discuss all pay differently in Diploma marking, and an IGCSE-trained student answers all of them with description because description was usually enough.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Most students meet this subject for the first time at Diploma level, so the gap is not an IGCSE habit but the absence of any habit. Diagram conventions and evaluation structure have to be built from nothing, and at Higher Level the quantitative paper surprises those who chose it to avoid mathematics.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: IGCSE reading papers rewarded locating and summarising; the Diploma rewards analysing how a text works. The unseen-text paper needs a repeatable method, and students who were strong at IGCSE English frequently dip hardest here because the old method is actively in the way.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The gap is application. An IGCSE answer that defined a term correctly earned marks; a Diploma answer must apply the framework to the stimulus material, and definitions alone cap the answer in the knowledge bands no matter how accurate they are.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Narrative is replaced by argument and sourcework becomes central. Students arrive able to recount events accurately and unable to sustain a line of argument across an essay, and the reading volume at Higher Level is a genuine shock after IGCSE.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Another subject most students meet first at Diploma level. Study recall comes easily and evaluation does not, which holds answers in the middle bands. The gap is learning to critique methodology, which is a skill rather than a body of content.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: IGCSE language papers were heavily receptive; Diploma assessment weights production much more. The gap is extended writing in the required text types and the oral, both of which need marked practice corrected at sentence level rather than general conversation.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: The shift is from producing finished pieces to documenting sustained development and defending it. Students with strong IGCSE portfolios often arrive with no habit of recording process, which is exactly what the criteria reward.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi Island
regions.note: Several schools here run IGCSE to Year 11 and then a Diploma, so the transition happens inside one institution and the subject teachers already know the student's component profile.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: More families move school at this point, from a British-curriculum school to a Diploma provider, which adds an unfamiliar teaching style to the assessment change and makes the first term harder than it needs to be.

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Raha Beach

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Small cohorts mean a DP1 class may contain only a handful of former IGCSE students, so the criterion-literacy gap is less likely to be addressed as a group and more likely to need individual work.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer Diploma provision following established IGCSE provision, so ask how many years each Higher Level course has run before planning a combination around it.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Shamkha

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Students frequently change school to reach a Diploma provider, sometimes with a longer commute, and local Higher Level specialists are scarce, which makes a well-targeted summer block more valuable here than anywhere in the emirate.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Bateen
regions.note: Established districts where university prerequisites drive the Diploma combination, so the Mathematics route decision at transition carries more weight than general readiness.

sections.heading: The subject-by-subject gap map
paragraphs: A transition course that cannot show you its gap map is selling reassurance. The map below is the whole of the product: for each subject the student is taking, what an IGCSE paper rewarded, what the Diploma paper rewards instead, and what a session therefore does. One competitor in this market has a single subheading on the IGCSE-to-IB gap and nobody researched for this project has a structured subject-by-subject version, which is why the first term of DP1 catches so many well-prepared students.

Read it as a list of unlearning tasks rather than learning ones. Almost every entry describes a habit that earned marks in Year 11 and costs marks in Year 12. That is why a transition block is not content teaching: the content arrives in term one from the school, on time, taught by a specialist. What does not arrive is anyone explaining that the way the student has been writing answers for two years is now the thing holding the mark down.

The pattern across subjects is consistent enough to state as a rule. IGCSE asks what and the Diploma asks why and so what. Wherever a student's IGCSE answer would have been complete at the point of stating the correct fact, the Diploma answer has only just begun. In the sciences this appears as missing reasoning steps; in the humanities as description where evaluation was asked for; in mathematics as an answer without the method that carries the marks.

Use the map to choose the sessions rather than booking a generic block. A student taking Biology, Chemistry and Mathematics at Higher Level needs command-term work and calculation-chain work and almost no essay-structure work. A student taking History, English and Economics needs the opposite. Buying ten generic sessions when six targeted ones would do is the most common waste in this part of the market.

sections.heading: Command terms: where the first term's marks actually go
paragraphs: If a transition block does only one thing, it should be this. Diploma questions are built on command terms with defined expectations, and the marks are allocated to what the command term asks for. A student who answers a question beginning evaluate by producing an excellent explanation has written a good answer to a different question and will score in the lower bands with no content error anywhere in sight.

IGCSE uses command terms too, but the stakes are lower because a large share of IGCSE marks sit on recall and description, which are the terms students default to under pressure. In the Diploma the higher-tariff questions almost all require something beyond description, and the default therefore fails exactly where the marks are concentrated. This is the mechanical reason a strong IGCSE cohort dips in its first Diploma term, and it corrects quickly once somebody names it.

The work is simple and it is not quick. Take the student's actual subjects, list the command terms their papers use, and for each one write what the examiner is paying for and what a complete answer contains. Then practise them separately, marked, until the shape of each answer is automatic. Three sessions typically covers the terms across a whole subject combination, because the terms repeat across subjects far more than students realise.

One warning about how this is often taught. A generic list of command-term definitions copied from a document achieves nothing, because the student can already read definitions. What changes behaviour is marked practice: writing an evaluate answer, seeing it scored against the real allocation, and seeing where the marks were not available for the sentences they wrote. We use official command-term definitions by reference and link to the source rather than reproducing subject guides, which we do not distribute.
bullets: Marks are allocated to what the command term asks for, not to accuracy alone
Description is the default under pressure and the lowest-tariff response
List the terms used in the student's actual subjects, not a generic set
Practise each term separately with marked work, not definitions
Three sessions usually covers a whole subject combination

sections.heading: Criterion writing: the skill IGCSE never asked for
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component marked against named criteria with published mark allocations. Most IGCSE subjects have no coursework at all, so for the majority of Abu Dhabi students entering DP1 from a British-curriculum school, writing a piece of work deliberately designed to satisfy a lettered criterion is a completely new activity. It is also, per hour spent, among the highest-return things a transition block can teach.

The skill has three parts. Reading a criterion and identifying what evidence would satisfy it, which is harder than it sounds because criteria are written in assessment language rather than instruction language. Structuring a piece of work so each criterion is visibly addressed rather than incidentally touched. And self-marking a draft against the criteria before submission, which is the habit that separates students who improve their internally assessed marks from those who do not.

Taught against real criteria for the student's real subjects, a four to six session block transfers across all six subjects, because the underlying move is the same everywhere even though the criteria differ. That makes it the cheapest broad-spectrum intervention available at this stage. Taught in the abstract, as study skills, it achieves very little, which is why a generic transition course tends to produce a confident student with unchanged marks.

The boundary applies here with particular force, since internally assessed work is involved. A tutor may teach the criteria and what each one rewards, discuss whether a proposed research question is answerable within the word limit, read a draft the student has written and give feedback on structure, argument and the use of evidence, teach referencing, and mark practice work. A tutor may not write any part of the submitted work, supply text, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, choose the question outright or generate data. A breach is a malpractice finding against the student. There is a provider in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is an expulsion risk with a price attached rather than a service.
bullets: Most IGCSE subjects have no coursework, so criterion writing is new
Three parts: reading a criterion, structuring to it, self-marking against it
Taught on the student's real criteria it transfers across all six subjects
Taught as abstract study skills it changes nothing

sections.heading: Choosing the Mathematics route from IGCSE evidence
paragraphs: This is the one transition decision with consequences past the Diploma, because university courses state which Mathematics route and level they require and the courses are not interchangeable. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented with a no-calculator paper. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-led with technology permitted throughout and a heavier interpretive and statistical emphasis. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, so the real decision has four possible answers.

The evidence to use is the IGCSE component breakdown, not the grade. Within a strong Cambridge 0580 Extended grade, or a strong Pearson 4MA1 performance, there are two very different profiles: the student who worked through the long multi-step questions at the end of the paper, and the student who banked the reliable marks and left those questions blank. The grade is the same. Readiness for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is not. Ask the school for the breakdown and read which questions were attempted.

Students and parents routinely treat Applications and Interpretation as the easier route. It is not easier, it is differently hard, and the marks there are lost in words rather than in algebra: an unjustified model, or a statistical result described in language the criteria do not reward. A strong writer with weak algebraic instinct often does better on that route and a strong algebraist who writes reluctantly often does worse, which makes this a question about the student rather than about difficulty.

Check prerequisites separately and at source. Requirements differ between courses at the same institution, change between admissions cycles, and are sometimes expressed as preferences rather than conditions. Read each institution's own published requirement for the specific course, record the date, and recheck before applying. Nothing on this page should be treated as the source of record for any university's requirements, and no part of this is a prediction about an admission outcome.

sections.heading: What else arrives in term one: TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS
paragraphs: Beyond the six subjects, the Diploma adds three strands that have no IGCSE equivalent at all. Theory of Knowledge is a course about knowledge itself, assessed by an exhibition and an essay. The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece of research in a subject. CAS is a sustained commitment outside the classroom. The first two feed up to three bonus points through a published matrix, which means they affect the final total directly.

The transition problem is not that these are hard. It is that they are unfamiliar in kind. A student who has spent two years preparing for examinations has no experience of a long independent project with distant deadlines and no weekly test to measure progress against, and the first thing to go wrong is sequencing: the Extended Essay feels remote until it collides with internal assessment deadlines in the second year, which in most schools cluster because the school works backwards from the same submission dates for everyone.

What a transition block can usefully do here is small and specific. Explain the bonus-point matrix so the student understands that these components carry real marks. Teach what the criteria reward, in the same way as for any internally assessed work. And help place the Extended Essay in a subject that is not already one of the three heaviest, which is a scheduling decision made in the first term that saves a great deal of difficulty in the fourth.

What a transition block should not do is start the Extended Essay. The school supervises it, the school sets the internal deadlines, and the research question must be the student's own. A tutor who proposes the question or drafts the opening has crossed a line that puts the student's Diploma at risk, and families should be wary of any transition course that advertises getting a head start on the Extended Essay as a feature.

sections.heading: What the block costs, and when a shorter one is enough
paragraphs: A targeted transition block is six to ten sessions, which is nine to fifteen hours. Published UAE market rates as read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and IB specialists at roughly AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate at 200-450 for specialist work. Budget online rates run roughly AED 33-65, with Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65. Those are other providers' published figures, not an IB Gram price list.

At the qualified band, nine to fifteen hours is roughly AED 1,350-4,500. That is the whole intervention, and it is the right size of spend for this problem. Compare it with the alternative, which is not zero: a transition gap left unnamed typically turns into a weekly session through DP1 and often through DP2, which is roughly seventy hours over two years and a five-figure AED commitment. The transition block is cheap precisely because it is aimed at a cause rather than at a symptom.

A shorter block is often enough and we will say so. Where the student's IGCSE component evidence is strong across the board and the chosen subjects are ones they have studied before, four sessions on command terms and criterion writing covers most of the real gap. The students who need the full ten are those taking two or three subjects new to them at Higher Level, or those whose component evidence shows a specific weakness that the chosen Higher Level will expose immediately.

One thing worth checking before buying anything, because it is free. Many Abu Dhabi schools run their own bridging or induction programme between IGCSE and DP1, sometimes in the summer and sometimes in the first weeks of term. Ask the coordinator what it covers. Where it already covers criterion writing and command terms properly, a paid block should be narrowed to the subject-specific gaps rather than repeating what the school is doing inside fees you are already paying.

sections.heading: Timing it around the UAE summer and the school year
paragraphs: The window for this block is narrow and it collides with the one period Abu Dhabi families are most likely to be away. IGCSE results arrive in August for the June series, with Pearson's June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and DP1 typically begins shortly afterwards. That leaves a few weeks, inside which many households are travelling.

Online delivery is what makes the block possible at all in that window, and this is a practical point rather than a sales one. Sessions run from wherever the family is, allowing for the time difference, so a block can proceed from Kerala, Kent or Jordan as readily as from Al Bateen. An arrangement that depends on somebody driving to a villa in Khalifa City simply cannot happen in August, which is why most transition support in this emirate ends up squeezed into September when the student is already in lessons.

A second timing option is worth considering and rarely offered: start before the results. The gap map does not depend on the IGCSE grades, because it depends on the component profile from mock papers and on the subject combination, both of which are known in June. A student who does the command-term and criterion work in June and July arrives in DP1 with the habit already forming, and the results, when they come, only refine which subject-specific sessions are needed.

Where Ramadan falls in the first Diploma term, as it does in some years, the pattern shifts rather than pauses. School days shorten, the household reorganises around Iftar, and the productive study window for many students moves to after the evening meal. That matters more in DP1 than in Year 11, because Diploma content arrives continuously rather than in revision blocks, and a month of missed consolidation in term one is visible in the mocks.

Online sessions run from wherever the family is spending the summer

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work with a checkable permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system, with no listed fee.

Two consequences for a parent buying a summer block. The permit is free, so a provider citing permit costs as a rate driver is inventing a cost. And no fine schedule is published for tutoring without a permit, so no figure should be quoted to you; press reporting states the ministry did not specify fine amounts, and a number circulating as a maximum could not be verified, which is why none appears here.

On the school side, private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and inspected by ADEK, described on u.ae as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK publishes inspection ratings and regulates schools; it approves no tutor and sets no tutoring rate. Dubai's regulator is KHDA, Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has a Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A tuition business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing and not something a tutoring platform holds by default.

One boundary that applies to summer blocks in particular. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct making the same point. A summer block with the teacher who is about to teach your child in DP1 is exactly the arrangement to avoid. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership and claims none.

process.title: Get the component breakdown
process.description: Ask the school for IGCSE component marks and the tier for each subject, plus the confirmed Diploma subject and level choices. The gap map is built from those two documents, and without them a transition block is generic by necessity.

process.title: Ask what the school already runs
process.description: Many Abu Dhabi schools run a bridging or induction programme between IGCSE and DP1. Find out what it covers before buying anything, so a paid block is narrowed to the gaps the school is not already closing inside fees you pay.

process.title: Agree the gap list in writing
process.description: We name the specific gaps, one per session, before the block starts: which command terms, which criteria, which calculation or argument style. If a provider cannot give you that list, the block will be general and the marks will not move.

process.title: Free trial lesson
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor on the first named gap, at no charge, with marked work in it rather than discussion. You see the teaching and the marking before committing. If the match is wrong we offer a different tutor.

process.title: Run the block and stop
process.description: Six to ten sessions, each producing marked work, ending before DP1 begins. The block has a stated end point and we hold to it, because a transition course that rolls into weekly tutoring was never a transition course.

process.title: Review in week four of DP1
process.description: A short look at the school's own marked work four weeks in, which tells you whether the gap closed and whether any level decision needs revisiting while the school's change window is still open. No ongoing commitment attaches to it.

whyPoints.title: A gap map, not study skills
whyPoints.description: The block names which IGCSE habit is costing marks in which Diploma subject, and spends each session on one of them. One competitor has a single subheading on this gap and none researched has a structured subject-by-subject version.

whyPoints.title: Command terms taught by marked practice
whyPoints.description: A list of definitions achieves nothing, because the student can already read definitions. What changes behaviour is writing an evaluate answer, seeing it scored against the real allocation, and seeing where no marks were available for what they wrote.

whyPoints.title: Criterion writing transfers to all six subjects
whyPoints.description: Most IGCSE subjects have no coursework, so writing deliberately to a lettered criterion is new. Taught on the student's real criteria, one short block serves every subject, which makes it the cheapest broad intervention at this stage.

whyPoints.title: The maths route read from components
whyPoints.description: Two students with the same strong 0580 Extended grade can have opposite readiness for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and only the component breakdown shows which is which. That five-minute check decides two years.

whyPoints.title: It ends
whyPoints.description: Six to ten sessions with a stated finish before DP1 starts. A transition block that becomes a weekly commitment was sold as something it is not, and the alternative cost, roughly seventy hours across two years, is published on this page for comparison.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be shown
whyPoints.description: No guaranteed grade or points total, no statistic without its sample size, date and method, and no reproduction of IB, Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes or subject guides. Official sources are cited and linked instead.

faqs.question: What exactly does an IGCSE to IB transition course cover?
faqs.answer: In a useful version, three things. Command-term discipline, because Diploma marks are allocated to what the command term asks for and IGCSE trained the student to describe. Criterion writing, because most IGCSE subjects have no coursework and every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component marked against named criteria. And subject-specific gaps drawn from the student's own component breakdown. What it should not cover is general study skills or getting ahead on content, because the school teaches the content on time and getting ahead is usually wasted effort.

faqs.question: Why do strong IGCSE students lose marks in their first Diploma term?
faqs.answer: Because the habit that earned the IGCSE grade is now the thing capping the mark. IGCSE papers reward recall and description generously; Diploma papers allocate marks to analysis, evaluation and justification, and pay for the reasoning rather than the conclusion. A student who writes a correct answer and stops has produced exactly what two years of training produced, and it scores in the lower bands with no content error anywhere. Once somebody names the cause, it corrects quickly, which is why the dip is usually temporary and the panic usually unnecessary.

faqs.question: How long should a transition block be before DP1 starts?
faqs.answer: Six to ten sessions for most students, which is nine to fifteen hours, with a stated finish before term begins. Four sessions is often enough where the student's IGCSE component evidence is strong and the chosen subjects are familiar: three on command terms and one on criterion writing covers a surprising amount. The students who need the full ten are those taking two or three subjects new to them at Higher Level, or whose component evidence shows a specific weakness that the chosen Higher Level will expose in the first month.

faqs.question: Is it better to do the transition work before or after IGCSE results?
faqs.answer: Before, for most of it, which is the opposite of what families assume. The command-term and criterion work does not depend on the grades at all; it depends on the subject combination and the mock component profile, both known in June. Doing it in June and July means the habit is already forming when DP1 starts, and the results, when they arrive in August, only refine which subject-specific sessions are still needed. It also avoids squeezing the whole block into the two or three weeks when most households are travelling.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE habit causes the most trouble in IB Biology and Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Answering every command term with description. In Biology especially, outline, explain, distinguish, evaluate and discuss each pay differently in Diploma marking, and an IGCSE-trained student answers all of them the same way because description was usually sufficient. In Chemistry the companion problem is stating what happens without the mechanism, and longer calculation chains where an early slip propagates further than it did at IGCSE. Both are trainable in a handful of marked sessions, and both are invisible on a report that simply says the student needs more detail.

faqs.question: How do we decide between Maths AA and AI coming out of IGCSE?
faqs.answer: From the component breakdown, not the grade. Inside a strong Cambridge 0580 Extended grade sit two very different students: one who worked through the long multi-step questions at the end of the paper, and one who banked the reliable marks and left them blank. Their readiness for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is not comparable even though the grade is. Ask the school which questions were attempted, then test both routes on genuine material in one session. Check published course requirements separately, at each institution's own page, and record the date.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation the easier option after IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No, it is differently hard, and treating it as the soft route is the commonest error in this transition. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented with a no-calculator paper, so the marks go on algebraic accuracy. Applications and Interpretation permits technology throughout, and the marks go on justifying a model and describing a result in language the criteria reward, which is a writing demand. A strong writer with weak algebraic instinct usually does better on the applications route; a strong algebraist who writes reluctantly usually does worse.

faqs.question: What is criterion writing and why does it matter so much in DP1?
faqs.answer: It is writing a piece of work deliberately structured so that each lettered criterion is visibly satisfied, rather than hoping a good piece of work happens to meet them. Every Diploma subject has an internally assessed component marked this way, with published mark allocations, and most IGCSE subjects have no coursework at all, so the activity is genuinely new. Taught against the real criteria of the student's actual subjects, a four to six session block transfers to all six subjects, which makes it the highest-return work available at this stage.

faqs.question: Can a transition tutor help my child start the Extended Essay early?
faqs.answer: A tutor can explain the bonus-point matrix, teach what the criteria reward, discuss whether a proposed research question is answerable within the word limit, and help think about which subject the essay should sit in, which is a useful scheduling decision. A tutor may not propose the research question, draft any part of the essay, supply text or rewrite a paragraph into its final form. The school supervises the Extended Essay and sets its internal deadlines. Be wary of any transition course advertising a head start on the Extended Essay as a feature.

faqs.question: Does the school already run an IGCSE to IB bridging programme?
faqs.answer: Many Abu Dhabi schools do, either in the summer or in the first weeks of term, and it is inside fees you are already paying, so ask the coordinator what it covers before buying anything. Where the school's programme handles command terms and criterion writing properly, a paid block should be narrowed to the subject-specific gaps your child's component breakdown shows. Where it is a social induction rather than an academic one, which is also common, the academic gap remains open and a short targeted block is worth the money.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE to IB transition block cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Six to ten sessions is nine to fifteen hours, which at the published UAE qualified-tutor band of AED 150-300 an hour is roughly AED 1,350-4,500, and more at specialist rates of AED 200-450 and above. Those bands come from Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate as read in October 2026 and are market figures rather than an IB Gram price list. Set it against the alternative: an unnamed gap that becomes weekly tutoring through both Diploma years is roughly seventy hours and a five-figure AED commitment.

faqs.question: My child is taking Economics and Psychology for the first time. Does that change the block?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually lengthens it. Where a subject is new at Diploma level there is no IGCSE habit to unlearn, but there is also no foundation: diagram conventions in Economics and methodological critique in Psychology have to be built from nothing, and at Higher Level Economics adds a quantitative paper that surprises students who chose it to avoid mathematics. Two or three new subjects at Higher Level is the profile that genuinely needs the full ten sessions rather than four, and the sessions should be subject-specific rather than generic.

faqs.question: Will the transition block continue into the first Diploma term?
faqs.answer: Not by default, and we would rather it did not. The block has a stated end point before DP1 begins, and a transition course that rolls into a weekly commitment was sold as something it is not. What we do offer is a short review four weeks into DP1, using the school's own marked work, to see whether the gap closed and whether any level decision needs revisiting while the school's change window is still open. Ongoing support follows only where that marked evidence calls for it.

faqs.question: Can sessions run while we are travelling in August?
faqs.answer: Yes, allowing for the time difference, and it is the practical reason online delivery suits this window. IGCSE results arrive in August and DP1 begins shortly after, which leaves a few weeks that overlap with peak travel for Abu Dhabi families. Sessions run from wherever you are spending the summer. An arrangement depending on someone driving to a villa in Khalifa City cannot happen in August at all, which is why most transition support in this emirate ends up compressed into September once the student is already in lessons.

faqs.question: Do tutors running a transition block in Abu Dhabi need a permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and, according to u.ae, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so no amount should be quoted to you. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in the emirate and approves no individual tutor.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee my child will settle into the Diploma after this block?
faqs.answer: No. A transition block closes named gaps and produces marked evidence that they closed; it does not guarantee a grade, a points total or an easy first term, and no honest provider offers that. What makes the block worth buying is that it addresses a cause rather than a symptom, with a list of gaps agreed in writing before it starts and marked work in every session. We publish no outcome statistics at all, because a figure without its sample size, date and method is a marketing claim rather than evidence.

abu-dhabi/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.closingHeading: Name the gaps, then buy the sessions
abu-dhabi/igcse-to-ib-transition-course.closingBody: If you are looking at an IGCSE to IB transition course in Abu Dhabi, make the gap list the condition of the purchase. Ask the school for IGCSE component marks and the tier for each subject, confirm the Diploma subjects and levels, and ask the coordinator what bridging the school already runs. Send us those three things and we will come back with a named gap per session, a block length with a stated finish before DP1 starts, and the Mathematics route read from the component evidence rather than the grade. A free trial lesson on the first gap comes first, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects to a named syllabus code rather than to a general level. Each works one-to-one over live video with Abu Dhabi students, marks past-paper work against the published scheme, and keeps a running record of where the marks are going.

intro.heading: Tuition you can audit, not tuition you have to trust
paragraphs: Most IGCSE tuition is sold on reassurance and reviewed on feeling. A parent books an hour a week, the student says the sessions are useful, the next report arrives, and nobody can say which of those three things caused the other. That is a poor way to spend AED 200 an hour for eighteen months. The alternative is not more faith in the tutor. It is a small, dull set of documents that exist whether the term went well or badly, and that let you see the difference between a child who is learning and a child who is being kept company for sixty minutes.

This page is built around those documents. A marked script with the mark scheme beside it. An error log that separates a knowledge gap from a method slip from a misread command term. A session note that names the paper and the component rather than the subject. A draft history on any coursework piece that shows whose thinking produced it. None of this is exotic. It is what a working subject teacher already produces for a class of twenty-five, and it is reasonable to expect it for one student at a private rate.

Abu Dhabi sharpens the case. Private schools here answer to ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Enrolment sits in three rough bands: the island schools around Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and Al Mushrif; the Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas Island corridor; and the newer mainland communities out towards Al Shamkha and Mussafah. A family in Al Reef and a family in Al Rawdah face the same syllabus and completely different evenings.

Delivery here is online and one-to-one. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. That is said plainly because it changes what you are comparing. A visiting tutor is limited to whoever can reach Al Reef before seven in the evening. A live video session is limited only by who is free at that hour, which is how a household ends up with an IGCSE Chemistry 0620 specialist instead of a generalist with a car and a free Thursday.

What follows is the market in numbers, the evidence to ask for, the Cambridge and Pearson calendar read backwards from the entry deadline rather than forwards from the exam, and the point at which the honest answer is to stop paying. Figures in AED are market rates published by other providers, with the band attributed to whoever published it. They are context for your decision rather than a price list of ours; our own commercial answer is a first lesson at no charge followed by a consultation.
bullets: Marked scripts, an error log and dated session notes within every four sessions
Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel syllabus codes written on the plan, not just subjects
Market rates in AED attributed to the provider that published the figure
Entry deadlines, forecast-grade dates and results dates counted backwards
A stated coverage position when no specialist is free for a rare subject

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.programmesIntro: An IGCSE plan in Abu Dhabi has to know which board your child sits, which tier the school has entered them for, and what comes after Year 11. Those three decisions change the papers, the grade ceiling and the university paperwork more than any choice of tutor does.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Subjects carry four-digit codes that decide everything about the plan: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500, English as a Second Language 0510. Two children in the same Abu Dhabi year group can sit different codes in the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the school sits in before you build a revision calendar around any published date.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Codes begin 4: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. The structure differs from Cambridge in ways that matter for revision, including tiering by Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, and a different balance of question styles across the papers.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools enter students for both boards across a nine-subject timetable, so a household can be running 0580 Mathematics and 4PH1 Physics at once. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than against a date someone remembered from last year.

programmes.name: Core, Extended, Foundation and Higher tiers
programmes.description: Tiering is the single most consequential decision in an IGCSE timetable, and it is usually made by the school rather than the family. Cambridge Core and Extended papers differ in content and in grade ceiling. Pearson Foundation and Higher do the same under different names. A child entered for the wrong tier is either being capped or being asked to sit material the lessons never covered.
programmes.countryNote: Tier decisions in Abu Dhabi schools are commonly confirmed around the final entry deadline, and for a June sitting that deadline falls in the spring term, well before the papers are sat. That means the conversation has to happen in the autumn and winter terms, with marked evidence in hand, rather than in the spring when the entry has already been lodged and the tier is fixed.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level, IB Diploma and equivalency
programmes.description: IGCSE grades act as the entry gate to A Level and to the IB Diploma Programme, and as part of the Ministry of Education equivalency file for students who later apply to UAE universities. Subject choices made in Year 9 therefore reach into Year 13. The jump in reading load and independent work between Year 11 and Year 12 catches out students who were carried by memory at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: On the British track, Gulf Today reported the UAE equivalency requirement as five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before relying on it.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi households ask for most often, with the syllabus codes that decide which papers are sat. A plan that says Physics is not a plan. A plan that says 0625 Extended, Papers 2 and 4, with Paper 6 as the alternative to practical, is one you can check.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Marks leak in three predictable places: multi-step algebra where method marks are lost to arithmetic, the wordy later questions where the problem is never translated into mathematics, and bearings or transformation work that is rehearsed once and then forgotten. Extended candidates also need fluency in topics Core never touches.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the heaviest losses, usually because formulae are recalled but units and rearrangement are not. The alternative to practical paper rewards a specific skill set, including reading a scale correctly, identifying a control variable and describing a method precisely enough for somebody else to repeat it.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles calculations split into a mass-to-moles step and a ratio step, and students who lose marks almost always lose them at the second. Organic chemistry rewards pattern recognition rather than memory, and the extended-response questions on electrolysis and rates need a structure the mark scheme can follow.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap. Students revise the topics they enjoy and arrive at the paper strong on transport in plants and silent on homeostasis. Command-term discipline decides the longer answers: describe, explain and suggest ask for different things and are marked differently.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, double or single award
subjects.description: A child on Combined Science is not studying a reduced version of three separate sciences; the content map is different. Revising from separate-science notes wastes hours on material that will never be examined, and leaves gaps in the parts the award does assess.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading questions are marked for selection and inference rather than for retelling, and the directed writing task is assessed on audience and register as much as on accuracy. Students who write well and read quickly tend to lose marks for answering the question they expected rather than the one on the paper.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The entry choice between First Language and Second Language English sets a ceiling that affects later applications, so it deserves a conversation with the school rather than a shrug. Within the paper, the summary task and the note-making task carry marks that respond quickly to technique work.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Both reward a diagram or a definition before the explanation, and both punish a student who writes a general essay. Evaluation marks on the longer questions need a judgement with a reason attached, which is a teachable habit rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 / 0470)
subjects.description: Case-study recall is the differentiator in Geography; source handling is the differentiator in History. In both, the mark scheme rewards specific named detail, and a student who has learned the concept but no example will stall at the middle of the mark range.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: Theory papers need precise vocabulary, and the practical components need methodical evidence rather than clever shortcuts. Pseudocode and trace tables are the two skills that most reliably move a grade, because both are examined and both are rarely practised at home.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Foreign Language (Cambridge 0508 / 0544)
subjects.levels: First Language and Foreign Language routes
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside an international curriculum for most students in the emirate under federal requirements, and the first-language and foreign-language routes assess very different things. Treating one as an easier version of the other is the most common planning error families make here.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi is three different school-run problems wearing one city's name. Where a household sits decides what time a session can realistically start, which schools the children attend, and how much a visiting tutor would have to charge to make the trip worth taking.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Dense island addresses within a short drive of several British-curriculum schools, which keeps local tutor supply high for Mathematics and English and thin for the rarer IGCSE options. Sessions here can start early because the school run is short.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Rawdah
regions.note: Villa communities feeding the long-established island schools. Families often run two or three children at different stages at once, which makes a fixed weekly slot per child more valuable than a flexible one shared between them.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A large low-rise spread with internal distances that surprise newcomers. A tutor crossing from the island adds a real drive in each direction, which is why households here tend to compare an online hour against a visiting hour on cost per teaching minute.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Corridor addresses between the island and Khalifa City, close to several large academies. Evening slots compete with sport and extracurricular commitments, so Year 11 households often move the weekly session to a Friday or Saturday morning.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short bridge from the island but a distinct catchment, with families whose children often transfer in mid-course from other systems. Mid-year joiners usually need a syllabus-gap audit before anybody books a weekly hour.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise living with lift and parking delays that quietly eat into a visiting tutor's hour. Study space is often a shared dining table, so a session plan here has to assume headphones and a defined sixty minutes rather than a quiet study.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A newer residential catchment where several families are on their first IGCSE cycle. Questions here lean towards how the two boards differ and what the tier decision actually means, rather than towards last-minute exam rescue.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Mainland communities with a wide spread of school fees and curricula, and the longest drives to the island schools. Online delivery removes the single largest cost a household here would otherwise pay a visiting tutor for.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Reef
regions.note: Outer communities where a weekday visiting session often cannot start before seven in the evening once traffic is counted. A live video slot at half past four is a different lesson entirely, because the student is not yet tired.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif and Al Rawdah
schoolClusters.note: The longest-established British and international schools in the emirate sit within a few kilometres of each other here, which means households often compare IGCSE results across three schools their neighbours attend. Students we support in this cluster most often ask for Mathematics, Chemistry and First Language English.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Reem and the Khalifa City to Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: A newer band of academies serving the island fringe and the inland communities. Transfers in and out are more common here, so IGCSE gap audits and tier conversations come up more often than straight exam rescue. ADEK publishes inspection ratings for all of them.

schoolClusters.city: The mainland: Mussafah, Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Al Shamkha and Al Reef
schoolClusters.note: A wider fee range and a wider spread of curricula, with several large schools entering big IGCSE cohorts. Distance from the island schools is what pushes households here towards online delivery rather than a visiting tutor's travel premium.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tuition.modesIntro: Three ways an Abu Dhabi household uses IGCSE tuition. All three are delivered one-to-one over live video, and all three produce the same documents, because the whole point of the plan is that you can read it later.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject at a time
modes.description: A fixed slot on the same evening each week for one subject and one syllabus code. The hour opens with the error log from last week, works a past-paper question type under time, and closes with one named thing to practise. This is the format that produces a usable record, because each session is comparable to the one before it.

modes.title: Paper clinics in the weeks before a series
modes.description: Short, intense blocks aimed at one paper rather than one subject, built around sitting the paper under exam timing and then marking it against the published scheme. Useful when a student knows the content and still loses marks, and useful when a mock result has arrived and nobody can explain it.
bullets: Full paper sat under time, then marked against the scheme

modes.title: Coursework and controlled-component review
modes.description: Process coaching on the pieces that are assessed inside school. The tutor reads what the student has written, explains against the published criteria where the piece currently sits, and asks the questions that make the student do the next revision. The words that go to the examiner are the student's own in every case.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition in Abu Dhabi buys that the school day cannot
paragraphs: IGCSE tuition in Abu Dhabi buys three things a classroom cannot give one child: time on that child's specific errors, a second reading of a marked script, and a plan that names a paper rather than a subject. Market rates run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a subject specialist, on the figures other providers publish. None of that buys more content. The content is already being delivered six hours a day by a school ADEK licenses and inspects.

The gap a private hour fills is diagnostic. A Year 11 teacher marking thirty IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Paper 4 scripts can tell you that your child lost marks on moles and on the six-mark electrolysis question. A private hour can tell you that the moles marks went because the mass-to-moles step was right and the ratio step was not, and that the electrolysis answer had the chemistry in it but no structure the mark scheme could reward. The first of those is a grade. The second is something to practise on Tuesday.

That is why the rest of this page is about evidence rather than enthusiasm. Every claim a tutor makes about progress can be checked against a document, and a provider who will not produce the document is telling you something useful about the provider. The sections below set out what should exist after four paid sessions, how to decide which subject gets the money when nine are running at once, what the Abu Dhabi market actually charges and who published those figures, and the dates that decide whether a plan has any room left in it at all.

sections.heading: The paper trail a term of IGCSE tuition should leave behind
paragraphs: Five documents, and none of them is difficult to produce. A marked script, an error log, a dated session note, a draft history on anything assessed inside school, and a written plan carrying the syllabus code. If all five exist at the end of a half-term, you can answer the only question that matters: has this child's performance on the actual papers moved, and in which direction.

The marked script is the anchor. It has to be a past paper sat under time, marked against the published scheme rather than against a tutor's sense of it, with the lost marks annotated by cause. The error log is the memory of the tuition. Without it, each session fixes something and the fix evaporates, which is how a family can pay for twenty hours and find the same mistake in the February mock that was in the October one.

The session note is the cheapest of the five and the one most often missing. Three lines is enough, provided those lines name the paper, the component and the specific skill worked on. The plan is what lets you say no to drift: when a tutor proposes a different topic every week, the plan is the document that asks why. A provider who produces none of these is not necessarily teaching badly, but you have no way of knowing either way, and at a private rate that is the thing you are actually buying.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, two funded hours: triage by evidence
paragraphs: Almost no Abu Dhabi family funds tuition in nine subjects, and the ones who try usually buy a thin hour in each and move nothing. The useful question is which single subject, in which single paper, will convert the next two hundred dirhams into the most marks. The evidence answers that better than the student's opinion does, and better than the subject the parent found hardest at school.

Start by sorting the lost marks into four causes. Content never learned. Method known but executed carelessly. Structure missing on extended-response questions. Time run out. Only the first and the third reliably respond to paid teaching hours. The second responds to a checking protocol that costs nothing, and the fourth responds to sitting papers split against a clock at the kitchen table, also free.

The second filter is the shape of the timetable. A child with a grade 4 in one subject and grade 7s elsewhere has a certificate problem in one place, and funding that subject alone is the efficient move. A child who is a grade 5 across the board has a study-habit problem that one subject's tuition will not touch. The table below is the version of this conversation we have most often with households in Khalifa City and on Al Reem Island, where two children and one budget is the normal case. One more filter is worth applying before any money is spent: how many papers are left to sit in that subject. Funding a subject whose final paper is three weeks away buys very little, while the same hour in a subject with a full year of assessment ahead compounds. Sort the nine subjects by papers remaining, then by cause of lost marks, and the funding order usually becomes obvious without anybody arguing about which subject is hardest.
