abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: An IGCSE tutor is almost never hired for IGCSE alone. The question behind the search is usually what the grade is for, and that answer sits one stage either side of Years 10 and 11. These are the four stages Abu Dhabi families ask about.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Year 9
programmes.description: The years before the entry form exists. Checkpoint tests are available in March, May and October, and they are the last low-stakes signal a family gets before tiering decisions start to matter. Algebraic fluency, scientific vocabulary and extended writing built here are what make an Extended or Higher entry viable two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families moving in from CBSE, American or Ministry-curriculum schools usually land in Years 8 or 9, and the gap that shows up is algebra and written explanation rather than arithmetic. Year 9 is the cheapest moment in the whole sequence to fix it, and almost nobody buys tuition then.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, each with its own syllabus code, tier and paper structure. Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses for the same subject differ in assessment design, not only in content, so a tutor working from the wrong code teaches the right physics into the wrong paper.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools sit both boards and some sit both within one year group, which is why the first thing we ask for is the entry form or the exam-board name from the school, not the subject. A parent in Al Reem Island and a parent in Khalifa City can have children in the same subject on different syllabuses.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects taken in depth, with entry requirements expressed directly in IGCSE grades. The jump is not volume but independence: content arrives faster, worked examples stop, and the written answers expected are longer and more structured than anything IGCSE asked for.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools set subject-specific IGCSE grade thresholds for sixth-form entry, so a Year 11 grade is simultaneously a qualification and an admissions decision. That is the real reason a Year 11 grade 6 in Mathematics causes more anxiety than it looks like it should.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subject groups at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, which is a different working style from IGCSE where almost everything is decided in a final written paper.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has both British-curriculum and IB schools, and a number of Year 11 families are choosing between them during the exam term itself. The IGCSE subjects that most affect that choice are Mathematics and the separate sciences, because they determine whether Higher Level is realistic.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask for, with the syllabus codes we work from and the tier or entry decision that matters most in each. The code is the thing to send us; the subject name alone is not enough to plan a session.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended; Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tiering decision that matters most, because the lower tier caps the grade and because sixth-form and Diploma mathematics entry is usually expressed as a Mathematics grade. Algebraic manipulation is the single most common blocker; most lost marks in later topics trace back to it.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside or instead of the main syllabus by students heading for Higher Level or A Level mathematics. Calculus and trigonometric identities appear earlier than students expect. Worth tutoring in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because it front-loads the hardest material.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism account for a disproportionate share of lost marks, and the practical-skills component is rehearsed least of all. Extended-only topics appear on specific papers, so a Core candidate revising from an Extended textbook wastes weeks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade and are usually taught once, early, and never revisited. Organic chemistry is a memory problem with a structure, and students who learn the structure stop losing the marks. Equation-writing precision is where Extended candidates slip.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy subject in which marks are lost to imprecise language rather than missing knowledge - describing instead of explaining, naming a process without its location. Data and graph questions are the reliably fixable part and respond fastest to tutoring.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: Two or one IGCSE grades covering all three sciences, often chosen for timetable reasons rather than ability. The common problem is coverage: students assume a topic is out of scope because it was not taught, when it sits on the paper. A syllabus audit is the first session.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0500 First Language; 0510 and 0511 as a Second Language
subjects.description: The entry route sets the ceiling here too: the Second Language syllabus is a different qualification from First Language and is read differently by sixth forms and universities. Directed writing and summary are the two most teachable components in the whole IGCSE set.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Marks are decided by how closely a student argues from the text rather than by how much they have read about it. The fixable skill is quotation selection and integration. Unseen poetry is where unprepared candidates lose most, and it is the component that rewards drilling.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study command words carry the marks: identify, explain, analyse and evaluate each demand a different answer length and shape. Students who write everything they know score in the lower bands. Taught as answer structure rather than content, these two move quickly.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two very different qualifications routinely confused at option time. Computer Science examines algorithms, data representation and pseudocode under timed conditions; ICT examines practical application work. Choosing the wrong one for a target A Level is a decision tuition cannot undo later.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source-handling and case-study recall in defined proportions. In Geography, the loss is almost always failure to use named examples; in History, failure to answer the question asked rather than narrating the period. Both respond to structured answer frames more than to further reading.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0508 First Language Arabic; 0544 Arabic Foreign Language
subjects.description: Two separate syllabuses on different pacing, and a student placed in the wrong one spends two years either bored or drowning. Federal regulation requires private schools to teach Arabic language, so for most Abu Dhabi students this is a timetabled subject rather than an elective.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi IGCSE families are concentrated in a handful of residential corridors, and what changes between them is not the syllabus but the evening: when the bus drops, how late clubs run, and what time a Year 11 student can realistically do focused work. Session planning starts there.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah and Al Bateen
regions.note: Established island neighbourhoods close to several long-standing British-curriculum schools, so journeys home are short and a 16:30 session is realistic. Year 11 families here most often ask for Mathematics and the separate sciences.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-density towers with schools within a short radius and a large proportion of recently arrived families. Mid-year transfers are common, which makes syllabus-code checks more valuable here than anywhere else in the emirate.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa housing with long bus runs to island schools, so a 17:00 start is the practical floor for a Year 10 or Year 11 student who needs to be alert. Two 50-minute sessions beat one two-hour block in this corridor.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Families feeding a mix of British and IB schools, which is why the IGCSE-to-Diploma question comes up here more often than the IGCSE-to-A-Level one. Weekend morning sessions are heavily requested in the spring term.

regions.name: Yas Island and Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Newer school capacity and a younger year-group profile, so Year 9 and Year 10 enquiries outnumber Year 11 ones. That is the better-value end of the two-year arc, and families here tend to arrive earlier than average.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Ghadeer
regions.note: Mainland communities a long drive from the island, where a visiting tutor's travel premium is at its highest and online delivery changes the arithmetic most. Evening slots from 17:30 are standard.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Large mixed districts with students travelling across the emirate to school. Timetables vary household by household, so we set the weekly slot after the first week rather than guessing at booking.

regions.name: Between the Bridges and Al Nahyan
regions.note: Central districts with access to schools on both sides of the water. A common pattern here is a Year 11 student taking one subject with a tutor while the school runs its own after-school clinic for another.

schoolClusters.city: The island: Al Mushrif, Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's longest-established British-curriculum provision, which means IGCSE entry practice here is settled and well documented. Boards and tiers still differ school by school, so ask your school's examinations officer which board and which code before buying tuition in any subject.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha, Yas and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: Newer capacity across the mainland corridor and the islands, with a higher share of families who changed curriculum within the last two years. This is where syllabus-code mismatches and tier misplacements most often surface, usually in Mathematics.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi is actually hired to fix
paragraphs: The literal answer: an IGCSE tutor teaches one or more Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE subjects to a student in Years 10 or 11, outside school hours, usually weekly. In Abu Dhabi the service exists as visiting tutors who drive to the family's address and as one-to-one tuition over live video. Published market rates put the first at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, and a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE tuition from AED 150. IB Gram delivers only the second. We run no home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

What families ask for and what they need are different about half the time. The request is usually a subject and a worry. The need is often a decision that has already been made badly: a tier that caps the grade, a syllabus the tutor is not teaching to, a second-language English entry where a first-language one was assumed, or a subject count that will not satisfy Ministry of Education equivalency later. None of those is fixed by weekly teaching, and all of them are cheaper to fix in Year 10 than in March of Year 11.

A second recurring gap is the scale itself. Cambridge reports some IGCSE syllabuses on 9 to 1 and others on A* to G; Pearson reports International GCSE on 9 to 1. A parent reading a report with a 6 in one subject and a B in another is reading two different measurement systems, and school reports rarely explain which is which. Before you buy an hour of anything, get the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject in writing from the school's examinations officer. That email is free and it changes what you should spend money on.

sections.heading: Tiering: the decision that sets a ceiling before teaching starts
paragraphs: In tiered IGCSE subjects a candidate sits one of two sets of papers. Cambridge calls them Core and Extended; Pearson calls them Foundation and Higher. The lower tier examines less of the syllabus and awards a restricted range of grades. That restriction is the whole point of this section: a family planning around a top grade in a subject entered at the lower tier is planning around an outcome the entry has already removed, and no quantity of weekly tuition changes it.

The decision is usually made by the school on the basis of Year 9 and Year 10 performance, which is reasonable. What is less reasonable is how rarely it is explained to the family in those terms. Parents are told their child is doing Core Mathematics and hear a reassurance about workload rather than a statement about a ceiling. Then in Year 11 they buy tuition aimed at a grade 8, and the tutor spends the first session explaining that the papers cannot award it.

Tier changes are possible and they have deadlines. Those deadlines are set by the board and administered through your school's examinations officer, and they sit months before the examination itself. For a June series the entry window closes in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper, and forecast grades are collected from the centre some weeks after that; for a November series the entry window closes over the summer. The exact day is not something to lift from a page like this one, because it is revised and because it varies by board and by centre - the examinations officer holds the current key dates and the statement of entry repeats them. The practical sequence is: ask which tier, ask what the ceiling is, ask what evidence would support a move up, and ask by when. If the answer to the last question has already passed, the honest tutoring plan is to maximise the grade available at the current tier, which is a different plan with different content.

sections.heading: How many IGCSEs your child actually needs, and which ones do not count
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi students typically sit eight to ten IGCSE subjects. The number that matters for UAE recognition is smaller and specific. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause is where families get caught. A student with a strong Arabic grade and a strong Islamic Education grade has two excellent results that do not count towards the five, which can leave a thinner margin than the report card suggests. It is worth doing the arithmetic in Year 10 rather than after results day, because the remedy - entering one further subject in a later series - needs an entry deadline that has not yet passed. One competitor page currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries states that candidates must take six subjects; the sourced requirement is five.

Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutor performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. The American track has different conditions, including English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB there is no points threshold we are willing to publish, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site. sections.heading: Year 10 against Year 11: when an hour is worth most
paragraphs: Almost all IGCSE tutoring in this market is bought in Year 11, and almost all of it would have been worth more in Year 10. The reason is not motivational. It is that an hour in Year 10 can teach, and an hour in February of Year 11 can mostly only triage. Teaching builds something the student keeps; triage redistributes a fixed amount of attention across topics that are all now urgent. The same money buys different goods.

There is a specific mechanism behind this in the quantitative subjects. Algebraic manipulation underpins the later topics in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry. A student with insecure algebra in Year 10 can have it rebuilt in six to eight weekly sessions, after which the rest of the syllabus becomes teachable. The same student in Year 11 with four months to go cannot be taken off the syllabus for eight weeks, so the tutor patches topic by topic and the underlying weakness keeps reappearing. The grade usually still moves. It moves less, for more money.

The honest version of the Year 11 conversation runs like this. With four to six months, pick two subjects, not five. Start from a marked mock rather than a syllabus list, because the mock shows where marks are actually being dropped and the syllabus shows only what exists. Work in order of marks available rather than textbook order. Accept that paper technique - reading the command word, allocating time by marks, showing the step the marker needs - is often worth more than additional content at this point. And if the tier has capped the grade, say so in week one rather than week ten.

sections.heading: The exam series counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a session calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is the thing that constrains every tutoring plan. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October - those Checkpoint tests are not IGCSE, and the February/March examination series belongs to India rather than the UAE, so an Abu Dhabi plan is built on June or November and nothing else. Pearson's International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

Two mechanical details catch families out. The first is zones: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Download the timetable your school's examinations officer confirms, not the first one a search returns. The second is that provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and can be revised, so a plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than against dates copied from a page like this one.

Counted backwards, a series has a fixed shape. Entries close months before the papers. Forecast grades are collected weeks before them. Mocks sit a term earlier and are the only realistic data a tutoring plan should be built on. Results reach centres before candidates - Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Enquiries about results and retake entries both have their own deadlines after that, which is why a family deciding in September to resit in November is often already late.

sections.heading: Nine subjects slipping, one budget: which hour to buy first
paragraphs: A Year 11 report with five amber subjects produces a predictable instinct: tutor all five. Spread across five subjects, a typical household budget buys roughly fortnightly contact in each, which is below the frequency at which anything consolidates. The result is five subjects that each feel attended to and none that moves. Triage is unpleasant and it is the correct response.

The ranking logic is mechanical rather than emotional. Subjects that gate the next stage come first: Mathematics and the separate sciences determine whether Higher Level Diploma or A Level science is viable, so a grade there is worth more than the same grade elsewhere. Next come subjects where the gap is technique rather than content, because technique moves fastest - Business Studies and Economics case-study structure, English directed writing and summary, Geography named examples, History answering the question rather than narrating. Last come content-heavy subjects where the student is simply behind, since those need more weeks than the calendar has.

Two subjects should usually be dropped from the tutoring plan rather than added to it. The subject the student is already passing comfortably, because the marginal grade there buys nothing. And the subject where the student has given up entirely, unless the problem is diagnosably narrow - in which case it belongs in the first group, not the last. A tutor willing to tell you which two subjects not to pay for is giving you better advice than one who agrees to all five.

sections.heading: From IGCSE into the Diploma Programme or A Level: the gap by subject
paragraphs: Year 11 families in Al Raha and Khalifa City are frequently choosing between a British sixth form and an IB Diploma place while the examinations are still running. The choice is usually discussed in terms of breadth against depth, which is accurate and not very actionable. What is actionable is the specific gap between each IGCSE subject and the first term of the course that follows it, because that gap is what makes the first report of Year 12 look worse than anybody expected.

The pattern is consistent. Mathematics at Extended or Higher covers most of what Analysis and Approaches or an A Level course assumes, except that the pace of algebraic work doubles and worked examples largely stop. The sciences assume a practical write-up style that IGCSE only gestures at, and Diploma internal assessment requires a level of independent design that no IGCSE component asks for. English Literature moves from close reading of set texts to sustained argument. Economics and Business introduce diagrammatic analysis that must be drawn correctly under time pressure.

Which is why the highest-value block in the whole sequence is often four to eight sessions in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, aimed at content rather than study skills. Not a general bridging course: the actual algebra, the actual write-up conventions, the actual essay structure the specific course assumes on day one. Students who do that arrive in September able to listen to the first lesson instead of decoding it, and the first Year 12 report reflects it.

sections.heading: Sitting IGCSE as a private candidate in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Some students need an IGCSE grade without a school place for it: a subject the school does not offer, a resit after a disappointing series, a child being educated at home, or a family that arrived mid-cycle. That route exists and runs through examination centres rather than through tutors. Entries for private candidates are made by a centre registered with the relevant board, and the centre decides what it will accept, what it charges and what deadlines it imposes on top of the board's own.

The practical constraints are worth knowing before planning around this. Subjects with assessed practical or coursework components are the hardest to arrange privately, because somebody has to administer them; written-only syllabuses are more straightforward. Entry deadlines are the board's, and they are early - a June series closes entries in the spring, months ahead of the first paper, and a November series closes over the summer - but centres frequently set their own earlier cut-offs, and a centre's fee is separate from the board's entry fee. Zone timetables apply to private candidates exactly as they do to school candidates.

Tutoring a private candidate is a different job from tutoring a school student. There is no school scheme of work setting the pace, no teacher issuing deadlines and no mock unless somebody arranges one. So the plan has to supply all three: a syllabus-ordered sequence with dates, written tasks with hand-in dates, and at least two full papers sat under timed conditions and marked against the real criteria. We do not enter candidates, administer examinations or arrange centres, and we are not permitted to supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes - those come from the board's own site and from the centre.
bullets: Entries are made through a centre registered with the board, not through a tutor

process.title: Send the subject, the board and the code
process.description: Subject name alone is not enough to plan a session. Send the board, the syllabus code and the tier for each subject, plus the year group and the target series. If you do not have them, your school's examinations officer can send all four in one email and it costs nothing.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial lesson
process.description: A tutor works with your child on one topic from the actual syllabus, ideally starting from a marked piece of school work. No charge and no card details taken. You end the session with a written note naming the gap, the tier position and what a block of sessions would target.

process.title: Tier and entry check before anything is bought
process.description: We read the entry details against the board's own published key dates and state plainly what grade the current tier can award and whether any change deadline is still open. If the tuition you were about to buy is aimed above the tier ceiling, you find out in week zero.

process.title: Weekly sessions against a marked baseline
process.description: Fifty to sixty minutes, one-to-one over live video, working from your child's marked mock or past paper rather than a syllabus checklist. Topic order is set by marks available. Each session ends with one short written task carrying a hand-in date.

process.title: Half-term review against the syllabus
process.description: Every half term the plan is checked against the board's published syllabus rather than the textbook, so topics the school has not reached yet are visible as a risk instead of a surprise. You get the revised topic order in writing, with what changed and why.

process.title: Pre-series technique block
process.description: In the final weeks the work shifts to timed sections, command-word reading and time allocation by marks, with papers marked against the real criteria. This stage has an end date set by the series, which is the point: a plan that cannot end has no shape.

whyPoints.title: We work from the syllabus code, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different assessments of similar mathematics, and 0500 and 0510 are different English qualifications entirely. Teaching the right content into the wrong paper structure is the most common way tuition fails to move a grade.

whyPoints.title: The tier ceiling is stated in week zero
whyPoints.description: If a subject is entered at Core or Foundation, we say what grade the papers can award before you pay for anything aimed above it, and whether a change deadline remains open. That conversation costs us sales and saves families months of misdirected work.

whyPoints.title: Plans are built on a marked paper, not a syllabus list
whyPoints.description: A syllabus shows what exists; a marked mock shows where marks are actually dropped. Topic order follows marks available rather than textbook order, which usually means starting somewhere other than where the student expected.

whyPoints.title: Session dates are set against the board's published calendar
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, forecast-grade dates and the zone timetable all constrain a plan, and they are read from the board's own key dates rather than from memory. A pre-series block that ends after the paper has been sat is not a plan.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool that is not limited by a drive
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a family in Al Reef or Al Ghadeer selects from everyone who teaches their specific syllabus, rather than from the adults willing to drive out there at 17:30. For minority subjects and second-language English routes that is the entire difference.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on coursework and board materials
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. We do not produce assessed work for a student, and we do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes - those come from the board's own site. Both limits are stated before anybody pays.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Core Mathematics in Abu Dhabi - can a tutor still get them a grade 8?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the most important thing on this page. Tiered Cambridge and Pearson subjects award a restricted range of grades at the lower tier, so Core and Foundation entries cannot reach the top grades however well a candidate performs. Tuition aimed at a grade the papers cannot award is wasted money. What is worth doing is asking the school's examinations officer two questions in writing: what is the maximum awardable grade at the current tier, and is the deadline for a tier change still open. If it is open, the tutoring plan is evidence for a move up. If it has passed, the plan is to maximise the grade available at the current tier, which is different work.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tuition is a service we offer only in India. Abu Dhabi lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, with your child's marked papers shared on screen and annotated live. Published market rates for a visiting tutor here run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel folded in, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, so the drive is most of the premium. The practical gain is the pool: a family in Al Reef chooses from everyone who teaches their syllabus rather than from those willing to make the journey.

faqs.question: We are in Abu Dhabi - how many IGCSE passes will the Ministry of Education actually count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited AS Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. That exclusion catches families out, because two strong results may not count towards the requirement. One ranking competitor page states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. Equivalency is a Ministry process - verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority, since IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees any part of it.

faqs.question: Why does my child's report show a 6 in one subject and a B in another?
faqs.answer: Because they are different scales. Cambridge reports some IGCSE syllabuses on a 9 to 1 numeric scale and others on A* to G, and Pearson reports International GCSE on 9 to 1. A report can therefore legitimately mix the two, and the numbers and letters are not aligned in the way parents instinctively assume. This matters when setting targets and when comparing two subjects to decide where to spend money. Ask the examinations officer which scale applies to each syllabus your child is entered for, alongside the board, the code and the tier. One email answers all four and changes what you should buy.

faqs.question: Is it better to start IGCSE tutoring in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, by a wide margin, and this is a mechanical point rather than a motivational one. In Year 10 an hour can teach something the student keeps - insecure algebra rebuilt over six to eight sessions makes the later topics in Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry teachable. In February of Year 11 the same hour mostly triages: the tutor cannot take a student off the syllabus for eight weeks, so weaknesses get patched topic by topic and keep resurfacing. Grades still move in Year 11. They move less, for more money, across fewer subjects. If you are reading this in Year 10, the cheap window is now.

faqs.question: Five of my child's subjects are slipping - should we tutor all five?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. A typical household budget spread across five subjects buys roughly fortnightly contact in each, which is below the frequency at which anything consolidates, so five subjects feel attended to and none moves. Rank them instead. Subjects that gate the next stage come first, which usually means Mathematics and the separate sciences, because they decide whether Higher Level or A Level science is viable. Technique gaps come second, because they move fastest: case-study command words, directed writing, named examples in Geography. Drop the subject your child already passes comfortably, since the marginal grade there buys nothing.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE exams actually take place, and when do entries close?
faqs.answer: In the UAE, Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Those are the only two an Abu Dhabi candidate can sit, because Cambridge offers the February/March series to India only; the Checkpoint tests in March, May and October are not IGCSE. Pearson International GCSE runs in May/June and November, and the November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students the following January. Entries for both boards close months before the first paper, and the date that applies to your child is on the centre's statement of entry. Every Cambridge centre also sits in one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after using the wrong zone timetable.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market figures as at October 2026, none of them ours: Unitors advertises IGCSE tuition from AED 150 per hour and IB from AED 200; EdFlik lists from AED 45 to AED 65; Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52; TutorChase quotes AED 270; BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, with home tutors advertising up to AED 500, and specialist exam-year tuition at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Monthly packages seen in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Ask any provider for the rate, the session length and whether marking is included.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel teach the same IGCSE content?
faqs.answer: Similar content, genuinely different assessment. The syllabuses diverge on paper structure, component weighting, tiering arrangements and how practical skills are examined, which is why a tutor needs the code rather than the subject name. Pearson also operates differently in how series are structured across the year. A student who moves school mid-course can end up with notes written for one board and an entry for the other, and that mismatch costs real marks on paper technique even when the underlying knowledge is sound. Send us the code from the entry form; where a child sits subjects across both boards, that is workable but the plans have to be kept separate.

faqs.question: My child moved to Abu Dhabi from a CBSE school in Year 9 - what is the actual gap?
faqs.answer: Rarely arithmetic, usually algebraic fluency and written explanation. Students arriving from Indian-curriculum schools are often ahead on procedural calculation and behind on the extended written answer that IGCSE science and humanities papers require, where marks depend on explaining rather than stating. The second gap is coursework-style working: showing the step a marker needs rather than the answer alone. Year 9 is the cheapest point to address both, because nothing has been entered yet and a tier decision is still ahead. A single diagnostic session on one past paper from the intended board usually identifies which of the two is dominant.

faqs.question: Is my child's tutor legally allowed to tutor privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own channels, with the service page listing a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. ADEK's ethics rules also bar school staff from paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework or controlled assessment?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may teach the skills the component assesses, explain what the criteria reward, discuss a plan the student has made, ask questions that expose a weak argument, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not supply content for submission, rewrite a draft into their own prose, or hand over finished sections. The work has to be the student's own, and boards treat breaches as malpractice with consequences that fall on the student. We also do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; those are the board's material and come from the board's own site.

faqs.question: Can my child resit one IGCSE subject in November without changing school?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the mechanics run through a centre rather than through a tutor. Cambridge offers a November series and Pearson offers November for International GCSE, so a single-subject resit is a normal arrangement. The constraints are deadlines and components: entries close well ahead of the papers, centres often impose their own earlier cut-offs and charge their own fee on top of the board's, and subjects with assessed practical components are harder to arrange than written-only ones. Decide in the weeks around results rather than in September, because by then the useful preparation window has already narrowed and some deadlines have passed.

faqs.question: What is actually worth buying in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12?
faqs.answer: Content, not study skills - and the specific content the next course assumes on day one. For Mathematics that is algebraic fluency at roughly double the IGCSE pace, with function notation and early calculus vocabulary, because worked examples largely stop. For the sciences it is formal practical write-ups, uncertainty and data analysis, which IGCSE only gestures at and Diploma internal assessment demands. For English Literature it is sustained comparative argument rather than close reading of set texts. Four to eight sessions aimed at the real Year 12 course beat a generic bridging programme, and students who do it can listen to the first lesson rather than decode it.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match an IGCSE tutor, and what if the subject is unusual?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects on either board - Mathematics, the three sciences, English, Business, Economics - a match is normally within a few days, and the free trial lesson comes before any payment. For minority subjects, second-language English routes and some language syllabuses it can take longer, and if nobody suitable is available we say so rather than offering an approximate match. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a niche syllabus, the tutor may be based elsewhere and teaching into Gulf Standard Time; we state that up front, because a tutor who does not know your board is worse than a wait.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Get the entry facts first, then buy the teaching
abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE tutor in Abu Dhabi, send one email to your school's examinations officer before you send one to us: board, syllabus code, tier and target series for every subject. Then book the free 45-minute trial lesson. Your child works on one real topic from that syllabus, you get a written note naming the gap and the tier position, and no card details are taken. If the tier has already capped the grade you were planning around, you will hear it in week zero rather than in May. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below teaches one or two IGCSE subjects to a named specification, works one-to-one over live video with Abu Dhabi students, and produces marked scripts and session notes from the first week rather than from the first review. Distance to your address is not a variable.

intro.heading: Two questions hiding inside one search
paragraphs: Typing igcse tutor near me is shorthand for something more specific, and it is worth separating the parts. The first part is competence: can this person teach Cambridge 0620 Extended, or Pearson 4MA1 Higher, well enough to move marks. The second is logistics: can a session happen on a Tuesday at half past four without the family rearranging the evening. Distance is relevant to the second question only, and even then it is a proxy for time rather than for kilometres.

The reason this matters in Abu Dhabi is that the two questions pull in opposite directions. The pool of people who can reach Al Reef before seven in the evening is small. The pool of people who can teach Chemistry 0620 Extended to a student aiming at the top of the scale is also small. Intersect those two sets and you are often left with nobody, which is how families end up paying specialist rates for a generalist who happens to live nearby.

Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, and the school map is spread across three broad bands: the island schools around Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and Al Mushrif; the Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas Island corridor; and the newer mainland communities out towards Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Mussafah. A household in each of those bands has a materially different evening, and the clock table further down this page sets out what that means in practice.

Our own position is simple and stated up front. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram sends nobody to a UAE address; visiting tuition exists in our India operation only. So the honest version of near me here is not a shorter drive, it is a tutor who is available at your hour and matched to your specification, with the evidence of their work arriving in writing every week.

Everything below is built around things you can check. What time a session can realistically begin from each part of the emirate. How common your child's subject and tier actually are, and what happens when nobody suitable is free. What the first four marked scripts should contain and in what order to read them. What a session note has to say to be worth keeping. The arithmetic of a drive, in dirhams per teaching minute. And how to verify, yourself, that the person teaching your child is permitted to do so. None of that requires you to judge teaching you cannot see. Each item is a document, a timetable fact or a number you can put beside a competing quote, which is the only basis on which a stranger's hour is worth buying at a specialist rate.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Matching on specification means knowing three things before anybody is proposed: the board, the tier and the series. The blocks below set out what each of those changes about who is a suitable tutor, which is the part a postcode search cannot answer.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, by code
programmes.description: A tutor for Cambridge needs the specification rather than the subject: 0580 Mathematics, 0607 International Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0653 Combined Science, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences, 0500 First Language English, 0510 English as a Second Language. Tiering is Core and Extended, and the tier changes which past papers are the right practice set.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that using the correct zone timetable is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Confirm the zone with your Abu Dhabi school's exams officer before building a schedule.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, by code
programmes.description: Pearson codes begin with 4: Mathematics A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. Tiering is Foundation and Higher. A tutor who has taught only Cambridge will recognise the content and misjudge the question style, the mark distribution across papers and the balance of short to extended responses.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series, so plan against the live official document.

programmes.name: Tier, and why it narrows the tutor pool
programmes.description: The higher tier of a minority subject is where availability becomes genuinely thin, because the number of people who teach it well in any one city is small. A tutor comfortable with Core content may be out of their depth on Extended material, and the gap is invisible for several weeks because the early topics overlap.
programmes.countryNote: Tier entries are fixed at the entry deadline, not on the day of the exam, and in the UAE that deadline belongs to a June or a November series - Cambridge offers the February/March series to India only, so there is no third window to fall back on. A June candidate has entries closed in the spring, months before the first paper; a November candidate has them closed over the summer, and Pearson's November 2026 papers then ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Working backwards from either, the tier question, and therefore the question of who is a suitable tutor, needs settling a full term earlier with marked evidence in hand. The centre's examinations officer holds the exact closing date for your series.

programmes.name: Resits and private candidates
programmes.description: Students resitting one or two subjects, or sitting as private candidates, need a tutor who knows the entry mechanics as well as the content. The content has usually been taught before, so the work is paper practice with forensic marking rather than a second pass through the specification.
programmes.countryNote: A private candidate has to be entered through a centre that accepts external candidates, and the entry deadlines are the board's rather than the school's. Confirm both the accepting centre and its deadline early, because the availability of centre places in the emirate is the binding constraint more often than tutor availability is.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi households ask for most, with a note on what a tutor needs to demonstrate before taking the booking. Specification knowledge is checkable in one conversation; it does not need a trial term to establish.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Ask which tier they usually teach and how the papers differ between the two boards. A tutor who answers precisely has taught both; one who talks about IGCSE maths generally has taught one and assumed the other is close enough, which produces the wrong practice set.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The useful test is the practical paper. Ask what an alternative-to-practical question actually assesses. A specialist will name scale reading, control variables and method description precisely, because those marks are predictable and rarely rehearsed at home.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: One of the thinner pools at the higher tier in this market. Ask how they teach the two steps of a moles calculation separately, and how they structure an extended response on electrolysis, since those two things account for a large share of recoverable marks.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The breadth of recall makes a topic-confidence audit the right first session. Ask how they decide what to cover first, because a tutor who answers with the textbook order has not planned around which specification points carry the most marks.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Ask how they mark a reading answer, specifically how selection and inference are credited against retelling. English is the subject where reassuring feedback most often substitutes for marking against the published scheme, so a sample annotated answer is worth requesting.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The summary and note-making tasks are formula-driven and respond quickly, so a competent tutor should be able to describe the formula in a sentence. Also ask whether the route choice between first and second language English has been settled with the school.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Ask what earns an evaluation mark. The answer should mention a judgement with a stated condition attached, not a balanced discussion. Tutors who describe these subjects as essay writing tend not to be marking against the band descriptors.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 / 0470)
subjects.description: Both reward specific named detail, so ask how case studies and sources are built into weekly work. A tutor who produces one case-study card per topic leaves the student with a usable revision set, which is worth more than an hour of discussion.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: Ask them to complete a trace table in the format the mark scheme expects. It takes two minutes and it separates tutors who have taught the examined course from programmers who know the material but not the paper.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Foreign Language (Cambridge 0508 / 0544)
subjects.levels: First Language and Foreign Language routes
subjects.description: Confirm which route the school has entered, because the two assess very different things. A tutor comfortable with the foreign-language route is not automatically suitable for first language, and the mismatch is usually discovered late.

abu-dhabi/igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: The map below is about time rather than distance. What matters for a weekday session is when the student is home, fed and able to concentrate, and that varies by an hour and a half across the emirate even though the syllabus does not vary at all.

regions.name: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah and Al Zahiyah
regions.note: Short school runs and the densest concentration of British-curriculum schools, so local tutor supply is at its best here for common subjects. A session can often start by half past four, which is the single biggest advantage any household can have.

regions.name: Al Mushrif, Al Karamah and Al Nahyan
regions.note: Villa addresses within the island's school belt. Households here frequently run two or three children at different stages, so staggered fixed slots matter more than a single flexible one that becomes whoever is available.

regions.name: Al Rawdah and Al Maryah Island
regions.note: Central addresses close to several schools but with parking and lift delays that eat into a visiting hour. A live session loses none of that time, which is worth more than it sounds across a thirty-session year.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: The corridor between the island and the inland communities, with internal distances that surprise newcomers. A visiting tutor crossing from the island adds a real drive each way, so comparisons here are usually made on cost per teaching minute.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island and Yas Island
regions.note: Distinct catchments with high rates of mid-course transfer. New arrivals usually need a specification audit before anybody is matched, because the subject names carry across systems and the papers do not.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise living where study space is often shared and evenings are noisy. Headphones, a defined sixty minutes and a timer on screen do more here than any change of tutor, and a visiting hour loses minutes at the lift.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Long drives to the island cluster, which pushes the earliest realistic visiting start past seven on a school night. Weekend morning sessions are common and usually more productive than a tired weekday hour.

regions.name: Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Al Reef
regions.note: Outer communities with large school cohorts. The practical consequence of distance here is that the local tutor pool for a higher-tier minority subject is often empty, so matching on specification means matching beyond the neighbourhood.

sections.heading: The proximity question, answered with a map and a clock
paragraphs: Distance only matters because of what it does to the clock. A tutor twelve kilometres away is not worse than one two kilometres away; a session that cannot begin until a quarter past seven is worse than one that begins at half past four, because the student is a different person at those two times. So the useful way to think about near me is to ask what hour is reachable, and then ask who is good, rather than the other way round.

Run the arithmetic on your own evening before comparing any tutors. What time does the student actually walk through the door? How long before they are fed and able to sit down? What else is already in that evening, including Arabic or Islamic Education homework, sport and the other eight subjects? For most island households the answer is a workable slot from about half past four. For most mainland households on a school night it is closer to half past six, and for a visiting tutor it is later again once the drive is added at both ends.

The second half of the calculation is what proximity costs in choice. Abu Dhabi has a real tutoring market, but the subset of it that can be physically present in Al Reef on a Tuesday at six is narrow, and the subset of that subset which teaches Chemistry 0620 Extended confidently is narrower still. Families who insist on both usually end up compromising on the part they cannot see, which is teaching quality.

Removing the drive from the equation does not make a tutor good. It just stops geography making the decision for you. That is why the rest of this page is about the evidence a tutor produces in the first month, since once proximity is no longer the filter, something else has to be, and the only honest candidate is the marked work.

sections.heading: Corridor arithmetic: what time a session can actually start
paragraphs: The table below is the version of this conversation we have with families several times a week. It is not a traffic report; it is a planning tool. The numbers are the realistic earliest start for a weekday session, and the difference between the two right-hand columns is the drive that a visiting arrangement has to absorb somewhere, either in the rate or in the student's concentration.

Two things to notice. First, the live-video column is roughly the same everywhere, because what sets it is when the student gets home rather than when a tutor can arrive. Second, the gap between the columns widens the further out you live, which means the cost of insisting on physical presence is unevenly distributed across the emirate. A family in Al Mushrif pays very little for it. A family in Al Shamkha pays an hour of their child's best concentration.

The practical response for outer communities is to invert the week. Put the demanding work, particularly a full paper under timing, on a weekend morning when there is a genuine two-hour window, and keep weekday contacts short and mechanical. Two thirty-minute sessions on a school night often achieve more than one tired hour, and they survive a term better.

Ramadan shifts all of this, and planning for it in advance is easier than improvising. Session times commonly move later in the evening, after Iftar, and concentration patterns change for most students. A plan that spans Ramadan should put the timed papers either side of it and keep the intervening weeks light and consistent rather than ambitious.

sections.heading: Why the nearest tutor is rarely the right specification
paragraphs: Availability is not uniform across subjects, and no provider in this market publishes where it thins out. We do, because the alternative is taking a booking and then finding somebody approximately suitable, which is how a household discovers in February that their Chemistry tutor is a biologist who did chemistry at school.

The pattern is consistent. Mathematics and the common sciences at the lower tier are well covered almost everywhere. Higher-tier minority subjects, second-language English at the Extended route, Computer Science and the first-language Arabic route are where the pool is genuinely thin in any one city, and insisting on a local match in those cases means choosing from a list of one or two.

What should happen when nobody suitable is free is a stated position rather than silence. Ours is to say how long a match is likely to take, whether the session would need to sit at a different hour, and whether a nearby alternative serves, such as supporting the examined components with a specialist in the adjacent discipline while the right person becomes available. Sometimes the honest answer is that we cannot help with that combination at present.

There is a question worth asking any provider here, and the answer is diagnostic. Ask what happens if the tutor they propose turns out to be wrong for your child in week three. A provider with real depth will describe a replacement process with the records handed over. A provider without it will reassure you that the match will be right, which is not a process.

sections.heading: The first four marked scripts, read in order
paragraphs: Once proximity has stopped being the filter, the marked work is what you judge a tutor on, and four scripts across the first month is enough to form a view. Read them in a deliberate order, because the questions they answer build on each other.

The first script answers whether the tutor marks against the published scheme or against their own sense of the subject. Look for marks allocated per point, annotations naming the command word or the missing step, and a total that could be defended to an examiner. A script covered in encouraging comments and no mark allocation tells you the marking is impressionistic.

The second answers whether the diagnosis is specific. Lost marks should be attributed to a cause rather than a topic: method known but executed carelessly, structure missing on the extended response, content never learned, time run out. Four causes, counted. A diagnosis that says revise electrolysis is a topic label; one that says the chemistry is sound and the answer has no structure the scheme can credit is a plan.

The third and fourth answer the only question that matters, which is whether anything moved. The same question type, sat a fortnight apart, with the earlier losses marked. If the second attempt gains marks on precisely the thing the first attempt lost them on, the teaching is working. If the second attempt is a different question type entirely, nobody can tell, and that is worth raising before another month passes.

sections.heading: A session note worth keeping, and three that are not
paragraphs: A session note takes two minutes to write and makes a term auditable. Most providers either do not produce one or produce something that cannot be used, and since the note is the only record of what happened in a room you were not in, it is reasonable to be particular about it.

A useful note names four things. The paper and component worked on, with the syllabus code. What specifically was addressed, at the level of the question type rather than the topic. What the student did unaided by the end of the hour. And the one named task set before the next session. Four lines. A parent can read thirty of these in ten minutes and see the shape of a term.

Three notes that are not worth keeping. The first says good progress on algebra today, which names neither the paper nor the component and could describe any hour of any week. The second lists topics covered, which records delivery rather than learning and will look identical in October and in March. The third is a long narrative about the student's attitude, which is occasionally useful and never a substitute for a record of what was taught.

There is a reason to insist beyond tidiness. When a tutor changes, or when you need to take evidence to a head of department, the notes are what travels. A household with thirty readable notes can hand over a term of work in an email. A household without them is starting again, and paying for the restart.

sections.heading: What ten minutes of drive costs, per teaching minute
paragraphs: Visiting rates in this market sit above online rates for the same teacher, and the gap is the drive. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, on what other providers publish. Bestimate's 2026 table shows 180 to 350 for in-home work and independent home tutors are quoted at 200 to 500.

Those figures are per hour, which conceals the thing that actually varies. Convert to dirhams per teaching minute and the arithmetic changes shape, because a visiting hour routinely contains fewer teaching minutes than it looks: arrival, settling, a parent conversation at the door, and an early finish because the tutor has another household to reach. None of that is dishonest. It is simply what a drive does to an hour.

The table runs the comparison on a single assumed rate so the structure is visible rather than the price. Use your own quoted figures in the same frame and the question answers itself: which arrangement delivers the most teaching minutes for the money, and who is absorbing the travel. In every visiting arrangement somebody pays for the drive, and it is either the household in dirhams or the tutor in unpaid time, which eventually becomes the household's problem anyway.

One further note on monthly packages, because they are where comparisons break. Figures seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visiting sessions. Those are not the same purchase: eight contacts with eight sets of notes against four longer contacts with a travel component inside the price. Compare contacts and teaching minutes, not monthly totals.

sections.heading: Checking the permit yourself, in four steps
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit, and a parent can check the position in a single conversation. The permit exists because individual tutoring is regulated activity: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit, Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time.

Four steps. Ask whether the person holds the private tuition work permit. Ask which eligibility category they hold it under, since the permit is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see it, because a document that exists can be shown. And check the fee claim: the permit is granted at no charge for two years, so anybody describing a fee they paid for it is describing something else.

Two things not to accept. Do not accept a claim of regulator approval. No tutoring individual or platform holds KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB or Cambridge accreditation by virtue of tutoring, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises. IB Gram holds none of those and claims none. And do not accept a quoted fine figure for tutoring without a permit: individuals operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule is published, so any specific amount you are quoted is invented.

There is a related arrangement to avoid entirely. Press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the detail as press-reported and confirm the current ADEK document before quoting it, but do not build a plan around your child's own teacher.
